original p. 79

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.10 (Kannada); Sūkta 3, Eleventh Mantra: Saṃhitā and Pada text

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ - "Pāvakā" — "pāvaṃ kāyatīti pāvakā": from the root "kai" ("kai gai rai śabde," to sound) with "ka" after an upasarga-less word (आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः, āto 'nupasarge kaḥ, पा. ३-२-३); the substitution of "ā" for the final of the root by आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति (ād eca upadeśe 'śiti, पा. ६-१-४५); elision of the final "ā" before the affix (आतो लोप इटि च, āto lopa iṭi ca, पा. ६-४-६४); the feminine "ṭāp" (अजाद्यतष्टाप्, ajādy-ataṣ ṭāp, पा. ४-१-४) → "pāvakā"; being a kṛt-ending compound-member, the accent of the second member is retained by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९) as an end-acute. Alternatively, if "pūñ" ("he purifies") is intended, the affix "ṇvul" (ण्वुल्तृचौ, ṇvul-tṛcau, पा. ३-१-१३३) is added, and "yu/vu" are replaced by "ana/aka" (युवोरनाकौ, yuvor anākau, पा. ७-१-१), with the guṇa and "av-" substitution, giving "pāvaka," then "ṭāp" for the feminine "pāvakā." A difficulty is noted: by प्रत्ययस्थात्कात्पूर्वस्यात इदाप्यसुपः (pratyayasthāt kāt pūrvasyāta idāpy asupaḥ, पा. ७-३-४४) the "a" before "ka" would become "i" ("pāvikā"); the answer is that the non-occurrence of "i" in "pāvakā" is Vedic usage, by पावकादीनां छन्दसि प्रत्ययस्थात्कादित्वं नेति वाच्यम् [the print is garbled here; given as I read it]. The end-acute is likewise accepted as Vedic. - "Sarasvatī" — from "sṛ" with the Uṇādi "asun" → "saras"; the affix is "n"-marked (nit), so the first syllable is acute. The following "matup" and "ṅīp" are "p"-marked and unaccented.

Sūkta 3, The Eleventh Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

चोदयित्री सूनृतानां चेतन्ती सुमतीनाम् । यज्ञं दधे सरस्वती ॥११॥

codayitrī sūnṛtānāṃ cetantī sumatīnām | yajñaṃ dadhe sarasvatī ||11||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, rendered letter by letter; [?] where unclear.

चोदयित्री । सूनृतानाम् । चेतन्ती । सुमतीनाम् । यज्ञम् । दधे । सरस्वती ॥११॥

original p. 80

Rik 3.11: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar, Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha, English rendering; Special topic (opening)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यो सरस्वती सेयमिमं यज्ञं दधे । धारितवती । कीदृशी । सूनृतानां प्रियाणां सत्यवाक्यानां चोदयित्री प्रेरयित्री । सुमतीनां शोभनबुद्धियुक्तानामनुष्ठातॄणां चेतन्ती । तदीयमनुष्ठेयं ज्ञापयन्ती ॥ yo [print; "yā" would be expected] sarasvatī seyam imaṃ yajñaṃ dadhe | dhāritavatī | kīdṛśī | sūnṛtānāṃ priyāṇāṃ satya-vākyānāṃ codayitrī prerayitrī | sumatīnāṃ śobhana-buddhi-yuktānām anuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ cetantī | tadīyam anuṣṭheyaṃ jñāpayantī ||

Translation: "That Sarasvatī — she has taken up ('dadhe' = 'dhāritavatī') this sacrifice. What kind of one? 'Codayitrī' — the inciter, the impeller, of 'sūnṛtānām' — of pleasant, true utterances (or of those who speak them); 'cetantī' — the one who makes known, to the 'sumatīnām' — those of good understanding, the performers — what is to be performed by them." The print's first word reads "yo"; the sense needs "yā" ("who"), and the print is recorded as it stands.

Grammar within the Bhāṣya characterized; the print is partly garbled in the middle, and no reading of the unclear stretch is given: "Codayitrī" — root "cud" (to impel), "ṇic," then "tṛc"; "c"-marked, so the penultimate is acute (चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः); "ṅīp" (ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप्, पा. ४-१-५); the feminine ending is acute by उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वात् (udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt, पा. ६-१-१७४). "Sūnṛtānām" — "ūna parihāṇe" (to lessen) with "kvip"; "sūnīti priyam ucyate" — "sūn" denotes the pleasant; "ṛtaṃ satyam"; hence "sūnṛtam" = pleasant and true; the second member's acute follows the rule for compounds beginning with "para-ādi" in the Veda (बहुलमुत्तरपदादिः, as printed [?]). "Cetantī" — root "citī saṃjñāne" (to perceive); the "śap" is elided and "p"-marked, so unaccented; the stem's own accent remains; "ṅīp" etc. "Sumatīnām" — "mati" is first-syllable-acute; the genitive-plural ending's accent (पा. ६-१-१८२, as printed [?]).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सरस्वती (sarasvatī) — the goddess Sarasvatī | सूनृतानाम् (sūnṛtānām) — [of] pleasant and true words, or [of] men who speak such words | चोदयित्री (codayitrī) — one who impels | सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — (those who are devoted to sacrifices and the like) men of good understanding | चेतन्ती (cetantī) — one who makes (them) know (what is to be done in good works) | (such Sarasvatī) यज्ञम् (yajñam) — the sacrifice (that we are performing) | दधे (dadhe) — has taken up (carries through).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The goddess Sarasvatī, whom we praise, is she who impels men to speak pleasant and true words, or who inspires those who speak the truth to engage in good works, and who, by making known to men of good understanding what is to be done, helps them in doing right. May such a Sarasvatī bring the sacrifice that we perform to a faultless completion.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Saraswati, the inspirer of those who speak only the truth and instructress of the right-minded has supported the sacrifice."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This mantra is used in the sacrifice called Sautrāmaṇī; and also in the Vaiśvadeva, the Ukhāsambharaṇa (which, the source adds in English, "takes place at the new and full moon days") and the Ekāṣṭakā (the eighth day after full moon). Chiefly, this mantra is used in the rite called Vaiśvadeva, in the offering of the bali to Sarasvatī. Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." English words are as printed in the source. Nirukta reference-numbers are in small Kannada numerals and marked [?].

original p. 81

Special topics on Rik 3.11; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

चोदयित्री (codayitrī) — A form derived from the root "cud" ("cuda preraṇe," to impel); the sense is "she who impels." Western scholars explain it with the words : "Inspire, incite, rouse, stimulate, furnish, quickly, hasten, hurry, stir, agitate, encourage."

सूनृतानाम् (sūnṛtānām) — The word "sūnṛta" is read both among the fourteen words that indicate "speech" (Ni. 1-1[?]) and among the three words that indicate "anna" (food) (Ni. 2-7[?]) [numbers as read, uncertain]. This word is derived from the word "ṛta," which means "true, truth." Hence, in the Ṛgveda, Western scholars explain the word "sūnṛta" with such words as : "One delighting in truth, good word, agreeable speech, truth, song, receiving good qualities, joy-giving, glorious deed."

चेतन्ती (cetantī) — The sense of this word is, with a slight addition, the same as that of "codayitrī"; for it, such senses as "Perceive, conceive, understand, inspire" may be given.

सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — This word is formed from the root "man" (to think). For it one may give : "Think, meditate, contemplate, imagine, observe, believe, regard." In this Ṛk, for this word the senses "those who have good understanding," "those devoted to good deeds, or those who do them," "right-thinking, right-minded" may be given.

The chief import of this Ṛk: the goddess Sarasvatī impels men to speak true words and to do good works, and makes people's minds devoted to good activities. Therefore, she gives us good understanding in the sacrifice that we are now performing, makes that sacrifice reach completion with all its parts, and favours us so that we obtain its fruit.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Codayitrī": to the root "cud preraṇe" the affix "ṇic" is added; the penultimate light vowel takes guṇa, giving "codi-"; then "tṛc" (ण्वुल्तृचौ, ṇvul-tṛcau, पा. ३-१-१३३); "iṭ" comes to it by आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (पा. ७-२-३५); the "i" of "codi" takes guṇa (सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः, पा. ७-३-८४) and "ay" by एचोऽयवायावः (eco 'yavāyāvaḥ, पा. ६-१-७८) → "codayitṛ"; for the feminine, ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् (ṛnnebhyo ṅīp, पा. ४-१-५) — "ṅīp" after words ending in "ṛ" and "n" — and then यणादेशः (the semivowel substitution "ṛ → r") … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." This page is dense accent-derivation in Kannada prose, repeating the Sanskrit grammar of p. 80. Per the standing convention it is characterized, not translated line by line; the sūtras are kept. Some details are garbled in the print and are not given.

original p. 82

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.11 concluded — characterized

Continuing "codayitrī": …"codayitr + ī" → "codayitrī". Since "tṛc" is "c"-marked (चितः, पा. ६-१-१६३) the last syllable is acute; the feminine ending then takes the acute by उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वात् (udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt, पा. ६-१-१७४) — when an "ṇ"-substituted semivowel following a consonant stands for an acute vowel, the following case-ending is acute — hence "ī" is acute.

"Sūnṛtānām" — "ūna parihāṇau" (to lessen), with "kvip" by क्विप् च (पा. ३-२-७६) → "ūn"; "sutarām ūnayati apriyam" — "he who most completely removes what is unpleasant" — so "sūn" is a word for "the pleasant"; "ṛtam" = true; "sūn ca tad ṛtaṃ ca" — a karmadhāraya compound, "sūnṛtam." Here, by परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलम् (parādiś chandasi bahulam, पा. ६-२-१९९), in the Veda the beginning of the latter member is variably acute; so the first syllable of the second member is acute. Through "āyasmayādīni chandasi" (आयस्मयादीनि छन्दसि, पा. १-४-२०) the words "ayasmaya" and others in the Veda get the "bha" and "pada" labels as suitable; hence the "bha"-label arises, and since there is no "pada"-label, न लोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (na lopaḥ prātipadikāntasya, पा. ८-२-७) — the elision of the final "n" of a stem — does not apply to the "n" of "sūn."

"Cetantī" — root "citī saṃjñāne"; in place of "laṭ" the "śatṛ" affix (लटः शतृशानचावप्रथमासमानाधिकरणे, पा. ३-२-१२४) → "cit + at"; "śap" comes, then guṇa of the light penultimate, and by अतो गुणे (पा. ६-१-९४) the single form → "cetat"; "śatṛ" is "uk"-marked (उगितश्च, ugitaś ca, पा. ४-१-६), so "ṅīp" for the feminine, giving "cetat + ī"; by आच्छीनद्योर्नुम् (āc chīnadyor num, पा. ७-१-८०) "num" is the augment, optionally, when "śī" or "nadī"-labelled endings follow; "cetantī" results; by हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्… (पा. ६-१-६८) the elision. Both "śap" and "ṅīp" being "p"-marked, they are unaccented; the "śatṛ" affix is accented on the first syllable by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित् (पा. ६-१-१८६) [as printed, garbled] and the stem's own accent remains; the final vowel of "cetat," by धातोः (पा. ६-१-१६२) — the last vowel of a root is acute — is acute on the "e."

"Sumatīnām" — "śobhanā matiḥ yeṣāṃ te" — "those with good understanding," a bahuvrīhi; by नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) the second member is end-acute; after it, when the genitive plural ending is added, "nuṭ" is the augment and the vowel is lengthened — "sumatīnām." Here, by नामन्यतरस्याम् (nāmany atarasyām, पा. ६-१-१७७), in the case where the "matup"-final is elided... — if the stem is end-acute, the genitive plural ending "nām" is acute; thus the "nām" of "sumatīnām" is acute. ॥११॥ Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Accent-marks not reproduced; see the note at Rik 3.5. Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, rendered letter by letter.

original p. 83

Sūkta 3, Twelfth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pada-meanings

Sūkta 3, The Twelfth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

महो अर्णः सरस्वती प्र चेतयति केतुना । धियो विश्वा वि राजति ॥१२॥

maho arṇaḥ sarasvatī pra cetayati ketunā | dhiyo viśvā vi rājati ||12||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

महः । अर्णः । सरस्वती । प्र । चेतयति । केतुना । धियः । विश्वाः । वि । राजति ॥१२॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

द्विविधा हि सरस्वती विग्रहवद्देवता नदीरूपा च । तत्र पूर्वाभ्यामृग्भ्यां विग्रहवती प्रतिपादिता । अनया तु नदीरूपा प्रतिपाद्यते । तादृशी सरस्वती केतुना कर्मणा प्रवाहरूपेण महो अर्णः प्रभूतमुदकं प्र चेतयति । प्रकर्षेण ज्ञापयति । किंच । स्वकीयेन देवतारूपेण विश्वा धियः सर्वाण्यनुष्ठातृप्रज्ञानानि विराजति । विशेषेण दीपयति । अनुष्ठानविषया बुद्धिः । सर्वोत्पादयतीत्यर्थः । dvividhā hi sarasvatī vigrahavad-devatā nadī-rūpā ca | tatra pūrvābhyām ṛgbhyāṃ vigrahavatī pratipāditā | anayā tu nadī-rūpā pratipādyate | tādṛśī sarasvatī ketunā karmaṇā pravāha-rūpeṇa maho arṇaḥ prabhūtam udakaṃ pra cetayati | prakarṣeṇa jñāpayati | kiṃca | svakīyena devatā-rūpeṇa viśvā dhiyaḥ sarvāṇy anuṣṭhātṛ-prajñānāni virājati | viśeṣeṇa dīpayati | anuṣṭhāna-viṣayā buddhiḥ | sarvotpādayatīty arthaḥ |

Translation: "Sarasvatī is indeed of two kinds: a deity with a body (a goddess), and in the form of a river. Of these, the two preceding Ṛks presented her as the embodied one; by this Ṛk she is presented in river form. Such a Sarasvatī, 'ketunā' — by her action, in the form of her flow — makes known ('pra cetayati') 'maho arṇaḥ' — abundant water; that is, makes it known in an eminent way. Further, by her own form as a deity she 'virājati' — shines forth, illumines distinctly — all 'dhiyaḥ' — all the understandings of the performers; the understanding concerned with performance; the sense is: she produces them all." The final clause, "sarvotpādayatīty arthaḥ," is printed as given; It is read as continuing the sentence, and the sense is a little loose.

सरस्वत्या द्विरूपत्वं यास्को दर्शयति । तत्र सरस्वतीत्येतस्य नदीवद्देवतावच्च निगमा भवन्ति । नि. २-२३ । इति । एकशतसंख्याकेषूदकनामसु अर्णः क्षोद इति पठितम् । एतामृचं यास्को व्याचष्ट । महदर्णः सरस्वती प्रचेतयति प्रज्ञापयति केतुना कर्मणा प्रज्ञया वेमानि च सर्वाणि प्रज्ञानान्यभिविराजति । नि. ११-२१ । इति ॥ sarasvatyā dvirūpatvaṃ yāsko darśayati | tatra sarasvatīty etasya nadīvad devatāvac ca nigamā bhavanti | ni. 2-23 [?] | iti | ekaśata-saṃkhyākeṣūdaka-nāmasv arṇaḥ kṣoda iti paṭhitam | etām ṛcaṃ yāsko vyācaṣṭa | mahad arṇaḥ sarasvatī pracetayati prajñāpayati ketunā karmaṇā prajñayā vemāni ca sarvāṇi prajñānāny abhivirājati | ni. 11-2[?] | iti ||

Translation: "Yāska shows the twofold nature of Sarasvatī: 'Of this "Sarasvatī" the Vedic passages are both river-like and deity-like' (Nirukta 2-23 [?]). Among the hundred-and-one names of water, 'arṇaḥ' and 'kṣodaḥ' are read. Yāska explains this Ṛk thus: 'Sarasvatī makes known a great flood ("arṇaḥ"), by her action, and by her wisdom she shines over all these kinds of knowledge.' (Nirukta 11-2[?])."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya characterized, sūtras kept: "Mahaḥ" — "mahat" with the final "t" turned into "s" by vyatyaya (Vedic licence), then "ru" → "ḥ"; the accent of the bare stem falls on its last syllable. एङः पदान्तादति (eṅaḥ padāntād ati, पा. ६-१-१०९) would give the preceding form ("pūrvarūpa"), but by प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपरे (prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare, पा. ६-१-११५) the natural form is retained within the pāda. "Arṇaḥ" — from "ṛ," the Uṇādi affix "asun" (उ. ४-१९६ [?]), with the augment "nuṭ," and "ṛ" taking guṇa. "Ketunā" — the accent of the bare stem is on the last syllable. "Viśvāḥ" — "viśva" has the first syllable acute, as it ends in the affix "kvan" (क्वन् [?]). The print here closes the Bhāṣya with the marks "॥ ६ ॥ ॥ १ ॥" — these are read as the varga-end marks; the verse-number ॥१२॥ itself is printed at the end of the grammar on p. 85.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सरस्वती (sarasvatī) — the river Sarasvatī | केतुना (ketunā) — by an action in the form of flowing (by flowing) | महो अर्णः (maho arṇaḥ) — very abundant water | प्र चेतयति (pra cetayati) — makes known in an eminent way | (और) विश्वाः धियः (viśvāḥ dhiyaḥ) — (and) the understanding (the wisdom) of all people (devoted to sacrifice and rites) | वि राजति (vi rājati) — illumines. Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." English as printed in the source.

original p. 84

Rik 3.12: Bhāvārtha, English rendering; Special topics (opening)

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Since the river Sarasvatī flows with a very deep current, there is a great deal of water in this river; and this goddess also illumines the minds of those who praise her or who worship her by sacrifice — that is, she impels people's understanding so that it becomes keen.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Saraswati (river) manifests herself by her acts (flowing) as a mighty river and (in her own form) enlightens peoples's [sic] minds."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This mantra is used in the sacrifice called Sautrāmaṇī, for praising Sarasvatī. Yāska has explained this Ṛk in his Nirukta as follows — "mahad arṇaḥ sarasvatī pracetayati prajñāpayati ketunā karmaṇā prajñayā vemāni ca sarvāṇi prajñānāny abhivirājati" (महदर्णः सरस्वती प्रचेतयति प्रज्ञापयति केतुना कर्मणा प्रज्ञया वेमानि च सर्वाणि प्रज्ञानान्यभिविराजति — Ni. 11-2[?]). Both the river form and the form of the goddess of speech of Sarasvatī Yāska states in the passage "tatra sarasvatīty etasya nadīvad devatāvac ca nigamā bhavanti" (तत्र सरस्वतीत्येतस्य नदीवद्देवतावच्च निगमा भवन्ति — Ni. 2-2[?]). In this Ṛk, in the first half — that is, in the first two pādas — Sarasvatī is regarded and praised as being of river form, and in the third pāda as being of the form of a deity.

महो अर्णः (maho arṇaḥ) — The word "arṇa" is read among the hundred-and-one [print: "101" — read with care] names that indicate water. "Arṇa" means "water" and also "river." Here, although the river Sarasvatī was not a large river like the Sindhu and others, the praise of her as "maho arṇaḥ" — a big river with abundant floods — is right, we may say: for when one is praising, it is customary in the world to magnify and extol even a little of the quality that a deity has; moreover, the ṛṣi of this Ṛk, Madhucchanda, may have seen no large rivers such as the Sindhu, being far from them. It is therefore natural that he praises this river as a very large river, with abundant water in it.

केतुना (ketunā) — The Bhāṣyakāra and Yāska both explain this as "karmaṇā" — "by action." When it is explained as relating to the river, "ketunā" means "by the flow (of the nature of a figure of speech, rūpaka-karma)," so deep and so abundant; and when explained as relating to the deity, it may mean "by the action that stirs (impels) the minds of people." The deep, endless and impetuous flood of the river Sarasvatī (the source's English: "Saraswati's mighty, endless and impetuous flood") is described in many mantras, such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-6[?]-1[?] [?]. For this word Western scholars give "Brightness, banner, flag, activity, wisdom." Skandasvāmī gives for "ketunā" … "by the action that is of the nature of a roar (garjanā)…" Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.

original p. 85

Special topics on Rik 3.12 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Sūkta 3

Continuing "ketunā" from p. 84: …Skandasvāmī, that is, explains "ketunā" as "by the action of roaring"; Yāska explains it as "karmaṇā prajñayā vā" ("by action, or by wisdom"). The view of Uvvaṭa and Mahīdhara is the same as Skandasvāmī's. Veṅkaṭamādhava gives for "ketunā" only "karmaṇā."

धियः (dhiyaḥ) — "Buddhi, ālocanā" (understanding, reflection). Yāska and Skandasvāmī (in the sense of) "prajñā" and "karman"; Veṅkaṭamādhava, "prajñā"; Uvvaṭa and Mahīdhara, "buddhi." Among Western scholars, Grassmann gives "act of devotion," and another scholar name not legible in the print "Devotion, thought" .

विराजति (virājati) — The Bhāṣyakāra explains it as "viśeṣeṇa dīpayati" ("illumines in a special way") — that is, "causes to shine greatly, impels, kindles." For this word, which is the third person singular of the root "rāj," the senses "shine, preside, govern, brighten" may be given. "Dhiyo virājati" means "she impels the minds to engage in good works," or "she makes our minds contented."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Maho arṇaḥ": the "t" of "mahat" becomes "s" by vyatyaya (Vedic licence); for the "s," ससजुषो रुः (sasajuṣo ruḥ, पा. ८-२-६६) gives "ru"; for "ru," रुग्तोरोरुप्लुतादप्लुते (ato ror aplutād aplute, पा. ६-१-११३) gives "u"; "mah + u"; then अदुग्णे [print; I read it as the guṇa rule आद्गुणः (ād guṇaḥ), पा. ६-१-८७, but the print differs, and I do not alter it] gives guṇa → "maho." When it joins the word "arṇaḥ," एङः पदान्तादति (पा. ६-१-१०९) would produce the preceding form, but प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपरे (पा. ६-१-११५) keeps the natural form for "e/o" at the end of a word inside a pāda, when a short "a" follows, and not "v/y" (the print: when a "va" or "ya" follows after the short vowel, this does not apply); so, the natural form is retained, and we have "maho arṇaḥ." "Arṇaḥ" — from the root "ṛ gatau" ("ṛ, to go": "it flows, goes" — "arṇaḥ"); when the sense "water" is intended, the Uṇādi-sūtra उदके नुट् च (udake nuṭ ca, उ. सू. ४-१९६ [?]) — after "ṛ," "asun" with the augment "nuṭ"; with them, "ṛ + nas" → guṇa → "ar + nas"; by रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे (पा. ८-४-१) the "n" becomes "ṇ"; "ru"-substitution and visarga: "arṇaḥ." "Ketunā" — from the stem-accent it is end-acute. "Viśvāḥ" — "viśva" is formed with the "kvan" affix and is first-syllable acute. ॥१२॥

इल्लिगे ३नेय सूक्तवु संपूर्णवु — illige 3neya sūktavu sampūrṇavu — "Here the third sūkta is complete." Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Sanskrit is printed in Kannada script and rendered here into Devanagari/IAST; reference-numbers in small Kannada numerals are marked [?] where uncertain. Heading printed: "॥ ओम् ॥ — ನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು (the fourth sūkta)".

Sūkta 4 — "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye"

original p. 86

Sūkta 4: title; Sāyaṇa's introduction; the Anuvāda (opening)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

प्रथमे मण्डले द्वितीयेऽनुवाके चत्वारि सूक्तानि । तत्र सुरूपेत्यादिकं दशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं सुरूपकृत्नुं दशेत्यनुक्रान्तत्वात् । पूर्वस्मान्मधुच्छन्दसो गायत्रस्य चानुवृत्तेरस्य एवर्षिश्छन्दसी । इन्द्रं पृच्छेति चतुर्थ्यामृचि लिङ्गदर्शनादिन्द्रो देवता । अभिप्लवषडहे ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः प्रातःसवने स्तोमवृद्ध्यावापार्थानि सुरूपकृत्नुमूतय इत्यादीनि षट् सूक्तानि । सूत्रितं चाभिप्लवपृष्ठ्याहानीति खण्डे ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः सुरूपकृत्नुमूतय इति षट् सूक्तानि । आ. ७-५ [?] । इति । आद्यानि त्रीणि सूक्तानि महाव्रते निष्केवल्य औष्णिहतृचाशीतौ शस्तव्यानि । उक्तं च शौनकेन । सुरूपकृत्नुमूतय इति त्रीण्येन्द्र सानसिं रयिमिति सूक्ते । ऐ. आ. ५-२-५ [?] । इति । चतुर्विंशेऽहनि माध्यन्दिने सवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः सुरूपकृत्नुमूतय इति वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । होत्रकाणामिति खण्डे मदे मदे हि नो ददिः सुरूपकृत्नुमूतये । आ. ७-४ [?] । इति सूत्रितत्वात् । अग्निष्टोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे सुरूपकृत्नुमूतय इति धाय्या । सुरूपकृत्नुमूतये तक्षन्रथम् । आ. ५-१८ [?] । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ prathame maṇḍale dvitīye 'nuvāke catvāri sūktāni | tatra surūpetyādikaṃ daśarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktaṃ surūpakṛtnuṃ daśety anukrāntatvāt | pūrvasmān madhucchandaso gāyatrasya cānuvṛtter asya evarṣi-cchandasī | indraṃ pṛccheti caturthyām ṛci liṅga-darśanād indro devatā | abhiplava-ṣaḍahe brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ prātaḥ-savane stoma-vṛddhy-āvāpārthāni surūpakṛtnum ūtaya ity ādīni ṣaṭ sūktāni | sūtritaṃ cābhiplava-pṛṣṭhy-āhānīti khaṇḍe brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ surūpakṛtnum ūtaya iti ṣaṭ sūktāni | ā. 7-5 [?] | iti | ādyāni trīṇi sūktāni mahāvrate niṣkevalya auṣṇiha-tṛcāśītau śastavyāni | uktaṃ ca śaunakena | surūpakṛtnum ūtaya iti trīṇy endra sānasiṃ rayim iti sūkte | ai. ā. 5-2-5 [?] | iti | caturviṃśe 'hani mādhyandine savane brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ surūpakṛtnum ūtaya iti vaikalpikaḥ stotriyas tṛcaḥ | hotrakāṇām iti khaṇḍe made made hi no dadiḥ surūpakṛtnum ūtaye | ā. 7-4 [?] | iti sūtritatvāt | agniṣṭome vaiśvadeva-śastre surūpakṛtnum ūtaya iti dhāyyā | surūpakṛtnum ūtaye takṣan ratham | ā. 5-18 [?] | iti sūtritatvāt ||

Translation: "In the first Maṇḍala, in the second Anuvāka, there are four sūktas. Of these, the first, beginning 'surūpa…', is of ten Ṛks, as the Anukramaṇī has it: 'surūpakṛtnuṃ daśa.' Because of the continuation (anuvṛtti) from the preceding, the ṛṣi and metre of this one are the same — Madhucchandas, and Gāyatrī. By the evidence of the gender-mark in the fourth Ṛk, 'indraṃ pṛccha,' Indra is the deity. In the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha (six-day rite), at the morning pressing, the six sūktas beginning 'surūpakṛtnum ūtaye' are (to be recited) by the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin for the increase and the insertion (āvāpa) of the stoma; and this is laid down in the sūtra, in the section 'abhiplava-pṛṣṭhy-āhāni': 'the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's six sūktas beginning "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye"' (Āśv. [Śrauta-sūtra] 7-5 [?]). The first three of these sūktas are to be recited, in the Mahāvrata, as the niṣkevalya-śastra, together with an Auṣṇiha tṛca, in the 'aśīti' (the eighty-verse recitation). And it has been said by Śaunaka: 'surūpakṛtnum ūtaye — three; and the two sūktas "indra sānasiṃ rayim"' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 5-2-5 [?]). On the twenty-fourth day, at the midday pressing, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's tṛca 'surūpakṛtnum ūtaye' is an optional stotriya tṛca; and in the section on the Hotrakas it is laid down: 'made made hi no dadiḥ, surūpakṛtnum ūtaye' (Āśv. 7-4 [?]). In the Agniṣṭoma, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, 'surūpakṛtnum ūtaye' is the dhāyyā (the 'placing' verse): 'surūpakṛtnum ūtaye; takṣan ratham' (Āśv. 5-18 [?])."

॥ Anuvādaḥ ॥ Kannada commentary, translated

As we said earlier (see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part II, page 3 [?]), the three sūktas of the first anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala are finished. From here the second Anuvāka begins. In this anuvāka there are four sūktas — (1) "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye," (2) "ā tvetā niṣīdata," (3) "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam," (4) "indram id gāthino bṛhat." Each of these four sūktas has ten Ṛks. As for the preceding sūktas, the ṛṣi of all four of these sūktas is the same Madhucchandas Vaiśvāmitra; the deity of this sūkta is Indra. In the first three Ṛks no deity's name is explicitly given; but because in the fourth Ṛk the words "indraṃ pṛccha" are used, and since from there on in the 5th, 6th, 7th and 10th [?] Ṛks too the word "Indra" occurs, Indra is the deity of this whole sūkta. There is no rule that the deity's name must occur in all the Ṛks of a sūkta; where some Ṛks have it, the remaining Ṛks present that deity's subject, and so… continues on the next page Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 2 [?], Varga 7, 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā."

original p. 87

Viniyoga of Sūkta 4; heading: ṛṣi, deity, metre; Rik 4.1 (Saṃhitā, Pada)

Continuing: …so the same deity must be said to apply to all the Ṛks of the sūkta. The order of application (viniyoga) of this sūkta is as follows. In the sacrifice called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, in the morning pressing, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin — the assistant ṛtvij of the Hotṛ — is to recite this sūkta "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye," together with the next five sūktas, for the increase of the stoma. In this regard, the sūtra: "sūtritaṃ cābhiplava-pṛṣṭhy-āhānīti khaṇḍe brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ surūpakṛtnum ūtaya iti ṣaṭ sūktāni" (सूत्रितं चाभिप्लवपृष्ठ्याहानीति खण्डे ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः सुरूपकृत्नुमूतय इति षट् सूक्तानि — Āśv. Sū. 7-5 [?]). Of these six sūktas the first three are used in the rite called Mahāvrata as niṣkevalya-śastra mantras, as stated in the section "abhiplava-pṛṣṭhy-āhāni." Here Śaunaka has quoted the sentence of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka: "surūpakṛtnum ūtaya iti trīṇy endra sānasiṃ rayim iti sūkte" (Ai. Ā. 5-2-5 [?]) — that is, the three sūktas beginning "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye" and the two sūktas beginning "indra sānasiṃ rayim" are to be recited. Further, in the above-mentioned rite, on the twenty-fourth day, at the midday pressing, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin may optionally recite the tṛca "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye" (three Ṛks). The Āśvalāyana-sūtra says in the section "hotrakāṇām": "made made hi no dadiḥ surūpakṛtnum ūtaye" (Āśv. Sū. 7-4 [?]) — that the tṛca "made made hi no dadiḥ" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-8[?]-2) and the tṛca "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye" (1-4-1) are to be recited; and in the Agniṣṭoma, when reciting the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras — "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-4-1) and "takṣan rathaṃ suvṛtam" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-111-1) (Āśv. Sū. 5-18 [?]) — it is said in the Āśvalāyana sūtra that these Ṛks may be recited as special mantras.

॥ ओम् ॥

सूक्त—४ Sūkta 4 ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—२ ॥ सूक्त—४ ॥ ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय—१ ॥ वर्ग—७, ८ [?] ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्ये १० ॥ number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10 ऋषिः — मधुच्छन्दा वैश्वामित्रः (ṛṣiḥ — madhucchandā vaiśvāmitraḥ) देवता — इन्द्रः (devatā — indraḥ) छन्दः — गायत्री (chandaḥ — gāyatrī)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Accent-marks not reproduced; see the note at Rik 3.5. Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; [?] where unclear.

सुरूपकृत्नुमूतये सुदुघामिव गोदुहे । जुहूमसि द्यविद्यवि ॥१॥

surūpakṛtnum ūtaye sudughām iva goduhe | juhūmasi dyavidyavi ||1||

original p. 88

Rik 4.1: Pada-pāṭha, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings (opening)

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading note: the print divides the compounds with marks read as "sudughām-iva" and "go-duhe," "dyavi-dyavi"; The divisions are given as read from the printed signs.

सुरूपकृत्नुम् । ऊतये । सुदुघाम्ऽइव । गोऽदुहे । जुहूमसि । द्यविऽद्यवि ॥१॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

सुरूपकृत्नुं शोभनरूपोपेतस्य कर्मणः कर्तारमिन्द्रमूतयेऽस्मद्रक्षणार्थं द्यवि द्यवि प्रतिदिनं जुहूमसि । आह्वयामः । आह्वाने दृष्टान्तः । गोदुहे गोदुगर्थं सुदुघामिव सुष्ठु दोग्ध्रीं गामिव । यथा लोके गोर्दोग्धा दोहार्थं तस्याभिमुखेन दोहनीयां गामाह्वयति तद्वत् । वस्तोरित्यादिषु द्वादशसंख्याकेष्वहर्नामसु द्यविद्यवीति पठितम् । surūpakṛtnuṃ śobhana-rūpopetasya karmaṇaḥ kartāram indram ūtaye 'smad-rakṣaṇārthaṃ dyavi dyavi pratidinaṃ juhūmasi | āhvayāmaḥ | āhvāne dṛṣṭāntaḥ | goduhe go-dugarthaṃ sudughām iva suṣṭhu dogdhrīṃ gām iva | yathā loke gor dogdhā dohārthaṃ tasyābhimukhena dohanīyāṃ gām āhvayati tadvat | vastor ity ādiṣu dvādaśa-saṃkhyākeṣv ahar-nāmasu dyavidyavīti paṭhitam |

Translation: "'Surūpakṛtnum' — the doer of action endowed with beautiful form — Indra — we call, 'ūtaye' — for our protection — 'dyavi dyavi' — day by day. The illustration for the calling: 'goduhe' — for the milker of the cow ('go-dug'), 'sudughām iva' — like a good milch-cow ('suṣṭhu dogdhrī gauḥ'). As, in the world, the milker of a cow calls the cow that is to be milked, to face him, for the sake of the milking, so (we call Indra). Among the twelve names for 'day,' beginning with 'vastoḥ,' 'dyavidyavi' is read."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, not transcribed line by line; every sūtra cited is kept): "Surūpakṛtnum": "karoti iti kṛtnuḥ" — the affix "knu" after "kṛ" and "hi" (कृहिभ्यां क्नुः, उ. सू. ३-३० [?]); since "knu" is "k"-marked, the guṇa does not occur; the "t" is inserted, a Vedic usage; the compound's accent is on its last syllable. "Ūtaye": "av" (to protect) takes "ktin" in the Vedic list "ūti-yūti-jūti-sāti-hetī-kīrtayaś ca" (ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च, पा. ३-३-९७), which is irregularly formed (nipātana) and has the end-acute. "Sudughām": "su" + "dugdhā"; the affix "kap" after "duh" (दुहः कब्घश्च, पा. ५-४-८० [?]), and the "h" becomes "gh"; "kap" being "p"-marked, the accent of the root remains with the "u" acute. With "su" as a gati-compound, the second member's accent is retained; with "iva" the case-ending is not elided (इवेन विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च, as on p. 58). "Goduhe": "gāṃ dogdhīti godhuk" — "kvip" in the sense of "doer" by सत्सूद्विषद्रुहदुहयुजविदभिदच्छिदजिनीराजामुपसर्गेऽपि क्विप् (पा. ३-२-६१); the accent of the second member of a kṛt compound is retained. "Juhūmasi": "hve" (hūyate) in the first-person plural laṭ; "śap" is replaced by "ślu" in the Veda (बहुलं छन्दसि, पा. २-४-७३); doubling of the root (श्लौ, पा. ६-१-१०); the "samprasāraṇa" and the "pūrvarūpa" (संप्रसारणाच्च, पा. ६-१-१०८); the lengthening (हलः, पा. ६-४-२, as printed); shortening of the reduplicative syllable (ह्रस्वः, पा. ७-४-५९); "ch/j" substitution (चुत्वम्…, as printed); the "mas" ending takes "i" by इदन्तो मसिः (पा. ७-१-४६); the "m" is acute by the accent of the affix. "Dyavi dyavi": "dyu" has the bare-stem accent on the last syllable; in the sense of repetition the word is doubled (नित्यवीप्सयोः, पा. ८-१-४); and the second is, by परमाम्रेडितम् (पा. ८-१-२) and अनुदात्तं च (पा. ८-१-३) [numbers as printed], unaccented.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ Kannada, translated; continued on the next page

गोदुहे (goduhe) — for the sake of milking | सुदुघामिव (sudughām iva) — like a cow that gives milk (or that gives much milk) | सुरूपकृत्नुम् (surūpakṛtnum) — (him) who does good (beautiful) deeds — (Indra) … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." English as printed in the source. The verse cited below is as printed; The same Ṛk was already quoted in Sūkta 3, p. 25 of this volume's earlier text.

original p. 89

Rik 4.1: Pada-meanings concluded; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

…who does (Indra) | ऊतये (ūtaye) — for (our) protection | द्यविद्यवि (dyavidyavi) — every day | जुहूमसि (juhūmasi) — we call (we call him to come near us).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Kannada, translated

Just as we call, with love, a cow that gives milk, to come near us, so every day, for our protection, we call to us Indra, who can do wonderful — that is, daring — deeds.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"We invoke the performer of beautiful actions (Indra) day by day for our protection like a good milch-cow for the purpose of milking."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सुरूपकृत्नुम् (surūpakṛtnum) — This word is not used elsewhere in the Ṛgveda than in this Ṛk. The Bhāṣyakāra explains this word as "śobhana-rūpopetasya karmaṇaḥ kartāram" ("the doer of action endowed with beautiful form") — one who does works of a good form. The explanation of Skandasvāmī and Veṅkaṭamādhava is the same. Griffith and Macdonell follow Sāyaṇa's sense. Grassmann, the German scholar: "He who knows to perform beautiful things" — one with the power to do beautiful deeds; Ludwig: "Creater [sic] of beautiful forms" — one who can create beautiful shapes. But Geldner: "when he assumes his good forms or he who shows himself from his best side" — "one who shows his own best form" — and in support of this meaning he has cited the Ṛk:

रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव तदस्य रूपं प्रतिचक्षणाय । इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-४७-१८) rūpaṃ-rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva tad asya rūpaṃ praticakṣaṇāya | indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hy asya harayaḥ śatā daśa || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-18) The source's English (from Geldner): "He has become suitable to every form; this true form of his is to be recognised again and again. Indra assumes many forms by virtue of his mysterious power; for, ten hundred horses have been yoked for him."

— the chief import being that Indra, by his own power of māyā, is able to assume many forms. And… Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Ṛg-vedic and Nirukta reference-numbers are in small Kannada numerals and all are marked [?]. The glosses on verses are editorial and tentative; the source gives none. In the Nirukta passage one word is unclear and flagged.

original p. 90

Special topics on Rik 4.1 (continued): Indra's many forms; "surūpakṛtnum" and "lokakṛtnum"; "ūtaye" (opening)

Continuing from p. 89: In the Ṛk

रूपंरूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानस्तन्वं परि स्वाम् । (ऋ. सं. ३-५३-८ [?]) rūpaṃ-rūpaṃ maghavā bobhavīti māyāḥ kṛṇvānas tanvaṃ pari svām | (ṛ. saṃ. 3-53-8 [?]) Gloss: "Maghavan becomes form after form, working his magic arts around his own body."

too it is said that Indra is able to assume many forms. In the Nirukta as well (Ni. 10-1[?]) this Ṛk is explained thus:

विश्वामित्रस्यार्षम् । यावन्ति कानिचिद्रूपाणि मघवा इन्द्रो भवितुमिच्छति तानि सर्वाण्यप्रतिबन्धेन बोभवीति पुनःपुनर्भवतीति । कथम् । मायाः कृण्वानः इदं भवामीदं भवामीत्येवं "तन्वं परि स्वां" स्वां तनुं तत्तदाकृत्यानेकविधां विकुर्वाणः । तेनासौ [?]चिन्त्यप्रभावत्वाच्छक्नोति तत्तद्रूपमावेष्टुम् ॥ इत्यादि viśvāmitrasyārṣam | yāvanti kānicid rūpāṇi maghavā indro bhavitum icchati tāni sarvāṇy apratibandhena bobhavīti punaḥ-punar bhavatīti | katham | māyāḥ kṛṇvānaḥ idaṃ bhavāmīdaṃ bhavāmīty evaṃ "tanvaṃ pari svāṃ" svāṃ tanuṃ tat-tad-ākṛtyānekavidhāṃ vikurvāṇaḥ | tenāsau [?]cintya-prabhāvatvāc chaknoti tat-tad-rūpam āveṣṭum || ity ādi

Translation: "(This Ṛk is) the revelation of Viśvāmitra. Whatever forms Maghavan Indra wishes to become, all of them he becomes without hindrance, again and again. How? 'Working māyās': 'I become this, I become this' — thus 'around his own body' — his own body, in this and that shape, transforming it in many ways. Therefore, through his [a]-inconceivable power ("[a]cintya-prabhāvatvāt" — the first letter of the word is not clear to me), he is able to enter into this or that form," and so on.

That is, in this Ṛk the ṛṣi Viśvāmitra says this: Indra, by his power of māyā, is able to transform his own body in many ways — that is, to take on, as the occasion requires, many different bodily forms. In the time of slaying enemies he can take a terrible form, and in fulfilling the wishes of the worshipper or of the people who praise him he can take a lovely form; and he has the power of māyā suited to such actions. Therefore, since in the Ṛk in hand the word "surūpakṛtnum" is used in calling Indra, with love, for our protection, the ṛṣi may have used the word to signify that Indra should come here, taking, by his power of māyā, a beautiful — that is, a gracious — form, to guard us. The word "kṛtnu" occurs, as the latter member of a compound, in the word "lokakṛtnum," which is found only in these two Ṛks:

तं ते मदं गृणीमसि वृषणं पृत्सु सासहिम् । उ लोककृत्नुमद्रिवो हरिश्रियम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-१७-४ [?]) taṃ te madaṃ gṛṇīmasi vṛṣaṇaṃ pṛtsu sāsahim | u lokakṛtnum adrivo hariśriyam || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-17-4 [?]) Gloss: "That exhilaration of yours we praise, the bull, the conqueror in battles, the world-maker, O wielder of the stone, the splendour of the bay horses."

तं त्वा मदाय घृष्वय उ लोककृत्नुमीमहे । तव प्रशस्तयो महीः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ८-२-? [?]) taṃ tvā madāya ghṛṣvaya u lokakṛtnum īmahe | tava praśastayo mahīḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 8-2-? [?]) Gloss: "Thee, the world-maker, we entreat for the exhilaration, for the bold one; great are your praises."

— This word is, in both Ṛks, applied to Indra, that is, it applies to Indra.

ऊतये (ūtaye) — "For protection; for guarding." This word and its other forms — ūtayaḥ, ūtīḥ, ūtibhiḥ, ūtim, ūtiṣu, ūtī, ūtīḥ, ūtyā — are used in many places in the Ṛgveda. In the Nirukta (Ni. 5-3 [?]), "ūtiḥ" is explained as "āvanam" (protection), and… Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Reference-numbers marked [?]; glosses editorial.

original p. 91

Special topics on Rik 4.1 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

Continuing "ūtaye": …and he explains the word "ūtaye" in the Ṛk quoted as an example:

आ त्वा रथं यथोतये सुम्नाय वर्तयामसि । (ऋ. सं. ८-३-१ [?]) ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaye sumnāya vartayāmasi | (ṛ. saṃ. 8-3-1 [?]) Gloss: "As (one turns) a chariot for aid, we turn you hither for favour."

as "avanāya, rakṣaṇāya" (for protecting). Such examples are many in the Ṛgveda. Ṛks in which Indra is entreated to save the worshippers from the harm of enemies, to make them fearless, and to protect them, occur in many places in the Ṛgveda:

त्रातारमिन्द्रमवितारमिन्द्रं हवेहवे सुहवं शूरमिन्द्रम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-४७-११) trātāram indram avitāram indraṃ have-have suhavaṃ śūram indram || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-11) Gloss: "Indra the saviour, Indra the helper, Indra, easily invoked at every call, the hero."

बाधतां द्वेषो अभयं कृणोतु सुवीर्यस्य पतयः स्याम ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-४७-१२) bādhatāṃ dveṣo abhayaṃ kṛṇotu suvīryasya patayaḥ syāma || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-12) Gloss: "May he drive off hatred, may he make fearlessness; may we be masters of good heroism."

There are many Ṛks of this kind concerning Indra.

सुदुघामिव गोदुहे (sudughām iva goduhe) — "As one calls a cow for milk." This simile — or similes of the same sense (the source's term: "lupta-upamā") — are used in many places in the Ṛgveda, so it seems that in that age this sentence was a customary one to cite as an illustration:

तं त्वा वयं सुदुघामिव गोदुहो जुहूमसि श्रवस्यवः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ८-५२-४ [?]) taṃ tvā vayaṃ sudughām iva goduho juhūmasi śravasyavaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 8-52-4 [?]) Gloss: "Thee we call, like milkers a good milch-cow, seeking fame."

इन्द्रं धेनुं सुदुघामन्यामिषमुरुधारामरंकृतम् । (ऋ. सं. ८-१-१०) indraṃ dhenuṃ sudughām anyām iṣam urudhārām araṃkṛtam | (ṛ. saṃ. 8-1-10) Gloss: "Indra — the good milch-cow, another refreshment, broad-streamed, well-fashioned." [tentative; the print gives only this line]

उपह्वये सुदुघां धेनुमेतां सुहस्तो गोधुगुत दोहदेनाम् । (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-२६ [?]) upahvaye sudughāṃ dhenum etāṃ suhasto godhug uta dohad enām | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-26 [?]) Gloss: "I call this good milch-cow near; may the skilful-handed milker milk her."

A cow that gives milk is dear to everyone; likewise Indra, who protects from the harm of enemies, is desired by all — such is the import.

द्यविद्यवि (dyavidyavi) — "Every day." By नित्यवीप्सयोः (nityavīpsayoḥ, पा. ८-१-४) there is doubling: when a single word is read twice, the sense is "each one." Examples: dive-dive ("every day"), āharahaḥ, māsi-māsi ("every month"), yajñe-yajñe ("at every sacrifice"), bhare-bhare ("in every battle"), have-have ("at every call"), dame-dame ("in every house"), and the like.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept 4th Sūkta, Rik 1. "Surūpakṛtnum": a root meaning "to make" ("kṛ"); after the seven roots ṛ-ṣap-śilp-śap-bāp-rūpa-parṣa [?] (the list as printed: "khuṣpa śilpa śaṣpa bāpa rūpa parṣa …" — I read it with doubt; Uṇ. Sū. 3-3[?]8 [?]) — "ṛñ avadāraṇe" (to tear), "śīlasamādhau" (to practise), "śaśu hiṃsāyām" (to kill), "bādhṛ loḍane" (to disturb), "rū śabde" (to sound), "pūpālanapūraṇayoḥ" (to protect and fill), "talapratiṣṭhākaraṇe" — an affix "pa" … Page headers: p. 92 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4"; p. 93 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." These two pages are pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose, the Kannada rendering of the grammar already given in Sanskrit on p. 88. Per the standing convention they are characterized in order, not translated line by line; each sūtra the pages cite is kept in three layers with its number as read. Sūtra-numbers in small Kannada numerals are marked [?]. Nothing in them changes the sense of the Rik as given on p. 89.

original pp. 92–93

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.1 (Kannada) — characterized

p. 92 — "surūpakṛtnum" and the beginning of "ūtaye." - "Surūpa" — "rūpa" is formed from the root "rūp" (or "rūpa") with the affix "pa" that is added after the seven roots listed in the Uṇādi-sūtra, "…(ṛ?)-śilp-śaṣp-bāp-rūp-parṣ… (उ. सू. ३-३४ [?] and context, as printed, read with doubt)," and, by nipātana, the lengthening of the vowel gives "rūpa." Explained as "rūpyate (praśasyate) iti rūpam": that which is praised by people. "Śobhanaṃ rūpaṃ yasya tat" — a bahuvrīhi compound — "surūpam." Then the genitive tatpuruṣa "surūpasya kṛtnuḥ." - "Kṛtnu" — "karotīti kṛtnuḥ": the affix "knu" after "kṛ" and "han" (कृहनिभ्यां क्नुः, उ. सू. ३-३० [?]); "knu" being "k"-marked, there is no guṇa; "han" is stated in the sūtra because the "t" of the affix is added (a Vedic feature). - Accent of the compound. After the "su" the bahuvrīhi would by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. ६-२-१) retain the first member's accent; but नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) makes the last member's last syllable acute in a bahuvrīhi after "nañ" or "su"; so "surūpa" is end-acute. In "kṛtnu" the affix's accent is the acute, per कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् [as read]; with "surūpakṛtnu" as a genitive tatpuruṣa, समासस्य (पा. ६-१-२२३) makes the compound end-acute. The second-case singular ending "am" must be added after "surūpakṛtnu"; by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (पा. ३-१-४) the ending "am" is unaccented. By अमिपूर्वः (पा. ६-१-१०७) the "am" combines in the "pūrvarūpa" with the "u," and by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. ८-२-५) the single substitute is acute. - "Ūtaye" — ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च (पा. ३-३-९७) with the word मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः (पा. ३-३-९६) — the "udātta" of the preceding sūtra being carried over — these words ending in the affix "ktin" are formed irregularly (nipātana) and are end-acute: "ūti" is end-acute. The root "av" (to protect) takes "ktin" by ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्च (पा. ६-४-२०) with "ūṭ" replacing "av," giving "ūti"; the accents of the root and of the affix would conflict, and the nipātana's acute on the "i" overrides. "Ū" is unaccented by the "śeṣa-anudātta" rule. …

p. 93 — "ūtaye" concluded; "sudughām," "goduhe," "juhūmasi." - "Ūti" + the dative ending "ṅe": the "ṅī"/"jhi" affixes; since "ūti" is a word ending in short "i" and not "nadī"-labelled, by घेर्ङिति (पा. ७-३-१११) the guṇa is substituted — "ūte" + "e" → by एचोऽयवायावः "ūtaye." The "ṅe" ending is unaccented as "sup"; the accent of the "i" of "ūti" is the "nipātana" acute, and the "ay" substitute is acute as the substitute of an acute; by उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः (पा. ८-४-६६) the following unaccented syllable becomes svarita. Thus "ūtaye": first syllable unaccented, second acute, third svarita. - "Sudughām" — "suṣṭhu dugdhe iti sudughā" ("she who yields milk well"): the root "duh prapūraṇe" (to fill, to milk) takes "kap" when "su" is an upapada — दुहः कब्घश्च (duhaḥ kab ghaś ca, पा. ३-२-७० [?]) — and the "h" of "duh" becomes "gh"; the "a" of "kap" being "p"-marked, there is no guṇa, and by अनुदात्तोपदेश… the root's accent remains; धातोः (पा. ६-१-१६२) gives the root's last vowel — the "u" of "dugh" — the acute. With "su" the compound is a "gati-kāraka-upapada" compound, so by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९) the original accent remains; the feminine "ṭāp"; the second-case singular "sudughām"; and with "iva," by इवेन समासो विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च (the vārttika as on p. 58) the compound keeps the earlier accent. - "Goduhe" — "gāṃ dogdhīti godhuk": सत्सूद्विषद्रुहदुहयुजविदभिदच्छिदजिनीराजामुपसर्गेऽपि क्विप् (पा. ३-२-६१) — after "pad" (to go), "sad," "dviṣ," "druh," "duh," "yuj," "vid," "bhid," "chid," "ji," "nī," "rāj" — "kvip" occurs whether or not an upasarga precedes, when a subanta stands as upapada; the "kvip" is applied to "duh" with "go" as upapada; in the compound, the kṛt-ending second member's accent is kept (कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम्). - "Juhūmasi" — the root "hve" (ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च, "to challenge, to call"), of the third (juhotyādi) class; "laṭ" first-person plural "mas"; the "śap" that follows is elided as "ślu" by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. २-४-७३) and जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः (पा. २-४-७५); doubling of the root by श्लौ (पा. ६-१-१०); the doubled pair is called "abhyasta" by उभे अभ्यस्तम् (पा. ६-१-५) … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept; accent-marks not reproduced; see the note at Rik 3.5.

original p. 94

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.1 concluded; Sūkta 4, Second Mantra: Saṃhitā and Pada text

Continuing "juhūmasi" from p. 93: …the root "hve," being the cause, takes "samprasāraṇa" (ह्वेञ् … संप्रसारणम्): "hu + e + mas" → "hu + mas"-type form by संप्रसारणाच्च (पा. ६-१-१०८) — when "samprasāraṇa" is followed by an "ac," the single "pūrvarūpa" replaces both — and then by हलः (पा. ६-४-२, as printed) the stem-final before a consonant is lengthened ("hū"); the doubling by श्लौ (पा. ६-१-१०); the reduplicative syllable is shortened by ह्रस्वः (पा. ७-४-५९) — "hu-hū-mas"; for the "h" of the reduplicative syllable the "c"-class substitute by कुहोश्चुः (kuhoś cuḥ, पा. ७-४-६२) → "ju"; then the "ru/ghosa" substitutions अभ्यासे चर्च (पा. ८-४-५४); "mas" takes the augment "i" by इदन्तो मसिः (पा. ७-१-४६) → "juhūmasi." By the accent of the affix the "ma" is acute.

"Dyavidyavi" — the root "dyut dīptau" (to shine); after it the Uṇādi affix "do" (उणादयो बहुलम्, पा. ३-३-१); because of the word "bahulam" the affix "do" comes. Bhaṭṭoji-dīkṣita, in the Kaumudī, in explaining the Uṇādi-sūtra गमेर्डोः [as printed; "dyoḥ"?] (उ. सू. ३-३१ [?]), says that from the "bāhulaka" rule "dyau" too arises; Bhojadeva holds that "do" is the affix after the root "dyu abhigamane" ("to approach"). "Dyoḥ" is end-acute, by the Uṇādi accent rule (फिषः etc. as printed, "ṭi-sū. 1" [?]). In the seventh case singular, with the doubling by नित्यवीप्सयोः (पा. ८-१-४), the word is "dyavi-dyavi"; of it, the second part is called "āmreḍita" by परमाम्रेडितम् (पा. ८-१-२), and, by अनुदात्तं च (पा. ८-१-३), the "āmreḍita" is unaccented — so the second "dyavi" is unaccented. ॥१॥ Accent-marks not reproduced.

Sūkta 4, The Second Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उप नः सवना गहि सोमस्य सोमपाः पिब । गोदा इद्रेवतो मदः ॥२॥

upa naḥ savanā gahi somasya somapāḥ piba | godā id revato madaḥ ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; [?] where unclear. The sense-lines are transcribed in full; the grammar is characterized, with its sūtras.

उप । नः । सवना । आ । गहि । सोमस्य । सोमऽपाः । पिब । गोऽदाः । इत् । रेवतः । मदः ॥२॥

original p. 95

Rik 4.2: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे सोमपाः सोमस्य पातरिन्द्र सोमं पातुं नोऽस्मदीयानि सवना सवनानि त्रीणि प्रत्युप समीप आगहि । आगच्छ । आगत्य च सोमस्य सोमं पिब । रेवतो धनवतस्तव मदो हर्षो गोदा इद्गोप्रद एव । त्वयि हृष्टे सत्यस्माभिर्गावो लभ्यन्त इत्यर्थः ॥ he somapāḥ somasya pātar indra somaṃ pātuṃ no 'smadīyāni savanā savanāni trīṇi praty upa samīpa āgahi | āgaccha | āgatya ca somasya somaṃ piba | revato dhanavatas tava mado harṣo godā id gopradā eva | tvayi hṛṣṭe saty asmābhir gāvo labhyanta ity arthaḥ ||

Translation: "O 'somapāḥ' — O drinker of Soma, Indra! In order to drink the Soma, come near, 'upa āgahi' — come — 'nah savanā' — to our three pressings (savanas). And having come, drink the Soma ('somasya piba' = 'somam piba'). 'Revataḥ' — of you, the wealthy; the 'madaḥ' — the exhilaration — is 'godā id' — a giver of cows indeed: that is, when you are delighted, we obtain cows."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya characterized; the print is somewhat garbled in the middle and only what was read clearly is given: "Upa" — a particle, hence first-syllable acute. "Savanā" — "sūyate somaḥ eṣu iti savanāni": "lyuṭ" in the locative-of-place sense (ल्युट्…, पा. ३-३-११७); the ending "śas/jas" replaced by "ḍā" (सुपो डादेशः, as printed) and the loss of "ṭi"; the accent on the vowel before the affix in the "ṇit/ñit"-marked affix. "Gahi" — from "gam" with the "śap" dropped by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. २-४-७३); the root's "m" is dropped by अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७); the "hi" ending by आतो हेः (पा. ६-४-१०५ [?]) — the print then discusses why the loss of "m" is to be treated as "asiddha" and the resulting accent, which I do not reproduce. "Somapāḥ" — vocative; the आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. ६-१-१९८) loss of accent; "piba" has its accent lost by तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) with reference to the preceding word, though that word is not itself an existent "pada"-unit by "parāṅgavadbhāva" — the print debates this (the "asāmarthya" argument) and concludes the "nighāta" does apply. "Godāḥ" — "gāṃ dadātīti godāḥ": "kvip" (क्विप् च, पा. ३-२-७६) in the sense of the doer, and the root-final "ā" becomes "i" by आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च (पा. ३-२-७४) [as printed "…vanip"]; "vic" … and "ghu-mā-sthā-…" (घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि, पा. ६-४-६६) — the "ī"-substitution of the final "ā" — would be expected, but "godāḥ" is irregular by Vedic usage. "Revān" — "rayir dhanam asyāstīti": "matup" after "rayi" (रयेर्मतौ बहुलं छन्दसि, पा. ६-१-३७ [?]), the samprasāraṇa, the guṇa; the "matup" is acute by ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (पा. ६-१-१७६); by छन्दसीरः (पा. ८-२-१५) the "va." "Madaḥ" — "mad" (to be glad) with "ap" (मदोऽनुपसर्गे, पा. ३-३-६७ [?]); "p"-marked and thus unaccented in the affix; the root-accent remains.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सोमपाः (somapāḥ) — O Indra, who drink the Soma | नः (naḥ) — our | सवना (savanā) — to the morning, midday and third pressings in the sacrifice (or: to the sacrifices that we perform) | उपागहि (upāgahi) — be one who comes near (coming here) | सोमस्य (somasya) — the Soma-juice | पिब (piba) — drink | रेवतः (revataḥ) — (of you) who are endowed with riches, lordship and the like | मदः (madaḥ) — the joy (that arises from drinking the Soma) | गोदाः (godāḥ) — gives (us) cows.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! You are a drinker of Soma. Therefore, coming to the three pressings of the sacrifice that we are now performing — the morning, the midday and the third — drink the Soma that we have prepared. When you drink it you are made glad; and you, who are endowed with lordship, will be the giver to us of cows (wealth in cows). Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." English as printed. The count of "-dāḥ" words is in small Kannada numerals, read as "1?" and marked [?].

original p. 96

Rik 4.2: English rendering; Special topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"O Soma-drinker, come hither to our Sacrifices and Partake of the Soma; you being rich the satisfaction you get from drinking Soma is verily the cause of the gift of cattle."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

उप आ गहि (upa ā gahi) — "Upa" — near: near the sacrifice we are performing; "ā gahi" — "come," be one who comes.

सवना (savanā) — "sūyate somaḥ eṣu iti savanāni" ("those in which Soma is pressed") — the name "savana" is given to the rite (the sacrifice) that extracts the Soma-juice. "Savana" may be explained as the three pressings beginning with the morning pressing, or as the sacrifice that has the rite of pressing. In either way the chief sense is one.

गोदाः (godāḥ) — "gāṃ dadātīti godāḥ; goprade" — one who gives cows, or wealth in cattle. Similarly "somaṃ pibatīti somapāḥ." In the Ṛgveda there are [1?] examples of words ending in the affix "dāḥ" the number is not certain:

अश्वदाः । आत्मदाः । ओजोदाः । गोदाः । द्रविणोदाः । धनदाः । बलदाः । भूरिदाः । वस्त्रदाः । वाजदाः । वासोदाः । सहोदाः । सहस्रदाः । सुदाः । स्वस्तिदाः । हिरण्यदाः । भूरिदाः ॥ aśvadāḥ | ātmadāḥ | ojodāḥ | godāḥ | draviṇodāḥ | dhanadāḥ | baladāḥ | bhūridāḥ | vastradāḥ | vājadāḥ | vāsodāḥ | sahodāḥ | sahasradāḥ | sudāḥ | svastidāḥ | hiraṇyadāḥ | bhūridāḥ || (Translation of the word-list, mine: "giver of horses; giver of self; giver of vigour; giver of cows; giver of wealth; giver of riches; giver of strength; giver of plenty; giver of garments; giver of prizes; giver of clothing; giver of might; giver of a thousand; good giver; giver of well-being; giver of gold; giver of plenty." The word "bhūridāḥ" is printed twice in the list, as I read it; I record this without correction.)

इत् (it) — "eva" (indeed). Example: "indraḥ godā id" — "Indra is indeed a giver of cows"; the sentence "indro godā it" means that Indra is a giver of cows only. The word "it" is used in the sense of emphasis (avadhāraṇa).

रेवतः (revataḥ) — "rayir dhanam asyāstīti revān, tasya revataḥ" — one who has wealth: "of the wealthy (Indra)."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized "Upa" — a particle (nipāta), hence, by निपाता आद्युदात्ताः (Phiṭ-sūtra [number as printed, "80" ?]) first-syllable acute. "Savanā" — "sūyate somaḥ eṣv iti savanāni": करणाधिकरणयोश्च (karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca, पा. ३-३-११७) — "lyuṭ" is added to a root in the sense of instrument or locus; to "ṣuñ" (abhiṣave) comes "lyuṭ," "su + yu"; धात्वादेः षः सः (dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ, पा. ६-१-६४) — the initial "ṣ" of the root becomes "s" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Pure grammar in Kannada prose, the rendering of the Sanskrit of p. 95; characterized, with sūtras kept; numbers as read, [?] where uncertain.

original p. 97

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.2 — characterized

Continuing "savanā": …युवोरनाकौ (yuvor anākau, पा. ७-१-१) turns "yu" into "ana": "su + ana," then the guṇa and "av" substitutions → "savana." For the second-case plural ending, सुपां सुलुक्… (supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇāccheyāḍādyāyājālaḥ, पा. ७-१-३९) — the "ḍā" substitute — "savana + ā"; the "na" and the following "a" (टेः, पा. ६-४-१४३): the "ṭi" of "savana" is elided before "ḍit" → "savanā." By लिति (liti, पा. ६-१-१९३) the vowel before the "l"-marked affix is acute.

"Gahi" — the root "gam gatau," in the imperative (loṭ) second-person singular, the ending "sip" → "gam + si"; "śap" (कर्तरि शप्, पा. ३-१-६८), which is elided here by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. २-४-७३); सेर्ह्यपिच्च (ser hy apic ca, पा. ३-४-८७) — "hi" replaces "si," and it is not "p"-marked — so "hi" is "ṅit"-like and the sārvadhātuka सार्वधातुकमपित् (पा. १-२-४) is "ṅit," whence अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७) drops the "m": "ga + hi." Then अतो हेः (ato heḥ, पा. ६-४-१०५) would drop the "hi" after an "a"-ending stem; but the rule असिद्धवदत्राभात् (asiddhavad atrābhāt, पा. ६-४-२२) makes the "m"-elision "asiddha" with respect to it, so that "hi" is not elided — the print argues this at length with the paribhāṣā about "samānāśraya" rules, and concludes that "hi" is retained: "gahi."

"Somapāḥ" — a vocative; by आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. ६-१-१९८) it is first-syllable acute. The following "piba" is unaccented by तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८). The preceding word "somasya" is not a vocative; the text debates whether the "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (पा. ८-१-७२) and "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (पा. २-१-२) rules apply between "somapāḥ" and "somasya," and concludes that, because the two words lack a mutual syntactic connection ("asāmarthya"), "parāṅgavad-bhāva" does not occur, and "somasya" is not treated as non-existent.

"Godāḥ" — "gāṃ dadāti iti godāḥ": the root "ḍudāñ dāne" (to give), ending in "ā"; आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः would give "ka," but "kvip" (क्विप् च, पा. ३-२-७६) is the general rule; since the Veda has the specific rule आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च (पा. ३-२-७४), "manin, kvanip, vanip" may come after a root ending in "ā" when a subanta or an upasarga stands as upapada; from the "ca" in that sūtra, "vic" also comes — and so on. The page ends in the middle of this argument about which affix applies to "godāḥ"; it continues on the next page. Page headers: p. 98 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4"; p. 99 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." These two pages are an advanced scholastic grammatical debate in Kannada prose about whether the "ī"-substitution of घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि (ghu-mā-sthā-gā-pā-jahāti-sāṃ hali, पा. ६-४-६६) can apply to "godāḥ" (the root "dā" with "kvip"). They have no bearing on the sense of the Rik, already given on pp. 95–96, and per the standing convention the argument is characterized in outline rather than transcribe it line by line, keeping the sūtras the pages name. Numbers as read; [?] where uncertain.

original pp. 98–99

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.2 (continued): the "godāḥ" / "īt" debate; "revataḥ"

The question. The "ghu" labelled roots (the roots "dā" and "dhā") take "ī" before an "ārdhadhātuka" affix that begins with a consonant ("hali") and is "k"- or "ṅ"-marked (ईत्वं हलि…). With "kvip," however, the whole affix is elided (वेरपृक्तस्य, पा. ६-१-६७), and "godāḥ" shows no "ī." The page-98 argument asks whether "kvip" can be regarded as an affix beginning with a consonant ("halādi") so as to call for "ī," and answers that it cannot, since it is entirely elided; yet, because of the "pratyaya-lakṣaṇa" principle (प्रत्ययलोपे प्रत्ययलक्षणम्, पा. १-१-६२ — "when an affix is elided, the operation that depends on the affix still applies"), the objector argues "ī" should still come. Two views are put: that this sūtra is vidhāyaka (enabling) or niyāmaka (restricting). The reply draws on the principle वर्णाश्रये नास्ति प्रत्ययलक्षणम् (varṇāśraye nāsti pratyaya-lakṣaṇam — "where the operation depends on a letter, there is no 'pratyaya-lakṣaṇa'"). Examples are taken from "tṛṇahim" (तृणह इम्, पा. ७-३-९२ [?]) and "gaveḥitam," and the page notes that when the chief ground of an operation is a letter (varṇa), the prohibition applies; when the chief ground is the affix itself, "pratyaya-lakṣaṇa" applies.

The Mahābhāṣya line (p. 99). The Mahābhāṣya-kāra's phrase ईर्ध्यायतेर्दधातेर्वा [as printed, "dhīrghyāyater dādhāter vā"; read with doubt] is discussed: if "kvip" were added after "dhā," the "ī" of "ghumāsthā" would need to arise; "hali" would then be read as "an-aji" (not "ajādi"), and the reply says that the rule for "ī" requires a "k/ṅ"-marked or "ārdhadhātuka" affix that does not begin with a vowel; in "godāḥ" the "kvip" is "ajādi," since it is elided; therefore "ī" does not arise, and "vic" is taken instead (the "ca" of the sūtra आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च, पा. ३-२-७४, brings in "vic"). A parallel is "saṃśasthā" (अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते, "…aṃbāgo-bhū-" — the sūtra as printed is garbled), where, if "kvip" were assumed, "ī" would again be required, and so "vic" is again assumed. Vārttikas of Kātyāyana (ईत्वे ह्वयतिप्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः [as I read it]) and the Padamañjarī are cited in support. The conclusion: in "godāḥ" the affix is "vic" (not "kvip") and no "ī" results. The debate is closed with a remark on the "asiddha"/"samprasāraṇa" rules, and on "pratyayāpratyaya-sādhāraṇa" operations (illustrated by सोर्मनसी अलोमोषसी, पा. ६-२-१०२ [?], with "sudṛṣat," "śobhanāḥ dṛṣadaḥ yasya prāsādasya"), which I do not reproduce.

"Revataḥ" p. 99, end — "rayiḥ asya asti iti revān": "matup" after "rayi" (तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप्, पा. ५-२-९४); the "m" becomes "v" by छन्दसीरः (पा. ८-२-१५), and by रयेर्मतौ बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. ६-१-३७ [?]) the "samprasāraṇa" of "y" (to "i") is variably made in the Veda: "rayi + vat" → "revat" (the "ay" becoming "e" by guṇa: आद्गुणः, पा. ६-१-८७, after the "pūrvarūpa" of संप्रसारणाच्च, पा. ६-१-१०८); the nominative singular "revān"; the "matup" is acute by ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (पा. ६-१-१७६) (the print says "the acute when the preceding short vowel has the udātta") …

original p. 100

Rik 4.2 grammar concluded; Sūkta 4, Third Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

Continuing "revataḥ" from p. 99: …the "matup" is acute as following a word-final short vowel or the augment "nuṭ" (ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप्, पा. ६-१-१७६). "Madaḥ" — "mad" (to be glad) with "ap" (मदोऽनुपसर्गे, पा. ३-३-६७ [?]): when a subanta (not an upasarga) stands as upapada before the root "mad," "ap" comes; being "p"-marked it is unaccented. ॥२॥

Sūkta 4, The Third Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अथा ते अन्तमानां विद्याम सुमतीनाम् । मा नो अति ख्य आ गहि ॥३॥

athā te antamānāṃ vidyāma sumatīnām | mā no ati khya ā gahi ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अथ । ते । अन्तमानाम् । विद्याम । सुऽमतीनाम् । मा । नः । अति । ख्यः । आ । गहि ॥३॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अथ सोमपानानन्तरं हे इन्द्र ते तवान्तमानामन्तिकतमानामतिशयेन समीपवर्तिनां सुमतीनां शोभनमतियुक्तानां शोभनप्रज्ञानां पुरुषाणां मध्ये स्थित्वा विद्याम । वयं त्वां जानीयाम । यद्वा । सुमतीनां शोभनबुद्धीनां कर्मानुष्ठानविषयाणां लाभार्थमित्यध्याहारः । बुद्धिलाभाय त्वां स्मरेमेत्यर्थः । त्वमपि नोऽस्मानतिक्रम्यान्येषां त्वत्स्वरूपं मा प्रकथय । किंतु त्वा गह्यस्मानेवागच्छ । atha somapānānantaraṃ he indra te tavāntamānām antikatamānām atiśayena samīpa-vartināṃ sumatīnāṃ śobhana-mati-yuktānāṃ śobhana-prajñānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ madhye sthitvā vidyāma | vayaṃ tvāṃ jānīyāma | yadvā | sumatīnāṃ śobhana-buddhīnāṃ karmānuṣṭhāna-viṣayāṇāṃ lābhārtham ity adhyāhāraḥ | buddhi-lābhāya tvāṃ smarema ity arthaḥ | tvam api no 'smān atikramyānyeṣāṃ tvat-svarūpaṃ mā prakathaya | kiṃ tu tvā [print; "tvam"?] gahy asmān evāgaccha |

Translation: "'Atha' — after the drinking of the Soma — 'O Indra, te' — of you; 'antamānām' — of those nearest, those who stand exceedingly close; 'sumatīnām' — of men of good understanding, of good wisdom — standing in the midst of them, 'vidyāma' — we would know you. Or: 'sumatīnām' — 'of good understanding' — the supplied sense is 'for the obtaining of understanding for those engaged in the performance of rites'; that is, 'we would remember you for the gaining of understanding.' And you, passing us over, do not declare your own form to others; but come to us ('ā gahi')." The print's "tvā gahy" is read as the sentence "kiṃ tu … gahi — come to us alone"; the second word of the clause is slightly unclear, and it is given as printed with the sense the Kannada gives.

अथेति निपात आद्युदात्तः । निपातस्य चेति दीर्घत्वम् । अन्तमानाम् । अतिशयेनान्तिका इत्यतिशायने तमप् । पा. ५-३-५५ । तमो तादेशश्च । पा. ६-४-१५४-५ [?] । इति तादिलोपः । अन्तोऽस्यास्तीत्यन्तिकः समीपः । अत इनिठनाविति ठन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । दूरोत्कर्षस्य ह्यवसानं नास्ति । सामीप्योत्कर्षस्य पुनर्यो यस्य समीपः स एव तस्यान्त इत्यन्तवत्त्वात्सामीप्यमन्तिकमुच्यते । विद्याम । वेत्तेर्लिङ् । यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च । पा. ३-४-१०३ । इति यासुडुदात्तः । पादादित्वात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति न निघातः । सुमतीनाम् । मतिशब्दे क्तिन्नन्तेऽपि मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः । पा. ३-३-९६ । athety nipāta ādyudāttaḥ | nipātasya ceti dīrghatvam | antamānām | atiśayenāntikā ity atiśāyane tamap | pā. 5-3-55 | tamo tādeśaś ca | pā. 6-4-154-5 [?] | iti tādi-lopaḥ | anto 'syāstīty antikaḥ samīpaḥ | ata inithanāv iti ṭhan | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | dūrotkarṣasya hy avasānaṃ nāsti | sāmīpyotkarṣasya punar yo yasya samīpaḥ sa eva tasyānta ity antavattvāt sāmīpyam antikam ucyate | vidyāma | vetter liṅ | yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca | pā. 3-4-103 | iti yāsuḍ udāttaḥ | pādāditvāt tiṅ atiṅa iti na nighātaḥ | sumatīnām | matiśabde ktinnante 'pi mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ | pā. 3-3-96 |

Translation (of the grammar, in outline, with its sūtras): "'Atha' — a particle, hence first-syllable acute; by निपातस्य च (पा. ६-३-१३६ [?]) the lengthening in 'athā.' 'Antamānām' — 'atiśayena antikāḥ': the affix 'tamap' in the sense of excess (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, पा. ५-३-५५), with the replacement of the 'ti'-portion (तिल्लोपः as printed, "tādi-lopaḥ") — 'anto 'syāstīti antikaḥ' — 'near'; 'ṭhan' by अत इनिठनौ (पा. ५-२-११५); being 'n'-marked (nit) it is first-syllable acute. For there is no limit (avasāna) to 'far-ness'; but in the excellence of 'near-ness' he who is near to someone is that someone's 'anta' (end); thus nearness is called 'antika' on account of the 'anta'-possessing. 'Vidyāma' — 'vid' in the optative (liṅ); 'yāsuṭ' is acute in the parasmaipada (यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च, पा. ३-४-१०३); since the word stands at the beginning of the pāda, 'tiṅ atiṅaḥ' does not cause nighāta. 'Sumatīnām' — 'mati' ending in 'ktin' is acute in the Veda by मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः (पा. ३-३-९६)…" Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept; English as printed.

original p. 101

Rik 4.3: grammar concluded; Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

Grammar, continuing "sumatīnām": …the "i" of "mati" is acute (the Sanskrit of p. 100 gives the rule); "śobhanā matir yeṣāṃ te sumatayaḥ" — a bahuvrīhi, in which the first member's natural accent is overridden by नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२), so the last syllable of the second member is acute; but where "śobhanā matayaḥ sumatayaḥ" is a karmadhāraya, there is an exception to the first-member accent in the case of an indeclinable prefix, and the second member has the natural accent given by कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् — it is end-acute. After "matup" (as short-final-acute), the genitive-plural "nām" of "sumati" is acute by नामन्यतरस्याम् (पा. ६-१-१७७).

"Khyaḥ" — the root "khyā prakathane" (to declare), the aorist (luṅ) second-person singular "sip" → "khyā + si"; च्लि लुङि (cli luṅi, पा. ३-१-४३) puts "cli" after the root in "luṅ"; सिचि … by अस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्योऽङ् (asyati-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ, पा. ३-१-५२) "aṅ" replaces "cli" after "as," "vac," "khyā"; आतो लोप इटि च (पा. ६-४-६४) elides the final "ā" before "aṅ" — "khya + a + s"; इतश्च (itaś ca, पा. ३-४-१०० [as printed]) elides the final "i" of parasmaipada endings (here of "sip," giving "s"); the "s" is changed to "ru" and visarga: ससजुषो रुः (पा. ८-२-६६) and खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः (पा. ८-३-१५) → "khyaḥ." After "mā," न माङ्योगे (na māṅ-yoge, पा. ६-४-७४) — the augment "aṭ" does not occur → "mā khyaḥ."

"Gahi" — from "gam"; the "śap" is elided by "bahulaṃ chandasi"; because "hi" replaces "si" (सेर्ह्यपिच्च, पा. ३-४-८७) it is not "p"-marked; so the "m" of the root is elided by अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७); the elision, being "asiddha" (असिद्धवदत्राभात्, पा. ६-४-२२), does not permit the "hi"-loss that अतो हेः (पा. ६-४-१०५) would otherwise require → "gahi."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अथ (atha) — after the drinking of the Soma | (हे इन्द्र) (he indra) — O Indra | वयम् (vayam) — we | ते (te) — your | अन्तमानाम् (antamānām) — of those who are exceedingly near | सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — of men of good understanding (of the discerning, or of the wise) — in their midst | विद्याम (vidyāma) — we know you (we remember you, or, for the sake of obtaining wisdom for the performance of rites, we remember you) | (त्वम् अपि) नः (naḥ) — us | अति (ati) — passing over (to others) | मा ख्यः (mā khyaḥ) — do not declare (your own form) | आ गहि (ā gahi) — be one who comes (to our side).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! After the drinking of the Soma, we, being near you, remember you for the sake of good understanding in the performance of good works, or for the gaining of excellent wisdom. You must come near us. Do not make your form known to others, and do not cause them to have good understanding.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"We recognize you in the midst of the right-minded who are nearest to you; come to us; do not reveal yourself to others."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In this Ṛk, apart from a few special words that are difficult, the ṛṣi's intention is not very clear, though the words are easy and commonly used. The Bhāṣyakāra and others have written the meaning, by using some supplied words (adhyāhāra), in such a way that it can be understood somewhat; but the sense is not quite … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." English as printed.

original p. 102

Special topics on Rik 4.3; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

…it does not fit well. To make clear the sense of the sentences "sumatīnāṃ vidyāma" and "mā no ati khyaḥ," still some more words are needed, and such words are not in the Ṛk. Whether it be because the loss (of words) is a Vedic licence (chandasi), or because the ṛṣi has left out some words that were necessary and chief, thinking that the intention in his own mind would be clear from the words in the Ṛk — it appears so. Hence the sense of this Ṛk and of the next two or three Ṛks remains unclear.

अथा (athā) — the letter "a" of "thā" [the syllable "tha"] of this word is lengthened in accord with Vedic usage. Such examples are needed in the Ṛgveda. For example: sacasva — sacasvā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-9), śrudhi — śrudhī (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-1 [?]), pṛccha — pṛcchā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-4-4), piba — pibā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1[?]4-10), and the like.

सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — The explanation of this word has already been given (see p. 81 [as printed]).

मा (mā) — a negative word of prohibition, "do not." This word is used especially in the Veda. अति (ati) — "beyond, besides, passing over" English as printed: "Beyond, besides &c.".

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Atha" — a nipāta, so first-syllable acute (निपाता आद्युदात्ताः); निपातस्य च (पा. ६-३-१३६ [?]) lengthens the vowel in mantra: "athā." "Antamānām" — "antaḥ asya asti" ("this has an end"), the etymology of "antika": by अत इनिठनौ (पा. ५-२-११५) "ini" or "ṭhan" after a stem ending in short "a"; with "ṭhan," ठस्येकः (ṭhasyekaḥ, पा. ७-३-५०) gives "ika": "anta + ika"; by यस्येति च (पा. ६-४-१४८) the "a" of the stem is elided → "antika." There is no limit to remoteness; but for the excellence of proximity, "that which is near to something has its 'end' there"; because it has an "anta" (limit), the word "antika" means "near." "Atiśayena antikāḥ" — to express excess, अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (पा. ५-३-५५) puts "tamap" after the stem in the sense of excess → "antika + tama"; तमो …: तिकतमः — by टेः / "ti-ka"-loss (as printed: तेस्तादेशश्च, पा. ६-४-१५४ वा. ९ [?]) the "tika" portion [as printed: "ti-ka"] is elided before "tamap"; the result is "antama." In the genitive plural, "antamānām." "Vidyāma" — from "vid jñāne" (to know) by liṅ; for the "liṅ" यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च (पा. ३-४-१०३) — in the parasmaipada the augment "yāsuṭ" comes, which is acute and "ṅit" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept; numbers as read.

original p. 103

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.3 concluded; end of the Seventh Varga

…"yāsuṭ" is acute; because the word stands at the beginning of the pāda, तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) does not bring nighāta. "Sumatīnām" — the word "mati" ends in "ktin," but in the Veda मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः (पा. ३-३-९६ [as printed]) makes the affix acute after the roots "vṛṣ" (to shower), "iṣ" (to wish), "duṣ-pac" (to cook), "man" (to think), "vid" (to be), "bhū," "vī" (and "rā" in "rādaḥ"); so after "man," "ktin" is added, and अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७) drops the nasal of "man" → "mati"; the "i" of "ktin" is acute by the preceding sūtra. "Śobhanā matiḥ yeṣāṃ te sumatayaḥ" — as a bahuvrīhi the first member's natural accent is overridden by नञ्सुभ्याम्; "śobhanāś ca tāḥ matayaḥ" — as a karmadhāraya the indeclinable-prefix accent is overridden by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९), and the second member is end-acute. When "matup" is not applied, the genitive-plural "nām" of "sumati" (short-final, end-acute stem) takes the acute by नामन्यतरस्याम् (पा. ६-१-१७७).

"Khyaḥ" — "khyā prakathane": in the aorist (luṅ), second-person singular "sip" — ख्या + सिप्; after the root in "luṅ," "cli" (च्लि लुङि, पा. ३-१-४३); "cli" is replaced by "aṅ" after the roots "as," "vac" and "khyā" (अस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्योऽङ्, पा. ३-१-५२); "ā" elided (आतो लोप इटि च, पा. ६-४-६४); the "i" of the ending "sip" elided (इतश्च, पा. ३-४-१००) — "khya + a + s"; "s" → "ru" → visarga (ससजुषो रुः, पा. ८-२-६६; रुत्वविसर्गौ) → "khyaḥ." After "mā," न माङ्योगे (पा. ६-४-७४): no "aṭ" (and, by the print, no "āṭ") augment, and the rule लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः (पा. ६-४-७१) which would give the "aḍ" augment does not apply.

"Gahi" — "gam gatau," imperative (loṭ) second-person singular "sip"; "śap" is elided by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. २-४-७३); सेर्ह्यपिच्च (पा. ३-४-८७) puts "hi" in the place of "sip," and the "sārvadhātuka" not being "p"-marked is "ṅit" (सार्वधातुकमपित्, पा. १-२-४) — by the root's "anudātta-upadeśa" the "m" is dropped (अनुदात्तोपदेश…, पा. ६-४-३७); since the "m"-loss is "asiddha" (असिद्धवदत्राभात्, पा. ६-४-२२), the "hi" does not lose its place by अतो हेः (पा. ६-४-१०५) → "gahi." ॥३॥

इल्लिगे ७ ನೇ ವರ್ಗವು ಮುಗಿದುದು — illige 7neya vargavu mugidudu — "Here the seventh varga is finished."

original p. 104

Sūkta 4, Fourth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pada-meanings (opening)

Sūkta 4, The Fourth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

परेहि विग्रमस्तृतमिन्द्रं पृच्छा विपश्चितम् । यस्ते सखिभ्य आ वरम् ॥४॥

parehi vigram astṛtam indraṃ pṛcchā vipaścitam | yas te sakhibhya ā varam ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading note: the Saṃhitā text reads "pṛcchā" with a long final vowel (a Vedic lengthening); the Pada text has "pṛccha." The word "vipaścitam" is divided in the Pada text as "vipaḥ-citam," as read from the printed sign.

परा । इहि । विग्रम् । अस्तृतम् । इन्द्रम् । पृच्छ । विपःऽचितम् । यः । ते । सखिऽभ्यः । आ । वरम् ॥४॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अत्र यजमानं प्रति होता ब्रूते । हे यजमान त्वमिन्द्रं परेहि । इन्द्रस्य समीपे गच्छ । गत्वा च विपश्चितं मेधाविनं होतारं मां पृच्छ । असौ होता सम्यक् स्तुतवान्न चेत्येवं प्रश्नं कुरु । य इन्द्रस्ते तव यजमानस्य सखिभ्य ऋत्विग्भ्यो वरं श्रेष्ठं धनपुत्रादिकमा समन्तात्प्रयच्छतीति शेषः । तादृशमिन्द्रमिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । पुनरपि कीदृशम् । विग्रं मेधाविनमस्तृतमहिंसितम् । विप्र इत्यादिषु चतुर्विंशतिसंख्याकेषु मेधाविनामसु विग्रो विपश्चिच्चेति पठितौ । विग्रं वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । अस्तृतम् । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । इन्द्रशब्द ऋजेन्द्राग्रेत्यादिना रन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सखिभ्यः । समाने ख्यः ... उ. ४-१३६ [?] । इति समान उपपदे ख्यातेरिन् । डिदित्यनुवृत्तेस्तस्य डित्त्वाट्टिलोपश्च । पा. ६-४-१४३ । तत्सन्नियोगेन यलोपः । उपपदस्योदात्तत्वम् । समानस्य छन्दस्यमूर्धप्रभृत्युदर्केषु । पा. ६-३-८४ । इति सभावः । अतः सखिशब्द आद्युदात्तः । व्रियत इति वरः । ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्च । पा. ३-३-५८ । इत्यप् । तस्य पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वर एव ॥ atra yajamānaṃ prati hotā brūte | he yajamāna tvam indraṃ parehi | indrasya samīpe gaccha | gatvā ca vipaścitaṃ medhāvinaṃ hotāraṃ māṃ pṛccha | asau hotā samyak stutavān na ceti evaṃ praśnaṃ kuru | ya indras te tava yajamānasya sakhibhya ṛtvigbhyo varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhana-putrādikam ā samantāt prayacchatīti śeṣaḥ | tādṛśam indram iti pūrvatrānvayaḥ | punar api kīdṛśam | vigraṃ medhāvinam astṛtam ahiṃsitam | vipra ity ādiṣu catur-viṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu medhāvi-nāmasu vigro vipaścic ceti paṭhitau | vigraṃ vṛṣādi-tvād ādyudāttaḥ | astṛtam | avyaya-pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | indra-śabda ṛjendrāgrety ādinā ran | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | sakhibhyaḥ | samāne khyaḥ … u. 4-136 [?] | iti samāna upapade khyāter in | ḍid ity anuvṛtter tasya ḍittvāṭ ṭilopaś ca | pā. 6-4-143 | tat-sanniyogena yalopaḥ | upapadasyodāttatvam | samānasya chandasy amūrdha-prabhṛty-udarkeṣu | pā. 6-3-84 | iti sabhāvaḥ | ataḥ sakhi-śabda ādyudāttaḥ | vriyata iti varaḥ | grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca | pā. 3-3-58 | ity ap | tasya pittvād dhātusvara eva ||

Translation: "Here the Hotṛ speaks to the sacrificer: 'O sacrificer, go to Indra ("parehi"): go into the presence of Indra; and having gone, ask me, the Hotṛ, 'vipaścitam' — the wise — "Has this Hotṛ praised properly or not?" — put the question thus. That Indra who gives 'varam' — the best, wealth, sons and the like — in full ('ā') to 'te sakhibhyaḥ' — to your friends, the priests (ṛtvijaḥ) of you the sacrificer' — such is the supplied sense. The construction 'such an Indra' connects with what went before. Of what sort again? 'Vigram' — wise; 'astṛtam' — unharmed. Among the twenty-four names for 'wise' beginning with 'vipra,' 'vigra' and 'vipaścit' are read." The Bhāṣya's reading "vipaścitam … pṛccha māṃ hotāram" makes the ṛtvij the one to be asked; It is given as printed.

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept): "Vigram" — first-syllable acute as belonging to the "vṛṣādi" class; "astṛtam" — the first-member accent (an indeclinable prefix) is retained; "Indra" — by the Uṇādi "ṛjrendrāgra-…" (as on p. 39) the affix "ran," "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute; "sakhibhyaḥ" — समाने ख्यः [the Uṇādi sūtra, number garbled: "4-136" ?], from "khyā" after "samāna" as upapada with "in," "ḍit," with elision of "ṭi" (टेः, पा. ६-४-१४३) and of "y"; the upapada's acute; the substitution "sa" for "samāna" by समानस्य छन्दस्यमूर्धप्रभृत्युदर्केषु (पा. ६-३-८४); hence "sakhi" is first-syllable acute. "Varam" — "vriyate iti varaḥ": "ap" by ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्च (पा. ३-३-५८); "p"-marked, so the root's accent remains.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

In this Ṛk the priest called the Hotṛ speaks, addressing the sacrificer —

(O sacrificer, you) विग्रम् (vigram) — the wise | इन्द्रम् परेहि (indram parehi) — go to Indra's side | (having gone) अस्तृतम् (astṛtam) — (about Indra) who is not struck by the harm of enemies | विपश्चितम् पृच्छ (vipaścitam pṛccha) — ask this wise one (whether the Hotṛ has praised you properly or not) | यः (yaḥ) — (the Indra who) | ते (te) — your | सखिभ्यः (sakhibhyaḥ) — to the friendly priests | वरम् (varam) — excellent wealth, sons and the like | आ (yacchati) — gives.
