Rik 4.4: Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Hotṛ speaks thus, addressing the sacrificer: O sacrificer! Go to the side of Indra, who is wise (intelligent) — and ask him whether this Hotṛ has praised you well. Because Indra is pleased with the hymns that the Hotṛ has chanted, he will favour you, and your friends the priests, with the best boons — wealth, sons and the like.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Go (worshipper) to the wise (and) uninjured Indra and ask him of the (fitness of the) learned (priest who recites his praise.) Indra will bestow the best of blessings to your friends (priests)."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

विग्रम्, विपश्चितम् (vigram, vipaścitam) — These words are read among the twenty-four words that indicate "intelligent" (Ni. 3-1[?]). For these words the sense is "buddhimān, medhāvī, vivekin" (one with understanding, intelligent, discerning). The word "vigra" is used in the Ṛgveda in only two places. In the present Ṛk, and also in the Ṛk

ता विग्रं धैथे जठरं पृणध्या आ यत्सद्म सभृतयः पृणन्ति ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-६८-२ [?]) tā vigraṃ dhaithe jaṭharaṃ pṛṇadhyā ā yat sadma sabhṛtayaḥ pṛṇanti || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-68-2 [?]) Gloss (mine; tentative; the print gives only this line): "You two keep the wise one, to fill the belly, when those who bring together fill the abode."

this word is used. Nowhere else. The word "vipaścit" is used in about 3[?] places in the Ṛgveda the number is not legible.

अस्तृतम् (astṛtam) — The negative form of the word "stṛta," formed from the root "stṛ"; "na stṛtam = astṛtam" — not struck down, "ahiṃsitam" ("unharmed").

सखिभ्यः (sakhibhyaḥ) — "To the friends" — that is, to the priests who are called the sacrificer's friends. On the point that the priests are the sacrificer's friends:

आ प्यायस्व सखीन्त्सन्या मेधयेत्याहर्त्विजो वा अस्य सखायस्तानेवाप्याययेति ॥ (तै. सं. ६-३-२ [?]) ā pyāyasva sakhīn tsanyā medhayety āhartvijo vā asya sakhāyas tān evāpyāyayeti || (tai. saṃ. 6-3-2 [?]) Translation (mine, following the Kannada gloss): "'Swell, bring your friends to prosperity with intelligence' — thus he says; the priests, indeed, are his (the sacrificer's) friends; he swells them indeed." — The Kannada adds: here "ṛtvijo vā asya sakhāyaḥ" says plainly that the priests are the sacrificer's friends.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Parā" — a nipāta, first-syllable acute by निपाता आद्युदात्ताः (Phiṭ-sūtra [number as printed "80" ?]); by the "śeṣa-anudātta" the last letter is unaccented. In the saṃhitā, the "ā" of "parā" combines, by guṇa-sandhi, with the unaccented "i" of "ihi," giving "e" as the single substitute; this single substitute, coming in place of unaccented vowels … Page headers: p. 106 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4"; p. 107 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." These two pages are pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose, the Kannada rendering of the grammar given in Sanskrit on p. 104, with a good deal of added scholastic debate. They do not bear on the sense of the Rik, which was given on pp. 104–105. Per the standing convention they are characterized in outline, not translated line by line; the sūtras the pages name are kept in three layers, numbers as read, [?] where uncertain. Several sentences in the middle of p. 106 and the foot of p. 107 are crowded in the print and are not reproduced.

original pp. 106–107

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.4 (Kannada) — characterized

p. 106 — "parā," "ihi," "vigram." - Continuing "parehi" from p. 105. The single substitute "e" replaces the pair of unaccented vowels, and is by स्थानिवदादेशोऽनल्विधौ (sthānivad ādeśo 'nal-vidhau, पा. १-१-५६) treated as the original, hence unaccented; since it comes after the acute "ra," it becomes svarita by उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः (पा. ८-४-६६). - "Ihi" — "iṇ gatau" (to go); in the imperative second-person singular "sip," सेर्ह्यपिच्च (पा. ३-४-८७) puts "hi" for "si"; the "śap" is elided as the root belongs to the "ad" class (अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः, पा. २-४-७२); since "hi" is not "p"-marked, the "sārvadhātuka" is "ṅit" (सार्वधातुकमपित्, पा. १-२-४); hence guṇa is barred by क्ङिति च (पा. १-१-५) and by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. ७-३-८४) → "ihi." Since "ihi" stands after "parā," which is not a tiṅanta, तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) makes it wholly unaccented. - "Vigram" — two analyses are weighed. (a) From "gṛ śabde" (to sound) with the upasarga "vi" and the affix "ḍa" by अन्येष्वपि दृश्यते (पा. ३-२-१०१) — "ḍa" after any root, since the sūtra says "dṛśyate" ("is seen") — with the "ṭi"-loss debated, and "ṛ" becoming "r" by yaṇ ("vi-gr-a"); the accent then follows the compound rule गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९), which would give an end-acute that is not the attested accent. (b) Therefore the word is entered in the "vṛṣādi" class (वृषादीनां च, पा. ६-१-२०३) and is first-syllable acute — "vigra," as in विचिर् पृथग्भावे (the root "vicir pṛthagbhāve") with the intensive/causal sense "viveka": "viśeṣeṇa gṛhṇāti" ("he takes in a special way") = "vigraḥ" (the wise, discerning). Different derivations are offered; the page concludes that either way the sense is "medhāvī."

p. 107 — "vigram" concluded; "astṛtam," "indra," "sakhibhyaḥ." - The Uṇādi affix "ran" is considered for "vigra" (ऋज्रेन्द्राग्रवज्रविप्र…, as on p. 39) — "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute; the second-case singular "am" (an "ap"-class ending) is joined with a pūrvarūpa by अमि पूर्वः (पा. ६-१-१०७). - "Astṛtam" — "na stṛtam"; by तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ… (पा. ६-२-२) — with an indeclinable first member the first member's own accent is retained. - "Indra" — by the Uṇādi list "ṛjrendrāgra-vajra-vipra-kubra-cubra-kṣura-khura-bhadrogra-bhera-bhela-śukra-śakla-gaurava-nvera-mālāḥ [?]" (उ. सू. २-२८ [as printed "3-1…"]) "ran" is added; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute; the last letter is unaccented by "śeṣānudātta"; in the saṃhitā it is svarita by उदात्तस्वरितपरस्य सन्नतरः (पा. १-२-४०) in the way already described. - "Sakhibhyaḥ" — समाने ख्य… (Uṇādi-sūtra: the print gives "ṭi-sū. 4-…"; I could not settle the number): after "khyā" with "samāna" as the upapada, the affix "iṇ"; "ḍit" and hence टेः (पा. ६-४-१४३) loss of "ṭi" (the vowel-end) and of "y" (the "ya"-loss); the upapada is acute; समानस्य छन्दस्यमूर्धप्रभृत्युदर्केषु (पा. ६-३-८४) substitutes "sa" for "samāna" (the first member, when the second begins with a non-"mūrdhan"-class word) → "sakhi," first-syllable acute. The Uṇādi-sūtra समानेख्यः सश्चोदात्तः [as printed] is also cited, with the remark that the grammarians of the Mādhava school hold that "sa" is substituted in the Veda by the rule "samānasya chandasi mūrdha…," and that in ordinary speech the word "sakhi" is established by Svaramañjarī-kāra and others by other rules. The page ends mid-sentence in this comparison, continuing on p. 108.

Rik 4.4 grammar concluded; Sūkta 4, Fifth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

Continuing "sakhibhyaḥ" from p. 107: …in the system of the Mādhava school the word "sakhi" is established only in the Veda (by the "samānasya chandasi…" rule). "Varam" — "vriyate iti varaḥ": ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्च (पा. ३-३-५८) — after "grah," "vṛ," "dṛ," "niścī [print: niści]" and "gam" the affix "ap" comes; "vṛ + a" takes guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. ७-३-८४) → "varaḥ"; "ap" is "p"-marked and so unaccented, "va" is acute by धातोः (पा. ६-१-१६२). ॥४॥

Sūkta 4, The Fifth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उत ब्रुवन्तु नो निदो निरन्यतश्चिदारत । दधाना इन्द्र इद्दुवः ॥५॥

uta bruvantu no nido nir anyatas cid ārata | dadhānā indra id duvaḥ ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading note: the Saṃhitā text reads "indra id duvaḥ"; the Pada text resolves it as "indre it duvaḥ." The printed Pada text shows "ā-rata" as one word.

उत । ब्रुवन्तु । नः । निदः । निः । अन्यतः । चित् । आरत । दधानाः । इन्द्रे । इत् । दुवः ॥५॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

नोऽस्माकं संबन्धिन ऋत्विज इति शेषः । ते ब्रुवन्तु । इन्द्रं स्तुवन्तु । उतमपि च हे निदो निन्दितारः पुरुषा निरारत । इतो देशान्निर्गच्छत । अन्यतश्चिदन्यस्मादपि देशान्निर्गच्छत । कीदृशा ऋत्विजः । इन्द्रे दुवः परिचर्यां दधानाः कुर्वाणाः । इच्छब्दोऽवधारणे । सर्वदा परिचर्यां कुर्वन्त एव तिष्ठन्तित्यर्थः । निन्दन्तीति निदः । णिदि कुत्सायाम् । क्विपि नुमभावश्छान्दसः । सुपोऽनुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरः । आमन्त्रितत्वेऽपि वाक्यान्तरस्थेन स्ववाक्यगतपदादत्स्वरत्वान्न निघात इत्याद्युदात्तत्वमेव । अन्यतः । लिति प्रत्ययोत्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं चिदित्यपिकबर्थे । तेन न केवलमितः । इतो निर्गत्यान्यतोऽपि निर्गच्छतेति गम्यते । स एष धात्वर्थयोः संबन्ध आरतेति लुजा द्योत्यते । स हि धातुसंबन्धाधिकारे विधीयते । आरत । अर्तेश्छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति लोडर्थे लुङ् । मध्यमबहुवचनस्य तादेशः । सर्तिशास्त्यर्तिभ्यश्च । पा. ३-१-५६ । इति च्लेरङादेशः । ऋदृशोऽङि गुणः । पा. ७-४-१६ । इति गुणः । आडागमः । दधानाः । शानचश्चित्त्वात्तत्प्राप्तमन्तोदात्तं बाधित्वा परत्वादभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । दुवः । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तः ॥५॥ no 'smākaṃ sambandhina ṛtvija iti śeṣaḥ | te bruvantu | indraṃ stuvantu | utamapi ca he nido nindi-tāraḥ puruṣā nir ārata | ito deśān nirgacchata | anyataś cid anyasmād api deśān nirgacchata | kīdṛśā ṛtvijaḥ | indre duvaḥ paricaryāṃ dadhānāḥ kurvāṇāḥ | ic chabdo 'vadhāraṇe | sarvadā paricaryāṃ kurvanta eva tiṣṭhantity arthaḥ | nindantīti nidaḥ | ṇidi kutsāyām | kvipi numa-bhāvaś chāndasaḥ | supo 'nudāttatvād dhātusvaraḥ | āmantritatve 'pi vākyāntarasthena sva-vākya-gata-padād-at-svaratvān na nighāta ity ādyudāttatvam eva | anyataḥ | liti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvaṃ cid ity apika-barthe | tena na kevalam itaḥ | ito nirgatyānyato 'pi nirgacchateti gamyate | sa eṣa dhātvarthayoḥ sambandha āratety luñā dyotyate | sa hi dhātu-sambandhādhikāre vidhīyate | ārata | arter chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭa iti loḍarthe luṅ | madhyama-bahuvacanasya tādeśaḥ | sarti-śāsty-arti-bhyaś ca | pā. 3-1-56 | iti cler aṅādeśaḥ | ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ | pā. 7-4-16 | iti guṇaḥ | āḍāgamaḥ | dadhānāḥ | śānacaś cittvāt tat-prāptam antodāttaṃ bādhitvā paratvād abhyastānām ādir ity ādyudāttatvam | duvaḥ | nab-viṣayasyānisantasyety ādyudāttaḥ ||5||

Translation: "'Naḥ' — the supplied sense is 'our priests, those belonging to us.' Let them speak, let them praise Indra. And, O 'nidaḥ' — O revilers, men who blame — 'nirārata' — go out from here, from this place; 'anyataś cit' — go out from any other place as well. What kind of priests? 'Duvaḥ dadhānāḥ' — those who perform service ('paricaryā') in Indra; 'it' is in the sense of emphasis: the sense is 'they remain doing service at all times.' 'Nidaḥ' — 'nindantīti nidaḥ' — those who blame; the root 'ṇidi kutsāyām' (to blame); in the 'kvip' formation the absence of the 'num' augment is Vedic; the accent is that of the root since the case-ending is unaccented; though a vocative, since it stands in a different sentence from the preceding word, there is no nighāta (loss of accent), and so it is first-syllable acute indeed. 'Anyataḥ' — the part before the affix is acute; 'cit' has the sense of 'api' (also): not only from here, but from elsewhere too — 'having gone out from here, go out from other places also' is understood. This connection of the senses of the roots is indicated by the 'luṅ' in 'ārata.' 'Ārata' — the root 'ṛ' in the Veda takes 'luṅ' in the sense of the imperative (छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः, पा. ३-४-६); the second-person plural ending is replaced by 'ta'; the 'cli' is replaced by 'aṅ' (सर्त्तिशास्त्यर्त्तिभ्यश्च, पा. ३-१-५६); guṇa by ऋदृशोऽङि गुणः (पा. ७-४-१६); the augment 'āṭ.' 'Dadhānāḥ' — because 'śānac' is 'c'-marked, the end-acute that this would give is set aside, and, by the later rule अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. ६-१-१८९), the first syllable is acute. 'Duvaḥ' — first-syllable acute by नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (a Phiṭ-sūtra, as on p. 39). ॥५॥" Reading notes: (i) in the second sentence of the Bhāṣya the print has "utamapi ca"; the sense is "uta api ca," as the Rik itself reads "uta"; The print is transcribed as it stands. (ii) "ṇidi kutsāyām" is printed with the root-initial "ṇ," as in the dhātupāṭha. (iii) The reference "pā. 7-4-16" is printed "7-4-16," and it is given so, though it has not been verified. original p. 109

Rik 4.5: Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रे इत् (indre it) — in Indra alone (only in Indra) | दुवः (duvaḥ) — service (that is, worship) | दधानाः (dadhānāḥ) — those who make | नः (naḥ) — our (priests) | ब्रुवन्तु (bruvantu) — let them praise (Indra) | उत (uta) — and | निदः (nidaḥ) — men who blame (Indra) | अन्यतश्चित् (anyataś cit) — from here, and from other places too | निरारत (nirārata) — go out.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Let our priests (and sons and other kinsmen), who are devoted to the service of Indra, praise Indra; and let the men who blame Indra go out from here and from other places as well.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Let our (priests and relatives) engaged in the service of Indra, sing his praises. O revilers, depart from (here and) every other place."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Other commentators, and Western scholars too, have explained the meaning of this Ṛk in various ways English as printed:

  1. Wilson — "Let our ministers earnestly performing his worship exclaim, — depart, ye revilers from hence and every other place (where he is adored)."

  2. Dr. Sitanath — "Let our revilers say — you have estranged yourself from all other (gods) because of your having preference of service only for Indra."

  3. Vedarthayatna — "Whether the revilers may say to us that we might indeed be lost to all other gods by serving Indra alone."

नः (naḥ) — The Bhāṣyakāra explains the word "naḥ" as "our" ("belonging to us, our priests who share in our sacrifice"). Skandasvāmī says "priests, and sons and others." But, rather than supplying the words "priests" or "sons and others," to explain "naḥ" by joining it with the word "nidaḥ" would be more fitting … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.

original p. 110

Special topics on Rik 4.5 (continued); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins

Continuing "naḥ" from p. 109: …to explain "naḥ" together with "nidaḥ" would be more fitting; that is, "naḥ nidaḥ" — "our revilers, those who revile us." When it is explained thus, it is not necessary to supply a sense such as "let them praise Indra" for the verb "bruvantu"; rather, the sentence "uta bruvantu no nidaḥ" gets the sense "let the revilers of us say (what they will)."

निदः (nidaḥ) — "ṇidi kutsāyām" (to blame): "nindantīti nidaḥ" — since they are those who blame, they are called "nidaḥ."

अन्यतः (anyataḥ) — In this Ṛk the word is only "anyataḥ," "from elsewhere"; therefore the word "itaḥ" ("from here") must be supplied here.

चित् (cit) — "api," "also." इत् (it) — "eva," "indeed": it is used here in the sense of emphasis.

दुवः (duvaḥ) — This word is used in many Ṛks to give various senses. For this word such senses may be given as : "paricaryā (service), sevā, zeal, favour, preference, homage, zeal for service, gift, present" and the like.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Nidaḥ" — "nindanti iti nidaḥ"; "kvip" after the root "ṇidi kutsāyām." The root is "i"-marked (iditaḥ), and by इदितो नुम् धातोः (idito num dhātoḥ, पा. ७-१-५८) the augment "num" would be added; but, because of the Vedic variation of all rules ("chandasi vikalpa"), it does not occur here. "Nidaḥ" — the case-ending "sup" is unaccented, and the accent of the root remains (the "i" is acute by the root-accent). "Bruvantu naḥ" — one sentence: "let our priests praise Indra." "Nir ārata anyataś cit" — another sentence: "(you who blame) go out, leaving this place, and leaving other places also." "Nidaḥ" is a vocative that stands at the beginning of the second sentence; so it is not treated as following the preceding word; by the vārttika समानवाक्ये निघातयुष्मदस्मदादेशा वक्तव्याः [as printed] the nighāta applies only in the same sentence, and thus the vocative does not lose its accent; by आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. ६-१-१९८) it is first-syllable acute. "Anyataḥ" — "anyasmāt" with the affix "tasil" by पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (पा. ५-३-७ [as printed "…-3-1"]); since "tasil" is "l"-marked, लिति (पा. ६-१-१९३) puts the acute on the syllable before the affix. "Cit" — has the sense of "api." Hence the meaning: "not only from this place but from other places too — go out." The connection of the senses of the two roots is shown… Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Accent-marks not reproduced. Note on the varga number: the Kannada marginal note at the end of the grammar reads "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಏಳನೆಯ ವರ್ಗವು ಮುಗಿದುದು" — "here the seventh varga is finished" — i.e. it says seventh (ಏಳನೆಯ), where the eighth had been expected given the page headers read as "Varga 8 [?]"; and p. 103 above, which already closed a varga at the end of Rik 4.3, was marked "seventh" too. This is a discrepancy in the source or in the reading of the small numerals, and is recorded without being resolved.

original p. 111

Rik 4.5 grammar concluded; end of the Eighth Varga [as printed "seventh"]; Sūkta 4, Sixth Mantra: Saṃhitā and Pada

Continuing from p. 110: …the connection of the senses of the two roots is shown by the "luṅ" in "ārata," which is laid down in the section on the connection of roots (धातुसंबन्धे प्रत्ययाः, पा. ३-४-१); where the roots' senses are connected, the affixes denoting the three times (past, future, present) may be used optionally for one another; hence "luṅ" comes in the sense of the imperative (loṭ). After "luṅ," "cli" (च्लि लुङि, पा. ३-१-४३) comes; the second-person plural ending "tha" → "ta" (तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तन्ताम्, पा. ३-४-१०१); by सर्तिशास्त्यर्तिभ्यश्च (पा. ३-१-५६) "cli" is replaced by "aṅ" after "sṛ," "śās" and "ṛ" → "ṛ + a + ta"; ऋदृशोऽङि गुणः (पा. ७-४-१६) gives guṇa → "ar-a-ta"; the augment "āṭ" (आडजादीनाम्, पा. ६-४-७२) → "ā + ar + ata"; the vṛddhi by आटश्च (पा. ६-१-९०) as the single substitute → "ārata." "Dadhānāḥ" — "śānac" is "c"-marked and would give an end-acute; but, by the rule that the later of two conflicting rules prevails (विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम्, पा. १-४-२), अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. ६-१-१८९) gives first-syllable acute. "Duvaḥ" — नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (a Phiṭ-sūtra): a neuter word not ending in "is/-s" is acute on its first syllable; "duvaḥ" is therefore first-syllable acute. ॥५॥

इल्लिगे ೭ನೇಯ ವರ್ಗವು ಮುಗಿದುದು — illige 7neya vargavu mugidudu — "Here the seventh varga is finished" [as printed].

Sūkta 4, The Sixth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उत नः सुभगाँ अरिर्वोचेयुर्दस्म कृष्टयः । स्यामेदिन्द्रस्य शर्मणि ॥६॥

uta naḥ subhagāṃ arir vocēyur dasma kṛṣṭayaḥ | syāmed indrasya śarmaṇi ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading notes: (i) the printed Saṃhitā shows "subhagā" with a mark above the last letter which is read as a nasal sign, giving "subhagāṃ" — standing for the Pada's "subhagān" — but the reading is not certain. (ii) The Pada has "ariḥ" with the "ḥ"; the Saṃhitā "arir" is its sandhi form. (iii) The Pada text, as printed, divides "su-bhagān" with a visible sign; It is given so. Sūkta 4, Sixth Mantra: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Reading note: the second sentence's "ariḥ uta śatrur" — the print has "ariruta śatrurvo 'pi"; the "vo" that follows "śatruḥ" looks like a printer's slip for the next word's "vocēyuḥ" run on; It is given as read and marked [?]. The final "syāmed … bhavema eva" is printed with an irregular spelling, "bhavemyaiva," which is read as "bhavema eva."

हे दस्म शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितरिन्द्र त्वदनुग्रहादरिरुत शत्रुर्वोऽपि नोऽस्मान्सुभगान्शोभनधनोपेतान्वोचेयुः । उच्यासुः । कृष्टयो मनुष्या अस्मन्मित्रभूता वदन्तीति किमु वक्तव्यमिति शेषः । ततो धनसंपन्ना वयमिन्द्रस्य शर्मणीन्द्रप्रसादलब्धे सुखे स्यामेत् । भवेम्यैव । मघुमित्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु धननामसु रयिः क्षत्रं भग इति पठितम् । मनुष्या इत्यादिषु पञ्चविंशतिसंख्याकेषु मनुष्यनामसु कृष्टय इति पठितम् ॥ he dasma śatrūṇām upakṣapayitar indra tvad-anugrahād ariḥ uta śatrur vo 'pi no 'smān subhagān śobhana-dhanopetān vocēyuḥ | ucyāsuḥ | kṛṣṭayo manuṣyā asman-mitra-bhūtā vadantīti kimu vaktavyam iti śeṣaḥ | tato dhana-sampannā vayam indrasya śarmaṇīndra-prasāda-labdhe sukhe syāmed | bhavema eva | maghum ity ādiṣv aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu dhana-nāmasu rayiḥ kṣatraṃ bhaga iti paṭhitam | manuṣyā ity ādiṣu pañcaviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu manuṣya-nāmasu kṛṣṭaya iti paṭhitam ||

Translation: "O 'dasma' — O destroyer of enemies, who bring the enemies to ruin — Indra! By your favour may 'ariḥ' — even an enemy — say of us that we are 'subhagān' — possessed of fine wealth. 'Vocēyuḥ' = 'ucyāsuḥ' (the optative of 'vac,' 'may they say'). 'Kṛṣṭayaḥ' — the people, the men who are our friends, say this — what need is there to say so (of them)! — that is the supplied thought. Therefore, 'syām it' — may we indeed be, 'indrasya śarmaṇi' — in the happiness gained by Indra's grace, endowed with wealth. Among the twenty-eight names of wealth beginning with 'magham,' 'rayiḥ,' 'kṣatram' and 'bhagaḥ' are read; among the twenty-five names of men beginning with 'manuṣyāḥ,' 'kṛṣṭayaḥ' is read."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept): "Uta" — a particle, first-syllable acute (निपाता आद्युदात्ताः, Phiṭ-sūtra 4-1[?]). "Subhagān" — "bhaga" ends, in the "kṛtvādi" class, with the first member's accent set aside: नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) would give the end-acute, but "bhaga" is read in the list beginning with "kṛtva" — क्रत्वादयश्च (पा. ६-२-११८) — so the second member is first-syllable acute. In the saṃhitā: दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा. ८-३-९) the "n" of "subhagān" becomes "ru" before a vowel; भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (पा. ८-३-१७) the "y"; लोपः शाकल्यस्य (पा. ८-३-१९) the "y" is elided; since the elision is "asiddha," no further sandhi occurs; आतोऽटि नित्यम् (पा. ८-३-३) the "ā" takes the nasal sign. "Ariḥ" — "vacana-vyatyaya" (a change of number: singular for plural); from "ṛ" with the Uṇādi "i" (अर्त्तेरिः, उ. सू. ४-१३७ [?]) with the end-acute by the accent of the affix. "Vocēyuḥ" — "ucyāsuḥ": the root "vac" (to speak) in the benedictive (āśīrliṅ), "jhi → jus" (झेर्जुस्, पा. ३-४-१०८); "liṅ" = "yāsuṭ" (लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य, पा. ७-२-७९); the "ṅit" "yāsuṭ" is acute by यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च (पा. ३-४-१०३); the "ṅit" bars guṇa and, by वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (पा. ६-१-१५), the "samprasāraṇa" → "uc"; by Vedic छन्दस्युभयथा (पा. ३-४-११७) the augment "āṭ" is absent; "s" is elided (लोपोऽनन्त्यस्य, as printed); the accents conflict, the "e" of the "yāsuṭ" being the single substitute of "a + ī" is acute (एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः, पा. ८-२-५). "Dasma" — from "dasu upakṣaye" (to waste away) by the Uṇādi दसेर्णिच्च…मुक् (उ. सू. १-१४४ [?]) with the augment "muk"; being a vocative standing after a pada it loses its accent (आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् and तिङ्ङतिङः). "Kṛṣṭayaḥ" — by क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् (पा. ३-३-१७४) the affix "ktic" in the sense of a name; since it is "c"-marked, it is end-acute. "Syāma" — "as bhuvi" (to be); the "a" of "as" is elided (श्नसोरल्लोपः, पा. ६-४-१११); "yāsuṭ" is acute; the word stands at the beginning of the pāda, so no nighāta. "Śarmaṇi" — "śṝ hiṃsāyām"; "hinasti duḥkham iti śarma" ("that which destroys suffering"); by अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते (पा. ३-२-७५) "manin" is added; "iṭ" is barred (नेड्वशि कृति, पा. ७-२-८); the "n"-marked affix gives first-syllable acute. ॥६॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) दस्म (he dasma) — O Indra, destroyer of enemies | (तव अनुग्रहात्) (tava anugrahāt) — by your grace | अरिः उत (ariḥ uta) — even enemies | नः (naḥ) — us | सुभगान् (subhagān) — as wealthy, or as lordly | वोचेयुः (vocēyuḥ) — may they say | कृष्टयः (kṛṣṭayaḥ) — (when our enemies themselves speak well of us, what need to say that) the men who are our friends (say it) | इन्द्रस्य (indrasya) — Indra's (that arises from his favour) | शर्मणि (śarmaṇi) — in happiness | स्याम इत् (syāma it) — we shall indeed be. English as printed in the source; Ṛg-vedic reference-numbers in small Kannada numerals are marked [?], and most of the list in the "dasma" paragraph could not be read reliably.

original p. 113

Rik 4.6: Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, destroyer of enemies! By your favour, even our enemies will praise us, saying that we are wealthy and lordly. If it is so, what wonder that our other friends, the men of our own side, should say it? Besides this, by your (Indra's) grace we shall be happy indeed.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Destroyer of foes, let our enemies say we are prosperous; let men (congratulate us); may we ever live in happiness through your (favour)."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of this Ṛk is, in a small measure, similar to that of the preceding Ṛk; that is, the chief import of the two Ṛks is the same.

सुभगान् (subhagān) — Since the word "bhaga" is read among the twenty-eight words that indicate wealth, beginning with "magha" (Ni. 2-1[?]), "bhaga" here means "wealth." "Subhagān" means "those who have abundant wealth."

अरिः (ariḥ) — Here the singular is used in the sense of the plural. In ordinary speech, when we say "enemy" (the source's English), it is customary to mean the people belonging to the side of our enemy, those who are not our well-wishers. In the same way, here, though the singular "ariḥ — enemy" is used, it must be taken in the plural sense — "our enemies, those who are ill-disposed to us."

दस्म (dasma) — For this word the Bhāṣyakāra says "śatrūṇām upakṣapayitaḥ" and explains it as "destroyer of enemies." The form is derived from the root "dasu upakṣaye." Skandasvāmī explains this word as "darśanīya" — "of beautiful appearance." The Bhāṣyakāra himself, too, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1[?]3, the 3rd and 11th [?] Ṛks, explains the word "dasma" as "darśanīya." This word is used in the Ṛgveda not only in the Ṛks mentioned above but also in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1[?]-1[?]; [the references that follow — about ten of them, in small Kannada numerals — are not legible enough for me to give, and I omit them rather than guess]. The various forms of the root "meda"-… [the print reads "medan"; I take it to be the stem "daṃs"] — daṃsaḥ, daṃsanā, daṃsobhiḥ, daṃsanābhiḥ, daṃsanaiḥ, daṃsayaḥ, daṃsasā, daṃsāṃsi — are used in many places in the Ṛgveda. Geldner and other scholars explain this word as "master" … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Nirukta reference-numbers in small Kannada numerals are marked [?]. Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.

original p. 114

Special topics on Rik 4.6 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

कृष्टयः (kṛṣṭayaḥ) — This word is read among the twenty-five words that signify "man" (manuṣya), beginning with "manuṣyāḥ" (Ni. 2-3[?]). Because the word is derived from the root "kṛṣ" (to plough, to practise agriculture), the sense is "people who practise agriculture, men who plough" — that is, in general, "people, men."

शर्मणि (śarmaṇi) — The word "śarma" is read among the twenty-two [print: "two-and-twenty"; read with caution] words that signify "house" (Ni. 3-4[?]); so Skandasvāmī explains "indrasya śarmaṇi" as "in Indra's house" — that is, "in Indra's world." This does not seem to fit very well. Besides this, since "śarma" is read among the twenty-two [print: "twenty-two" again, though I read the first as "eleven"] words that signify "happiness" (Ni. 3-1[?]), it is fitting to take the sense "happiness" for the word "śarma."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept. - "Uta" — the words that belong to the "eva-ādi" class (एवादीनामन्तः, Phiṭ-sūtra [number as printed "4-1[?]"]) have the last syllable acute; so "uta" is end-acute. Note: the Sanskrit on p. 112 had called "uta" first-syllable acute (by the nipāta rule); the two pages differ, and the discrepancy is recorded without being resolved. - "Subhagān" — "bhaga" belongs to the "kṛtvādi" class; so by नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) the end-acute that a bahuvrīhi after "su" would take is set aside, and by क्रत्वादयश्च (पा. ६-२-११८) the words of the "kratu"-class are first-syllable acute; thus the stem's own accent is prescribed (प्रातिपदोक्त); "subhagān" is an accusative plural. In the saṃhitā: दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा. ८-३-९) turns the "n" into "ru" when followed by a vowel in the same pāda; भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (पा. ८-३-१७) gives "y" for "ru" after "bho," "bhago," "agho" or a short or long "a"; लोपः शाकल्यस्य (पा. ८-३-१९) elides the "y" (in Śākalya's view); since the elision is "asiddha" (पूर्वत्रासिद्धम्, पा. ८-२-१), the rule अकःसवर्णे दीर्घः (पा. ६-१-१०१) does not lengthen the vowels; आतोऽटि नित्यम् (पा. ८-३-३) gives the nasal sign to the "ā": "subhagā[ṃ] ariḥ" this is the form whose nasal sign was flagged at p. 111. - "Ariḥ" — a singular where the plural would be expected; from "ṛ" with the Uṇādi "i" (अर्त्तेरिः, उ. सू. ४-१३७ [as printed "4-1[?]"]); with guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. ७-३-८४) → "ari"; end-acute by the affix-accent. - "Vocēyuḥ" — the root "vac paribhāṣaṇe" (to speak) in the benedictive (āśīrliṅ); the third-person plural "jhi" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Pure grammar in Kannada prose, the rendering of the Sanskrit of p. 112, characterized in order, sūtras kept; numbers as read, [?] where uncertain. The sense of the Rik is already given on pp. 112–113. Continuing "vocēyuḥ":) *…**लिङ्याशिषि…* (liṅ āśiṣy aṅ, पा. ३-१-८६ [as printed; the usual number is different, and the print is recorded]) puts "aṅ" in the āśīrliṅ; झेर्जुस् (पा. ३-४-१०८) puts "jus" for "jhi"; the "j" of "jus" is an "it" by चुटू (पा. १-३-७) and the "s" ... elided by तस्य लोपः (पा. १-३-९); "vac + a + us" — वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (पा. ६-१-१५) and वचेरुम् [as printed "vace um," पा. २-४-२०] — before "aṅ" the augment "um" comes to "vac"; आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७) gives guṇa; यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च (पा. ३-४-१०३) — the augment "yāsuṭ" in the parasmaipada, acute and "ṅit"; किदाशिषि (पा. ३-४-१०४) — "yāsuṭ" in the āśīrliṅ is "kit" (so no guṇa); the Mādhava school adds that by this very sūtra "yāsuṭ" comes. Hence "vac + yās + us." By छन्दस्युभयथा (पा. ३-४-११७) in the Veda the affix is both "sārvadhātuka" and "ārdhadhātuka"; hence "yās + us" takes the "sārvadhātuka" label, and लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) elides the "s" of "yās" ("s" not at the end); अतो येयः (पा. ७-२-८०) turns the "yā" (after an "a"-final stem) into "iy" → "voc-iy-us"; आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७) → "vocēyuḥ." The "sārvadhātuka" accent is lost by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित् (पा. ६-१-१८६) and the affix "aṅ" keeps its own acute; the single substitute "ē" of "i + a" … is acute by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. ८-२-५). - "Dasma" — "dasu upakṣaye" with the Uṇādi ईषियुधीन्धिदसिश्याधूसूभ्योऽमुक् [as printed] (उ. सू. १-१४४ [?]) the affix "ma" with the augment "muk"; as a vocative standing after another word it loses its accent (आमन्त्रितस्य च, as printed). - "Kṛṣṭayaḥ" — क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् (पा. ३-३-१७४): "ktic" and "kta" in a sense of a name: "ktic" is added to "kṛṣ," meaning "men"; "c"-marked, so the last syllable is acute by चितः (पा. ६-१-१६३). - "Syāma" — "as bhuvi" (to be) in the optative (vidhi-liṅ), first-person plural; "yāsuṭ"; by लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) the "s" is elided; the affix "mas" loses its final "s" (नित्यं ङितः, पा. ३-४-९९); श्नसोरल्लोपः (पा. ६-४-१११) the "a" of "as" is elided before an affix that is "k" or "ṅ"-marked; hence "s-yā-ma" → "syāma." (The page ends mid-derivation of "syāma"; it continues on p. 116.

Rik 4.6 grammar concluded; Sūkta 4, Seventh Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

Continuing "syāma" from p. 115: …"yāsuṭ" is acute; since "syāma" stands at the beginning of the pāda, तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) does not cause the nighāta. "Śarmaṇi" — "śṝ hiṃsāyām" (to injure): "hinasti duḥkham iti śarma" ("that which destroys sorrow"); अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते (पा. ३-२-७५ [as printed "3-2-7?"]) the affix "manin"; ṇ-ending "śṝ" takes guṇa → "śar-man"; "iṭ" does not come to a "kṛt" ending in a "val" affix by नेड्वशि कृति (पा. ७-२-८), though आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (पा. ७-२-३५) would require it; since "manin" is "n"-marked, ञित्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. ६-१-१९७) gives the first-syllable acute. ॥६॥

Sūkta 4, The Seventh Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ ईमाशुमाशवे भर यज्ञश्रियं नृमादनम् । पतयन्मन्दयत्सखम् ॥७॥

ā īm āśum āśave bhara yajña-śriyaṃ nṛmādanam | patayan mandayat-sakham ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading notes: (i) the print of the first line in the Saṃhitā runs the words together as "ā īm āśum āśave …"; in the Saṃhitā "ā īm" shows a svarita-type mark that is not reproduced. (ii) The Saṃhitā has "patayan mandayat-sakham" with the final "n" before "m"; the Pada has "patayat | mandayat-sakham." The reading "patayat" in the Pada text is the one the Bhāṣya below also gives.

आ । ईम् । आशुम् । आशवे । भर । यज्ञऽश्रियम् । नृऽमादनम् । पतयत् । मन्दयत्ऽसखम् ॥७॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ईमिति निपात इदंशब्दार्थे वर्तते । हे यजमानाशवे कृत्स्नसोमयोगव्याप्तायेन्द्रायेमा भर । इमं सोममाहर । कीदृशं सोमम् । आशुं सवनत्रयव्याप्तं यज्ञश्रियं यज्ञस्य संपद्रूपं नृमादनं नृणामृत्विग्यजमानानां हर्षहेतुं पतयत्पतनयुक्तं कर्मणि प्राप्नुवन्तं मन्दयत्सखं । य इन्द्रो मन्दयति यजमानान् हर्षयति तस्मिन्निन्द्रे सखिभूतोऽयं सोमः । तत्प्रीतिहेतुत्वात्तृप्तिहेतुत्वाद्वा ॥ īm iti nipāta idaṃ-śabdārthe vartate | he yajamānāśave kṛtsna-soma-yoga-vyāptāyendrāyemā bhara | imaṃ somam āhara | kīdṛśaṃ somam | āśuṃ savana-traya-vyāptaṃ yajña-śriyaṃ yajñasya sampad-rūpaṃ nṛmādanaṃ nṛṇām ṛtvig-yajamānānāṃ harṣa-hetuṃ patayat-patana-yuktaṃ karmaṇi prāpnuvantaṃ mandayat-sakhaṃ | ya indro mandayati yajamānān harṣayati tasmin indre sakhibhūto 'yaṃ somaḥ | tat-prīti-hetutvāt tṛpti-hetutvād vā ||

Translation: "'Īm' — a particle, used in the sense of the word 'idam' ('this'). O sacrificer! 'Āśave' — to Indra, who pervades the whole union with Soma (the whole Soma sacrifice) — 'ā bhara' — bring this Soma; carry it. What kind of Soma? 'Āśum' — pervading the three pressings; 'yajñaśriyam' — the 'wealth' (sampad) of the sacrifice; 'nṛmādanam' — the cause of joy to men, the priests and the sacrificer; 'patayat' — endowed with 'fall' (that is, 'moving, going forward in the rite'); 'mandayatsakham' — a friend of the one who gladdens: the Indra who gladdens ('mandayati') the sacrificers, who makes them glad — to that Indra this Soma is a friend, since it is the cause of his pleasure or of his satisfaction." Reading notes: the phrase "patayat-patana-yuktam karmaṇi prāpnuvantam" is printed with some run-together letters; It is read as given; the Bhāṣya's gloss of "patayat" is somewhat loose; the Kannada Pada-meaning, on p. 117, renders it "the one with the power to bring about the actions that fall away / are lost," which shows the same uncertainty.

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept): "Āśum" — the Uṇādi कृवापाजिमिस्वदिसाध्यशूभ्य उण् (उ. सू. १-१ [as printed]) — the affix "uṇ" after "kṛ," "vā," "pā," "ji," "mi," "svad," "sādh," "aś[ū]" — "n"-marked, with the accent of the affix. "Āśave" — as before. "Yajñaśriyam" — as a compound its end is acute (समासस्य, पा. ६-१-२२३). "Nṛmādanam" — "mādyanty anena iti mādanaḥ": "lyuṭ" in the sense of instrument or place (करणाधिकरणयोश्च, पा. ३-३-११७); "lit" accent before the affix, but by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९) the first-member accent remains. "Patayat" — "pat" (to fall) in the causal (चुरादिणिच्, पा. ३-१-२५), with आतो लोपः (पा. ६-४-६४) … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept. English as printed.

original p. 117

Rik 4.7: grammar concluded; Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering

Continuing "patayat" from p. 116: …"pat" in the causal with "ṇic" (सत्यापपाश…, as printed: the "cur-ādi" "ṇic," पा. ३-१-२५); the final "a" of the stem is elided (आतो लोपः; read here as अतो लोपः, पा. ६-४-४८, as printed "6-4-48"); the elided "a" is treated as if present (स्थानिवत्) so the "upadhā" vṛddhi (अत उपधायाः, पा. ७-२-११६) does not occur (१-१-५८), and in the "laṭ" the "śatṛ" replaces (लटः शतृशानचौ, पा. ३-२-१२४); because the Veda has छन्दस्युभयथा (पा. ३-४-११७) the affix is taken as "ārdhadhātuka" and so (the print argues) the "śap" is not applied (शबभावादुपदेशात्) and "nighāta" is absent (पा. ६-१-१८६); the affix's acute alone remains. Even where the "ārdhadhātuka" character is taken, all rules are optional in the Veda (विभाषा छन्दसि, as printed: "pari. 93" [?]); so "ṇi"-elision (णेरनिटि, पा. ६-४-५१) does not occur (णिलोपाभावः); and by सुपां सुलुगित्यनोलुक् [as printed], the "luk" for "sup" is considered, and by न लुमताङ्गस्य (पा. १-१-६३) — "an operation that depends on an affix that has been elided by 'lu' does not apply" — the "ugit" rule (उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः, पा. ७-१-७०) does not bring "num." Thus "patayat" is end-acute. "Mandayatsakham" — "mandayati iti mandayat" (the same stem in "śatṛ"; end-acute); "mandayatīndre sakhā" — a compound of the type "śastra-mimāti" (the print: सप्तमी…, "yogavibhāgāt samāsaḥ"), with the first-member accent retained by तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ… (पा. ६-२-२). ॥७॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(O sacrificer) यज्ञश्रियम् (yajñaśriyam) — which is of the form of the wealth of the sacrifice | नृमादनम् (nṛmādanam) — which causes joy to men — the priests, the sacrificer and the others | पतयत् (patayat) — with the power to bring about the actions that are failing (that are going astray) | मन्दयत्सखम् (mandayatsakham) — friendly to Indra, who gladdens the sacrificer and the others | ईम् आशुम् (īm āśum) — this Soma-juice which pervades all three pressings — that is, which is made ready in all of them | आशवे (āśave) — to Indra, who pervades the sacrifice — that is, who bears the chief share in the sacrifice (the chief god) | आ भर (ā bhara) — bring.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

This is a sentence addressed by the Hotṛ to the sacrificer or to the Adhvaryu: O sacrificer (or Adhvaryu)! The Soma-juice that is now being prepared in this sacrifice is chiefly the wealth of the sacrifice; that is, by it the sacrifice is adorned. Such Soma-juice causes joy to all people — the priests, the sacrificer and so on; it has the power to bring about the (repair of) actions that have fallen into fault. Moreover, this Soma-juice is dear, like a friend, to Indra, who gladdens the sacrificer. Quickly bring such a Soma-juice for Indra.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Offer to Indra, pervader (of the whole Soma Sacrifice) the Soma juice that is present (at the three Savana ceremonies) the wealth of the Sacrifice, the Source of joy to men (including priests and worshipper), the favourite of Indra who gives happiness to the worshippers." original p. 118

Special topics on Rik 4.7; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This Ṛk is spoken addressing the sacrificer or the Adhvaryu.

ईम् (īm) — Skandasvāmī explains "īm" as "enam," that is, "this Soma," "the Soma-juice."

आशुम् (āśum) — For this word the general sense is "quickly; vigilantly." Though it is a qualifying word, it is used here as the thing qualified (viśeṣya). Geldner thinks that in this Ṛk the word is used as an adverb (kriyā-viśeṣaṇa). In the Ṛgveda this word "āśu" is used as an adjective, in the sense "going fast," of horses, in many places. In the same sense it is also used as an adjective of the words "chariot," "wheel," "bird," "messenger," "Vāyu," "Indra" and "Soma," in many places.

नृमादनम् (nṛmādanam) — Since men are gladdened by drinking the Soma-juice that produces intoxication, it is natural. Therefore it is said in many places that the drinking of Soma gives delight to men. The use of this word:

त्वं सोम नृमादनः पवस्व चर्षणीसहे । (ऋ. सं. ९-३४-४ [?]) tvaṃ soma nṛmādanaḥ pavasva carṣaṇīsahe | (ṛ. saṃ. 9-34-4 [?]) Gloss: "You, O Soma, the gladdener of men, flow clear for the conqueror of the peoples."

त्वं सुतो नृमादनो दधन्वान्मत्सरिन्तमः । (ऋ. सं. ९-६२-३ [?]) tvaṃ suto nṛmādano dadhanvān matsarintamaḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 9-62-3 [?]) Gloss: "You, pressed, the gladdener of men, the bearer, most exhilarating."

— occurs only in these Ṛks, nowhere else. The word "mādana" derives from the root "mad" ("to be glad; to rejoice, exhilarate" ).

पतयत् (patayat) — Many scholars have discussed the sense of this word at length. Skandasvāmī's view is "gamayantam" — "causing to go." Veṅkaṭamādhava explains the word "patayat" in "manuṣyān pātayeti hi somaḥ" — "'Soma makes men fall'": the sense being "the Soma that protects men" [as the Kannada reads it; I note that the quotation as printed is hard to interpret, and I give the Kannada's sense only]. Western scholars explain this word as "accelerating, quickening, inspiring to friends."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized. "Āśum" — कृवापाजिमिस्वदिसाध्यशूभ्य उण् (उ. सू. १-१ [as printed]) — after the roots "ḍukṛñ karaṇe" (to do), "vā gati-gandhanayoḥ" (to go, to give), "pā pāne" (to drink), "ji abhibhave" (to conquer), "ḍu miñ prakṣepaṇe" (to throw), "svad āsvādane" (to taste), "sādh saṃsiddhau" (to accomplish), "aśū vyāptau" (to pervade) the affix "uṇ" comes; from "aśū" + "uṇ," by अत उपधायाः (पा. ७-२-११६) vṛddhi of the penultimate before an "ñit" or "ṇit" affix → "āśu"; the first syllable is acute by the affix-accent. "Āśave" is to be understood like this. "Bhara" — "hṛñ haraṇe" (to carry) in the imperative (loṭ) … Page headers: p. 119 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā"; p. 120 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." These two pages are pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose for "bhara," "yajñaśriyam," "nṛmādanam" and "patayat," with extended scholastic argument about "patayat"; they do not bear on the sense of the Rik, given on pp. 116–118. Per the standing convention they are characterized in outline, not translated line by line; every sūtra the pages name is kept in three layers, numbers as read in small Kannada numerals, [?] where uncertain. A good part of p. 120 is crowded with technical objections and replies that are not reproduced.

original pp. 119–120

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.7 (Kannada), continued — characterized

p. 119. - "Bhara" continuing from p. 118 — "hṛñ haraṇe," in the imperative second-person singular "sip" → "hṛ + si"; सेर्ह्यपिच्च (पा. ३-४-८७) puts "hi" for "si" and it is non-"p"-marked; "śap" (कर्तरि शप्, पा. ३-१-६८) comes after the root; सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. ७-३-८४) gives guṇa → "har-a-hi"; the guṇa of "ṛ" is "ar," and by उरण् रपरः (ur aṇ raparaḥ, पा. १-१-५१) the substitute of "ṛ" is followed by "r"; by अतो हेः (पा. ६-४-१०५) the "hi" is elided after a short "a"; हृग्रहोर्भश्छन्दसि (hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi, पा. ८-२-३२ [?]) substitutes "bh" for the "h" of "hṛ" and "grah" in the Veda → "bhara." Since it stands after "ā" (not a tiṅanta) and not at the pāda's beginning, तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) makes it wholly unaccented; in the saṃhitā it is preceded by the svarita of "ve" and becomes "anudāttas" by स्वरितात्संहितायामनुदात्तानाम् (पा. १-२-३९) — it is pracaya (level). - "Yajñaśriyam" — "yaj" + "naṅ" (यजयाचयतविच्छप्रच्छरक्षो नङ्, पा. ३-३-९०) → "yajña"; by स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (पा. ८-४-४०) the "s/t"-class letters become "ś/c"-class in contact with "ś/c"-class, so the "n" of "naṅ" takes the "c"-class nasal "ñ"; यजस्य… with ज्ञ (the conjunct "j + ñ") → "yajña." "Śrī" — from "śriñ sevāyām" (to serve) by the vārttika क्विब्वचिप्रच्छ्यायतस्तुकटप्रुजुश्रीणां दीर्घोऽसंप्रसारणं च (the vārttika as printed, read with doubt): "kvip" with lengthening → "śrī." "Yajñasya śrīḥ" — a genitive tatpuruṣa; then the second-case singular "am" → "yajñaśrī + am"; भ्रूवां ियोरियङुवङौ [as printed: अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां य्वोरियङुवङौ, पा. ६-४-७७] — "iyaṅ/uvaṅ" for "ī/ū" of a root-final, of a "śnu"-stem, and of "bhrū," before an "ac"-initial affix — gives "iy" for "ī" → "yajñaśriyam." The compound is end-acute by समासस्य (पा. ६-१-२२३). - "Nṛmādanam" — "mādyante anena" ("they delight by this") → "mādanaḥ"; "lyuṭ" in the sense of instrument by करणाधिकरणयोश्च (पा. ३-३-११७); "lyuṭ" is "l"-marked, so लिति (पा. ६-१-१९३) puts the acute on the syllable before the affix, namely "ā"; in the compound "nṛmādana," गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९) retains the kṛt-final member's accent; the "ā" is acute. - "Patayat" — the root "pat" "gatau" is in the "cur-ādi" class (the tenth) read with short "a" at the end (as "pata" — the "gaṇa" list, by the verse: "satyāpa, pāśa, rūpa, vīṇā, tula, śloka, senā, loma, tvaca, varma, varṇa, cūrṇa" ["satyāpapāśarūpavīṇātulaślokasenālomatvacavarmavarṇacūrṇa-"]); चुरादिभ्यो णिच् (पा. ३-१-२५) puts "ṇic" after these … (continues on p. 120).

p. 120. Continuing "patayat": …"ṇic" comes; the final "a" of "pata" is elided before an "ārdhadhātuka" (अतो लोपः, पा. ६-४-४८); the "ṇ" and "c" of "ṇic" are "it"-letters (चुटू, पा. १-३-७; तस्य लोपः, पा. १-३-९); "upadhā" is the vowel before the last letter (अलोऽन्त्यात्पूर्व उपधा, पा. १-१-६५); by अत उपधायाः (पा. ७-२-११६) vṛddhi of the penultimate short "a" before an "ñit/ṇit" affix would be expected; but स्थानिवदादेशोऽनल्विधौ (पा. १-१-५६) makes the substitute (the elision of "a" before "ṇic") act as the original, so the "a" is regarded as still present and so is not "upadhā" — the print argues the point at length — and no vṛddhi arises. Then the "laṭ" → "śatṛ" (लटः शतृशानचावप्रथमासमानाधिकरणे, पा. ३-२-१२४); the "śatṛ" is "ārdhadhātuka" and "sārvadhātuka" alike by छन्दस्युभयथा (पा. ३-४-११७); कर्तरि शप् (पा. ३-१-६८) would give "śap"; the debate asks whether "śap" is absent when "śatṛ" is taken as "ārdhadhātuka"; णेरनिटि (पा. ६-४-५१) — "ṇi" is elided before an "ārdhadhātuka" without "iṭ" — would then also apply, but since all rules are optional in the Veda (सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्ते, paribhāṣā [number as printed "93"]), the "ṇi" is kept: "pat + i + at" → guṇa and "ay" → "patayat." The "am" case-ending after it (सुपां सुलुक्, पा. ७-१-३९) is elided by "luk" (सुडनपुंसकस्य, पा. १-१-४३) as a name for the non-neuter "su/au/jas/am/auṭ" being "sarvanāmasthāna"; प्रत्ययलोपे प्रत्ययलक्षणम् (पा. १-१-६२) and उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः (पा. ७-१-७०) would bring "num," but न लुमताङ्गस्य (पा. १-१-६३) bars it — the print enumerates the words "luk," "ślu," "lup" and the rest. original p. 121

Rik 4.7 grammar concluded; Sūkta 4, Eighth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

Concluding the grammar of "patayat" from p. 120: …where the affix has been elided by "lu"-type elision, no operation depending on the elided affix takes place on the stem — the "pratyaya-lakṣaṇa" is thus prohibited — and so, because the "sarvanāmasthāna" affix is not following, the "num" augment of उगिदचाम् is not added. In the same way "mandayat" is end-acute; "mandayati sakhā" — "(one who is) a friend in the Indra who gladdens" — is a compound formed by the "saptamī" (locative-compound) rule, सप्तमी शौण्डैः (पा. २-१-४० [as printed "2-1-4?"]), which the print divides by the word "saptamī," for the locative word compounds with a competent locative word; by तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थतृतीयासप्तम्युपमानाव्ययद्वितीयाकृत्याः (पा. ६-२-२ [as printed "6-2-2"; the sūtra reads 'tṛtīyā-saptamī'…]) the first member (a locative) retains its natural accent; and राजाहस्सखिभ्यष्टच् (पा. ५-४-९१) the affix "ṭac" comes after "sakhi." ॥७॥

Sūkta 4, The Eighth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अस्य पीत्वा शतक्रतो घनो वृत्राणामभवः । प्रावो वाजेषु वाजिनम् ॥८॥

asya pītvā śatakrato ghano vṛtrāṇām abhavaḥ | prāvo vājeṣu vājinam ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अस्य । पीत्वा । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो । घनः । वृत्राणाम् । अभवः । प्र । आवः । वाजेषु । वाजिनम् ॥८॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मयुक्तेन्द्र त्वमस्य सोमस्य संबन्धिनमंशं पीत्वा वृत्राणां वृत्रनामकासुरप्रमुखाणां शत्रूणां घनोऽभवः । हन्ताभूः । ततो वाजेषु संग्रामेषु वाजिनं संग्रामवन्तं स्वभक्तं प्रावः । प्रकर्षेण रक्षितवानसि । अस्येतीदंशब्देन प्रयोगसमये पुरोदेशस्थः सोमो निर्दिश्यते न तु पूर्वप्रकृतः सोमः परामृश्यते । अतोऽनन्वादेशत्वान्नात्रेदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्त इत्येतदोदात्त— [print: "…श्चितीयादौ"] । पा. २-४-३२ । इत्यशादेशः । अतो न सर्वानुदात्तत्वं किंतु तृदा-… he śatakrato bahu-karma-yuktendra tvam asya somasya sambandhinam aṃśaṃ pītvā vṛtrāṇāṃ vṛtra-nāmakāsura-pramukhāṇāṃ śatrūṇāṃ ghano 'bhavaḥ | hantābhūḥ | tato vājeṣu saṃgrāmeṣu vājinaṃ saṃgrāmavantaṃ sva-bhaktaṃ prāvaḥ | prakarṣeṇa rakṣitavān asi | asyetīdaṃ-śabdena prayoga-samaye puro-deśasthaḥ somo nirdiśyate na tu pūrva-prakṛtaḥ somaḥ parāmṛśyate | ato 'nanvādeśatvān nātredamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudātta … [the print runs on: "…traitīyādau | pā. 2-4-32 | ity aśādeśaḥ | ato na sarvānudāttatvaṃ kiṃtu tṛdā-…"] ||

Translation: "O 'śatakrato' — O Indra, endowed with many deeds — having drunk 'the portion belonging to this Soma,' you have become 'ghanaḥ' — the slayer ('hantā') — 'vṛtrāṇām' — of the enemies headed by the demon named Vṛtra. Then, 'vājeṣu' — in the battles — 'vājinam' — the one who has a battle (the one who fights), your own devotee — 'prāvaḥ' — you have protected in an eminent way. By the word 'idam' in 'asya,' the Soma standing in front at the time of use is pointed out — not the Soma mentioned earlier; hence, since this is not an 'anvādeśa' (a back-reference), the substitution of 'a' for 'idam' (before the third case-ending, etc.) does not apply here, … and the whole word is therefore not unaccented, but …" The print of the last lines — the grammar of "asya" — is partly garbled, and it continues on the next page; The sense is given, not a reading of the garbled stretch. original p. 122

Rik 4.8: grammar concluded (characterized); Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

Grammar within the Bhāṣya, concluded the Sanskrit; given in outline: "Asya" — since "idam" is not here used in 'anvādeśa' (back-reference), the substitute "a" (इदमो मः etc.) with the unaccented 'a' does not take the sense of anvādeśa, and the accented form results: the accent of "asya" is thus the first-syllable acute. The statement on the case-ending is "vibhaktir udāttā" — हलि लोपः (पा. ७-२-१०६) — the "id" of "idam" is elided before a consonant-beginning ending; the "a" substitutes; अकारः प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः; "asya" is accented by the case-ending, as in अनुदात्तादिः etc. (पा. ६-१-१६१, "…vibhaktirudāttā"). "Pītvā" — "pā pāne" with "ktvā" (पिबतेः क्त्वा); घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि (पा. ६-४-६६) gives "ī"; end-acute by the affix's accent. "Ghanaḥ" — मूर्तौ घनः (पा. ३-३-७७ [as printed "3-3-77"]) — "ghan" is formed from "han" (to strike) with हन्तेर्घादेशः: "ghana" in the sense of 'a solid mass'; the "kārinī" (the doer-sense) with "ac," as in "tadasyāstīti" (the possessive "ac" after "ghana" as "arśa-ādi"); "citvāt" — end-acute. "Vājeṣu" — "vāja" is first-syllable acute as belonging to the "vṛṣādi" class. "Vājinam" — the accent of the affix "ini." ॥८॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

  1. शतक्रतो (śatakrato) — O Indra, who do many deeds of daring | (you) अस्य (asya) — a small portion of this Soma-juice | पीत्वा (pītvā) — having drunk | वृत्राणाम् (vṛtrāṇām) — of the (enemies) called Vṛtras | घनः (ghanaḥ) — the destroyer | अभवः (abhavaḥ) — become | (और) वाजेषु (vājeṣu) — in the many battles (that we fight with our enemies) | वाजिनम् (vājinam) — the one who fights (our hero, your devotee) | प्रावः (prāvaḥ) — protect in a special way.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, who do many daring deeds! Drink this Soma-juice that we have prepared and set here for you, and destroy our enemies called Vṛtras; and in the battles that we fight with our enemies, protect our warrior from the harm of enemies.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"O (Indra) performer of many deeds, having drunk of this (Soma), you have become destroyer of our enemies headed by Vritra and protected our warrior in battles."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अस्य (asya) — The Soma-juice that you have set here for you; the Bhāṣyakāra has supplied the word "aṃśam" and explained it as "a share of this Soma-juice." Skandasvāmī and Veṅkaṭamādhava hold that the word "asya," which is in the genitive case, is used in the sense of the second case (accusative), by the rule "u-sa-yo-gi…" the print is cut off at this point, and continues on the next page. original p. 123

Special topics on Rik 4.8 (continued): "asya," "śatakrato," "vṛtrāṇām" (opening)

Continuing "asya" from p. 122: …in the sense of the "u-sa-yo-gi…" rule, and have explained it with the words "āmum somam" — "this Soma-juice." In the Ṛgveda, in the context of giving the sense of one case-ending, the use of another case-ending is found especially often.

शतक्रतो (śatakrato) — The Bhāṣyakāra explains this word as "bahukarmayukta" — one who does many daring deeds. Veṅkaṭamādhava has explained the word "kratu" as "prajñā" (wisdom). Skandasvāmī has given both of these senses. Here the word "śata" is used in the sense "many." In English also it is the custom to use the words "hundred" and "thousand" in the sense of "many." In the Purāṇas and other works the word "śatakratu" has the sense "one who has performed a hundred Aśvamedha sacrifices"; and, since it is well known that Indra, before obtaining the rank of Indra, performed a hundred Aśvamedha sacrifices and attained that rank, and that those who perform a hundred sacrifices obtain the rank of Indra, it is said in the Purāṇas and elsewhere that in many contexts Indra causes many obstacles, so that others may not perform a hundred sacrifices. But Indra's place in the Vedas is different, and his place as stated in the Purāṇas and later works is different. That is: in the Vedas Indra is praised as the foremost and most excellent among the gods, and there are many sūktas that praise his daring deeds. Why so? In the Ṛgveda the praises of Indra are as many as those of any other deity; in the Purāṇas and later works, the place of Indra is described as a lower place, subject to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and the other deities. In the Ṛgveda and in the other Vedas the word "śatakratu," when used of Indra, is found especially often.

वृत्राणाम् (vṛtrāṇām) — "Vṛtra" is a well-known demon; Indra destroyed him. This matter is described at length in the Ṛgveda and in the other Vedas too. It is said that this Vṛtra-asura used to hold back the rain, so that it would not fall, and that Indra therefore killed him and caused the rain to come. Yāska (the author of the Nirukta) and others hold that the word "vṛtra" is used for the cloud, in the sense of a figure (upamārtha). In the Nirukta it stands thus:

कोऽर्को [?] वृत्रः । मेघ इति नैरुक्ताः । त्वाष्ट्रोऽसुर इत्यैतिहासिकाः । आपां च ज्योतिषश्च मिश्रभावकर्मणो वर्षकर्म जायते । तत्रोपमार्थेन युद्धवर्णा भवन्ति ॥ (नि. २-१८ [?]) ko 'rko [?] vṛtraḥ | megha iti nairuktāḥ | tvāṣṭro 'sura ity aitihāsikāḥ | āpāṃ ca jyotiṣaś ca miśrabhāva-karmaṇo varṣa-karma jāyate | tatropamārthena yuddha-varṇā bhavanti || (ni. 2-18 [?]) (Reading note: the first words are printed as "ko'rko vṛtraḥ"; what I expect from the Nirukta is "ko vṛtraḥ," and the "rko" may be a printing slip or a ligature I cannot read. I give it as printed with [?].)

Translation: "'Who is Vṛtra?' — 'The cloud,' say the etymologists (nairuktāḥ); 'the Asura, son of Tvaṣṭṛ,' say the historians (aitihāsikāḥ). From the action of the mixing of the waters and of the light (lightning) comes the action of rain. There, by way of simile, the descriptions are of battle." (Nirukta 2-18 [?])

The sense of this: who is Vṛtra? For the word "vṛtra," the author of the Nirukta says "the cloud," and the Itihāsa writers say "an Asura, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ." Rain arises from the union of the waters and the lightning (water and … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Reference-number marked [?].

original p. 124

Special topics on Rik 4.8: the Vṛtra myth; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

…(water and lightning) — rain comes from their conjunction. Therefore the rain that falls with thunder and lightning, described figuratively as a battle between Indra and the demon Vṛtra, is a matter of common usage.

Because the rain that comes with the thunder, the lightning and the rolling of the clouds, with the blowing of the wind, and with the streams of water pouring in torrents, looks like a battle, it appears to have become the custom to describe this rain as a battle. The cloud that is imagined in the battle thus described is Vṛtra. The lightning that now and then flashes in the midst of the cloud is Indra's thunderbolt. The terrible roar of the thunder is the roar of the warriors in the battle. Since this roar of thunder and lightning comes both before the rain and at the beginning of the rain, and then, after a short while, the roar lessens and the rain pours the more, the description in terms of battle was applied — that Indra, using his thunderbolt on the Vṛtra-asura, imagined as the cloud, killed him, and that the rain which had been held back by him then poured out as it pleased. Because the word "vṛtra" is read among the thirty words that signify the cloud (Ni. 1-1[?]), it is possible to support this sense.

In the Bhāgavata and other Purāṇas there is an extended description that Vṛtra was the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, the Prajāpati, and that Indra killed him. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda and in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa such descriptions are found in many places. More detail on this matter will be given later.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Asya" — the word "idam" (from "idi paramaiśvarye," the root "to rule") — the "i" of the root carries the "it"-label (इदितो नुम् धातोः, पा. ७-१-५८), so the augment "num" is added, giving "ind"; by the Uṇādi (इन्देः कमिन्नलोपश्च, उ. सू. ४-१४७ [as printed "4-1[?]"]) the affix "kamin" after "ind," with the elision of the "n" of the root; both "k" and "i" being "it"-letters, "am" remains: "id + am" = "idam." The "Daśapādī" author takes the sūtra इणोदमुक् [as printed] — the affix "damuk" after "iṇ gatau," giving "idam." From the word "idam," what appears directly in front at the time of use — the Soma-juice — is pointed to; the Soma that has been mentioned in the preceding mantras is not referred to here. Therefore this is not an "anvādeśa." "Anvādeśa" means referring again, for the sake of telling another operation, to what was mentioned earlier with the purpose of telling some operation … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." The sense of the Rik is already given on p. 122.

original p. 125

Rik 4.8 grammar (continued) — characterized

Continuing "asya" from p. 124: …"anvādeśa" is "re-taking, for the purpose of telling another action, what has been mentioned earlier." Here the Soma that is directly visible is pointed to by "asya"; so this is not an anvādeśa. Hence, by इदमो न्वादेशेऽशनुदात्त ऋतृतीयादौ [the rule as printed; the standard form is इदमो ऽन्वादेशे ऽशनुदात्त ऋतृतीयाद्यौ, पा. २-४-३२] — "when a third-case or later ending follows, and the word 'idam' is used in anvādeśa, 'aś' is substituted, unaccented" — the substitution of "aś" does not take place; therefore "asya" is not wholly unaccented. By त्यदादीनामः (पा. ७-२-१०२) "a" replaces the final of the "tyad"-class words when a case-ending follows; applied to "idam," when the sixth-case singular "ṅas" follows, अतो गुणे (पा. ६-१-९४) gives the "pararūpa"; by इदमो मः … "id + sya"; हलि लोपः (पा. ७-२-११३) — the "id" of "idam" is elided before a consonant-initial third-or-later case-ending — "id" loses its "d"-final; leaving "a" and "sya": "asya." The "a" is acute by the bare-stem accent; ऊडिदम्पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः (पा. ६-१-१७१) — the case-endings are acute after "ūṭh," "idam," the pada-words beginning with "pad," "ap," "pum," "rai," "dyu" etc., when they are not "sarvanāmasthāna" — the case-ending "sya" is acute; then by अनुदात्तं पदमेकवर्जम् (पा. ६-१-१५८) the others are unaccented, so the "a" of "asya" is unaccented.

"Pītvā" — "pā pāne" (to drink) with "ktvā"; by घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि (पा. ६-४-६६) the "ā" of "pā" becomes "ī" → "pītvā"; end-acute by the affix's accent. The words "pītvā" and "śatakrato" have no mutual syntactic connection ("sāmarthya"), so "parāṅgavad-bhāva" does not apply to "pītvā."

"Śatakrato" — "pañcaviṃśati-triṃśac-catvāriṃśat-pañcāśat-ṣaṣṭi-saptati-aśīti-navati śatam" (पञ्चविंशतिर्…शतं, the list with "śata" among the "nipātanas"); "daśadaśataḥ parimāṇasya" ("of a measure of ten tens") the "ta" affix and the substitution "śa" give "śata" — end-acute by the affix, in the view that the Uṇādi words are not "vyutpanna" (derived); in the other view (that they are not derived), end-acute by the bare-stem accent. "Kratu" — from "ḍukṛñ karaṇe" the Uṇādi कृञः कतुः (उ. सू. १-७२ [as printed "1-7?"]) the affix "katu" → "kratu" — end-acute by the affix-accent. The two words in a bahuvrīhi compound: "śatakratu," vocative "śatakrato"; being a vocative standing after another word it is unaccented by आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. ६-१-१९८, as printed). "Ghanaḥ" — मूर्तौ घनः (पा. ३-३-७७) in the sense of solid; or "ghana" from "han" with "ap" in the sense of "hantā"; "han" is replaced by "ghana" (हनो घः?); "ghano 'sya asti" — अर्श आदिभ्योऽच् (पा. ५-२-१२७) "ac" is added in the possessive; "ac" is "c"-marked and so end-acute by चितः (पा. ६-१-१६३); and from "ghanaḥ asya asti" the derivation proceeds …

Rik 4.8 grammar concluded; Sūkta 4, Ninth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

Concluding the grammar: …"ghanaḥ" is end-acute by चितः (पा. ६-१-१६३). "Vājeṣu" — वृषादीनां च (पा. ६-१-२०३) — the first syllable of words in the "vṛṣādi" class is acute; "vāja" is among them, so first-syllable acute. "Vājinam" — "vājo 'syāsti" ("who has 'vāja'"): अत इनिठनौ (पा. ५-२-११५) the affix "ini"; the accent of the affix. ॥८॥

Sūkta 4, The Ninth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तं त्वा वाजेषु वाजिनं वाजयामः शतक्रतो । धनानामिन्द्र सातये ॥९॥

taṃ tvā vājeṣu vājinaṃ vājayāmaḥ śatakrato | dhanānām indra sātaye ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तम् । त्वा । वाजेषु । वाजिनम् । वाजयामः । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो । धनानाम् । इन्द्र । सातये ॥९॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मयुक्त यद्वा बहुप्रज्ञानयुक्तेन्द्र धनानां सातये संभजनार्थं वाजेषु युद्धेषु वाजिनं बलवन्तं त्वा पूर्वमन्त्रोक्तगुणयुक्तं त्वां वाजयामः । अन्नवन्तं कुर्मः । रण इत्यादिषु षट्चत्वारिंशत्सु संग्रामनामसु पौंस्ये महाधने वाजेष्वग्मन्निति पठितम् । अष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेष्वन्ननामसु बन्धो वाजः पाज इति पठितम् । उरु तुवीत्यादिषु द्वादशसु बहुनामसु शतं सहस्रमिति पठितम् । अपोऽप्स इत्यादिषु षड्विंशतिसंख्याकेषु कर्मनामसु शक्म क्रतुरिति पठितम् । केतः केतुरित्यादिष्वेकादशसु प्रज्ञानामसु क्रतुरसुरिति पठितम् ॥ त्वा । अनुदात्तं सर्वमित्यनुवृत्तौ त्वामौ द्वितीयायाः इति त्वादेशः । वाजेषु । वज व्रज गतौ । वाजयति गमयति शरीरनिर्वाहमनेनेति वाजो बलमन्नं वा । ण्यन्तात्करणे घञ् । तत्र ञित्स्वरस्यापवादे कर्षात्वतः । पा. ६-१-१५९ । इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते तस्याप्यपवादत्वेन वृषादीनां च । पा. ६-१-२०३ । इत्यादि [read: आद्युदात्तत्वम्] । वाजयामः । वाजोऽस्यास्तीति वाजवान् । तं करोति इत्यर्थे तत्करोति तदाचष्टे । पा. ३-१-२६, … he śatakrato bahu-karma-yukta yadvā bahu-prajñāna-yuktendra dhanānāṃ sātaye sambhajanārthaṃ vājeṣu yuddheṣu vājinaṃ balavantaṃ tvā pūrva-mantroktaguṇa-yuktaṃ tvāṃ vājayāmaḥ | annavantaṃ kurmaḥ | raṇa ity ādiṣu ṣaṭcatvāriṃśatsu saṃgrāma-nāmasu pauṃsye mahādhane vājeṣv agmann iti paṭhitam | aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣv anna-nāmasu bandho vājaḥ pāja iti paṭhitam | uru tuvīty ādiṣu dvādaśasu bahu-nāmasu śataṃ sahasram iti paṭhitam | apo 'psa ity ādiṣu ṣaḍviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu karma-nāmasu śakma kratur iti paṭhitam | ketaḥ ketur ity ādiṣv ekādaśasu prajñā-nāmasu kratur asur iti paṭhitam || tvā | anudāttaṃ sarvam ity anuvṛttau tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ iti tvādeśaḥ | vājeṣu | vaja vraja gatau | vājayati gamayati śarīra-nirvāham anena iti vājo balam annaṃ vā | ṇyantāt karaṇe ghañ | tatra ñit-svarasyāpavāde karṣātvataḥ | pā. 6-1-159 | ity antodāttatve prāpte tasyāpy apavādatvena vṛṣādīnāṃ ca | pā. 6-1-203 | ity ādi [read: ādyudāttatvam] | vājayāmaḥ | vājo 'syāstīti vājavān | taṃ karoti ity arthe tat karoti tad ācaṣṭe | pā. 3-1-26, …

Translation: "O 'śatakrato' — O Indra, endowed with many deeds, or: endowed with much wisdom — 'dhanānāṃ sātaye' — for the sharing, the enjoyment, of riches — 'tvā' — you, 'vājeṣu' — in battles, 'vājinam' — the strong; you, who are endowed with the qualities stated in the previous mantra — 'vājayāmaḥ' — 'we make you possessed of food' (we cause you to have 'anna'). Among the forty-six names of battle beginning with 'raṇa,' 'pauṃsya,' 'mahādhana' and 'vājeṣu' are read ('agmann' is read there); among the twenty-eight names of food, 'bandhaḥ,' 'vājaḥ,' 'pājaḥ' are read; among the twelve names of 'many,' beginning with 'uru, tuvi,' 'śatam' and 'sahasram' are read; among the twenty-six names of action beginning with 'apaḥ, apsaḥ,' 'śakma' and 'kratuḥ' are read; among the eleven names of wisdom beginning with 'ketaḥ, ketuḥ,' 'kratuḥ' and 'asuḥ' are read." The print here has the counts as given; the Nighaṇṭu quotation 'vājeṣv agmann' is printed as given and is flagged as hard to read.

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized): "Tvā" — unaccented ("anudāttaṃ sarvam" by continuation), by त्वामौ द्वितीयायाः (पा. ८-१-२३) "tvā" replaces "tvām." "Vājeṣu" — root "vaja/vraja gatau" (to go); "vājayati" — "he makes go"; "vāja" is strength or food, by which the support of the body is accomplished; "ghañ" after the causal root in the sense of instrument; the "ñit"-accent (end-acute by the "ñit" rule, ञित्यादिर्नित्यम्, पा. ६-१-१९७, with the exception कर्षात्वतो घञोऽन्त उदात्तः, पा. ६-१-१५९) would give an end-acute, but the more special वृषादीनां च (पा. ६-१-२०३) makes it first-syllable acute. "Vājayāmaḥ" — "vājo 'syāstīti vājavān"; "taṃ karoti" ("he makes him that"); "tat karoti tad ācaṣṭe" (तत्करोति तदाचष्टे, पा. ३-१-२६) — the causal "ṇic" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Rik 4.9: grammar concluded; Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

Grammar within the Bhāṣya, concluded the Sanskrit on the top of this page, transcribed as read, with its sūtras; given in outline since it is pure derivation: Reading notes: the sūtra-numbers in this paragraph are read from small numerals and are low-confidence; the sūtra wording "iṣṭhavaṇau prātipadikasya" is hard to read in the print and it is transcribed as it can be made out.

…ṇic | iṣṭhavaṇau prātipadikasya | pā. 6-4-155 [?] | iti tasmin svare iṣṭhavad-bhāvād vinmator luk | pā. 5-3-65 [?] | iti matupo luk | ṭeḥ | pā. 6-4-143 | ity akāra-lopaḥ | ṇic-cit-tvād antodāttatvaṃ śapaḥ pittvenānudāttatvaṃ lasārvadhātuka-svareṇākhyātasyāpy anudāttatvaṃ | pādāditvāt tiṅ atiṅa iti na nighātaḥ | śatakrato | āmantritanighātaḥ | dhanānām | nab-viṣayasyānisantasyety ādyudāttaḥ | sātaye | udātta ity anuvṛttyā ūtiyūti-jūti-sāti-heti-kīrtayaś ceti ktin-nudāttaḥ || (Devanagari: …णिच् । इष्ठेवणौ प्रातिपदिकस्य । पा. ६-४-१५५ [?] । इति तस्मिन्स्वरे इष्ठवद्भावाद्विन्मतोर्लुक् । पा. ५-३-६५ [?] । इति मतुपो लुक् । टेः । पा. ६-४-१४३ । इत्यकारलोपः । णिच्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वं शपः पित्त्वेनानुदात्तत्वं लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणाख्यातस्याप्यनुदात्तत्वं । पादादित्वात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति न निघातः । शतक्रतो । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । धनानाम् । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तः । सातये । उदात्त इत्यनुवृत्त्यादिः ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्चेति क्तिन्नुदात्तः ॥) Translation, in outline: "'Ṇic' … after the 'iṣṭha' and 'vat' affixes (इष्ठेमेयस्सु टेः, पा. ६-४-१५५ etc.) the 'iṣṭhavad-bhāva' treats the stem as if before an 'iṣṭha'-affix, whence the elision of the 'vin'/'matup' (विन्मतोर्लुक्, पा. ५-३-६५ [?]); टेः (पा. ६-४-१४३): the final 'a' of the stem is elided; by the 'c'-mark of 'ṇic' the end-acute; the 'śap' being 'p'-marked is unaccented; by the sārvadhātuka-accent rule the verb is unaccented too; since the word stands at the beginning of the pāda, the 'tiṅ atiṅaḥ' nighāta does not apply. 'Śatakrato' — the vocative's nighāta. 'Dhanānām' — first-syllable acute (नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य). 'Sātaye' — by the continuation of 'udātta' from ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च (पा. ३-३-९७), the 'ktin' is acute." ॥९॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

  1. शतक्रतो (śatakrato) — one who performs many daring deeds, or who is endowed with much wisdom | इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | धनानाम् (dhanānām) — of wealth and other possessions | सातये (sātaye) — for the attainment | वाजेषु (vājeṣu) — in battles | वाजिनम् (vājinam) — who are strong | तम् (tam) — who are endowed with the qualities stated in the earlier mantra | त्वा (tvā) — you | वाजयामः (vājayāmaḥ) — we make endowed with food (we offer to you food in the form of the oblation).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, endowed with wisdom! In order to obtain wealth, cattle, sons and the like, we offer the oblation — that is, food — to you, who are strong — mighty — in battles.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"O Indra performer of many sacrifices (or one endowed with great wisdom), we offer sacrificial food to you who are powerful in battles, for the acquisition of riches."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of the word "vāja" has been explained earlier. वाजयामः (vājayāmaḥ) — For this verb the Bhāṣyakāra gives "annavantaṃ kurmaḥ" — "we make endowed with food"; Skandasvāmī gives "vājayati-r arcayati-karmā, stumaḥ" — "the root 'vājay' has the sense of 'worship'; we praise"; and Veṅkaṭamādhava gives "stutibhir balinaṃ kurmaḥ" — "we make you strong by praises, by hymns of praise."

In explaining the senses of the words "vāja," "śata" and "kratu" in this Ṛk, the Bhāṣyakāra has cited sentences from the Nirukta:

वाजे (vāje) — Among the forty-six words that signify battle, beginning with "raṇa," the word "vāje" is read (Ni. 2-1[?]-1[?]) number illegible.

original p. 128

Special topics on Rik 4.9 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

वाजः (vājaḥ) — Among the twenty-eight words that signify food, beginning with "andha," the word "vājaḥ" is read (Ni. 2-7[?]-4 [?]).

शत (śata) — Among the twelve words that signify "many," beginning with "uru," the word "śatam" is read (Ni. 3-1[?]-1 [?]).

क्रतुः (kratuḥ) — Among the twenty-six words that signify action, beginning with "apaḥ," the word "kratuḥ" is read (Ni. 2-1 [?]); and —

केतः — among the eleven words that signify wisdom, beginning with "ketaḥ," the word "kratuḥ" is read (Ni. 3-1[?]-1[?]).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ - "Tvā" — त्वामौ द्वितीयायाः (tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ, पा. ८-१-२३), with "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ, पा. ८-१-१८) continued — "tvā" and "mā" are substituted, in order, for the second-case singular forms "tvām" and "mām" of "yuṣmad" and "asmad," when the words are unaccented, not at the beginning of a pāda, and stand after another word; so here "tvām" becomes "tvā" and is unaccented. - "Vājeṣu" — "vaja/vraja gatau" (to go), with "ṇic" in the causal sense: "vājayati — gamayati": "that by which the support of the body is accomplished"; i.e. "vāja" is strength, or food; "ghañ" after the root in the sense of instrument (करणे); अत उपधायाः (पा. ७-२-११६) gives vṛddhi of the penultimate; णेरनिटि (पा. ६-४-५१) elides the "ṇi" → "vāja." The "ñit"-accent (ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम्, पा. ६-१-१९७) is set aside by the exception कर्षात्वतो घञोऽन्त उदात्तः (पा. ६-१-१५९) — when the "ghañ" ends a word after "kṛṣ" or a root with "ā," the word is end-acute — and this in turn is set aside by वृषादीनां च (पा. ६-१-२०३), so the word is first-syllable acute. - "Vājayāmaḥ" — "vājo 'syāsti iti vājavān" — "tadasyāstyasminniti matup" (पा. ५-२-९४) and by मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (पा. ८-२-९) the "m" of "matup" becomes "v" after a stem whose penultimate is "m" or "a/ā" (not in the "yava"-class); so "vājavat"; adding "su," अत्वसन्तस्य चाधातोः (पा. ६-४-१४) lengthens the penultimate before the "sarvanāmasthāna" of "atvasanta" stems, and उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः (पा. ७-१-७०) brings "num" → "vājavān-t-s"; हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्सुतिस्यपृक्तं हल् (पा. ६-१-६८) elides "su"; संयोगान्तस्य लोपः (पा. ८-२-२३) elides the "t" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept. Accent-marks not reproduced; see the note at Rik 3.5.

Rik 4.9 grammar concluded; Sūkta 4, Tenth Mantra: Saṃhitā

Continuing "vājayāmaḥ" from p. 128: …by संयोगान्तस्य लोपः (पा. ८-२-२३) the "t" of the conjunct is elided; पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् (पा. ८-२-१) makes the elision "asiddha" with respect to the following rules; so न लोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (पा. ८-२-७) — the elision of the "n" at the end of a stem — does not apply, and one gets "vājavān," the stem "vājavat." "We make him vājavat" — "vājavantaṃ kurmaḥ" ("we make him possessed of food, or of strength") — is intended: "tat karoti tad ācaṣṭe" (तत्करोति तदाचष्टे, पा. ३-१-२६): in the sense "he does that" — and "he declares it" — "ṇic" is added after a second-case word; "vājavat + am + ṇic"; सनाद्यन्ता धातवः (पा. ३-१-३२) — words ending in "sanādi" affixes are called roots; सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः (पा. २-४-७१) — the case-ending "am" is elided. तावुपमेयः — by प्रातिपदिकस्य (print: ज्ञाविष्ठवत्प्रातिपदिकस्य, पा. ६-४-१५५-वा. १ [?]) — "iṣṭhavat" treatment: whatever operations the "iṣṭhan" affix would bring, these also occur when "ṇic" follows; with "iṣṭhan" following, विन्मतोर्लुक् (पा. ५-३-६५ [?]) elides "vin" and "matup" — so by "iṣṭhavat" the "matup" is elided before "ṇic," and टेः (पा. ६-४-१५५) the "a" before the "ṇic" is elided: "vāja + i," then the root "vāji" with "laṭ," first-person plural "mas," कर्तरि शप् (पा. ३-१-६८) "śap" with guṇa and "ay" → "vājay + mas"; अतो दीर्घो यञि (पा. ७-३-१०१) lengthens the "a" before a "yañ"-initial sārvadhātuka → "vājayāmas" → "vājayāmaḥ" (with "ru" and visarga). The "śap" is unaccented by being "p"-marked (अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ, पा. ३-१-४); "mas" is unaccented by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित् (पा. ६-१-१८६) and by अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ (पा. ८-१-१८): the unaccented rule in general does not apply to a word that stands at the beginning of a pāda, by the prohibition, so, since "vājayāmaḥ" is the first word of the second pāda, तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) does not make it unaccented. "Śatakrato" — a vocative, unaccented by आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. ८-१-१९); "dhanānām" — first-syllable acute by the Phiṭ-sūtra नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य; "sātaye" — "udātta" being continued, by ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च (पा. ३-३-९७) the "ktin" affix is acute. ॥९॥

Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; [?] where unclear.

यो रायोऽवनिर्महान्त्सुपारः सुन्वतः सखा । तस्मा इन्द्राय गायत ॥१०॥

yo rāyo 'vanir mahān supāraḥ sunvataḥ sakhā | tasmā indrāya gāyata ||10||

original p. 130

Rik 4.10: Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings (opening)

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यः । रायः । अवनिः । महान् । सुऽपारः । सुन्वतः । सखा । तस्मै । इन्द्राय । गायत ॥१०॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

य इन्द्रो रायो धनस्यावनी रक्षकः स्वामिना वा तस्मा इन्द्राय गायत । हे ऋत्विजस्तृप्त्यर्थं स्तुतिं कुरुत । कीदृश इन्द्रः । महान्गुणैरधिकः सुपारः सुष्ठु कर्मणः पूरयिता सुन्वतो यजमानस्य सखा सखिवत्प्रियः ॥ ya indro rāyo dhanasyāvanī rakṣakaḥ svāminā vā tasmā indrāya gāyata | he ṛtvijas tṛptyartham stutiṃ kurutā | kīdṛśa indraḥ | mahān guṇair adhikaḥ supāraḥ suṣṭhu karmaṇaḥ pūrayitā sunvato yajamānasya sakhā sakhivat priyaḥ || (The print has "kurutā" for "kuruta"; I give it as printed, noting that the sense — "make" — is not affected.)

Translation: "That Indra who is 'rāyaḥ avaniḥ' — the protector of wealth, or its master — to that Indra sing ('gāyata'). O priests, make praise for his satisfaction. What kind of Indra? 'Mahān' — greater by virtues; 'supāraḥ' — he who fulfils the rite well, the completer of the action; 'sunvataḥ sakhā' — the friend of the sacrificer who presses the Soma: dear as a friend."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept): "Rāyaḥ" — the case-ending is acute after "ūṭh," "idam," "pad" and the like (ऊडिदम्पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः, पा. ६-१-१७१); thus the genitive "ḥ" of "rai" ("rāyaḥ") is acute. "Avaniḥ" — "av" (to protect) in the long list of senses beginning "rakṣaṇa-gati-prīti-tṛpti-…" (as in the dhātupāṭha: "to protect, to go, to please, to satisfy, to enter, to hear, to command, to request, to make, to desire, to shine, to obtain, to embrace, to injure, to burn, to grow …"), with the Uṇādi अवितृस्तृतन्त्रिभ्य ईः? [print: अवेरनिः (उ. सू. २-१०४ [as printed "2-1[?]4"])] the affix "ani"; the affix gives the accent. "Supāraḥ" — "pṝ pālana-pūraṇayoḥ" (to protect, to fill): the root with "ṇic"-ending, taken from the "kartari" … "ac" (पचाद्यच्, पा. ३-१-१३४), "c"-marked, so end-acute (चितः, पा. ६-१-१६३). "Sunvataḥ" — शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (पा. ६-१-१७३) — the case-ending after "śatṛ" without "num" is acute when a "nadī" or "ajādi" ending follows. "Sakhā" — समाने ख्यः (as at p. 107) with "iṇ"; the "y" is elided; "sa" is acute. "Tasmai" — अदिरित्यनुवृत्त्या तृजितनियजिभ्यो डित् (उ. सू. १-१४०) the Uṇādi affix "ḍit" after "tan"; "ṭi"-elision (टेः); the affix accent. "Indrāya" — "indra" by "ran" (as before) is first-syllable acute; "karmaṇā yam abhipraiti sa sampradānam" (कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स सम्प्रदानम्, पा. १-४-३२) — the fourth case, since by the statement क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यम् (वा. पा. १-४-३२) the "kriyā" must be understood — "gāna-kriyā" (the act of singing) is the means by which it is reached, so Indra is the recipient (sampradāna) and gets the dative. ॥१०॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(O priests!) यः (yaḥ) — which Indra | रायः (rāyaḥ) — of the giver of riches | अवनिः (avaniḥ) — the protector, or the master | महान् (mahān) — one who is called "great" on account of the superabundance of qualities | सुपारः (supāraḥ) — one who brings the sacrificial and other rites to completion without hindrance | सुन्वतः (sunvataḥ) — (to the sacrificer) who has prepared the Soma-juice for (Indra) | सखा (sakhā) — one who is dear as a friend | तस्मै (tasmai) — such | इन्द्राय (indrāya) — for Indra (addressing Indra) | गायत (gāyata) — sing, with hymns of praise.
