Special topics on Rik 6.1: the classification of mantras by sense (Nirukta 7.1–3)

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The Pada-meanings, the Bhāvārtha and the English rendering of this Ṛk follow Sāyaṇa's Bhāṣya. Sāyaṇa's Bhāṣya follows the exposition given in the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa (of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda). Since the Brāhmaṇa is counted as a part of the Veda, and since it contains very ancient exposition, it must be believed to be the chief authority in the investigation of Vedic meaning. The sage Yāska, the author of the Nirukta, says as follows in regard to explaining Vedic mantras:

तद्यानि नामानि प्राधान्यस्तुतीनां देवतानां तद्दैवतमित्याचक्षते ॥ यत्काम ऋषिर्यस्यां देवतायामार्थपत्यमिच्छन्स्तुतिं प्रयुङ्क्ते तद्दैवतः स मन्त्रो भवति ॥ ताः त्रिविधा ऋचः परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृता आध्यात्मिकाश्च । तत्र परोक्षकृताः सर्वाभिर्नामविभक्तिभिर्युज्यन्ते प्रथमपुरुषैश्चाख्यातस्य ॥ अथ प्रत्यक्षकृता मध्यमपुरुषयोगास्त्वमिति चैतेन सर्वनाम्ना ॥ अथाध्यात्मिकाः उत्तमपुरुषयोगा अहमिति चैतेन सर्वनाम्ना ॥ परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृताश्च मन्त्रा भूयिष्ठा अल्पश आध्यात्मिकाः ॥ (निरुक्त—दैवतकाण्ड. अध्याय ७-खण्ड १–३) tad yāni nāmāni prādhānya-stutīnāṃ devatānāṃ tad daivatam ity ācakṣate || yat-kāma ṛṣir yasyāṃ devatāyām ārthapatyam icchan stutiṃ prayuṅkte tad-daivataḥ sa mantro bhavati || tās trividhā ṛcaḥ parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtā ādhyātmikāś ca | tatra parokṣakṛtāḥ sarvābhir nāma-vibhaktibhir yujyante prathama-puruṣaiś cākhyātasya || atha pratyakṣakṛtā madhyama-puruṣa-yogās tvam iti caitena sarvanāmnā || athādhyātmikāḥ uttama-puruṣa-yogā aham iti caitena sarvanāmnā || parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtāś ca mantrā bhūyiṣṭhā alpaśa ādhyātmikāḥ || (nirukta — daivata-kāṇḍa, adhyāya 7, khaṇḍa 1–3) (Reading note: the opening clause is printed "tad yāni nāmāni prādhānya-stutīnāṃ devatānāṃ" and I give it so; the "yat-kāma ṛṣir yasyāṃ devatāyām ārthapatyam icchan" clause is as printed. The adverb "alpaśaḥ" is printed "alpaśa.")

Translation:Mine, following the Kannada account below. "'Those names of the deities who are praised chiefly (as the subject of a hymn) — of that (hymn) they say "its deity is so-and-so." Whatever the desire with which a seer, wishing for lordship (of that thing), addresses praise to a deity — that mantra has that deity. Those Ṛks are of three kinds: parokṣa-kṛta (made in the indirect form), pratyakṣa-kṛta (made in the direct form), and ādhyātmika (made in the personal form). Of these, the parokṣa-kṛta are joined with all the case-forms of the noun and with the third person of the verb. Then the pratyakṣa-kṛta are joined with the second person, and with the pronoun "tvam" (thou). Then the ādhyātmika are joined with the first person, and with the pronoun "aham" (I). The parokṣa-kṛta and the pratyakṣa-kṛta mantras are the most numerous; the ādhyātmika are few.'"

That is: among mantras there are many kinds — daivata-mantra, stuti-mantra, āśīr-mantra, śapatha, abhiśāpa, kaścid-bhāva, paridevanā, nindā, praśaṃsā, and so on. A "daivata-mantra" is a mantra that describes the greatness of the gods; "stuti" is a mantra that contains stotra and entreaties; "āśīḥ" is a mantra that gives a blessing — one that wishes the good of another; "śapatha" is a vow, a promise; "abhiśāpa" is a curse — wishing another harm; "kaścid-bhāva" is the description of a certain matter or of a truth; "paridevanā" is lamentation, distress; "nindā" is blame; "praśaṃsā" is praise; "dānastuti" is the praise of gifts; and so on.

Of the many kinds of mantras mentioned above, the Ṛks called "daivata" are of three kinds: parokṣa-kṛta, pratyakṣa-kṛta and ādhyātmika. A "parokṣa-kṛta" mantra is one in which the deity who is praised is not present before one — so that the praise is made in the form in which the third-person nouns and the third-person verbs are used with reference to that deity ("third person both in subject and predicate" — English as printed). A "pratyakṣa-kṛta" mantra is one in which the deity is imagined as standing visibly before one, and is praised by addressing him, using the second-person words "you," "your" and so on ("second person" — English as printed). An "ādhyātmika" mantra is one in which praise is made by using the first person ("first person" — English as printed). Of these three kinds of mantras, the two — parokṣa-kṛta and pratyakṣa-kṛta — are more numerous; the ādhyātmika mantras are only few. The Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa exposition of Rik 6.1; Skandasvāmī's commentary (opening)

The Ṛk "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam," which is relevant here, ought by the above (classification) to belong to the group "parokṣa-kṛta" among daivata mantras. But since the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa explains this Ṛk with an adhyātmika meaning, the Bhāṣyakāra has explained it in accordance with that. In that Brāhmaṇa, in giving the exposition of this Ṛk, it is said:

युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमित्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो ब्रध्नः । आदित्यमेवास्मै युनक्ति । अरुषमित्याह । अग्निर्वा अरुषः । अग्निमेवास्मै युनक्ति । चरन्तमित्याह । वायुर्वै चरन् । वायुमेवास्मै युनक्ति । परि तस्थुष इत्याह । इमे वै लोकाः परि तस्थुषः । इमानेवास्मै लोकान् युनक्ति । रोचन्ते रोचना दिवीत्याह । नक्षत्राणि वै रोचना दिवि । नक्षत्राण्येवास्मै रोचयति ॥ (तै. ब्रा. ३-९-४ [?]) yuñjanti bradhnam ity āha | asau vā ādityo bradhnaḥ | ādityam evāsmai yunakti | aruṣam ity āha | agnir vā aruṣaḥ | agnim evāsmai yunakti | carantam ity āha | vāyur vai caran | vāyum evāsmai yunakti | pari tasthuṣa ity āha | ime vai lokāḥ pari tasthuṣaḥ | imān evāsmai lokān yunakti | rocante rocanā divīty āha | nakṣatrāṇi vai rocanā divi | nakṣatrāṇy evāsmai rocayati || (tai. brā. 3-9-4 [?]) Translation: "'Yuñjanti bradhnam,' he says: yonder Sun is 'bradhna'; he yokes the Sun to him. 'Aruṣam,' he says: Agni is 'aruṣa'; he yokes Agni to him. 'Carantam,' he says: Vāyu is the 'moving'; he yokes Vāyu to him. 'Pari tasthuṣaḥ,' he says: these worlds are 'pari tasthuṣaḥ'; he yokes these worlds to him. 'Rocante rocanā divi,' he says: the stars are the 'rocanā' in the sky; he makes the stars shine for him." (This is the same passage that Sāyaṇa abridged on pp. 203–204.)

That is, in this the sense is given, in an adhyātmika connection, that "bradhna" = the Sun, "aruṣa" = Agni, "carat" = Vāyu, "pari tasthuṣaḥ" = the three worlds, "rocanā" = the stars. Although we need not accept this meaning as authoritative, there is no refutation here of the meanings that other commentators give for this Ṛk. Since Skandasvāmī has explained this Ṛk in a different way, we give it here.

Skandasvāmī's commentary (Sanskrit, printed in Kannada script; first part, p. 206): Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; [?] marks every place where letters are crowded or doubtful. The Brāhmaṇa-style argument at the foot of the page is very compressed; The Sanskrit is given as read, with a translation in outline, saying where the sense is uncertain.

योगः संबन्धः । युञ्जन्ति संबन्धयन्ति । केन, सामर्थ्यात् स्तुतिभिर्हविर्भिश्च । के, सामर्थ्यात् स्तोतारो यष्टारश्च । ब्रध्नं महन्नामैतत् । महान्तमिन्द्रम् । अरुषं रुशतिर्दीप्त्यर्थः । रुशद्वत्सारुशतीति प्रदर्शनात् । तस्य वा रोचतेर्वा दीप्तिकर्मण आज्पूर्वस्येदं रूपम् । आजश्च ह्रस्वत्वम् । अरुरं आरोचमानं वा दीप्तमित्यर्थः । आरुषत्यायतीति गतिकर्मसु पाठादृषतेर्गत्यर्थस्यारुषशब्दो गन्तृवचनः । शत्रून् यज्ञान् वा प्रतिगन्तारम् । चरन्तं परि सर्वतो गच्छन्तम् । यत्र यत्रेन्द्रो गच्छति तत्र तत्रैनं स्तोतारो यष्टारश्च स्तुवन्ति चेत्यर्थः । अथवा, युञ्जन्तीति युजिः शुद्धोऽपि सामर्थ्यात् सोपसर्गार्थे प्रष्टव्यः । स्वार्थसिद्धौ स्तोतारो यष्टारश्चैनं नियुञ्जते । महान्तं दीप्तं चेन्द्रं सर्वतो गच्छन्तं, यत्र यत्र गच्छति कश्च तत्रैनं मनुष्या इदमिदं च नः कुर्विन्त्यर्थं याचन्त इत्यर्थः । रथोऽत्र सामर्थ्यात् युज्यमानः नेन्द्रं युञ्जन्ति । इन्द्रस्य रथं ब्रध्नमरुषं yogaḥ sambandhaḥ | yuñjanti sambandhayanti | kena, sāmarthyāt stutibhir havirbhiś ca | ke, sāmarthyāt stotāro yaṣṭāraś ca | bradhnaṃ mahan-nāmaitat | mahāntam indram | aruṣaṃ ruśatir dīptyarthaḥ | ruśadvatsāruśatīti pradarśanāt | tasya vā rocater vā dīpti-karmaṇa āj-pūrvasyedaṃ rūpam | ājaś ca hrasvatvam | aruraṃ ārocamānaṃ vā dīptam ity arthaḥ | āruṣatyāyatīti gati-karmasu pāṭhād ṛṣater gatyarthasyāruṣa-śabdo gantṛ-vacanaḥ | śatrūn yajñān vā pratigantāram | carantaṃ pari sarvato gacchantam | yatra yatrendro gacchati tatra tatrainaṃ stotāro yaṣṭāraś ca stuvanti cety arthaḥ | athavā, yuñjantīti yujiḥ śuddho 'pi sāmarthyāt sopasargārthe praṣṭavyaḥ | svārtha-siddhau stotāro yaṣṭāraś cainaṃ niyuñjate | mahāntaṃ dīptaṃ cendraṃ sarvato gacchantaṃ, yatra yatra gacchati kaś ca tatrainaṃ manuṣyā idam idaṃ ca naḥ kurv ity arthaṃ yācanta ity arthaḥ | ratho 'tra sāmarthyāt yujyamānaḥ nendraṃ yuñjanti | indrasya rathaṃ bradhnam aruṣaṃ … (Reading notes: (i) this stretch is dense and several of its words are crowded in the print — the clauses "ruśadvatsāruśatīti pradarśanāt," "āj-pūrvasyedaṃ rūpam," "kaś ca tatrainaṃ" and "nendraṃ yuñjanti" are as I read them, flagged [?], and I translate only what I can support; (ii) the sentence ends at the foot of the page and continues on p. 207.) Translation, in outline (what I can support): "'Yoga' is connection. 'Yuñjanti' — they connect; by what? — by capacity, with praises and with oblations; who? — by capacity, the praisers and the sacrificers. 'Bradhna' is a name of the 'great' — the great Indra. 'Aruṣam' — the root 'ruś' is in the sense of shining; … [the grammatical explanation of 'aruṣa' as 'shining,' or as 'one who goes' from the root 'ṛṣ' in the list of roots of motion — hence 'aruṣa' is 'one who goes' — 'one who goes against enemies or to sacrifices']. 'Carantam' — going all around, in every direction: wherever Indra goes, there the praisers and the sacrificers praise him. Or: 'yuñjanti,' though the plain root 'yuj,' is by capacity to be understood in the sense of a prefixed verb ('niyuñjate'): the praisers and sacrificers 'engage' him for the accomplishing of their own aims; Indra, great and shining and going in all directions — wherever he goes, there men beg of him, 'do this and that for us.' … [the remainder — on the chariot — is garbled in the print and I do not translate it]."

Skandasvāmī's commentary (concluded)

…च सर्वतो गच्छन्तम् । के, सामर्थ्यात् सारथयो मातलिप्रभृतयः । अन्येऽस्य रथं युञ्जन्ति । स नः स्वयं युनक्ति ब्रध्नादिगुणः युञ्जन्ति न किंचिदिति । एवं गुणकीर्तनादिन्द्रस्यैयं स्तुतिः । किंच तस्थुषः रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि । तस्थुष इति षष्ठीनिर्देशात् प्रभावेनेति वाक्यशेषः । स्थितस्य व्याप्रियमाणेन्द्रस्य प्रभावेन रोचन्ते दीप्यन्ते । रोचना दीप्तिस्वभावकानि नक्षत्राणि दिवि द्युलोके । कथंपुनरिन्द्रप्रभावेन नक्षत्राणि दीप्यन्ते । उच्यते । वक्ष्यते — "इन्द्रो दीर्घाय चक्षस आ सूर्यं रोहयद्दिवि" इति । सूर्यस्य प्रभावश्च सुषुम्नो नाम रश्मिः तत्संबन्धाच्चन्द्रमा नक्षत्राणि च दीप्यन्ते । अथवा युजिरुत्पूर्वार्थे । अन्तर्णीतण्यर्थश्च प्रष्टव्यः । उद्योजयन्त्युत्साजयन्ति वृष्टिकर्माणि ब्रध्नमरुषं चेन्द्रम् । किं कुर्वन्तम् । उच्यते । चरन्तं परि तस्थुषः । परिशब्दो लक्षणे कर्मप्रवचनीयः तस्थुष इत्यनेन च संबध्यते । तस्थिवःशब्दः स्थावरवचनः । गच्छन्तं स्थावराणि प्रति । स्थावरग्रहणं चात्र जङ्गमस्यापि प्रदर्शनार्थम् । सोमपानायासुरयुवल्लोलुपतयो जङ्गमस्थावरात्मकं कृत्स्नं (जनम्, जगत्) परिभ्रमन्तमित्यर्थः । के उद्योजयन्ति । उच्यते । रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि । एकवाक्यताप्रसिद्ध्यर्थं यत्रच्चब्दावध्याहार्यौ । आदित्यरश्मयो रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि ते आदित्यरश्मयो हि प्रावृडारम्भे रसादातारः । ते रसानर्पयन्तः उद्योजयन्तीन्द्रं वृष्टिकर्मणि । एतस्मिन्नर्थे रश्मिविषयत्वात् रोचनेत्येतत् पदमूष्मान्तन्यायं दृश्यते न स्वरान्तमन्तो नैष पदकाराभिप्रायः । ज्योतिष्पेक्षं वा रश्मीनां नपुंसकत्वम् । अध्वर्युवस्त्वादित्यदेवताम्ऋचं मन्यन्ते । कथम् । एतेषां हि विनियोजनेऽसियुक्तश्चाश्लोऽसनयो… [garbled] । श्रुतेः । एवं हि श्रुतिर्भवति — युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमरुषमित्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो ब्रध्नः । अरुषोऽमुमेवास्मादादित्यं युनक्ति । सुवर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै इति । तस्मादादित्यदेवत्येयमिति । तन्न । तत्रापि विनियोगवशान्नियुज्यमानोऽश्लो ब्रध्नोऽरुषश्चोच्यते । भक्तिमात्रं तु श्रुतिः । अपि च यदि श्रुतिबलात् तत्रादित्यो देवता, तथा नामु इह त्वैन्द्रप्रकरणे समाना ब्रध्नारुषयोश्चेन्द्रेऽपि संभवात् । परस्यां च ऋचः शब्दैनानुवादात् । तेनेहादिष्वस्य ब्रध्नस्यान्नादेशात् तस्याश्च ऋचो हरिसंबन्धाद्यैन्द्रतायाः असंदिग्धत्वाद् ऐन्द्रत्वमेवास्या ऋच इति ॥ …ca sarvato gacchantam | ke, sāmarthyāt sārathayo mātali-prabhṛtayaḥ | anye 'sya rathaṃ yuñjanti | sa naḥ svayaṃ yunakti bradhnādi-guṇaḥ yuñjanti na kiñcid iti | evaṃ guṇa-kīrtanād indrasyeyaṃ stutiḥ | kiṃca tasthuṣaḥ rocante rocanā divi | tasthuṣa iti ṣaṣṭhī-nirdeśāt prabhāveneti vākya-śeṣaḥ | sthitasya vyāpriyamāṇendrasya prabhāvena rocante dīpyante | rocanā dīpti-svabhāvakāni nakṣatrāṇi divi dyuloke | kathaṃ punar indra-prabhāvena nakṣatrāṇi dīpyante | ucyate | vakṣyate — "indro dīrghāya cakṣasa ā sūryaṃ rohayad divi" iti | sūryasya prabhāvaś ca suṣumno nāma raśmiḥ tat-sambandhāc candramā nakṣatrāṇi ca dīpyante | athavā yujir ut-pūrvārthe | antarṇīta-ṇyarthaś ca praṣṭavyaḥ | udyojayanty utsājayanti vṛṣṭi-karmāṇi bradhnam aruṣaṃ cendram | kiṃ kurvantam | ucyate | carantaṃ pari tasthuṣaḥ | pari-śabdo lakṣaṇe karma-pravacanīyaḥ tasthuṣa ity anena ca sambadhyate | tasthivaḥ-śabdaḥ sthāvara-vacanaḥ | gacchantaṃ sthāvarāṇi prati | sthāvara-grahaṇaṃ cātra jaṅgamasyāpi pradarśanārtham | somapānāyāsura-yuva-llolupatayo jaṅgama-sthāvarātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ (janam, jagat) paribhramantam ity arthaḥ | ke udyojayanti | ucyate | rocante rocanā divi | ekavākyatā-prasiddhy-arthaṃ yat-tac-chabdāv adhyāhāryau | ādityaraśmayo rocante rocanā divi te ādityaraśmayo hi prāvṛḍārambhe rasādātāraḥ | te rasān arpayantaḥ udyojayantīndraṃ vṛṣṭi-karmaṇi | etasminn arthe raśmi-viṣayatvāt rocaneti etat padam ūṣmānta-nyāyaṃ dṛśyate na svarāntam anto naiṣa padakārābhiprāyaḥ | jyotiṣpekṣaṃ vā raśmīnāṃ napuṃsakatvam | adhvaryu-vastv-āditya-devatām ṛcaṃ manyante | katham | eteṣāṃ hi viniyojane … [garbled] | śruteḥ | evaṃ hi śrutir bhavati — yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam ity āha | asau vā ādityo bradhnaḥ | aruṣo 'mum evāsmādādityaṃ yunakti | suvargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai iti | tasmād āditya-devatyeyam iti | tan na | tatrāpi viniyoga-vaśān niyujyamāno 'śvo bradhno 'ruṣaś cocyate | bhakti-mātraṃ tu śrutiḥ | api ca yadi śruti-balāt tatrāditya devatā, tathā nāmu iha tv aindra-prakaraṇe samānā bradhnāruṣayoś cendre 'pi sambhavāt | parasyāṃ ca ṛcaḥ śabdenānuvādāt | teneha ādiṣv asya bradhnasyānnādeśāt tasyāś ca ṛco hari-sambandhād aindratāyā asandigdhatvād aindratvam evāsyā ṛca iti || (Reading notes: (i) the first words "ca sarvato gacchantam" continue the sentence broken at the foot of p. 206; (ii) the clause I mark "[garbled]" — "eteṣāṃ hi viniyojane … " — is crowded and I do not reproduce it; (iii) the readings "ūṣmānta-nyāyam," "tasthivaḥ-śabdaḥ," "adhvaryu-vastv-āditya-devatām ṛcam," and the final run from "tan na" to "aindratvam eva" are as I read them, with the word-divisions mine, and the whole last passage should be re-checked against the page image; (iv) I translate in outline.) Translation, in outline: "…and going in every direction. Who (engages him)? By capacity, charioteers such as Mātali; others yoke his chariot; 'he himself yokes us' — one endowed with 'bradhna' and other qualities; they yoke nothing (else) (?). Thus this is praise of Indra by the proclaiming of his qualities. Further: 'tasthuṣaḥ rocante rocanā divi' — by the genitive 'tasthuṣaḥ' the supplied word is 'by the power': by the power of Indra, who is stationed and active, 'rocante' — shine; 'rocanā' — the stars, whose nature is shining, 'divi' — in heaven. How, then, do the stars shine by Indra's power? It will be said: 'Indra made the Sun rise in heaven for long sight' (a quotation, as printed). The Sun's power is the ray called Suṣumna, and by connection with it the Moon and stars shine. Or else the root 'yuj' has the sense 'ut-' ('up'): it must be understood with the causal sense included — 'they urge up, they stir up Indra, great and ruddy, to the rain-work.' Doing what? 'Carantam pari tasthuṣaḥ' — 'pari' is a karmapravacanīya in the sense of 'around' and is connected with 'tasthuṣaḥ' — the word means 'the stationary': going toward the stationary; the mention of the stationary here is also to show the moving ones: moving around the whole world (people, creatures), moving, out of eagerness for the Soma-drinking. Who stir him up? — 'rocante rocanā divi': for the unity of the sentence 'yat' and 'tat' must be supplied: the Sun's rays shine in heaven; those rays, at the beginning of the rainy season, take up the juices; offering those juices, they stir Indra to the rain-work. (Grammatical remarks on the neuter 'rocanā' follow.) … Then the Adhvaryu-priests regard the Ṛk as addressed to the Sun (?). — [Objection:] 'For in the application of these (mantras) …' — by Śruti: '"Yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam," it says: yonder Sun is "bradhna"; he yokes that very Sun for him, for the sake of the whole of the world of heaven (suvarga)'; therefore this Ṛk has the Sun as its deity. — [Reply:] No. There too, by force of the application, the horse that is being yoked is called 'bradhna' and 'aruṣa'; the Śruti is only a figurative statement (bhakti-mātra). Moreover, even if the Sun were the deity by force of Śruti, here, in the context of Indra, 'bradhna' and 'aruṣa' are equally possible of Indra, and the next Ṛk repeats the sense; therefore, by the use of 'bradhna' and 'aruṇa' as designations of the horses and by the connection of this Ṛk with 'hari' (the two bay horses), its being Aindrī is unquestioned: this Ṛk is addressed to Indra alone."

Source note on this long argument: Skandasvāmī's chief point is that Rik 6.1 has Indra, not the Sun, as its deity; his chief ground is the connection of "bradhna" and "aruṣa" with Indra's horses and with the "harī" of the next Ṛk. The details of the Mīmāṃsā-style reasoning are given above only in outline; the Sanskrit is preserved in full for checking. Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." original p. 208

Anuvāda of Skandasvāmī's commentary; Western and other views (opening)

Anuvāda of Skandasvāmī's commentary, in Kannada: "Yoga" means connection. So the sense is that it supplies a connection for the verb "yuñjanti." How is there a connection between Indra and the people? One must understand that, because the people satisfy Indra with stotras and oblations, there is a relation between Indra and the people who praise him, or who worship him in sacrifices and the like. For the word "bradhna," meaning "mahat" (great, large), "bradhna" is read among the words that give the sense of "wished-for objects" ("iṣṭa-prāpti"-type words, Ni. 3-[?]). So if "bradhnam" is taken as a qualifier of Indra, "bradhnam indram" means "the great Indra, endowed with great capacity." "Aruṣam" is also a qualifier of Indra. The root "ruś" has the sense of shining, of lustre; so "aruṣam" means "one who shines." In the Ṛk

रुशद्वत्सा रुशती श्वेत्यागादारैगु कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११३-२ [?]) ruśadvatsā ruśatī śvety āgād āraigu kṛṣṇā sadanāny asyāḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-113-2 [?]) (Reading note: the second half of the line is printed "āraigu" and I cannot settle it; I give it as printed, [?].) Gloss (mine; tentative): "The bright one, with her calf, the shining white one, has come; the dark one has left her abodes." — and the Kannada notes: here the word "ruśat" is plainly said to mean shining, lustre. (Sāyaṇa too gives this meaning for "ruśat" in this Ṛk.)

Besides, according to the statement "āruṣatyāyatīti gati-karmasu pāṭhād ṛṣater gatyarthasyāruṣa-śabdo gantṛ-vacanaḥ" (आरुषत्यायतीति गतिकर्मसु पाठादृषतेर्गत्यर्थस्यारुषशब्दो गन्तृवचनः — "because 'āruṣati' is read among the verbs of motion, the word 'āruṣa,' from the root 'ṛṣ' in the sense of going, means 'one who goes'"), from the root "āruṣati," which has the sense of going, "aruṣam" means "gantāram" — one who goes (whether to war with enemies, or to receive the oblations in sacrifices). "Carantam" — one who goes to all regions. The sense: wherever Indra goes, there those who praise him go and worship him. Or: "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣaṃ carantam" — wherever the powerful and shining Indra goes, there men pray to him with stotras that their own desired aims be fulfilled.

Or: the words "bradhnam aruṣaṃ carantam" need not be used as qualifiers of Indra. These words may be taken, with the senses "large, shining, moving everywhere," as qualifiers of the chariot. Since "yuñjanti" is said here, one may say that Indra's charioteers, such as Mātali, "yuñjanti" — "harness" (the horses to) — such a chariot. Therefore the whole discussion in this connection takes the form of praise of Indra. Since the genitive "tasthuṣaḥ" is used, one must supply after it the word "prabhāvena" ("by the power"). Having supplied it, "pari tasthuṣaḥ prabhāveṇa rocante rocanā divi" means: the rays of the Sun, shining in the sky, carrying drops of water in the rainy season, urge Indra, so that rain is produced on earth — that is, they stir him to action. That is: "the stars that shine by the power of Indra, who pervades all regions — 'rocanā,' the stars, in 'divi,' the sky — 'rocante' — shine," is the sense. How the stars shine by Indra's power is confirmed by the mantra "indro dīrghāya cakṣase ā sūryaṃ rohayad divi" (इन्द्रो दीर्घाय चक्षस आ सूर्यं रोहयद्दिवि — indro dīrghāya cakṣasa ā sūryaṃ rohayad divi; ṛ. saṃ. 1-7-3 [as printed "1-?-3"]), "Indra caused the Sun to rise in the sky for far-seeing." Others explain: Indra placed the Sun in the heavenly region (the sky) so that the world might be lit at all times. By connection with the ray named Suṣumna, which is a power of the Sun, the Moon and the stars also … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose, translated; references in small Kannada numerals are marked [?]. Veṅkaṭamādhava's Sanskrit is read from an enlarged slice and flagged.

original p. 209

Anuvāda concluded: Skandasvāmī vs. the Brāhmaṇa; Veṅkaṭamādhava's view; where the Ṛk occurs; the question of the sūkta's deity

Continuing from p. 208: …the stars also shine, or these rays "yuñjanti" Indra in the rain-work — that is, they stimulate him. How? The word "tasthuṣaḥ" in "carantaṃ pari tasthuṣaḥ" indicates the fixed beings, and also the moving beings; so the sense is that Indra moves among the whole world, fixed and moving, for the drinking of Soma or for fighting.

In the sacrifice, the Adhvaryu and some other priests who carry the chief role regard this Ṛk as addressed to the Sun, for the following reasons. In regard to the application of this Ṛk, the Śruti sentence (of the Brāhmaṇa) — "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam ity āha | asau vā ādityo bradhnaḥ | aruṣo 'mum evāsmād ādityaṃ yunakti suvargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai" (युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमरुषमित्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो ब्रध्नः । अरुषोऽमुमेवास्मादादित्यं युनक्ति सुवर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै — "'yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam,' he says: yonder Sun is 'bradhna'; … [he yokes the Sun to him] for the totality of the heavenly world") — says it. Since "bradhna" is plainly said here to mean the Sun, and since the word "Indra" is not found in this Ṛk, a doubt arises, quite naturally, in the question whether this Ṛk is addressed to the Sun. But that is not right. Because "bradhna" also means "horse" (Ni. 1-[?]-[?]). Hence for the sentence "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣaṃ carantam" the sense "they harness the shining, swiftly moving horses (to the chariot)" fits equally of the Sun and of Indra; it does not follow that it is spoken of the Sun alone. Besides, in the next Ṛk of this sūkta the word "harī," the name of Indra's horses, is plainly given, and in the fifth Ṛk the word "Indra" is read; so this mantra must be understood as addressed to Indra.

Further, in Veṅkaṭamādhava's commentary there is not much that is special; he says only:

युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नम् । युञ्जन्ति महान्तमरोचमानं दिवि चरन्तं तस्थिवांसो देवा वा लोका वा । रोचनानि नक्षत्राणि इन्द्रतेजसा संधुक्षितान्यहत्वेऽपि प्रसारणमन्यत्रापि दृष्टम् ॥ yuñjanti bradhnam | yuñjanti mahāntam arocamānaṃ divi carantaṃ tasthivāṃso devā vā lokā vā | rocanāni nakṣatrāṇi indra-tejasā sandhukṣitāny ahatve 'pi prasāraṇam anyatrāpi dṛṣṭam || (Reading note: this Sanskrit is compressed and its end is crowded; the clause "ahatve 'pi prasāraṇam anyatrāpi dṛṣṭam" is as I read it and I mark it [?]; the Kannada explains it as a remark on the form "tasthivāṃsaḥ.") Translation (mine, following the Kannada account): "'Yuñjanti bradhnam': the gods — or the worlds — standing about 'join' the great, (shining), moving in the sky; the 'rocanāni' are the stars, kindled by Indra's lustre. (The lengthening ['prasāraṇa'] in the word 'tasthivāṃsaḥ' is seen elsewhere also.)"

That is: Veṅkaṭamādhava has only repeated Skandasvāmī's meaning. "Tasthivāṃsaḥ" means the gods or the worlds, and "rocanā" the stars. Besides, he says: "Not only that the daytime is lit by Indra's lustre, but that lustre (or capacity, power) is spread everywhere."

Where the Ṛk occurs. The Ṛk "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam" is found not only in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā but also in: Sāmaveda Saṃhitā (1-[?]-[?]); Atharvaveda Saṃhitā 20-26-4 [?], 20-42-10 [?], 20-68-6 [?]; Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā (Śukla Yajurveda) 23-5 [?]; Taittirīya-saṃhitā (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) 2-4-10-1 [?]; Maitrāyaṇīya-saṃhitā 3-16-3 [?]; Kauṣītaki-āraṇyaka 4-6 [?] — all these references are small Kannada numerals, read with doubt, and given as best readings — and in Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa 2-8-4 [?] there is an exposition of the meaning of this mantra and of the two mantras that follow it.

The question of the sūkta's deity. There is a dispute as to the deity of this sūkta. For it is more favourable to firm interpretation if one says that the sūkta was spoken in view of one such deity … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." original p. 210

The deity of Sūkta 6 debated (Oldenburg); Dr. Sitanath Pradhan's and Max Müller's renderings; Pada-meanings

Continuing the question of the sūkta's deity: In the Anukramaṇī it is said that the first three Ṛks and the tenth Ṛk of this sūkta are addressed to the deity Indra; that the 4th, 6th, 8th and 9th [?] are addressed to the Maruts; and that the 5th and 7th Ṛks are addressed to both deities, Indra and the Maruts. But the German scholar Oldenburg holds that when one considers the matters presented in the sūkta, it is not the Maruts but the Aṅgirases who are presented in place of the Maruts; and since "Aṅgiras" is also a name of Indra, there is no subject of the Maruts in this sūkta. Moreover, there is room for the statement that a large part of this sūkta is in praise of the Sun. Even among the ancient scholars there were different views about the deities presented in this sūkta.

Since this sūkta does not present any definite sacrifice or rite, Dr. Sitanath Pradhan states the chief intention shown in this sūkta in this way (English as printed in the source):

"It is the twilight of the early dawn; the stars are still shining. The singers yoke the sun-horse and at the same time Indra's two horses; It is the same sun who was born (at the time after the bursting open of the rock with the dawns. The patriarchs, Angirases have since regularised the sun-rise and sun-set; they who had then found out the concealed cows with the help of Indra and had then invoked Indra may the sun now appear with Indra! Indra joins in the song of the host of the devout singers. Thence come hither o wanderer; or from the bright realm of heaven. For him do our eulogies combinedly strive. We pray to Indra, for reward from here or from heaven, from the earthy or from the aerial region."

Max Müller explains the meaning of this Ṛk as follows (English as printed):

"Those who stand around him while he moves on, harness the bright red (steed); the lights in heaven shine forth."

The Kannada adds that this rendering follows the original without the slightest departure.

According to this, we explain the Pada-meaning and the Bhāvārtha in Kannada:

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

परि तस्थुषः (pari tasthuṣaḥ) — the people who stand all around | अरुषम् (aruṣam) — shining (English as printed: "spirited") | चरन्तम् (carantam) — one with swift movement | ब्रध्नम् (bradhnam) — a horse | युञ्जन्ति (yuñjanti) — they harness (to the chariot) | (तस्मिन् काले) रोचना (rocanā) — the stars, or the rays of the Sun | दिवि (divi) — in the sky | रोचन्ते (rocante) — shine. Bhāvārtha; the chariot of the Sun or of Indra; the deities of the Ṛks; Aṅgiras and Paṇi

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Since the Sun has just risen, his rays spread through the whole sky and shine. At this time the people who stand all around harness to the chariot the shining, strong, swift-moving horse. Since the light has just begun, the stars are still shining.

Here the doubt arises whether "ratha" (chariot) means the Sun's chariot or Indra's. Indra's chariot must have two horses. The Sun's chariot must have seven horses. But since it is said "eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā" (एको अश्वो वहति सप्तनामा — eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā; ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-2 [?]) — "one horse, of seven names, carries" — it is right to say even one horse. And the second Ṛk plainly gives the name "harī," that of Indra's two horses. For these reasons we must believe what is said in the Anukramaṇī to be authoritative.

Now we shall consider the matter that sets forth the deities of the Ṛks 4, 6, 8 and 9 [?]: In the fifth Ṛk — "vīḷu cid ārujatnubhir guhā cid indra vahnibhiḥ | avinda usriyā anu" — it is said that the demons called Paṇi carried off the cows from the world of the gods and hid them in a cave that no one could know; and that Indra, with the help of those capable of destroying the stronghold (the Maruts or the Aṅgirases), searched for them and brought them back. Here "those who are capable" — the ancient commentators such as Sāyaṇa, Skandasvāmī and Veṅkaṭamādhava say, are the "Maruts." But modern Western scholars such as Max Müller and Macdonell hold that the word "ārujatnubhiḥ" refers to the Aṅgirases; because —

वीळु चिद्दृळ्हा पितरो न उक्थैरद्रिं रुजन्नङ्गिरसो रवेण । चक्रुर्दिवो बृहतो गातुमस्मे अहः स्वर्विविदुः केतुमुस्राः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-७१-२ [?]) vīḷu cid dṛḷhā pitaro na ukthair adriṃ rujann aṅgiraso raveṇa | cakrur divo bṛhato gātum asme ahaḥ svar vividuḥ ketum usrāḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-?1-2 [?]) Gloss (mine; tentative): "Our fathers, by their hymns, the Aṅgirases, breaking the firm, the rock, with their cry — they made for us a path of the great heaven; they found the day, the light, the banner, the cows." (The digits of the reference are small and I give "1-?1-2 [?]" in the IAST line, and the form "1-71-2" only as my best reading in the Devanagari line.)

in this Ṛk and in some other places it is said that the Aṅgirases helped Indra in seizing the demon called Paṇi; so they think that the Ṛks of this sūkta have been spoken in view of the Aṅgirases. Moreover, the German scholar Oldenburg is of the opinion that in all the Ṛks of this sūkta that are connected with the Maruts the meaning concerning the Aṅgirases is quite natural. Thus this matter, too, is one that has to be called disputed. Page headers: p. 212 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6"; p. 213 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." These two pages are pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose for "yuñjanti," "bradhnam," "aruṣam," "carantam," "tasthuṣaḥ," "rocante," "rocanā" and "divi"; they do not bear on the sense of Rik 6.1 (pp. 203–204 and the commentary after them). Characterized in outline; sūtras kept; numbers as read, [?] where uncertain. Accent-marks not reproduced.

original pp. 212–213

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.1 (Kannada) — characterized; Sūkta 6, Second Mantra: Saṃhitā

p. 212. "Yuñjanti" — the root "yujir yoge" (to join): the third-person plural "laṭ," "jhi" → "ant"; because it is a "rudhādi" root (रुधादिभ्यः श्नम्, पा. ३-१-७८) the vikaraṇa "śnam" comes in place of "śap"; the "m" of "śnam" is an "it" and, as an "mit" augment, it is placed after the last vowel of the stem (मिदचोऽन्त्यात्परः, पा. १-१-४७) — so "yu-na-j"; झोऽन्तः (पा. ७-१-३) and श्नसोरल्लोपः (पा. ६-४-१११) elide the "a" of "śnam" before a "ñit/ṅit" sārvadhātuka; नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि (पा. ८-३-२४) puts anusvāra for "n" before a "jhal" letter; अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः (पा. ८-४-५८) the "parasavarṇa" nasal: "yuñjanti." The accent: the "śnam" and the personal ending are unaccented, and only the first syllable is acute (आद्युदात्तश्च, पा. ३-१-३). "Bradhnam" — end-acute by the accent of the bare stem (prātipadika). "Aruṣam" — "ṛṣ/ruṣa/riṣa" (roots of injuring): "ruṣā" are the destroyers; the affix "ka" (इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः, पा. ३-१-१३५); the affix's acute; "na santi ruṣā yasya saḥ" — a bahuvrīhi; नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) end-acute; the second-case "am" with अमि पूर्वः (पा. ६-१-१०७) the pūrvarūpa, and एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. ८-२-५).

p. 213. "Carantam" — "śap" unaccented as "p"-marked; the "śatṛ" affix is unaccented by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित् (पा. ६-१-१८६); the root's accent alone remains. "Tasthuṣaḥ" — the root "ṣṭhā gati-nivṛttau": in "liṭ," the substitute "kvasu" (क्वसुश्च, पा. ३-२-१०७); the "kvasu" being "iṭ"-less here; the doubling (लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य, पा. ६-१-८); शर्पूर्वाः खयः (पा. ७-४-६१) — in the reduplicative syllable, the "kh/ay" letters that follow "ś/ṣ/s" remain; ह्रस्वः (पा. ७-४-५९); अभ्यासे चर्च (पा. ८-४-५४): "tasthā + vas"; वस्वेकाजाद्घसाम् (पा. ७-२-६७) — "iṭ" for "vas" after a monosyllabic root with doubling; "sthā," ending in "ā," is a root for which "iṭ" is prescribed; the print argues that, since the "iṭ" is "antaraṅga," it should come first; but by the principle that the operation which is the ground of "samprasāraṇa" and the "samprasāraṇa" itself is stronger, वसोः संप्रसारणम् (पा. ६-४-१३१) and संप्रसारणाच्च (पा. ६-१-१०८) apply first, and शासिवसिघसीनां च (पा. ८-३-६०) gives "ṣa": "tasthuṣaḥ." The affix "vasu" gives the acute. "Rocante" — the "tiṅ" unaccented; "śap" "p"-marked; the root-accent alone. "Rocanā" — अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः (पा. ३-२-१४९) "yuc" after a root with an unaccented marker and a consonant initial; युवोरनाकौ (पा. ७-१-१) "ana"; the light penultimate takes guṇa; the affix is "c"-marked, so it is end-acute (चितः, पा. ६-१-१६३). "Divi" — the case-ending is acute by ऊडिदम्पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः (पा. ६-१-१७१). ॥१॥ Accent-marks are printed on the next page; not reproduced here.

Sūkta 6, The Second Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; [?] where unclear.

युञ्जन्त्यस्य काम्या हरी विपक्षसा रथे । शोणा धृष्णू नृवाहसा ॥२॥

yuñjanty asya kāmyā harī vipakṣasā rathe | śoṇā dhṛṣṇū nṛvāhasā ||2||

original p. 214

Rik 6.2: Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings (opening)

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युञ्जन्ति । अस्य । काम्या । हरी इति । विपक्षसा । रथे । शोणा । धृष्णू इति । नृवाहसा ॥२॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अस्य ब्रध्नादिशब्दप्रतिपाद्यस्येत्यादिमूर्तिभिस्तत्र तत्रावस्थितस्येन्द्रस्य रथे हरी [?] नामानौ द्वावश्वौ सारथयो युञ्जन्ति । इन्द्रसंबन्धिनोरश्वयोर्हरिनामत्वं हरी इन्द्रस्य रोहितोऽग्नेः । नै. १-१५ [?] इति पठितत्वात् । कीदृशौ हरी । काम्या कामयितव्यौ विपक्षसा । विविधे पक्षसी रथस्य पार्श्वे युक्तयोर्ययोस्तौ विपक्षसौ । रथस्य द्वयोः पार्श्वयोर्योजितावित्यर्थः । शोणा रक्तवर्णौ धृष्णू प्रगल्भौ नृवाहसा नृणां पुरुषाणामिन्द्रतत्सारथिप्रमुखानां वोढारौ ॥ asya bradhnādi-śabda-pratipādyasyety ādi-mūrtibhis tatra tatrāvasthitasyendrasya rathe harī [?] nāmānau dvāv aśvau sārathayo yuñjanti | indra-sambandhinor aśvayor hari-nāmatvaṃ harī indrasya rohito 'gneḥ | nai. 1-15 [?] iti paṭhitatvāt | kīdṛśau harī | kāmyā kāmayitavyau vipakṣasā | vividhe pakṣasī rathasya pārśve yuktayor yayos tau vipakṣasau | rathasya dvayoḥ pārśvayor yojitāv ity arthaḥ | śoṇā rakta-varṇau dhṛṣṇū pragalbhau nṛvāhasā nṛṇāṃ puruṣāṇām indra-tat-sārathi-pramukhānāṃ voḍhārau || (Reading note: the first clause is crowded in the print — the first words ("asya bradhnādi-…") and the word before "nāmānau" (which I read "harī [?]") are as I could make them; the Nirukta reference "1-15" is small numerals, [?].)

Translation: "Of this (Indra) — who is conveyed by the words 'bradhna' and the rest, abiding here and there in those forms — in his chariot the two horses named Hari — 'sārathayaḥ' — the charioteers 'yuñjanti' — yoke. That the two horses connected with Indra bear the name 'harī' is because it is read (in the Nighaṇṭu list of horse-names): 'harī indrasya, rohito 'gneḥ' (Nirukta [1-15 ?]). What kind of 'harī'? 'Kāmyā' — to be desired, desirable. 'Vipakṣasā' — those two (horses) which are yoked on the two various sides ('pakṣasī') of the chariot — yoked on both flanks of the chariot, the sense. 'Śoṇā' — red-coloured; 'dhṛṣṇū' — bold; 'nṛvāhasā' — the two bearers of men: Indra, his charioteer and the chief among them."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept): "Asya" — the genitive of "idam," as at p. 124 (the "a" substitute, with the case-ending acute). "Kāmyā" — "kamu kāntau" (to desire), the causal "ṇic" (कमेर्णिङ्, पा. ३-१-३०) in the sense of the desiderative; the affix "yat" by कामयितव्यौ…; अचो यत् (पा. ३-१-९७, as printed "3-1-?2"); तित्स्वरितापवादत्वेन यतोऽनावः (पा. ६-१-२१३) — by exception to the "tit-svarita" rule, "yat" gives the first-syllable acute to a word of two or more vowels with "ṇic" included, so "kāmyā" is first-syllable acute; the dual ending "au" is replaced by "ā" (सुपां सुलुक्…). "Harī" — "harato ratham" ("they carry the chariot"); the Uṇādi हृषिपिशिरुहिवृत्तिविदिचिदिकीर्तिभ्यश्च [as printed, garbled] (उ. सू. ४-१३५ [?]) the affix "in"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Vipakṣasā" — "pakṣas" from "paca" with the Uṇādi पचिवचिभ्यां सुट् च (उ. सू. ४-२१५ [?]) — "asun" with the augment "suṭ"; वि + पक्षसौ — a bahuvrīhi "vibhinne pakṣasī pārśve yayoḥ tau vipakṣasau"; "vi" is a particle (nipāta), hence the first member is acute; the first member's accent is retained; the dual is replaced by "ā." "Rathe" — "ramu krīḍāyām" (to play), the Uṇādi "kthan" (हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्थन्, उ. सू. २-२ [?]), "kit," so no guṇa; अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनाम्… (पा. ६-४-३७); "m" elided; first-syllable acute by the "n"-mark. "Śoṇā" — "śoṇṛ varṇa-gatyoḥ" (colour, going), "ghañ" in the sense of "gam"-derived instrument, "ñit," so first-syllable acute; the dual ending replaced by "ā." "Dhṛṣṇū" — "ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye" (to be bold): the affix "knu" (त्रसिगृधिधृषिक्षिपेः क्नुः, पा. ३-२-१४० [as printed]); "kit," so no guṇa; the affix's accent; "nṛvāhasā" — "na vahata iti"; the Uṇādi वहेर्वहिपाधाङ्भ्यश्छन्दसि (उ. सू. ४-२१० [?]) "asun"; "ṇit" by णिदित्यनुवृत्तेः — vṛddhi; "nṛṇāṃ vāhasau" — a genitive tatpuruṣa, retaining the kṛt-final member's accent. ॥२॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ Kannada, translated; continued on the next page

(The charioteers and others) अस्य (asya) — (as said before, the one who is conveyed by the words "Āditya" and the rest) of this Indra | रथे (rathe) — in the chariot (to the chariot) | काम्या (kāmyā) — (to Indra) beloved, or dear | शोणा (śoṇā) — … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose translated; English as printed; references in small Kannada numerals marked [?].

original p. 215

Rik 6.2: Pada-meanings concluded; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics

Continuing the Pada-meanings from p. 214: शोणा (śoṇā) — red-coloured | धृष्णू (dhṛṣṇū) — full of enthusiasm | नृवाहसा (nṛvāhasā) — those who carry Indra and the charioteer (who have taken the form of men) | विपक्षसा (vipakṣasā) — yoked to the left and right flanks of the chariot | हरी (harī) — the two horses | युञ्जन्ति (yuñjanti) — they yoke (they harness).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The charioteer and others yoke Indra's two favourite horses, on the two flanks, left and right, to Indra's chariot. Those horses, though red in colour, are full of enthusiasm and have the capacity to carry men — that is, their master Indra, the charioteer and others. Such excellent horses they yoke to Indra's chariot.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"They are harnessing to his (Indra's) chariot, one on each side, his favourite pair of bay coloured horses, high-spirited and able to carry their brave lord."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The pāda "yuñjanty asya kāmyā" is quoted in the Āpastamba-śrauta-sūtra (20-[?]-[?]) and the Maitrāyaṇīya-saṃhitā (3-[?]-[?]) numbers small and uncertain. In the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa (2-8-4 [?]) there is an exposition of this Ṛk. There it says "śoṇā dhṛṣṇū nṛvāhasety āha | aho rātre vai nṛvāhasā" (शोणा धृष्णू नृवाहसेत्याह । अहो रात्रे वै नृवाहसा — "'śoṇā dhṛṣṇū nṛvāhasā,' he says: day and night, indeed, are the 'nṛvāhasā'") — that is, for the word "nṛvāhasā" an adhyātmika meaning, "day and night," is given; nothing further of special note.

काम्या (kāmyā) — wished-for, dear; favourite. हरी (harī) — Indra's two horses have the name "harī." विपक्षसा (vipakṣasā) — the separate flanks, that is, the left and right flanks. रथे (rathe) — "ramante 'smin iti rathaḥ" (रमन्तेऽस्मिन्निति रथः — "that in which they delight is the 'ratha'") — "ramu krīḍāyām" (to play): because one sits in it and moves, it is called "ratha." शोणा (śoṇā) — English as printed "crimson, bright, bay or chestnut." धृष्णू (dhṛṣṇū) — full of enthusiasm; English "fiery, high-spirited." नृवाहसा (nṛvāhasā) — those who have the capacity to carry (or to draw) men. The words "kāmyā, harī, vipakṣasā, śoṇā, dhṛṣṇū, nṛvāhasā" are all dual (second-case or first-case dual) words, and are qualifiers of the word "harī." Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Pure grammar in Kannada prose, restating the Sanskrit of p. 214; characterized in outline; sūtras kept; numbers as read.

original p. 216

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.2 (Kannada) — characterized

"Asya" — in the previous mantra the word "idam" is not a back-reference (anvādeśa), because the Indra described by the words "bradhna" and the rest has been mentioned only by those words and "asya" does not point back to a repeated operation; so, by इदमो ऽन्वादेशे ऽशनुदात्त ऋतृतीयादौ (पा. २-४-३२) the "aś" substitute does not occur and the unaccented "a" … does not arise; the whole of "idam" is replaced by "a" (with the case-ending acute): "asya" is a pronoun (sarvanāma), acute on its case-ending. "Kāmyā" — "kamu kāntau"; the "ṇic" (कमेर्णिङ्, पा. ३-१-३० [as printed]); vṛddhi of the penultimate (अत उपधायाः, पा. ७-२-११६) → "kām-i"; the root-name by सनाद्यन्ता धातवः (पा. ३-१-३२); अचो यत् (पा. ३-१-९७) "yat" after a root ending in a vowel; णेरनिटि (पा. ६-४-५१) the "ṇi" elided → "kāmya"; by exception to तित्स्वरितम् (पा. ६-१-१८५), यतोऽनावः (पा. ६-१-२१३) gives first-syllable acute; the dual "au" → "ā" (सुपां सुलुक्…, पा. ७-१-३९). "Harī" — "harato ratham"; the Uṇādi "in" after "hṛñ" (उ. सू. ४-१३५ [?]); "n"-marked, first-syllable acute; the dual "ā" is, in the Veda, "ī." "Vipakṣasā" — पचिवचिभ्यां सुट् च (उ. सू. ४-२१५ [?]): after "pac" and "vac" the Uṇādi affix "asun" and the augment "suṭ"; "pac + suṭ + as" → चोः कुः (पा. ८-२-३०) "k"; आदेशप्रत्यययोः (पा. ८-३-५९) "ṣ" for the "s" → "pakṣas"; "vibhinne pakṣasī pārśve yayoḥ tau vipakṣasau" — a bahuvrīhi ("yoked to the two different flanks of the chariot"); "vi" a particle, first-syllable acute; बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. ६-२-१) retains it; the dual → "ā." "Rathe" — "ramante 'smin iti rathaḥ" — from "ramu krīḍāyām" the Uṇādi हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्थन् (उ. सू. २-२ [?]); "kit," so the root's "m" is elided by अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७) …; "n"-marked, hence first-syllable acute. Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; [?] where unclear. Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.

original p. 217

Rik 6.2 grammar concluded; Sūkta 6, Third Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

"Śoṇā" concluding the grammar of Rik 6.2 — "śoṇṛ varṇa-gatyoḥ" (colour, going); the affix "ghañ" in the instrument sense (the horses are the means of going); "ñit," so first-syllable acute; the dual "au" is replaced by "ā" (सुपां सुलुक्…, पा. ७-१-३९). "Dhṛṣṇū" — "ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye" (to be bold) — the affix "knu" (त्रसिगृधिधृषिक्षिपेः क्नुः, पा. ३-२-१४०); "kit," so no guṇa for the light penultimate (क्ङिति च, पा. १-१-५); the affix's accent. "Nṛvāhasā" — "nṝn vahataḥ" — an etymological analysis ("those who carry men"); the Uṇādi वहिहाधाङ्भ्यश्छन्दसि (उ. सू. ४-२१० [?]) "asun" after these roots in the Veda; "ṇit" by continuation (णिदित्यनुवृत्तेः), vṛddhi of "vah" → "vāh-as" (अत उपधायाः, पा. ७-२-११६); the dual "ā" (सुपां सुलुक्); the whole is first-syllable acute as "n"-marked; गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९) — the kṛt-final member's accent retained, so the first-syllable acute stands. ॥२॥

Sūkta 6, The Third Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

केतुं कृण्वन्नकेतवे पेशो मर्या अपेशसे । समुषद्भिरजायथाः ॥३॥

ketuṃ kṛṇvann aketave peśo maryā apeśase | sam uṣadbhir ajāyathāḥ ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

केतुम् । कृण्वन् । अकेतवे । पेशः । मर्याः । अपेशसे । सम् । उषत्ऽभिः । अजायथाः ॥३॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ opening, p. 217

हे मर्या मनुष्या इदमाश्चर्यं पश्यतेत्यध्याहारः । किमाश्चर्यमिति तदुच्यते । आदित्यरूपोऽयमिन्द्र उषद्भिर्दाहकै रश्मिभिः प्रतिदिनमुषःकाले वा संभूयोऽजायथाः । उदपद्यत । अथवा सूर्यस्यैवास्तमये मरणमुपचर्य । व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं कृत्वा संबोधनं क्रियते । हे मर्य प्रतिदिनं त्वमजायथा इति योज्यं किं कुर्वन् । अकेतवे रात्रौ निद्राभिभूतत्वेन प्रज्ञानरहिताय he maryā manuṣyā idam āścaryaṃ paśyatety adhyāhāraḥ | kim āścaryam iti tad ucyate | āditya-rūpo 'yam indra uṣadbhir dāhakai raśmibhiḥ pratidinam uṣaḥ-kāle vā sambhūyo 'jāyathāḥ | udapadyata | athavā sūryasyaivāstamaye maraṇam upacarya | vyatyayena bahuvacanaṃ kṛtvā sambodhanaṃ kriyate | he marya pratidinaṃ tvam ajāyathā iti yojyaṃ kiṃ kurvan | aketave rātrau nidrābhibhūtatvena prajñāna-rahitāya (Reading notes: the page ends at "prajñāna-rahitāya" and the sentence continues on the next page; the form "maryā" for the vocative plural is printed so, with the Pada text giving "maryāḥ"; "dāhakai" is printed "dāhakaiḥ" with a letter I read as slightly crowded.)

Translation (of the part on this page): "'O "maryāḥ" — O men! — behold this wonder': this is the supplied sense. What is the wonder? It is said: this Indra, who is of the form of the Sun, is born every day, becoming one with the burning rays, at dawn — he arises. Or: since the very setting of the Sun is a figurative 'death,' the vocative plural is used by a change of number — 'O mortal! you are born every day' (the sentence is to be construed so). Doing what? 'Aketave' — for the one (in the night) without understanding, overcome by sleep …" . Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; [?] where unclear. The Nirukta reference is in small numerals and marked [?].

original p. 218

Rik 6.3: Bhāṣya concluded; grammar (characterized); Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha (opening)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ concluding

प्राणिने केतुं कृण्वन् । प्रातः प्रज्ञानं कुर्वन् । अपेशसे रात्र्यान्धकारावृतत्वेनानभिव्यक्तत्वाद्रूपरहिताय पदार्थाय प्रातरन्धकारनिवारणेन पेशो रूपमभिव्यज्यमानं कुर्वन् । पेश इति रूपनामानि पिंशतेः । नि. ३-११ [?] । इति यास्कः । अकेतवेऽपेशस इति चतुर्थी षष्ठ्यर्थे द्रष्टव्या ॥ prāṇine ketuṃ kṛṇvan | prātaḥ prajñānaṃ kurvan | apeśase rātry-āndhakārāvṛtatvenānabhivyaktatvād rūpa-rahitāya padārthāya prātar-andhakāra-nivāraṇena peśo rūpam abhivyajyamānaṃ kurvan | peśa iti rūpa-nāmāni piṃśateḥ | ni. 3-11 [?] | iti yāskaḥ | aketave 'peśasa iti caturthī ṣaṣṭhy-arthe draṣṭavyā ||

Translation: "Giving 'ketu' (awareness) to the living being: making knowledge (prajñāna) in the morning; 'apeśase' — to an object that, being covered by the darkness of night, is unmanifest and so is without form — making 'peśaḥ,' form, to be manifested by the removal of the morning-darkness. 'Peśaḥ' is a name for form, from 'piṃś' (to adorn) — thus Yāska (Nirukta [3-11 ?]). 'Aketave' and 'apeśase' are datives to be understood in the sense of the genitive."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept; read from the slice): "Ketum" — a bare stem, acute by its own accent (prātipadika-svara). "Kṛṇvan" — "kṛvi hiṃsā-karaṇayoś ca" (to injure, to do): the substitute "śatṛ" for "laṭ"; इदितो नुम् धातोः (पा. ७-१-५८) the augment "num"; "śap" might arise but धिन्विकृण्व्योर च (पा. ३-१-८०) — the affix "u" after "dhinv" and "kṛṇv," and "a" for the final "v" — "kṛṇv" + "u"; अतो लोपः (पा. ६-४-४८) elides the "a"; since that elision is treated as present (sthānivadbhāva), the guṇa of the light penultimate by पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च (पा. ७-३-८६) does not occur; the accent is the affix's. "Aketave" — a bahuvrīhi with "nañ"; नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) makes the second member end-acute. "Peśaḥ" — a "sab-viṣaya"-class neuter stem, first-syllable acute (नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य, Phiṭ-sūtra). "Maryāḥ" — in the Veda "mṛ" with "kyap" (छन्दसि निष्टर्क्यदेवहूयप्रणीयोन्नीयोच्छिष्यमर्यस्तर्यध्वर्यखन्यखान्यदेवयज्याऽऽपृच्छ्यप्रतिषीव्यब्रह्मवाद्यभाव्यस्ताव्योपचाय्यपृड्यानि, पा. ३-१-१२३ — as printed, abbreviated) — "mṛ + kyap" — "marya"; the vocative loses its accent (आमन्त्रितस्य च, पा. ८-१-१९); since there is no mutual connection of sense with the preceding word, "parāṅgavad-bhāva" does not occur. "Apeśase" — नञ्सुभ्याम् — end-acute. "Sam" — a particle, first-syllable acute. "Uṣadbhiḥ" — "uṣa plusa dāhe" (to burn): "laṭ" and its substitute "śatṛ"; "śap" would arise, but by vyatyaya "śa" (the tudādi vikaraṇa); the sārvadhātuka is not "p"-marked (सार्वधातुकमपित्, पा. १-२-४), so no guṇa for the light penultimate; "śa" gives the accent by the affix's acute; and since "śatṛ" is unaccented (the root's upadeśa-based), the "lasārvadhātuka" is unaccented; the single substitute is acute (एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः). "Ajāyathāḥ" — in the sense "ajāyata" the second-person verb stands for the third (by vyatyaya), and by पुरुषव्यत्ययो निघातः — no nighāta applies.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) मर्याः (he maryāḥ) — O men (look at this wonder) | आदित्यरूपनादे (ādityarūpanāde) — (Indra) who has the form of the Sun | उषद्भिः (uṣadbhiḥ) — daily at dawn, with the rays | अकेतवे (aketave) — to those who, because of sleep at night, are without understanding | केतुम् (ketum) — (at dawn, awakening) understanding | अपेशसे (apeśase) — (at night) to things that, covered by darkness, cannot be seen as having any form, giving light | पेशः (peśaḥ) — (of things) each of their forms (the power to see them) | कृण्वन् (kṛṇvan) — making | सं अजायथाः (saṃ ajāyathāḥ) — he is born (appears).

Or: मर्याः (maryāḥ) — O man (the plural used for the singular) | (त्वम्) (tvam) — you | उषद्भिः (uṣadbhiḥ) … समजायथाः (samajāyathāḥ) — every day, at the time of sunset, like one who dies, you become without understanding, and at morning you are born with consciousness; so we say: "be aware."

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Kannada, translated; opening

O Indra! You, in the form of the Sun, rise every day at dawn, and set at sunset; when you set, creatures are overcome by sleep … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose translated; English as printed; the Nirukta and Taittirīya references in small numerals are marked [?].

original p. 219

Rik 6.3: Bhāvārtha concluded; English rendering; Special topics

Concluding the Bhāvārtha from p. 218: …creatures are overcome by sleep, and are without consciousness, and from the darkness of night are unable to see the forms of anything. When you rise at dawn, creatures awake and, with consciousness or understanding, are able to see the forms of all things in the light. Therefore, to the creatures who are overcome by sleep, you give — every day — consciousness, and the power to see the forms of all things.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"O mortals, (look at this wonder). Indra (in the form of Aditya) rises every day at dawn giving sense to the senseless (while in sleep) and form to the formless. or O mortal, having been dead (asleep) at the setting of the sun you are born ever with morning rays."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of this Ṛk is not plain. For the word "ketu," the Nirukta (Ni. 3-[?]) says "prajñā" (understanding). In the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa (2-[?]-[?]) it is said that "ketu" means "dhvaja" (banner): "ketuṃ kṛṇvann aketave iti dhvajaṃ pratimuñcati" (केतुं कृण्वन्नकेतव इति ध्वजं प्रतिमुञ्चति — "'ketuṃ kṛṇvann aketave,' with this he fastens the banner"); when setting up a banner they recite this mantra. Though "ketu" has the sense of "banner," that sense does not fit here. Those who follow the method laid down in the Gṛhyasūtras recite this mantra in order to invoke the "ketu-graha" (the planet Ketu) when they perform the worship of the nine planets (navagraha); but in this mantra there is no subject concerning the planet Ketu. Since the word "ketu" alone is common to both, this is likely to be a customary (rūḍha) use; likewise the use of mantras that contain the names of other planets in the worship and invocation of those planets is probably a conventional one. For in the Ṛgveda there is no consideration of the nine planets. Only the two names, Sūrya and Candra, are found there. The names of the stars are not there either. Only in the Yajurveda are the names of the stars, and the descriptions of the full-moon and new-moon days, explained. The names of the nine planets are not there either. Therefore it may be said without doubt that the worship of the planets (graha-yajña) was not in use in the time of the Vedas and came into custom later.

पेशः (peśaḥ) — "peśa iti rūpa-nāma piṃśate" (पेश इति रूपनाम पिंशते — "'peśa' is a name of form, from 'piṃś'," Ni. 3-[?]-[?]); "peśa" means form. अपेशसे (apeśase) — to one without form.

मर्याः (maryāḥ) — men. This word is the first-case plural. In this Ṛk the verb "ajāyathāḥ" is in the second person, singular … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Kannada prose translated; grammar characterized, sūtras kept; numbers as read.

original p. 220

Special topics on Rik 6.3 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

Continuing "maryāḥ" from p. 219: …the verb "ajāyathāḥ" is in the second-person singular; if "maryāḥ" were taken as the agent (kartṛ), then, since the verb is singular, the two do not agree. For the convenience of the metre the singular "marya" is used in the long form "maryā," say some; but in such cases there is no cause for such a metrical advantage or disadvantage here; for after the word "maryā" comes "apeśase," and the final long "ā" of "maryā" should have combined with the first "a" of the following word (by savarṇa-dīrgha), which has not happened here. Besides, in the Pada-text the plural word with the visarga, "maryāḥ," is plainly given. Therefore, as Sāyaṇa has said at the beginning of his Bhāṣya, this word should be said to be used merely for addressing ordinary people (the public). Western scholars hold the same view. In the view that uses the singular "marya," the agent-word "tvam" must be supplied here.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept

"Ketum" — फिषः (Phiṭ-sūtra 1) — by the bare-stem accent, "ketu" is end-acute. "Kṛṇvan" — "kṛvi hiṃsā-karaṇayoś ca" (to injure; to do): after "laṭ," the substitute "śatṛ" (लटः शतृशानचावप्रथमासमानाधिकरणे, पा. ३-२-१२४); the root is "i"-marked (इदितो नुम् धातोः, पा. ७-१-५८), so "num" is added; by the paribhāṣā मिदचोऽन्त्यात्परः (पा. १-१-४७) the "num" is placed after the last vowel: "kṛṇv"; the agent-affix "śap" would come by कर्तरि शप् (पा. ३-१-६८), but, as it would be unsuitable, by धिन्विकृण्व्योर च (पा. ३-१-८०) — after "dhinv" and "kṛṇv," the final "v" is replaced by "a," and in place of the "śap" vikaraṇa the affix "u" comes — "kṛṇ + u + at"; अतो लोपः (पा. ६-४-४८) — an "a" before an ārdhadhātuka that begins with a vowel is elided — the "a" before "u" is elided; then पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च (पा. ७-३-८६) would give guṇa to the light penultimate before a sārvadhātuka or ārdhadhātuka affix, but the "a"-elision is treated as present, अचः परस्मिन्पूर्वविधौ (पा. १-१-५७) — so the guṇa does not occur. The page ends in the middle of an argument about whether a single intervening letter blocks the operation — "vyavadhāna" — concluding that a mere letter-interposition does not prevent the rule when a rule's own wording requires it ("vacana-prāmāṇyāt"); it continues on the next page. Page headers: p. 221 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā"; p. 222 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." The grammar on p. 221 and the top of p. 222 is pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose, restating the Sanskrit of p. 218; characterized in outline, sūtras kept; numbers as read. Accent-marks on the Saṃhitā/Pada are printed on p. 222; not reproduced. Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; [?] where unclear.

original pp. 221–222

Rik 6.3 grammar concluded (characterized); Sūkta 6, Fourth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

p. 221 — "kṛṇvan" (concluded) and the other words of Rik 6.3. Continuing p. 220: …even with many interposed letters the rule does not apply; but here, through sthānivadbhāva, the "n" and "a" interpose and so no guṇa comes: "kṛṇ + u + at." Taking the "śatṛ" as the ground, सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. ७-३-८४) would give guṇa, but it is barred by क्ङिति च (पा. १-१-५); इकोयणचि (पा. ६-१-७७) gives the "y/v" substitute → "kṛṇv-at"; since "śatṛ" is not at the beginning of the (substituted) stem, तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिद… does not give it the unaccented; the affix-accent holds: "śatṛ" is acute on its "a." ऋवर्णान्नस्य णत्वं वाच्यम् (वा. पा. ८-४-११) — "ṇ" for "n" after "ṛ," so "kṛṇv"; then "su" … उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः (पा. ७-१-७०) the "num" augment; हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्सुतिस्यपृक्तं हल् (पा. ६-१-६८) elides "su"; संयोगान्तस्य लोपः (पा. ८-२-२३) elides the "t"; the elision being "asiddha," the "n" is not elided: "kṛṇvan." "Aketave" — a "nañ" bahuvrīhi (नञ्सुभ्याम्, पा. ६-२-१७२), second member end-acute. "Peśaḥ" — first-syllable acute (नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य). "Maryāḥ" — छन्दसि निष्टर्क्य…मर्यस्तर्यध्वर्य… (पा. ३-१-१२३, as printed in the abbreviated list): the Veda has the forms formed with "kyap" from "mṛ"; since "marya" is among the nipātanas, being a vocative it is unaccented (आमन्त्रितस्य च, पा. ८-१-१९); "peśaḥ" and "maryāḥ" have no mutual connection, so "parāṅgavad-bhāva" does not occur (सुबामन्त्रिते पराङ्गवत्स्वरे, पा. २-१-२). "Apeśase" — नञ्सुभ्याम्, end-acute. "Sam" — a particle, first-syllable acute. "Uṣadbhiḥ" — "uṣa dāhe" (to burn): "laṭ" and "śatṛ"; in place of "śap," by vyatyaya, the vikaraṇa "śa"; the sārvadhātuka is not "p"-marked, so no guṇa for the light penultimate (क्ङिति च); "śa" is acute by the affix …

p. 222 — "uṣadbhiḥ" and "ajāyathāḥ" concluded. Continuing: …the "a" of "śa" and the "a" of "śatṛ" — since both are "a" — combine as pararūpa (अतो गुणे, पा. ६-१-९४), and the single substitute from the acute and unaccented is acute (एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः, पा. ८-२-५). "Ajāyathāḥ" — a second-person form standing, by vyatyaya, for the first-person "ajāyata"; it is unaccented by तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८). ॥३॥

Sūkta 6, The Fourth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आदह स्वधामनु पुनर्गर्भत्वमेरिरे । दधाना नाम यज्ञियम् ॥४॥

ād aha svadhām anu punar garbhatvam erire | dadhānā nāma yajñiyam ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आत् । अह । स्वधाम् । अनु । पुनः । गर्भत्वम् । आ । ईरिरे । दधानाः । नाम । यज्ञियम् ॥४॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ opening

अत्रास्ति विशेषविनियोगः । चतुर्विंशेऽहनि प्रातःसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्र आदह स्वधामन्निति द्वे ऋचौ । इन्द्रेण सं हि दृक्षस इत्येका । अयं तृचः षळहस्तोत्रियसंज्ञकः । तथा च सूत्रितं चतुर्विंशे होताजनिष्वेति खण्डे । इन्द्रेण सं हि दृक्षस आदह स्वधामन्नित्येका द्वे च । आ. ६-९ [?] । इति । यद्यप्येतदैन्द्रं सूक्तं तथाप्यादहेत्यादिषु षट्सु मारुतो वर्ण्यन्ते । प्रायेणैन्द्रे मारुत इत्यनुक्रमणिकायामुक्तत्वात् । अनु. ३-११ [?] ॥ आदित्ययुवानन्तर्यार्थो निपातः । आहेत्यवधारणार्थः । आदह वर्षतोरनन्तरमेव । स्वधामनु । इतः परं जनिष्यमाणमन्नमुदकं वानुलक्ष्य मरुतो देवा गर्भत्वमेरिरे । मेघमध्ये जलस्य गर्भाकारं प्रेरितवन्तः । जलस्य कर्तारं पर्जन्यं प्रेरितवन्तः । प्रतिसंवत्सरमेवं कुर्वन्तीति दर्शयितुं पुनःशब्दः प्रयुक्तः । कीदृशा मरुतः । यज्ञियं यज्ञार्हं नाम दधानाः धारयन्तः । सप्तसु गणेषु मरुतामावृज्ञान्यावृज्ञेत्यादीनि यज्ञयोग्यानि नामान्यन्यत्राम्नातानि । अन्ध इत्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेष्वन्ननामसूर्क्र रसः … atrāsti viśeṣa-viniyogaḥ | caturviṃśe 'hani prātaḥ-savane brāhmaṇācchaṃsi-śastra ādaha svadhām ann iti dve ṛcau | indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣasa ity ekā | ayaṃ tṛcaḥ ṣaḷaha-stotriya-saṃjñakaḥ | tathā ca sūtritaṃ caturviṃśe hotājaniṣveti khaṇḍe | indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣasa ādaha svadhām ann ity ekā dve ca | ā. 6-9 [?] | iti | yady apy etad aindraṃ sūktaṃ tathāpy ādahety ādiṣu ṣaṭsu maruto varṇyante | prāyeṇaindre maruta ity anukramaṇikāyām uktatvāt | anu. 3-11 [?] || āditya-yuvān-antaryārtho nipātaḥ | āhety avadhāraṇārthaḥ | ādaha varṣator anantaram eva | svadhām anu | itaḥ paraṃ janiṣyamāṇam annam udakaṃ vānulakṣya maruto devā garbhatvam erire | megha-madhye jalasya garbhākāraṃ preritavantaḥ | jalasya kartāraṃ parjanyaṃ preritavantaḥ | prati-saṃvatsaram evaṃ kurvantīti darśayituṃ punaḥ-śabdaḥ prayuktaḥ | kīdṛśā marutaḥ | yajñiyaṃ yajñārhaṃ nāma dadhānāḥ dhārayantaḥ | saptasu gaṇeṣu marutām āvṛjñān yāvṛjñety ādīni yajña-yogyāni nāmāny anyatrāmnātāni | andha ity ādiṣv aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣv anna-nāmasūrk rasaḥ … (Reading notes: (i) the quotation of the Sūtra is "ā. 6-9 [?]" and of the Anukramaṇī "anu. 3-11 [?]" — small Kannada numerals read with doubt; (ii) the compound "āditya-yuvān-antaryārtho" is printed in this form — I read it as "āt" ("then") with the sense "immediately after," and give the printed letters as they stand; (iii) "āvṛjñān yāvṛjñety" is crowded and I give it as read, flagged — it is meant to be the Marut names listed elsewhere; (iv) the last line ends mid-list at the foot of the page, "…anna-nāmasūrk rasaḥ," and continues on p. 223.)

Translation (of the part on this page): "Here is a special application: on the twenty-fourth day, at the morning pressing, in the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's śastra, the two Ṛks 'ād aha svadhām anu' (Ṛks 4 and 6 [?]) and the one 'indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase' are used. This tṛca is called the 'ṣaḷaha-stotriya.' So it is laid down in the Sūtra, in the section 'caturviṃśe hotājaniṣva': 'indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣasa — one; ād aha svadhām anu — and two' (Āśv. [6-9 ?]). Although this sūkta is addressed to Indra, in the six Ṛks beginning 'ādaha' the Maruts are described; because the Anukramaṇī says 'mostly in an Indra (sūkta), the Maruts' (Anu. [3-11 ?]). 'Āt' is a particle in the sense of 'immediately after'; 'aha' is in the sense of emphasis: 'ād aha' — immediately after the raining. 'Svadhām anu' — looking to the coming food, or to the water, the Maruts, the gods, 'garbhatvam erire' — drove (set in motion) the form of a germ of water in the midst of the cloud: they impelled Parjanya, the maker of water. The word 'punaḥ' is used to show that they do this every year. What kind of Maruts? 'Yajñiyam nāma dadhānāḥ' — bearing a name fit for sacrifice. In the seven groups of the Maruts, names fit for sacrifice are recited elsewhere. Among the twenty-eight names of food beginning with 'andha,' 'ūrk' and 'rasaḥ' …" . Rik 6.4: Bhāṣya concluded; grammar (characterized); Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ concluding from p. 222

…स्वधेति पठितम् । ऊर्ण इत्यादिष्वेकशतसंख्याकेषूदकनामसु तेजः स्वधाऽन्नमिति पठितम् ॥ आदह निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तः । स्वधाम् । स्वं लोकं दधाति पुष्णातीति । स्वधा । आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः । पा. ३-२-३ । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अनु पुनःशब्दौ निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तौ । गर्भस्य भावो गर्भत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । एरिरे । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थादीरतेर्गतावित्यस्मादनुदात्तेतः परस्य लिटो झस्य इरेच् । पा. ३-४-८१ । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । सह सुपा । पा. २-१-४ । इत्यत्र सुपेति योगविभागादाङौ सह तिङः समासेऽपि समासस्य । पा. ६-१-२२३ । इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । इजादेश्च गुरुमतोऽनृच्छः । पा. ३-१-३६ । इत्याम् न भवति मन्त्रत्वात् । अहशब्दयोगान्निघाताभावः । तुपश्यपश्यताहै पूजायाम् । पा. ८-१-४२ । इति निषेधात् । दधानाः । शानचश्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्तेऽभ्यस्तानामादिः । पा. ६-१-१८९ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । यज्ञमर्हतीति यज्ञियम् । यज्ञर्त्विग्भ्यां घखञौ । पा. ५-१-७१ । इति घप्रत्ययः । आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम् । पा. ७-१-२ । इतीयादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः ॥ …svadheti paṭhitam | ūrṇa ity ādiṣv ekaśata-saṃkhyākeṣūdaka-nāmasu tejaḥ svadhā 'nnam iti paṭhitam || ādaha nipātatvād ādyudāttau | svadhām | svaṃ lokaṃ dadhāti puṣṇātīti | svadhā | ā-to 'nupasarge kaḥ | pā. 3-2-3 | kṛd-uttara-pada-prakṛti-svaratvam | anu punaḥ-śabdau nipātatvād ādyudāttau | garbhasya bhāvo garbhatvam | pratyaya-svaraḥ | erire | antarbhāvita-ṇyarthād īrater gatāv ity asmād anudātteta ḥ parasya liṭo jhasya irec | pā. 3-4-81 | cittvād antodāttaḥ | saha supā | pā. 2-1-4 | ity atra supeti yoga-vibhāgād āṅau saha tiṅaḥ samāse 'pi samāsasya | pā. 6-1-223 | ity antodāttatvam | ijādeś ca gurumato 'nṛcchaḥ | pā. 3-1-36 | ity ām na bhavati mantratvāt | aha-śabda-yogān nighātābhāvaḥ | tupaśyapaśyatāhai pūjāyām | pā. 8-1-42 | iti niṣedhāt | dadhānāḥ | śānacaś cittvād antodāttatve prāpte 'bhyastānām ādiḥ | pā. 6-1-189 | ity ādyudāttatvam | yajñam arhatīti yajñiyam | yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau | pā. 5-1-71 | iti gha-pratyayaḥ | āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām | pā. 7-1-2 | itīyādeśaḥ | pratyaya-svareṇekāra udāttaḥ || (Reading notes: (i) the first line carries on the Nighaṇṭu sentence from p. 222 ("…rasaḥ svadheti paṭhitam"); I give it as read; (ii) "svadheti paṭhitam" — "svadhā is read" among the food-names; and among the hundred-and-one names of water, "svadhā" is read as "tejaḥ … annam"; (iii) several sūtra-numbers in the grammar are small numerals and the sūtra-names are as printed, flagged for checking.)

Translation (sense in full; grammar in outline): "'…svadhā' is read (among the food-names); among the hundred-and-one names of water beginning with 'ūrṇa,' 'tejaḥ' and 'svadhā' (also 'annam') are read. 'Ād aha' — a particle, first-syllable acute. 'Svadhām' — 'svaṃ lokaṃ dadhāti puṣṇātīti' — 'it supports, nourishes its own world': 'svadhā'; (affix) 'ka' (Pāṇini 3-2-3) after a root ending in ā when no prefix; the kṛt-final member's accent is retained. 'Anu' and 'punaḥ' are both particles, first-syllable acute. 'Garbhatvam' — 'garbhasya bhāvo garbhatvam' — the state of a germ; accent of the affix. 'Erire' — from 'īr gatau' (to go, to move), with the causal sense included; the substitute 'irec' for 'jha' of the 'liṭ' after a root with an unaccented marker (Pāṇini 3-4-81); end-acute by the 'c'-mark. 'Saha supā' (Pāṇini 2-1-4) — here, by dividing the sūtra at 'supā,' the compound of 'ā' (prefix) with the verb takes (in a compound) the accent of the whole compound, end-acute (Pāṇini 6-1-223); 'ām' does not come, since this is a mantra. By connection with the word 'aha' there is no nighāta (Pāṇini 8-1-42, 'tupaśyapaśyatāhai pūjāyām' — the prohibition). 'Dadhānāḥ' — where 'śānac' being 'c'-marked would be end-acute, अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. ६-१-१८९) gives first-syllable acute. 'Yajñiyam' — 'yajñam arhatīti yajñiyam': by 'yajña-ṛtvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau' (Pāṇini 5-1-71) the affix 'gha,' replaced by 'iya' (Pāṇini 7-1-2); the 'i' is acute by the affix's accent."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

आत् अह (āt aha) — immediately after (the end of the rainy season) | यज्ञियम् (yajñiyam) — worthy of sacrifice | नाम (nāma) — name | दधानाः (dadhānāḥ) — bearing (the Maruts, that is, the Marut-deities) | स्वधाम् अनु (svadhām anu) — (to produce) food in the form of grain (that must grow later) and water | पुनः (punaḥ) — again (now too, as in the previous rainy season) | गर्भत्वम् (garbhatvam) — (the water that gathers together in the cloud, as a germ) the water gathering in the cloud | एरिरे (erire) — impelled (that is, impelled Parjanya, who produces the rain).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

After the rainy season has passed, the Marut-deities, who are famous by names honoured in sacrifices and the like, in order to give people grain in the form of food and water, again, as before, now also, as a part of the work of rain, impelled Parjanya, so that, like a germ, the water gathers together in the midst of the clouds.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Thereafter (the Maruts) who bear the names invoked in sacrificial rites, having seen the rain about to be engendered instigated him to resume his embryo condition (in the clouds)."
