The Ṛg-vedic verse was read from an enlarged slice; its reference is in small Kannada numerals and cut at the left edge of the enlargement, and is marked [?]; the gloss is the source's own English.

original p. 238

Rik 6.7: Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening): the Vṛtra legend

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Marut-deities! That you go about together with the fearless Indra is seen by all. Not only that: the two of you — Indra and the Marut-deities — are always full of delight, and your radiance and your power and capacity are equal. That is, Indra and the Marut-deities, you two are alike in radiance, power and capacity.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"You are seen, O Maruts, marching forth together with Indra who is not frightened; (both) rejoicing and of equal splendour."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The Bhāṣyakāra here indicates an ancient legend. In the battle that took place long ago, when Indra destroyed the demon Vṛtra, the gods who were with Indra were frightened by the terrible snorting and roaring of the demon Vṛtra, and fled. But the Marut-deities alone, without any fear, remained with Indra to help him. This matter is described in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-2 [?] and in the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa (3-20 [?]):

वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अजहुर्ये सखायः । मरुद्भिरिन्द्र सख्यं ते अस्त्वथेमा विश्वाः पृतना जयासि ॥ (ऋ. सं. ८-९६-२ [?]) vṛtrasya tvā śvasathād īṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahur ye sakhāyaḥ | marudbhir indra sakhyaṃ te astv atheme viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsi || (ṛ. saṃ. 8-96-2 [?]) English, as printed in the source: "Before the snorting of Vritra, all the gods, your comrades beating a hasty retreat abandoned you. Let your friendship be, O Indra, with the Maruts; then you will conquer all battles."

The meaning of this: O Indra! From the terrible breath of the demon Vṛtra, all the gods who were your friends were frightened and, leaving your side, ran away. But let there be friendship for you with the Marut-deities. (With their help) you will be victorious in all the battles. For this very reason, it is said here that the Marut-deities may be seen going about with Indra; that is, the sense is that since the Marut-deities are friendly with Indra, they help Indra in battles and the like.

इन्द्रेण (indreṇa) — the word "Indra" can be explained as meaning "supreme lordship." If so, the word "indreṇa" may be applied, together with the word "abibhyuṣā," as a qualifier of "marudgaṇa" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose translated; grammar characterized; the Nirukta reference in small numerals is marked [?].

original p. 239

Special topics on Rik 6.7 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

Continuing from p. 238: …then "indreṇa abibhyuṣā" means "by the host of Marut-deities, who have supreme lordship and are free of fear."

The sage Yāska, in his Nirukta, explains this Ṛk thus: "indreṇa hi saṃdṛśyase saṅgacchamāno 'bibhyuṣā gaṇena mandū madiṣṇū yuvāṃ stotāro 'pi vā mandunā teneti syāt samānavarcasety etena vyākhyātam" (इन्द्रेण हि संदृश्यसे संगच्छमानोऽबिभ्युषा गणेन मन्दू मदिष्णू युवां स्तोतारोऽपि वा मन्दुना तेनेति स्यात्समानवर्चसेत्येतेन व्याख्यातम् — as in the Bhāṣya on p. 236; Ni. 4-[?]). This is as the Bhāṣyakāra explained it. But Yāska has taken the words "mandū" and "samānavarcasā" as if they were dual words, and so has said that they are qualifiers of both Indra and the Maruts; whereas the Bhāṣyakāra has taken these words as third-case (instrumental) forms and used them, with the four words "indreṇa," "abibhyuṣā," "mandū" and "samānavarcasā," as qualifiers of the Marut-host only. Then, in place of the Marut-host, Indra himself must be addressed: "O Indra! You are seen, we may say, going with the Marut-deities, who are possessed of supreme lordship, fearless and of equal radiance." Skandasvāmī explains it in the same way. Since the chief intention of the two kinds of meaning is one, one may say it either way.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Saṃdṛkṣase" — "saṃpaśyethāḥ" — the "laṭ"-like "leṭ" in the sense of "liṅ" (लिङर्थे लेट्, पा. ३-४-७), after the root "dṛś" in the sense of prayer; the Vārttika सनोर्गम्मृच्छिभ्याम् / "the ātmanepada after 'sam' with 'ṛ, śru, dṛś'" — the print says that the substitution of the ātmanepada for the "la" after the roots "ṛ," "śru," "dṛś" with the prefix "sam" is laid down in the Vārttika: सम्मृच्छिश्रुदृशिभ्यः; "thās" (second-person singular ātmanepada) → थासः से (पा. ३-४-८०) "se" → "dṛś + se"; लेटोऽडाटौ (पा. ३-४-९४) the augment; "sip" variably in "leṭ" (सिब्बहुलं लेटि, पा. ३-१-३४); the guṇa of the light penultimate would arise by पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च (पा. ७-३-८६) but is set aside by the "saṃjñā-pūrvaka" principle (संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्यः, परिभाषा [number as printed "३-१"]); व्रश्चभ्रस्जसृजमृजयजराजभ्राजच्छशां षः (पा. ८-२-३६) — "ṣ" for the final of "vraśc," "bhrasj," "sṛj," "mṛj," "yaj," "rāj," "bhrāj," "ch" and "śā" — and for the final "ś" of "dṛś," by the rule's "pada-anta"-and-"jhal" reading, "ṣ" in the place of the "ś" before a "jhal" letter; then "ṣ" + "s" → "kṣ" (षढोः कः सि, पा. ८-२-४१) — "ṣ" and "ḍh" → "k" before "s" … Page headers: p. 240 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6"; p. 241 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12 [?]"; p. 242 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā." These three pages are pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose for "dṛkṣase," "saṃjagmānaḥ," "abibhyuṣā," "mandū" and "samānavarcasā," together with a note on the saṃhitā-sandhi of "saṃjagmāno abibhyuṣā." They do not bear on the sense of Rik 6.7. Read at ordinary enlargement; characterized in outline; sūtras that could be read with confidence are kept, numbers as read.

original pp. 240–242

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.7 (Kannada) — characterized; Sūkta 6, Eighth Mantra: Saṃhitā

p. 240. Continuing "dṛkṣase": …by षढोः कः सि (पा. ८-२-४१) the "ṣ" of the root before "s" becomes "k"; by आदेशप्रत्यययोः (पा. ८-३-५९) the "s" of the affix after "k" becomes "ṣ" — so "dṛk + ṣe"; since बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. २-४-७३) allows "luk" for "śap," "śap" might not intervene; the print shows that, with "sip," the form "dṛ + k + ṣa + se" arises and then, by पाघ्राध्मास्थाम्नादाण्दृश्यर्त्तिसर्तिशदसदां पिबजिघ्रधमतिष्ठमनयच्छपश्यर्च्छधौशीयसीदाः (पा. ७-३-७८) "paśya" would replace "dṛś" before a sārvadhātuka beginning with a consonant "śit"-marked affix, but since the "sip" here is not "śit"-marked for that purpose (and the "leṭ" is not a "ś"-affix in that sense), the substitution "paśya" does not occur; "śap" is "p"-marked, so unaccented (अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ, पा. ३-१-४); the "ṣe" is unaccented as a "tiṅ" ending; the root's accent remains; the "a" of "śap" and the "a" before it merge by आतो गुणे / अतो गुणे (पा. ६-१-९४); हिं च … the "dṛkṣase" is not made unaccented by तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) because the particle "hi" precedes it (हि च, पा. ८-१-३४ — "a verb after 'hi' is not made unaccented"). "Saṃjagmānaḥ" — "gamḷ gatau" with the prefix "sam," "liṭ" in the present sense (वर्तमाने लिट्, as printed; छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः, पा. ३-४-६); समो गम्यृच्छिभ्याम् (पा. १-३-२९) the ātmanepada after "sam" with "gam" and "ṛ"; लिटः कानज्वा (पा. ३-२-१०६) "kānac"; लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य (पा. ६-१-८) doubling; हलादिः शेषः (पा. ७-४-६०); कुहोश्चुः (पा. ७-४-६२) "ga" → "ja"; गमहनजनखनघसां लोपः क्ङित्यनङि (पा. ६-४-९८) the elision of the penultimate "a" of "gam" before a "kit/ṅit" affix: "ja-g-m-āna" → "jagmāna"; end-acute by the "c"-mark of "kānac" (चितः); कुगतिप्रादयः (पा. २-२-१८) the compound with "sam," and the kṛt-final member's accent retained (गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्, पा. ६-२-१३९).

p. 241 — "abibhyuṣā." The root "ñibhī bhaye" (to fear); "liṭ" in the Veda (छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः, पा. ३-४-६); the parasmaipada is prescribed by शेषात्कर्तरि परस्मैपदम् (पा. १-३-७८); क्वसुश्च (पा. ३-२-१०७) "kvasu"; "kit," so no guṇa; doubling and shortening; अभ्यासे चर्च (पा. ८-४-५४) — "bi-bhī + vas"; the print then argues the question of the augment "iṭ": by वस्वेकाजाद्घसाम् (पा. २-२-६७?) [as printed] "iṭ" for "kvasu" comes only after a root that is monosyllabic and, having been doubled, ... since "bhī" is a monosyllabic root that is not among "kṛ, sṛ, bhṛ, vṛ, stu, dru, śru," the augment does not come before "vasu"; वसोः संप्रसारणम् (पा. ६-४-१३१) the "samprasāraṇa" of "vas" and संप्रसारणाच्च (पा. ६-१-१०८) the pūrvarūpa; अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां य्वोरियङुवङौ (पा. ६-४-७७) would give "iy" for the "ī" of "bhī," but अजाद्यतष्टाप्-type argument shows that the "iyaṅ" is barred and एरनेकाचोऽसंयोगपूर्वस्य (पा. ६-४-८२) "ya" for the "ī" — "bibhy + uṣ + ā"; आदेशप्रत्यययोः (पा. ८-३-५९) "ṣ" for "s"; and the print adds that, since the "s" of "vas" is not by itself an "ādeśa" nor a "pratyaya," शासिवसिघसीनां च (पा. ८-३-६०) is the sūtra that applies; the negative prefix "a-" is added in a compound with the first member's accent retained.

p. 242 — "mandū," "samānavarcasā"; the sandhi of "saṃjagmāno abibhyuṣā." The print notes (after the discussion of "vasu" with and without "grahaṇa") that in the saṃhitā, in "saṃjagmāno 'bibhyuṣā," the "o" (from "aḥ") before the short "a" — ङसिङसोश्च/एङः पदान्तादति (पा. ६-१-१०९) would absorb the "a" and give the avagraha — but प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपरे (पा. ६-१-११५) keeps the natural form inside the pāda: "saṃjagmāno abibhyuṣā." "Mandū" — "madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu" (to praise, to delight, to be intoxicated, to sleep, to desire, to go): the root is "i"-marked, so इदितो नुम् धातोः (पा. ७-१-५८) the "num" augment; the Uṇādi affix "ku" (कुशङ्कुपीयुनीलगुलिगु [as printed], उ. सू. १-३५ [?]), after the list of words formed with "ku" by nipātana — "mandu" — the end-acute by the affix's accent; the dual "au" → "ū" (प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः, पा. ६-१-१०२). "Samānavarcasā" — "samānaṃ varcaḥ yayoḥ tau" (dual) or "samānaṃ varcaḥ yasya saḥ" (third-case singular), the bahuvrīhi compound; "samāna" is end-acute by its stem; by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. ६-२-१) the first member's own accent remains. ॥७॥

Sūkta 6, The Eighth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12 [?] · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; the left edge of the first lines of the Bhāṣya was clipped in the enlargement, so a few word-beginnings are marked [?].

अनवद्यैरभिद्युभिर्मखः सहस्वदर्चति । गणैरिन्द्रस्य काम्यैः ॥८॥

anavadyair abhidyubhir makhaḥ sahasvad arcati | gaṇair indrasya kāmyaiḥ ||8||

original p. 243

Rik 6.8: Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अनवद्यैः । अभिद्युऽभिः । मखः । सहस्वत् । अर्चति । गणैः । इन्द्रस्य । काम्यैः ॥८॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

मखः प्रवर्तमानोऽयं यज्ञोऽनवद्यैर्दोषरहितैरभिद्युभिर्द्युलोकमभिगतैः काम्यैः फलप्रदत्वेन कामयितव्यैर्गणैर्मरुत्समूहैः सहितमिन्द्रस्येन्द्रं सहस्वद्बलोपेतं यथा भवति तथार्चति । पूजयति । अयं यज्ञो मरुत इन्द्रं चातिशयेन प्रीणयतीत्यर्थः । यज्ञ इत्यादिषु पंचदशसु यज्ञनामसु मखो विष्णुरिति पठितम् । चतुश्चत्वारिंशत्सु अर्चतिकर्मसु अर्चति गायतीति पठितम् ॥ makhaḥ pravartamāno 'yaṃ yajño 'navadyair doṣa-rahitair abhidyubhir dyuloka-m abhigataiḥ kāmyaiḥ phala-pradatvena kāmayitavyair gaṇair marut-samūhaiḥ sahitam indrasyendraṃ sahasvad-balopetaṃ yathā bhavati tathārcati | pūjayati | ayaṃ yajño maruta indraṃ cātiśayena prīṇayatīty arthaḥ | yajña ity ādiṣu pañcadaśasu yajña-nāmasu makho viṣṇur iti paṭhitam | catuścatvāriṃśatsu arcati-karmasu arcati gāyatīti paṭhitam || (Reading notes: the printed "dyulokam abhigataiḥ" is run together and I divide it as shown; the Kannada Pada-meaning, given below, confirms the sense "joined with the Marut-groups who have gone to the heavenly world"; "indrasyendram" is a printed oddity (the genitive "indrasya" followed by the accusative "indram") that I give as printed and flag [?].)

Translation: "'Makhaḥ' — this sacrifice, now going on, 'arcati' — honours, worships — Indra in such a manner that he becomes full of overpowering strength ('sahasvat'), together with the Marut-groups ('gaṇaiḥ'), who are faultless ('anavadyaiḥ'), who have gone to the heavenly world ('abhidyubhiḥ'), who are desirable ('kāmyaiḥ') because they bestow fruit. The sense: this sacrifice gratifies both the Maruts and Indra exceedingly. Among the fifteen names of sacrifice beginning with 'yajña,' 'makhaḥ' and 'viṣṇuḥ' are read; among the forty-four verbs of honouring, 'arcati' and 'gāyati' are read."

Grammar (characterized, sūtras kept; read from the slice and the page at ordinary enlargement): "Anavadyaiḥ" — "na vidyate avadyaṃ yeṣāṃ te anavadyāḥ" — a bahuvrīhi with "nañ"; नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) the second member is end-acute. "Abhidyubhiḥ" — "abhigatā dyaur yaiḥ te abhidyavaḥ" — a bahuvrīhi; "abhi" is acute by its stem-accent (end-acute), and by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. ६-२-१) that accent alone remains. "Makhaḥ" — a stem accent. "Sahasvat" — "sahaḥ balam asminn asti" ("in which there is 'sahas,' strength"); तसौ मत्वर्थे (पा. १-४-१९) — before "matup" the stem is called "bha" and "pada," and so the "s" does not become "ru"; मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (पा. ८-२-९) the "m" of "matup" → "v" after a stem with "m" or "a/ā" penultimate (outside the "yava"-class) → "vat"; "sahas" is first-syllable acute as a नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य word; "matup" is "p"-marked, and its accent is dropped, leaving the stem's accent. "Kāmyaiḥ" — "kamu kāntau" with "ṇic" (कमेर्णिङ्, पा. ३-१-३०), vṛddhi of the penultimate (अत उपधायाः, पा. ७-२-११६), then "yat" (ण्यन्ताद्यत् — अचो यत्, पा. ३-१-९७, as printed "3-1-?2"), the "ṇi" elided (णेरनिटि, पा. ६-४-५१); by the exception यतोऽनावः (पा. ६-१-२१३) to the "tit-svarita" rule (पा. ६-१-१८५), first-syllable acute. The print remarks that "kam" is a root of the "ghaṭādi" class, where "mit" shortening is barred (मितां ह्रस्वः, पा. ६-४-९२, not applying). ॥८॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

मखः (makhaḥ) — (this sacrifice that we are performing) the sacrifice | अनवद्यैः (anavadyaiḥ) — free of faults | अभिद्युभिः (abhidyubhiḥ) — those who bring about heaven (the Maruts, leading to the heavenly world) | काम्यैः (kāmyaiḥ) — desired by those who seek fruit | गणैः (gaṇaiḥ) — with the Marut-troops | (सहितनाद) (sahitanāda) — accompanied | इन्द्रस्य (indrasya) — Indra | सहस्वत् (sahasvat) — so as to make him powerful | अर्चति (arcati) — let it worship. Note on order: the grammar section, which in the print runs from p. 244 through p. 245, and the Pada-meanings are already given above under "Page 243"; what follows is the remainder of p. 244. Page headers: p. 244 "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 245 "A. 1, A. 1, Va. [?]".

original pp. 244–245

Rik 6.8: Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics, end of grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Marut-troops are free of fault and have become able to go to the heavenly world. People who seek the fruit of their wishes desire them. May this sacrifice that we are performing for Indra, accompanied by such Marut-troops, gratify him with worship and the like, and make him strong.

English Translation as printed in the source

This sacrifice is performed in adoration of Indra so as to m[a]ke [sic: printed "mıke"] him powerful, along with the irreproachable, heavenward-tending and amiable bands (of the Maruts).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — Special Topics ॥

The sense of this Ṛk is somewhat strained (kliṣṭa). Its meaning can be stated thus: "May Indra, who is accompanied by the Marut-troops, be well pleased with me by means of this sacrifice that we are performing, and thereby become strong." Of the qualifying words used of the Maruts — "anavadyaiḥ," "abhidyubhiḥ," "kāmyaiḥ" — the meanings are plain.

  • मखः (makhaḥ) — "Among the fifteen sacrifice-names beginning with 'yajña,' the words 'makhaḥ' and 'viṣṇuḥ' are read" (Nighaṇṭu 3-[?]; the numeral printed as "३-१९" is not certain).
  • अर्चति (arcati) — "Among the forty-four 'arcati-karma' names beginning with 'arcati, gāyati,' the word 'arcati' is read" (Nighaṇṭu 3-[?]; printed "३-१९" [?]).

Grammar — see the characterization given under "Page 243" (the print there is continuous: "anavadyaiḥ," "abhidyubhiḥ," "makhaḥ," "sahasvat," "kāmyaiḥ"); p. 245 carries only its last lines, ending at ॥८॥. Accent-marks printed; not reproduced.

Sūkta 6, The Ninth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Page 246 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 247 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. [?]". Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; the bhāṣya was read from enlarged slices. Accent-marks on the Pada text are printed but not reproduced.

अतः परिज्मन्ना गहि दिवो वा रोचनादधि । समस्मिन्नृञ्जते गिरः ॥९॥

ataḥ parijman ā gahi divo vā rocanād adhi | sam asminn ṛñjate giraḥ ||9||

original pp. 246–247

Rik 6.9: Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha, English, start of Special Topics

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अतः । परिऽज्मन् । आ । गहि । दिवः । वा । रोचनात् । अधि । सम् । अस्मिन् । ऋञ्जते । गिरः ॥९॥

ataḥ | pari-jman | ā | gahi | divaḥ | vā | rocanāt | adhi | sam | asmin | ṛñjate | giraḥ ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे परिज्मन् परितो व्यापिन्मरुद्गण अतोऽस्मान्मरुद्गणस्थानादन्तरिक्षाद्वा गहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । दिवो वा । द्युलोकाद्वा समागच्छ । रोचनादधि । दीप्यमानादादित्यमण्डलाद्वा समागच्छ । अस्मदीयकर्मकाले यत्र यत्र तिष्ठसि ततः सर्वस्मादागच्छेत्यर्थः । किमर्थमागमनमिति तदुच्यते । अस्मिन्कर्मणि वर्तमाने ऋत्विग्गिरः स्तुतीः सम्ऋञ्जते । सम्यक् प्रसाधयति । ऋञ्जतिः प्रसाधनकर्मा । नि. ६-[?] इति यास्कः । एताः स्तुतीः श्रोतुमागच्छेत्यर्थः । यद्यप्यृत्विजा मन्त्रस्य प्रयुज्यमानत्वादृञ्जतिधातोरुत्तमपुरुषेण भवितव्यं तथापि परोक्षकृतत्वेन निर्देशात् [two or three words unclear] प्रथमपुरुषप्रयोगः । परोक्षकृतलक्षणं च यास्क आह । ताः त्रिविधा ऋचः परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृता आध्यात्मिक्यश्च । तत्र परोक्षकृताः सर्वाभिर्नामविभक्तिभिर्युज्यन्ते प्रथमपुरुषैश्चाख्यातस्य । नि. २-१ इति ॥ he parijman parito vyāpin marud-gaṇa ato 'smān marud-gaṇa-sthānād antarikṣād vā gahi | asmin karmaṇy āgaccha | divo vā | dyulokād vā samāgaccha | rocanād adhi | dīpyamānād āditya-maṇḍalād vā samāgaccha | asmadīya-karma-kāle yatra yatra tiṣṭhasi tataḥ sarvasmād āgacchety arthaḥ | kim-artham āgamanam iti tad ucyate | asmin karmaṇi vartamāne ṛtvig-giraḥ stutīḥ sam-ṛñjate | samyak prasādhayati | ṛñjatiḥ prasādhana-karmā | ni. 6-[?] iti yāskaḥ | etāḥ stutīḥ śrotum āgacchety arthaḥ | yady apy ṛtvijā mantrasya prayujyamānatvād ṛñjati-dhātor uttama-puruṣeṇa bhavitavyaṃ tathāpi parokṣa-kṛtatvena nirdeśāt [?] prathama-puruṣa-prayogaḥ | parokṣa-kṛta-lakṣaṇaṃ ca yāska āha | tās tri-vidhā ṛcaḥ parokṣa-kṛtāḥ pratyakṣa-kṛtā ādhyātmikyaś ca | tatra parokṣa-kṛtāḥ sarvābhir nāma-vibhaktibhir yujyante prathama-puruṣaiś cākhyātasya | ni. 2-1 iti ||

Translation: "O 'parijman' — O Marut-host, pervading on all sides! 'Ataḥ' — from this place of yours, the Marut-host, or from the atmosphere — 'gahi' — come to this rite. 'Divo vā' — or come from the world of heaven. 'Rocanād adhi' — or come from the shining disc of the sun. The sense is: at the time of our rite, wherever you are standing, from there come. For what purpose the coming? That is said: while this rite is going on, the priests' voices, the praises, 'sam ṛñjate' — adorn well, that is, accomplish well. 'Ṛñjati' is a verb of accomplishing (Yāska, Nirukta 6-[?]). The sense: come to hear these praises. Although, since the mantra is being used by the priest, the root 'ṛñj' ought to be in the first person, nevertheless, because the statement is made in the indirect (parokṣa-kṛta) manner, the third person is used. And Yāska gives the mark of the 'parokṣa-kṛta': 'Those verses are of three kinds: indirect, direct, and personal-spiritual. Of these, the indirect are joined with all the case-endings of nouns, and with the third person of the verb' (Nirukta 2-1)." The Nirukta numeral for the "ṛñjati" reference is printed with a Kannada digit pair that could not be read with certainty; "Nirukta 2-1" for the parokṣa-kṛta definition reads clearly.

Grammar (characterized; dense sūtra-citation, sense already given): The page explains the accent of each word of the Pada text. "Ataḥ" — "etad" + "tasil" in the fifth case (पञ्चम्यास्तसिल्, पा. ५-३-७ [?, numeral not certain]), with "etad" replaced by "a" (एतदोऽश्, पा. ५-३-५ [?]); "śit" marking makes the substitution of the whole stem (शित्त्वात् सर्वादेशः, the reference printed as पा. १-१-५५ [?]); "tasil" is "l"-marked, so the syllable before the suffix is acute (लिति, as printed). "Parijman" — from "aja gati-kṣepaṇayoḥ" with the affix "manin" (अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते, पा. ३-२-७५ [?, printed "३-२-२३"]), the "a" dropped by Vedic usage, and being a vocative it takes "nighāta" (full lowering of accent) (आमन्त्रितस्य च). "Gahi" — "gam" with "śap" dropped (गमेर्बहुलं छन्दसि, पा. २-४-७३ [?]); the "n" elided by the rule for roots with an accent-less "n" (अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलि क्ङिति, पा. ६-४-३७), and "hi" is likewise lowered as a "ṅit"; the printed derivation of "lopaḥ" and "hilopaḥ" (आतो हेः, पा. ६-४-१०५ [?]) is too compressed to reproduce. "Divaḥ" — by the rule on the "ūṭh" substitution for "div" (ऊडिदंपदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः, as printed "ऊडिदमित्यादिना") the case-ending is acute. "Vā" — "cādi" particles are accent-less (चादयोऽनुदात्ताः, फि. ४-[?]). "Rocanāt" — "ruca dīptau" with "yuc" (अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः, पा. ३-२-१४९ [?]), "yu" → "ana" (युवोरनाकौ, पा. ७-१-१), "cit" so end-acute. "Adhi" — as an "adhi-pari" particle without sense of its own it is called a "karma-pravacanīya" (अधिपरी अनर्थकौ, पा. १-४-९३), joined with the "nipāta" designation; first-syllable acute. "Asmin" — the stem "idam" ends in a substitution by "a" etc.; the third-and-following case-endings are then accent-less (पा. २-४-३२ [?]-type rule, "śit" marking, the case-ending is lowered; the whole word is accent-less). "Ṛñjate" — "ṛñji bhṛjī bharjane"; with the preverb "sam" it denotes "accomplishing"; "nighāta." "Giraḥ" — by its stem accent. Printed sūtra-numbers in this paragraph are the least certain part of the page; They are given only where reasonably legible, with [?] where not.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ Kannada, translated, p. 247

हे परिज्मन् (he parijman) — O Maruts, pervading on every side! अतः (ataḥ) — from your place, the atmosphere | दिवो वा (divo vā) — or from the world of heaven | रोचनात् (rocanāt) — from the shining sun-disc | अस्मिन् (asmin) — to this sacrifice that we are performing, that is, to the sacrificial place | अधि गहि (adhi gahi) — come | (वा) — [the priest, the Ṛṣi] | गिरः (giraḥ) — praises | सम्ऋञ्जते (sam-ṛñjate) — he offers for your adornment.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Marut-deities, you are all-pervading. At this time of our sacrifice, if you are in the atmosphere, come from there; if in the heavenly world, come from there; or if you are in the sphere of the sun, come from there. Wherever you are now, come from there. Now the priest — that is, the Ṛṣi Madhucchandas, the seer of this mantra — praises you with praises, for your coming.

English Translation as printed

O pervader-on-all-side[s] [the print has "all-sides" with a hyphen run-on], come hither from the regions (of the Maruts) or from the sky or from the radiant solar sphere. For in the rite (the priest) fully recites your praises.

॥ Special Topics ॥ Kannada, translated; continues onto the next page Page 248 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 249 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. [?]". P. 249 also carries a small "32" at the foot, apparently a printer's signature mark. The Kannada here is quite legible, but the sūtra-numerals are small and several are marked [?].

  • परिज्मन् (parijman) — "going round on all sides"; "moving everywhere." That is, the wind blows always in all places — on earth, in the atmosphere, in heaven, and so on.
  • दिवो वा रोचनादधि (divo vā rocanād adhi) — The commentator says "either from heaven or from the sphere of the sun." Or the word "rocanāt" may be taken to mean "shining," and as a qualifier of "divaḥ" it may be understood as desired. Here, since "adhi" is present, the commentator has explained "rocanāt" as "from the shining sun-sphere." Skandasvāmin says that "adhi" should be construed with the verb "ā gahi."
  • ऋञ्जते (ṛñjate) — "Ṛñjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā" (Nirukta 6-[?]), says Yāska in the Nirukta. Here the priest who praises, the seer of this mantra, Madhucchandas himself, [text continues on p. 248].
original pp. 248–249

Rik 6.9: end of Special Topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (characterized)

॥ Special Topics (continued from p. 247) ॥

…[the priest] does not use the first-person verb but uses a third-person verb-form. The reason: since the deities being praised, the Maruts, are not present before him, he praises them indirectly (and not directly). Such verses — in which the deities are not addressed, but only their praise, or merely some matter, is stated, with the verbs in the third person — belong to the group of verses called "parokṣa-kṛta" (indirect). Among the Ṛks there are three kinds: parokṣa-kṛta, pratyakṣa-kṛta, and ādhyātmika. This matter of Yāska's I have explained earlier (page "[?]1" — the numeral is not clear).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā — Grammatical Derivation ॥ characterized in outline, with every named sūtra kept in three layers, as the page is dense scholastic derivation of accent and affix that adds nothing to the sense already given

  1. "Ataḥ" (अतः, ataḥ). The print explains: "pañcamyās tasil" — पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (pañcamyās tasil, "tasil [comes] after [a word in] the fifth case," पा. ५-३-७ [?]) — the affix "tasil" comes optionally after "kim," the pronouns, and "bahu," when they stand in the fifth case, with the exception of "dvi"-etc. words. So "etad + ṅasi" is analysed "etasmāt," and "tasil" comes. Since a word ending in a taddhita affix is a pratipadika, the fifth-case ending is elided by सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः (supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ, "the case-ending is elided after a root or a stem," पा. २-४-७१) — the print gives this as "2-4-71" and I accept it, being a standard sūtra. Then एतदोऽश् (etado 'ś, "the substitute 'a' for 'etad' before 'tasil'-like affixes," पा. ५-३-५ [?]) is discussed at length: the print says some read the sūtra as "etado 'n" (substituting "an") and some as "etado 'ś" (as in the Kāśikā), the latter being "śit," hence a whole-stem substitution (शित्त्वात् सर्वादेशः, śittvāt sarvādeśaḥ); a further reference to अनेकाल् शित् सर्वस्य (anekāl śit sarvasya, "a multi-lettered substitute, or one marked 'ś,' replaces the whole," पा. १-१-५५) is made, so that "etad" is wholly replaced by "a" and "ataḥ" results. The print adds that the discussion of whether "n" would receive the "it" designation (and therefore be dropped) is settled by the fact that "an" is a multi-lettered substitute. The affix "tasil," being "l"-marked, makes the letter before it acute (लिति, पा. ६-१-१९३ [?]). "Parts of this paragraph — on how the "an"/"aś" reading affects the sūtra, and on the Kāśikā's wording — are too crowded and too partially legible for me to reproduce line by line.

  2. "Parijman" (परिज्मन्, parijman). अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते (anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante, "[the affixes 'vanip' etc.] are also seen after other roots," पा. ३-२-७५ [?, printed "३-२-२३"]) — from "aja gati-kṣepaṇayoḥ," with the affix "manin" among "kvip, vanip, viṭ"-type affixes; by Vedic licence the "a" of the root "aja" is dropped (the print notes the Vedic precedent "parijmānaṃ sukhaṃ ratham" [Ṛg-saṃhitā, 1-[?]; the reference is unclear], where "parijman" is derived in another form). Being a vocative, it is accent-less by आमन्त्रितस्य च (āmantritasya ca, "[a vocative is lowered]," पा. ८-१-१९).

  3. "Gahi" (गहि, gahi). From "gam̐ gatau" — in the imperative second-person singular, "sip" is placed; by सेर्ह्यपिच्च (ser hy apic ca, "'hi' replaces 'si' of the imperative, and is not 'pit'," पा. ३-४-८७) "sip" becomes "hi," so "gam + hi." Since "hi" is not "pit," it is treated as "ṅit" (सार्वधातुकमपित्, sārvadhātukam apit, "a sārvadhātuka not marked 'p' is as if 'ṅ'-marked," पा. १-२-४), and so अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलि क्ङिति (anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanotyādīnām anunāsika-lopo jhali kṅiti, "of roots with accent-less teaching, and of 'van-ati,' 'tan-oti' and the like, the nasal is dropped before 'jh'-class sounds when followed by 'k' or 'ṅ'-marked affixes," पा. ६-४-३७) drops the "m" of "gam." The print then explains, with असिद्धवदत्राभात् (asiddhavad atrābhāt, "[what follows] is treated as not-having-occurred in this section up to 'bhāt'," पा. ६-४-२२), that this elision of the nasal is treated as invisible for the purpose of अतो हेः (ato heḥ, "'hi' is elided after a short-'a' ending," पा. ६-४-१०५). Hence "hi" is not elided here (the root-final does not count as "a"-ending); the form remains "gahi."

  4. "Divaḥ" (दिवः, divaḥ). The case-ending is acute by ऊडिदंपदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः (ūḍidam-padādy-ap-pum-rai-dyubhyaḥ, पा. ६-१-१७१).

  5. "Vā" (वा, vā). A member of the "cādi" group of particles, accent-less by चादयोऽनुदात्ताः (cādayo 'nudāttāḥ, फि. ४-१२ [?, printed "४-१२"]).

  6. "Rocanāt" (रोचनात्, rocanāt). "ruca dīptau" is an accent-less-marked root, so "yuc" comes after a root beginning with a consonant and "anudātta-it" (अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः, anudāttetaś ca halādeḥ, पा. ३-२-१४९ [?, printed "३-२-१४९"]); thus "ruc + yu." By युवोरनाकौ (yuvor anākau, "'yu' and 'vu' are replaced by 'ana' and 'aka'," पा. ७-१-१) "yu" → "ana"; "ruc + ana," with guṇa of the light penultimate → "rocana"; the fifth-case singular gives "rocanāt." Since the affix is "c"-marked, चितः (citaḥ, "[a word] with 'c' as marker has its end acute," पा. ६-१-१६३) applies, and with the Vārttika on that sūtra (चितः सप्रकृतेर्बह्वकजर्थम्, citaḥ saprakṛter bahv-akaj-artham, "the end of the whole [stem + affix] taking a 'c'-marked affix is acute — for the sake of 'bahuc' and 'akac'") — "the end of the full stem + affix is acute; otherwise the places where the affixes 'bahuc' and 'akac' come would not be fulfilled." The print illustrates with विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात् (vibhāṣā supo bahuc purastāt, पा. ५-३-६८), "the affix 'bahuc' comes optionally before [the stem] — as in 'īṣad-ūnaḥ paṭuḥ — bahupaṭuḥ' ('slightly deficient clever one')," and अव्ययसर्वनाम्नामकच् प्राक् टेः (avyaya-sarvanāmnām akac prāk ṭeḥ, पा. ५-३-७१) — here the page ends with the sūtra-statement broken off at "…ಎಂಬುದ" and the argument continues on p. 250.

Printed numerals in this section — all the reference-numbers in "पा." brackets — are small and some are uncertain; [?] marks where they could not be confirmed. Those that agree with the standard Aṣṭādhyāyī numbering as recalled — 1-1-55, 2-4-71, 6-4-22, 6-4-37, 6-4-105, 7-1-1, 8-1-19 — are given without comment; The rest has not been checked. Page 250 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 251 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. [?]". Rik 6.10 is the last Rik of Sūkta 6. Accents are printed on the Saṃhitā and Pada of Rik 6.10, and not reproduced.

original pp. 250–251

Rik 6.9: end of grammar; Rik 6.10: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar begins

Grammar of Rik 6.9, continued (characterized) Kannada, translated; the page-top continues the "Rocanāt" discussion of p. 249 Final Rik of the sūkta. Accents are printed on this page; not reproduced.

  • "Rocanāt," end of discussion. The affix "akac" coming by अव्ययसर्वनाम्नामकच् प्राक् टेः (avyaya-sarvanāmnām akac prāk ṭeḥ, पा. ५-३-७१, "'akac' comes before the last 'ṭi' syllable of an indeclinable or a pronoun") comes "behind the 'ṭi'"; the example given is "anyake." The print says that if the Vārttika on "citaḥ" were not taken in this sense, the final letter would not be acute in these two examples; in "rocana," the end of the whole stem-and-affix combination is acute.
  • "Adhi" (अधि, adhi). अधिपरी अनर्थकौ (adhi-parī anarthakau, "'adhi' and 'pari,' when without a distinct sense, are 'karma-pravacanīya,'" पा. १-४-९३): the print says that "adhi" and "pari," not conveying a particular meaning, receive the name "karma-pravacanīya" and also the name "nipāta"; since "adhi" holds the name "nipāta" along with "karma-pravacanīya," it is first-syllable acute by निपाता आद्युदात्ताः (nipātā ādyudāttāḥ, फि. [?]; the numeral is printed "४-८०" but I am not sure of it).
  • "Asmin" (अस्मिन्, asmin). When "idam" is followed by the seventh-case ending, by त्यदादीनामः (tyadādīnām aḥ, "of 'tyad' etc. the last letter is replaced by 'a'," पा. ७-२-१०२) the last letter takes "a," and then अतो गुणे (ato guṇe, पा. ६-१-९७) gives the later form ("ida + ṅi"). The print then argues that since "parijman" has pointed to the Marut-troop and "asmin" refers back to it ("asmin" here refers to the sacrifice, which is named to be the very place of coming), this is a case of "anvādeśa" — a reference back — by the definition quoted in the print ("kiñcit kāryaṃ vidhātum upāttasya kāryāntaraṃ vidhātuṃ punar upādānam anvādeśaḥ," "anvādeśa is the repeated mention of what has been mentioned for one purpose, in order to enjoin another operation on it"). Hence इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ (idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau, "in an anvādeśa, 'idam' is replaced by an accent-less 'aś' before the third-case and following endings," पा. २-४-३२): "aś," being "śit," replaces the whole of "idam." The seventh-case ending "ṅi" is replaced by "smin" by जसिङसोः स्मात्स्मिनौ [the print reads "ङसिङ्योः स्मात्स्मिनौ," ṅasi-ṅyoḥ smāt-sminau, पा. ७-१-१५], "'smāt' and 'smin' replace the fifth- and seventh-case endings after an a-ending pronoun"; so "asmin." The ending is accent-less by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (anudāttau sup-pitau, पा. ३-१-४). So "asmin" is wholly accent-less.
  • "Ṛñjate" (ऋञ्जते, ṛñjate). "Ṛji bhṛji bharjane" (the root meaning "to fry"; also, in use, "to adorn"). The root is "idit," so "num" comes by इदितो नुम् धातोः (idito num dhātoḥ, पा. ७-१-५८). Then the anusvāra and parasavarṇa (पा. ८-३-२४ and ८-४-५८) give "ṛñj-." In the present ātmanepada third-person singular, "ṛñjate." It is accent-less by तिङ्ङतिङः (tiṅ atiṅaḥ, पा. ८-१-२८). The print then quotes the verse on the force of the preverb: "उपसर्गेण धात्वर्थो बलादन्यत्र नीयते । प्रहाराहारसंहारविहारपरिहारवत् ॥" (upasargeṇa dhātv-artho balād anyatra nīyate | prahārāhāra-saṃhāra-vihāra-parihāravat ||, "By a preverb the meaning of a root is forcibly led elsewhere — as in 'prahāra,' 'āhāra,' 'saṃhāra,' 'vihāra,' 'parihāra'"). The print appears to read "upasarge ca" for "upasargeṇa" — the first word is read here from small type; The standard form of this well-known verse is given and the discrepancy flagged. The Kannada explains: the root "hṛ" means "taking," but with "pra" it means "a blow," with "ā" it means "food, eating," with "saṃ" it means "killing, destruction," with "vi" "sport, roaming," with "pari" "abandoning" — thus various meanings appear through the force of the preverb. "In the same way, in other places too, differing meanings arise for roots through the force of the preverb: that is the sense of the verse. Here, although the root 'ṛji' is read in the sense of 'frying,' the preverb 'sam' is joined to it, so the root 'ṛji' conveys the sense of 'adorning.'"
  • "Giraḥ" (गिरः, giraḥ). The stem-accent (prātipadika-svara) comes. ॥९॥

Sūkta 6, The Tenth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इतो वा सातिमीमहे दिवो वा पार्थिवादधि । इन्द्रं महो वा रजसः ॥१०॥

ito vā sātim īmahe divo vā pārthivād adhi | indraṃ maho vā rajasaḥ ||10||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इतः । वा । सातिम् । ईमहे । दिवः । वा । पार्थिवात् । अधि । इन्द्रम् । महः । वा । रजसः ॥१०॥

itaḥ | vā | sātim | īmahe | divaḥ | vā | pārthivāt | adhi | indram | mahaḥ | vā | rajasaḥ ||10||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Kannada script; read from the page at 150 dpi and not separately enlarged. [?] marks where a word is not clearly read.

इन्द्रं देवं प्रति सातिं धनदानमीमहे । आधिक्येन योजयामहे । कस्मात्कुत इति तदुच्यते । इतोऽस्मादभिदृश्यमानात्पार्थिवात्पृथिवीलोकाद्वा दिवो वा द्युलोकाद्वा महो महतः प्रौढाद्रजसो वा पक्ष्यादीनां रञ्जकादन्तरिक्षलोकाद्वा । आयमिन्द्रो यतः कुतश्चिदानीयास्मभ्यं धनं प्रयच्छेदित्यर्थः । सप्तदशसु याच्ञाकर्मसु ईमहे याम… [?] इति पठितम् ॥ इतः । इदमंशब्दात्पञ्चमी… indraṃ devaṃ prati sātiṃ dhana-dānam īmahe | ādhikyena yojayāmahe | kasmāt-kuta iti tad ucyate | ito 'smād abhidṛśyamānāt pārthivāt pṛthivī-lokād vā divo vā dyulokād vā maho mahataḥ prauḍhād rajaso vā pakṣyādīnāṃ rañjakād antarikṣa-lokād vā | āyam indro yataḥ kutaścid ānīyāsmabhyaṃ dhanaṃ prayacched ity arthaḥ | saptadaśasu yācñā-karmasu īmahe yām[?] iti paṭhitam || itaḥ | idam-aṃśabdāt pañcamī…

Translation: "Toward Indra, the god, we 'īmahe' — we earnestly request, we employ with eagerness — 'sāti,' the giving of wealth. From where? That is said: 'itaḥ' — from this earth-world, the 'pārthiva' that is here seen — or 'divo vā' — from the heavenly world — or 'maho vā rajasaḥ' — from the great, expansive 'rajas,' that is, the atmosphere, the region that colours the birds and others ['rañjaka' — 'that which gives colour']. The sense: may this Indra, bringing it from wherever, give us wealth. Among the seventeen verbs of begging, 'īmahe' is read ['yāmi' [?] — the reading of the end of the quotation is not clear]."

Grammar (begins; characterized): The page begins the derivation of "itaḥ" — from "idam" with the affix "tasil" after the fifth case, with "idam" replaced by "iś" (इदम इश्, पा. ५-३-३ [?]; "śit," so whole-stem substitution, शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः); a long scholastic discussion follows about whether the accent of "tasil" (the "l"-marked affix, making the syllable before it acute) or the accent of the case-ending (the "ūḍidam"-type rule, ऊडिदंपदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः, पा. ६-१-१७१) prevails, the rule आभ्यां विभिः [?] / लिति (पा. ६-१-१९३) / परत्वान्नित्यत्वाच्च — "pratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam" (पा. १-४-२, "when there is conflict, the later rule prevails") — and पश्चात्सेशः प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः (paścāt seśaḥ prāg-diśo vibhaktiḥ, पा. ५-३-१ [?]) being the rule that names the "tasil"-type endings "vibhakti." It is argued that the case-ending is accent-less and the stem "idam" is acute; whether the rule "sakṛd-gatau vipratiṣedhe yad bādhitaṃ tad bādhitam eva" (the Paribhāṣā "once a rule has been set aside by another it stays set aside," परि. ४० [?]) applies is raised, and the page ends in mid-argument, at "…tasil udāttatvaṃ," continuing on p. 252. Much of this page (the second half, in particular) is too crowded and too small in print for me to reproduce line by line, and I do not attempt it. Page 252 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 253 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. [?]". P. 252 is a page of continuous small print in Kannada script — the end of Sāyaṇa's own grammatical notes — read from enlarged slices; numerals marked [?] are not certain.

original pp. 252–253

Rik 6.10: end of Sanskrit grammar, Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics; Kannada grammar begins

Sāyaṇa's grammatical notes on Rik 6.10, continued and ended Sanskrit in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; the first lines belong to the argument about "itaḥ" begun on p. 251, and only its tail is given This stretch — the end of the "itaḥ" discussion — is a compressed objection-and-answer, with a half-clipped sūtra-quotation and a numeral that cannot be read; The words are given as far as they could be read and are not completed. Its upshot, as far as it can be followed, is that the objection is answered, "itaḥ" standing as formed.

…स्यादिति चेन्न । यत्र च्छबयोः सावर्णान्तत्वे न गोश्चान्नावर्णेति । पा. ६-१-[१२?]… निषेधात् । न च पुंसः प्रसङ्गविज्ञानं … चेत्येतत्सार्वत्रिकं लक्ष्यानुरोधेन क्वचिदेव तदाश्रयणादिति । … syād iti cen na | yatra cchabayoḥ sāvarṇāntatve na goś cānnāvarṇeti [?] | pā. 6-1-[?] … niṣedhāt | na ca puṃsaḥ prasaṅga-vijñānaṃ … cety etat sārvatrikaṃ lakṣyānurodhena kvacid eva tad-āśrayaṇād iti |

सातिम् । षणु दाने । धात्वादेः षः सः । पा. ६-१-६४ । भावे क्तिन् । जनसनखनां सञ्झलोः । पा. ६-४-४२ । इति नकारस्यात्वम् । तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च । पा. ७-२-९ । इति निषेधादिण्न भवति । नित्स्वरे प्राप्ते उदात्त इत्यस्य निवृत्त्या ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च । पा. ३-३-९७ । इति निपातनादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । sātim | ṣaṇu dāne | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | pā. 6-1-64 | bhāve ktin | jana-sana-khanāṃ sañjhaloḥ | pā. 6-4-42 | iti nakārasyātvam | titutra-tathasi-susara-kaseṣu ca | pā. 7-2-9 | iti niṣedhād iṇ na bhavati | nit-svare prāpte udātta ity asya nivṛttyā ūti-yūti-jūti-sāti-heti-kīrtayaś ca | pā. 3-3-97 | iti nipātanād antodāttatvam |

"Sātim" — from "ṣaṇu dāne"; the initial "ṣ" becomes "s" (धात्वादेः षः सः, dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ, "the initial 'ṣ' of a root becomes 's'," पा. ६-१-६४); "ktin" in the sense of the action (भावे क्तिन्, bhāve ktin); the "n" of the root is replaced by "ā" (जनसनखनां सञ्झलोः, jana-sana-khanāṃ sañjhaloḥ, "'ā' replaces the nasal of 'jan,' 'san,' 'khan' before 'jh'-class sounds and 'san'," पा. ६-४-४२); the augment "iṭ" does not come, by the prohibition तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च (titutra-tatha-sisu-sara-kaseṣu ca, पा. ७-२-९); the accent that would come by "n"-marking (the rule for "nit"-affixes) is set aside, and ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च (ūti-yūti-jūti-sāti-heti-kīrtayaś ca, पा. ३-३-९७) lists "sāti" as an irregular formation ("nipātana") with the end-acute.

ईमहे । ईज् गतौ । श्यनोऽपि बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । अस्य धातोर् … [?] तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशात् । पा. ६-१-१८६ । इति लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । न च तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । चवायोगे प्रथमा । पा. ८-१-५९ [the standard number; the print's numeral is small] । इति निषेधात् । उत्तरवाक्ययोरपि हि वाशब्दयोगादन्यथा वाक्यापरिपूर्तेश्च विभक्तेरवश्यमध्याहारात् [?] अपेक्ष्यैषा प्रथमा तिङ्विभक्तिरिति । īmahe | īj gatau | śyano 'pi bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | asya dhātor … [?] tāsy-anudātten-ṅid-ad-upadeśāt | pā. 6-1-186 | iti lasārvadhātukasyānudāttatve dhātu-svara eva śiṣyate | na ca tiṅ-ṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | cavā-yoge prathamā | pā. 8-1-59 [standard number] | iti niṣedhāt | uttara-vākyayor api hi vā-śabda-yogād anyathā vākyāparipūrteś ca vibhakter avaśyam adhyāhārāt [?] apekṣyaiṣā prathamā tiṅ-vibhaktir iti |

"Īmahe" — "īj gatau"; "śyan" is also optionally elided in the Veda (बहुलं छन्दसि, bahulaṃ chandasi), so there is "luk." Since the personal ending is accent-less by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तम् (tāsy-anudātten-ṅid-ad-upadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam, पा. ६-१-१८६), only the root's own accent remains. And there is no "nighāta" (lowering of the verb) by तिङ्ङतिङः (tiṅ atiṅaḥ, पा. ८-१-२८), because of the prohibition चवायोगे प्रथमा (cavā-yoge prathamā, "the first [verb] is not lowered when joined with 'ca,' 'vā,' etc.," पा. ८-१-५९ [the standard number; the print's numeral is small]). The last clause (that in both the later half-lines the word "vā" is connected, and that otherwise the sentence would be incomplete, so that this "first tiṅ-ending" must be supplied) I read only in part and give as my best reading, marked [?].

दिवः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । divaḥ | ūḍidam ity ādinā vibhakter udāttatvam |

"Divaḥ" — the case-ending is acute by "ūḍidam…" etc.

पार्थिवात् । प्रथ प्रख्याने । प्रथित इति पृथिवी । प्रथेः षिवन् सम्प्रसारणं च । उ. १-[१३०?] । इति षिवन्प्रत्ययः । षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च । पा. ४-१-४१ । इति ङीष् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । शेषनिघातेनानुदात्तादिः पृथिवीशब्दः । पृथिव्या विकार इत्यर्थे ओरञ् इत्यनुवृत्तावनुदात्तादेश्च । पा. ४-३-१४० । इत्यञ् । यस्येति च । पा. ६-४-१४८ । इतीकारलोपः । तद्धितेष्वचामादेः । पा. ७-२-११७ । इत्यादिवृद्धिः । रपरत्वम् । पा. १-१-५१ । ञ्णित्यादिर्नित्यमित्याद्युदात्तः । pārthivāt | pratha prakhyāne | prathita iti pṛthivī | prather ṣivan samprasāraṇaṃ ca | u. 1-[130?] | iti ṣivan-pratyayaḥ | ṣid-gaurādibhyaś ca | pā. 4-1-41 | iti ṅīṣ | pratyaya-svareṇodāttaḥ | śeṣa-nighātenānudāttādiḥ pṛthivī-śabdaḥ | pṛthivyā vikāra ity arthe oraj ity anuvṛttāv anudāttādeś ca | pā. 4-3-140 | ity añ | yasyeti ca | pā. 6-4-148 | itīkāra-lopaḥ | taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ | pā. 7-2-117 | ity ādi-vṛddhiḥ | rasparatvam | pā. 1-1-51 | ñṇity ādir nityam ity ādyudāttaḥ |

"Pārthivāt" — from "prath prakhyāne" ("that which is spread out is 'pṛthivī'"); the Uṇādi "prather ṣivan samprasāraṇaṃ ca" gives the affix "ṣivan" (Uṇādi 1-[130?]; the print's numerals are "१-१३०" but I do not trust them); the feminine "ṅīṣ" by षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च (ṣid-gaurādibhyaś ca, पा. ४-१-४१); the affix gives the acute, and by the lowering of the rest the stem "pṛthivī" begins accent-less. In the sense "a modification of the earth" ("pṛthivyā vikāraḥ"), the affix "añ" comes by ओरञ् (oraj, "'añ' in the sense of 'its modification' after a stem ending in a short 'u' [here 'o']") carried forward with अनुदात्तादेश्च (anudāttādeś ca, पा. ४-३-१४०); the "ī" is dropped by यस्येति च (yasyeti ca, पा. ६-४-१४८); the first vowel takes vṛddhi by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ, पा. ७-२-११७); with "r" following (रपरत्वम्, पा. १-१-५१); and by "ñit/ṇit" the first syllable is acute (ञ्णित्यादिर्नित्यम्, पा. ६-१-१९७ [as the rule is usually numbered]).

अधि । निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तः । इन्द्रम् । रन्प्रत्ययान्त आद्युदात्तः । महः । महत इत्यस्याकारतकारयोर्लोपश्छान्दसः । साके… [?] इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । रजसः । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥१०॥ adhi | nipātatvād ādyudāttaḥ | indram | ran-pratyayānta ādyudāttaḥ | mahaḥ | mahata ity asyākāra-takārayor lopaś chāndasaḥ | sāvekāce [?] iti vibhakter udāttatvam | rajasaḥ | nab-viṣayasyānisantasyety ādyudāttatvam ||10||

"Adhi" — a particle, first-syllable acute. "Indram" — ending in the affix "ran," first-syllable acute. "Mahaḥ" — from "mahat," the "a" and "t" being dropped by Vedic licence; the case-ending is acute ("sāvekāce [?]" is read from small type and uncertain). "Rajasaḥ" — by नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (nab-viṣayasyānisantasya, फि. [?]), first-syllable acute. ॥१०॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ Kannada, translated, p. 252

(वयम् vayam — we) इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | इतः पार्थिवात् वा (itaḥ pārthivāt vā) — either from this earth-world that is seen before our eyes | दिवो वा (divo vā) — or from the heavenly world | महः (mahaḥ) — great | रजसो वा (rajaso vā) — or from the atmosphere that is the refuge of birds and the like | सातिम् (sātim) — for the obtaining of wealth | अधीमहे (adhīmahe, so printed; the "adhi" of the Pada text taken together with "īmahe") — we pray.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Now, before our eyes, whether from this earth-world, from the heavenly world, or from the atmosphere-world, we pray to Indra that he bring wealth and give it to us.

English Translation

We pray to Indra for riches either from this earth, heaven, or from the vast intermediate region.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — Special Topics ॥ Kannada, translated; p. 253

  • सातिम् (sātim) — This word, derived from the root "ṣaṇu dāne," has the sense of "gift," "giving." What is given? Wealth and prosperity, or the other things we need.
  • ईमहे (īmahe) — We pray, we beg. Among the seventeen verbs meaning "to beg," beginning with "yāmi," the word "īmahe" is read (Nighaṇṭu [?]).
  • पार्थिवात् (pārthivāt) — "pṛthivyā vikāraḥ pārthivaḥ, tasmāt" — that which is a modification of the earth: that is, the "earth-world."
  • रजसः (rajasaḥ) — The commentator says "pakṣyādīnāṃ rañjakād antarikṣa-lokāt" — "from the atmosphere-world, that which gives colour/delight to the birds and the others." That is, the one that gives joy to the birds, that is, that is their refuge and the main place for them to move about [the Kannada: saṃtoṣavannu uṃṭumāḍuva, eṃdare āśraya-bhūtavāda, mukhya saṃcāra-māḍalu avakāśavuḷḷa].

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā — Grammatical Derivation, Kannada commentary (characterized) ॥ Reference numerals in this section follow the print where legible; the "सावेकाच" clause in the Sanskrit notes above is read from small type and is uncertain. Page 254 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 255 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. [?]". Characterized in outline per the project convention; every named sūtra and paribhāṣā is kept in three layers. Numerals in brackets are small and several are uncertain, marked [?].

  • "Itaḥ" (इतः, itaḥ). Since "idam" is a fifth-case word, "tasil" is added by पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (pañcamyās tasil, पा. ५-३-७), and the fifth-case ending is elided (luk) after the "tasil." Then "idam + tasil": by इदम इश् (idama iś, "'iś' replaces 'idam' before a 'prāg-diśīya' affix," पा. ५-३-३) "idam" gets the substitute "iś." Since "iś" is "śit," by the paribhāṣā अनेकाल् शित् सर्वस्य (anekāl śit sarvasya, पा. १-१-५५) it takes the place of the whole of "idam." Then "i + tas" → with "ru" and visarga: "itaḥ."
  • The print then takes up a question of accent: the rule ऊडिदंपदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः (ūḍidam-padādy-ap-pum-rai-dyubhyaḥ, पा. ६-१-१७१) ("the case-ending is acute after the stems 'ūṭh-' etc.," more exactly, after the six substitutes of "pad, dan, nas, māsa, hṛd, niś, asan" etc. [पा. ६-१-६३] and the words "ap, pum, rai, div," which are end-acute) applies to the endings following them, not to "pronoun" or "idam"-type words; and लिति (liti, "the syllable before an 'l'-marked affix is acute," पा. ६-१-१९३) applies to "tasil." The print argues that these two rules each have scope of their own — "liti" in cases like "ābhyām" and "ābhiḥ" (where the case-ending is "bhyām," "bhis" etc.), while "ūḍidam" is applicable in words like "pācakaḥ" (the end-"ṇvul" form) and "pacanam" (the end-"lyuṭ" form) — and that "neither is called 'nitya' (inevitably applicable)" by the definition कृताकृतप्रसङ्गित्वं नित्यत्वम् (kṛtākṛta-prasaṅgitvaṃ nityatvam, "a rule is 'nitya' if it applies whether or not the other has applied"): "Whether or not the rule 'ūḍidam' applies, the rule 'liti' stays applicable; whether or not 'liti' applies, 'ūḍidam' stays applicable; therefore both are 'nitya,' and one cannot be said to be stronger on the ground of being 'nitya.'" The argument continues onto the next page.
original pp. 254–255

Rik 6.10: Kannada grammar (vipratiṣedha argument; "sātim," "īmahe")

The "itaḥ" accent-conflict (continued from p. 253; characterized). The page opens: "…[neither rule] is disabled; both rules apply to 'itaḥ.' Which rule then comes into force? — when this is asked, the answer is विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम् (vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam, "in a conflict, the later rule prevails," पा. १-४-२)." The print explains the term: "vipratiṣedha" is the situation in which two rules, each having its own sphere of application elsewhere, are found to apply at once to a single form; of the two, the later rule in the Aṣṭādhyāyī operates. So the later rule, लिति (liti, पा. ६-१-१९३), prevails, and the syllable before "tasil" (the "i" of "itaḥ") is acute. The print then notes that the rule प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः (prāg-diśo vibhaktiḥ, पा. ५-३-१) and the following sūtras up to दिक्शब्देभ्यः… (पा. ५-३-२७ [?]) give the affixes in that section the name "vibhakti," so that "tasil" is itself a "vibhakti," and by ऊडिदम् the case-ending of "idam" would have been acute [unless the later rule prevails].

Then follows the discussion on the principle सकृद्गतौ विप्रतिषेधे यद्बाधितं तद्बाधितमेव (sakṛd-gatau vipratiṣedhe yad bādhitaṃ tad bādhitam eva, "in a conflict that arises once, what has been set aside stays set aside," Paribhāṣā [?]) and the counter-principle पुनःप्रसङ्गविज्ञानात्सिद्धम् (punaḥ-prasaṅga-vijñānāt siddham, "established by the recognition of a fresh occasion for application," Paribhāṣā [?]): the first says a rule once set aside by a "vipratiṣedha" does not revive; the second says that when a fresh occasion arises it may apply again. The print argues, through the examples "yataḥ" and "tataḥ" (where the rule सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः (sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ, "the third and following case-endings, when after a stem with more than one vowel, are acute," पा. ६-१-[१६८?]) would apply and where "tasil" would be acute), that the principle of "no revival" is not meant to apply everywhere — "it holds only where the usage requires it" — and so in "yataḥ, tataḥ" the "tasil" ending is acute, while the case-endings of the plural "su" after words of more than one vowel behave otherwise. The text then notes the rule न गोश्वन्साववर्णराडङ्क्रुङ्कृद्भ्यः (na go-śvan-sāvavarṇa-rāḍ-aṅ-kru-ṅkṛdbhyaḥ, पा. ६-१-१८२) — the printed list "go, śvan, … rāj, …kṛt" — which forbids the acute of the third-and-following case-endings (sāvekāc rule) for these words, and that, for "yataḥ," "tataḥ," the final result is: they are first-syllable acute [or: acute on the first syllable, "ādyudātta"]. This whole passage is scholastic argument over accent-rule precedence and is too compressed and partly clipped in the print to be reproduced line by line; the outline above is a best summary of its direction. Not every step of it is claimed to have been followed.

"Sātim" (सातिम्, sātim; p. 255). The Kannada commentary restates the derivation: from "ṣaṇu dāne"; धात्वादेः षः सः (dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ, पा. ६-१-६४) turns the initial "ṣ" into "s," so the root is "san-"; the "n"... "ktin" is added in the sense of the action (भावे … क्तिन्). Then जनसनखनां सञ्झलोः (jana-sana-khanāṃ sañjhaloḥ, पा. ६-४-४२) — "when an affix beginning with a 'jh'-class sound, or 'san,' or an affix marked 'kit'/'ṅit', follows, 'ā' replaces the final of 'jan,' 'san,' 'khan'" — so the "n" of "san" becomes "ā" and there is "sa + ā + ti," in long-vowel sandhi "sāti." Next, "iṭ" would come by आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ, पा. ७-२-३५) — an "ārdhadhātuka" beginning with a consonant other than "y" — but the ten items "ti, tu, tra, ta, tha, si, su, sara, ka, se" in तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च (titutra-tatha-sisu-sara-kaseṣu ca, पा. ७-२-९) prevent "iṭ" with "kṛt" affixes; "ktin," a "kṛt," takes no "iṭ." Since the affix "ktin" is "n"-marked, ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (ñnity ādir nityam, पा. ६-१-१९७) would make the first syllable acute [for ṇit/ñit affixes; for "nit" in the strict sense, the print says "the first syllable would be acute by the rule"], but the listed words "ūti, yūti, jūti, sāti, heti, kīrti" in ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च (ūti-yūti-jūti-sāti-heti-kīrtayaś ca, पा. ३-३-९७) are formed irregularly ("nipātana") as end-acute — and so "sātim" is end-acute.

"Īmahe" (ईमहे, īmahe; p. 255). After the root "īj gatau," the present, first-person plural "mahiṅ" is placed; the "ṭi" part of the ending becomes "e" by टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे (ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e, पा. ३-४-७९). "Śyan" would come by दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् (divādibhyaḥ śyan, पा. ३-१-६९), but बहुलं छन्दसि (bahulaṃ chandasi, पा. २-४-७३) gives "luk" (elision). The print says: although this sūtra mentions "śap" only, the word "bahulam" makes "śyan" also elided. So "īmahe." Since the root "īj" is "j"-marked [?], by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तम् (पा. ६-१-१८६) the personal ending would be accent-less; and so the "ī" of the root keeps its end-acute by धातोः (पा. ६-१-१६२, the rule giving the root its end-acute). तिङ्ङतिङः (tiṅ atiṅaḥ, पा. ८-१-२८) would lower a verb after a non-verb; but चवायोगे प्रथमा (cavā-yoge prathamā, पा. ८-१-५९) forbids lowering of the first verb when "ca," "vā" etc. are in connection, so the word does not become wholly accent-less. The page ends in mid-sentence, at "Ādare…" ("But [if]…"), the argument on "īmahe" continuing on p. 256. Page 256 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 257 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. [?]". P. 257 also carries a small "33" at the foot, evidently a printer's signature mark. Characterized in outline; sūtras kept.

original pp. 256–257

Rik 6.10: end of grammar; close of Sūkta 6

"Īmahe" — the "cavā-yoge" difficulty (continued from p. 255; characterized). The print raises a doubt: since this mantra contains only one finite verb, how can it be "first-uttered" (prathamoccārita) and hence escape the lowering of accent? The answer given: the Rik really consists of three sentences — (1) "itaḥ pārthivāl lokād vā indraṃ prati sātim adhi īmahe" (from this earth-world, we ask Indra for gain); (2) "indraṃ prati sātim divo vā adhi īmahe" (or from heaven); (3) "rajasaḥ (antarikṣa-lokād vā) indraṃ prati sātim adhi īmahe" (or from the atmosphere). The "īmahe" of the first sentence is the first-uttered one; the "cavā-yoge prathamā" prohibition therefore applies to it (the verb, being first, is not lowered). In the second and third sentences, because of the presence of "vā," the word "īmahe" must be supplied (adhyāhāra) in connection with them; otherwise the sentence would not give a full meaning. The print's direction is followed here; the finer steps are clipped by the crowded type.

"Divaḥ" (दिवः). By ऊडिदम् (ūḍidam, पा. ६-१-१७१) the case-ending is acute.

"Pārthivāt" (पार्थिवात्, pārthivāt). "Prathate iti pṛthivī" — from "prath prakhyāne," with प्रथेः षिवन् सम्प्रसारणं च (prather ṣivan samprasāraṇaṃ ca, Uṇādi [१-१३० as printed; uncertain]) the affix "ṣivan" comes, with "samprasāraṇa" — so "prath + ivan," whence "pṛth + ivan" (the "r" turning to "ṛ"); the "ṣ" is "it"; by षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च (ṣid-gaurādibhyaś ca, पा. ४-१-४१) the feminine "ṅīṣ" comes after a "ṣit" stem and the stems of the "gaura" class. By the maxim that a marker which has no other use becomes a qualifier of the stem, the "ṣ" of "ṣivan" qualifies the stem. The "ī" of "ṅīṣ" is acute by the affix-accent (आद्युदात्तश्च, पा. ३-१-३, ādyudāttaś ca, "an affix is first-syllable acute"), and the remaining syllables are lowered by अनुदात्तं पदमेकवर्जम् (anudāttaṃ padam eka-varjam, पा. ६-१-१५८), so "pṛthivī" has its acute on the last syllable and the earlier ones are accent-less. To express "a modification of 'pṛthivī'" the affix "añ" comes by ओरञ् (पा. ४-३-१३७) with अनुदात्तादेश्च (पा. ४-३-१४०); since the result ends in a taddhita, it is a stem (कृत्तद्धितसमासाश्च, kṛt-taddhita-samāsāś ca, पा. १-२-४६), and the case-ending is elided by सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः (पा. २-४-७१); the "ī" is dropped by यस्येति च (पा. ६-४-१४८); the first vowel takes vṛddhi by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (पा. ७-२-११७) — "ṛ" → "ār," with "r" following by उरण् रपरः (uraṇ raparaḥ, पा. १-१-५१); and by ञ्णित्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. ६-१-१९७) the first syllable is acute. Thus "pārthiva" is first-syllable acute.

"Adhi" (अधि). First-syllable acute as a particle (निपाता आद्युदात्ताः, फि. [?]; printed "४-८०" or similar — uncertain).

"Indram" (इन्द्रम्, indram). ऋज्रेन्द्राग्र… (ṛjrendrāgra-…, Uṇādi [२-२८ as printed, uncertain]) — the word ends with the affix "ran" and is first-syllable acute.

"Mahaḥ" (महः, mahaḥ). From "mahat," the "a" and "t" are dropped by Vedic licence (the printed "(अत्)" marks the dropped part). By सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः (sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ, पा. ६-१-१६८) the case-ending is acute.

"Rajasaḥ" (रजसः, rajasaḥ). By नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (nab-viṣayasyānisantasya, फि. [?]; the print gives a small numeral that I cannot read) first-syllable acute. ॥१०॥

Close of Sūkta 6 (as printed on p. 257). The print marks the end of the sūkta with a ruled line and the statement (Kannada, translated): "Here the sixth sūkta in the first maṇḍala is complete. In the Prathamāṣṭaka, Prathamādhyāya, the eighth [?] varga is complete." The ordinal is read as "eighth" — the word printed is "ಎಂಟನೆಯ" — and it is recorded as read. It disagrees with the closing note of Sūkta 5 (p. 201), which had been read as "tenth," and with the small-numeral page headers; They are not reconciled. See the open flags below.

original p. 257

॥ ॐ ॥

Sūkta 7 — "indram id gāthino bṛhat" (ಏಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು, "The Seventh Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)

इन्द्रमित्यादिकं दशर्चं यत्सूक्तं तत्सुरूपकृत्नुमित्यादिषु चतुर्थम् । ऋषिश्छन्दोदेवता विनियोगश्च पूर्ववत् । विशेषविनियोगस्तूच्यते । महाव्रते निष्केवल्यशस्त्रे इन्द्रमिद्गाथिन इति सूक्तम् । तथा च पञ्चमारण्यके सूत्रितम् । शिरोगायत्रमिन्द्रमिद्गाथिनः । ऐ. आ. ३-२-१ । इति । तथा चतुर्विंशेऽहनि ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः शस्त्रे इन्द्रमिद्गाथिन इति षळहस्तोत्रियस्तृचः । चतुर्विंशे होताजनिष्वेत्युपक्रम्य आयाहि सुषुमा हि त इन्द्रमिद्गाथिनो बृहत् । आ. २-२ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् । अतिरात्रे प्रथमे पर्याये ऽच्छावाकशस्त्रे यमेव तृचो ऽनुरूपः [?] । सूत्रितं च इन्द्राय मद्वने सुतमिन्द्रमिद्गाथिनो बृहत् । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥

indram ity-ādikaṃ daśarcaṃ yat sūktaṃ tat surūpakṛtnum ity-ādiṣu caturtham | ṛṣi-chando-devatā viniyogaś ca pūrvavat | viśeṣa-viniyogas tūcyate | mahāvrate niṣkevalya-śastre indram id gāthina iti sūktam | tathā ca pañcamāraṇyake sūtritam | śiro-gāyatram indram id gāthinaḥ | ai. ā. 3-2-1 | iti | tathā caturviṃśe 'hani brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ śastre indram id gāthina iti ṣaḷaha-stotriyas tṛcaḥ | caturviṃśe hotājaniṣṭety upakramya āyāhi suṣumā hi ta indram id gāthino bṛhat | ā. 2-2 | iti sūtritatvāt | atirātre prathame paryāye 'cchāvāka-śastre yam eva tṛco 'nurūpaḥ [?] | sūtritaṃ ca indrāya madvane sutam indram id gāthino bṛhat | ā. 6-4 | iti ||

Translation: "The sūkta of ten riks beginning indram is the fourth among those beginning surūpakṛtnum [i.e., the fourth sūkta of that anuvāka]. Its ṛṣi, meter, deity and application are as before. Its special application is now stated. In the Mahāvrata rite, the sūkta indram id gāthinaḥ is used in the niṣkevalya-śastra. So it is laid down in the Fifth Āraṇyaka: 'śiro-gāyatram indram id gāthinaḥ' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 3-2-1). Likewise, on the twenty-fourth day [of the Ṣaḷaha-related rite], in the śastra of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the ṣaḷaha-stotriya triplet is indram id gāthinaḥ — as laid down in the (Āśvalāyana) sūtra, which, beginning from 'on the twenty-fourth [day] the hotā …', continues 'āyāhi suṣumā hi ta' and 'indram id gāthino bṛhat' (Āśvalāyana, ref. "2-2" [?]). In the Atirātra, in the first paryāya, in the Acchāvāka's śastra, [the corresponding triplet is used as the anurūpa] [the clause beginning yam eva tṛco 'nurūpaḥ is hard to read in the scan; sense given with reservation]; and it is so laid down: 'indrāya madvane sutam, indram id gāthino bṛhat' (Āraṇyaka ref. "6-4" [?])."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering of the above) ॥

This sūkta indram id gāthino bṛhat is the fourth (last) sūkta of the second anuvāka, which begins with surūpakṛtnum ūtaye. It has ten riks. Its ṛṣi, deity, meters and application are the same as in the preceding sūkta. It does, however, have a special application: in the sacrifice called Mahāvrata, the sūkta indram id gāthino is recited as the niṣkevalya-śastra mantra. This is stated in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka (the fifth āraṇyaka — "Pañcamāraṇyaka") in the words śiro-gāyatram indram id gāthinaḥ. And on the twenty-fourth day [of the rite], when the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin — a priest of the hotṛ group — recites the triplet called ṣaḷaha-stotriya, the rik indram id gāthino is to be recited; this is stated in the Āśvalāyana sūtra, beginning from the section called hotājaniṣṭa. That is: in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section hotājaniṣṭa, the rik ā yāhi suṣumā hi te (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8-12-1 [?]) and the rik indram id gāthino bṛhat (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-7-1) are to be recited, on the twenty-fourth day, in the triplet called ṣaḷaha-stotriya. And in the Āraṇyaka too: "indrāya madvane sutam, indram id gāthino bṛhat" (Āraṇyaka 6-4) — that is, the rik indrāya madvane sutam (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 9-63-11 [?]) and the rik indram id gāthino bṛhat are to be recited together in the triplet mentioned above — so the sūtra directs. The top of this page carries the end of the Kannada anuvāda translated above; its content is given there.

Sūkta 7, Rik 1

॥ Sūkta — 7 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 2 ॥ Sūkta — 7 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 13, 14 [?] ॥ small-print Kannada digits, re-read at 300 dpi: "13, 14". This fits the run of two vargas per sūkta from Sūkta 3 (5, 6) and Sūkta 8 (15, 16), but not the "eighth varga" of the Sūkta 6 colophon; unreconciled. An earlier reading here of "9, 10" was wrong. ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–10 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Madhucchandā Vaiśvāmitra ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indra ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रमिद्गाथिनो बृहदिन्द्रमर्केभिरर्किणः । इन्द्रं वाणीरनूषत ॥१॥

indram id gāthino bṛhad indram arkebhir arkiṇaḥ | indraṃ vāṇīr anūṣata ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रम् । इत् । गाथिनः । बृहत् । इन्द्रम् । अर्केभिः । अर्किणः ॥ इन्द्रम् । वाणीः । अनूषत ॥१॥

indram | it | gāthinaḥ | bṛhat | indram | arkebhiḥ | arkiṇaḥ || indram | vāṇīḥ | anūṣata ||1||

original p. 259

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya on Rik 1

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

गाथिनो गीयमानसामयुक्ता उद्गातार इन्द्रमिदिन्द्रमेव बृहत् । त्वामिद्धि हवामहे [ऋग्वे. ६-४६-१] इत्यस्यामृच्युत्पन्नेन बृहन्नामकेन साम्नानूषत । स्तुतवन्तः । अर्किणो ऽर्चनहेतुमन्त्रोपेता होतारो ऽर्केभिर् ऋग्रूपैर्मन्त्रैरिन्द्रमेवानूषत । ये त्वध्वर्यवस्ते वाणीर्वाग्रूपाभिर्यजूरूपाभिरिन्द्रमेवानूषत । अर्कशब्दस्य मन्त्रपरत्वं यास्केनोक्तम् । अर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्ति । नि. ५-४ । इति । श्लोक इत्यादिषु सप्तपञ्चाशत्सु वाङ्नामसु वाशी वाणीति पठितम् ॥

gāthino gīyamāna-sāma-yuktā udgātāra indram id indram eva bṛhat | tvām id dhi havāmahe [ṛgve. 6-46-1] ity asyām ṛcy utpannena bṛhan-nāmakena sāmnānūṣata | stutavantaḥ | arkiṇo 'rcana-hetu-mantropetā hotāro 'rkebhir ṛg-rūpair mantrair indram evānūṣata | ye tv adhvaryavas te vāṇīr vāg-rūpābhir yajū-rūpābhir indram evānūṣata | arka-śabdasya mantra-paratvaṃ yāskenoktam | arko mantro bhavati yad anenārcanti | ni. 5-4 | iti | śloka ity-ādiṣu saptapañcāśatsu vāṅ-nāmasu vāśī vāṇīti paṭhitam ||

Translation: "The gāthinaḥ — the udgātṛ priests, who are endowed with sung Sāmans — praised Indra, and Indra alone, with the Bṛhat [Sāman] — that is, with the Sāman named Bṛhat, produced upon the rik tvām id dhi havāmahe (Ṛgveda 6-46-1) — they praised him. The arkiṇaḥ — the hotṛ priests, who are furnished with mantras that are the means of worship — praised Indra, and Indra alone, with the arkas, that is, with mantras in the form of ṛks. And the adhvaryus praised Indra alone with vāṇīs — with speech in the form of yajus-formulae. That the word arka denotes 'mantra' is stated by Yāska: 'An arka is a mantra, because with it they offer worship' (Nirukta 5-4). Among the fifty-seven words for 'speech' beginning with śloka, the words vāśī and vāṇī are listed." The remainder of the Sanskrit on this page and the next carries Sāyaṇa's grammatical derivation of गाथिनः [gāthinaḥ], बृहत् [bṛhat], अर्केभिः [arkebhiḥ], अर्किणः [arkiṇaḥ], वाणीः [vāṇīḥ] and अनूषत [anūṣata] — suffixes, accent, and Vedic irregularities of case-ending — in the standard dense register. Characterized rather than transcribed line by line (Convention 5); the sense of each word is already fixed by the passage above. In outline: gāthinaḥ is formed with the suffix than (from the root gai, "to sing") and then ini ("one who has gāthās"); bṛhat has its instrumental ending dropped (the standard luk of case-endings in the Veda); arkebhiḥ lacks the usual ais substitution by Vedic license; arkiṇaḥ is "those who have arkas"; vāṇīḥ is a nominative form standing in an instrumental sense; anūṣata is an aorist of the root nu ("to praise") in the middle voice with a Vedic irregularity.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

गाथिनः (gāthinaḥ) — those who sing, that is, the Sāman-singers beginning with the udgātṛ | इन्द्रम् इत् (indram it) — Indra alone | बृहत् (bṛhat) — with the Sāman-mantra called Bṛhat | अनूषत (anūṣata) — praise, that is, sing | अर्किणः (arkiṇaḥ) — the ṛtvijs, the hotṛ and others, who recite the worship-mantras (the invocatory mantras) | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | अर्केभिः (arkebhiḥ) — with ṛk-mantras | (अनूषत — praise) | (the adhvaryu and the other ṛtvijs) इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | वाणीः (vāṇīḥ) — with the yajurveda mantras that take the form of sentences | (अनूषत — praise).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

At the time of sacrifice, the ṛtvijs praise Indra in many ways. That is: the Sāman-singers, the udgātṛ and others, sing with the mantra called Bṛhat-sāman found in their Sāma Veda (this mantra is the rik at Ṛgveda 6-46-1); the hotṛ group praise him with the ṛks that serve as their śastra; and the adhvaryu and the other ṛtvijs praise Indra with mantras in the form of the sentences of their own Veda, the Yajurveda. In other words, the ṛtvijs praise Indra with the Vedic mantras of all three kinds — Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman.

original p. 260

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

The chanters (of the Sama hymns) praise only Indra with (a Saman called) Brihat; the recetirs of mantras (Rics) praise Indra with the Ric-Verses; (and the remaining priest Adhvaryus) praise Indra with prose-like Sentences (of Yajus).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The three Vedas in one rik. Although this rik does not explicitly name the Vedas Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, the Bhāṣyakāra takes the words बृहत् (bṛhat), अर्केभिः (arkebhiḥ) and वाणीः (vāṇīḥ) to point to the mantras of the three Vedas — Sāma, Ṛg and Yajur respectively. Western scholars do not accept this view. They hold that the Ṛgveda is older than the other Vedas, and so there is no reason for the later Vedas — Yajur and Sāma — to be indicated within it.

Though this argument cannot be dismissed outright, the Ṛgveda's own Puruṣa-sūkta (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-90-9 [?]) states the words yajus and sāman explicitly. Moreover:

  1. Most of the Sāma Veda's mantras are themselves Ṛgveda mantras, and even in the Ṛgveda's own period it was the custom to recite many Ṛgveda riks in sung form; so there is nothing impossible in a Sāman-mantra being indicated here.
  2. It is something everyone must grant that the Yajurveda is later than the Ṛgveda and Sāma Veda. But although it did not then exist in its present, systematized form, one may confidently say that many Yajur-mantras — chiefly, the sentences used in the sacrifice — were then in special use. Many such sentences, together with the procedures and rules of sacrificing, may have been gathered together to form the Yajurveda as it now stands.
  3. Further, the Ṛgveda in many places names the Yajurveda's chief priest, the Adhvaryu, explicitly.
  4. And since the word वाणीः (vāṇīḥ) is used in this rik, there is ample room to suppose that it refers to Yajus-sentences that are not bound in meter.

For these reasons, the Bhāṣyakāra's explanation of the words as the Ṛk-Yajus-Sāman mantras of the three Vedas cannot be set aside.

"Gāthinaḥ" — gāthā eṣāṃ santīti gāthinaḥ ("those who have gāthās"). Gāthā is also a name for Sāma-Veda mantras; those who sing these gāthās — that is, the Sāman-mantras — are called gāthinaḥ.

original p. 261

"Bṛhat" — the ordinary sense of bṛhat is "great." But in the Sāma Veda there is the principal Sāman-mantra, sung in sacrifices, called Bṛhat-sāman; and in the Ṛgveda it is this rik:

त्वामिद्धि हवामहे सातौ वाजस्य कारवः । त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठास्वर्वतः ॥

tvām id dhi havāmahe sātā vājasya kāravaḥ | tvāṃ vṛtreṣv indra satpatiṃ naras tvāṃ kāṣṭhāsv arvataḥ ||

(Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 6-46-1)

Translation (of the rik as cited here): "Indeed we call upon you, O Indra — we the singers — for the winning of strength [or: in the winning of spoil]; you, O Indra, the lord of the good, in battles with Vṛtra [or: against Vṛtras]; the men [call upon] you in the races of the horse." My rendering of the rik rests on the plain word-sense; the source here offers no Kannada translation of it, only the citation. Spelling of sātā follows the scan.

The source adds: this mantra is found in the Sāma Veda at 334 [?]; 982 [?]; in the Atharvaveda 20-71-1 [?]; in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Śukla Yajurveda) 27-34 [?]; the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) 2-4-14-2 [?]; the Maitrāyaṇīya Saṃhitā 2-2-6 [?], and other places. All numerals in this sentence are small and compressed in the scan; given with reservation. This Bṛhat-sāman is one principal mantra of the Sāma Veda; the Yajurveda explains it in many places.

"Arkebhiḥ" — Yāska, in the Nirukta, gives the sense of the word arka: अर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्ति (arko mantro bhavati yad anenārcanti) — "an arka is a mantra, because with it they worship" (Nirukta 5-4). The root arc means "to worship" (pūjāyām); because worship is done with it, the mantra is called arka.

"Arkiṇaḥ" — अर्काः स्तुतिसाधनभूता मन्त्रा येषां सन्तीत्यर्किणः (arkāḥ stuti-sādhana-bhūtā mantrā yeṣāṃ santīty arkiṇaḥ) — "those who have arkas, mantras that are the instruments of praise" — that is, those who praise with mantras (arkas) that are the means of praise.

"Vāṇīḥ" — vāṇī is listed among the fifty-seven speech-words beginning with śloka and dhārā (Nirukta/Nighaṇṭu 1-11 [the source's "ನಿ. ೧-೧೧"; reading of the numerals is uncertain]). Here the Bhāṣyakāra explains vāṇīḥ as Yajurveda sentences. Since the Yajurveda has few mantras bound in meter, it is the custom to call its mantras "sentences" (vākya). In this rik the nominative-case word vāṇīḥ is used in the sense of the instrumental.

"Anūṣata" — the aorist (luṅ) form of the root ṇu stutau ("to praise"). Although the root takes parasmaipada, here, by a Vedic inversion (vyatyaya), it is used as if it were ātmanepada.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

Characterized, not transcribed (Convention 5). This section (pp. 261–263) works through the derivation and accent of each word in the rik, in sūtra-by-sūtra detail. Points of substance below. Caveat for every characterized grammar section in this volume: the Pāṇini/Uṇādi sūtra numbers are read from very small Kannada-script print and were not cross-checked against Pāṇini; treat them as pointers to the passage, not as verified citations. Continues the Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 1 in the same register — the optional-lengthening discussion for vāṇīḥ and the finite-verb analysis of anūṣata, completed on the next page. Characterized as above; not transcribed.

  • गाथिनः (gāthinaḥ) — from the root gai ("to sing") + the than suffix by an Uṇādi sūtra (Uṇ. 2-4 [?]), then -in by Pāṇini 5-2-116 ("vrīhy-ādibhyaś ca"), so the word means "one possessing gāthās"; the accent falls on the suffix-vowel.
  • बृहत् (bṛhat) — instrumental singular in sense, the case-ending being deleted by the Pāṇinian luk rule (Pā. 7-1-39 [?]); the word is final-udātta by an Uṇādi sūtra (Uṇ. 2-84 [?]) that treats bṛhat as irregularly formed (nipātita). The source remarks that, because the suffix śatṛ carries the ati-class final accent, bṛhat is atipratyayānta in effect.
  • अर्केभिः (arkebhiḥ) — from arc ("to worship") + gha, giving arka, with the palatal-to-velar change (kutva); the expected ais of the instrumental plural is not substituted, "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 7-1-10).
  • अर्किणः (arkiṇaḥ) — arka + the suffix ini ("possessing").
  • वाणीः (vāṇīḥ) — initial-udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. 6-1-203); lengthening in the nominative plural resolved by the optional Vedic rule on pūrvasavarṇa-lengthening.
  • अनूषत (anūṣata) — root ṇu with n for ṇ; aorist with sic; the augment iṭ absent and the vowel lengthened as Vedic features; guṇa is blocked.

Rik 1 grammar closes; Rik 2

The first nine lines complete the Rik 1 grammar — the analysis of anūṣata, ending with the observation that, since the root nu belongs to the kuṭādi class, the sic aorist behaves as if marked ṅit and so guṇa does not arise. Then the number ॥१॥ closes Rik 1. Characterized, not transcribed.

॥१॥

Sūkta 7, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्र इद्धर्योः सचा सम्मिश्ल आ वचोयुजा । इन्द्रो वज्री हिरण्ययः ॥२॥

indra id dharyoḥ sacā sammiśla ā vacoyujā | indro vajrī hiraṇyayaḥ ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रः । इत् । हर्योः । सचा । सम्ऽमिश्लः । आ । वचःऽयुजा ॥ इन्द्रः । वज्री । हिरण्ययः ॥२॥

indraḥ | it | haryoḥ | sacā | sam-miślaḥ | ā | vacaḥ-yujā || indraḥ | vajrī | hiraṇyayaḥ ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्द्र इदिन्द्र एव हर्योर्हरिनामकयोरश्वयोः सचा सह युगपदा सम्मिश्लः सर्वतः सम्यग्मिश्रयिता । कीदृशयोर्हर्योः । वचोयुजा । इन्द्रस्य वचनमात्रेण रथे युज्यमानयोः सुशिक्षितयोरित्यर्थः । अयमिन्द्रो वज्री वज्रयुक्तो हिरण्ययो हिरण्मयः । सर्वाभरणभूषित इत्यर्थः ॥

indra id indra eva haryor hari-nāmakayor aśvayoḥ sacā saha yugapad ā sammiślaḥ sarvataḥ samyag-miśrayitā | kīdṛśayor haryoḥ | vacoyujā | indrasya vacana-mātreṇa rathe yujyamānayoḥ suśikṣitayor ity arthaḥ | ayam indro vajrī vajra-yukto hiraṇyayo hiraṇmayaḥ | sarvābharaṇa-bhūṣita ity arthaḥ ||

Translation: "Indra himself, together with (sacā) — simultaneously with — his two horses named Hari, comes, being the all-round good mixer/combiner (sammiślaḥ). What kind of horses? Vacoyujā: yoked to the chariot at Indra's mere word — that is, well-trained. This Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt (vajrī), is golden (hiraṇyayaḥ, = hiraṇmayaḥ) — adorned with all ornaments." Sāyaṇa's grammatical notes follow on page 264 — in the Sanskrit itself — and are characterized there. The first part of this page is the Sanskrit grammar of Rik 2 inside the bhāṣya itself. Characterized, not transcribed. Points of substance: हर्योः (haryoḥ) — "the two that carry" (harataḥ), from hṛ, with the suffix in; initial-udātta. सचा (sacā) — glossed "with" (Nirukta 5-5, "sacā saheti"). सम्मिश्लः (sammiślaḥ) — "mixing" from miśra + ghañ (Pā. 3-3-18) with a Vedic l for r, so "one who mixes thoroughly"; accent of the first member retained in the bahuvrīhi. वचोयुजा (vacoyujā) — "yoked with a word"; the dual case-ending replaced by ā; the second member yuj has the final accent. वज्री (vajrī) — "having a vajra", suffix ini (Pā. 5-2-115). हिरण्ययः (hiraṇyayaḥ) — by Pāṇini 6-4-175 [?] (the source's printed number reads "6-4-17[?]"), the m of hiraṇmaya is dropped irregularly in the Veda, so hiraṇyaya is the form; it is udātta on the ā by the suffix-accent.

original p. 264

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सम्मिश्लः (sammiślaḥ) — the one who thoroughly mixes everything | इन्द्र इत् (indra it) — Indra himself | वचोयुजा (vacoyujā) — yoked to the chariot at Indra's mere word | हर्योः (haryoḥ) — with the horses called Hari (of Indra) | सचा (sacā) — together with | आ (yāti) — comes hither | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | वज्री (vajrī) — the wielder of the thunderbolt | हिरण्ययः (hiraṇyayaḥ) — the golden one, that is, adorned with golden ornaments.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra, who mixes [combines with] everything, is coming here. At his mere word, his horses are yoked to the chariot. Seated in the chariot to which such horses are yoked, he comes here. That Indra, adorned with ornaments of gold, bears the thunderbolt.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra, the good mixer of all things comes verily with his horses that are harnessed at his word; Indra, the richly-decorated (with gold), the weilder of the thundorbolt.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Sacā" — saha: with, together, in company.

"Sammiślaḥ" — The Bhāṣyakāra explains this word as सम्मिश्लः सर्वतः सम्यग्मिश्रयिता (sammiślaḥ sarvataḥ samyag miśrayitā) — "one who mixes well, in every way." Following him, Western scholars such as Wilson give meanings such as "blender, mixer, mixing oneself very much with, attached to." For the word's component-sense, [Sāyaṇa's note] is:

सम्मिश्लः । मिश्रणं मिश्रः । मिश्रयतेर्घञ् । पा. सू. ३-३-१८ । सम्यक् मिश्रो यस्यासौ सम्मिश्रः । लत्वं छान्दसम् । सम्यक् मिश्रयितेत्यर्थः । sammiślaḥ | miśraṇaṃ miśraḥ | miśrayater ghañ | pā. sū. 3-3-18 | samyak miśro yasyāsau sammiśraḥ | latvaṃ chāndasam | samyak miśrayitety arthaḥ | "Sammiślaḥ: 'mixing' is miśra; [formed from] miśrayati with ghañ (Pāṇini 3-3-18). 'He of whom the mixing is thorough' is sammiśra; the l [for r] is Vedic. The sense: one who mixes thoroughly."

original p. 265

Though this sense is correct for the word in itself, it does not fit the word in this rik. If sammiślaḥ is taken to mean "joined" (saṃyuktaḥ) or "accompanied" (sahitaḥ), the sense runs right. The Bhāṣyakāra himself, at another rik, explains the plural sammiślāsaḥ (in the verse at Ṛgveda 1-64-10 [?]) as sammiśrāḥ saṃyuktāḥ ity arthaḥ — "mixed, joined." Examples of riks containing the word follow, for illustration. All Ṛgveda numbers below are read from small print and are given with "[?]". The Sanskrit of each rik is transcribed from the Kannada script, with word-division as read. Where the scan made a word doubtful, it is marked.

विश्वे देवासो रयिभिः समोकसः सम्मिश्लास्तविषीभिरर्किणः । [?] viśve devāso rayibhiḥ samokasaḥ sammiślās taviṣībhir arkiṇaḥ | [?] — (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-64-10 [?])

("All the gods, sharing the same dwelling with their riches, united with their powers, the singers…" — last two words doubtful in the scan.)

यः सम्मिश्लो हर्योर्यः सुते सचा वज्री रथो हिरण्ययः ॥ yaḥ sammiślo haryor yaḥ sute sacā vajrī ratho hiraṇyayaḥ || — (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8-33-4 [?])

The source remarks that in this rik, too, the words and sense of the (present) rik recur with little difference.

प्रभङ्गी शूरो मघवा तुवीमघः सम्मिश्लो वीर्याय कम् ॥ prabhaṅgī śūro maghavā tuvīmaghaḥ sammiślo vīryāya kam || — (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8-70-14 [?])

सम्मिश्लो अरुषो भव सूपस्थाभिर्न धेनुभिः ॥ sammiślo aruṣo bhava sūpasthābhir na dhenubhiḥ || — (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 9-61-20 [?])

मन्द्रो होता स जुह्वा यजिष्ठः सम्मिश्लो अग्निरा जिघर्ति देवान् ॥ [?] mandro hotā sa juhvā yajiṣṭhaḥ sammiślo agnir ā jigharti devān || [?] — (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-6-4 [?])
