Rik 10: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, English

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र त्वां विद्म । जानीमः । कीदृशं त्वाम् । वृषन्तमं कामानामतिशयेन वर्षितारं वाजेषु संग्रामेषु हवनश्रुतम् अस्मदीयस्याह्वानस्य श्रोतारम् । वृषन्तमस्य अत्यन्तं कामादीनां वर्षितुस्तवोतिं रक्षामस्मद्विषयामुद्दिश्य हूमहे । त्वामाह्वयामः । कीदृशीमूतिम् । सहस्रसातमाम् अतिशयेन धनसहस्राणां दात्रीम् । विद्म — विदो लटो वा । पा. ३-४-८३ । इति मसो मादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घः । वृषन्तमम् । पृषु वृषु मृषु सेचने । कनिन् युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः । उ. १-१५६ । इति कनिन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तमपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तः । आद्युदात्तत्वमेव शिष्यते । आयस्मयोदीनि छन्दसि । पा. १-४-२० । इति भत्वेन पदत्वाभावान्नलोपाभावः । पा. ८-२-७ [?] । वाजेषु । वाजशब्दो वृषादिराद्युदात्तः । हवनश्रुतम् । हू इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति ल्युट् संप्रसारणम् । हवनं शृणोतीति क्विप् तुगागमः । वृषन्तमस्य । उक्तम् । हूमहे । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । ऊतिम् । ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च । पा. ३-३-९७ । इति क्तिन् उदात्तो निपातितः । सहस्रसातमाम् । सहस्रं सनोति सहस्रसाः । षणु दाने । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । पा. ३-२-६७ । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् । पा. ६-४-४१ । इत्याकारादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । तमपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । टाप् । अजाद्यतष्टाप् [?] ॥१०॥

he indra tvāṃ vidma | jānīmaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | vṛṣantamaṃ kāmānām atiśayena varṣitāraṃ vājeṣu saṃgrāmeṣu havanaśrutam asmadīyasyāhvānasya śrotāram | vṛṣantamasya atyantaṃ kāmādīnāṃ varṣitus tavotiṃ rakṣām asmad-viṣayām uddiśya hūmahe | tvām āhvayāmaḥ | kīdṛśīm ūtim | sahasrasātamām atiśayena dhana-sahasrāṇāṃ dātrīm | vidma — vido laṭo vā | pā. 3-4-83 | iti maso mādeśaḥ | pratyaya-svareṇāntodāttaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | vṛṣantamam | pṛṣu vṛṣu mṛṣu secane | kanin yuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ | u. 1-156 | iti kanin | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | tamapaḥ pittvād anudāttaḥ | ādyudāttatvam eva śiṣyate | āyasmayodīni chandasi | pā. 1-4-20 | iti bhatvena padatvābhāvān na-lopābhāvaḥ | pā. 8-2-7 [?] | vājeṣu | vāja-śabdo vṛṣādir ādyudāttaḥ | havanaśrutam | hū ity anuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti lyuṭ saṃprasāraṇam | havanaṃ śṛṇotīti kvip tugāgamaḥ | vṛṣantamasya | uktam | hūmahe | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | ūtim | ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca | pā. 3-3-97 | iti ktin udātto nipātitaḥ | sahasrasātamām | sahasraṃ sanoti sahasrasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | pā. 3-2-67 | viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt | pā. 6-4-41 | ity ākārādeśaḥ | kṛd-uttara-pada-prakṛti-svaratvam | tamapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | ṭāp | ajādyataṣṭāp [?] ||10||

Translation: "O Indra! Tvāṃ vidma — we know you. What kind? Vṛṣantamam — the one who rains desires to the utmost; vājeṣu — in battles; havanaśrutam — the one who hears our invocation. For the protection (ūtim) of you, the vṛṣantama — the supreme showerer of desires and the like — directed at us, hūmahe: we call you. What kind of protection? Sahasrasātamām — that which, to the utmost, gives thousands of riches." The grammar of vidma, vṛṣantamam, havanaśrutam, hūmahe, ūtim, sahasrasātamām follows in the Sanskrit and is noted briefly: vidma — the substitute ma for mas in the laṭ of vid (Pā. 3-4-83), with the Saṃhitā lengthening; vṛṣantamam — root vṛṣu secane with kanin (Uṇ. 1-156), initial-udātta, then tamap (unaccented since pit); no loss of n because in the Veda the stem has bha status and so is not a pada; havanaśrutam — the lyuṭ from root hve with saṃprasāraṇa, then kvip with tuk; ūtim — the ktin udātta by irregular formation; sahasrasātamām — root ṣaṇu dāne with viṭ, the ā for the nasal, then tamap and ṭāp.) (The final sūtra reference is compressed in the scan.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | वृषन्तमम् (vṛṣantamam) — (as the bestower of desired things) the giver of rain | वाजेषु (vājeṣu) — in battles | हवनश्रुतम् (havanaśrutam) — one who hears our invocation (our cry for help) | विद्म (vidma) — we know | हि (hi) — indeed | वृषन्तमस्य (vṛṣantamasya) — of you, who rain down desires | सहस्रसातमाम् (sahasrasātamām) — which gives in thousands of ways | ऊतिम् (ūtim) — protection (or, for our protection) | हूमहे (hūmahe) — we call (we pray for).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! We know you as the giver of desired things and as one who hears our call in battles. Therefore, for your manifold protection, you who are the giver of rain in the form of desired things, we call upon you.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, we know you, the rainer of blessings, the hearer of our call in battles; we invoke the thousand-fold protection of you, the showerer of bounties.

original pp. 437–438

Rik 10: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of this rik is easy to understand. There are no special difficulties, and no words that need supplying.

"Vidma" — the final syllable is lengthened for the convenience of the meter in the Saṃhitā.

"Vṛṣantamam," "vṛṣantamasya" — vṛṣṭi-prada, "bestower of rain"; that is, the one who gives us the rain in the form of desired ends.

"Havanaśrutam" — one who hears our invocation, who attends to our cry.

"Sahasrasātamām" — the explanation of this word was already given earlier (see the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, rik 1-3-9).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 437–438, noted briefly

विद्म (vidma) — root vida jñāne ("to know") with laṭ; in the parasmaipada the first-person plural mas; śap is dropped by luk ("ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ," Pā. 2-4-72 [?]); "vido laṭo vā" (Pā. 3-4-83 [?]): for the nine parasmaipada endings of laṭ after vid the substitutes ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, ṇal, va, ma are optionally given, so mas → ma, giving vidma; the Saṃhitā lengthening by "dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ" (Pā. 6-3-135 [?]), vidmā. वृषन्तमम् (vṛṣantamam) — root pṛṣu, vṛṣu, mṛṣu secane; kanin by "kaninn yuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. 1-156 [?]); the k and n of kanin are lost as it, leaving vṛṣ + an → vṛṣan; initial-udātta since nit; then tamap in the sense of excess, unaccented since pit (so the initial-udātta stands); by "ayas-mayādīni chandasi" (Pā. 1-4-20 [?]) the bha status prevents the pada status, so the n is not dropped by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7 [?]). वा (vā) — vāja is a vṛṣādi word, so initial-udātta. हवनश्रुतम् (havanaśrutam) — root hveñ with lyuṭ; lyuṭ → ana; hve + ana: by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34 [?]) the saṃprasāraṇa of hve — hu — arises (the sūtra "hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam"-type carried over by anuvṛtti); with pūrvarūpa, guṇa and av, havana; "havanaṃ śṛṇoti iti": kvip after the root śru with havana as upapada; by "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk" (Pā. 6-1-71 [?]), tuk, giving havanaśrut; the accusative singular am gives havanaśrutam. वृषन्तमस्य (vṛṣantamasya) — the derivation of vṛṣantama was given earlier in this mantra; genitive singular. हूमहे (hūmahe) — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ ātmanepada first plural mahiṅ; "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. 3-4-79 [?]) gives e; śap, which is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73 [?]); "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34 [?]) carries saṃprasāraṇa; then pūrvarūpa by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108 [?]); "hali ca" (Pā. 8-2-77 [?]) lengthens the vowel of an aṅga ending in a saṃprasāraṇa before a consonant: hūmahe. ऊतिम् (ūtim) — "ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca" (Pā. 3-3-97 [?]): these ktin words are irregularly udātta on the end. सहस्रसातमाम् (sahasrasātamām) — "sahasraṃ sanoti iti sahasrasāḥ": root ṣaṇu dāne; ṣ → s (Pā. 6-1-64 [?]), ṇ → n; viṭ after jana, sana, khana, krama, gama in the Veda (Pā. 3-2-67 [?]); the nasal replaced by ā before viṭ and van (Pā. 6-4-41 [?]); savarṇa-dīrgha, sahasrasā; second-member accent; tamap is pit, so unaccented; sahasrasā keeps the accent of the earlier formation; being feminine, tamā + ṭāp ("ajādyataṣṭāp," Pā. 4-1-4 [?]); ṭāp is pit; savarṇa-dīrgha (by "antaratamaḥ" the ā in place of the two) is unaccented; accusative singular am, pūrvarūpa by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-107 [?]): sahasrasātamām.

॥१०॥

original p. 439

Sūkta 10, Rik 11

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ तू न इन्द्र कौशिक मन्दसानः सुतं पिब । नव्यमायुः प्र सू तिर कृधी सहस्रसामृषिम् ॥११॥

ā tū na indra kauśika mandasānaḥ sutaṃ piba | navyam āyuḥ pra sū tira kṛdhī sahasrasām ṛṣim ||11||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । कौशिक । मन्दसानः । सुतम् । पिब ॥ नव्यम् । आयुः । प्र । सु । तिर । कृधि । सहस्रऽसाम् । ऋषिम् ॥११॥

ā | tu | naḥ | indra | kauśika | mandasānaḥ | sutam | piba || navyam | āyuḥ | pra | su | tira | kṛdhi | sahasra-sām | ṛṣim ||11||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र तु क्षिप्रं नो ऽस्मान्प्रत्या गच्छेति शेषः । हे कौशिक कुशिकस्य पुत्रेन्द्र मन्दसानो हृष्यन्भूत्वा सुतमभिषुतं सोमं पिब । यद्यपि विश्वामित्रः कुशिकस्य पुत्रस्तथापि तद्रूपेणेन्द्रस्यैवोच्यते [reading uncertain] । आयं वृत्तान्तो ऽनुक्रमणिकायामुक्तः [?] । कुशिकस्त्वैषीरथिरिन्द्रतुल्यं पुत्रमिच्छंस्तपश्चर्यं चकार । तस्येन्द्र एव गाथी पुत्रो जज्ञे । अनु. ऋग्वे. ३-१ [?] । इति । हे इन्द्र नव्यं सर्वैर्देवैः स्तुत्यं कर्मानुष्ठानपरमायुर्जीवितं प्र सू तिर । प्रकर्षेण सुष्ठु वर्धय । ततो मां सहस्रसां सहस्रसंख्याकलाभोपेतमृषिमिन्द्रियद्वारं [?] कृधि । कुरु ॥

he indra tu kṣipraṃ no 'smān pratyā gaccheti śeṣaḥ | he kauśika kuśikasya putrendra mandasāno hṛṣyan bhūtvā sutam abhiṣutaṃ somaṃ piba | yady api viśvāmitraḥ kuśikasya putras tathāpi tad-rūpeṇendrasyaivocyate [reading uncertain] | āyaṃ vṛttānto 'nukramaṇikāyām uktaḥ [?] | kuśikas tv aiṣīrathir indra-tulyaṃ putram icchaṃs tapaś-caryaṃ cakāra | tasyendra eva gāthī putro jajñe | anu. ṛgve. 3-1 [?] | iti | he indra navyaṃ sarvair devaiḥ stutyaṃ karmānuṣṭhāna-param āyur jīvitaṃ pra sū tira | prakarṣeṇa suṣṭhu vardhaya | tato māṃ sahasrasāṃ sahasra-saṃkhyā-lābhopetam ṛṣim indriya-dvāraṃ [?] kṛdhi | kuru ||

Translation: "O Indra, tu — quickly — come to us (this is the word to be supplied). O kauśika — O Indra, son of Kuśika — mandasānaḥ — being glad — sutam piba: drink the pressed Soma. Although Viśvāmitra is the son of Kuśika, [the epithet is here said of Indra in that form] [the clause is compressed]. This story is told in the Anukramaṇikā [?]: 'Kuśika, the son of Iṣīratha, wishing a son equal to Indra, performed austerities; Indra himself was born to him as Gāthin' (Ṛgveda Anukramaṇī 3-1 [?]). O Indra, navyam āyuḥ pra sū tira: greatly, well, increase [our] navyam — praiseworthy by all gods, devoted to the performance of rites — āyuḥ, life. Then kṛdhi — make — mām, me, sahasrasām — endowed with gains reckoned in thousands — ṛṣim, a seer [the printed phrase after 'ṛṣim' is not clear]." The grammar of तु, नः, इन्द्र, कौशिक, मन्दसानः, सुतम्, पिब, नव्यम्, आयुः, प्र, सु, तिर, कृधि, सहस्रसाम्, ऋषिम् follows in the Sanskrit on p. 439 and is noted briefly: the Saṃhitā lengthening of tu, su, kṛdhi; kauśika with the taddhita aṇ; mandasānaḥ — root madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu with sānac (Uṇ. 2-[?]) in the Veda, initial-udātta; sutam with kta; piba — the root pā with śa and pibādeśa; navyam — root ṇu stutau with yat ("ac-o yat") and guṇa by vānto yi pratyaye (Pā. 6-1-79 [?]) to give nav, "yato 'nāvaḥ" initial-udātta; āyuḥ with uṇ (Uṇ. 1-[?]) from iṇ gatau; tira — root tṝ with śa (the a-type vikaraṇa); kṛdhi — root kṛ with hi → dhi, the śnu dropped; sahasrasām and ṛṣim — root ṛṣī gatau with in (Uṇ. 4-[?]). Sūtra numbers and some phrases are compressed in the scan.

original p. 440

Rik 11: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | तु (tu) — quickly | नः (naḥ) — to us (near us) | आ (gaccha) — come | (हे) कौशिक ((he) kauśika) — O Indra, son of Kuśika | you मन्दसानः (mandasānaḥ) — being glad | सुतम् (sutam) — the Soma-juice, pressed and prepared | पिब (piba) — drink | नव्यम् (navyam) — [which is] requested (that is, desired) | आयुः (āyuḥ) — life | प्र सु तिर (pra su tira) — increase specially (for me) | सहस्रसाम् (sahasrasām) — [one who is] winning thousands of gains | ऋषिम् (ṛṣim) — a seer | कृधि (kṛdhi) — make (me).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Come quickly to us, and drink with delight this Soma-juice that we have pressed. Increase our life, and make me, an ordinary person, one who gains thousands of benefits.

॥ English Translation ॥

Come quickly, Indra, son of Kusika, and drink the soma libation with delight; prolong the life which we merit and make me a Rishi abundantly endowed with thousands of benefits.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Tu," "su," "kṛdhi" — the final syllables of these words in this rik are lengthened for the convenience of the meter.

"Ā" — in this rik only the prefix ā occurs; with it the verb gaccha ("come") has to be supplied. Such usages are needed in the Ṛgveda.

"Kauśika" — here Indra is addressed as the son of Kuśika. In this connection the Bhāṣyakāra cites an account from the Anukramaṇikā:

कुशिकस्त्वैषीरथिरिन्द्रतुल्यं पुत्रमिच्छन् ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्येन्द्र एव गाथी पुत्रो जज्ञे ॥ (ऋ. अनु. ३-१) kuśikas tv aiṣīrathir indra-tulyaṃ putram icchan brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasyendra eva gāthī putro jajñe || (ṛ. anu. 3-1) "Kuśika, the son of Iṣīratha, wishing a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity; Indra himself was born as his son, Gāthin."

Skandasvāmī, on this subject:

अत्र इतिहासमाचक्षते । इषीरथपुत्रः कुशिको नाम राजा पुत्रमिन्द्रतुल्यं कामयमानो ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्य गाथी नामेन्द्र एव स्वयं पुत्रो जात इति ॥ atra itihāsam ācakṣate | iṣīrathaputraḥ kuśiko nāma rājā putram indra-tulyaṃ kāmayamāno brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasya gāthī nāmendra eva svayaṃ putro jāta iti || "Here they tell a legend: a king named Kuśika, son of Iṣīratha, desiring a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity; Indra himself was born to him as a son named Gāthin."

original p. 441

Rik 11: Special Topics (continued)

Veṅkaṭamādhava:

पुत्रमिन्द्रसमम् इच्छन् कुशिको ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्येन्द्रः स्वयमेव पुत्रो ऽभूत् । सास्य कौशिकता ॥ putram indra-samam icchan kuśiko brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasyendraḥ svayam eva putro 'bhūt | sāsya kauśikatā || "Desiring a son equal to Indra, Kuśika practised celibate austerity; Indra himself became his son. That is his Kauśika-hood."

The chief point is this: in ancient times a king named Iṣīratha had a son called Kuśika. He, desiring a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity. Then Indra himself was born as his son, under the name Gāthin. The sage Viśvāmitra was the son of King Gāthin; and since Madhucchandas, the seer who saw this rik, was born in the family of Viśvāmitra, he addresses Indra, born in his own family — that is, in the family of Kuśika — as "Kauśika."

"Navyam" — the Bhāṣyakāra says that the word navya is another form of the root ṇu stutau, and explains it as sarvair devaiḥ stutyaṃ karmānuṣṭhānaparam — "that is to be praised by all gods, devoted to the performance of rites," or, as the Kannada gloss gives it, "that is wanted by all, even the gods": that is, long life, as everyone naturally desires to live long. Or, as Skandasvāmī says, if the word navyam is given the sense "new" (navam — fresh), then the sense would be: a new vitality for the words navyam āyuḥ — or, to bring out the underlying idea, a still greater lifespan henceforth. In sum: "make us live long; increase our life — prolong our life" [the source's own English].

"Sahasrasām" — thousands of gains, benefits, or many kinds of desired things.

"Ṛṣim" — the root ṛṣī gatau ("to go") has the senses of motion and knowledge; so ṛṣi means one who knows, one endowed with wisdom, or — as the Bhāṣyakāra says — atīndriyadraṣṭāram [the word reads as atīndriya-draṣṭāram, "one who sees what is beyond the senses," as the print has it: "one with the power to know things that are not in the field of the outer senses"; a great person]. Here "ṛṣi" means Madhucchandas, the seer who saw this mantra. When he prays to Indra, "Give me long life, and make me an excellent seer," he uses the first-person [accusative] mām-less, third-person-style expression, instead of the first-person verb form.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 441–443, noted briefly

तु (tu) — in the Saṃhitā lengthened by "ṛcitunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām" (Pā. 6-3-133 [?]); a nipāta, initial-udātta ("nipātā ādyudāttāḥ," Phiṭ-sūtra 80 [?]). Sūtra numbers read from small print; pointers only. The grammar continues below.

original pp. 442–443

Rik 11 grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 442–443, noted briefly

नः (naḥ) — nas replaces asmān by "bahuvacanasya vasnasau" (Pā. 8-1-21 [?]); unaccented as a substitute; in the Saṃhitā it becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. 8-4-66 [?]) after an udātta. इन्द्र (indra), कौशिक (kauśika) — vocatives, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19 [?]). मन्दसानः (mandasānaḥ) — hṛṣyan ("rejoicing"); root madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu; by "ṛñji-vṛdhi-mani-saṃhibhyaḥ kit" [print: "ṛñji vṛdhimaniṣu sahibhyaḥ kit" (Uṇ. 2-[?])] and "chandasy asānac śujyabhyāṃ" [?] the suffix asānac is carried over, being kit; the source remarks that in the Dhātupāṭha of the bālamanoramā tradition the roots ṛji gatau and madī harṣe are listed, but since madī harṣe is not idit it takes no num; therefore the statement "madi in the sūtra" does not suit, and may be due to a copyist's slip [the source's own suggestion]; the suffix is cit, so final-udātta ("citaḥ," Pā. 6-1-163 [?]). सुतम् (sutam) — kta-ending; the suffix accent. नव्यम् (navyam) — root ṇu stutau; ṇ → n ("ṇo naḥ," Pā. 6-1-65 [?]); yat after a vowel-ending root ("ajo yat," Pā. 3-1-97 [?]), nu + ya; since ya is an ārdhadhātuka, guṇa ("sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ," Pā. 7-3-84 [?]), u → o; then "vānto yi pratyaye" (Pā. 6-1-79 [?]): before a y-initial suffix o and au become av and āv, so no → nav; navya; "yato 'nāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-213 [?]) gives initial-udātta; accusative singular navyam. आयुः (āyuḥ) — "iṇ-nīṇ-ajibhyaḥ…" [print: "aitervṛṇṭi…" (Uṇ. 2-[?])] and "janer usiḥ" (Uṇ. 2-[?]) give usi (uṣ); the carried-over word nit from "ārtiprapavasiyajita-…" gives both nit and … for the suffix uṇ after iṇ gatau; it is ṇit and nit, so vṛddhi by "aco ñṇiti" (Pā. 7-2-115 [?]) — i → ai; then ai → āy ("eco 'yavāyāvaḥ," Pā. 6-1-78 [?]), āyus; ru and visarga, āyuḥ; initial-udātta, "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197 [?]). सु (su) — in the Saṃhitā lengthened by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. 6-3-136 [?]). तिर (tira) — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ (bhvādi); loṭ second singular sip; sip → hi (Pā. 3-4-87 [?]); śap should arise but by Vedic inversion the vikaraṇa śa arises, which is apit and so ṅit-like; hence "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4 [?]) and no guṇa by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5 [?]); "ṛta id dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-100 [?]): i in place of the ṛ of a root ending in ṛ, which is "an iṭ substitute ... alo 'ntyasya" (Pā. 1-1-52 [?]); then "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51 [?]): tir; hi is dropped after a stem ending in a ("ato heḥ," Pā. 6-4-105 [?]); tira. कृधि (kṛdhi) — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe, loṭ, sip, hi; the śap arising on kṛ is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi"; hi → dhi after śṛ, spṛ, kṛ, vṛ, bhṛ in the Veda (Pā. 6-4-102 [?]). सहस्रसाम् (sahasrasām) — explained in the earlier mantra (Rik 10). ऋषिम् (ṛṣim) — root ṛṣī gatau; "igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ" [print: "igupadhātkit" (Uṇ. 4-[?])] and "sarvadhātubhya in" (Uṇ. 4-118 [?]): the suffix in after a root with ik in the penultimate position, which is kit, so ṛṣ + in; the suffix is kit, so no guṇa; nit, so initial-udātta ("ñnityādir nityam," Pā. 6-1-197 [?]); the accusative singular am with pūrvarūpa gives ṛṣim.

॥११॥

original p. 444

Sūkta 10, Rik 12 (the last)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इमा भवन्तु विश्वतः । वृद्धायुमनु वृद्धयो जुष्टा भवन्तु जुष्टयः ॥१२॥

pari tvā girvaṇo gira imā bhavantu viśvataḥ | vṛddhāyum anu vṛddhayo juṣṭā bhavantu juṣṭayaḥ ||12||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

परि । त्वा । गिर्वणः । गिरः । इमाः । भवन्तु । विश्वतः ॥ वृद्धऽआयुम् । अनु । वृद्धयः । जुष्टाः । भवन्तु । जुष्टयः ॥१२॥

pari | tvā | girvaṇaḥ | giraḥ | imāḥ | bhavantu | viśvataḥ || vṛddha-āyum | anu | vṛddhayaḥ | juṣṭāḥ | bhavantu | juṣṭayaḥ ||12||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

प्रवर्ग्ये परि त्वेत्यभिष्टुयात् । [the next phrase is compressed] खण्डे परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिरो ऽधि द्वयोरर्धर्चा उक्थ्यं वचः । आ. ४-६ [?] । इति सूत्रितम् । तथा हविर्धानप्रवर्तने सेयं परिधानीया । हविर्धाने प्रवर्तयन्तीति खण्डे परि त्वा गिर्वण इति परिदध्यात् । आ. ४-४ [?] । तथा ब्राह्मणं च । परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इत्युत्तममृचं परिदधाति । ऐ. ब्रा. १-२९ [?] । इति ॥

pravargye pari tvety abhiṣṭuyāt | [phrase compressed] khaṇḍe pari tvā girvaṇo giro 'dhi dvayor ardharcā ukthyaṃ vacaḥ | ā. 4-6 [?] | iti sūtritam | tathā havirdhāna-pravartane seyaṃ paridhānīyā | havirdhāne pravartayantīti khaṇḍe pari tvā girvaṇa iti paridadhyāt | ā. 4-4 [?] | tathā brāhmaṇaṃ ca | pari tvā girvaṇo gira ity uttamām ṛcaṃ paridadhāti | ai. brā. 1-29 [?] | iti ||

हे गिर्वणो ऽस्मदीयस्तुतिभाजेन्द्र विश्वतः सर्वेषु कर्मसु प्रयुज्यमाना इमा गिरो ऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतयस्त्वां परि भवन्तु । सर्वतः प्राप्नुवन्तु । कीदृश्यो गिरः । वृद्धायुमनु प्रवृद्धेनायुषोपेतं त्वामनुसृत्य वृद्धयो वर्धमानाः । किंच ता गिरो जुष्टाः त्वया सेविताः सत्यो जुष्टयो ऽस्माकं प्रीतिहेतवो भवन्तु ॥ गिर्वणः । गीर्भिर्वन्यत इति गिर्वणाः । वन षण संभक्तौ ...

he girvaṇo 'smadīya-stuti-bhājendra viśvataḥ sarveṣu karmasu prayujyamānā imā giro 'smadīyāḥ stutayas tvāṃ pari bhavantu | sarvataḥ prāpnuvantu | kīdṛśyo giraḥ | vṛddhāyum anu pravṛddhenāyuṣopetaṃ tvām anusṛtya vṛddhayo vardhamānāḥ | kiṃca tā giro juṣṭāḥ tvayā sevitāḥ satyo juṣṭayo 'smākaṃ prīti-hetavo bhavantu || girvaṇaḥ | gīrbhir vanyata iti girvaṇāḥ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau ...

Translation: "[In the pravargya rite, one should praise with pari tvā.] It is laid down in the section [of the Āśvalāyana Sūtra] 'pari tvā girvaṇo giraḥ, adhi dvayor ardharcā ukthyaṃ vacaḥ' (Āśvalāyana 4-6 [?]). Likewise, in the setting forth of the havirdhāna cart this [rik] is to be recited as the closing verse: in the section 'havirdhāne pravartayanti' one should close with 'pari tvā girvaṇaḥ' (Āśvalāyana 4-4 [?]). And the Brāhmaṇa too says: 'one closes with the last ṛk, pari tvā girvaṇo giraḥ' (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 1-29 [?]). The Sanskrit before 'khaṇḍe' is compressed in the scan. O girvaṇaḥ — O Indra, who enjoy our praises — imāḥ giraḥ, these our praises, used in all rites, viśvataḥ, tvāṃ pari bhavantu: may [they] encompass you on all sides; may they reach you everywhere. What kind of praises? Vṛddhāyum anu — following you, who are endowed with long-lived life; vṛddhayaḥ — growing. And further: may those praises, juṣṭāḥ — enjoyed (served) by you — become juṣṭayaḥ, the cause of our delight." The grammar of girvaṇaḥ, vṛddhāyum, vṛddhayaḥ, juṣṭāḥ, juṣṭayaḥ continues in the Sanskrit on this page, noted briefly: that girvaṇaḥ is "he who is served with girs," from the root vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau with the suffix asun, the preceding vowel lengthened by Vedic license, a vocative with initial-udātta by the stem; that viśvataḥ is formed with tasil; that vṛddhāyum is a bahuvrīhi "he whose life is grown," accented on the end of the first member by "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. 6-2-199 [?]); that vṛddhayaḥ is from vṛdhu vṛddhau with ktin; and that juṣṭāḥ is from juṣī prītisevanayoḥ with kta, the augment iṭ barred. Some of this is compressed in the scan.

original p. 445

Rik 12: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) गिर्वणः ((he) girvaṇaḥ) — O Indra, worthy of being praised by us | विश्वतः (viśvataḥ) — in all (that is, in all the rites in which we make use of them) | इमाः गिरः (imāḥ giraḥ) — these words in the form of praise | त्वा (tvā) — you | परि भवन्तु (pari bhavantu) — may they come from every side and join (you) | वृद्धायुम् (vṛddhāyum) — you who have long life | अनु (anu) — following | वृद्धयः (vṛddhayaḥ) — growing | जुष्टाः (juṣṭāḥ) — [the words] served (accepted) by you | जुष्टयः (juṣṭayaḥ) — [may they be] the means of giving us delight | भवन्तु (bhavantu) — may they be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, lover of praise! May these words of praise that we make come to you from every side and bring you delight. As these words give you delight, may your life-span (your strength) increase; and as these words of ours bring you delight, may they bring delight to us as well.

॥ English Translation ॥

O deserver of praise, may these our praises be on all occasions around you (accepted by you); may they increase your power, O long-lived, and being agreeable to you, may they become our enjoyments.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of this rik is a long run of connected phrases; the intention is not clearly fitted together, and the seer's purpose is not made plain.

"Girvaṇaḥ" — गीर्भिर्वन्यत इति गिर्वणाः । वन षण संभक्तौ । अस्मदीयस्तुतिभाक् (gīrbhir vanyata iti girvaṇāḥ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | asmadīya-stuti-bhāk) — "one who is served with praises; the root vana/ṣaṇa in the sense of sharing: one who partakes of our praise": that is, one who is worshipped with our words, who is praised, who is worthy of praise.

"Viśvataḥ" — in all places, or on all occasions.

"Vṛddhāyum" — प्रवृद्धेनायुष्येणोपेतम् (pravṛddhenāyuṣyeṇopetam) — "endowed with increased lifespan": endowed with a life that is great or growing, one who lives for a long time. Skandasvāmī explains this word as vṛddhān śatrūn atigantāram — "one who overcomes enemies that have grown great," one who subdues enemies.

"Anu" — anusṛtya, prāpya — "following," "reaching": that is, may the hymns we make reach you; may you hear them.

original p. 446

Rik 12: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

"Vṛddhayaḥ" — vardhamānāḥ — growing; much, specially, flourishing, abundant.

"Juṣṭāḥ," "juṣṭayaḥ" — the root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ has the senses "to be fond of" and "to serve"; so these words mean "that which gives delight, that which is an object of delight."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 446–447, noted briefly

गिर्वणः (girvaṇaḥ) — "gīrbhir vanyate iti girvaṇāḥ": root gṝ śabde (kryādi) with kvip ("kvip ca," Pā. 3-2-76 [?]); "ṛta id dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-100 [?]) gives i in place of ṛ, which, as an alo 'ntyasya substitute, comes at the end; root vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau with asun ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," Uṇ. 4-188 [?]); gir + bhis + vanas receive the technical name prātipadika, and by "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71 [?]) bhis is dropped; by "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam" (Pā. 1-1-62 [?]) gir counts as a pada; so "vor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-76 [?]): the penultimate ik of a stem ending in r or v is lengthened at the end of a pada, which would lengthen the i of gir; but "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (Paribhāṣā 93 [?]) makes this optional, so it does not arise; the vocative singular su is added to girvaṇas, the su dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal" (Pā. 6-1-68 [?]); ru and visarga: girvaṇaḥ; a vocative, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19 [?]). विश्वतः (viśvataḥ) — from tasil, which is l-marked, so the vowel before it is udātta ("liti," Pā. 6-1-193 [?]). वृद्धायुम् (vṛddhāyum) — root vṛdhu vṛddhau with kta; vṛdh + ta; vṛdh is udit, so by "udito vā" (Pā. 7-2-56 [?]) the iṭ augment before ktvā is optional (the print then discusses whether kta too takes iṭ, citing "yasya vibhāṣā" (Pā. 7-2-15 [?]): a suffix beginning kt-/ktavat does not take iṭ after a root to which iṭ is optional); so the iṭ that "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. 7-2-35 [?]) would give is barred; vṛdh + ta → by "jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-40 [?]) t → dh after a jhaṣ; then dh + dh → ddh by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi" (Pā. 8-4-53 [?]): vṛddha; the root iṇ gatau, with uṇ in the Veda ("chandasīṇaḥ," Uṇ. 1-2 [?]), uṇ being ṇit, so vṛddhi ("aco ñṇiti," Pā. 7-2-115 [?]) gives ai + u, then "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78 [?]) gives āy + u → āyu; vṛddham āyur yasya saḥ: vṛddhāyuḥ, a bahuvrīhi, with the first member's accent ("bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam," Pā. 6-2-1 [?]); accusative singular vṛddhāyum. वृद्धयः (vṛddhayaḥ) — ktin ("striyāṃ ktin," Pā. 3-3-94 [?]) after vṛdh; the iṭ augment does not arise by "titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca" (Pā. 7-2-9 [?]); th → dh and j-type changes as before: vṛddhi; initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197 [?]); nominative plural vṛddhayaḥ. जुष्टाः (juṣṭāḥ) — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ, idit; kta; "śvīditaḥ niṣṭhāyām" (Pā. 7-2-14 [?]): after śvi and idit roots, niṣṭhā does not take iṭ, so kta has no augment; the suffix accent would arise but is set aside by "niṣṭhā ca … nityaṃ mantre" (Pā. 6-1-210 [?]), and juṣṭa and arpita are, by the previous sūtra's carried-over words "juṣṭārpite ca chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-209 [?]), always initial-udātta in the mantra. जुष्टयः (juṣṭayaḥ) — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ, ktin; the augment iṭ barred by Pā. 7-2-9 [?]; "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41 [?]) turns t → ṭ: juṣṭi; initial-udātta by the suffix accent; nominative plural juṣṭayaḥ.

॥१२॥

Close of Sūkta 10

॥ इति दशमं सूक्तं समाप्तम् ॥ iti daśamaṃ sūktaṃ samāptam | "Thus the tenth sūkta is completed."

Kannada colophon: ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಪ್ರಥಮಮಂಡಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಹತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಮುಗಿದುದು । "Here the tenth sūkta in the first maṇḍala is concluded."

original p. 448

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ ಹನ್ನೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 11 — "indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan" ("The Eleventh Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)

इन्द्रं विश्वा इत्यृचस्य [reading of this word uncertain] सूक्तस्य मधुच्छन्दसः पुत्रो जेतैनामक ऋषिः । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । इन्द्रमष्टौ जेता माधुच्छन्दस इति । छन्दस्त्वानुष्टुभमिति पूर्वसूत्रोक्तम् । इन्द्रो देवतानुवर्तते ॥ विनियोगस्तु । महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये कृत्स्नसूक्तं [?] शंसनीयम् । ऊरू इति खण्डे शौनकेन सूत्रितम् । इन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्नित्यानुष्टुभं तस्य प्रथमायाः पूर्वमर्धर्चं शस्त्रोत्तरेणार्धर्चेनोत्तरस्याः पूर्वमर्धर्चं व्यतिषजति पाद्यैः पादानानुष्टुप्कारम् [?] । प्रागुत्तमायाः । ऐ. आ. ३-१-१ [?] । इति । ब्राह्मणं च प्रथमारण्यके पङ्क्तेः प्र वो मह इति खण्डे । इन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्निति पदानुषङ्गः । ऐ. आ. १-५-२ [?] । इति । तथा पृष्ठ्यस्य पञ्चमे ऽहनि निष्केवल्ये शस्त्र इन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्नित्यनुरूपस्तृचः । स्तोमो वर्धमान इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । उप नो हरिभिः सुतमिन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन् । आ. ६-१२ [?] । इति ॥

indraṃ viśvā ity-ṛcasya [reading uncertain] sūktasya madhucchandasaḥ putro jetaināmaka ṛṣiḥ | tathā cānukrāntam | indram aṣṭau jetā mādhucchandasa iti | chandastvānuṣṭubham iti pūrvasūtroktam | indro devatānuvartate || viniyogas tu | mahāvrate niṣkevalye kṛtsna-sūktaṃ [?] śaṃsanīyam | ūrū iti khaṇḍe śaunakena sūtritam | indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhann ity ānuṣṭubhaṃ tasya prathamāyāḥ pūrvam ardharcaṃ śastrottareṇārdharcenottarasyāḥ pūrvam ardharcaṃ vyatiṣajati pādyaiḥ pādānānuṣṭupkāram [?] | prāguttamāyāḥ | ai. ā. 3-1-1 [?] | iti | brāhmaṇaṃ ca prathamāraṇyake paṅkteḥ pra vo maha iti khaṇḍe | indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhann iti padānuṣaṅgaḥ | ai. ā. 1-5-2 [?] | iti | tathā pṛṣṭhyasya pañcame 'hani niṣkevalye śastra indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhann ity anurūpas tṛcaḥ | stomo vardhamāna iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | upa no haribhiḥ sutam indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan | ā. 6-12 [?] | iti ||

Translation: "The ṛṣi of the sūkta beginning indraṃ viśvā is Jetā, son of Madhucchandas. So the Anukramaṇī says: 'indram aṣṭau jetā mādhucchandasaḥ' — indram [is the sūkta of] eight [riks; see the note below], seer Jetā, son of Madhucchandas. That the meter is Anuṣṭubh was stated in the preceding sūtra. The deity, Indra, continues. Its application: in the Mahāvrata, in the niṣkevalya [śastra], the whole sūkta [reading uncertain] is to be recited; Śaunaka lays this down in the section ūrū: 'indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan — Anuṣṭubh; of it, the first half of the first rik is joined with the first half of the next, with the half-rik that follows in the śastra, [the rest of the sentence on the pāda-wise interchange is hard to read]' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 3-1-1 [?]). And the Brāhmaṇa, in the first Āraṇyaka, in the section pra vo mahe on the paṅkti: 'the words indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan are to be appended' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1-5-2 [?]). Again, on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya rite, in the niṣkevalya śastra, the triplet indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan is the anurūpa: in the section stomo vardhamānaḥ it is laid down: 'upa no haribhiḥ sutam; indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan' (Āśvalāyana 6-12 [?])." The first words of the printed Sanskrit, as read, run indraṃ viśvā ity-ṛcasya; the Anukramaṇī count aṣṭau — eight — agrees with the sūkta's eight riks.

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The ṛṣi of the sūkta indraṃ viśvā is Jetā, son of the sage Madhucchandas. The Anukramaṇikā too says "indram aṣṭau jetā mādhucchandasaḥ" — that is, "of the [eight] riks indraṃ viśvā, the ṛṣi is Jetā, son of Madhucchandas." The meter, Anuṣṭubh, was stated earlier. The deity is Indra. Application: in the sacrifice called Mahāvrata, when reciting the mantras of the niṣkevalya-śastra, this whole sūkta is to be recited; Śaunaka says so in the section ūrū of the Śrauta-sūtra, and the Aitareya Āraṇyaka (3-1-1 [?]) gives the order of application of this sūkta, and the Brāhmaṇa-portion that explains it is in the same Āraṇyaka (1-5-2 [?]) in the section pra vo mahe. And on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya sacrifice, when reciting the niṣkevalya-śastra, the three riks beginning indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan are to be used for the stomāvāpa; Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra says so in the sūtra upa no haribhiḥ sutam indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan.
