Sūkta 13, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

नक्तोषासा सुपेशसास्मिन्यज्ञ उप ह्वये । इदं नो बर्हिरासदे ॥७॥

naktoṣāsā supeśasāsmin yajña upa hvaye | idaṃ no barhir āsade ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

नक्तोषसा । सुऽपेशसा । अस्मिन् । यज्ञे । उप । ह्वये ॥ इदम् । नः । बर्हिः । आऽसदे ॥७॥

naktoṣasā | su-peśasā | asmin | yajñe | upa | hvaye || idam | naḥ | barhiḥ | ā-sade ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

नक्तशब्द उषःशब्दश्च लोके कालविशेषवाचिनौ । इह तु तत्कालाभिमानिन्यौ वह्निमूर्तिद्वयोः प्रयुज्येते । नक्तोषासा नक्तोषसो नामिके वह्निमूर्ती अस्मिन्नेत्र वर्तमाने यज्ञे कर्मण्युप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । किमर्थम् । नो ऽस्मदीयमिदं वेद्यामास्तीर्णं बर्हिर्गर्भमासदे । आसत्त्वं । प्राप्तं । कीदृशौ । सुपेशसा शोभनरूपयुक्ते ॥ नक्तं तोषात्तः नक्तोषसा । द्वितीयोद्भिवचनस्य सुषां सुलुगित्याकारः मलोप उपधादीर्घश्छन्दसः । देवताद्वन्द्वे च । पा. ६-२-१४१ । इति पूर्वोत्तरपदयोर्युगपत्प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सुपेशसा । रोभनं पेशो रूपं ययोस्ते । पूर्वपदादाकारः । पेशःशब्दो ऽसन्त्ये ऽन्तोदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ सन्नाभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वस्यापवादत्वेनाद्युदात्तम् । … अस्मिन् । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वात् । आसदे । षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । धात्वादेः षः सः । आङ्पूर्वात्सदेस्तुमर्थे भावे क्विप् । … कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

naktaśabda uṣaḥśabdaś ca loke kāla-viśeṣa-vācinau | iha tu tat-kālābhimāninyau vahni-mūrti-dvayoḥ prayujyete | naktoṣāsā naktoṣaso nāmike vahni-mūrtī asminn eva vartamāne yajñe karmaṇy upa hvaye | āhvayāmi | kim-artham | no 'smadīyam idaṃ vedyām āstīrṇaṃ barhir garbham āsade | āsattvaṃ | prāptaṃ | kīdṛśau | supeśasā śobhana-rūpa-yukte || naktaṃ toṣāt taḥ naktoṣasā | dvitīyodbhi-vacanasya suṣāṃ suluk ity ākāraḥ malopa upadhā-dīrghaś chandasaḥ | devatā-dvandve ca | pā. 6-2-141 | iti pūrvottara-padayor yugapat prakṛti-svaratvam | supeśasā | śobhanaṃ peśo rūpaṃ yayos te | pūrvapadād ākāraḥ | peśaḥ-śabdo 'santye 'ntodāttaḥ | bahuvrīhau sannābhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvasyāpavādatvenādyudāttam | ... asmin | ūḍidam ity-ādinā vibhakter udāttatvāt | āsade | ṣadḷ viśaraṇa-gaty-avasādaneṣu | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | āṅ-pūrvāt sader tumarthe bhāve kvip | ... kṛd-uttara-pada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||

Translation: "The words nakta (night) and uṣas (dawn) in ordinary speech denote particular times; but here the presiding forms of those times, two Fire-forms, are meant. Naktoṣāsā — the two Fire-forms named Night and Dawn — in this very sacrifice now in progress, upa hvaye: I invoke. For what? Naḥ idam barhiḥ āsade — so that [they] may sit on this our barhis spread on the altar. What are they like? Supeśasā — endowed with beautiful forms." Grammar noted briefly: naktoṣāsā is a dvandva of two deities, "night and dawn," in which both members keep their natural accent by Pā. 6-2-141 [?], with the Vedic ā for the dual ending and lengthening; supeśas is a bahuvrīhi "of beautiful form," initial-udātta; āsade is the infinitive of sad with the prefix ā and kvip in the sense of tumun, with the kṛdanta second-member accent. Some of the Sanskrit is compressed.

original p. 556

Rik 7: word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

नः (naḥ) — our | इदम् (idam) — this, spread on the altar | बर्हिः (barhiḥ) — the darbha grass prepared as a seat | आसदे (āsade) — in order that they may come and sit [on] it (that is, to sit on the darbha that we have spread) | सुपेशसा (supeśasā) — endowed with beautiful forms | नक्तोषासा (naktoṣāsā) — the deities of night and dawn (or the presiding deities of those times) | अस्मिन् यज्ञे (asmin yajñe) — in this sacrifice now proceeding | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I invoke.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

In the sacrifice we are performing, we have spread darbha on the altar and made a seat. To sit on this seat, I now call, in this ongoing sacrifice, the two deities named Naktoṣāsā (the presiding deities of night and of dawn), who shine in beautiful forms.

॥ English Translation ॥

I invoke here at this sacrifice Night and Dawn, the beautifully adorned goddesses, that they may sit down on this our sacrificial grass.

original pp. 557–558

Rik 7: Special Topics

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In this rik the presiding deities of night and of the morning time, called Naktoṣāsā, are invoked. Yāska's explanation of the word naktoṣāsā is as follows:

उषासानक्ता । उषासानक्तेत्येते नक्ता च उषाश्च व्याख्याताः । नक्तेति रात्रिनाम नक्तेति [?] अव्यक्तवर्णा ॥ uṣāsānaktā | uṣāsānaktety ete naktā ca uṣāś ca vyākhyātāḥ | nakteti rātri-nāma nakteti [?] avyakta-varṇā || (Nirukta 8-11 [?]; the print is compressed and I give it as a best reading.)

Although naktoṣāsā and uṣāsānaktā are two different forms in the text, the sense is the same. The explanation of the word uṣas was given earlier. Naktā is a name of night. For naktā is "of indistinct colour"; since things are not clearly seen in the dark of night, it is called naktā; at this time living beings are unable to do their work. Yāska explains: "anakti kledayati bhūtāni āvaśyāyena iti" — "it anoints, it wets beings with dew"; "api vā naktā avyaktavarṇā" — "or naktā is of indistinct colour; as the day makes the forms of everything manifest, the night does not." Since the darkness gives no chance for beings' works to go on properly, it is troublesome to them; for this reason the night is called naktā; or because nothing is clearly seen, it is called naktā. By day the forms of all things are clear; at night nothing is seen: so this meaning is given for the word naktā for night-time (Nirukta 8-11).

The meaning of the word uṣas has been given before: "vibhāvarī, sūnarī and the other sixteen words are names of dawn" (Nirukta 1-8 [?]); and

उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥ uṣāḥ kasmād ucchatīti satyā rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ || "Why is uṣas so called? From ucchati ('it shines out'); [it is] the last part of the night."

Uṣas is called so because it removes the darkness of night; it is the last part of night. To support this sense, he gives a rik:

इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा । यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवाय एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥ idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āgāc citraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā | yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya evā rātry uṣase yonim āraik || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-113-1 [?]; printed "१-११३-१") ("This best light of lights has come; the wondrous sign has been born, pervading. As [Night], impelled for Savitṛ's impulse, so has Night yielded her womb to Dawn." — my gloss, tentative.)

and explains it in his Nirukta: "idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āgamat | citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñāte-tamam ajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamam | yathā prasūtā savituḥ prasavāya rātrir ādityasya | evaṃ rātry uṣase yonim aricat sthānam | strī-yonir abhiyuta enāṃ garbhaḥ" (Nirukta 2-19 [?]) — "the best light of lights has come; the wondrous sign, the most distinguished, has been born; as the night, set in motion for the urging of Savitṛ, the sun, so the night has given up to the dawn her place, her womb."

The best, most brilliant light of the sun is rising; the dawn-time, which precedes that light, runs before it like a banner — the light of the sun shines through the whole day, and at the time of setting becomes the womb, i.e., the cause, for the night; so the night, at the end of its own time, becomes the cause for dawn. Yoni means a birth-place. At the end of the day night, and at the end of night dawn, are one: they come into view in a cycle of change: that is the chief idea. Hence uṣas means the light that, after the night has passed, spreads through all the quarters before sunrise and shines forth: dawn.

The Bhāṣyakāra's explanation: "nakta-śabda uṣaḥ-śabdaś ca loke kāla-viśeṣa-vācinau | iha tu tat-kālābhimāniny-agni-mūrti-dvaye prayujyete" — nakta and uṣas in ordinary use denote particular times, night and morning; here, in this rik or in the Ṛgveda, these words denote the presiding deities of night and of morning-time; hence naktoṣāsā or uṣāsānaktā are used in the sense of two forms of Agni — as the deities presiding over night and the morning-time. The word supeśasā ("of fine form or shape") used in this rik supports this sense: since night and dawn are divisions of time, they have neither form nor shape. In the view that these are the presiding deities of those times, a form can be assigned to those deities. Since in this rik an invocation (upa hvaye) is stated, it is to be understood that the presiding deities of these times are meant. The s in naktoṣasā is lengthened for the convenience of the meter in the Saṃhitā.

"Supeśasā" — peśas is read among the sixteen words for 'form' beginning with nirṇik, varpas (Nirukta 3-7 [?]); so peśas means form; hence supeśasā = śobhanarūpayukte — "endowed with beautiful form."

"Āsade" — ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu: "to sit; to come and sit."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar page 559, noted briefly

नक्तोषसा (naktoṣasā) — "naktaṃ ca uṣāś ca": a dvandva compound; the dual au → ā ("supāṃ suluk…," Pā. 7-1-39 [?]); the m of naktam is dropped, and the a of uṣas, as penultimate, lengthens, both by Vedic license; "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. 6-2-141 [?]) — in a dvandva of deity-words both members keep their natural accent together. सुपेशसा (supeśasā) — "śobhanaṃ peśo yayos te": the neuter peśas is initial-udātta by "nabviṣayasyānisantasya" (Phiṭ-sūtra 36 [?]); a bahuvrīhi would keep the first member's accent (Pā. 6-2-1 [?]), overridden by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. 6-2-172 [?]) giving final-udātta, overridden again by "ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi" (Pā. 6-2-119 [?]) — as peśas is two-syllabled and initial-udātta, it stays initial-udātta. अस्मिन् (asmin) — the ending is udātta by "ūḍidam…" (Pā. 6-1-171 [?]). आसदे (āsade) — root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; ṣ → s ("dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ," Pā. 6-1-64 [?]); "sampadādibhyaḥ kvip" (Pā. 3-3-108 vārttika 9 [?]): kvip after the root sad preceded by ā, in the sense of the action; sad is udātta by the root; ā + sad compound ("kugatiprādayaḥ," Pā. 2-2-18 [?]); the kṛdanta second member's accent by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139 [?]); the dative singular ṅe, unaccented, then svarita ("udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ," Pā. 8-4-66 [?]).

॥७॥

original p. 559

Sūkta 13, Rik 8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता सुजिह्वा उप ह्वये होतारा दैव्या कवी । यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमम् ॥८॥

tā sujihvā upa hvaye hotārā daivyā kavī | yajñaṃ no yakṣatām imam ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता । सुऽजिह्वा । उप । ह्वये । होतारा । दैव्या । कवी इति ॥ यज्ञम् । नः । यक्षताम् । इमम् ॥८॥

tā | su-jihvā | upa | hvaye | hotārā | daivyā | kavī iti || yajñam | naḥ | yakṣatām | imam ||8||

original pp. 560–563

Rik 8: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

छान्दसो ऽत्र सर्वनामत्वात्प्रसिद्धार्थवाची । ता तौ याजिकानां प्रसिद्धौ द्वावग्नी उपह्वये । आह्वयामि । नो ऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञं यक्षतां । तावुभौ यजतामनुतिष्ठतां । कीदृशौ । सुजिह्वौ शोभनजिह्वोपेतौ । प्रियवचनौ शोभनज्वालौ वेत्यर्थः । होतारौ होमनिष्पादकौ दैव्या दैव्यौ देवसंबन्धिनौ । अत एवोमावग्नी दैव्यहोतृनामकौ । कवी मेधाविनौ ॥

chāndaso 'tra sarvanāmatvāt prasiddhārtha-vācī | tā tau yājñikānāṃ prasiddhau dvāv agnī upahvaye | āhvayāmi | no 'smadīyam imaṃ yajñaṃ yakṣatāṃ | tāv ubhau yajatām anutiṣṭhatāṃ | kīdṛśau | sujihvau śobhana-jihvopetau | priya-vacanau śobhana-jvālau vety arthaḥ | hotārau homa-niṣpādakau daivyā daivyau deva-saṃbandhinau | ata evomāv agnī daivya-hotṛ-nāmakau | kavī medhāvinau ||

Translation: "[Tā is the Vedic dual of the pronoun, standing for something well known:] tā tau — those two fires, well known to the sacrificers — upa hvaye: I invoke. May they yakṣatām — perform, carry out — imam yajñam, this our sacrifice. What kind? Sujihvā — having good tongues; that is, of sweet speech, or of fine flames; hotārā — accomplishers of the homa; daivyā — belonging to the gods; hence the two fires bear the names Daivya and Hotṛ [Daivya-hotārā]; kavī — wise." Grammar noted briefly below.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सुजिह्वा (sujihvā) — having excellent tongues, that is, speaking pleasant words or having fine flames | कवी (kavī) — wise | ता (tā) — those, well known in the rites of sacrifice | दैव्या (daivyā) — belonging to the gods | होतारा (hotārā) — accomplishers of the homa | the two fire-forms called Daivya-hotārā उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I invoke (near me) | नः (naḥ) — our (i.e., that we perform) | इमं यज्ञम् (imaṃ yajñam) — this sacrifice | यक्षताम् (yakṣatām) — may they perform.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The two named Daivya and Hotṛ (special forms of Agni) are gods; they speak pleasant words (or are brightly flaming); they are very wise, and accomplish the hotṛ work. I call such two divine hotṛs; may they come here and take the hotṛ seat and carry out the sacrifice we perform.

॥ English Translation ॥

I invoke those Daivya and Hotara, those two divine hotries who are good-tongued and wise. May they perform this our sacrifice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

On the words daivyā hotārā, Yāska's explanation:

दैव्या होतारा दैव्यौ होतारावयं चाङ्गिरसौ च मध्यमः ॥ daivyā hotārā daivyau hotārāv ayaṃ cāṅgirasau ca madhyamaḥ || (Nirukta 8-?? [?])

— that is, this points to Agni. Since Agni invokes the gods, he stands in the middle between gods and men; and the source gives an example:

दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै । प्रचोदयन्ता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशन्ता ॥ daivyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai | pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśantā || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-110-7 [?]; printed "१०-११०-७") ("The two divine invokers, first, of fair speech, fashioning the sacrifice for man to worship, urging on at the gatherings, the two poets, showing in all directions the eastern light." — my gloss, tentative.)

For this, Durgācārya's commentary: "yāv etau daivyau hotārau | deveṣu bhavau daivyau | devāv eva daivyau | svārthe eva taddhitaḥ | manuṣyahotārāv apekṣya | daivyā hotārā hotṛ-maitrāvaruṇau iti viśeṣaṇam | hotārau hotārāv āhvātārau devānāṃ vāyv-agnī | prathamā prathamau mukhyau manuṣya-hotārāv apekṣya | suvācā suvācau praśasta-vācau susṭutau | mimānā yajñaṃ yajña-nirmātārau nityam | manuṣaḥ manuṣyasya yajadhyai yajanāya | pracodayantā pracodayamānau | vidatheṣu yajñeṣu | kārū kartārau." The chief idea: among the gods, Agni and Vāyu are known as hotṛs; among men, the priests Hotṛ and Maitrāvaruṇa are hotṛs. Agni (or Agni and Vāyu) stand in the middle between gods and men and make a connection with them; so Agni is called "middle." The names daivyā hotārā occur not only in the Āpri-sūktas but also in

त्वष्टारं वायुमृभवो य ओहते दैव्या होतारा उषसं स्वस्तये । tvaṣṭāraṃ vāyum ṛbhavo ya ohate daivyā hotārā uṣasaṃ svastaye | (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-65-10 [?]; printed "१०-६५-१०") (A best reading of compressed print; no gloss offered.)

दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा पुरोहित ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेमि साधुया ॥ daivyā hotārā prathamā purohitā ṛtasya panthām anv emi sādhuyā || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-66-13 [?]; printed "१०-६६-१३") ("I follow, in a straight way, the path of order, the two first divine invokers, the two house-priests." — my gloss, tentative.)

These two riks alone have them [in non-Āpri contexts]. In Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 6-?-1 [?] the word jātavedasā is used of them, and in 10-? [?] purohitau. Since the words mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai, yajñeṣu mānuṣeṣu kārū, pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū in these riks say that these deities carry out or urge on the sacrifices that men perform, calling them purohitas is natural. Among the deities, the hotṛs are Agni and Vāyu; among men the hotṛ is the helper-priest called Maitrāvaruṇa, and these are called hotṛs. This Maitrāvaruṇa directs the other priests, by praiṣa mantras, to carry out their duties. In the Yajurveda (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 6-1-?) it is said, "the Maitrāvaruṇa assigns speech to the [other priests] in front."

"Sujihvā" — śobhanā jihvā yayos tau: "of beautiful tongues": śobhana-jihvopetau, priyavacanau, śobhana-jvālau vā: "with good tongues, of sweet speech, or of beautiful flames." Speaking of Agni, the sense is "with beautiful flames."

"Yakṣatām" — yajatām: "may they sacrifice," i.e., carry out the sacrifice.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 562–563, noted briefly

ता (tā) — "tau": tad + dual au → auṭ; "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39 [?]) gives ā; "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. 7-2-102 [?]): d → a; "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97 [?]) pararūpa; savarṇadīrgha; the single substitute is udātta ("ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ," Pā. 8-2-5 [?]). सुजिह्वा (sujihvā) — "śobhanā jihvā yayos tau": jihvā is irregularly formed with van by "śevayahvajihvāgrīvāpvāmīvāḥ" (Uṇ. 1-154 [?]) from liha āsvādane, l → j and the loss of guṇa; initial-udātta; in the bahuvrīhi the first member's accent would stand (Pā. 6-2-1 [?]), overridden by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. 6-2-172 [?]) giving final-udātta to jihvā; the dual au → auṭ, with vṛddhi of the a + o ("vṛddhir eci," Pā. 6-1-85 [?]) barred, but by the maxim "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" the resulting ā [print: "ō" from vṛddhi] is udātta; in Saṃhitā sujihvā + upa, "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78 [?]) gives āv; "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19 [?]) drops the v; guṇa is barred by pūrvatrāsiddham (Pā. 8-2-1 [?]). होतारा (hotārā) — root hu dānādanayoḥ, tṛn ("nvul-tṛcau," Pā. 3-1-133 [?]); laghūpadha-guṇa; the dual au → ā; "ṛto jisarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-110 [?]) guṇa of the ṛ with raparatva; "āp tṛn-tṛc…" (Pā. 6-4-11 [?]) lengthens the penultimate; initial-udātta. दैव्या (daivyā) — deva from divu with ac ("nandigrahipacādibhyo…," Pā. 3-1-134 [?]), final-udātta by cit; "devād yañ ñau" [print: "devād yaj ñau" (Pā. 4-1-85 vārttika 3 [?])]: yañ after deva in the senses of the prāgdīvyatīya group, here "devasya imau"; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ (Pā. 7-2-117 [?]) gives vṛddhi; "ñniti" gives initial-udātta ("ñnityādir nityam," Pā. 6-1-197 [?]); yasyeti ca drops the a of deva before ya: daivya; the dual as before. यक्षताम् (yakṣatām) — root yaja devapūjāyām; loṭ third dual tām; "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. 3-4-85 [?]); "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-101 [?]); sip — siṃ-bahulaṃ leṭi (Pā. 3-1-34 [?]) with bahulagrahaṇa gives sip even though the śap-vikaraṇa; yaj + s + a + tām: "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. 8-2-30 [?]) j → g; "khari ca" (Pā. 8-4-55 [?]) g → k; "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59 [?]) s → ṣ: yakṣatām; wholly unaccented ("tiṅ atiṅaḥ," Pā. 8-1-28 [?]).

॥८॥

original p. 564

Sūkta 13, Rik 9

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इळा सरस्वती मही तिस्रो देवीर्मयोभुवः । बर्हिः सीदन्त्वस्रिधः ॥९॥

iḷā sarasvatī mahī tisro devīr mayobhuvaḥ | barhiḥ sīdantv asridhaḥ ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इळा । सरस्वती । मही । तिस्रः । देवीः । मयःऽभुवः ॥ बर्हिः । सीदन्तु । अस्रिधः ॥९॥

iḷā | sarasvatī | mahī | tisraḥ | devīḥ | mayaḥ-bhuvaḥ || barhiḥ | sīdantu | asridhaḥ ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अत्र महीशब्दो महत्त्वगुणयुक्तां भारतीं वाचष्टे । अन्यैर्हि आप्रीसूक्तेषु सद्वैश्विळा सरस्वती भारतीत्याम्नातत्वात् । इळादिशब्दाभिधेया वह्निमूर्तयस्तिस्रो देवीर्दीप्यमाना बर्हिर्वेद्यामास्तीर्णं सीदन्तु । प्राप्नुवन्तु । कीदृश्यः । मयोभुवः सुखोत्पादिका अस्रिधः शोषणेन क्षयेन वा रहिताः ॥ इळा । ईड स्तुतौ । छान्दसो डस्य ळत्वम् । क्विप् । धातुस्वरः । टापं चापि हलन्तानां यथा वाचा दिशा निशेति टाप् । सरस्वती । सरोस्यसुनन्तो नित्त्वाद्यादयुदात्तः । तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् । आदुपधत्वाद्वत्त्वम् । तसौ मत्वर्थ इति भत्वेन पदत्वस्य बाधितत्वाद्रुत्वाद्यभावः । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । मतुब्ङीपौ पित्त्वादनुदात्तौ । मही । महतीशब्दे तकारलोपश्छान्दसः । यस्येति चेत्यकार-लोपः । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण ङीप उदात्तत्वम् । तिस्रः । त्रिशब्दाज्जसि त्रिचतुरोः स्त्रियां तिसृचतसृ । पा. ७-२-९९ । इति तिसृ-आदेशः । अचि र ऋतः । पा. ७-२-१०० । इति रेफादेशः । तिसृभ्यो जसः । पा. ६-१-१६६ । इति जस उदात्तत्वम् । देवीः । देवानां पत्न्यो देव्यः पुंयोगादाख्यायामिति ङीष् । यस्येति चेत्यकार लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण ङीष उदात्तत्वम् । जसि दीर्घाज्जसि च । पा. ६-१-१०५ । इति निषिद्धं दीर्घत्वम् । वा छन्दसीति पक्षे दीर्घत्वं जायते । मयोभुवः । मीञ् हिंसायाम् । हिनस्ति दुःखमिति सुखं मयः । तद्भावयन्तीति मयोभुवः । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थाद्भवेः क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । बर्हिः । बृंहेर्नलोपश्चेति सि प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । सीदन्तु । षद्लृ विशरणादौ । पाघ्रेत्यादिना सीदादेशः । अस्रिधः । स्रिधेर्हिंसार्थस्य शोषणार्थस्य वा सम्पदादिभ्यो भावे क्विपि नञ् । बहुव्रीहिः । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरं बाधित्वा नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं ॥

atra mahī-śabdo mahattva-guṇa-yuktāṃ bhāratīṃ vācaṣṭe | anyair hi āprī-sūkteṣu sad-vaiśvā iḷā sarasvatī bhāratīty āmnātatvāt | iḷādi-śabdābhidheyā vahni-mūrtayas tisro devīr dīpyamānā barhir vedyām āstīrṇaṃ sīdantu | prāpnuvantu | kīdṛśyaḥ | mayobhuvaḥ sukhotpādikā asridhaḥ śoṣaṇena kṣayena vā rahitāḥ || iḷā | īḍa stutau | chāndaso ḍasya ḷatvam | kvip | dhātu-svaraḥ | ṭāpaṃ cāpi halantānāṃ yathā vācā diśā niśeti ṭāp | sarasvatī | saro 'sy asunanto nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | tad asyāstīti matup | ādupadhatvād vattvam | tasau matvartha iti bhatvena padatvasya bādhitatvād rutvādy abhāvaḥ | ugitaś ceti ṅīp | matub-ṅīpau pittvād anudāttau | mahī | mahatī-śabde takāra-lopaś chāndasaḥ | yasyeti ca ity akāra-lopaḥ | udātta-nivṛtti-svareṇa ṅīpa udāttatvam | tisraḥ | tri-śabdāj jasi tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ | pā. 7-2-99 | iti tisṛ-ādeśaḥ | aci ra ṛtaḥ | pā. 7-2-100 | iti rephādeśaḥ | tisṛbhyo jasaḥ | pā. 6-1-166 | iti jasa udāttatvam | devīḥ | devānāṃ patnyo devyaḥ puṃyogād ākhyāyām iti ṅīṣ | ... mayobhuvaḥ | mīñ hiṃsāyām | hinasti duḥkham iti sukhaṃ mayaḥ | tad bhāvayantīti mayobhuvaḥ | antarbhāvita-ṇyarthād bhaveḥ kvip | kṛd-uttara-pada-prakṛti-svaratvam | barhiḥ | bṛṃher nalopaś ceti si pratyayaḥ | pratyaya-svaraḥ | sīdantu | ṣadḷ viśaraṇādau | pāghretyādinā sīdādeśaḥ | asridhaḥ | sridher hiṃsārthasya śoṣaṇārthasya vā sampadādibhyo bhāve kvipi nañ | bahuvrīhiḥ | pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaraṃ bādhitvā nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ ||

Translation: "Here the word mahī denotes Bhāratī, endowed with the quality of greatness; for in other Āpri-sūktas the triple Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Bhāratī is recited. The three shining Fire-forms denoted by the words Iḷā and the rest, tisro devīḥ, sīdantu: may sit, may take their seat, on the barhis spread on the altar. What are they like? Mayobhuvaḥ — producing happiness; asridhaḥ — free of drying up or of decay." Grammar noted briefly: iḷā from īḍ with the Vedic ḷ and kvip; sarasvatī from saras with matup and ṅīp; mahī with the Vedic loss of the t of mahatī; tisraḥ from tri with tisṛ (Pā. 7-2-99 [?]) and r for ṛ (Pā. 7-2-100 [?]), the ending udātta by Pā. 6-1-166 [?]; devīḥ with ṅīṣ; mayobhuvaḥ — 'that which makes happiness be,' with kvip from bhū with the causative inside; sīdantu with sīd for sad (Pā. 7-3-78 [?]); asridh 'without drying up' with nañ. Some Sanskrit is compressed.

original pp. 565–566

Rik 9: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

मयोभुवः (mayobhuvaḥ) — giving happiness | अस्रिधः (asridhaḥ) — not cruel, or doing no harm | इळा (iḷā) — the goddess named Iḷā | सरस्वती (sarasvatī) — the goddess Sarasvatī | मही (mahī) — the goddess [named Bhāratī] endowed with the quality of greatness | तिस्रः देवीः (tisraḥ devīḥ) — these three goddesses, forms of Agni, shining, called by the words Iḷā and the rest | बर्हिः (barhiḥ) — the darbha spread on the altar as a seat | सीदन्तु (sīdantu) — may they sit (that is, may they come and sit on the darbha).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May the three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī (Mahī) — who are forms of Agni, shine brilliantly, give happiness to all, and harm none — come to the darbha spread on the sacrificial altar as a seat and sit upon it.

॥ English Translation ॥

May Ila, Saraswati, Mahi (Bharati), the three comfort-giving and unhurting goddesses sit on the sacrificial grass.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

On the subject of tisro devīḥ, Yāska says only "tisro devīḥ | tisro devīs tisro devyaḥ ||" (Nirukta 8-?? [?]), and, for an example, quotes the rik

आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्वदिह चेतयन्ती । तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदन्तु ॥ ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tūyam etv iḷā manuṣvad iha cetayantī | tisro devīr barhir edaṃ syonaṃ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadantu || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-110-8 [?]; printed "१०-११०-८") ("May Bhāratī come quickly to our sacrifice, and Iḷā, awakening [us] here like Manu; may the three goddesses, with Sarasvatī, skilful workers, sit on this pleasant barhis." — my gloss, tentative.)

and explains: "aitu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipram | bharate ādityas tasya bhā | iḷā ca manuṣvad iha cetayamānā | tisro devyo barhir idaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sarvāṇi āsīdantu" (Nirukta 8-?? [?]), that is: "may Bhāratī, 'the light of Āditya, who bears [the world],' come quickly to our sacrifice; and Iḷā, awakening here like Manu; may the three goddesses, and Sarasvatī, sit on this pleasant barhis." The Kannada explanation of Yāska's gloss continues on p. 566, to be taken up with the next batch. The Kannada explanation of Yāska's gloss on p. 566:) "Bhāratī" — bharata is one of the twelve Ādityas; bhā means the lustre of the Āditya; hence bhāratī is the light of the sun, or the fire shining in the orb of the sun. "Iḷā" — iḷā means the earth. Manuṣvat cetayantī — having the power to urge as men do: she makes the people on earth take up food and other nourishment, and gives wealth; so the iḷā-deity is a special form of Agni who dwells in the earth-region. "Sarasvatī" — since she is the presiding deity of the lightning in the atmosphere, Sarasvatī is said to be the form of Agni who dwells in the atmosphere. Hence it is customary to say that the three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Bhāratī are three forms of the fire that is in heaven, atmosphere and earth. (The source refers the reader to its pages 64–69 [sic: "६४–६९ನೇ ಪೇಜು"] for further treatment.

original pp. 566–568

Rik 9: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

"Mahī" — the Bhāṣyakāra says: mahī-śabdo mahattva-guṇa-yuktāṃ bhāratīṃ vācaṣṭe, anyair hi āprī-sūkteṣu sad-vaiśvā iḷā sarasvatī bhāratīty āmnātatvāt [as in the bhāṣya above]: the word mahī in this rik means bhāratī, endowed with the quality of greatness; for in the Āpri-sūktas elsewhere the three are plainly named Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Bhāratī; here only two names are given and, in the place of the third, mahī — so one may easily infer that mahī denotes Bhāratī. Some Western scholars hold that mahī denotes a separate deity; that is not right; mahī was probably used in place of bhāratī for the convenience of the meter.

"Barhiḥ sīdantu" — vedyām āstīrṇaṃ prāpnuvantu — "let them reach the darbha spread out as a seat," i.e., let them sit on the seat made of darbha.

"Iḷā, sarasvatī, mahī" — īḍa stutau; saraḥ asyāstīti; mahī mahatī, takāra-lopaś chandasi — since she is praised she is iḷā; since she has saras (water) she is sarasvatī; the t of mahatī falls away in the metre, so mahī: thus the sense of the parts is established.

"Devīḥ" — devānāṃ patnyo devyaḥ | tāḥ | athavā devīr dīpyamānāḥ: "wives of the gods, or shining ones": they are devīḥ because they are wives of the gods or because they shine.

"Mayobhuvaḥ" — mīñ hiṃsāyām; hinasti duḥkham iti sukhaṃ mayaḥ | tad bhāvayantīti mayobhuvaḥ: mī is "to injure"; that which destroys sorrow is happiness (mayas); those who produce it are mayobhuvaḥ: "makers of happiness."

"Asridhaḥ" — sridher hiṃsārthasya śoṣaṇārthasya vā bhāve kvip; śoṣeṇa kṣayeṇa vā rahitāḥ: "without drying up, without decay" — those who have no sridh, i.e., not cruel, not given to harm; asridhaḥ — free of destruction.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 567–568, noted briefly

इळा (iḷā) — root īḍa stutau; the long ī is shortened by Vedic license; kvip ("kvip ca," Pā. 3-2-76 [?]), dropped; accent of the root; ḍ → ḷ in the Veda ("dvayor ḍalayor aikyam smaryate" [print compressed]); the feminine ṭāp after a consonant-ending stem ("ajādyataṣṭāp," Pā. 4-1-4 [?] with the statement ṭāp ca api halantānām yathā vācā niśā diśā). सरस्वती (sarasvatī) — root sṛ gatau with asun ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," Uṇ. 4-188 [?]); guṇa, raparatva: saras; initial-udātta, nit; "saras asyāsti": matup ("tad asyāsty asminn iti matup," Pā. 5-2-94 [?]); "mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-9 [?]) turns the m of matup into v after a stem with a as the penultimate; "tasau matvarthe" (Pā. 1-4-19 [?]) gives bha status, blocking pada-status, so the ru-rule ("sasajuṣo ruḥ," Pā. 8-2-66 [?]) and the like do not apply; "ugitaś ca" (Pā. 4-1-6 [?]) gives ṅīp; both matup and ṅīp are pit and unaccented. मही (mahī) — the t of mahatī is dropped by Vedic license, and the a after h by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148 [?]); the ī is udātta by "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-161 [?]). तिस्रः (tisraḥ) — "tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ" (Pā. 7-2-99 [?]): tisṛ replaces tri in the feminine before a suffix beginning with a vowel [when the sense is feminine]; "tisṛ" + jas; "ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-110 [?]) would give guṇa, barred by "aci ra ṛtaḥ" (Pā. 7-2-100 [?]) which gives r before a vowel-initial ending; ru, visarga: tisraḥ; "tisṛbhyo jasaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-166 [?]): jas after tisṛ is udātta. देवीः (devīḥ) — "devānāṃ patnyaḥ": the feminine of a word formed on the husband's name, "puṃyogād ākhyāyām" (Pā. 4-1-48 [?]): ṅīṣ; the a dropped; jas; the pūrvasavarṇa lengthening optional by "vā chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-106 [?]). मयोभुवः (mayobhuvaḥ) — "mīñ hiṃsāyām" (kryādi): mi + asun ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," Uṇ. 4-188 [?]); guṇa, ay: mayas; mayas means "happiness"; "mayo bhāvayanti" — root bhū with the causative sense inside, kvip ("kvip ca," Pā. 3-2-76 [?]); "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvoriyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. 6-4-77 [?]) gives uv; mayas + bhū: ru, u and guṇa (Pā. 6-1-113 [?]); "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139 [?]) gives the accent of the kṛdanta second member, final-udātta: mayobhūḥ; nominative plural mayobhuvaḥ.

॥९॥

original p. 569

Rik 9 grammar closes; Sūkta 13, Rik 10

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

बर्हिः (barhiḥ) — root bṛha bṛhi vṛddhau, idit, so num ("idito num dhātoḥ," Pā. 7-1-58 [?]); "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. 3-146 [?]) gives isi and loss of the n; laghūpadha-guṇa; the suffix accent, final-udātta. सीदन्तु (sīdantu) — root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; ṣ → s ("dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ," Pā. 6-1-64 [?]); loṭ third plural jhi → jh → ant ("jho 'ntaḥ," Pā. 7-1-3 [?]); u for i of loṭ ("eruḥ," Pā. 3-4-86 [?]); śap; sad + a + antu: "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. 7-3-78 [?]) gives sīda; sīdantu; wholly unaccented ("tiṅ atiṅaḥ," Pā. 8-1-28 [?]). अस्रिधः (asridhaḥ) — root sridh in the sense of harm or drying up; kvip in the action sense by "sampadādibhyaḥ kvip" (Pā. 3-3-108 vārttika [?]); "na vidyate sridh yāsāṃ tāḥ asridhaḥ": a bahuvrīhi with nañ; the first member's accent would stand ("bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam," Pā. 6-2-1 [?]), overridden by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. 6-2-172 [?]), which gives final-udātta to the member after nañ.

॥९॥

original p. 569

Sūkta 13, Rik 10

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इह त्वष्टारमग्रियं विश्वरूपमुप ह्वये । अस्माकमस्तु केवलः ॥१०॥

iha tvaṣṭāram agriyaṃ viśvarūpam upa hvaye | asmākam astu kevalaḥ ||10||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इह । त्वष्टारम् । अग्रियम् । विश्वऽरूपम् । उप । ह्वये ॥ अस्माकम् । अस्तु । केवलः ॥१०॥

iha | tvaṣṭāram | agriyam | viśva-rūpam | upa | hvaye || asmākam | astu | kevalaḥ ||10||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

पत्नीसंयाजे त्वष्टुः पुरोनुवाक्येह त्वष्टारमग्रियमिति । शं युवाकाय संप्रेषिते इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । सं ते पयांसि समु यन्तु वाजा इह त्वष्टारमग्रियम् । आ. १-१० । इति ॥

patnīsaṃyāje tvaṣṭuḥ puronuvākyehe tvaṣṭāram agriyam iti | śaṃ yuvākāya saṃpreṣite iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam | ā. 1-10 | iti ||

त्वष्टारं त्वष्टृनामकमग्निमिह कर्मण्युपह्वये । कीदृशम् । अग्रियं श्रेष्ठं विश्वरूपं बहुविधरूपोपेतं । सो ऽस्माकं केवलो ऽसाधारणो ऽस्तु । इतरयजमानेभ्यो ऽस्यधिकमनुग्रहं करोत्वित्यर्थः ॥ त्वष्टारम् । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । तृन् । स्वरतिसूतीत्यादिना । पा. ७-२-४४ । इति वेट् [reading uncertain] … अग्रियम् । अग्रादित्यन्तप्रादित्यादिभ्यो घच्च । पा. ४-४-११६ । … विश्वरूपम् । विश्वानि रूपाणि त्वष्टृस्थन्नेन यस्य । … अस्माकम् । … केवलः । वृषादेराकृतिगणत्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

tvaṣṭāraṃ tvaṣṭṛ-nāmakam agnim iha karmaṇy upahvaye | kīdṛśam | agriyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ viśvarūpaṃ bahuvidha-rūpopetaṃ | so 'smākaṃ kevalo 'sādhāraṇo 'stu | itara-yajamānebhyo 'py adhikam anugrahaṃ karotv ity arthaḥ || tvaṣṭāram | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | tṛn | svaratisūtīty-ādinā | pā. 7-2-44 | iti vet [reading uncertain] ... agriyam | agrād ity anta-prādity-ādibhyo ghac ca | pā. 4-4-116 | ... viśvarūpam | viśvāni rūpāṇi tvaṣṭṛ-sthannena yasya | ... asmākam | ... kevalaḥ | vṛṣāder ākṛtigaṇatvād ādyudāttaḥ ||

Translation: "In the patnīsaṃyāja, this is Tvaṣṭṛ's puronuvākyā: iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam. It is laid down in the section 'śaṃ yuvākāya saṃpreṣite': 'saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā, iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam' (Āśvalāyana 1-10). I invoke here, in this rite, tvaṣṭāram — the fire named Tvaṣṭṛ. What kind? Agriyam — the foremost; viśvarūpam — endowed with forms of many kinds. May he be asmākam kevalaḥ — ours alone: that is, may he grant us more favour than to other sacrificers." Grammar noted briefly: tvaṣṭṛ from takṣū/tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe with tṛn; agriya is formed with gha (Pā. 4-4-116 [?]); viśvarūpa is a bahuvrīhi; kevala is initial-udātta as a member of the vṛṣādi class. The grammar in the Sanskrit is compressed in the scan.

original pp. 570–571

Rik 10: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अग्रियम् (agriyam) — the foremost | विश्वरूपम् (viśvarūpam) — having forms of many kinds | त्वष्टारम् (tvaṣṭāram) — the deity named Tvaṣṭṛ (a special form of Agni) | इह (iha) — in this sacrifice | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I invoke | that Tvaṣṭṛ अस्माकम् (asmākam) — to us (in our regard) | केवलः (kevalaḥ) — [being] uniquely, very attached | अस्तु (astu) — may he be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The deity named Tvaṣṭṛ is the foremost among the gods. He has many kinds of forms (shapes), and is the maker of things. I call such a deity to this sacrifice. May he be exceedingly kind to us.

॥ English Translation ॥

I invoke Twashtir, the foremost and the multi-form here. May he be solely ours.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The application of this mantra: in the homa called patnīsaṃyāja in the sacrifice, the rik iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam is used as the puronuvākyā mantra. In the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (1-10), in the section śaṃ yuvākāya saṃpreṣite, it is said that the riks saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā and iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam (Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-13-10) are to be used as yājyā and puronuvākyā mantras. Yāska's explanation:

त्वष्टा । त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः ॥ माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (नि. ८-१४) tvaṣṭā | tvaṣṭā tūrṇam aśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣer vā syād dīpti-karmaṇas tvakṣater vā syāt karoti-karmaṇaḥ || mādhyamikas tvaṣṭety āhur madhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agnir iti śākapūṇiḥ || (ni. 8-14)

That is: "Tvaṣṭā" — the etymologists say it is one who quickly pervades; or from tviṣ, a root of shining; or from tvakṣ, a root of making. Some say he is mādhyamika ("of the middle region"), i.e., one who stands between heaven and earth. Śākapūṇi says he is Agni.

Some say that Tvaṣṭṛ, like Viśvakarman, is the craftsman of the gods; for, in the rik Yāska cites as an example,

य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा । तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान्देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥ ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpair apiṃśad bhuvanāni viśvā | tam adya hotar iṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāram iha yakṣi vidvān || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-110-9 [?]; printed "१०-११०-९") ("He who with forms adorned these two, heaven and earth, the begetters, and all the worlds — that god Tvaṣṭṛ, O hotṛ, impelled today, most diligent, knowing, here sacrifice to." — my gloss, tentative.)

it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of heaven and earth, and the cause of the forms suited to the beings in all the worlds — of their beauty, wisdom and growth. Besides, the Yajurveda says: "tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāṃ rūpakṛt" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 6-1-?-? [?]) — "Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of the forms of animals in pairs"; "tvaṣṭā rūpāṇām adhipatiḥ" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 3-?-? [?]); "tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti" — these Yajurveda sentences point to Tvaṣṭṛ's skill in making things. And:

मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासो ऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुम् ॥ mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajram atakṣad āyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjann api kratum || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-48-3 [?]; printed "१०-४८-३") ("For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron thunderbolt; in me the gods have set resolve." — my gloss, tentative; this verse was also cited under Sūkta 7, Rik 3.)

Indra says that Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him with his own hands the thunderbolt-weapon. That Tvaṣṭṛ makes the sacrificial materials required by the gods, and many other things, is stated in many mantras of the Ṛgveda.

original pp. 572–575

Rik 10: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

Continuing the Special Topics, p. 572: Tvaṣṭṛ is well known as one of the twelve Ādityas; hence Yāska explains the word as "the shining one." "Agriyam" — foremost; chief; excellent. "Viśvarūpam" — viśvāni rūpāṇi tvaṣṭṛtvena yasya: "he who, as the maker, has all forms": since he is the cause (maker) of many forms, he is called viśvarūpa. "Asmākam astu kevalaḥ" — this third quarter of the rik, asmākam astu kevalaḥ, is found also in Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-7-10 [?], where it refers to Indra; the idea is "may he be our chief benefactor."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 572–575, noted briefly; the scholastic discussions on pp. 572–575 are outlined only

त्वष्टारम् (tvaṣṭāram) — root takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe; tṛn, the root being ūdit; "svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā" (Pā. 7-2-44 [?]) makes the augment iṭ optional; in the case without iṭ, tvakṣ + tṛ: "skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca" (Pā. 8-2-29 [?]) would drop the k at the end of a word or before a consonant; since here the kṣ is a conjunct at the end of a pada... the source says that for the final k dropping is inappropriate, and that "jhalo jhali" (Pā. 8-2-26 [?]) drops s in a conjunct after a jhal-letter: so k is dropped, tvaṣ + tṛ; "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41 [?]) turns t → ṭ: tvaṣṭṛ. The accusative singular am; "ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-110 [?]) guṇa; "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51 [?]); "āp tṛn tṛc…" (Pā. 6-4-11 [?]) lengthens the penultimate: tvaṣṭāram; tṛn is nit, so initial-udātta. अग्रियम् (agriyam) — "ghacchau ca" (Pā. 4-4-117 [?]) with "agrād yat" (Pā. 4-4-116 [?]) carried over: after agra in the sense "that is in it," gha and cha arise; gha → iya by "āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām" (Pā. 7-1-2 [?]); agra + iya; "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148 [?]) drops the a: agriya; the source argues at length (pp. 572–574) that the replacements iya, etc., are bahiraṅga or antaraṅga with respect to the accent rule "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. 3-1-3 [?]), concluding by the paribhāṣā "asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge" that the antaraṅga accent is considered first — so the iya replacement is made when the suffix is introduced, and then "citaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-163 [?]) gives the iya its final-udātta; the source observes that the cit-marker would be pointless otherwise (vyarthaṃ san kiṃcid artham jñāpayati) and adds Vārttika "ayanādi-ādeśeṣu śiṣyavad-vacanaṃ svara-siddhy-artham" (Pā. 7-1-2 vārttika [?]); hence agriya is final-udātta. विश्वरूपम् (viśvarūpam) — "viśvāni rūpāṇi tvaṣṭṛ-utpannatvena yasya": a bahuvrīhi; "tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāṃ rūpakṛt" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 6-1-?-? [?]) confirms the sense; viśva is formed with kvan, initial-udātta; the first member's accent would stand ("bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam," Pā. 6-2-1 [?]), overridden by "bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām" (Pā. 6-2-106 [?]), which makes viśva final-udātta when the compound is a name. अस्माकम् (asmākam) — root asu kṣepaṇe with madik, "yuṣyasibhyāṃ madik" (Uṇ. 1-142 [?]): the suffix madik after yuṣ and as gives asmad; final-udātta by the suffix; ām of the genitive plural; "yoci" (Pā. 7-2-89 [?]) replacement of the yuṣmad/asmad ending by yā is considered and the source shows that "sāma ākam" (Pā. 7-1-33 [?]) — ākam in place of sām after yuṣmad/asmad — applies even to the ākam replacement after the yā (the sāmo 'kam rule is nitya, "nityatva"); "āmi sarvanāmnaḥ suṭ" (Pā. 7-1-52 [?]) adds suṭ, which is then sām, and the source discusses why it is stated as sasuṭka in the sūtra: so that suṭ is not blocked; the point settled is "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-2-90 [?]) does not apply. केवलः (kevalaḥ) — a member of the vṛṣādi ākṛti-gaṇa, so initial-udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. 6-1-203 [?]).

॥१०॥

original p. 575

Sūkta 13, Rik 11

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अव सृजा वनस्पते देव देवेभ्यो हविः । प्र दातुरस्तु चेतनम् ॥११॥

ava sṛjā vanaspate deva devebhyo haviḥ | pra dātur astu cetanam ||11||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अव । सृज । वनस्पते । देव । देवेभ्यः । हविः ॥ प्र । दातुः । अस्तु । चेतनम् ॥११॥

ava | sṛja | vanaspate | deva | devebhyaḥ | haviḥ || pra | dātuḥ | astu | cetanam ||11||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे वनस्पते एतन्नामकाग्ने देव हविर्भुग्भ्यो देवेभ्यो ऽस्मदीयं हविरव सृज । समर्पयेत्यर्थः । प्र दातुर्यजमानस्य चेतनं परलोकविषयं विज्ञानं त्वत्प्रसादादस्तु ॥ वनस्पते । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । देव । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । षाष्ठिकमामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । हविः । इसः प्रत्ययस्वरः । दातुः । ददातेस्तृच् । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तः । जसि ऋत उत् । पा. ६-१-१११ । इत्युत्वम् । एकादेशो रपरत्वं च । राद्ध्वसस्य । पा. ८-२-२४ । इति सलोपः । एकादेशस्वरेणोकार उदात्तः । चेतनम् । चिती संज्ञाने । करणे ल्युट् । योरनादेशः । लघूपधगुणः । लिती इति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् ॥

he vanaspate etan-nāmakāgne deva havirbhugbhyo devebhyo 'smadīyaṃ havir ava sṛja | samarpayety arthaḥ | pra dātur yajamānasya cetanaṃ paraloka-viṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ tvat-prasādād astu || vanaspate | āmantrita-nighātaḥ | deva | pādāditvān na nighātaḥ | ṣāṣṭhikam āmantritādyudāttatvam | haviḥ | isaḥ pratyaya-svaraḥ | dātuḥ | dadāteṣ tṛc | cita ity antodāttaḥ | jasi ṛta ut | pā. 6-1-111 | ity utvam | ekādeśo raparatvaṃ ca | rāddhvasasya | pā. 8-2-24 | iti salopaḥ | ekādeśa-svareṇokāra udāttaḥ | cetanam | citī saṃjñāne | karaṇe lyuṭ | yor anādeśaḥ | laghūpadha-guṇaḥ | liti iti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvam ||

Translation: "O vanaspate — O Agni bearing this name — O god! Ava sṛja: release, i.e., convey, our oblation to the gods who eat oblations. May pra dātur astu cetanam — by your favour let there be, for the giver, the sacrificer, cetanam, knowledge concerning the world beyond." Grammar noted briefly: vanaspate is a vocative; deva stands at the head of the pāda and is not lowered; haviḥ with isi; dātuḥ — tṛc with the genitive ending ut by Pā. 6-1-111 [?] and loss of s by Pā. 8-2-24 [?]; cetanam — root citī saṃjñāne with lyuṭ, initial-udātta.

original pp. 576–577

Rik 11: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

देव (deva) — shining | वनस्पते (vanaspate) — O Agni, named Vanaspati | देवेभ्यः (devebhyaḥ) — to the gods | हविः (haviḥ) — the oblation that we have prepared | अव सृज (ava sṛja) — convey, offer | दातुः (dātuḥ) — to the sacrificer who gives the oblation to the gods | चेतनम् (cetanam) — excellent knowledge (concerning the other world) | अस्तु (astu) — [by your favour] may there be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, named Vanaspati! Convey the oblation we give to the gods, and, by your favour, let the sacrificer who gives the oblation have excellent knowledge.

॥ English Translation ॥

Present, divine Vanaspati, our oblation to the gods, and may true knowledge be the reward of the giver.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Vanaspate" — Yāska's explanation of the word vanaspati:

वनस्पते इत्येनमाह्वयति । एष हि वनानां पाता वा पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः ॥ (नि. ८-३) vanaspate ity enam āhvayati | eṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ || (ni. 8-3) "Vanaspate — it calls upon him; for he is the protector, or the guardian, of woods; vana is from vanoti."

कत्कोः वनस्पतिः । यूप इति काठक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (नि. ८-१८ [?]) [the print reads: "ketuḥ vanaspatiḥ …" ; best reading] … yūpa iti kāṭhakyaḥ | agnir iti śākapūṇiḥ || "Vanaspati — Kāṭhakya says it is the sacrificial post; Śākapūṇi says it is Agni."

That is, Agni is called vanaspati, because Agni is the protector or guardian of woods; though Agni is within the tree, he does not burn it, so he is called its protector. Or because the vana (wood) is useful for sacrificial materials like the dāru, he is so called. Vanaspati means "king of trees," a large tree. Kāṭhakya's idea is that vanaspati is the trunk of the tree erected to tie the animal at the sacrifice [the yūpa]; Śākapūṇi's, that it is Agni.

To support Kāṭhakya's view Yāska cites a rik:

अञ्जन्ति त्वामध्वरे देवयन्तो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन ॥ añjanti tvām adhvare devayanto vanaspate madhunā daivyena || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 3-8-1 [?]; printed "३-८-१") ("They anoint you, O Vanaspati, at the sacrifice, [those] desiring the gods, with divine honey." — my gloss, tentative.)

— that is: "O Vanaspati (yūpastambha), at the sacrifice the priests anoint you with ghee purified by mantras": addressing the sacrificial post to which the animal is tied. In the 3rd, 6th and 11th riks of the same sūkta vanaspati is likewise addressed as yūpastambha; and it is well known that the post is the deity of that sūkta. In the 11th rik of that sūkta — "vanaspate śatavalśo viroha sahasravalśā vi vayaṃ ruhema" — "O Vanaspati, grow with a hundred shoots, with a thousand shoots may we grow" — the sense is applied to the tree of which the post is made. In Ṛgveda 10-? "vanaspate raśanayā niyūya" — "O Vanaspati, bind with a rope" — confirms the sense of yūpastambha for vanaspati. So vanaspati means the sacrificial post; the sense "Agni" is indirect.

"Dātuḥ" — haviḥ-pradātuḥ yajamānasya: to the sacrificer who gives the oblation.

"Cetanam" — paraloka-viṣayaṃ vijñānam: the Bhāṣyakāra says it is knowledge about the world beyond; cetana means knowledge, discrimination. Veṅkaṭamādhava says dātur yajamānasya prajñāpanaṃ deveṣu priyā nivedita-sya: "regarding the sacrificer, you must make the gods aware [of what he has offered]."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar page 577, noted briefly

वनस्पते (vanaspate) — wholly unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19 [?]). देव (deva) — since it is not at the head of the second pāda, "apādādau" (Pā. 8-1-18 [?]) lowers it; here it stands at the head of the second pāda ("deva devebhyo haviḥ"?), so that prohibition applies; "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 6-1-198 [?]) gives it initial-udātta.

original p. 578

Rik 11 grammar closes

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

हविः (haviḥ) — root hu dānādanayoḥ, isi ("arciśucihusṛpi…," Uṇ. 2-108 [?]); guṇa; the source says this word is among the paryudāsa statements "aniseḥ," and discusses ("prasajya-pratiṣedha" versus "paryudāsa") whether the negative in "nabviṣayasyānisantasya" is a pure prohibition or an exclusion of isanta words, concluding it is an exclusion, so haviḥ, being an isanta neuter, does not get initial-udātta from that rule; the suffix accent stands: final-udātta. दातुः (dātuḥ) — root ḍudāñ dāne; tṛc ("nvul-tṛcau," Pā. 3-1-133 [?]); tṛc is cit, so final-udātta ("citaḥ," Pā. 6-1-163 [?]); genitive singular ṅas; "ṛta ut" (Pā. 6-1-111 [?]): ut in place of the ṛ's a-element [i.e., ṛ + as becomes uḥ]; dātur + s; "rātsasya" (Pā. 8-2-24 [?]) drops the s after r in a conjunct; "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-23 [?]) cannot apply alone since it would also drop other letters, so "rātsasya" is needed as a restriction (niyama), with the example ūrk (where the k after r is not dropped); the r becomes visarga: dātuḥ; the single substitute u is udātta ("ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ," Pā. 8-2-5 [?]). चेतनम् (cetanam) — root citī saṃjñāne; lyuṭ in the instrument/locus sense ("karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca," Pā. 3-3-117 [?]); "yuvor anākau" (Pā. 7-1-1 [?]) gives ana; laghūpadha-guṇa ("pugantalaghūpadhasya ca," Pā. 7-3-86 [?]); "liti" (Pā. 6-1-193 [?]): the vowel before the l-marked suffix is udātta.

॥११॥

original p. 579

Sūkta 13, Rik 12 (the last)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

स्वाहा यज्ञं कृणोतनेन्द्राय यज्वनो गृहे । तत्र देवाँ उप ह्वये ॥१२॥

svāhā yajñaṃ kṛṇotanendrāya yajvano gṛhe | tatra devām̐ upa hvaye ||12||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

स्वाहा । यज्ञम् । कृणोतन । इन्द्राय । यज्वनः । गृहे ॥ तत्र । देवान् । उप । ह्वये ॥१२॥

svāhā | yajñam | kṛṇotana | indrāya | yajvanaḥ | gṛhe || tatra | devān | upa | hvaye ||12||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

स्वाहाशब्दो हविष्प्रदानवाची सन् एतन्नामकमग्निविशेषं लक्षयति । तदग्निसंपादितं यज्ञमिन्द्रायेन्द्रप्रीतयुष्ट्यर्थं यज्वनो यजमानस्य गृहे ऋत्विजः कृणोतन । कुरुत । तत्र यज्ञे देवानुप ह्वये ॥ कृणोतन । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । इदितो नुम् । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनस्य तस्थस्थमिपामिति तादेशः । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च । पा. ७-१-४५ । इति तनबादेशः । शपि प्राप्ते धिन्विकृण्व्योरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः । तस्सन्नियोगेन वकारस्याकारः । तस्यातो लोप इति लोपः । तस्याचः परस्मिन्निति स्थानिवद्भावाद्वैकारस्य लघूपधगुणो न भवति । तनपः पित्त्वेनाजात्त्वादुकारस्य गुणः । इन्द्राय । ऋज्रेन्द्रेत्यादिना रन् । नित्त्वाद्युदात्तः । यज्वनः । यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु । सुयोजोर्ज्वनिप् । पा. ३-२-१०३ । जसि भसंज्ञायामोमल्लोपे प्राप्ते न संयोगाद्वमन्तात् । पा. ६-४-१३७ । इति निषेधः । वनिपः पित्त्वेन धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । गृहे । गृह उपादाने । गेहे कः । पा. ३-१-१४४ । इति कप्रत्ययः । ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना । पा. ६-१-१६ । संप्रसारणं पराद्रूपत्वं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । तत्र । त्रल् । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । देवाँ उपेत्यत्र संहितायां दीर्घादटीति नकारस्य रुत्वम् । आकोऽटि नित्यमित्याकारस्यानुनासिकादेशः । भोभगो इति यत्वं । तस्य लोपः शाकल्यस्येति लोपः ॥ १२ ॥

svāhā-śabdo havis-pradāna-vācī san etan-nāmakam agni-viśeṣaṃ lakṣayati | tad-agni-saṃpāditaṃ yajñam indrāyendra-prīty-artham yajvano yajamānasya gṛhe ṛtvijaḥ kṛṇotana | kuruta | tatra yajñe devān upa hvaye || kṛṇotana | kṛvi hiṃsā-karaṇayoś ca | idito num | loṇ-madhyama-bahuvacanasya tasthasthamipām iti tā-deśaḥ | taptanaptanathanāś ca | pā. 7-1-45 | iti tana-bādeśaḥ | śapi prāpte dhinvi-kṛṇvyor acceṭy u-pratyayaḥ | tat-sanniyogena vakārasyākāraḥ | tasyāto lopa iti lopaḥ | tasyācaḥ parasminn iti sthānivad-bhāvād vaikārasya laghūpadha-guṇo na bhavati | tanapaḥ pittvenājāttvād ukārasya guṇaḥ | indrāya | ṛjrendrety-ādinā ran | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | yajvanaḥ | yaja deva-pūjā-saṅgati-karaṇa-dāneṣu | suyajor ṅvanip | pā. 3-2-103 | jasi bhasaṃjñāyām om-mallope prāpte na saṃyogād vamāntāt | pā. 6-4-137 | iti pratiṣedhaḥ | vanipaḥ pittvena dhātu-svara eva śiṣyate | gṛhe | gṛha upādāne | gehe kaḥ | pā. 3-1-144 | iti ka-pratyayaḥ | grahijyety-ādinā | pā. 6-1-16 | saṃprasāraṇaṃ parādrūpatvaṃ | pratyaya-svaraḥ | tatra | tral | liti iti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvam | devām̐ upety atra saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghād aṭīti nakārasya rutvam | āko 'ṭi nityam ity ākārasyānunāsikādeśaḥ | bhobhago iti yatvaṃ | tasya lopaḥ śākalyeti lopaḥ || 12 ||

Translation: "The word svāhā, signifying the giving of an oblation, indicates a particular fire bearing this name. The sacrifice accomplished by that fire — for Indra, for Indra's satisfaction — O priests, kṛṇotana: perform, in the house of the sacrificer (yajvanaḥ, the one who sacrifices). In that sacrifice I invoke the gods." Grammar noted briefly: kṛṇotana — the imperative second plural of kṛvi with tana (Pā. 7-1-45 [?]), the u-vikaraṇa (Pā. 3-1-80 [?]) and a for v; indra with ran; yajvan with ṅvanip (Pā. 3-2-103 [?]), the case-ending of the plural...; gṛha with ka, saṃprasāraṇa; tatra with tral; and devām̐ upa with the nasalization and loss of y as before. The bhāṣya is compressed in places.

Rik 12: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

O priests! इन्द्राय (indrāya) — for Indra's satisfaction | यज्वनः (yajvanaḥ) — of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice | गृहे (gṛhe) — in the house (the sacrificial hall) | स्वाहा (svāhā) — [performed] by the utterance svāhā (or svāhā, the fire named Svāhā, accomplishing it) | यज्ञम् (yajñam) — the sacrifice | कृणोतन (kṛṇotana) — perform | तत्र (tatra) — to that sacrificial ground | देवान् (devān) — the gods | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I invoke.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O priests, the adhvaryu and the others! In the sacrificer's house, perform the sacrifice for Indra's satisfaction with the cry svāhā; or perform it, offering the oblations belonging to the fire named Svāhā. For that I call the gods there.

॥ English Translation ॥

Perform the sacrifice to Indra conveyed through swaha in the house of the sacrificer. I invoke the gods thither.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Svāhā" — Yāska's explanation:

स्वाहाकृतयः । स्वाहाकृतयः स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति वा । स्व वाग्गाहेति वा । स्वं प्राहेति वा । स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा ॥ (नि. ८-२१) svāhākṛtayaḥ | svāhākṛtayaḥ svāhety etat su āheti vā | sva vāg āheti vā | svaṃ prāheti vā | svāhutaṃ havir juhotīti vā || (ni. 8-21) "Svāhākṛtayaḥ — svāhā is [explained as] su āha, 'he speaks well'; or sva vāg āha, 'his own speech says'; or svaṃ prāha, 'he says his own'; or svāhutaṃ havir juhoti, 'he offers the oblation well offered.'"

Four different etymological senses of the word svāhā are thus given: (1) su āha — su = well; āha = says: because the word is uttered clearly, or distinctly, it is called svāhā. (2) sva vāg āha — sva = one's own; vāk = word: "his own word": the Brāhmaṇa states, "taṃ sva vāg abhyavadad yajñeti; hence the origin of the svāhākāra": when making the homa, the one who makes it himself adds at the end of the Vedic mantra, a rik, the word svāhā. (3) svaṃ prāha — svam = his own oblation; āha — "he says": "he says he offers his own oblation." (4) svāhutaṃ havir juhoti — "the oblation he himself offered, he offers by uttering the word svāhā": that is, because he gives the oblation into Agni, it is svāhā. To exemplify the sense of svāhākāra, Yāska cites this rik [the source's text breaks off at the page foot and continues on p. 581; see below]. Continuing Yāska on svāhā, the rik cited as example [p. 581]:

original pp. 581–583

Rik 12: Special Topics (continued) and grammar; close of Sūkta 13

सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः । अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यृतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदन्तु देवाः ॥ sadyo jāto vy amimīta yajñam agnir devānām abhavat purogāḥ | asya hotuḥ pradiśy ṛtasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ havir adantu devāḥ || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-110-11 [?]; printed "१०-११०-११") ("Born at once, Agni measured out the sacrifice; he became the leader of the gods. At the word of this hotṛ, in the direction of order, let the gods eat the oblation made with svāhā." — my gloss, tentative.)

The chief sense of it: Agni, who has just been born (that is, who has now been established in the sacrifice), sits before the gods and carries out the duty of the hotṛ — the work of calling the gods — and so brings the sacrifice to completion. Such a hotṛ, being in the eastern quarter, is offered oblations with the word svāhā, so that the gods may eat them. Hence svāhā means the word uttered at the end of a mantra when, for the gods' delight, the oblation is poured into the fire established for the sacrifice in the prescribed manner.

In some Āpri-sūktas the plural svāhākṛtayaḥ is used: since the eleven prayāja mantras used when offering to the eleven deities of this sūkta all include the svāhākāra, the plural svāhākṛtayaḥ is used. In the Purāṇas and other works the word svāhā is used in another sense: in the Mahābhārata it is said that the sage Aṅgiras gave his son Bṛhaspati's daughters the name Svāhā; in the Purāṇas Svāhādevī is called the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati and the wife of Agni.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 581–583, noted briefly

कृणोतन (kṛṇotana) — root kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, idit, so num ("idito num dhātoḥ," Pā. 7-1-58 [?]): kṛnv; loṭ second plural thas... "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. 3-4-85 [?]) makes it behave as laṅ, so "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-101 [?]) gives ta for tha; "taptanaptanathanāś ca" (Pā. 7-1-45 [?]): ta may be replaced by tap, tanap, tana, thana, giving tana; śap would arise but "dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca" (Pā. 3-1-80 [?]) gives u with a for the final v; so kṛn + u + tana; "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-48 [?]) drops the a; the guṇa of the ṛ is blocked by sthānivadbhāva ("acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau," Pā. 1-1-57 [?]); since tanap is pit (tanap), the apit rule ("sārvadhātukam apit," Pā. 1-2-4 [?]) does not apply, so "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5 [?]) does not block guṇa; "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84 [?]) gives guṇa to the u — o: kṛṇotana; n → ṇ ("yuvarṇānnasya ṇatvaṃ vaktavyam," vārttika [?]); unaccented ("tiṅ atiṅaḥ," Pā. 8-1-28 [?]). इन्द्राय (indrāya) — root idi paramaiśvarye with ran ("ṛjrendrāgra…," Uṇ. 2-28 [?]), initial-udātta. यज्वनः (yajvanaḥ) — root yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; "suyajor ṅvanip" (Pā. 3-2-103 [?]): ṅvanip after yaj and su (ṣuñ abhiṣave) in the Veda; the ṅvanip is not kept as ṅit for the purposes of guṇa; yajvan + as (genitive singular ṅas); the stem has bha status ("yaci bham," Pā. 1-4-18 [?]); "allopo 'naḥ" (Pā. 6-4-134 [?]) would drop the a of an, but "na saṃyogād vamāntāt" (Pā. 6-4-137 [?]) blocks the loss after a conjunct ending in v or m ("jv" here); so yajvanaḥ; since vanip is pit, the root accent stands. गृहे (gṛhe) — "gehe kaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-144 [?]): ka after grah meaning house; "grahijyāvayi…" (Pā. 6-1-16 [?]) gives saṃprasāraṇa of r → ṛ: gṛha (saṃprasāraṇa is the name for the replacement of y, v, r, l by i, u, ṛ, ḷ — "igyaṇaḥ saṃprasāraṇam," Pā. 1-1-45 [?]); "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108 [?]) gives pūrvarūpa; ka is the suffix accent; locative singular gṛhe. तत्र (tatra) — "saptamyās tral" (Pā. 5-3-10 [?]): tral after tad in the locative sense; tral is a taddhita, so the word is a prātipadika ("kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca," Pā. 1-2-46 [?]); the ending is dropped ("supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ," Pā. 2-4-71 [?]); "prāg diśo vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 5-3-1 [?]) gives tral the vibhakti name; hence, since the next word follows, "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. 7-2-102 [?]) turns the d of tad into a, "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97 [?]) pararūpa: tatra; "liti" (Pā. 6-1-193 [?]): the syllable before tral is udātta. देवाँ उप (devām̐ upa) — deva from divu with ac ("pacādibhyo 'c," Pā. 3-1-134 [?]) with laghūpadha-guṇa; the accusative plural śas: "prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-102 [?]) and "tasmāc chaso naḥ puṃsi" (Pā. 6-1-103 [?]): s of śas → n after pūrvasavarṇadīrgha in the masculine; devān; in the Saṃhitā "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. 8-3-9 [?]) turns the n into ru before the following aṭ-letter in the same pāda; "āto 'ṭi nityam" (Pā. 8-3-3 [?]) nasalizes the ā; "bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. 8-3-17 [?]) gives y; "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19 [?]) drops it: devām̐ upa; "ād guṇaḥ" would give o but, since the loss of y is "unseen" (pūrvatrāsiddham, Pā. 8-2-1 [?]), the y still stands for the earlier rule, and no guṇa arises.

॥१२॥

॥ ಹದಿನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 14 — "aibhir agne duvo giraḥ" ("The Fourteenth Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 583, lower half)

ऐभिरग्न इत्यादिकस्य द्वादशर्चस्य तृतीयसूक्तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । तच्च सूक्तं बहुदेवताकम् । अत एवानुक्रम्यते । ऐभिर्वैश्वदेवमिति । विनियोगस्तु । व्यूढद्वादशाहस्य प्रथमे च्छन्दोमे तृतीयसवने वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे ऐभिरग्ने दुवो गिर इति सूक्तम् ॥ तथा च सूत्रितम् । अथ च्छन्दोमाः समुद्रादूर्मिरित्युपक्रम्यैभिरग्ने दुवो गिर इति वैश्वदेवम् । आ. ८-[?] । इति ॥

aibhir agna ity-ādikasya dvādaśarcasya tṛtīya-sūktasya ṛṣi-chandasī pūrvavat | tac ca sūktaṃ bahu-devatākam | ata evānukramyate | aibhir vaiśvadevam iti | viniyogas tu | vyūḍha-dvādaśāhasya prathame cchandome tṛtīya-savane vaiśvadeva-śastre aibhir agne duvo gira iti sūktam || tathā ca sūtritam | atha cchandomāḥ samudrād ūrmir ity upakramyaibhir agne duvo gira iti vaiśvadevam | ā. 8-[?] | iti ||

Translation: "The twelve-rik sūkta beginning aibhir agne is the third sūkta [of this anuvāka]; its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. This sūkta has many deities; that is why the Anukramaṇikā says only aibhir vaiśvadevam ['aibhir…: to the Viśvedevas']. Its application (viniyoga): in the first chandoma day of the vyūḍha-dvādaśāha, at the third pressing, in the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the sūkta aibhir agne duvo giraḥ is recited. And so it is laid down in the Sūtra: 'Now the Chandomas: beginning with samudrād ūrmiḥ … and aibhir agne duvo giraḥ is the Vaiśvadeva [recitation].' (Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra 8-[?] — the Sanskrit shows a two-part numeral whose second part I cannot read; the Kannada rendering gives it as 9-[?].)" The ornament and the sūkta heading precede this note on p. 583; the first few lines of the page are the close of Sūkta 13, Rik 12, already covered.

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The twelve-rik sūkta that begins aibhir agne is the third sūkta of the fourth anuvāka. Its ṛṣi and meter are the same as the preceding sūkta. Because it has many deities, it is a bahu-devatāka sūkta; therefore the Anukramaṇikā calls it a sūkta to the Viśvedevas. Application: when the vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited at the third pressing of the first chandoma day of the vyūḍha-dvādaśāha sacrifice, this sūkta aibhir agne duvo giraḥ is to be recited. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra says: "Now the Chandomas: beginning with samudrād ūrmiḥ … aibhir agne duvo giraḥ is the Vaiśvadeva"; that is, the mantras from samudrād ūrmiḥ onwards up to aibhir agne duvo giraḥ are called chandomā mantras. (Āś. Sū. 9-[?])

original p. 584

aibhir agne duvo giro viśvebhiḥ somapītaye | devebhir yāhi yakṣi ca ||1||

हे अग्ने एभिरस्मिन्यज्ञे संभावितैर्विश्वेभिर्देवेभिः सर्वैर्देवैः सह सोमपीतये सोमपानोपपेतयागार्थं दुवोऽस्मदीयां परिचर्यां गिरोऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतीश्च प्रत्या(?) याहि । आगच्छ । यक्षि च । आगत्य यज च ॥

he agne ebhir asmin yajñe saṃbhāvitair viśvebhir devebhiḥ sarvair devaiḥ saha somapītaye somapānopapeta-yāgārthaṃ duvo 'smadīyāṃ paricaryāṃ giro 'smadīyāḥ stutīś ca praty-ā(?) yāhi | āgaccha | yakṣi ca | āgatya yaja ca ||

Translation: "O Agni! Together with these — all the gods, those honoured (saṃbhāvita) at this sacrifice — come, for the drinking of soma and for the sacrifice that goes with the soma-drinking, to our service (duvaḥ) and to our words of praise (giraḥ). Yāhi: come. Yakṣi ca: and, having come, sacrifice." The first words of the second line of the print are partly unclear; "praty-ā(?)" stands for what appears to be pratyā ["towards; for each"] — it is given with a query.

Then the grammar of the bhāṣya follows (pp. 585–587): Grammar passage: given as legible in part; "…" marks stretches that could not be read at 150 dpi. Sūtras 2-4-32, 7-1-11 and 7-3-103 agree with the standard Pāṇinian numbering of idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudātta…, nedamadasor akoḥ and bahuvacane jhaly et; "bahulaṃ chandasi" is cited without number.

एभिः । पूर्वनिर्दिष्टानां देवानामिदमा परामर्शादिदमोऽन्वादेशे ऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ । पा. २-४-३२ । इत्येशनुदात्तः । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः । नेदमदसोरकोः । पा. ७-१-११ । इति भिस ऐशादेशाभावः । विभक्तिरनुदात्तैव … दुवः । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । विश्वेभिः । विश्वशब्दो विशेः क्वनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐस् न भवति । बहुवचने झल्येत् । पा. ७-३-१०३ । इत्येत्वम् । सोमपीतये । सोमशब्दो … मनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सोमस्य पीतिर्यस्मिन्यागे स सोमपीतिः । तस्मै । तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी । देवेभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसादेशाभावः । बहुवचने झल्येदित्येत्वम् । यक्षि । यजेर्लोटः सिप् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । व्रश्चादिना षत्वम् । षढोः कः सि [?] … सिपः पित्त्वेनानुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वर एव ॥

ebhiḥ | pūrva-nirdiṣṭānāṃ devānām idam ā parāmarśād idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau | pā. 2-4-32 | ity eśanudāttaḥ | śittvāt sarvādeśaḥ | nedam-adasor akoḥ | pā. 7-1-11 | iti bhisa aiśādeśābhāvaḥ | vibhaktir anudāttaiva … duvaḥ | nab-viṣayasyāniṣantasyety ādy-udāttatvam | viśvebhiḥ | viśva-śabdo viśeḥ kvananto nittvād ādy-udāttaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa ais na bhavati | bahuvacane jhaly et | pā. 7-3-103 | ity etvam | soma-pītaye | soma-śabdo … manan-to nittvād ādy-udāttaḥ | somasya pītir yasmin yāge sa soma-pītiḥ | tasmai | tādarthye caturthī | devebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisādeśābhāvaḥ | bahuvacane jhaly ety etvam | yakṣi | yajer loṭaḥ sip | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | vraścādinā ṣatvam | ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si [?] … sipaḥ pittvenānudāttatvād dhātu-svara eva ||

Translation of the grammar, in outline: ebhiḥ — the pronoun idam refers back to the gods just mentioned, so it is in the anvādeśa ("re-mention") condition; therefore by P. 2-4-32 it receives the substitute aś [ena], which is unaccented; being marked with ś the substitute replaces the whole word; by P. 7-1-11 (nedamadasor akoḥ) the bhis ending is not given the ais substitute; the case-ending is unaccented. duvaḥ — first-syllable accent by the rule on words ending in -is/related forms [citation partly unclear]. viśvebhiḥ — viśva is from viś + kvan, so with an indicatory n it has the first-syllable accent; by "variously in the Veda" bhis does not become ais; by P. 7-3-103 the a becomes e before a jhal-initial plural ending. somapītaye — soma is formed with man, first-syllable accent; "he in whose sacrifice there is the drinking (pīti) of soma" is somapīti; "for him" — fourth case in the sense of purpose. devebhiḥ — as for viśvebhiḥ. yakṣi — yaj, imperative, sip; the śap is dropped by "variously in the Veda"; the ṣ is substituted by the vraśca rule; the k; since sip has an indicatory p it is unaccented, so the verb-root accent alone remains. Grammar pages, pp. 586–587, noted briefly; the gloss in this paragraph is outline only.

original pp. 586–588

Rik 1: Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar), noted briefly

Grammar pages (the Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā on pp. 586–587), noted briefly. The Kannada treats ebhiḥ (the idam → aś [ena] substitution under P. 2-4-32 idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudātta…, the blocking of ais under P. 7-1-11 nedamadasor akoḥ, P. 7-1-9 āto bhisa ais and 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi, the e of P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhaly et, and the accentual rules 6-1-158 anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam / 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau [numbers read from small print, pointers only]), duvaḥ, viśvebhiḥ (from viś + kvan, Uṇādi [?]), somapītaye (soma from su with man, Uṇādi 1-[?]; the fourth case under P. 2-1-36 caturthī tadarthārtha-balihita-sukha-rakṣitaiḥ with the Vārttika on tādarthya; the ṣyañ of P. 5-1-124 guṇavacana-brāhmaṇādibhyaḥ karmaṇi ca discussed on pp. 587, with the examples yūpāya dāru ("wood for a sacrificial post") and kuṇḍalāya hiraṇyam ("gold for an earring"), which the bhāṣya gives for the sense of purpose), devebhiḥ (bhis → ais blocked by bahulaṃ chandasi), and yakṣi (yaj + lot + sip, śap dropped by P. 2-4-73, ṣatva by 8-2-36 vraśca-bhrasja…, ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si P. 8-2-41, hi for si by 3-4-87 serhy apicca — all pointers only, numerals uncertain).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ Kannada

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | एभिः (ebhiḥ) — these [gods], honoured at this our sacrifice (Kannada saṃbhāvitarāda) | विश्वेभिः (viśvebhiḥ) — all | देवेभिः (devebhiḥ) — with the gods | दुवः (duvaḥ) — the service (śuśrūṣā) that we render | गिरः (giraḥ) — words in the form of hymns of praise | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for the drinking of soma | प्रति आ याहि (prati ā yāhi) — come so as to receive | यक्षि च (yakṣi ca) — and bring the sacrifice to completion.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, come with all the gods, to receive the service we render in this our sacrifice and the hymns of praise, and to drink the soma. After you have come, bring this sacrificial act to completion in all its parts.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source The print shows a bare numeral "74" after the English, at the foot of p. 585, outside the text; It is left unexplained [?].

Come, Agni with all those gods to receive our adoration and praises and for drinking soma; and also perform the sacrifice.

original pp. 588–592

Sūkta 14, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ त्वा कण्वा अहूषत गृणन्ति विप्र ते धियः । देवेभिरग्न आ गहि ॥२॥

ā tvā kaṇvā ahūṣata gṛṇanti vipra te dhiyaḥ | devebhir agna ā gahi ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks are printed in the source; not reproduced.

आ । त्वा । कण्वाः । अहूषत । गृणन्ति । विप्र । ते । धियः ॥ देवेभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥२॥

ā | tvā | kaṇvāḥ | ahūṣata | gṛṇanti | vipra | te | dhiyaḥ || devebhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे विप्र मेधाविन्नग्ने कण्वा मेधाविन ऋत्विजस्त्वा यज्ञनिष्पादकं त्वामाहूषत आह्वयन्ति । तथा ते धियस्त्वदीयानि कर्माणि गृणन्ति कथयन्ति । ततो हे अग्ने देवेभिर्देवैः सहा गहि । आगच्छ । विप्र इत्यादिषु चतुर्विंशतिसंख्याकेषु मेधाविनामसु कण्व ऋभुरिति [?] पठितम् ॥

he vipra medhāvinn agne kaṇvā medhāvina ṛtvijas tvā yajña-niṣpādakaṃ tvām āhūṣata āhvayanti | tathā te dhiyas tvadīyāni karmāṇi gṛṇanti kathayanti | tato he agne devebhir devaiḥ sahā gahi | āgaccha | vipra ity-ādiṣu caturviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu medhāvi-nāmasu kaṇva ṛbhur iti [?] paṭhitam ||

Translation: "O wise (vipra) Agni! The kaṇvas — the wise priests (ṛtvij) — have invoked (āhūṣata) you, the one who accomplishes the sacrifice; and they recite (gṛṇanti) your dhiyaḥ — your deeds. Therefore, O Agni, come together with the gods. [The word kaṇva is] read among the twenty-four names for 'wise man' beginning with vipra." In the print, the last clause names the item read after "kaṇva" with a letter-group read as ṛbhur; It is given with [?], and the Kannada Special Topics (below) confirms only that kaṇva itself is in the list.

Then, as in Rik 1, the grammar follows (p. 588, lower half, and pp. 589–592). Grammar pages, noted briefly: the bhāṣya and the Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treat — ā (a nipāta, first-syllable accent, Phiṭ 4-[?] nipātā ādyudāttāḥ); tvā (P. 8-1-23 tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ — the substitute tvā for tvām, wholly unaccented; the number agrees with the standard numbering); kaṇvāḥ (root kaṇ "to sound", the Uṇādi sūtra on the kvan suffix aśūpruṣiliṭikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan, Uṇ. 1-[?]; first-syllable accent because of the indicatory n); ahūṣata (hve "to compete, to call", luṅ in the present sense by P. 3-4-6 chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭaḥ — the number agrees with the standard; then cli, sic [P. 3-1-43, 3-1-44 — read from the Kannada print, they agree with the standard numbering of cli luṅi and cleḥ sic], the ātmanepada by P. 1-3-72, the sampra-sāraṇa of hve, and the lengthening and ṣatva — a long run of 'pointer' sūtras whose numerals I leave unchecked); gṛṇanti (gṝ "to sound", laṭ by P. 3-2-123 vartamāne laṭ, śnā by P. 3-1-81 kryādibhyaḥ śnā, hrasva by P. 6-4-113 [?]); vipra (vocative: accent by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca [?]); te (P. 8-1-18 anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau and 8-1-22 te mayāv ekavacanasya, the substitute te for tava); devebhiḥ (ais blocked by bahulaṃ chandasi); gahi (root gam/gamḷ with lot, sip, hi for si by P. 3-4-87 serhy apicca, śap dropped by P. 2-4-73, the dropping of m by anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanotyādīnām… P. 6-4-37, the asiddhavat rule 6-4-22). Crowded; reproduced in outline only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) विप्र ((he) vipra) — O wise [i.e. learned] Agni | कण्वाः (kaṇvāḥ) — the wise priests (descendants of the ṛṣi Kaṇva) | त्वा (tvā) — you | आ अहूषत (ā ahūṣata) — invoke (pray to) | in the same way ते (te) — your | धियः (dhiyaḥ) — works | गृणन्ति (gṛṇanti) — praise | therefore अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | देवेभिः (devebhiḥ) — with the gods | आ गहि (ā gahi) — be pleased to come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O wise Agni, in order to praise your qualities, the wise priests (or the descendants of the ṛṣi Kaṇva) pray to you and call you to the sacrifice; and they praise your excellent deeds. Therefore, come to our sacrifice along with all the gods.

॥ English Translation ॥ The print ends the line with a comma.

The Kanwas invoke you, wise Agni, and extrol [sic] your deeds; come Agni with the gods,

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

कण्वाः (kaṇvāḥ) — Among the twenty-four names for the medhāvī (wise), beginning with vipra, the word kaṇva is read (Nirukta/Nighaṇṭu 3-[?] — the printed reference reads "ni. 3-19" in small print, which I cannot confirm; in the standard Nighaṇṭu the medhāvi list is 3.15), so kaṇva here can mean "wise, intelligent". Although the commentator takes the word in this general sense, since the ṛṣi of this rik is himself of the lineage of Kaṇva, it seems more natural to take kaṇvāḥ here as "the sacrificer-priests and others born in the Kaṇva lineage."

धियः (dhiyaḥ) — Among the twenty-six names for karma (action) beginning with apaḥ, dhīḥ is read (Ni. 2-[?], the print's numerals are unclear), so dhiyaḥ means "actions, works".

original pp. 592–593

Sūkta 14, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रवायू बृहस्पतिं मित्राग्निं पूषणं भगम् । आदित्यान्मारुतं गणम् ॥३॥

indravāyū bṛhaspatiṃ mitrāgniṃ pūṣaṇaṃ bhagam | ādityān mārutaṃ gaṇam ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रवायू इति । बृहस्पतिम् । मित्रा । अग्निम् । पूषणम् । भगम् ॥ आदित्यान् । मारुतम् । गणम् ॥३॥

indravāyū iti | bṛhaspatim | mitrā | agnim | pūṣaṇam | bhagam || ādityān | mārutam | gaṇam ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ compressed; the reading is given as printed, with [?] where uncertain

इन्द्रादिदेवान्मारुतं मरुतां वायूनां सम्बन्धिनं गणं च हे अग्ने यक्षीति पदद्वयमनुवर्तते ॥ इन्द्रश्च वायुश्चेन्द्रवायू । देवताद्वन्द्वे च । पा. ६-३-२६ । इति प्राप्तस्यानङ उभयत्र वायोः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः । पा. ६-३-२६ वा. । इति प्रतिषेधः । देवताद्वन्द्वे च । पा. ६-२-१४१ । इति प्राप्तस्योभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरस्य नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादौ । पा. ६-२-१४३ [?] । इति निषेधः । समासान्तोदात्तत्वमेव । बृहस्पतिम् । तस्करबृहतोः करपत्योश्चोरदेवतयोरभिधेययोः सुट् तलोपश्च वक्तव्यः । मै. [?] इति तलोपः सुडागमश्च । बृहच्छब्दमाद्युदात्तं केचिद्वर्णयन्तीति नामनः [?] । पा रक्षणे । पातीति पतिः । पातेर्डतिः । उ. ४-[?] । प्रत्ययस्वरेणाद्युदात्तः । समास उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपत् । पा. ६-२-१४० । इत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । मित्रा । द्वितीयायाः सुसां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराजादेशः । आदित्यान् । अदितेरपत्यमादित्यः । दित्यदित्यादित्यपत्युत्तरपदाण्ण्यः । पा. ४-१-८५ । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मारुतम् । मरुतां विकारः । अनुदात्तादेश्च । पा. ४-३-१४० । इत्यञ् । ञित्त्वात्पादाद्युदात्तः ॥

indrādi-devān mārutaṃ marutāṃ vāyūnāṃ sambandhinaṃ gaṇaṃ ca he agne yakṣīti pada-dvayam anuvartate || indraś ca vāyuś cendravāyū | devatādvandve ca | pā. 6-3-26 | iti prāptasyānaṅa ubhayatra vāyoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ | pā. 6-3-26 vā. | iti pratiṣedhaḥ | devatādvandve ca | pā. 6-2-141 | iti prāptasyobhaya-pada-prakṛti-svarasya nottarapade 'nudāttādau | pā. 6-2-143 [?] | iti niṣedhaḥ | samāsāntodāttatvam eva | bṛhaspatim | taskara-bṛhatoḥ kara-patyoś cora-devatayor abhidheyayoḥ suṭ talopaś ca vaktavyaḥ | mai. [?] iti talopaḥ suḍāgamaś ca | bṛhac-chabdam ādyudāttaṃ kecid varṇayantīti nāmanaḥ [?] | pā rakṣaṇe | pātīti patiḥ | pāter ḍatiḥ | u. 4-[?] | pratyaya-svareṇādyudāttaḥ | samāsa ubhe vanaspaty-ādiṣu yugapat | pā. 6-2-140 | ity ubhaya-pada-prakṛti-svaratvam | mitrā | dvitīyāyāḥ su-sāṃ su-lug ity-ādinā vibhaktar ā-jādeśaḥ | ādityān | aditer apatyam ādityaḥ | dityadity-ādityapaty-uttarapadāṇ ṇyaḥ | pā. 4-1-85 | pratyaya-svaraḥ | mārutam | marutāṃ vikāraḥ | anudāttādeś ca | pā. 4-3-140 | ity añ | ñittvāt pādādy-udāttaḥ ||

Translation: "[The two words of Rik 1] he agne yakṣi ('O Agni, sacrifice') continue to be understood: [sacrifice] to Indra and the other gods, and to the mārutam gaṇam — the host belonging to the Maruts, the winds. Indravāyū — Indra and Vāyu, a dvandva of deities [the rest of this passage is grammar on why the ānaṅ substitution and the compound-accent rules do not apply — the compound keeps the accent of the end of the compound]. Bṛhaspatim — [the grammar here concerns the Vārttika that suṭ is added and t is dropped in bṛhaspati and taskara — the readings are marked as uncertain above]; pā means 'to protect'; 'he protects' is pati; first-syllable accent by the suffix-accent; both parts keep their own accent, as in vanaspati. Mitrā — the case-ending replaced by ā by the rule 'su-, sām, … luk' [with the second case sense, singular — see Special Topics]. Ādityān — the child (apatya) of Aditi is Āditya (P. 4-1-85, the suffix accent). Mārutam — what belongs to or is a product of the Maruts, with añ by P. 4-3-[?]; since añ has an indicatory ñ, the first syllable of the word is accented." Grammar noted briefly; "[?]" marks stretches where the print is compressed or the sūtra numeral is unclear. The numbers 6-3-26, 6-2-141 and 4-1-85 agree with the standard numbering.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे अग्ने) ((he agne)) — O Agni | इन्द्रवायू (indravāyū) — Indra and Vāyu | बृहस्पतिम् (bṛhaspatim) — Bṛhaspati | मित्रा (mitrā) — Mitra | अग्निम् (agnim) — Agni | पूषणम् (pūṣaṇam) — Pūṣan | भगम् (bhagam) — Bhaga | आदित्यान् (ādityān) — the Ādityas | मारुतं गणम् (mārutaṃ gaṇam) — the hosts of the Maruts | all these — having in view [or: for them] — (यक्षि) ((yakṣi)) — sacrifice.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, perform the sacrifice with these in view: Indra, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Mitra, Agni, Pūṣan, Bhaga, the Ādityas (or: the deities), and the hosts of the Maruts.

॥ English Translation ॥ A bare numeral "75" stands after the English at the foot of p. 593; as with "74" on p. 585 it is outside the text — apparently a running number of the English renderings; It is taken so, but flagged [?].

Sacrifice to Indra, Vayu, Bribaspati [sic], Mitra, Agni, Pushan, Bhaga, the Adityas. and [sic] the hosts of Maruts.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अग्ने यक्षि (agne yakṣi) — Because this rik has no verb, the commentator says the two words agne yakṣi ("O Agni, sacrifice") must be supplied (adhyāhāra). But Agni is himself one of the group named in this rik, so it seems unfitting to say "O Agni, sacrifice to Agni". For this reason the author of the Vedārthayatna supplies the two words ahaṃ hvaye — "I invoke" — to mean: "I invoke the deities beginning with Indra and Vāyu."

इन्द्रवायू (indravāyū) — indraś ca vāyuś ca indravāyū; the compound of two deities (devatā-dvandva): the two deities Indra and Vāyu are named by a single word in the dual.

मित्रा (mitrā) — here the second-case ending must be taken in the singular sense [= mitram].

आदित्यान् (ādityān) — aditer apatyāni ādityāḥ: the children of Aditi, the mother of the gods, are called Ādityas; the meaning is "the deities", or the twelve Ādityas.

मारुतम् (mārutam) — the final letter of the genitive plural mārutām has been shortened for the sake of the metre.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics), Rik 3 — continuation (p. 594) ॥

मारुतं गणम् (mārutaṃ gaṇam) — The host (samūha) of the Marut deities. The Purāṇas and similar works say that there are seven Maruts (the sapta-marut-gaṇas); in the Ṛgveda too the word marut is ordinarily used in the plural. Mārutaṃ gaṇam therefore means "the company, the group, of the Marut deities." Rik 3 grammar, pp. 594–596 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, grammar pages, noted briefly: the Kannada treats indravāyū (P. 6-3-26 devatādvandve ca with the Vārttika that ānaṅ is barred for vāyu; P. 6-2-141 devatādvandve ca and the bar in P. 6-2-142 [?]), bṛhaspatim (the Vārttika on tasya… bṛhatoḥ karapatyoś coradevatayoḥ suṭ talopaś ca; Pā. 6-1-157 [?] for the kukkuṭādīnām… discussion; P. 1-1-41 ādyantau ṭakitau; the Uṇādi ḍati from pā "to protect", Uṇ. 4-[?]; the accent rule P. 6-2-140 [?]), mitrā (P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…; ekādeśa under P. 8-2-5), ādityān (P. 4-1-85 dityadity-ādityapatyuttarapadāṇ ṇyaḥ, with the ṇya accent; 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; 7-2-117 taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ; 6-1-103 and 8-4-6 [?] for the accusative plural ān), and mārutam (Uṇ. 1-94 [?] mṛgror utiḥ, mṛj "to cleanse"; P. 4-3-[?] anudāttādeś ca with añ, P. 6-1-197 [?] ñnityādir nityam, the first-syllable accent). Sūtra numbers read from small print are pointers only.
