Sūkta 14, Rik 10

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वेभिः सोम्यं मध्वग्न इन्द्रेण वायुना । पिबा मित्रस्य धामभिः ॥१०॥

viśvebhiḥ somyaṃ madhv agna indreṇa vāyunā | pibā mitrasya dhāmabhiḥ ||10||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened pibā, the Pada the short piba.

विश्वेभिः । सोम्यम् । मधु । अग्ने । इन्द्रेण । वायुना ॥ पिब । मित्रस्य । धामऽभिः ॥१०॥

viśvebhiḥ | somyam | madhu | agne | indreṇa | vāyunā || piba | mitrasya | dhāma-bhiḥ ||10||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने त्वं विश्वेभिः सर्वैः पूषभगादिभिर्देवैरिन्द्रेण वायुना मित्रस्य सम्बन्धिभिर्धामभिस्तेजोभिर्मूर्तिविशेषरूपैश्च सह सोम्यं सोमसम्बन्धि मधु मधुरं भागं पिब । विश्वेभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसादेशाभावः । सोम्यं । सोममर्हति यः । इत्यनुवृत्तौ मये च । पा. ४-४-१३८ । इति यप्रत्ययः सोमस्य विकार इत्यर्थे । यस्येति चेत्यकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । फलिपाटिनमिमनीत्यादिना । उ. १-[?] । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्णित्त्वाद्याद्युदात्तः [?] । वायुना । कृवापाजीत्यादिना उण् । आतो युक् चिण्कृतोः । पा. ७-३-३३ । इति युक् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । पिब । पा पाने । लोटः सेर्हिरादेशः । शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना पिबादेशः । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । कपः पित्त्वादधातुस्वरः । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङः इति संहितायां दीर्घः । धामभिः । धाञ् । आतो मनिन्निति मनिन् । नित्स्वरः ॥१०॥

he agne tvaṃ viśvebhiḥ sarvaiḥ pūṣa-bhagādibhir devair indreṇa vāyunā mitrasya sambandhibhir dhāmabhis tejobhir mūrti-viśeṣa-rūpaiś ca saha somyaṃ soma-sambandhi madhu madhuraṃ bhāgaṃ piba | viśvebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisādeśābhāvaḥ | somyaṃ | somam arhati yaḥ | ity anuvṛttau maye ca | pā. 4-4-138 | iti ya-pratyayaḥ somasya vikāra ity arthe | yasyeti cety akāra-lopaḥ | pratyaya-svaraḥ | phali-pāṭi-nami-manīty-ādinā | u. 1-[?] | u-pratyayaḥ | nid ity anuvṛtter ṇittvād ādyudāttaḥ [?] | vāyunā | kṛvā-pāji-ty-ādinā uṇ | āto yuk ciṇ-kṛtoḥ | pā. 7-3-33 | iti yuk | pratyaya-svaraḥ | piba | pā pāne | loṭaḥ ser hir ādeśaḥ | śapi pā-ghrety-ādinā pibādeśaḥ | ato heḥ iti her luk | kapaḥ pittvād adhātu-svaraḥ | pādāditvān na nighātaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | dhāmabhiḥ | dhāñ | āto maninn iti manin | nit-svaraḥ ||10||

Translation: "O Agni! Together with all the gods — Pūṣan, Bhaga and the rest — with Indra, with Vāyu, and with Mitra's dhāmas (his radiances and special forms), drink the somya — belonging to the soma — madhu, the sweet portion. Viśvebhiḥ — bhis does not become ais [by 'variously in the Veda']. Somyam — the suffix ya by P. 4-4-138 in the sense 'the product of soma' [the standard rule]. Vāyunā — from vā, the suffix uṇ; yuk augment by P. 7-3-33 [the standard numbering]. Piba — from pā "to drink", loṭ, hi in place of si, piba by P. 7-3-78 pāghrādhmā… [read from the print as pāghrā…], the luk of hi by ato heḥ; unaccented... lengthened in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ [as printed]. Dhāmabhiḥ — from dhā, manin by āto maniṇ…." Grammar, noted briefly.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | विश्वेभिः (viśvebhiḥ) — with all the gods, Pūṣan, Bhaga and the rest | इन्द्रेण (indreṇa) — with Indra | वायुना (vāyunā) — with Vāyu | मित्रस्य धामभिः (mitrasya dhāmabhiḥ) — with the special forms (mūrti-viśeṣa-rūpa) and radiances of Mitra | सह (saha) — together | सोम्यं मधु (somyaṃ madhu) — the sweet soma-juice | पिब (piba) — drink.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, drink the sweet soma-juice together with Indra, with Vāyu, with the other gods such as Pūṣan and Bhaga, and with the special forms of Mitra, that are in the nature of radiance.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, drink this sweet soma juice with the Visve devas, Indra, Vayu, and the various forms of Mitra.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This rik is used in the Agniṣṭoma [?] sacrifice as the yājyā mantra in the recitation of the praüga-śastra. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning stotram agre śastrāt [as read], directs that the rik viśvebhiḥ somyaṃ madhu be used as the yājyā mantra (Āś. 5-[?]; the print gives "(ಆ. ೫-೧೮)", which I read as 5-18 [?]).

पिब (piba) — in the Saṃhitā text the final syllable is lengthened, to suit the metre.

मित्रस्य धामभिः (mitrasya dhāmabhiḥ) — mitrasya sambandhibhir dhāmabhis tejo-mūrti-viśeṣa-rūpaiś ca: "with the various forms of Mitra" (the print gives this English gloss in Latin letters: "with various forms of Mitra"). Dhāmabhiḥ: "with radiances, or with forms of light" — "Rays" [the print's English word]. Which the forms of Mitra are, the Kannada says, is not clear.

Grammar pages (pp. 618–620), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā takes up viśvebhiḥ (P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi; the blocking of ais under P. 7-1-9), somyam (P. 4-4-137 somaṃ arhati yaḥ and 4-4-138 mayaḍ ca; the ya suffix in the sense of "product of soma", taddhita, sup luk, loss of a by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca), madhu (the Uṇādi u suffix, Uṇ. 1-[?] phalipāṭinamijanimanīti; nit, first-syllable accent), vāyunā (the Uṇādi uṇ in kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhya uṇ, Uṇ. 1-1; the yuk augment of P. 7-3-33 āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ). The page runs on to p. 620 in the same vein; Only the words treated and the sūtras that could be read are given.

original pp. 619–622

Sūkta 14, Rik 11

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

त्वं होता मनुर्हितो ऽग्ने यज्ञेषु सीदसि । सेमं नो अध्वरं यज ॥११॥

tvaṃ hotā manurhito 'gne yajñeṣu sīdasi | semaṃ no adhvaraṃ yaja ||11||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

त्वम् । होता । मनुःऽहितः । अग्ने । यज्ञेषु । सीदसि ॥ सः । इमम् । नः । अध्वरम् । यज ॥११॥

tvam | hotā | manuḥ-hitaḥ | agne | yajñeṣu | sīdasi || saḥ | imam | naḥ | adhvaram | yaja ||11||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने मनुर्हितो मनुषा होत्रादिरूपेण मनुष्येण हितः संपादितो होमनिष्पादको यस्त्वं यज्ञेषु सीदसि तिष्ठसि स त्वं नोऽस्मदीयमिममध्वरं यज्ञं यज निष्पादय ॥ मनुर्हितः । मन्यते इति मनुः । निदित्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलमन्यत्रापि । उ. [?] । उस् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । हितः । धाञो धातोर्निष्ठायां क्तप्रत्ययः । दधातेर्हिः । पा. ७-४-४२ । इति हिरादेशः । मनुषा हितो मनुर्हितः । कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलम् । पा. २-१-३२ । इति समासः । … पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सीदसि । षद्ऌ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । लटः सिप् । शपि पाघ्रादिना सीदादेशः । निघातः । सेममित्यत्र संहितायां सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणम् । पा. ६-१-१३४ । इति सोर्लोपे गुणः । अध्वरम् । न विद्यते ध्वरो हिंसा यस्मिन्नाध्वरः । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । नो ऽध्वरमित्यत्र संहितायां [सस]जुषो रुः …

he agne manurhito manuṣā hotrādi-rūpeṇa manuṣyeṇa hitaḥ saṃpādito homa-niṣpādako yas tvaṃ yajñeṣu sīdasi tiṣṭhasi sa tvaṃ no 'smadīyam imam adhvaraṃ yajñaṃ yaja niṣpādaya || manurhitaḥ | manyate iti manuḥ | nid ity anuvṛttau bahulam anyatrāpi | u. [?] | us | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | hitaḥ | dhāño dhātor niṣṭhāyāṃ kta-pratyayaḥ | dadhāter hiḥ | pā. 7-4-42 | iti hirādeśaḥ | manuṣā hito manurhitaḥ | kartṛ-karaṇe kṛtā bahulam | pā. 2-1-32 | iti samāsaḥ | … pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | sīdasi | ṣadḷ viśaraṇa-gaty-avasādaneṣu | laṭaḥ sip | śapi pā-ghrādinā sīdādeśaḥ | nighātaḥ | semam ity atra saṃhitāyāṃ so 'ci lope cet pāda-pūraṇam | pā. 6-1-134 | iti sor lope guṇaḥ | adhvaram | na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasminn ādhvaraḥ | nañ-subhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvam | no 'dhvaram ity atra saṃhitāyāṃ [sa-sa]juṣo ruḥ …

Translation: "O Agni! You, manurhitaḥ — appointed by man (by the human sacrificer, in the role of hotṛ and so on), made the accomplisher of the homa — you sit (sīdasi) at the sacrifices. Such as you are, yaja — perform, bring to completion — this sacrifice of ours (adhvaram)." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: manurhitaḥ (manu from man "to know", the Uṇādi us; hita from dhā with kta, hi for dhā by P. 7-4-42; compound by P. 2-1-32 kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam; accent of the first member by P. 6-2-48 [?]); sīdasi (sad with sīda-substitute by pāghrādhmā…); the sandhi semam from sa imam by P. 6-1-134 so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam; adhvaram ("that in which there is no dhvara, violence") with the accent of P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām. Sūtra numbers 7-4-42, 2-1-32 and 6-1-134 agree with the standard numbering; the others are as read.

Grammar pages (pp. 621–622), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā goes through manurhitaḥ (man of the fourth class "to know"; Uṇ. 1-[?] with bahulam anyatrāpi, nit; the compound-accent conflict resolved in favour of the first member by P. 6-2-48 tṛtīyā karmaṇi over 6-1-223, 6-2-2, 6-2-139 and 6-1-186 [pointers only]; the Vedabhāṣya's view that the Phiṭ-rule on dhā-compounds is set aside here); sīdasi (ṣad, with laṭ, sip, the sīda substitute by P. 7-3-78 and the nighāta); semam — saḥ + imam: if the s were kept (sa imam) the pāda would have nine syllables instead of eight; by P. 6-1-134 the s of saḥ is lost before a vowel when the pāda is thereby completed, and the guṇa follows [the Kannada works through the pūrvatrāsiddham P. 8-2-1 argument that the guṇa of a + i does or does not apply, and concludes that semam has eight syllables to the pāda, so the pāda is complete]; adhvaram (na vidyate dhvaraḥ hiṃsā yasmin — first-member accent overridden by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām; naḥ + adhvaram: s → ru by P. 8-2-66 sasajuṣo ruḥ, ru → u by P. 6-1-113 ato ror aplutād aplute, then guṇa by P. 6-1-87, with the eṅaḥ padāntād ati P. 6-1-109 pūrvarūpa barred by P. 6-1-115 prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare, so the text stands no 'dhvaram). Crowded; outline only; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni [you] | त्वम् (tvam) — you | मनुर्हितः (manurhitaḥ) — appointed by man in the function of hotṛ and the rest | होता (hotā) — accomplisher of the homa | यज्ञेषु (yajñeṣu) — at our sacrifices | सीदसि (sīdasi) — sit (with us) | सः (saḥ) — such as you are | नः (naḥ) — our | इमम् अध्वरम् (imam adhvaram) — this sacrifice | यज (yaja) — perform.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni! You bring the gods to the sacrifice, and you sit with us at the sacrificial times of us human beings who perform it. Such as you are, bring this sacrifice of ours to completion.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, appointed by man as the invoker of the gods you are present at the sacrifice. Therefore perform this our sacrifice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

मनुर्हितः (manurhitaḥ) — manyate iti manuḥ; manuṣā hotrādi-rūpeṇa manuṣyeṇa hitaḥ saṃpāditaḥ: appointed by man in the function of hotṛ and so on. The human sacrificer appoints him to take his share in the sacrificial work, or, because he carries the principal vessel in the sacrifice, he is the one who has been placed in the fire-pit.

original pp. 622–626

Sūkta 14, Rik 12 (last rik of the sūkta)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युक्ष्वा ह्यरुषी रथे हरितो देव रोहितः । ताभिर्देवाँ इहा वह ॥१२॥

yukṣvā hy aruṣī rathe harito deva rohitaḥ | tābhir devām̐ ihā vaha ||12||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. Saṃhitā has the lengthened yukṣvā, ihā, the Pada the short yukṣva, iha.

युक्ष्व । हि । अरुषीः । रथे । हरितः । देव । रोहितः ॥ ताभिः । देवान् । इह । आ । वह ॥१२॥

yukṣva | hi | aruṣīḥ | rathe | haritaḥ | deva | rohitaḥ || tābhiḥ | devān | iha | ā | vaha ||12||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे देवाग्ने रोहितो रोहिच्छब्दाभिधेयास्त्वदीया वडवा रथे युक्ष्व । योजय । हिशब्दः पादपूरणार्थः । कीदृशीः । अरुषीर्गतिमतीर्हरितो हर्तुं रथारूढान्पुरुषानेतुं समर्थाः । ताभिर्वडवाभिरिहास्मिन्कर्मणि देवानावह । युक्ष्व । युजिर् योगे । लोट् । स्वरितेत्त्वादात्मनेपदम् । थासः से । सवाभ्यां वामौ । रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् । तस्य बाहुलकाल्लुक् । कुत्वषत्वे । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । संहितायां द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङः इति दीर्घः । अरुषीः । ऋ गतौ । ऋन्ति गच्छन्तीत्यरुष्यो वडवाः । ऋहनिभ्यां [?] षन् । उ. [?] । धातोर्गुणो रपरत्वम् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तस्मात् स्त्रियां छान्दसो ङीप् । शसि प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः । पा. ६-१-१०२ । इति दीर्घः । रथे । रमेरोणादिकः क्थन् [?] … नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । हरितः । हृस्वरुहियुषिभ्य इतिः । उ. १-[?] … रोहितः । रुहेरसि तेनैव सूत्रेणेतिः … ताभिः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेः प्राप्तमुदात्तत्वं सावनर्णेति निषिध्यते । देवानित्यत्र पूर्ववदुत्वानुनासिकौ ॥१२॥

he devāgne rohito rohic-chabdābhidheyās tvadīyā vaḍavā rathe yukṣva | yojaya | hi-śabdaḥ pāda-pūraṇārthaḥ | kīdṛśīḥ | aruṣīr gatimatīr harito hartuṃ rathārūḍhān puruṣān etuṃ samarthāḥ | tābhir vaḍavābhir ihāsmin karmaṇi devān āvaha | yukṣva | yujir yoge | loṭ | svaritettvād ātmanepadam | thāsaḥ se | savābhyāṃ vāmau | rudhādibhyaḥ śnam | tasya bāhulakāl luk | kutva-ṣatve | pratyaya-svareṇāntodāttaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ iti dīrghaḥ | aruṣīḥ | ṛ gatau | ṛnti gacchantīty aruṣyo vaḍavāḥ | ṛhanibhyām [?] ṣan | u. [?] | dhātor guṇo raparatvam | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | tasmāt striyāṃ chāndaso ṅīp | śasi prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ | pā. 6-1-102 | iti dīrghaḥ | rathe | rameroṇādikaḥ kthan [?] … nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | haritaḥ | hṛ-sva-ruhi-yuṣibhya itiḥ | u. 1-[?] … rohitaḥ | ruher asi tenaiva sūtreṇetiḥ … tābhiḥ | sāv ekāca iti vibhakteḥ prāptam udāttatvaṃ sāvanarṇeti niṣidhyate | devān ity atra pūrvavad utvānunāsikau ||12||

Translation: "O radiant Agni! Yoke to your chariot your mares (vaḍavāḥ) known by the name Rohit. Hi is a mere filler for the metre. Of what sort? Aruṣīḥ — those that go, that move swiftly; haritaḥ — able to carry those who sit in the chariot. With those mares, here, in this rite, bring the gods." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: yukṣva (yuj, loṭ, ātmanepada, thās → se, śnam, with the śnam dropped by "variously in the Veda"; kutva and ṣatva); aruṣīḥ (ṛ "to go", the Uṇādi uṣan; first-syllable accent; the feminine ṅīp; the acc. plural by P. 6-1-102 prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ); rathe (ram "to play", the Uṇādi kthan, [?]); haritaḥ (Uṇ. 1-[?] hṛsvaruhiyuṣibhya itiḥ); rohitaḥ (ruh with the same iti suffix); tābhiḥ (the accent of the ending barred by sāvanarṇa…); devān + iha (the u and anunāsika as before). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 6-1-102 as read agrees with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 624–626, upper part), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats yukṣva (yuj with loṭ; the ātmanepada of a svarit-marked root, P. 1-3-72; thās → se P. 3-4-80; sa-vābhyāṃ vāmau P. 3-4-91; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam P. 3-1-78; bahulaṃ chandasi P. 2-4-73; coḥ kuḥ P. 8-2-30; khari ca P. 8-4-55; ādeśapratyayayoḥ P. 8-3-59; the verb unaccented by P. 8-1-28, but the accent of the ending remains because the pāda does not begin with it; dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ P. 6-3-135 for the lengthened yukṣvā), aruṣīḥ (ṛ "to go" with laṭ jhi → anti, śap, the juhotyādi class and ślu, doubling and the ṛ→ar ur at P. 7-4-66, ārtiprapiparty etc. — the Kannada works through two derivations from the two roots ṛ, with the Uṇādi uṣan (Uṇ. 4-[?] ṛhanibhyām ūṣan, an alternative reading with a long ū); yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148; jīp, prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ P. 6-1-102), rathe (ramu krīḍāyām, "that in which they play", janikaṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan, Uṇ. 2-[?]; P. 7-2-10 ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt blocks iṭ; anudāttopadeśa… P. 6-4-37 drops m), haritaḥ (hṛ "to take", sṛ, ruh, yuṣ: iti suffix, Uṇ. 1-[?]; guṇa, rapara), rohitaḥ (ruh + iti; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca P. 7-3-86), tābhiḥ (tad + bhis, tyadādīnām aḥ P. 7-2-102, ato guṇe P. 6-1-97 pararūpa, ājādyatas ṭāp P. 4-1-4, the accent of the instrumental ending sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ P. 6-1-168 blocked by na gośvannsāvavarṇarāḍaṅkvyādibhyaḥ P. 6-1-182 [?]; the ending unaccented by P. 3-1-4), and devān + iha (P. 8-3-1 and 8-3-5 ātoṭi nityam, anunāsika; bho-bhago-agho-apūrvasya yo 'śi P. 8-3-17 ru→y; lopaḥ śākalyasya P. 8-3-19; pūrvatrāsiddham P. 8-2-1 explains why the guṇa of P. 6-1-87 does not apply).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

देव (deva) — O radiant Agni | अरुषीः (aruṣīḥ) — swift-running | हरितः (haritaḥ) — able [to carry] easily | रोहितः (rohitaḥ) — named Rohit [your mares] | रथे (rathe) — to the chariot | युक्ष्व (yukṣva) — yoke | ताभिः (tābhiḥ) — with those mares | इह (iha) — for this ritual action of ours | देवान् (devān) — the gods | आ वह (ā vaha) — bring.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, you are radiant. Your mares called Rohit are powerful, swift in running, and able to carry those who sit [in the chariot] without effort. Yoke them to your chariot, and with their help bring the gods to this ritual action of ours.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, harness your twany [sic] red mares to your chariot and by means of them bring the gods hither.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

युक्ष्व (yukṣva) — the final syllable is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text to suit the metre.

अरुषीः (aruṣīḥ) — ṛ gatau; ṛnti gacchantīty aruṣyo vaḍavāḥ: the root ṛ has the sense "to go"; because horses are speedy they are called aruṣyaḥ; aruṣīḥ is the accusative plural.

Rik 12, grammar tail (p. 626, upper part), noted briefly. The close of the grammar for devān + iha: the ā-final takes the anunāsika; ru → y by P. 8-3-17 bho-bhago…; lopaḥ śākalyasya P. 8-3-19 drops the y; by pūrvatrāsiddham this dropped y is treated as not having happened, so the guṇa of P. 6-1-87 ād guṇaḥ does not apply; the form is devām̐ ihā as in the Saṃhitā. ॥12॥

Close of Sūkta 14. The print has no large colophon of the "illige … sūktavu samāptavu … vargavu mugidudu" kind after Rik 12 on p. 626; the sūkta simply ends with the ornament and the heading of the fifteenth. So the varga-numerals "26, 27 [?]" on the Sūkta 14 heading remain the only evidence for the varga count, and are unreliable.

॥ ಹದಿನೈದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 15 — "indra somaṃ piba" ("The Fifteenth Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 626, lower half)

इन्द्र सोममित्यादिकस्य द्वादशर्चस्य चतुर्थस्य सूक्तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । यद्यप्येतत्सूक्तं कृत्स्नमृतुदेवताकं तथापि प्रत्यृचमिन्द्रादिदेवतान्तराणि मिलितानि । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । इन्द्र सोममृत[?] तत्रैन्द्री मारुती त्वाष्ट्र्यग्नेय्यैन्द्री मैत्रावरुणी चतस्रो द्रविणोदस आश्विनाग्नेय्य ऋतुदेवताः सर्वत्रेति ॥ विनियोगस्तु स्मार्तो द्रष्टव्यः ॥

indra somam ity-ādikasya dvādaśarcasya caturthasya sūktasya ṛṣi-chandasī pūrvavat | yady apy etat sūktaṃ kṛtsnam ṛtu-devatākaṃ tathāpi pratyṛcam indrādi-devatāntarāṇi militāni | tathā cānukramyate | indra somam ṛta[?] tatraindrī mārutī tvāṣṭryāgneyyaindrī maitrāvaruṇī catasro draviṇodasa āśvināgneyya ṛtu-devatāḥ sarvatreti || viniyogas tu smārto draṣṭavyaḥ ||

Translation: "The twelve-rik sūkta beginning indra somam is the fourth sūkta [of this anuvāka]; its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. Although this whole sūkta has the Ṛtus (Seasons) for its deity, in each rik other deities, Indra and the rest, are joined with them. So the Anukramaṇikā says: 'indra somam …: there [the deities are] aindrī (Indra), mārutī (the Maruts), tvāṣṭrī (Tvaṣṭṛ), āgneyī (Agni), aindrī (Indra), maitrāvaruṇī (Mitra and Varuṇa), the four to the Draviṇodases, āśvinī (the Aśvins), āgneyī (Agni): the Ṛtus are the deities throughout.' Its application (viniyoga) is to be seen from the smārta usage." The Anukramaṇikā quotation begins with a word or two after "indra somam" that is read as ṛta… [?] and cannot be completed; the rest is as read.

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The twelve-rik sūkta indra somaṃ piba, the fourth sūkta of the fourth anuvāka. Its ṛṣi and meter are as in the preceding sūkta. Although all the riks of this sūkta have the Ṛtus as deities, in each rik the deities Indra and others are joined with the Ṛtu. In the Anukramaṇikā: "indra somam … aindrī, mārutī, tvāṣṭrī, āgneyī, aindrī, maitrāvaruṇī, four [riks] to the draviṇodas, āśvinī, āgneyī; the Ṛtus are the deities in all" — that is, the whole sūkta is in praise of the Ṛtu-deities. With that Ṛtu, the deities Indra, the Maruts, Tvaṣṭṛ, Agni, Indra, Mitrāvaruṇau [belong] one to each rik; the next four riks have the deity Draviṇodāḥ, and of the remaining two riks the deities are in order the Aśvinau and Agni. The application is to be understood from the smārta usage.

original p. 627

Sūkta 15, Rik 1

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 15 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 4 ॥ Sūkta — 15 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 28, 29 [?] ॥ small-print Kannada digits; the glyph for 2 and 3 is hard to tell apart in this print, so the first digit could also be 3 — a "38, 39" reading is possible; The figures that continue the run of Sūkta 14 are given and marked unreliable ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–12 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ ॥ Devatā — Ṛtavaḥ (the Seasons): 1 — Indra; 2 — the Maruts; 3 — Tvaṣṭṛ; 4 — Agni; 5 — Indra; 6 — Mitra-Varuṇau; 7–10 — Draviṇodāḥ; 11 — the Aśvins; 12 — Agni ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्र सोमं पिब ऋतुना त्वा विशन्त्विन्दवः । मत्सरासस्तदोकसः ॥१॥

indra somaṃ piba ṛtunā tvā viśantv indavaḥ | matsarāsas tadokasaḥ ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks are printed in the source; not reproduced.

इन्द्र । सोमम् । पिब । ऋतुना । आ । त्वा । विशन्तु । इन्दवः ॥ मत्सरासः । तत्ऽओकसः ॥१॥

indra | somam | piba | ṛtunā | ā | tvā | viśantu | indavaḥ || matsarāsaḥ | tat-okasaḥ ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ compressed; [?] marks doubtful readings

हे इन्द्र ऋतुना सह सोमं पिब । इन्दवः पीयमानाः सोमास्त्वा त्वामा विशन्तु । कीदृशाः । मत्सरासस्तृप्तिकराः तदोकसस्तन्निवासाः । सर्वदा त्वदुदरस्थायिन इत्यर्थः ॥ इन्द्र । षाष्ठिकमामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । सोमम् । आर्तिस्तुसुहुसृघृक्षिप्क्षुभायावापदियक्षिनीभ्यो मन् … नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पिब । पिबा मित्रस्य । ऋ. सं. १-१४-१० । इत्यत्रोक्तम् । … अस्य त्वा विशन्त्वित्युत्तरवाक्यगताख्यातार्थेन सह समुच्चेयार्थश्च शब्दो लुप्तः … चादिलोपे विभाषा [पा. ८-१-६३] … संहितायामोमाङोश्च … इन्दवः । प्र वो भ्रियन्त इन्दव इत्यत्रोक्तम् । मत्सरासः । … आज्जसेरसुक् । तदोकसः । तदेवौकः स्थानं येषां ते तदोकसः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥१॥

he indra ṛtunā saha somaṃ piba | indavaḥ pīyamānāḥ somās tvā tvām ā viśantu | kīdṛśāḥ | matsarāsas tṛptikarāḥ tadokasas tan-nivāsāḥ | sarvadā tvad-udara-sthāyina ity arthaḥ || indra | ṣāṣṭhikam āmantrītādyudāttatvam | somam | ārti-stu-su-hu-sṛ-ghṛ-kṣip-kṣubhā-yā-vā-pā-di-yakṣi-nībhyo man … nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | piba | pibā mitrasya | ṛ. saṃ. 1-14-10 | ity uktam | … asya tvā viśantv ity uttara-vākya-gatākhyātārthena saha samuccayārtha-ś ca śabdo luptaḥ … cādilope vibhāṣā [pā. 8-1-63] … saṃhitāyām omāṅoś ca … indavaḥ | pra vo bhriyanta indava ity atroktam | matsarāsaḥ | … āj jaser asuk | tadokasaḥ | tad eva okaḥ sthānaṃ yeṣāṃ te tadokasaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||1||

Translation: "O Indra! Drink the soma together with the Ṛtu. May the soma-juices (indavaḥ), as they are drunk, enter you. Of what kind? Matsarāsaḥ — causing satisfaction; tadokasaḥ — having that [i.e. you] for their abode: the sense is that they always remain in your belly." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: indra (accent of the vocative); somam (the Uṇādi man suffix, first-syllable accent); piba — the lengthened pibā was explained at Rik 14.10 (cited as "Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-14-10", which is Rik 10 of the previous sūkta); the ca ("and") connecting piba with the verb of the next clause has been dropped, and by P. 8-1-63 cādilope vibhāṣā the first verb is not made unaccented; indavaḥ — explained at pra vo bhriyanta indavaḥ (Rik 14.4); matsarāsaḥ — the plural asuk by P. 7-1-50 āj jaser asuk; tadokasaḥ — "those whose okas ('home') is that"; a bahuvrīhi, with the first-member accent. Grammar pages, noted briefly; P. 8-1-63 and P. 7-1-50 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 628–629), noted briefly. The Kannada treats indra (the vocative: first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca), somam (Uṇ. 1-[?] ārti-stu-su… — the man suffix, with the n indicatory), piba (the lengthening of the final a discussed at 1.14.10; the dropped ca — by P. 8-1-63 cādilope vibhāṣā, with the list ca, vā, hā, aha, eva, the rule being that a ca-less pair of verbs with one subject drops ca, while with different subjects aha is dropped; the guṇa of pibā ṛtunā barred by the shortening rule P. 6-1-127 ṛty akaḥ [as read, 6-1-128], which allows the prakṛtibhāva), indavaḥ (explained at 1.14.4; āj jaser asuk, P. 7-1-50), and tadokasaḥ (tat + okas, a bahuvrīhi, P. 6-2-1). Numerals as read; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | ऋतुना सह (ṛtunā saha) — together with the Ṛtu-deity | सोमम् (somam) — the soma-juice | पिब (piba) — drink | मत्सरासः (matsarāsaḥ) — giving satisfaction | इन्दवः (indavaḥ) — the soma-juices | तदोकसः (tadokasaḥ) — whose abode is your udara ("belly"), as a place of residence | त्वाम् (tvām) — you (your belly) | आ विशन्तु (ā viśantu) — let them enter.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Drink the soma-juice together with the Ṛtu-deity. It gives you satisfaction; and may the soma-juices, whose abiding home is your belly, enter your belly and remain there.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Indra, drink with the Ritu (season) the Soma juice; let the satisfying drops enter your stomach and stay there (as if that were their home).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

तदोकसः (tadokasaḥ) — tan-nivāsāḥ; sarvadā tvad-udara-sthāyina ity arthaḥ: "those who always dwell in your belly". Tad eva okaḥ sthānaṃ yeṣāṃ te tadokasaḥ: those for whom that very place is the home. Your belly is always the abode of the soma-juice; "may soma-juice always be in your belly" — that is, may you be always drinking soma.

original pp. 629–634

Sūkta 15, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

मरुतः पिबत ऋतुना पोत्राद्यज्ञं पुनीतन । यूयं हि ष्ठा सुदानवः ॥२॥

marutaḥ pibata ṛtunā potrād yajñaṃ punītana | yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhā sudānavaḥ ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened ṣṭhā, the Pada the short stha.

मरुतः । पिबत । ऋतुना । पोत्रात् । यज्ञम् । पुनीतन ॥ यूयम् । हि । स्थ । सुऽदानवः ॥२॥

marutaḥ | pibata | ṛtunā | potrāt | yajñam | punītana || yūyam | hi | stha | su-dānavaḥ ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे मरुतः ऋतुना सह पोत्रात्पोतृनामकस्य ऋत्विजः पात्रात्सोममिमं पिबत । ततोऽस्मदीयं यज्ञं पुनीतन शोधयत । हे सुदानवः शोभनदातारो मरुतः । यस्माद्यूयं स्थ युष्माकं हि शोधयितृत्वं प्रसिद्धम् । तस्माच्छोधयेत्यर्थः ॥

he marutaḥ ṛtunā saha potrāt potṛ-nāmakasya ṛtvijaḥ pātrāt somam imaṃ pibata | tato 'smadīyaṃ yajñaṃ punītana śodhayata | he sudānavaḥ śobhana-dātāro marutaḥ | yasmād yūyaṃ stha yuṣmākaṃ hi śodhayitṛtvaṃ prasiddham | tasmāc chodhayety arthaḥ ||

Translation: "O Maruts! Together with the Ṛtu, drink this soma from the vessel (potra) of the priest called Potṛ. Then purify our sacrifice (punītana). O Sudānavaḥ — good givers — Maruts! Since you are [such] — your power to purify is well known — therefore purify; that is the sense." The Sanskrit reading of "potṛ-nāmakasya" is from small print and fairly clear; the closing clause is compressed.

Then follows the grammar of the bhāṣya, pp. 630–631 upper part: This grammar run is compressed and crowded; the lines are given in part, with "…" where they could not be read or condensed. It explains: why the verb pibata is not unaccented, since marutaḥ before it is a vocative treated as if absent; that potra is "belonging to the Potṛ" with aṇ, whose vṛddhi is optional in the Veda; that punītana is the imperative of pū with the substitute tana for ta and the shortening of the stem vowel; the forms of yūyam (P. 7-2-93 yūyavayau jasi); and sudānavaḥ as a prādi-compound with the Uṇādi nu. The last clause says that by the particle hi the Maruts' power to purify is stated as the reason.

पिबत । अत्र तिङोऽदुपदेशात् … [क्रमः?] । … मरुत इत्यामन्त्रितत्वादामन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् [पा. ८-१-७२] … पोत्रात् । पोतुः सम्बन्धि पात्रं पोत्रम् । तस्येदमित्यण् । तद्धितेष्वचामादेः । पा. ७-२-११७ । इति प्राप्ता वृद्धिः सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति न भवति । … पुनीतन । पूञ् पवने । लोट् । लोटो लङ्वत् । पा. ३-४-८५ । तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तन्तामः । पा. ३-४-१०१ । इति तादेशः । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च । पा. ७-१-४५ । इति तनादेशः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः । पा. ७-३-८० । … यूयम् । युष्मदः … जसः । जसि प्रथमयोरम् … यूयवयौ जसि । पा. ७-२-९३ । … सुदानवः । दाभाभ्यां नुः । उ. ३-३२ [?] । सोः प्रादिसमासः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । … यूयं स्थेति युष्मच्छब्देन प्रतिनिर्दिश्य पुनीतनेति प्रार्थने पवने केषां हेतुत्वं हिशब्देनोच्यते ॥

pibata | atra tiṅo 'dupadeśāt … | … maruta ity āmantritatvād āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat [pā. 8-1-72] … potrāt | potuḥ sambandhi pātraṃ potram | tasyedam ity aṇ | taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ | pā. 7-2-117 | iti prāptā vṛddhiḥ sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyanta iti na bhavati | … punītana | pūñ pavane | loṭ | loṭo laṅvat | pā. 3-4-85 | tasthasthamipāṃ tāntantāmaḥ | pā. 3-4-101 | iti tādeśaḥ | taptanaptanathanāś ca | pā. 7-1-45 | iti tanādeśaḥ | pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ | pā. 7-3-80 | … yūyam | yuṣmadaḥ … jasaḥ | jasi prathamayor am … yūyavayau jasi | pā. 7-2-93 | … sudānavaḥ | dā-bhābhyāṃ nuḥ | u. 3-32 [?] | soḥ prādi-samāsaḥ | āmantrita-nighātaḥ | … yūyaṃ stheti yuṣmac-chabdena pratinirdiśya punītaneti prārthane pavane keṣāṃ hetutvaṃ hi-śabdenocyate ||

Grammar pages (pp. 632–634), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats: pibata (pā "to drink", loṭ, thā → ata [as read]; loṭo laṅvat P. 3-4-85 so that laṅ's rules apply to loṭ; tasthasthamipāṃ tāntantāmaḥ P. 3-4-101; pāghrādhmā… P. 7-3-78 for piba; śap with its pit-ness making it unaccented, accent staying on the root tāsyanudāttenn… P. 6-1-186 [?]; the vocative marutaḥ before it is treated as absent by P. 8-1-72, so pibata is at the start of a pāda and so remains unaccented, as P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ indicates [?]); potrāt (potuḥ idam — tasyedam P. 4-3-120 with aṇ; the technical name prātipadika by P. 1-2-46; the luk of sup P. 2-4-71; the vṛddhi of taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ P. 7-2-117 not applied, because all rules are optional in the Veda — with a long discussion of whether the vṛddhi might fall on the final ṛ or on the penultimate vowel (P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti, 7-2-116 [?] ata upadhāyāḥ), the viprati-ṣedha and antya-vṛddhi/upadhā-vṛddhi/ādi-vṛddhi conflict, with examples sauśrutaḥ, tvāṣṭra, pauṣkarasāda, jagat+ā, with the Kaumudī's statement that the ādi-vṛddhi wins over the other two); punītana (pū of the kryādi class, with śnā P. 3-1-81 and the lengthening of the vowel of śnā by P. 6-4-113 īhalyaghoḥ, ī also for the stem vowel, the shortening of pū by P. 7-3-80, the unaccentedness of śnā and tana as sārvadhātukas, the barring of the guṇa by P. 1-1-5 kṅiti ca); yūyam (yuṣmad from the root yuṣ "to be [separate]", the Uṇādi suffix madik, Uṇ. 1-[?]; accent; the substitution yūya for yuṣmad + jas by P. 7-2-93 yūyavayau jasi, with the ām of P. 7-1-28 jasi prathamayor am [?], and the discussion of whether yūya is replaced first or the śeṣe lopaḥ P. 7-2-90 applies, with the paribhāṣā "asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge" and the accent ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ P. 8-2-5). A crowded run of three pages; outline only, numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

मरुतः (marutaḥ) — O Maruts | ऋतुना (ṛtunā) — together with the Ṛtu-deity | पोत्रात् (potrāt) — from the vessel of the priest called Potṛ | पिबत (pibata) — drink (the soma-juice), (afterwards) | यज्ञम् (yajñam) — our sacrifice | पुनीतन (punītana) — make pure | सुदानवः (sudānavaḥ) — O Maruts, who give desired things well | यूयम् (yūyam) — you | हि स्थ (hi stha) — are you not renowned, in the mantras, as being of this kind?

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Maruts! First, together with the Ṛtu-deity, drink the soma-juice of our sacrifice from the vessel of the priest called Potṛ; and afterwards make our sacrifice pure. O Maruts, who grant what is wished, are you not those who are renowned in the mantras as having such power?

॥ English Translation ॥

O Maruts, drink with Ritu from the Potri's sacrificial cup; consecrate the sacrifice, for you are great givers.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

पोत्रात् (potrāt) — Among the sixteen priests who take a share in the sacrifice, one is called Potṛ. He ordinarily works along with the priest called Neṣṭṛ. Here, for potrāt pibata, the commentator explains: potuḥ sambandhi-pātrāt somaṃ pibata — "drink the soma that is in the vessel belonging to the Potṛ."

सुदानवः (sudānavaḥ) — śobhana-dātāraḥ, or su-pra-dātāraḥ: those who give good things, or give well (abundantly).

Rik 2, grammar tail (p. 635), noted briefly. The grammar of yūyam closes with the optional dropping of the final d of yuṣmad [P. 7-2-90 śeṣe lopaḥ], the pūrvarūpa of P. 6-1-102 [read as printed 6-1-107?] making yūyam with the accent of the single substituted ā; with P. 8-2-5 ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ. Stha — as "to be", laṭ, middle-person plural tha; the śap dropped by ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (P. 2-4-72); the a of as dropped by P. 6-4-111 śnasor allopaḥ; the s becomes ṣ by vyatyaya and ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ (P. 8-4-41) the th becomes ṭh, giving ṣṭha; the particle hi does not make the verb unaccented hi ca (P. 8-1-34), but here the verb is not unaccented because of tiṅ atiṅaḥ (P. 8-1-28) [as the Kannada has it]; in the Saṃhitā the lengthening of ṣṭhā is of the type āṅyeṣām api dṛśyate. Sudānavaḥ — the Uṇādi nu suffix after dā ("to give", ḍudāñ dāne) and bhā "to shine"; su + dānu by P. 2-2-18 kugatiprādayaḥ; as a vocative plural, unaccented, and given the first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-198. The Kannada adds a long note: sudānavaḥ here is not part of the predicate of yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhā, since if it were it would not be a vocative and could not take the vocative accent; so it must be taken as a separate vocative — "O (well-known) givers!" — and yūyam then points to the Maruts, whose power is known from the Mārutasūktas, with hi giving the reason for punītana ("purify"), as in the Bhāvārtha above. ॥2॥

original pp. 635–641

Sūkta 15, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अभि यज्ञं गृणीहि नो ग्नावो नेष्टः पिब ऋतुना । त्वं हि रत्नधा असि ॥३॥

abhi yajñaṃ gṛṇīhi no gnāvo neṣṭaḥ piba ṛtunā | tvaṃ hi ratnadhā asi ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Pada text has neṣṭar iti, the quoted form of the word.

अभि । यज्ञम् । गृणीहि । नः । ग्नावः । नेष्टः॒रिति । पिब । ऋतुना ॥ त्वम् । हि । रत्नऽधाः । असि ॥३॥

abhi | yajñam | gṛṇīhi | naḥ | gnāvaḥ | neṣṭar iti | piba | ṛtunā || tvam | hi | ratna-dhāḥ | asi ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ग्नाशब्दः स्त्रीवाची । तथा च यास्क आह । मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणां … । नि. [३-२१ ?] । ग्ना अस्य सन्तीति ग्नावान् । नेष्टृशब्दोऽत्र त्वष्टारं देवमाह । कस्मिंश्चिद्देवसत्रे नेष्टृत्वेन त्वष्टुर्वृत्तेस्तस्य । हे ग्नावः पत्नीयुक्त नेष्टः त्वष्टः नोऽस्मदीयं यज्ञमभि गृणीहि । अभितो देवानां समीपे स्तुहि । ऋतुना सह त्वं सोमं पिब । हि यस्मात्त्वं रत्नधा असि रत्नानां दाताऽसि दाता भवति तस्मात्सोमं पातुमर्हसीत्यर्थः ॥ अभि । उपसर्गाश्चाभिवर्जम् । फि. [?] । इति पर्युदासादेरन्तोदात्तत्वम् । गृणीहि । गृ शब्दे । लोटि सिपो हिः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । हेर्जित्त्वादीर्हल्यघोरिति ईत्वम् । श्नाप्रत्ययस्य ञित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । ग्नावः । ग्ना अस्य सन्तीति मतुप् । व्यत्ययेन वत्वम् । सम्बुद्धौ मतुवसो रुरिति रुत्वम् । विसर्गः । पादादित्वेनामन्त्रितनिघाताभावात् षाष्ठिकमामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । ग्नाव इत्यस्य विशेषणतया विशेषणवचनत्वान्नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरण इति निषेधाभावादविद्यमानवत्त्वेनोत्तरस्य नेष्टृशब्दस्य षाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वम् । पिब । शपः पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । पूर्वयोरामन्त्रितयोरविद्यमानवत्त्वेन निघाताभावः । रत्नधाः । रत्नानि दधातीति रत्नधाः । क्विप् च । धातुस्वरः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । असि । सिपः पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति हि चेति प्रतिषेधात् ॥३॥

gnā-śabdaḥ strī-vācī | tathā ca yāska āha | menā gnā iti strīṇāṃ … | ni. [3-21 ?] | gnā asya santīti gnāvān | neṣṭṛ-śabdo 'tra tvaṣṭāraṃ devam āha | kasmiṃścid deva-satre neṣṭṛtvena tvaṣṭur vṛtteḥ tasya | he gnāvaḥ patnī-yukta neṣṭaḥ tvaṣṭaḥ no 'smadīyaṃ yajñam abhi gṛṇīhi | abhito devānāṃ samīpe stuhi | ṛtunā saha tvaṃ somaṃ piba | hi yasmāt tvaṃ ratnadhā asi ratnānāṃ dātā 'si dātā bhavati tasmāt somaṃ pātum arhasīty arthaḥ || abhi | upasargāś cābhivarjam | phi. [?] | iti paryudāsād erantodāttatvam | gṛṇīhi | gṛ śabde | loṭi sipo hiḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | her jittvād īr halyaghor iti ītvam | śnā-pratyayasya ñittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ | tiṅ ataṅ iti nighātaḥ | gnāvaḥ | gnā asya santīti matup | vyatyayena vatvam | sambuddhau matuvaso ruḥ iti rutvam | visargaḥ | pādāditvenāmantrita-nighātābhāvāt ṣāṣṭhikam āmantritādyudāttatvam | gnāva ity asya viśeṣaṇatayā viśeṣaṇa-vacanatvān nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇa iti niṣedhābhāvād avidyamānavatvenottarasya neṣṭṛ-śabdasya ṣāṣṭhikam ādyudāttatvam | piba | śapaḥ pittvād dhātusvaraḥ | pūrvayor āmantritayor avidyamānavatvena nighātābhāvaḥ | ratnadhāḥ | ratnāni dadhātīti ratnadhāḥ | kvip ca | dhātusvaraḥ | samāse kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvena sa eva śiṣyate | asi | sipaḥ pittvād dhātusvaraḥ | tiṅ ataṅ iti nighāto na bhavati hi ceti pratiṣedhāt ||3||

Translation: "The word gnā means 'woman'. So Yāska says, menā gnā … [the Nirukta passage, 'women' — the Sanskrit of this quotation is partly unclear in print, and I give only its first words; Ni. 3-[?]]. Gnāvān is 'he who has gnā, i.e. a wife'. The word neṣṭṛ here means the god Tvaṣṭṛ — since in some divine sacrifices Tvaṣṭṛ acts as neṣṭṛ. O gnāvaḥ, O one joined to your wife, O Neṣṭṛ, Tvaṣṭṛ! Praise our sacrifice (abhi gṛṇīhi) — praise it all round in the presence of the gods. Together with the Ṛtu, drink the soma. For you are ratnadhāḥ — a giver of treasures; because you are a giver, you are fit to drink the soma." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: abhi (accent), gṛṇīhi (gṝ + śnā + hi, the lengthening of the ī, the shortening pvādīnām), gnāvaḥ (matup with va by vyatyaya; the vocative ru + visarga; the vocative accent on the first syllable by the ṣāṣṭhika rule; the neṣṭṛ after it treated as unaccented by the "as if not there" rule), piba, ratnadhāḥ (ratna + dhā + kvip), asi (the sip unaccented). Grammar, noted briefly.

Grammar pages (pp. 637 lower half–639 upper half), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: abhi (upasargāś cābhivarjam, Phiṭ-sūtra [number unclear in print] — the prepositions other than abhi have first-syllable accent; hence abhi has final accent by phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ, with a note that the Vedabhāṣya-kāra, citing evādīnām antaḥ (Phiṭ [?]), accepts final accent in such instances as mano martān abhi druhan; Ṛ. 6-[?]); gṛṇīhi (gṝ of the kryādi class; loṭ, sip, hi by P. 3-4-87 serhy apicca; śnā by P. 3-1-81; īhalyaghoḥ P. 6-4-113 for the ī; pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ P. 7-3-80; the endings śnā and hi as sārvadhātukas without pit so counted ñit, hence no guṇa, by P. 1-2-4; the verb unaccented by P. 8-1-28); gnāvaḥ (gnāḥ striyaḥ asya santi; matup by P. 5-2-94 tad asyāsty asminn iti matup; the m→v by vyatyaya; the num augment by P. 7-1-70 ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ; hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal P. 6-1-68 drops s; saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ P. 8-2-23 drops t; for gnāvan in the vocative, matuvasor ru sambuddhau chandasi P. 8-3-1 gives ru for the n, and r → visarga; before neṣṭaḥ the ru becomes u by P. 6-1-114 haśi ca and the ā+u guṇa gives gnāvo neṣṭaḥ — with a long note on pūrvatrāsiddham P. 8-2-1 and the rule that the dropping of a conjunct final is treated as not having happened for the ru rule, the Vārttika saṃyogāntalopo ruttve vācyaḥ, etc.); the accent of gnāvaḥ — it is at the start of the second pāda, so the P. 8-1-18 āmantritasya ca [? "āpādādau"] does not make it unaccented, and the first-syllable accent of P. 6-1-198 applies; gnāvaḥ is an adjective (viśeṣaṇa) of neṣṭaḥ, so P. 8-1-73 nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam [as read] does not bar P. 8-1-72 āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat; hence neṣṭaḥ, a vocative in the same pāda, takes the first-syllable accent, not the all-unaccented one. Piba (śap's pit-ness leaves the root accent; both preceding vocatives are treated as absent so piba is unaccented only by this; accent on the verb stays as P. 8-1-28's exception hi ca shows); ratnadhāḥ (dadhāti ratnāni, from ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ with kvip; accent of the root remains; the accent of the compound is that of its final member by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt); asi (as "to be", laṭ, sip, śap dropped by P. 2-4-72, s dropped by P. 6-4-111 śnasor allopaḥ; sip's pit-ness; hi ca P. 8-1-34 bars the loss of accent; P. 1-2-… udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ makes the i of si svarita). Numerals as read; pointers only; the long treatment of the vocative accent of gnāvaḥ neṣṭaḥ is given in outline.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ग्नावः (gnāvaḥ) — O you who are joined to your wife | नेष्टः (neṣṭaḥ) — O Tvaṣṭṛ | नः (naḥ) — our | यज्ञम् (yajñam) — sacrifice | अभि गृणीहि (abhi gṛṇīhi) — praise (before the gods), all round | ऋतुना (ṛtunā) — with the Ṛtu-deity | पिब (piba) — drink the soma-juice | हि (hi) — "because" | त्वम् (tvam) — you | रत्नधाः (ratna-dhāḥ) — the giver of the treasure (ratna, aiśvarya) that is the fruit of the sacrifice | असि (asi) — are.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Tvaṣṭṛ! You are renowned as one who bestows the treasure that is the fruit of the sacrifice. Such as you are, come with your wife, drink our soma-juice together with the Ṛtu-deity, and go to the gods and praise our sacrifice.

॥ English Translation ॥

Neshtri, (Twashtri) commend our sacrifice to the gods; drink with Ritu, for you are a giver of riches.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

ग्नावः (gnāvaḥ) — the word gnā means "woman". Yāska says "gnā gacchanty enāḥ" [Ni. 3-[?] — "those who go to them"]. Gnā asya santi iti gnāvān — he who has a wife is gnāvān; this vocative singular gnāvaḥ is an adjective of the word neṣṭaḥ.

नेष्टः (neṣṭaḥ) — in some sacrifices it is well known that Tvaṣṭṛ takes the share that belongs to the priest called Neṣṭṛ; therefore to address Tvaṣṭṛ by the word neṣṭṛ is not unnatural. Hence the commentator's view: the word neṣṭṛ here must be taken to mean the deity Tvaṣṭṛ.

रत्नधाः (ratnadhāḥ) — ratnānāṃ dātā: "giver of jewels" (of the best things). In the Ṛgveda the root dhā is commonly used where one would expect dā.

original pp. 639–641

Sūkta 15, Rik 4

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अग्ने देवाँ इहा वह सादया योनिषु त्रिषु । परि भूष पिब ऋतुना ॥४॥

agne devām̐ ihā vaha sādayā yoniṣu triṣu | pari bhūṣa piba ṛtunā ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened ihā, sādayā; the Pada the short forms.

अग्ने । देवान् । इह । आ । वह । सादय । योनिषु । त्रिषु ॥ परि । भूष । पिब । ऋतुना ॥४॥

agne | devān | iha | ā | vaha | sādaya | yoniṣu | triṣu || pari | bhūṣa | piba | ṛtunā ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने देवानिहास्मिन्कर्मण्या वह । ततो योनिषु स्थानेषु त्रिषु सवनेषु सादय । देवानुपवेशय । ततस्तान्परि भूष । अलंकुरु । ऋतुना सह त्वं सोमं पिब ॥ अग्ने देवानित्ययं पादो गतः । योनिषु । यु मिश्रणे । वहिश्रीत्यादिना । उ. [४-१३१ ?] । नि प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । त्रिषु । षट्त्रिचतुर्भ्यो हलादिः । पा. [६-१-१८१ ?] । इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । भूष । भूष अलंकारे । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । पिब ऋतुना । गतौ ॥

he agne devān ihāsmin karmaṇy ā vaha | tato yoniṣu sthāneṣu triṣu saveneṣu sādaya | devān upaveśaya | tatas tān pari bhūṣa | alaṅkuru | ṛtunā saha tvaṃ somaṃ piba || agne devān ity ayaṃ pādo gataḥ | yoniṣu | yu miśraṇe | vahi-śrī-ty-ādinā | u. [4-131 ?] | ni pratyayaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | triṣu | ṣaṭ-tri-catur-bhyo halādiḥ | pā. [6-1-181 ?] | iti vibhakter udāttatvam | bhūṣa | bhūṣa alaṅkāre | tiṅ ataṅ iti nighātaḥ | piba ṛtunā | gataḥ ||

Translation: "O Agni! Bring the gods here, to this rite. Then seat them (sādaya) in the three places (yoniṣu) — the three savanas: make them sit down. Then adorn them (pari bhūṣa); and together with the Ṛtu, drink the soma. [The pāda] agne devān [ihā vaha] has been gone through already [in Rik 3.11, per the Kannada]. Yoniṣu — root yu 'to mix', the Uṇādi ni suffix, first-syllable accent; triṣu — the case-ending is accented by P. 6-1-180/181 [ṣaṭ-tri-catur-bhyo halādiḥ]; bhūṣa — from bhūṣ 'to adorn', the verb unaccented. Piba ṛtunā — gone through [Rik 1]." The Sanskrit of the closing words was legible; the Uṇādi and Pāṇini numerals are marked [?] because they could not be read with certainty at 150 dpi.

Grammar pages (p. 641), noted briefly. The Kannada says that the pāda agne devām̐ ihā vaha has been treated at Sūkta 3, Rik 11 [the print's cross-reference numerals, read with a query]. Sādaya: ṣad "to sink, go, loosen", ṇic, the ṣ→s of dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ, the upadhā-vṛddhi P. 7-2-116 ata upadhāyāḥ; loṭ, sip, hi by P. 3-4-87; śap with guṇa and ay; luk of hi by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; the ṇic's a has the suffix-accent; śap's pit-ness leaves it unaccented; the final lengthening sādayā as in sajoṣāḥ etc. Yoniṣu: yu miśraṇe; Uṇ. 4-[?] vahi-śri-śru-yu-dru-gnā-tvaribhyo niḥ; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; locative plural yoniṣu; accent of ni. Triṣu: ṣaṭ-tri-catur-bhyo halādiḥ P. 6-1-180 [as printed 6-1-181?]; the name ṣaṭ for words ending in ṣ or n denoting numbers (ṣṇāntā ṣaṭ P. 1-1-24). Bhūṣa: bhūṣ alaṅkāre, loṭ, sip, hi, luk by P. 6-4-105; wholly unaccented by P. 8-1-28. Piba ṛtunā: the pair was explained in Sūkta 15 Rik 1 (print: "Ṛ. Saṃ. 15-1"). ॥4॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | देवान् (devān) — the gods | इह (iha) — for this rite | आ वह (ā vaha) — bring | त्रिषु योनिषु (triṣu yoniṣu) — in three separate places (in the three savanas) | सादय (sādaya) — seat | परि भूष (pari bhūṣa) — adorn | ऋतुना (ṛtunā) — with the Ṛtu-deity | पिब (piba) — drink (the soma-juice).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni! Bring the gods to this sacrifice of ours. Seat them in the three separate places — the morning, midday and evening savanas. Make suitable adornments. Together with the Ṛtu-deity, drink the soma-juice.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, bring the gods hither, seat them in three places (or in the three savanas), decorate them and drink with Ritu.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सादय (sādaya) — the last syllable of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text to suit the metre.

योनिषु त्रिषु (yoniṣu triṣu) — triṣu sthāneṣu: that is, the morning savana (prātaḥ-savana), the midday savana (mādhyandina-savana) and the third savana (tṛtīya-savana). A savana is the rite of drawing off the soma-juice. Because this rite is done with the recitation of mantras at three times — morning, midday and evening — these rites are called respectively the morning, midday and third savana.

परि भूष (pari bhūṣa) — alaṅkuru "adorn" is the commentator's gloss. Although the word bhūṣa has the sense "adorn", it may be doubted here whether there is any need to adorn the gods.

original pp. 642–646

Sūkta 15, Rik 5

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ब्राह्मणादिन्द्र राधसः पिबा सोममृतूँरनु । तवेद्धि सख्यमस्तृतम् ॥५॥

brāhmaṇād indra rādhasaḥ pibā somam ṛtūm̐r anu | taved dhi sakhyam astṛtam ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened pibā, the Pada the short piba.

ब्राह्मणात् । इन्द्र । राधसः । पिब । सोमम् । ऋतून् । अनु ॥ तव । इत् । हि । सख्यम् । अस्तृतम् ॥५॥

brāhmaṇāt | indra | rādhasaḥ | piba | somam | ṛtūn | anu || tava | it | hi | sakhyam | astṛtam ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र ब्राह्मणाद्ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिसम्बद्धाद्राधसो धनभूतात्पात्रात्सोममिमं पिब । किं कृत्वा । ऋतूननु ऋतुदेवानन्वनुसृत्य । ऋतवोऽपि पिबन्त्वित्यर्थः । हि यस्मात्तवेत्तव सख्यमस्तृतमृतूनामविच्छिन्नं तस्माद्ऋतुभिः सह पानं युक्तम् ॥ ब्राह्मणात् । ब्रह्मशब्देनात्र ब्रह्मवर्गे द्वितीयो ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी कथ्यते । स च पुल्लिङ्गे शेषनिघातेनानुदात्तादिः । तस्य सम्बन्धि [पात्रं] … अवयवविवक्षायामनुदात्तादेरञ् । पा. [४-३-१४०] । तेन ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तश्चमसपात्रे ऽत्र ब्राह्मणशब्दः । राधसः । सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पिब । पादादित्वाद् [?] … द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घत्वम् । ऋतूँरनु । दीर्घादटि समानपादे इति नकारस्य रुत्वम् । अत्रानुनासिकः पूर्वस्य तु वा । पा. ८-३-२ । इत्योकारस्यानुनासिकत्वम् । तव । युष्मदस्मद्भ्यां ङसोऽश् । पा. [७-१-२७] । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः । तवममौ ङसीति तवादेशः । युष्मदस्मदोर्ङसि इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । सख्यम् । सख्युः कर्म सख्यम् । सख्युर्यः । यस्येति लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अस्तृतम् । स्तृणातेर्हिंसार्थस्य क्तः । नञ्समासः । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥५॥

he indra brāhmaṇād brāhmaṇācchaṃsi-sambaddhād rādhaso dhana-bhūtāt pātrāt somam imaṃ piba | kiṃ kṛtvā | ṛtūn anu ṛtu-devān anvanusṛtya | ṛtavo 'pi pibantv ity arthaḥ | hi yasmāt tavet tava sakhyam astṛtam ṛtūnām avicchinnaṃ tasmād ṛtubhiḥ saha pānaṃ yuktam || brāhmaṇāt | brahma-śabdenātra brahma-varge dvitīyo brāhmaṇācchaṃsī kathyate | sa ca pulliṅge śeṣa-nighātenānudāttādiḥ | tasya sambandhi [pātraṃ] … avayava-vivakṣāyām anudāttāder añ | pā. [4-3-140] | tena ñittvād ādyudāttaś camasa-pātre 'tra brāhmaṇa-śabdaḥ | rādhasaḥ | sarva-dhātubhyo 'sun | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | piba | pādāditvād [?] … dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghatvam | ṛtūm̐r anu | dīrghād aṭi samānapāde iti nakārasya rutvam | atrānunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā | pā. 8-3-2 | ity okārasyānunāsikatvam | tava | yuṣmad-asmadbhyāṃ ṅaso 'ś | pā. [7-1-27] | śittvāt sarvādeśaḥ | tava-mamau ṅasīti tavādeśaḥ | yuṣmad-asmador ṅasi ity ādyudāttatvam | sakhyam | sakhyuḥ karma sakhyam | sakhyur yaḥ | yasyeti lopaḥ | pratyaya-svaraḥ | astṛtam | stṛṇāter hiṃsārthasya ktaḥ | nañ-samāsaḥ | avyaya-pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||5||

Translation: "O Indra! Drink this soma from the rādhas — the vessel that is a treasure (a precious vessel) — belonging to the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest. Having done what? ṛtūn anu — following the Ṛtu-deities: let the Ṛtus too drink. For (hi) your friendship with the Ṛtus is unbroken (astṛtam, 'uninterrupted'); therefore it is fitting that you drink together with them." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: brāhmaṇāt (the word brahman here denotes the second of the brahma-group of priests, the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; the vessel belonging to him is brāhmaṇa, the suffix añ in the sense of "part of", P. 4-3-140 [as read], first-syllable accent from the ñ); rādhasaḥ (Uṇādi asun after any root; first-syllable accent); pibā (lengthened, P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ); ṛtūm̐r anu (n → ru by P. 8-3-9 dīrghād aṭi samānapāde; the nasal o by P. 8-3-2 atrānunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā); tava (the substitute tava for yuṣmad + ṅas); sakhyam ("the act of a friend", sakhi + ya); astṛtam (stṛ "to strike", kta, with the negative compound na + stṛta, accent of the prefix). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 8-3-2 as read agrees with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 643 lower half–646 upper half), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats: brāhmaṇāt — at a Soma-sacrifice four priests, Brahman, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Āgnīdhra and Potṛ, belong to the brahma group; the second is meant here by the word brāhmaṇa, derived from brahman (from bṛh "to grow", by the old method bṛṃher nalopaś ca, or by the Uṇādi bṛṃher noccha with manin); brahman is both neuter and masculine (Amara [?]); in the neuter brahman has first-syllable accent by ñit (P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam), in the masculine the end accent by the ūḍidam-padādy-apvādi class (P. 6-1-171 [?] ūḍidam…); and the Kannada then lists the shapes of the sacrificial vessels (camasa) of the several priests in three Sanskrit verses of the old (Prācīna) tradition on the soma-pātra: the camasa of the Brahman is square (caturaśra), of the Hotṛ round, the yajamāna's broad, the Udgātṛ's three-cornered; and so on — the verses are as follows, transcribed from the Kannada print with doubtful words marked [?]:

चतुरश्रो ब्रह्मचमसः होतुस्तु परिमण्डलः । पृथुस्तु यजमानस्य त्र्यश्रिरुद्गातुरिष्यते ॥१॥ प्रशास्तुरवतप्यः [?] स्यादुत्तप्तो ब्रह्मशंसिनः । पोतुरग्रे विशाखी स्यात् नेष्टुस्तु विगृहीतकः ॥२॥ अच्छावाकस्य राष्णावा नाग्नीध्रस्य मयूखगः । सव्यावृतस्सदस्यः स्यादेतच्च मसलक्षणम् ॥३॥ दण्डानामेष आकारश्चमसाश्चतुरश्रगाः । पोतुर्ब्रह्मण उद्गातुर्यज्ञाशास्तुश्च शंसिनः ॥४॥

caturaśro brahma-camasaḥ hotus tu parimaṇḍalaḥ | pṛthus tu yajamānasya tryaśrir udgātur iṣyate ||1|| praśāstur avatapyaḥ [?] syād uttapto brahma-śaṃsinaḥ | poturagre viśākhī syāt neṣṭus tu vigṛhītakaḥ ||2|| acchāvākasya rāṣṇāvā nāgnīdhrasya mayūkhagaḥ | savyāvṛtassadasyaḥ syād etac ca masalakṣaṇam ||3|| daṇḍānām eṣa ākāraś camasāś caturaśragāḥ | potur brahmaṇa udgātur yajñāśāstuś ca śaṃsinaḥ ||4||

The prose that follows reads potṛ-neṣṭṛ-acchāvākānām āgnīdhrasyeti ca kramaḥ ("the order is Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, Acchāvāka and Āgnīdhra"). The four verses are given from small print at 150 dpi; the second and fourth are the least certain, and their meaning is not clear beyond the first and the third — they are given as read, with no translation beyond the first line. The Kannada adds that these were said by the ancients in connection with the Agniṣṭoma's soma-pātra-handling; from them it appears that the handle of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's soma-vessel is uttapta — lifted up — so the vessel with its raised handle is like a limb of the priest: therefore it may be called his avayava ("part"); and añ is added in the sense of "a part of" by P. 4-3-134 anudāttādeś ca [as printed 4-3-14x], so brāhmaṇa means "the vessel as a part of the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin", with the first-syllable accent from the ñ. Rādhasaḥ — rādh with asun (Uṇ. 4-[?] sarvadhātubhyo 'sun). Piba — the lengthening at 1.14.10 [print "ṛ. saṃ. 1-14-10"] is cited; its pāda-initial position means P. 8-1-18/19 does not make it unaccented. Ṛtūm̐r anu — dīrghād aṭi samānapāde P. 8-3-9; atrānunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā P. 8-3-2, applying to the ū the anunāsika by the ru-section's option. Tava — the śas → aś substitution for ṅas after yuṣmad/asmad (P. 7-1-27), as a śit replacing the whole word by P. 1-1-55; the tava-mama substitution by P. 7-2-96 tavamamau ṅasi; the accent by P. 6-1-… ; śeṣe lopaḥ P. 7-2-90 dropping the final ad, and anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ P. 6-1-161 [as read]; the accent ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ P. 8-2-5. Sakhyam — sakhyuḥ karma; sakhyur yaḥ [P. 5-1-126] — the ya suffix after sakhi in the sense of 'action'; yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148 drops the i; suffix accent. Astṛtam — stṛñ ācchādane "to cover", a root of the svādi class; the Kannada argues that the root here is the himsā sense stṛ "to strike"; the kta has no iṭ by P. 7-2-10 ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt; or by P. 7-2-43 ṛtaś ca saṃyogāder guṇaḥ — the ṛ of a root with a conjunct initial; the negative compound nañ + stṛta with P. 6-2-2 [?]; ṛ→ir by P. 7-1-100 ṛta iddhātoḥ, ur aṇ raparaḥ P. 1-1-51, hali ca P. 8-2-77 (lengthening), and the n of -ṇa — hence astīrṇam; this shows the commentator's astṛtam is formed on the svādi root stṛ with kta. A crowded run; outline only; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | हि (hi) — for the reason that | तव इत् (tav-et) — yours indeed | सख्यम् (sakhyam) — friendship [with the Ṛtus] | अस्तृतम् (astṛtam) — is unbroken | therefore ब्राह्मणात् (brāhmaṇāt) — from the vessel of the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin | राधसः (rādhasaḥ) — from the precious camasa-vessel | सोमम् (somam) — the soma-juice | ऋतून् अनु (ṛtūn anu) — together with the Ṛtu-deities | पिब (piba) — drink.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! It is well known in the world that your friendship with the Ṛtu-deities is eternal. Therefore, drink the soma-juice, together with the Ṛtu-deities, from the precious camasa-vessel of the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.

॥ English Translation ॥

Drink the soma juice, Indra, from the cups of priest called Brahmanachamsi, after Ritu for whom your friendship is uninterrupted (everlasting).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

ब्राह्मणात् (brāhmaṇāt) — the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.

राधसः (rādhasaḥ) — dhana-bhūtāt pātrāt: rādhas just means "wealth". The sense "vessel" is not in the word itself, but the commentator supplies it. Or, since rādhas means "priceless", "of great value", the sense could be "costly vessel" (the print gives the English words "costly vessel").

अस्तृतम् (astṛtam) — avicchinnam: unbroken, "uninterrupted" [the print has "uninterruptedr", sic]; that has not stopped after continuing for a time; that is everlasting.

original pp. 646–650

Sūkta 15, Rik 6

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युवं दक्षं धृतव्रत मित्रावरुण दूळभम् । ऋतुना यज्ञमाशाथे ॥६॥

yuvaṃ dakṣaṃ dhṛtavrata mitrāvaruṇa dūḷabham | ṛtunā yajñam āśāthe ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the final-short forms dhṛtavrata, mitrāvaruṇa; the Pada has dhṛtavratā, mitrāvaruṇā. In the Saṃhitā the word is spelt dūḷabham with the Vedic ḷ.

युवम् । दक्षम् । धृतऽव्रता । मित्रावरुणा । दुःऽदभम् ॥ ऋतुना । यज्ञम् । आशाथे इति ॥६॥

yuvam | dakṣam | dhṛta-vratā | mitrāvaruṇā | duḥ-dabham || ṛtunā | yajñam | āśāthe iti ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे धृतव्रता स्वीकृतकर्माणौ मित्रावरुणा हे मित्रनामकवरुणनामकौ देवौ युवमुभौ युवामृतुना सहास्मदीयं यज्ञमाशाथे । व्याप्नुथः । कीदृशं यज्ञम् । दक्षं प्रवृद्धं दूळभं दुर्दहं शत्रुभिर्दग्धुं विनाशयितुमशक्यमित्यर्थः ॥ युवं । प्रथमाद्विवचनस्य जसि प्रथमयोरमित्यमादेशः । युवावौ द्विवचने । पा. [७-२-९२] । इति मपर्यन्तस्य युवादेशः । शेषे लोप इति टिलोपोऽन्त्यलोपो वा । अमि पूर्वत्वम् । भाषायामेव ह्यत्वम् । टिलोपपक्षे उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेणामः उदात्तत्वम् । अन्त्यलोपपक्षे एकादेश उदात्तः । दक्षं । दक्ष वृद्धौ । दक्ष्यन्त्येनेति करणे घञ् । एवं हि पुल्लिङ्गत्वनियमः । अन्यस्यानियम इति नपुंसकत्वम् । धृतव्रता मित्रावरुणा । धृतानि व्रतानि याभ्यां तौ धृतव्रतौ । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च मित्रावरुणौ । उभयत्र सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराकारः । मित्रशब्दो देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्यानङादेशः । प्रथमस्यामन्त्रितनिघातः । द्वितीयस्य पादादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । संहितायां छान्दसं ह्रस्वत्वम् । दूळभं । दह भस्मीकरणे । दुःखेन दह्यते इति दुर्दहं । ईषद्दुःसुषु कृच्छ्राकृच्छ्रार्थेषु । पा. [३-३-१२६] । दुरुपपदस्य खल् । … ळत्वं … । लिति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वमुदात्तत्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । आशाथे । अशू व्याप्तौ । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति वर्तमाने लिट् । मध्यमद्विवचनमाथाम् । टेरेत्वम् । अत आदेः । पा. [७-४-७०] । इत्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घः । अश्नोतेश्च । पा. [७-४-७२] । इति प्राप्तो नुडागमोऽनित्यमागमशासनमिति निवर्तते ॥६॥

he dhṛtavratā svīkṛta-karmāṇau mitrāvaruṇā he mitra-nāmaka-varuṇa-nāmakau devau yuvam ubhau yuvām ṛtunā sahāsmadīyaṃ yajñam āśāthe | vyāpnuthaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ yajñam | dakṣaṃ pravṛddhaṃ dūḷabhaṃ durdahaṃ śatrubhir dagdhuṃ vināśayitum aśakyam ity arthaḥ || yuvaṃ | prathamād dvivacanasya jasi prathamayor am ity amādeśaḥ | yuvāvau dvivacane | pā. [7-2-92] | iti mapayantasya yuvādeśaḥ | śeṣe lopa iti ṭilopo 'ntyalopo vā | ami pūrvatvam | bhāṣāyām eva hy atvam | ṭilopa-pakṣe udātta-nivṛtti-svareṇāmaḥ udāttatvam | antyalopa-pakṣe ekādeśa udāttaḥ | dakṣaṃ | dakṣa vṛddhau | dakṣyanty eneti karaṇe ghañ | evaṃ hi pulliṅgatva-niyamaḥ | anyasyāniyama iti napuṃsakatvam | dhṛtavratā mitrāvaruṇā | dhṛtāni vratāni yābhyāṃ tau dhṛtavratau | mitraś ca varuṇaś ca mitrāvaruṇau | ubhayatra supāṃ sulug ity-ādinā vibhakter ākāraḥ | mitra-śabdo devatādvandve cety ānaṅādeśaḥ | prathamasyāmantrita-nighātaḥ | dvitīyasya pādāditvād ādyudāttatvam | saṃhitāyāṃ chāndasaṃ hrasvatvam | dūḷabhaṃ | daha bhasmīkaraṇe | duḥkhena dahyate iti durdahaṃ | īṣad-duḥ-suṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu | pā. [3-3-126] | dur-upapadasya khal | … ḷatvaṃ … | liti pratyayāt pūrvam udāttatvam | kṛd-uttarapadatvena sa eva śiṣyate | āśāthe | aśū vyāptau | chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭa iti vartamāne liṭ | madhyama-dvivacanam āthām | ṭer ettvam | ata ādeḥ | pā. [7-4-70] | ity abhyāsasya dīrghaḥ | aśnoteś ca | pā. [7-4-72] | iti prāpto nuḍāgamo 'nityam āgama-śāsanam iti nivartate ||6||

Translation: "O dhṛtavratā — you two who have taken up the sacrificial work — Mitra and Varuṇa, the gods named Mitra and Varuṇa! You both, together with the Ṛtu, pervade (āśāthe, 'enter into, fill') our sacrifice. Of what sort is the sacrifice? Dakṣam — flourishing; dūḷabham — hard to burn (durdaha), that cannot be burnt, destroyed, by enemies." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: yuvam (the substitute yuva for yuṣmad in the dual by P. 7-2-92 yuvāvau dvivacane, with the accusative ending am by P. 7-1-28 [?]); dakṣam (dakṣ "to grow", ghañ in the instrument sense: "that by which they grow strong", with the neuter by option); dhṛtavratā mitrāvaruṇā ("those by whom vows are held"; mitrāvaruṇau a deity-dvandva with ānaṅ [mitra + ā + varuṇa]; the endings replaced by ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…; the first word unaccented as a vocative, the second given the first-syllable accent because it begins the pāda; in the Saṃhitā the final long ā is shortened by Vedic licence); dūḷabham (dah "to burn", khal after dur by P. 3-3-126 īṣad-duḥ-suṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal, with the Vedic change of h to bh, d to ḍ and ḍ to ḷ); āśāthe (aś "to pervade", liṭ of the dual middle āthām; the reduplication lengthened by P. 7-4-70 ata ādeḥ; the nuṭ augment of P. 7-4-72 aśnoteś ca is not applied because "the rules on augments are optional"). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 3-3-126 and P. 7-4-70 agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 648 lower half–650), noted briefly. The Kannada treats yuvam (yuṣmad + au; P. 7-2-92 yuvāvau dvivacane, the substitute yuva for the part of the word up to and including m; jasi prathamayor am; P. 7-2-88 prathamāyāś ca dvivacane bhāṣāyām [ā of yuvām is for the bhāṣā only, not for the Veda]; śeṣe lopaḥ P. 7-2-90 dropping ṭi or the final letter; ami pūrvaḥ P. 6-1-107; the accent of yuvam ends up final in one derivation and as the single substituted vowel in the other), dakṣam (dakṣ "to grow", ghañ by P. 3-3-121 halaś ca in the sense of instrument and location, which would give a masculine, but the neuter is allowed by the rule anyasyāniyamaḥ), dhṛtavratā mitrāvaruṇā (dhṛtāni vratāni yābhyām tau; the vocative endings with sup → ā, P. 7-1-39; devatādvandve ca P. 6-3-26 for the ānaṅ, the dual-ending ṅit on the ā, ṅ indicatory, final n being dropped by P. 8-2-7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; the first word a vocative unaccented by P. 8-1-72 — but the dvandva's end is at the start of the pāda, so P. 8-1-19 [āmantritasya ca] does not apply; the first-syllable accent follows by P. 6-1-198; the shortening in the Saṃhitā a Vedic licence), dūḷabham (dah + dur + khal; P. 3-3-126 with the long explanation of the Mahābhāṣya's splitting of the sūtra vyatyayo bahulam P. 3-1-85 into vyatyayaḥ "interchange of the suffixes śap etc. in the Veda" and bahulam "all rules are optional in the Veda", with the Vārttika on sup-… liṅga-nara-nām … kālahalac-svarakartṛyaṅām ca vyatyayaḥ; the change du-dah-bha → dūḍabha → dūḷabha with ḍ → ḷ by the Ṛgvedic rule on ḍ and ḍh as ḷ, ḷh; the accent before the l-marked suffix P. 6-1-193 liti), āśāthe (aś "to pervade", liṭ by P. 3-4-6 chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ; doubling P. 6-1-8 liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya; thās → āthām [middle dual 2nd]; ṭeḥ → e by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60 retaining the first consonant; ata ādeḥ P. 7-4-70 lengthening the reduplicative a, so āśāthe; aśnoteś ca P. 7-4-72 nuṭ barred). Numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

धृतव्रता (dhṛtavratā) — O you two who accept the sacrificial work done by us | मित्रावरुणा (mitrāvaruṇā) — O Mitra and Varuṇa | युवम् (yuvam) — you both | ऋतुना (ṛtunā) — together with the Ṛtu-deity | दक्षम् (dakṣam) — flourishing | दूळभम् (dūḷabham) — that cannot be burnt (destroyed) by enemies | यज्ञम् (yajñam) — the sacrifice | आशाथे (āśāthe) — you pervade (you are gracious to).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Mitra and Varuṇa! You accept our sacrificial work. By your favour our sacrifice flourishes; and because you are with us, no enemy can harm it. Be pleased to come, together with the Ṛtu-deity, to our sacrifice.

॥ English Translation ॥

Mitra and Varuna, propitious to pious acts, be present with Ritu at our sacrifice, efficacious and undisturbed by foes.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

धृतव्रता (dhṛtavratā) — dhṛta-karmāṇau or svīkṛta-karmāṇau: they who accept the sacrificial work that we perform. The final syllables of dhṛtavratā and mitrāvaruṇā are shortened in the Saṃhitā text to suit the metre.

This word dhṛtavratā occurs also in the Ṛgveda rik

इन्द्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं सोमं पिबतं मद्यं धृतव्रता ॥ indrāvaruṇā sutapāv imaṃ sutaṃ somaṃ pibataṃ madyaṃ dhṛtavratā || (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-68-10)

where it refers to Indra and Varuṇa. Besides, the forms dhṛtavrataḥ, dhṛtavratāḥ, dhṛtavratāya and dhṛtavrate are read in many riks.

दूळभम् (dūḷabham) — duḥ-dabham: śatrubhir dagdhuṃ vināśayitum aśakyam, "that which cannot be burnt, destroyed, by enemies". The word dūḷabha, with the same sense, is read also in other riks of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā — dūḷabhaḥ and dūḷabhāsaḥ — whose references the print gives in small numerals (I read them as 3-[?]-[?]; 2-[?]-[?]; 4-[?]-[?]; 8-[?]-[?], but not reliably, and do not reproduce them).
