Sūkta 15, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदा द्रविणसो ग्रावहस्तासो अध्वरे । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते ॥७॥

draviṇodā draviṇaso grāvahastāso adhvare | yajñeṣu devam īḷate ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

द्रविणःऽदाः । द्रविणसः । ग्रावऽहस्तासः । अध्वरे ॥ यज्ञेषु । देवम् । ईळते ॥७॥

draviṇaḥ-dāḥ | draviṇasaḥ | grāva-hastāsaḥ | adhvare || yajñeṣu | devam | īḷate ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अध्वरेऽग्निष्टोमे प्रकृतिरूपे यज्ञेषु विकृतिरूपेषूक्थ्यादिषु च देवमग्निमीळते । ऋत्विजः स्तुवन्ति । कीदृशा ऋत्विजः । द्रविणसो धनार्थिनो ग्रावहस्तासोऽभिषवसाधनपाषाणधारिणः । कीदृशं देवम् । द्रविणोदा धनप्रदम् । यद्वा । धनप्रदोऽग्निः सोमं पिबत्विति शेषः । तत्रेमं मन्त्रं यास्क एवं निर्वक्ति । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्धनं द्रविणमुच्यते यदेनदभिद्रवन्ति बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवन्ति तस्य दाता द्रविणोदास्तस्यैषा भवति । द्रविणोदा द्रविणस इत्यादि । नि. [८-१ ?] । सोऽयं यास्कोक्तो निर्वचनप्रपञ्चस्तस्मिन्नेव ग्रन्थेऽवगन्तव्यः ॥ द्रविणोदाः । द्रुदक्षिभ्यामिनन् । उ. [२-५०]। नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तो द्रविणशब्दः । तद्ददातीति द्रविणोदाः । क्विप् च । पूर्वपदस्य सकारोपजनश्छन्दसि । रुत्वोत्वे । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । देवविशेषणत्वे नैकवाक्यताऽपक्षे द्वितीयायाः स्वादेशः । अथवा द्रविणमात्मन इच्छन्ति द्रविणस्यन्ति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यो लालसायां सुग्वक्तव्यः । … द्रविणस्यतेः सम्पदादित्वाद्भावे क्विप् । अतो लोपः । क्वौ लुप्तं न स्थानिवद्भवति … एवं द्रविणशब्दो धनेच्छावाचकः । द्रविणेच्छां दस्यति … ग्रावयुक्ता हस्ता येषां ते ग्रावहस्तासः । आज्जसेरसुक् । ग्रावशब्दो वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अध्वरे । न विद्यते ध्वरो हिंसा यस्मिन् । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । ईळते । अनुदात्तेत्त्वादात्मनेपदम् । आदिप्रभृतिभ्य इति शपो लुक् । झस्यात्वादेशः ॥७॥

adhvare 'gniṣṭome prakṛti-rūpe yajñeṣu vikṛti-rūpeṣūkthyādiṣu ca devam agnim īḷate | ṛtvijaḥ stuvanti | kīdṛśā ṛtvijaḥ | draviṇaso dhanārthino grāvahastāso 'bhiṣava-sādhana-pāṣāṇa-dhāriṇaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ devam | draviṇodā dhana-pradam | yadvā | dhana-prado 'gniḥ somaṃ pibatv iti śeṣaḥ | tatremaṃ mantraṃ yāska evaṃ nirvakti | draviṇodāḥ kasmād dhanaṃ draviṇam ucyate yad enad abhidravanti balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yad enenābhidravanti tasya dātā draviṇodās tasyaiṣā bhavati | draviṇodā draviṇasa ity-ādi | ni. [8-1 ?] | so 'yaṃ yāskoktō nirvacana-prapañcas tasminn eva grantha 'vagantavyaḥ || draviṇodāḥ | dru-dakṣibhyām inan | u. [2-50] | nittvād ādyudātto draviṇa-śabdaḥ | tad dadātīti draviṇodāḥ | kvip ca | pūrvapadasya sakāropajanaś chandasi | rutvotve | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | deva-viśeṣaṇatve naikavākyatā-pakṣe dvitīyāyāḥ svādeśaḥ | athavā draviṇam ātmana icchanti draviṇasyanti | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | sarva-prātipadikebhyo lālasāyāṃ sug vaktavyaḥ | … draviṇasyateḥ sampadādittvād bhāve kvip | ato lopaḥ | kvau luptaṃ na sthānivad bhavati … evaṃ draviṇa-śabdo dhanecchā-vācakaḥ | draviṇecchāṃ dasyati … grāva-yuktā hastā yeṣāṃ te grāvahastāsaḥ | āj jaser asuk | grāva-śabdo vṛṣādittvād ādyudāttaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | adhvare | na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasmin | nañ-subhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvam | īḷate | anudāttettvād ātmanepadam | ādiprabhṛtibhya iti śapo luk | jhasyātvādeśaḥ ||7||

Translation: "At the adhvara — the Agniṣṭoma, the original (prakṛti) form of the sacrifice — and at the sacrifices (yajñeṣu) that are its modifications (vikṛti), such as the Ukthya and the rest, the priests praise (īḷate) the god Agni. What sort of priests? Draviṇasaḥ — seekers of wealth; grāvahastāsaḥ — holding in the hand the stones that are the means of pressing the soma. What sort of god? Draviṇodāḥ — the giver of wealth. Or: [the sense is] 'may Agni, the giver of wealth, drink the soma' (the rest being supplied). On this mantra Yāska comments as follows [Ni. 8-1 — the print's numeral is small, I give it with a query]: draviṇodāḥ — why is wealth called draviṇa? Because people run (abhidravanti) towards it; or because draviṇa is strength, by which they run towards it; he who gives it is draviṇodāḥ; of him is this [rik]. draviṇodā draviṇasaḥ … The full explanation given by Yāska should be looked for in that work itself." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: draviṇodāḥ (the Uṇādi inan after dru; first-syllable accent of draviṇa through the n mark; "he gives it" with kvip; an s is added to the first member in the Veda; the ru/u sandhi; the accent of the final member of the compound); a second explanation of draviṇasaḥ: draviṇasyanti, "they desire wealth for themselves" — kyac with suk, then kvip in the abstract sense, with the dropping of a and the paribhāṣā on sthānivad-bhāva; grāvahastāsaḥ ("those whose hands are provided with stones"; the plural ending asuk by P. 7-1-50; grāva has the first-syllable accent through its inclusion in the vṛṣādi list; the bahuvrīhi keeps the accent of its first member); adhvare ("that in which there is no dhvara, no violence", with the final accent by nañsubhyām); īḷate (ātmanepada from the anudāttet marking, śap dropped, jha → ata). Grammar, noted briefly; the Uṇādi number is as read.

Grammar pages (pp. 654 lower half–656), noted briefly. The Kannada treats draviṇodāḥ at length: Uṇ. 2-50 dru-dakṣibhyām inan, from dru "to run" + inan (guṇa, av, ṇatva by P. 8-4-2 aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi), then dā + kvip with luk of am after the first member, "an s augment", ru → u, the first-syllable accent of the first member overridden by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, so the end accent; and in the optional second analysis the kyac verb draviṇasyati "he desires wealth" with the kvip in the abstract sense and the loss of the final a (P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ), the sthānivat barred by the rule that what is dropped before kvip is not sthānin [Vārttika], and the further question of vali lopa (P. 6-1-66 lopo vyor vali), P. 6-1-67 vera prktasya and the asiddha rule P. 6-4-22 asiddhavad atrābhāt; the second analysis gives draviṇas for "seeker of wealth" (dhaneccu), or from dasu upakṣaye "to waste" with ṇic hidden, "he who wastes wealth by giving as desired and thereby removes the wish for wealth", with kvip, the loss of kvip, and draviṇodas a stem in s — which underlies the Nirukta usage draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti (Ni. 8-2); the Kannada concludes that if draviṇodāḥ is not an epithet of devam there are two sentences (draviṇodāḥ in the nominative by su), and if it is, one sentence (the accusative sense to be understood in the nominative). Draviṇasaḥ — in the sense "the soma-juice" under the two-sentence reading, by the Vedic procedure with the sag augment (P. 3-1-xx, as read); the accent by ñnityādir nityam P. 6-1-197; with the rest of the grammar of the compound-forms as in the earlier derivations. Grāvahastāsaḥ — grāvayuktāḥ hastāḥ yeṣām; āj jaser asuk P. 7-1-50; grāva from the vṛṣādi list (P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca) with first-syllable accent. Adhvare — the negative compound with nañ; the final accent by P. 6-2-172. Īḷate — īḍ "to praise", anudāttet, so ātmanepada by P. 1-3-12; the laṭ third plural jha, śap dropped by P. 2-4-72, jha → ata by P. 7-1-5, ṭeḥ → e by P. 3-4-79, and ḍ → ḷ in the Veda. A crowded run; outline only; numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

द्रविणसः (draviṇasaḥ) — priests desirous of wealth | ग्रावहस्तासः (grāva-hastāsaḥ) — holding in the hand the stones [that serve to press the soma] | द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ) — the giver of wealth (or: [the deity] called Draviṇodā) | देवम् (devam) — the god Agni | अध्वरे (adhvare) — in the original sacrifice, the Agniṣṭoma | यज्ञेषु (yajñeṣu) — in the modified sacrifices, the Ukthya and the like | ईळते (īḷate) — praise.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Priests who seek wealth, holding in their hands the stones for pressing the soma, in the Agniṣṭoma (the prakṛti) as in the vikṛti sacrifices such as the Ukthya, invoke and praise Agni, called Draviṇodā, to come and drink the soma.

॥ English Translation ॥

The priests desirous of wealth, with the soma-pressing stones in their hands praise the divine (Agni) Dravinodas who is the giver of riches, in the Soma and other sacrifices.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ) — Yāska has written a long explanation of this word:

द्रविणोदाः । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्धनं द्रविणमुच्यते यदेनदभिद्रवन्ति । बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवन्ति । तस्य दाता द्रविणोदाः ॥ (नि. [८-१])

draviṇodāḥ | draviṇodāḥ kasmād dhanaṃ draviṇam ucyate yad enad abhidravanti | balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yad enenābhidravanti | tasya dātā draviṇodāḥ || (ni. [8-1])

"Why is draviṇodāḥ so called? Wealth is called draviṇa because people run (abhidravanti) towards it; or strength is draviṇa because by it they run towards [the goal]. He who gives it is draviṇodāḥ." The Kannada explains: draviṇam dadātīti draviṇodāḥ — the word draviṇa has two senses, wealth and strength, so draviṇodāḥ is "giver of wealth or of strength"; this is the derivation. And Yāska then explains the rik as follows:

द्रविणोदा यस्त्वम् । द्रविणस इति द्रविणसादिन इति वा द्रविणसस्स्यात् [?] पिब त्विति वा । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते । याचन्ति स्तुवन्ति वर्धयन्ति पूजयन्तीति वा ॥

draviṇodā yas tvam | draviṇasa iti draviṇasādina iti vā draviṇasas syāt [?] piba tv iti vā | yajñeṣu devam īḷate | yācanti stuvanti vardhayanti pūjayantīti vā ||

[This is as read from small print; the middle clause is compressed and not clear to me.] That is: those priests who look for wealth, havis and the like invoke you, draviṇodāḥ, to drink soma at the sacrifices — this is the chief sense. Here draviṇodāḥ is a nominative singular; how then does it qualify devam, an accusative? The Kannada says: one must supply "yaḥ devaḥ taṃ devam" — "that god who is draviṇodāḥ". Draviṇasaḥ: the priests who seek wealth or havis (draviṇasaḥ = dhana-kāmāḥ, from the ritual, not the soma-juice sense). Īḷate — can also be taken as "ask, praise, extol, worship".

Further Yāska says:

तत्को द्रविणोदा इन्द्र इति क्रौष्टुकिः । स बलधनयोर्दातृतमस्तस्य च सर्वा बलकृतिः ॥

tat ko draviṇodā indra iti krauṣṭukiḥ | sa bala-dhanayor dātṛtamas tasya ca sarvā bala-kṛtiḥ ||

"Who then is draviṇodāḥ? Indra, says Krauṣṭuki; he is the greatest giver of strength and wealth, and all deeds of strength are his." (The Kannada: Krauṣṭuki's view is that draviṇodāḥ means Indra, since draviṇa means strength and wealth, and Indra gives them most.)

अथाप्यग्निं द्रविणोदसमाहुरेष पुनरेतस्माज्जायते । यो अश्मनोरन्तरग्निं जजान इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥

athāpy agniṃ draviṇodasam āhur eṣa punar etasmāj jāyate | yo aśmanor antar agniṃ jajāna ity api nigamo bhavati ||

"Moreover they call Agni draviṇodas; he is born again from this [Indra]: 'who produced Agni between the two stones' — such a nigama [Vedic citation] also exists." (Indra produced the heaven and earth, and Agni between them; so draviṇodāḥ may also mean Agni — the rik yo aśmanor antar agniṃ jajāna [Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-3] is cited in support [reference numerals unclear].)

अथाप्यृतुयोजेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवन्ति । तेषां पुनः पात्रस्यैन्द्रपानमिति भवति ॥ अथाप्येनं सोमपानेन स्तौति । अथाप्याह द्रविणोदाः पिबतु द्रविणोदस इति ॥

athāpy ṛtu-yojeṣu draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti | teṣāṃ punaḥ pātrasyaindra-pānam iti bhavati || athāpy enaṃ soma-pānena stauti | athāpy āha draviṇodāḥ pibatu draviṇodasa iti ||

"Again, in the sacrifices connected with the Ṛtus there are statements about draviṇodas; and again, 'the drinking of the vessel by Indra' is said; and he is praised with soma-drinking; and also it is said, 'draviṇodāḥ pibatu draviṇodasaḥ'." (The Kannada: in the sacrifices offered to the Ṛtus it is said that Indra drinks from the vessel in the hands of the priests; thus Indra is praised by the soma-drinking mantras, and the priests are called draviṇodasaḥ — all this is the view of Krauṣṭuki.)

अयमेवाग्निर्द्रविणोदा इति शाकपूणिः । आग्नेयेष्वेव हि सूक्तेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवन्ति ॥

ayam evāgnir draviṇodā iti śākapūṇiḥ | āgneyeṣv eva hi sūkteṣu draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti ||

"This very Agni is draviṇodāḥ, says Śākapūṇi; for it is in the sūktas addressed to Agni that the statements about draviṇodas occur." (The Kannada: this is Śākapūṇi's view; in Agni-sūktas the priests use the word draviṇodāḥ as an epithet of Agni.)

[तथो वैतत्स बलधनयोर्दातृतम इति सर्वासु देवतासु ऐश्वर्यं विद्यते । तथो ऽ'एतदोजसो जातमुतमन्य एनं' इति चाहेत्यप्यग्निरोजसा बलेन मथ्यमानो जायते तस्मादेनमाह सहसस्पुत्रं सहसः सूनुं सहसो यहुम् ॥]

[tatho vaitat sa bala-dhanayor dātṛtama iti sarvāsu devatāsu aiśvaryaṃ vidyate | tatho 'etad ojaso jātam utamanya enam' iti cāhety apy agnir ojasā balena mathyamāno jāyate tasmād enam āha sahasas-putraṃ sahasaḥ sūnuṃ sahaso yahum ||]

This passage is printed in small type and the readings of its first words — here given as tatho vaitat — are uncertain [?]; its sense, as the Kannada gives it, is: "All deities have lordship; so Agni too gives strength and wealth, and may be called draviṇodāḥ. Since draviṇa has the sense 'strength', and Agni is kindled by the force of strength (churned by rubbing), he is believed to be born of strength; hence the Veda praises Agni as 'sahasas-putra' (son of strength), 'sahasaḥ sūnu', 'sahaso yahu'." The Kannada then gives three riks in which these epithets of Agni occur:

द्रविणोदाः सर्पिरासुतिः प्रत्नो होता वरेण्यः । सहसस्पुत्रो अद्भुतः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [३-२-६]) draviṇodāḥ sarpirāsutiḥ pratno hotā vareṇyaḥ | sahasas-putro adbhutaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. [3-2-6])

त्वं ह यद्यविष्ठ्य सहसः सूनवाहुतः । ऋतावा यज्ञियो भुवः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [८-२३-३]) tvaṃ ha yad yaviṣṭhya sahasaḥ sūnav āhutaḥ | ṛtāvā yajñiyo bhuvaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. [8-23-3])

अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो । अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-७९-४]) agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho | asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. [1-79-4])

The references are as read from the small numerals; each is marked [?]. The Kannada concludes that although the other deities too give strength and wealth, Agni is above all the one proclaimed by the word draviṇodāḥ.

ग्रावहस्तासः (grāvahastāsaḥ) — those who hold the stones in their hand to crush the soma-creeper.

अध्वरे, यज्ञेषु (adhvare, yajñeṣu) — The words adhvara and yajña are in general sense both "sacrifice". Here, in order to avoid the fault of repetition, the commentator takes adhvara as the Agniṣṭoma, which is the prakṛti form, and yajña as particular sacrifices, the vikṛti forms, the Ukthya and others. Prakṛti means the original sacrificial work, containing the programme that applies in general to all sacrifices; vikṛti means the sacrificial work performed with modifications of certain details; the actions in all the vikṛtis are as in the prakṛti, differing only in one or two matters. We shall explain prakṛti and vikṛti sacrifices elsewhere [the print says "we explained earlier"].

original pp. 657–658

Sūkta 15, Rik 8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदा ददातु नो वसूनि यानि शृण्विरे । देवेषु ता वनामहे ॥८॥

draviṇodā dadātu no vasūni yāni śṛṇvire | deveṣu tā vanāmahe ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्रविणःऽदाः । ददातु । नः । वसूनि । यानि । शृण्विरे ॥ देवेषु । ता । वनामहे ॥८॥

draviṇaḥ-dāḥ | dadātu | naḥ | vasūni | yāni | śṛṇvire || deveṣu | tā | vanāmahe ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

द्रविणोदा देवो नोऽस्मभ्यं वसूनि धनानि ददातु । यानि धनानि शृण्विरे हविरुपयुक्तत्वेन श्रूयन्ते [?] । तानि च सर्वाणि धनानि देवेषु निमित्तभूतेषु वनामहे । सम्भजामः । धनैर्देवान्यष्टुं तानि स्वीकुर्म इत्यर्थः ॥ द्रविणोदाः । गतम् । वसूनि । शृस्पृस्निहीत्यादिना । उ. [१-११] । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तः । शृण्विरे । श्रु श्रवणे । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति वर्तमाने लिट् । झ इरेच् । पा. [३-४-८१] । छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकत्वे व्यत्ययेन श्नुः । तस्संनियोगेन शृभावश्च । उवङः प्राप्ते हुश्नुवोः सार्वधातुके । पा. [६-४-८७] । इति यणादेशः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः । ता । शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य । पा. [८-२-७] । इति नलोपः । वनामहे । वन षण सम्भक्तौ । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् ॥८॥

draviṇodā devo no 'smabhyaṃ vasūni dhanāni dadātu | yāni dhanāni śṛṇvire havir-upayuktatvena śrūyante [?] | tāni ca sarvāṇi dhanāni deveṣu nimitta-bhūteṣu vanāmahe | sambhajāmaḥ | dhanair devān yaṣṭuṃ tāni svīkurma ity arthaḥ || draviṇodāḥ | gatam | vasūni | śṛ-spṛ-snihī-ty-ādinā | u. [1-11] | u-pratyayaḥ | nid ity anuvṛtter ādyudāttaḥ | śṛṇvire | śru śravaṇe | chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭa iti vartamāne liṭ | jha ireč | pā. [3-4-81] | chandasy ubhayatheti sārvadhātukatve vyatyayena śnuḥ | tas-saṃniyogena śṛbhāvaś ca | uvaṅaḥ prāpte hu-śnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke | pā. [6-4-87] | iti yaṇādeśaḥ | cita ity antodāttatvam | yad-vṛttān nityam iti nighāta-pratiṣedhaḥ | tā | śeś chandasi bahulam iti śer lopaḥ | nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya | pā. [8-2-7] | iti nalopaḥ | vanāmahe | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | vyatyayenātmanepadam ||8||

Translation: "May the god Draviṇodā give us the vasūni — the riches — which are heard of (śṛṇvire) [as useful for the oblation]. And all those riches we accept (vanāmahe, 'we enjoy, we take') for the gods, who are the occasion: the sense is that we take them for the purpose of sacrificing to the gods with riches." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: vasūni (the Uṇādi u suffix; first-syllable accent); śṛṇvire (śru with liṭ in the present sense, jha → ire by P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec, śnu inserted by vyatyaya, śṛ for śru, and y for u by P. 6-4-87; accent on the last syllable because of the c; no loss of accent despite the relative yāni); tā (śas → śi with śi's drop, n-drop by P. 8-2-7); vanāmahe (vana "to love, to serve"; ātmanepada by vyatyaya). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 8-2-7 and P. 3-4-81 agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 658–659), noted briefly. Draviṇodāḥ was explained in the preceding mantra. Vasūni — vas "to dwell" with the Uṇādi u (Uṇ. 1-10 śvāsyu-snihi-trapy-asi-vasi-hani-klidi-bandhi-manibhyaś ca; nit carries over, so the suffix is eternal; first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam). Śṛṇvire — śru + liṭ (P. 3-4-6) + jha; P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec; P. 3-4-117 chandasy ubhayathā makes the suffix sārvadhātuka too; śruvaḥ śṛ ca P. 3-1-74 gives śṛ and śnu together; the iṅ-uvaṅ P. 6-4-77 aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau would apply, but it is barred in favour of hu-śnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke P. 6-4-87 yaṇ; and kvit the n → ṇ by P. 8-4-1 raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade; the accent on the last by cit P. 6-1-163; the verb is not unaccented, by yadvṛttān nityam P. 8-1-66 [as read]. Tā — tad + śas, the d → a by P. 7-2-102 tyadādīnām aḥ, ato guṇe P. 6-1-97, jaśśasoḥ śiḥ P. 7-1-20, śi sarvanāmasthānam P. 1-1-42, num augment by P. 7-1-72 napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ, lengthening by P. 6-4-8, śeś chandasi bahulam P. 6-1-70, n-drop P. 8-2-7. Vanāmahe — vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; the vyatyayo bahulam (P. 3-1-85) ātmanepada and the long discussion of the word upagraha in the Kārikā supy-… upagraha, in which parasmaipada and ātmanepada are the two; so vyatyaya of the voices can occur; the verb unaccented by P. 8-1-28.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ) — the god (Agni) who gives wealth | यानि (yāni) — which riches | शृण्विरे (śṛṇvire) — are known (heard) as useful for the oblation | ता वसूनि (tā vasūni) — those riches | नः (naḥ) — to us | ददातु (dadātu) — let him give | ता (tā) — all those riches | देवेषु (deveṣu) — for the sake of the gods | वनामहे (vanāmahe) — we accept.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We seek wealth for the sake of rites such as the sacrifice to the gods. May Agni, the giver of wealth, graciously give us all the riches that are well known to be fit for these rites.

॥ English Translation ॥

May Dravinodas give us riches that may be heard of; we ask them towards the service of the gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

यानि शृण्विरे (yāni śṛṇvire) — all such objects as we have heard have the various kinds of wealth and lordship. Since the rik says "deveṣu tā vanāmahe", those objects must be fit to be offered to the gods; therefore the commentator says they are objects "useful for giving oblation".

original pp. 659–663

Sūkta 15, Rik 9

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदाः पिपीषति जुहोत प्र च तिष्ठत । नेष्ट्राद्ऋतुभिरिष्यत ॥९॥

draviṇodāḥ pipīṣati juhota pra ca tiṣṭhata | neṣṭrād ṛtubhir iṣyata ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्रविणःऽदाः । पिपीषति । जुहोत । प्र । च । तिष्ठत ॥ नेष्ट्रात् । ऋतुऽभिः । इष्यत ॥९॥

draviṇaḥ-dāḥ | pipīṣati | juhota | pra | ca | tiṣṭhata || neṣṭrāt | ṛtu-bhiḥ | iṣyata ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

द्रविणोदा देव ऋतुभिः सह नेष्ट्रान्नेष्टृसम्बन्धिपात्रात्पिपीषति । सोमं पातुमिच्छति । ततो हे ऋत्विज इष्यत । होमस्थाने गच्छत । गत्वा च जुहोत । हुत्वा प्र तिष्ठत च । होमस्थानात्स्वस्थानान्तरं प्रति प्रस्थानमपि कुरुत ॥ द्रविणोदाः । गतम् । पिपीषति । पा पाने । पातुमिच्छतीति सन् । छान्दस ईकारः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । जुहोत । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनम् । तस्य लङ्वद्भावात्तादेशः । तस्य तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तबादेशः । तस्य पित्त्वाद्गुणः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्यनुवृत्तावनुदात्ते च । पा. [६-१-१८९] । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते भीह्रीभृहुमदजनधनदरिद्राजागराम् प्रत्ययात्पूर्वं पिति । पा. [६-१-१९२] । इत्योकार उदात्तः । तिष्ठत । ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनस्य थस्य लङ्वद्भावात्तादेशः । शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना तिष्ठादेशः । समवप्रविभ्यः स्थः । पा. [१-३-२२] । इत्यात्मनेपदं न भवति । तत्रानुवृत्तस्य निर्दिष्टग्रहणस्यानन्तर्यार्थत्वात् । अत्र चशब्देन व्यवधानात् ते प्रागाङ्कोः । पा. [१-४-८०] । इत्युपसर्गत्वेन प्राक्प्रयोक्तव्यस्यापि प्रशब्दस्य व्यवहिताश्चेति छन्दसि व्यवहितप्रयोगः । अत्र चशब्दो जुहोतेति पूर्वेण सह समुच्चयार्थः । न पुनरिष्यतेत्युत्तरेण । तेनाप्रथमत्वाच्चेनायोगे प्रथमा । पा. [८-१-३६] । इति निषेधाभावात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । नेष्ट्रात् । पोत्राद्यज्ञं पुनीतन । ऋग्वेदे [१-१५-२] इत्यत्र पोत्रशब्देन यदुक्तं तदत्र द्रष्टव्यम् । इष्यत । इष गतौ । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनम् ॥९॥

draviṇodā deva ṛtubhiḥ saha neṣṭrān neṣṭṛ-sambandhi-pātrāt pipīṣati | somaṃ pātum icchati | tato he ṛtvija iṣyata | homa-sthāne gacchata | gatvā ca juhota | hutvā pra tiṣṭhata ca | homa-sthānāt sva-sthānāntaraṃ prati prasthānam api kuruta || draviṇodāḥ | gatam | pipīṣati | pā pāne | pātum icchatīti san | chāndasa īkāraḥ | tiṅ ataṅ iti nighātaḥ | juhota | loṇ-madhyama-bahuvacanam | tasya laṅvad-bhāvāt tādeśaḥ | tasya tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ceti tabādeśaḥ | tasya pittvād guṇaḥ | abhyastānām ādir ity anuvṛttāv anudātte ca | pā. [6-1-189] | ity ādyudāttatve prāpte bhī-hrī-bhṛ-hu-mada-jana-dhana-daridrā-jāgarām pratyayāt pūrvaṃ piti | pā. [6-1-192] | ity okāra udāttaḥ | tiṣṭhata | ṣṭhā gati-nivṛttau | loṇ-madhyama-bahuvacanasya thasya laṅvad-bhāvāt tādeśaḥ | śapi pā-ghrety-ādinā tiṣṭhādeśaḥ | sam-ava-pra-vibhyaḥ sthaḥ | pā. [1-3-22] | ity ātmanepadaṃ na bhavati | tatrānuvṛttasya nirdiṣṭa-grahaṇasyānantaryārthatvāt | atra ca-śabdena vyavadhānāt te prāg āṅkoḥ | pā. [1-4-80] | ity upasargatvena prākprayoktavyasyāpi pra-śabdasya vyavahitāś ceti chandasi vyavahita-prayogaḥ | atra ca-śabdo juhoteti pūrveṇa saha samuccayārthaḥ | na punar iṣyatety uttareṇa | tenāprathamatvāc cenāyoge prathamā | pā. [8-1-36] | iti niṣedhābhāvāt tiṅ ataṅ iti nighātaḥ | neṣṭrāt | potrād yajñaṃ punītana | ṛgvede [1-15-2] ity atra potra-śabdena yad uktaṃ tad atra draṣṭavyam | iṣyata | iṣa gatau | loṇ-madhyama-bahuvacanam ||9||

Translation: "The god Draviṇodā, together with the Ṛtus, wishes (pipīṣati) to drink from the vessel (neṣṭrāt) belonging to the Neṣṭṛ priest. He wishes to drink the soma. Therefore, O priests, go (iṣyata) — go to the place of the oblation; having gone, offer the oblation (juhota); having offered, depart (pra tiṣṭhata) from the oblation-place to another place of your own." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: pipīṣati (pā "to drink", desiderative san, the Vedic long ī, the verb unaccented); juhota (loṭ middle plural, tas-substitute, śap's luk by juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ, reduplication, the accent on the o before the pit suffix by P. 6-1-192); tiṣṭhata (sthā "to stop going" with tiṣṭha by pāghrādhmā; P. 1-3-22 samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ, which would give the middle voice after pra, does not apply because the particle ca separates pra from the verb; the separated use of pra [P. 1-4-80, with vyavahitāś ca in the Veda]; the ca joins juhota and tiṣṭhata, not iṣyata; the verb is not unaccented because it is not the first of the pair and ca is connected: P. 8-1-36 ceda·yoge prathamā); neṣṭrāt (as for potrāt in Rik 2); iṣyata (iṣ "to go", loṭ middle plural; the yan). Grammar, noted briefly; the Pāṇini numbers as read; the standard numbers of 1-3-22, 1-4-80, 8-1-36 [?] agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 661–663), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats draviṇodāḥ (explained at the Rik 7); pipīṣati — pā with the desiderative san (P. 3-1-7 dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā), pā+sa doubled by P. 6-1-9 sanyaṅoḥ, the reduplicative vowel shortened by P. 7-4-59 hrasvaḥ, sanyataḥ P. 7-4-79 giving i; ī in the Veda; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59; verb unaccented by P. 8-1-28. Juhota — hu "to give, to offer", the juhotyādi class, loṭ, tha → ta, loṭo laṅvat P. 3-4-85, tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ P. 3-4-101, tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ca P. 7-1-45, śap with śluḥ P. 2-4-75, doubling by P. 6-1-10 ślau, hu → juhu, the h of hu → j by P. 7-4-62 kuhoś cuḥ, the u of hu → o by guṇa P. 7-3-84, the tha being pit by P. 1-2-4 sārvadhātukam apit making it ñit — hence no guṇa by kṅiti ca; the accent by P. 6-1-189 abhyastānām ādiḥ superseded by P. 6-1-192 bhī-hrī-bhṛ-hu-mad-jana-dhana-daridrā-jāgarāṃ pratyayāt pūrvaṃ pit, the o before the pit-suffix is accented. Tiṣṭhata — ṣṭhā, dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; tiṣṭha for sthā by P. 7-3-78; the discussion of P. 1-3-22 samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ and of the paribhāṣā that a rule stating a case in the fifth is to be applied only when the next item immediately follows (tasmād ity uttarasya P. 1-1-67), hence with ca intervening no ātmanepada; pra as an upasarga by P. 1-4-59 and P. 1-4-80 te prāg dhātoḥ (the Kannada gives the numbers 1-4-80 and 1-4-59 as read), the separated use of gati-upasargas allowed in the Veda by vyavahitāś ca P. 1-4-82; ca joins the first two verbs and not iṣyata; the unaccented tiṅ after ca by cavāyoge prathamā P. 8-1-59 [as read]. Neṣṭrāt — as for potrāt in Rik 15.2 (print: "Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-2"). Iṣyata — iṣ "to go", divādi class, loṭ, tha → ta, loṭo laṅvat, tasthasthamipāṃ… P. 3-4-101 ta; śyan by P. 3-1-69 divādibhyaḥ śyan; wholly unaccented by P. 8-1-28. ॥9॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ) — Agni, the giver of wealth | ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ) — together with the Ṛtu-deities | नेष्ट्रात् (neṣṭrāt) — from the vessel of Neṣṭṛ | पिपीषति (pipīṣati) — he wishes to drink (the soma-juice); (therefore, O priests) | इष्यत (iṣyata) — go [to the sacrificial place] | जुहोत (juhota) — make the oblation, and [afterwards] | प्र तिष्ठत च (pra tiṣṭhata ca) — leave the homa-place and go to your own places.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O priests! Agni, the giver of wealth, who is himself a deity, wishes to drink the soma from the vessel of Neṣṭṛ. Therefore all of you come to the place of sacrifice, make the oblation, and afterwards depart.

॥ English Translation ॥

Dravinodas desires to drink with the Ritu's from the cup of Neshtri; hasten, priests, present the oblation and depart.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

पिपीषति (pipīṣati) — pā pāne; pātum icchati: he wishes to drink; he desires to drink.

नेष्ट्रात् (neṣṭrāt) — the soma-juice from the vessel in the hand of the priest called Neṣṭṛ.

original pp. 663–666

Sūkta 15, Rik 10

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्त्वा तुरीयमृतुभिर्द्रविणोदो यजामहे । अध स्मा नो ददिर्भव ॥१०॥

yat tvā turīyam ṛtubhir draviṇodo yajāmahe | adha smā no dadir bhava ||10||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened smā; the Pada the short sma.

यत् । त्वा । तुरीयम् । ऋतुऽभिः । द्रविणःऽदः । यजामहे ॥ अध । स्म । नः । ददिः । भव ॥१०॥

yat | tvā | turīyam | ṛtu-bhiḥ | draviṇaḥ-daḥ | yajāmahe || adha | sma | naḥ | dadiḥ | bhava ||10||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे द्रविणोदो देव यद्यस्मात्कारणादृतुभिः सह त्वां यजामहे । अधेत्ययं निपातस्तच्छब्दार्थः । तस्मात्कारणान्नोऽस्मभ्यं ददिर्धनस्य दाता भव स्म । अवश्यं भव । तुरीयं चतुर्णां पूरणम् । तुरीयं । चतुरश्छयतावाद्यक्षरलोपश्च । पा. [५-२-५१] । इति भप्रत्ययः … [तस्य प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वात् …] इति वचनात्कृत आदेशे प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । द्रविणोदः । उक्तम् । पादादित्वादामन्त्रितस्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । यजामहे । अत्र शपः पित्त्वेन तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव । पूर्वस्यामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वाद्यद्वृत्तयोगाद्वा न निघातः । व्यवहितयोगेऽपि हि स इत्युक्तम् । अध । छान्दसो धकारः । स्म । चादिरनुदात्तः । संहितायां निपातस्य चेति दीर्घः । ददिः । डुदाञ् दाने । आदृगमहनजनः किकिनौ लिट् च । पा. [३-२-१७१] । इति किप्रत्ययः । लिड्वद्भावाद्द्विर्वचनादि । आतो लोप इटि च । पा. [६-४-६४] इत्याकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥१०॥

he draviṇodo deva yad yasmāt kāraṇād ṛtubhiḥ saha tvāṃ yajāmahe | adhety ayaṃ nipātas tacchabdārthaḥ | tasmāt kāraṇān no 'smabhyaṃ dadir dhanasya dātā bhava sma | avaśyaṃ bhava | turīyaṃ caturṇāṃ pūraṇam | turīyaṃ | caturaś chayatāv ādyakṣaralopaś ca | pā. [5-2-51] | iti bha-pratyayaḥ … [tasya pratyaya-svareṇodāttatvāt …] iti vacanāt kṛta ādeśe pratyaya-svareṇekāra udāttaḥ | draviṇodaḥ | uktam | pādāditvād āmantritasyādyudāttatvam | yajāmahe | atra śapaḥ pittvena tiṅaś ca lasārvadhātuka-svareṇa dhātu-svara eva | pūrvasyāmantritasyāvidyamānavatvād yad-vṛtta-yogād vā na nighātaḥ | vyavahita-yoge 'pi hi sa ity uktam | adha | chāndaso dhakāraḥ | sma | cādir anudāttaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ nipātasya ceti dīrghaḥ | dadiḥ | ḍudāñ dāne | ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca | pā. [3-2-171] | iti ki-pratyayaḥ | liḍ-vadbhāvād dvirvacanādi | āto lopa iṭi ca | pā. [6-4-64] ity ākāralopaḥ | pratyaya-svaraḥ ||10||

Translation: "O god Draviṇodas! Since (yat) we worship you together with the Ṛtus — adha, 'therefore' [the particle has the sense of tad] — be a giver (dadiḥ) of wealth to us (naḥ); bhava sma: be so without fail. Turīyam — the fourth [i.e. the fourth time, or the fourth rik: the filler of the number four]." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: turīyam (caturaś chayatāv ādyakṣaralopaś ca, P. 5-2-51 [as read; this is the standard numbering] — the suffix bha [read as chayat] and the dropping of the first syllable of catur; the suffix accent); draviṇodaḥ (explained earlier; the vocative at the start of the pāda has the first-syllable accent); yajāmahe (śap is pit, so the accent stays on the root; the preceding vocative treated as non-existent, or the relative yat prevents loss of accent); adha (a particle with Vedic dh); sma (a particle, unaccented; lengthened in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-136 nipātasya ca); dadiḥ (dā with the Uṇādi-type ki by P. 3-2-171 ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca, reduplicated as for a liṭ; ā-drop by P. 6-4-64; suffix accent).

Grammar pages (pp. 665–666), noted briefly. The Kannada says: turīyam = caturṇāṃ pūraṇam "the completer of four"; by P. 5-2-51 [as read] the suffixes chat and yat are added to catur in the sense of the ordinal, with the dropping of the first syllable of catur — the Kannada discusses what "first syllable" (ādyakṣara) is: not ca alone but the first consonant with the vowel; so catur loses ca — and tur + chat/yat with the substitute īya for cha by P. 7-1-2 āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām, whence tur + īya; the accent falls on the ī by the suffix accent; the Mahābhāṣya's ayanādiṣūpadeśivad-vacanaṃ svarasiddhyartham [Vārttika on the same sūtra]. Draviṇodaḥ — the derivation as in the Rik 7 and 8; a vocative at the start of the pāda is not made unaccented (P. 8-1-19 [?]) but takes the first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-198. Yajāmahe — yaj with laṭ, first person plural mahiṅ, śap, ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e P. 3-4-79 (e), ato dīrgho yañi P. 7-3-101; the verb is not made unaccented since draviṇodaḥ, the vocative before it, is treated as absent (P. 8-1-72) and the verb is at the start of a pāda (P. 8-1-19) — or by yadvṛttān nityam P. 8-1-66 because of yat; with a discussion of pūjanāt pūjitam (P. 8-1-67 [?]). Adha — the particle atha with the Vedic aspirate dh; first-syllable accent (Phiṭ 4-12 [?] nipātā ādyudāttāḥ). Sma — unaccented as a particle of the ca group (Phiṭ 4-[?] cādayo 'nudāttāḥ); the lengthened smā by P. 6-3-136 [? nipātasya ca]. Dadiḥ — ḍudāñ dāne; ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca P. 3-2-171 gives ki in the Vedic sense, treated as liṭ, hence doubling by P. 6-1-8 liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya, shortening by P. 7-4-59 hrasvaḥ, loss of ā before iṭ by P. 6-4-64 āto lopa iṭi ca; hence dadiḥ with suffix accent. ॥10॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदः (draviṇodaḥ) — O Agni, giver of wealth | यत् (yat) — because | ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ) — together with the Ṛtu-deities | तुरीयम् (turīyam) — [for] the fourth time | त्वा (tvā) — you | यजामहे (yajāmahe) — we worship | अध (adha) — therefore | नः (naḥ) — to us | ददिः (dadiḥ) — giver of wealth | भव स्म (bhava sma) — be, without fail.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni! We, desiring wealth, worship you together with the Ṛtu-deities, as the fourth [in the series]. Therefore accept our worship without fail, and be the giver of wealth to us.

॥ English Translation ॥

Dravinodas, Since we adore you for the fourth time along with the Ritus ; therefore be a giver (of riches) to us.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

तुरीयम् (turīyam) — "the fourth time". In this sūkta there are four riks in praise of Agni called Draviṇodā (the riks 7 to 10 of the sūkta); this is the fourth among them. Therefore turīyam here means "the fourth time", or "from the fourth rik we praise [you]".

original pp. 666–670

Sūkta 15, Rik 11

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अश्विना पिबतं मधु दीद्यग्नी शुचिव्रता । ऋतुना यज्ञवाहसा ॥११॥

aśvinā pibataṃ madhu dīdyagnī śucivratā | ṛtunā yajñavāhasā ||11||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अश्विना । पिबतम् । मधु । दीद्यग्नी इति दीदिऽअग्नी । शुचिऽव्रता ॥ ऋतुना । यज्ञऽवाहसा ॥११॥

aśvinā | pibatam | madhu | dīdyagnī iti dīdi-agnī | śuci-vratā || ṛtunā | yajña-vāhasā ||11||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अश्विनौ मधु माधुर्योपेतं सोमं पिबतम् । कीदृशौ । दीद्यग्नी द्योतमानाहवनीयाद्यग्नियुक्तौ शुचिव्रता शुद्धकर्माणौ ऋतुना ऋतुदेवतया सह यज्ञवाहसा यज्ञस्य निर्वाहकौ ॥ अश्विना । सम्बोधनद्विवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तः । पिबतम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । मधु । फलिपाटीत्यादिना । उ. [१-१८]। उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्णित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । दीद्यग्नी । दिवु क्रीडादौ । आन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते इति विच् । वेरपृक्तलोपाद्वलि लोपो बलीयान् इति प्रथमवकारस्य लोपः । पा. [६-१-६६, ६७] । प्रथमं प्रत्ययलोपे हि वर्णाश्रयविधौ प्रत्ययलक्षणं नास्ति … इति निषेधाद्वलिलोपो न स्यात् । छान्दसं द्विर्वचनम् । तुजादित्वादभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वम् । यज्ञलुगन्तताद्वा संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इत्यभ्यासस्य गुणाभावः । दीदिरग्निर्ययोस्तौ दीद्यग्नी । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । शुचिव्रता । शुचि व्रतं ययोस्तौ । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । दीद्यग्नीशब्दस्य सामान्यवचनत्वेन नामन्त्रित इत्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधाद्… । पूर्वस्य पराङ्गवद्भावात् … । यज्ञवाहसा । वह प्रापणे । यज्ञं वहत इति यज्ञवाहसौ । वहिहाधाङ्भ्यश्छन्दसि । उ. [४-२२०]। इत्यसुन् । तत्र हि गतिकारकोपपदात्कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं चेति वचनाल्लोपपदानामपि भवति । उ. [४-२१६]। इत्युक्तम् । जिदित्यनुवृत्तेरुपधावृद्धिः । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराकारः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । आसामर्थ्यात्पूर्वस्य न पराङ्गवद्भावः ॥११॥

he aśvinau madhu mādhuryopetaṃ somaṃ pibatam | kīdṛśau | dīdyagnī dyotamānāhavanīyādy-agni-yuktau śucivratā śuddha-karmāṇau ṛtunā ṛtu-devatayā saha yajñavāhasā yajñasya nirvāhakau || aśvinā | sambodhana-dvivacanasya supāṃ sulug ity ākāraḥ | āmantritādyudāttaḥ | pibatam | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | tiṅaś ca lasārvadhātuka-svareṇa dhātu-svara eva śiṣyate | madhu | phali-pāṭī-ty-ādinā | u. [1-18] | u-pratyayaḥ | nid ity anuvṛtter ṇittvād ādyudāttaḥ | dīdyagnī | divu krīḍādau | ānyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante iti vic | ver apṛkta-lopād vali lopo balīyān iti prathama-vakārasya lopaḥ | pā. [6-1-66, 67] | prathamaṃ pratyaya-lope hi varṇāśraya-vidhau pratyaya-lakṣaṇaṃ nāsti … iti niṣedhād vali-lopo na syāt | chāndasaṃ dvirvacanam | tujādittvād abhyāsasya dīrghatvam | yaja-luganta-tvād vā saṃjñā-pūrvako vidhir anitya ity abhyāsasya guṇābhāvaḥ | dīdir agnir yayos tau dīdyagnī | āmantritādyudāttatvam | pādāditvān na nighātaḥ | śucivratā | śuci vrataṃ yayos tau | supāṃ sulug ity ākāraḥ | dīdyagnī-śabdasya sāmānya-vacanatvena nāmantrita ity avidyamānavatva-pratiṣedhād … | pūrvasya parāṅgavad-bhāvāt … | yajñavāhasā | vaha prāpaṇe | yajñaṃ vahata iti yajñavāhasau | vahi-hā-dhāṅbhyaś chandasi | u. [4-220] | ity asun | tatra hi gati-kārakopapadāt kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ ceti vacanāl lopa-padānām api bhavati | u. [4-216] | ity uktam | jid ity anuvṛtter upadhā-vṛddhiḥ | supāṃ sulug ity-ādinā vibhakter ākāraḥ | āmantrita-nighātaḥ | āsāmarthyāt pūrvasya na parāṅgavad-bhāvaḥ ||11||

Translation: "O Aśvins! Drink the sweet (madhu, sweet-tasting) soma. Of what sort are you? Dīdyagnī — joined with the shining āhavanīya and other fires; śucivratā — of pure works; yajñavāhasā — together with the Ṛtu, the carriers (completers) of the sacrifice." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: aśvinā (the dual vocative with ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…; first-syllable accent of the vocative); pibatam (śap pit, unaccented; the root accent remains); madhu (the Uṇādi u suffix, first-syllable accent); dīdyagnī (div "to play" with vic, doubling of the verb stem in the Veda; the first v dropped; the compound "those whose fire is shining"; the vocative at the start of a pāda is not unaccented); śucivratā ("those whose vow is pure"; the ā ending for the dual vocative); yajñavāhasā (vah "to carry", Uṇ. 4-220 vahi-hā-dhāṅbhyaś chandasi with asun; the lengthening of the penultimate by ñit-ness; the accent of the compound that of the final member; the vocative unaccented as not first in the pāda). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 6-1-66 and 6-1-67 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 668 lower half–670), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: aśvinā (P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…, ā for the dual vocative; accent by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca; P. 8-1-18/19 does not apply, since it stands at the head of the pāda); pibatam (pā; loṭ 2nd dual thas; loṭo laṅvat P. 3-4-85; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ P. 3-4-101: thas → tam; śap P. 3-1-68; pāghrādhmā… P. 7-3-78: piba; ato guṇe P. 6-1-97 pararūpa: pibatam, with a note on the alternative view that piba is an ādyudātta nipātana in the sūtra — Vārttika pibāv ānipātanāt — and the debate over the accent of pibā-; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca P. 7-3-86 not applying; dhātoḥ P. 6-1-162 ending-accent; the rule aṅgavṛtte punar vṛttāv avidhiḥ (paribhāṣā) so the guṇa does not apply after piba-substitution; "the accent of the root alone remains, so the Vedabhāṣya says"; śap pit unaccented, the suffix tam a lasārvadhātuka unaccented by tāsyanudāttenṇiḍ-adupadeśāt P. 6-1-186 [as read]); madhu ("madhumantam", see Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-?-? in the earlier part, where the process is explained; here man "to know" with the Uṇādi u — phali-pāṭi-… Uṇ. 1-18 [?], nit so first-syllable accent); dīdyagnī (div "to play", with the suffixes manin, kvanip, vanip, vic which are added after the root div in the Veda, by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; div + vic with ver apṛktasya P. 6-1-67 dropping vi's v, and lopo vyor vali P. 6-1-66 dropping the v of div: the rule that [the dropping of the first v by the ver apṛktasya rule takes precedence], argued in detail by the paribhāṣā "varṇāśraye nāsti pratyayalakṣaṇam"; the Vedic doubling didiv with tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya P. 6-1-7 lengthening dīdi; or alternatively from div with yaṅ P. 3-1-22 dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ and its luk P. 2-4-74 [yaṅo vā], then sanyaṅoḥ P. 6-1-9, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60, and guṇo yaṅluk-ṛnoḥ P. 7-4-82 whose guṇa is barred by the paribhāṣā saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ; dīrgho 'kitaḥ P. 7-4-83 lengthening the reduplicative; "dīdiḥ agniḥ yayoḥ tau — a bahuvrīhi; the vocative accent on the first syllable; not unaccented by P. 8-1-19 as it begins the pāda"); śucivratā (śuci vrataṃ yayoḥ tau; the dual vocative ā by P. 7-1-39; the grammarian's discussion of whether dīdyagnī and śucivratā, both vocatives, are connected by sense with aśvinā, by P. 8-1-73 nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam [as read] and P. 8-1-72 āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat and P. 8-1-74 [?] supāmantrite parāṅgavat svare — the Kannada concludes that dīdyagnī and śucivratā are adjectives of aśvinā and aśvinā is the general term, so P. 8-1-73's bar applies and P. 8-1-72 does not make dīdyagnī ... unaccented; the whole is treated as one word, so śucivratā has the first-syllable accent only and the others are all-unaccented by anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam P. 6-1-158, with svarita from udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ P. 8-4-66 and the pracaya of svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām P. 1-2-39); yajñavāhasā (yajñaṃ vahataḥ; vah; Uṇ. 4-220 vahi-hā-dhāṅbhyaś chandasi asun; the compound accent by Uṇ. 4-216; P. 7-2-116 ata upadhāyāḥ for the ā; ñit; the vocative dual ending au → ā by P. 7-1-39; accent by P. 8-1-72: the preceding word ṛtunā does not become parāṅgavat, since P. 8-1-74 supāmantrite parāṅgavat svare does not apply here, as the two words have no mutual connexion; the wholly unaccented yajñavāhasā by P. 8-1-19). ॥11॥ A long, crowded grammatical argument about the accent of the cluster aśvinā … dīdyagnī śucivratā … ṛtunā yajñavāhasā; Its outline only is given, with numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

दीद्यग्नी (dīdyagnī) — those shining with the āhavanīya and other fires | शुचिव्रता (śucivratā) — whose works are pure | ऋतुना (ṛtunā) — together with the Ṛtu-deity | यज्ञवाहसा (yajña-vāhasā) — the carriers of the sacrifice | अश्विना (aśvinā) — O Aśvin-deities | मधु (madhu) — the sweet soma-juice | पिबतम् (pibatam) — drink.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Aśvins! You are ever shining with the āhavanīya and other fires; together with the Ṛtu-deity you carry through the sacrifice. Be pleased to drink the sweet soma-juice.

॥ English Translation ॥

Aswins, performers of pious acts, accepters of the sacrifice with the Ritus, and accompanied by brilliant Agni, drink the sweet draught.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

दीद्यग्नी (dīdyagnī) — divu krīḍādau; dīdir agnir yayos tau: "shining" — because the offerings for the Aśvin deities are made in the āhavanīya and other fires, they are said to be possessed of shining fire.

शुचिव्रता (śucivratā) — śuci vrataṃ yayos tau: "having pure works", that is, the works done by them are pure.

यज्ञवाहसा (yajña-vāhasā) — vaha prāpaṇe: yajñaṃ vahata iti yajñavāhasau: yajñasya nirvāhakau: "those who carry the sacrifice through" — who make it proceed without obstacle.

original pp. 671–676

Sūkta 15, Rik 12 (last rik of the sūkta)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

गार्हपत्येन सन्त्य ऋतुना यज्ञनीरसि । देवान्देवयते यज ॥१२॥

gārhapatyena santya ṛtunā yajñanīr asi | devān devayate yaja ||12||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

गार्हऽपत्येन । सन्त्य । ऋतुना । यज्ञऽनीः । असि ॥ देवान् । देवऽयते । यज ॥१२॥

gārha-patyena | santya | ṛtunā | yajña-nīḥ | asi || devān | deva-yate | yaja ||12||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे सन्त्य फलप्रदाग्निदेव गार्हपत्येन गृहपतिसम्बन्धिना रूपेण युक्तः सन्नृतुना ऋतुदेवेन सह यज्ञनीर्यज्ञस्य निर्वाहकोऽसि । तस्मात्त्वं देवयते देवविषयकामनायुक्ताय यजमानाय देवान्यज ॥ गार्हपत्येन । गृहपतिना संयुक्ते ञ्यः । पा. [४-४-९०] । यस्येति लोपः । ञित्त्वादादिवृद्धिराद्युदात्तत्वं च । गृहपतित्वमित्यर्थे पत्न्यन्तपुरोहितादिभ्यो यक् । पा. [५-१-१२८ ?] । इति यकि त्वन्तोदात्तत्वं स्यात् [?] । सन्त्य । सननं भवे [?] षणु दाने । क्रिच्क्तौ चेति क्रिच् । न क्रिचि दीर्घश्च । पा. [६-४-३९ ?] । इति दीर्घानुलोपाभावः । भवे छन्दसि । पा. [४-४-११०] । इति यत् । तत्र साधुः । पा. [४-४-९८] । इति वा । निघातः । यज्ञं नयतीति यज्ञनीः । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । देवयते । देवानात्मन इच्छतीति देवयन् । तस्मै । क्यचि च ईत्वं न भवति । न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्येति निषेधात् । अश्वाघस्य । पा. [७-४-३७] । इत्यात्वविधानादीत्वनिषेधे प्राप्तस्य दीर्घस्यैष निषेध इत्युक्तम् । शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अत्र क्यचि [?] … अन्तोदात्तत्वम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणोभयोः … एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । तस्मादन्तोदात्तत्वात्परस्या विभक्तेः शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इत्युदात्तत्वम् ॥१२॥

he santya phala-pradāgni-deva gārhapatyena gṛhapati-sambandhinā rūpeṇa yuktaḥ sann ṛtunā ṛtu-devena saha yajña-nīr yajñasya nirvāhako 'si | tasmāt tvaṃ devayate deva-viṣaya-kāmanā-yuktāya yajamānāya devān yaja || gārhapatyena | gṛhapatinā saṃyukte ñyaḥ | pā. [4-4-90] | yasyeti lopaḥ | ñittvād ādi-vṛddhir ādyudāttatvaṃ ca | gṛhapatitvam ity arthe patny-anta-purohitādibhyo yak | pā. [5-1-128 ?] | iti yaki tv antodāttatvaṃ syāt [?] | santya | sananaṃ bhave [?] ṣaṇu dāne | kric-ktau ceti kric | na kṛci dīrghaś ca | pā. [6-4-39 ?] | iti dīrghānulopābhāvaḥ | bhave chandasi | pā. [4-4-110] | iti yat | tatra sādhuḥ | pā. [4-4-98] | iti vā | nighātaḥ | yajñaṃ nayatīti yajñanīḥ | sat-sūdviṣety-ādinā kvip | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaraḥ | devayate | devān ātmana icchatīti devayan | tasmai | kyaci ca ītvaṃ na bhavati | na chandasy aputrasyeti niṣedhāt | aśvāghasya | pā. [7-4-37] | ity ātva-vidhānād ītva-niṣedhe prāptasya dīrghasyaiṣa niṣedha ity uktam | śatur anumo nady-ajādī iti vibhakter udāttatvam | atra kyaci [?] … antodāttatvam | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | śatuś ca lasārvadhātuka-svareṇobhayoḥ … ekādeśa udāttenodātta ity udāttaḥ | tasmād antodāttatvāt parasyā vibhakteḥ śatur anumo nady-ajādī ity udāttatvam ||12||

Translation: "O santya — O Agni, god who gives the fruit [of rites]! Joined to the form belonging to the master of the house — the gārhapatya fire — and together with the Ṛtu-god, you are the yajña-nīḥ, the one who carries the sacrifice through. Therefore, for the sacrificer who desires the gods (devayate), sacrifice to (yaja; "bring") the gods." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: gārhapatyena (ñya by P. 4-4-90 gṛhapatinā saṃyukte ñyaḥ — "joined with the gṛhapati"; the ñ gives vṛddhi of the first syllable and first-syllable accent; the alternative yak by P. 5-1-128 [?] would give end accent, which is why the ñya is preferred); santya (ṣaṇu "to give"; kric; yat "born in, good in" by P. 4-4-110 bhave chandasi or P. 4-4-98 tatra sādhuḥ); yajñanīḥ (nī + kvip after yajñam; final accent); devayate (devān ātmana icchati, with kyac P. 3-1-8, and śatṛ; the lengthening of the a of deva before kyac is barred by P. 7-4-35 na chandasy aputrasya; the ā of aśvāghasya P. 7-4-37 is cited in the argument; the end accent of the ending by P. 6-1-173 śatur anumo nady-ajādī). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 4-4-90, 4-4-110 and 4-4-98 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 673–676), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats: gārhapatyena (P. 4-4-90 gṛhapatinā saṃyukte ñyaḥ; the suffix ñya is added after gṛhapati in the sense "joined with" in a case-ending of the third case; gṛhapati + ṭā + ñya, cuṭū P. 1-3-7 for the ñ, tasya lopaḥ P. 1-3-9; the sup dropped by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ P. 2-4-71; yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ P. 7-2-117 vṛddhi; ur aṇ raparaḥ P. 1-1-51; gārhapatya; the accent by ñnityādir nityam P. 6-1-197 first-syllable; then a discussion of the alternative yak by P. 5-1-128 patny-anta-purohitādibhyo yak in the sense "being a gṛhapati", which would give gārhapatya with the end accent — so P. 4-4-90 is the one applied); santya (ṣaṇu dāne with kric, P. 3-3-174 kric kto ca saṃjñāyām [as read], dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; sanoti — san + ti → santi — na kṛci dīrghaś ca P. 6-4-39 [as read] and the Kannada's detailed argument on the rules anunāsikasya kvijhaloḥ kṅiti P. 6-4-15, anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanoty-ādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti P. 6-4-37, jit ... naklījit... dīrghaś ca [as read]; saneḥ kṛci lopaś cāsyānyatarasyām [as read, P. 6-4-42 in the standard numbering is janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ]; the concluding view that the n and the ā are both optionally dropped, so santi arises from the kric either way — the Mahābhāṣya's sarvavidhāyaṃ yogaḥ is cited with Kaiyaṭa's sanaḥ kṛci ity eva lopasya prakaraṇāt siddhatvāl lope [vā] ity api na vaktavyam; then santyam "that which is born in santi" by P. 4-4-110 bhave chandasi with yat, or tatra sādhuḥ P. 4-4-98; yasyeti ca; santya, in the vocative singular, with the end accent by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca and made unaccented as a vocative within the pāda by P. 8-1-19); yajñanīḥ (yajñam nayati; the list of roots after which kvip is added in the Veda, sat-sūdviṣa-druha-duha-yuja-vida-bhida-chida-jī-nī-rājām upasarge 'pi kvip P. 3-2-61, with a long grammarians' note on which of these roots in the ādādika class etc.; ṇ for n by P. 6-1-65 ṇo naḥ; the accent of the compound that of the final member by P. 6-2-139; the nominative ending dropped; ru → visarga; yajñanīḥ); devayate (devān ātmana icchati, "one who wishes the gods for himself" — supa ātmanaḥ kyac P. 3-1-8, then the root-name by P. 3-1-32 sanādyantā dhātavaḥ, the sup dropped by P. 2-4-71, deva + ya; the ī-substitute by P. 7-4-33 kyaci ca barred by P. 7-4-35 na chandasy aputrasya, for a stem not ending in putra; the further argument — a long scholastic debate whether P. 7-4-35 bars only the ī or also the lengthening of P. 7-4-25 akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ, with the paribhāṣā anantarasya vidhir vā bhavati pratiṣedho vā; the proof from P. 7-4-37 aśvāghasyāt — hence devayat by śatṛ P. 3-2-124 laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe [as read, P. 3-2-124 laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau]; śap; ato guṇe P. 6-1-97 pararūpa; the accent of the suffix kyac [cit P. 6-1-163] being final on ya, and the śatṛ ending accented by P. 6-1-173 śatur anumo nady-ajādī, so that the ending e of the dative singular is accented). ॥12॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सन्त्य (santya) — O Agni, capable of giving the fruit [of rites] | गार्हपत्येन (gārhapatyena) — joined with the gārhapatya fire | ऋतुना (ṛtunā) — together with the Ṛtu-deity | यज्ञनीः (yajña-nīḥ) — the carrier-through of the sacrifice | असि (asi) — you are | देवयते (devayate) — [therefore] for the sacrificer who desires the gods | देवान् (devān) — the gods | यज (yaja) — worship (propitiate).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni! You are the giver of what is wished for. Joined to the gārhapatya fire, together with the Ṛtu-deity, you carry through the sacrificial work of the sacrificer. Therefore, perform the sacrifice for the sacrificer who always desires the sacrifice to the gods.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, giver of rewards, being the lord of the house, and partaker with Ritu of the sacrifice, perform the sacrifice on behalf of the worshipper.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सन्त्य (santya) — ṣaṇu dāne (root san "to give"); sanane bhava: so the word santya, formed from this root, means "giver". Giver of what? One who gives the fruit of sacrificial rites; or, as in words like ratnadhātamam, one who gives wealth and lordship.

यज्ञनीः (yajña-nīḥ) — yajñaṃ nayati iti yajñanīḥ; yajñasya nirvāhakaḥ: one who carries the sacrifice through.

देवयते (devayate) — devān ātmana icchati iti devayan, tasmai yajamānāya: for the sacrificer who, for the sacrifice he performs, wishes the gods to come.

Close of Sūkta 15. The grammar of Rik 12 ends on p. 676 (upper part), after which the ornament and the heading of the sixteenth sūkta appear; the print again has no large closing colophon.

॥ ಹದಿನಾರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 16 — "ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ" ("The Sixteenth Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 676, lower half)

आ त्वा वहन्त्विति पञ्चमेमं नवर्चं सूक्तम् । ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । अनुविवर्ते विशेषादेशाभावादिन्द्रो देवता ॥ विनियोगस्तु । प्रातःसवने मैत्रावरुणस्योन्नीयमाने सूक्तमात्वा वहन्तु हरय इति ॥ तथा च द्विदेवत्यैः क्रश्नन्तीति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । उन्नीयमानेभ्योऽन्नाहा त्वावहन्तु । आ. [५-३-?] इति ॥ तथा षोडशिशस्त्र आ त्वा वहन्तु हरय इति तिस्रः । तथा सूत्रितमथ षोडशीति खण्डे । आ त्वा वहन्तु हरय इति तिस्रो गायत्र्यः । आ. [६-२-?] इति ॥

ā tvā vahantv iti pañcamemaṃ navarcaṃ sūktam | ṛṣi-chandasī pūrvavat | anuvivarte viśeṣādeśābhāvād indro devatā || viniyogas tu | prātaḥsavane maitrāvaruṇasyonnīyamāne sūktam ātvā vahantu haraya iti || tathā ca dvidevatyaiḥ kraśnantīti khaṇḍe sūtritam | unnīyamānebhyo 'nnāhā tvāvahantu | ā. [5-3-?] iti || tathā ṣoḍaśiśastra ā tvā vahantu haraya iti tisraḥ | tathā sūtritam atha ṣoḍaśīti khaṇḍe | ā tvā vahantu haraya iti tisro gāyatryaḥ | ā. [6-2-?] iti ||

Translation: "The nine-rik sūkta beginning ā tvā vahantu is the fifth [of this anuvāka]. Its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. Since no special deity is stated, the deity of the continuing [section] is Indra. Its application: at the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana), when the Maitrāvaruṇa priest is having the soma drawn up (unnayana), the sūkta ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ is recited. And so it is laid down in the Sūtra, in the section beginning dvidevatyaiḥ kraśnanti: 'for those [cups] being drawn up, ā tvā vahantu' (Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra 5-3-[?], the last numeral not read). Likewise, in the ṣoḍaśi-śastra, the three riks ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ are used; and it is laid down in the section beginning atha ṣoḍaśī: 'the three Gāyatrīs ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ' (Āś. 6-2-[?])." The Sanskrit phrases unnīyamānebhyo 'nnāhā tvāvahantu and the Sūtra numerals are as read from the print and are uncertain [?].

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The sūkta ā tvā vahantu, with nine riks, is the fifth sūkta of the fourth anuvāka. The ṛṣi and meter are as in the earlier sūktas; the deity is Indra. Application: at the morning pressing, in the rite called unnayana done by the priest named Maitrāvaruṇa, this sūkta is to be recited. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra says in the section dvidevatyaiḥ kraśnanti that for the unnayana the sūkta ā tvā vahantu is to be used (Āś. Sū. 5-3 [?]). Moreover, in the section ṣoḍaśī, for the ṣoḍaśi-śastra recitation the tṛca [three riks] of this sūkta beginning ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ is to be recited, as the same Sūtra says (Āś. Sū. 6-2).

original p. 677

Sūkta 16, Rik 1

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 16 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 4 ॥ Sūkta — 16 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 30, 31 [?] ॥ small-print Kannada digits; the digit glyphs 2/3 are hard to tell apart in this print, so this is unreliable ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–9 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indra ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ त्वा वहन्तु हरयो वृषणं सोमपीतये । इन्द्र त्वा सूरचक्षसः ॥१॥

ā tvā vahantu harayo vṛṣaṇaṃ somapītaye | indra tvā sūracakṣasaḥ ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks are printed in the source; not reproduced, per the convention for the later riks of this volume.

आ । त्वा । वहन्तु । हरयः । वृषणम् । सोमऽपीतये ॥ इन्द्र । त्वा । सूरऽचक्षसः ॥१॥

ā | tvā | vahantu | harayaḥ | vṛṣaṇam | soma-pītaye || indra | tvā | sūra-cakṣasaḥ ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ compressed; [?] marks doubtful readings

हे इन्द्र वृषणं कामानां वर्षितारं त्वां सोमपीतये सोमपानार्थं हरयस्त्वदीया अश्वा आ वहन्तु । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यानयन्तु । तथा सूरचक्षसः सूर्यसमानप्रकाशयुक्ता ऋत्विजस्त्वां मन्त्रैः प्रकाशयन्तीति शेषः ॥ हरन्तीति हरयः । इन् सर्वधातुभ्यः । उ. [४-११८] । इतीन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वृषणम् । कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः । उ. [१-१५६] । इति कनिन् । कित्त्वाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । वा षपूर्वस्य निगमे । पा. [६-४-९] । इति विकल्पितमुपधादीर्घत्वम् । सोमपीतये । ऐभिरग्न इत्येत्रोक्तम् । ऋग्वेदे [१-१४-१] । सूरचक्षसः । चक्षिङ् व्यक्तायां वाचि । सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् । चक्षिङः ख्याञ् । पा. [२-४-५४] । इति न भवति । आनसोः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्य इति निषेधात् । सू प्रेरणे । सुवतीति सूरः । सुसूधागृधिभ्यः क्रन् । उ. [२-२४] । इति क्रन् । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । नित्त्वरादाद्युदात्तः [?] । सूरवत्प्रकाशो येषाम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥१॥

he indra vṛṣaṇaṃ kāmānāṃ varṣitāraṃ tvāṃ somapītaye soma-pānārthaṃ harayas tvadīyā aśvā ā vahantu | asmin karmaṇy ānayantu | tathā sūracakṣasaḥ sūrya-samāna-prakāśa-yuktā ṛtvijas tvāṃ mantraiḥ prakāśayantīti śeṣaḥ || harantīti harayaḥ | in sarva-dhātubhyaḥ | u. [4-118] | itīn | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | vṛṣaṇam | kanin-yuvṛṣitakṣirāji-dhanvi-dyupratidivaḥ | u. [1-156] | iti kanin | kittvāl laghūpadha-guṇābhāvaḥ | vā ṣapūrvasya nigame | pā. [6-4-9] | iti vikalpitam upadhādīrghatvam | somapītaye | aibhir agna ity etrokam | ṛgvede [1-14-1] | sūracakṣasaḥ | cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ | pā. [2-4-54] | iti na bhavati | ānasoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavya iti niṣedhāt | sū preraṇe | suvatīti sūraḥ | susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran | u. [2-24] | iti kran | kittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | nittvarād ādyudāttaḥ [?] | sūravat prakāśo yeṣām | bahuvrīhau pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||1||

Translation: "O Indra! Let your horses (harayaḥ) bring you — the vṛṣan, the shower of desired things — for the drinking of the soma, to this rite; and let the sūracakṣasaḥ — priests who shine like the sun — [make you manifest] with mantras (the rest is supplied)." The grammar that follows, noted briefly: harayaḥ (hṛ "to carry", the Uṇādi in, first-syllable accent); vṛṣaṇam (vṛṣ "to shower", the Uṇādi kanin, no guṇa because the suffix has the indicatory k, the optional lengthening of the penultimate by P. 6-4-9 vā ṣapūrvasya nigame); somapītaye (explained at aibhir agne, Ṛ. 1-14-1); sūracakṣasaḥ (cakṣ "to speak clearly", Uṇādi asun; the substitute khyā of P. 2-4-54 does not apply, by the Vārttika barring it before āna and asun; sūra from sū "to impel", the Uṇādi kran; "those whose brilliance is like the sun's"; a bahuvrīhi with the accent of the first member). Grammar, noted briefly; the numeral of P. 2-4-54 as read agrees with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 678 lower half–679), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats harayaḥ (hṛñ haraṇe; sarvadhātubhya in Uṇ. 4-[?]; guṇa and raparatva by P. 7-3-84 and P. 1-1-51; first-syllable accent; the nominative plural jas, with the guṇa by P. 7-3-109 jasi ca [as read, 7-3-109]; eco 'yavāyāvaḥ P. 6-1-78 giving ay; the visarga), vṛṣaṇam (vṛṣu secane with the Uṇādi kanin, Uṇ. 1-[?]; kit, so no guṇa of the penultimate by P. 1-1-5 kṅiti ca — the guṇa that would come by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca P. 7-3-86 is therefore barred; accusative am; the optional lengthening by P. 6-4-8 [?] sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau and P. 6-4-9 vā ṣapūrvasya nigame — here, optional, taken as not applied; ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam [Vārttika on P. 8-4-1] giving ṇ: vṛṣaṇam); somapītaye (explained at 1.14.1); sūracakṣasaḥ (cakṣiṅ, the asun by Uṇ. 4-[?] sarvadhātubhyo 'sun being ārdhadhātuka, so P. 2-4-54 cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ would apply, but it is barred by the Vārttika ānasoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ [P. 2-4-54 Vārttika as read]; sū of the tudādi class — "he who impels people to action in the poems" — with the Uṇādi kran, Uṇ. 3-[?] susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran; kit so no guṇa by P. 1-1-5; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; the first-syllable accent from the n-mark; the bahuvrīhi by P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam). Numerals as read; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | वृषणम् (vṛṣaṇam) — [you] who shower (give) desired objects | त्वा (tvā) — you | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for the sake of drinking soma | हरयः (harayaḥ) — [your] horses | आ वहन्तु (ā vahantu) — let them bring (to this place where the rite is going on) | सूरचक्षसः (sūracakṣasaḥ) — priests radiant like the sun | त्वा (tvā) — you [let them praise].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! You are the giver of all desired things. The priests, radiant as the sun, praise you. Come with your horses to our sacrificial hall to drink the soma.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Indra, let your horses bring you, bestower of riches, to drink the Soma-Juice ; May the priests radiant as the Sun, praise you.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सूरचक्षसः (sūracakṣasaḥ) — sūrya-samāna-prakāśa-yuktāḥ ṛtvijas tvāṃ mantrais prakāśayantu: priests of sun-like brilliance, may they make you manifest — praise you with mantras; "let [you] be revealed (be made to appear)".

original pp. 680–685

Sūkta 16, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इमा धाना घृतस्नुवो हरी इहोप वक्षतः । इन्द्रं सुखतमे रथे ॥२॥

imā dhānā ghṛtasnuvo harī ihopa vakṣataḥ | indraṃ sukhatame rathe ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

इमाः । धानाः । घृतऽस्नुवः । हरी इति । इह । उप । वक्षतः ॥ इन्द्रम् । सुखऽतमे । रथे ॥२॥

imāḥ | dhānāḥ | ghṛta-snuvaḥ | harī iti | iha | upa | vakṣataḥ || indram | sukha-tame | rathe ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हरिशब्द इन्द्ररथस्य वोढारावश्वावाचष्टे । तथा च श्रुत्यन्तरम् । हर्योः स्थाथेति [?] । हरिभ्यां श्लेन्द्रो [?] देवतां गमयतीति च । एतदेवाभिप्रेत्य निघण्टुकार आह । हरी इन्द्रस्येति । तादृशौ हरी इमा योगार्थं वेद्यामासादितत्वेन पुरोवर्तिनीर्धानाः [भृज्जित?] यवतण्डुलानुद्दिश्य सुखतमे रथे इन्द्रमवस्थाप्येहास्मिन्कर्मण्युप वक्षतः । वेदिसमीपे वहताम् । कीदृशीर्धानाः । घृतस्नुवोऽलंकरणोपस्तरणाभिघारणादिना घृतस्रावणीः [?] । धीयन्त इति धानाः । धाश्वस्यजतिभ्यो नः । उ. [३-९७ ?] । इति नः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । घृतस्नुवः । घृतं स्नुवन्तीति घृतस्नुवः । क्विपि तुगभावश्छान्दसः । धातुस्वरः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । स्नोः संयोगपूर्वत्वेन यणभावादुवङादेशः । हरी । हृञ् हरणे । सर्वधातुभ्य इन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । प्रगृह्यत्वात्संहितायां प्रकृतिभावः । वक्षतः । प्रार्थनाप्ये लिङर्थे लेट् । तस्य प्रथमपुरुषद्विवचनं तस् । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । शपि प्राप्ते सिब्बहुलं लेटीति सिप् । ढत्वकुत्वषत्वानि । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । सुखतमे । गतम् ॥२॥

hari-śabda indra-rathasya vodhārāv aśvāv ācaṣṭe | tathā ca śruty-antaram | haryoḥ sthātheti [?] | haribhyāṃ ślendro [?] devatāṃ gamayatīti ca | etad evābhipretya nighaṇṭukāra āha | harī indrasyeti | tādṛśau harī imā yogārthaṃ vedyām āsāditatvena purovartinīr dhānāḥ [bhṛjjita?] yava-taṇḍulān uddiśya sukhatame rathe indram avasthāpyehāsmin karmaṇy upa vakṣataḥ | vedi-samīpe vahatām | kīdṛśīr dhānāḥ | ghṛtasnuvo 'laṅkaraṇopastaraṇābhighāraṇādinā ghṛta-srāvaṇīḥ [?] | dhīyanta iti dhānāḥ | dhāśvasyajatibhyo naḥ | u. [3-97 ?] | iti naḥ | pratyaya-svaraḥ | ghṛtasnuvaḥ | ghṛtaṃ snuvantīti ghṛtasnuvaḥ | kvipi tugabhāvaś chāndasaḥ | dhātu-svaraḥ | samāse kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | snoḥ saṃyogapūrvatvena yaṇābhāvād uvaṅādeśaḥ | harī | hṛñ haraṇe | sarvadhātubhya in | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | pragṛhyatvāt saṃhitāyāṃ prakṛtibhāvaḥ | vakṣataḥ | prārthanāpye liṅarthe leṭ | tasya prathamapuruṣa-dvivacanaṃ tas | leṭo 'ḍāṭāv ity aḍāgamaḥ | śapi prāpte sib bahulaṃ leṭīti sip | ḍhatva-katva-ṣatvāni | tiṅ ataṅ iti nighātaḥ | sukhatame | gatam ||2||

Translation: "The word hari denotes the two horses that carry Indra's chariot. So another Vedic text says [haryoḥ sthātha? — uncertain]; and 'by the two haris Indra brings the deity' [?]. With this in view the Nighaṇṭu-maker says: 'harī — [the two horses] of Indra.' Such a pair of horses — these dhānāḥ (parched grain, barley and rice) lie before them on the altar for the sacrifice [in the print the participle before 'barley-rice' is partly unclear: 'parched (?)']; having made Indra sit in the most comfortable chariot, let them bring him (upa vakṣataḥ) here to this rite, near the altar. Of what sort are the dhānāḥ? Ghṛtasnuvaḥ — dripping with ghee through the adorning, strewing and sprinkling [?]. Dhānāḥ are 'what is set down' (dhīyante)." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: dhānāḥ (dhā with the Uṇādi na, Uṇ. 3-[?]; suffix accent); ghṛtasnuvaḥ (ghṛta + snu "to drip" with kvip; the tuk is absent by Vedic licence; accent of the root; uvaṅ in place of y since the u of snu is preceded by a conjunct); harī (hṛ, the Uṇādi in; the dual keeps its form unchanged — pragṛhya — in the Saṃhitā); vakṣataḥ (leṭ in the sense of liṅ, in the meaning of a wish; the third dual tas, the augment aṭ by P. 3-4-94 leṭo 'ḍāṭau [as read], sip by sib bahulaṃ leṭi; ḍhatva, katva, ṣatva; the verb unaccented); sukhatame (as before [Rik 1.14? in the print "gatam"]). Grammar, noted briefly.

Grammar pages (pp. 681–685), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats dhānāḥ (ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; the Uṇādi na after dhā, śvasyajatibhyo naḥ [Uṇ. 3-[?]], dhā+na; the feminine sense calls for ṭāp by P. 4-1-4 ajādyatas ṭāp, hence dhānā + as → dhānāḥ by savarṇadīrgha; the first-syllable accent by the ñit/nit mark; the accent of the ṭāp result by P. 6-1-158 and 6-1-… ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ), ghṛtasnuvaḥ (snu "to drip" of the adādi class; ghṛtam snuvanti iti; kvip ca P. 3-2-76; kvip's luk; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; a long note on why the tuk of P. 6-1-71 hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk does not come — either as a Vedic licence or by the paribhāṣā āgamaśāstram anityam; the accent of the root by P. 6-1-162 dhātoḥ; the compound by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; snu + as: since the u is preceded by a conjunct, P. 6-4-77 aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau gives uvaṅ and not yaṇ, by the rule oḥ supi P. 6-4-83 not applying, hence ghṛtasnuvaḥ), harī (as for harayaḥ; prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ P. 6-1-102; the dual ī is pragṛhya by P. 1-1-11 īdūded dvivacanaṃ pragṛhyam; plutapragṛhyā aci nityam P. 6-1-125 keeps it unchanged before the i of iha; prakṛtibhāva: "remaining in the natural condition" — the Kannada's definition), and vakṣataḥ (vah; liṅarthe leṭ P. 3-4-7 liṅarthe leṭ in the sense of a wish; third dual tas; leṭo 'ḍāṭau P. 3-4-94; sib bahulaṃ leṭi P. 3-1-34; ho ḍhaḥ P. 8-2-31; ḍhatva; ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si P. 8-2-41; ādeśapratyayayoḥ P. 8-3-59; tiṅ atiṅaḥ P. 8-1-28). Crowded; outline only; numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हरी (harī) — the two horses of Indra | इमाः (imāḥ) — these (spread on the altar for the sake of the rite) | घृतस्नुवः (ghṛta-snuvaḥ) — well steeped in ghee (that is, drenched with ghee) | धानाः (dhānāḥ) — grains (barley, rice and so on), for the sake of acceptance | सुखतमे (sukhatame) — [seating him] in the most comfortable | रथे (rathe) — chariot | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | इह (iha) — here (to this place where the sacrifice is going on) | उप वक्षतः (upa vakṣataḥ) — let them bring near.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

In the sacrifice, the grains of barley, rice and the like, well steeped in ghee for the oblation, have been strewn all round the sacrificial pit, adorning it and spreading over it. To eat them, let the two horses called hari, belonging to Indra, bring Indra, seated in the most comfortable of chariots, to the neighbourhood of this sacrificial ground.

॥ English Translation ॥

Let the horses convey Indra in an easy-moving chariot hither where these grains of parched barley steeped in clarified butter are being prepared for the Sacrifice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

धानाः (dhānāḥ) — the grains of barley, rice and the like which are got ready for making an oblation in the fire. In the rite of preparing the fire (agni-saṃskāra), when adornment, strewing and the like are done with barley, rice and so on, the grains fall all round the fire-pit. These are the sacrificial share that must be offered to Indra's horses. The sense is that, in order to eat these, Indra's horses should come with Indra.

घृतस्नुवः (ghṛtasnuvaḥ) — ghṛtaṃ snuvanti iti ghṛtasnuvaḥ: those that are well steeped in ghee, or that drip ghee.

Sūkta 16, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रं प्रातर्हवामह इन्द्रं प्रयत्यध्वरे । इन्द्रं सोमस्य पीतये ॥३॥

indraṃ prātar havāmaha indraṃ prayaty adhvare | indraṃ somasya pītaye ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रम् । प्रातः । हवामहे । इन्द्रम् । प्रऽयति । अध्वरे ॥ इन्द्रम् । सोमस्य । पीतये ॥३॥

indram | prātaḥ | havāmahe | indram | pra-yati | adhvare || indram | somasya | pītaye ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

प्रातः कर्मारम्भे प्रातःसवने इन्द्रं हवामहे । आह्वयामः । तथैवाध्वरे सोमयागे प्रयति प्रगच्छति प्रारभ्य वर्तमाने सति माध्यन्दिने सवने तमिन्द्रं हवामहे । तथा यज्ञसमाप्त्यवसरे तृतीयसवने सोमस्य पीतये सोमपानार्थं हवामहे ॥ प्रातः । स्वरादिष्वन्तोदात्तो निपातितः । हवामहे । ह्वेञो लटि शपि परतो ह्वः संप्रसारणमित्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । परपूर्वत्वम् । गुणावादेशौ । प्रयति । इण् गतौ । लटः शतृ । आदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । शतुर्जित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । प्रादिसमासः । कृद्ग्रहणे गतिकारकपूर्वस्यापि ग्रहणम् । परि. [३८] । इति वचनात्प्रत्ययग्रहण इति नियमाभावात् शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अध्वरे । उक्तम् । संहितायामुदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितोऽनुदात्तस्य । पा. [८-२-४] । इत्येकारस्य स्वरितत्वम् । पीतये । पा पाने । क्तिनि छान्दसमन्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥३॥

prātaḥ karmārambhe prātaḥsavane indraṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | tathaivādhvare somayāge prayati pragacchati prārabhya vartamāne sati mādhyandine savane tam indraṃ havāmahe | tathā yajña-samāptyavasare tṛtīya-savane somasya pītaye soma-pānārthaṃ havāmahe || prātaḥ | svarādiṣv antodātto nipātitaḥ | havāmahe | hveño laṭi śapi parato hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam ity anuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | parapūrvatvam | guṇāvādeśau | prayati | iṇ gatau | laṭaḥ śatṛ | ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | śatur jittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | prādi-samāsaḥ | kṛdgrahaṇe gati-kāraka-pūrvasyāpi grahaṇam | pari. [38] | iti vacanāt pratyaya-grahaṇa iti niyamābhāvāt śatur anumo nady-ajādī iti vibhakter udāttatvam | adhvare | uktam | saṃhitāyām udātta-svaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya | pā. [8-2-4] | ity ekārasya svaritatvam | pītaye | pā pāne | ktini chāndasam antodāttatvam ||3||

Translation: "At the beginning of the rite, in the morning pressing (prātaḥ), we invoke Indra. So likewise, when the Soma sacrifice is going on (prayati) — that is, having begun and continuing — at the midday pressing, we invoke that same Indra. And at the close of the sacrifice, in the third pressing, we invoke him for the drinking of soma." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: prātaḥ (a particle, listed among those with end accent — svarādi); havāmahe (hve, laṭ, saṃprasāraṇa "variously in the Veda", parapūrva, guṇa and av); prayati (i "to go", śatṛ for laṭ, śap dropped, no guṇa because śatṛ has indicatory ś/ṛ, a prādi compound; the locative ending accented by P. 6-1-173 śatur anumo nady-ajādī, since the rule on "mention of a kṛt includes forms with gati or kāraka before it" applies [paribhāṣā 38, as read]); adhvare (explained earlier; in the Saṃhitā the e becomes svarita by P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya); pītaye (pā, ktin, Vedic end accent).

Grammar pages (pp. 684 lower half–686), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats prātaḥ (a particle with end accent in the svarādi list, Phiṭ-sūtra [number unclear]), havāmahe (hveñ "to compete, to call"; laṭ with mahiṅ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e P. 3-4-79; śap; hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam P. 6-1-32 with bahulaṃ chandasi P. 6-1-34; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108 pūrvarūpa; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; eco 'yavāyāvaḥ P. 6-1-78; ato dīrgho yañi P. 7-3-101; unaccented by P. 8-1-28), prayati (iṇ gatau, the adādi class; śatṛ by P. 3-2-124; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72; no guṇa by P. 1-1-5 kṅiti ca; iko yaṇaci P. 6-1-77 giving y, which bars iyaṅ P. 6-4-77; kugatiprādayaḥ P. 2-2-18 for the compound; and a long discussion of the paribhāṣā "mention of a kṛt includes a gati/kāraka-preceded form" against the paribhāṣā "mention of a suffix means that suffix only", concluding that the accent of the ending by P. 6-1-173 śatur anumo nady-ajādī applies to prayati also, though it ends in śatṛ), adhvare (explained at 15.7 [print: "Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-7"]; prayaty adhvare: in the Saṃhitā the e, being unaccented after an accented ya, becomes svarita by P. 8-4-66 udātta-svaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya), and pītaye (pā "to drink", striyāṃ ktin P. 3-3-94; ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali P. 6-4-66 giving ī; the suffix accent set aside for end accent in the Veda; the dative ṅe, ṅiti hrasvaś ca P. 1-4-6 shortening the ī of pīti before e with the nadī name, then the discussion of whether pīti is nadī or ghi by P. 1-4-7 śeṣo ghy asakhi, with gher ṅiti P. 7-3-111 giving guṇa, and eco 'yavāyāvaḥ giving ay: pītaye). ॥3॥ Numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

प्रातः (prātaḥ) — at the morning pressing that comes at the beginning of the rite | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we invoke | अध्वरे (adhvare) — in the Soma sacrifice | प्रयति (prayati) — when it is going on (at the midday pressing) | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | we invoke | likewise [at the third pressing, at the close of the sacrifice] | सोमस्य (somasya) — of the soma-juice | पीतये (pītaye) — for drinking | we invoke Indra.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

At all three pressing-times that are parts of the soma sacrifice — the morning, midday and third pressings — we invoke Indra to drink the soma.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke Indra at the morning rite, we invoke Indra at the succeeding Sacrifice, we invoke Indra to drink the Soma-Juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In the sacrificial rite there is the custom of preparing and pressing out soma-juice at three times — morning, midday and evening — for drinking. These rites are called in order the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing. Though only the morning time is mentioned in this rik, it is the ṛṣi's intention that since Indra is also invoked to drink soma in the sacrifices that follow, he is invoked at all three of the pressings mentioned.

प्रयति (prayati) — iṇ gatau; pragacchati: while the sacrificial rite is proceeding, that is, when it is going on; i.e. at the midday and evening pressings.

Sūkta 16, Rik 4

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उप नः सुतमा गहि हरिभिरिन्द्र केशिभिः । सुते हि त्वा हवामहे ॥४॥

upa naḥ sutam ā gahi haribhir indra keśibhiḥ | sute hi tvā havāmahe ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उप । नः । सुतम् । आ । गहि । हरिऽभिः । इन्द्र । केशिऽभिः ॥ सुते । हि । त्वा । हवामहे ॥४॥

upa | naḥ | sutam | ā | gahi | hari-bhiḥ | indra | keśi-bhiḥ || sute | hi | tvā | havāmahe ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र केशिभिः केसरयुक्तैर्हरिभिरश्वैस्त्वं नोऽस्मदीयं सुतमभिषुतं सोमं प्रत्युप समीपे आ गहि । आगच्छ । सुते हि अभिषुते सोमे निमित्तभूते सति यस्मात्कारणात्त्वा त्वां हवामहे ह्वयामः । तस्मादागच्छेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ गहि । गमेर्लोटः सेर्हिः । शप इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । इषुगमियमां छः । पा. [७-३-७७] इति छत्वं न भवति । न लुमताङ्गस्येति प्रतिषेधात् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । तस्य सिद्धवदेत्राभात् । पा. [६-४-२२] इत्यसिद्धत्वादतो हेरिति हेर्लुग्न भवति । केशिभिः । क्लेशेरन् लोपश्च । उ. [५-४३ ?] इत्यन् । मत्वर्थीय इनिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हवामहे । ह्व इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव । तिङ्ङतिङ इति न निघातो हि चेति प्रतिषेधात् ॥४॥

he indra keśibhiḥ kesara-yuktair haribhir aśvais tvaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ sutam abhiṣutaṃ somaṃ praty upa samīpe ā gahi | āgaccha | sute hi abhiṣute some nimitta-bhūte sati yasmāt kāraṇāt tvā tvāṃ havāmahe hvayāmaḥ | tasmād āgaccheti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || gahi | gamer loṭaḥ ser hiḥ | śapa ity anuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | iṣu-gami-yamāṃ chaḥ | pā. [7-3-77] iti chatvaṃ na bhavati | na lumatāṅgasyeti pratiṣedhāt | anudāttopadeśety-ādinānunāsika-lopaḥ | tasya siddhavad etrābhāt | pā. [6-4-22] ity asiddhatvād ato her iti her lug na bhavati | keśibhiḥ | kleśer an lopaś ca | u. [5-43 ?] ity an | matvarthīya iniḥ | pratyaya-svaraḥ | havāmahe | hva ity anuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | tiṅaś ca lasārvadhātuka-svareṇa dhātu-svara eva | tiṅ ataṅ iti na nighāto hi ceti pratiṣedhāt ||4||

Translation: "O Indra! With your long-maned (keśin, 'having a kesara, mane') horses, come near (upa ā gahi) to our pressed soma. For (hi) since the soma is pressed we invoke you; therefore come — the earlier [clauses] connect so." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: gahi (gam + loṭ, si → hi, śap dropped; the ch-substitute of P. 7-3-77 iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ does not apply, because of the bar na lumatāṅgasya; the nasal dropped by P. 6-4-37; and since that is treated as not-yet-done by P. 6-4-22 asiddhavad atrābhāt, the loss of hi by ato heḥ does not happen); keśibhiḥ (kleś with Uṇādi an, or the possessive ini; suffix accent); havāmahe (explained at Rik 3 above; the verb unaccented, but since the particle hi [sute hi] is present the nighāta is barred).

Grammar pages (pp. 688–689), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats gahi (gamḷ gatau, loṭ, thas-si, serhy apicca P. 3-4-87 giving hi — which is not pit, so śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi P. 2-4-73 / ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; the discussion that pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam P. 1-1-62 is barred by na lumatāṅgasya P. 1-1-63, so that the dropped suffix does not condition chatva by P. 7-3-77 iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ; the nasal m of gam is dropped by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanoty-ādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti — the Kannada explains that gam is among the anudāttopadeśa roots by the Kārikā list; ato heḥ P. 6-4-105 luk of hi would apply after a short-a stem, but asiddhavad atrābhāt P. 6-4-22 treats the m-drop as not done, so the stem is not short-a-final and the luk does not come), keśibhiḥ (kleśa "to harm" + an Uṇ. 3-[?]; keśa + ini in the sense of possession, P. 5-2-115 ata iniṭhanau; yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148; the suffix accent; the third plural bhis with svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne P. 1-4-17 giving the name pada, hence nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya P. 8-2-7, ru and visarga: keśibhiḥ), and havāmahe (explained at Rik 3; the verb is not unaccented since sute hi tvā havāmahe contains hi — P. 8-1-34 hi ca — and, by P. 8-1-67 pūjanāt pūjitam [as read 8-1-68], the intervening tvā does not break the connexion, "as explained earlier"). ॥4॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | सुते (sute) — since the soma has been made ready | त्वा (tvā) — you | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we invoke (therefore) | केशिभिः (keśibhiḥ) — with the long-maned | हरिभिः (haribhiḥ) — [your] horses | नः (naḥ) — our | सुतम् (sutam) — the soma-juice that has been made ready [to be drunk] | उप आ गहि (upa ā gahi) — come to our neighbourhood.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! We have made ready the soma-juice for you, and we invoke you. With your long-maned horses, come near us to drink it.

॥ English Translation ॥

Come Indra to our extracted soma libation by means of your long-maned horses. For we invoke you as soon as the soma is prepared.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

केशिभिः (keśibhiḥ) — with those that have kesara; kesara is the long hair that grows on the neck of horses.
