Sūkta 16, Rik 5

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सेमं नः स्तोममा गह्युपेदं सवनं सुतम् । गौरो न तृषितः पिब ॥५॥

semaṃ naḥ stomam ā gahy upedaṃ savanaṃ sutam | gauro na tṛṣitaḥ piba ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । इमम् । नः । स्तोमम् । आ । गहि । उप । इदम् । सवनम् । सुतम् ॥ गौरः । न । तृषितः । पिब ॥५॥

saḥ | imam | naḥ | stomam | ā | gahi | upa | idam | savanam | sutam || gauraḥ | na | tṛṣitaḥ | piba ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र स त्वं नोऽस्मदीयमिमं स्तोमं स्तुतिं प्रत्या गहि । आगत्य । आगमनेहेतुरुच्यते । उप देवयजनसमीपे सुतमभिषुतसोमयुक्तमिदानीमनुष्ठीयमानं सवनं प्रातःसवनादिरूपं कर्म वर्तते । तस्माद्गौरो न गौरमृग इव तृषितः सन्निमं सोमं पिब ॥ सः इमम् । इत्यत्र संहितायां सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणम् । पा. [६-१-१३४] । इति सुलोपः । गहि । गतम् । सवनं । सूयतेऽस्मिन्सोम इति । सूञ् प्राणिप्रसवे । अधिकरणे ल्युट् । लिति । इति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । लुडन्तत्वात्सप्तम्याः सुपां सुलोपो भवन्तीति वक्तव्यम् । मु. [?] । तदा द्वितीया । अभिषुतसोमयुक्तमिदं सवनमिति कर्मण्येव वा द्वितीया । तदा सुतशब्द ईषदर्थः [?] । कृषितः । तृष पिपासायाम् । निष्ठेति क्तः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । पश्चादिट् आगमा अनुदात्ता इत्यनुदात्तत्वम् ॥५॥

he indra sa tvaṃ no 'smadīyam imaṃ stomaṃ stutiṃ praty ā gahi | āgatya | āgamane hetur ucyate | upa deva-yajana-samīpe sutam abhiṣuta-soma-yuktam idānīm anuṣṭhīyamānaṃ savanaṃ prātaḥsavanādi-rūpaṃ karma vartate | tasmād gauro na gaura-mṛga iva tṛṣitaḥ sann imaṃ somaṃ piba || saḥ imam | ity atra saṃhitāyāṃ so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam | pā. [6-1-134] | iti su-lopaḥ | gahi | gatam | savanaṃ | sūyate 'smin soma iti | sūñ prāṇi-prasave | adhikaraṇe lyuṭ | liti | iti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvam | luḍantatvāt saptamyāḥ supāṃ sulopo bhavantīti vaktavyam | mu. [?] | tadā dvitīyā | abhiṣuta-soma-yuktam idaṃ savanam iti karmaṇy eva vā dvitīyā | tadā suta-śabda īṣad-arthaḥ [?] | tṛṣitaḥ | tṛṣa pipāsāyām | niṣṭheti ktaḥ | pratyaya-svareṇodāttaḥ | paścād iṭ āgamā anudāttā ity anudāttatvam ||5||

Translation: "O Indra! Such as you are, come (ā gahi) to this our stoma, our praise. Having come — the reason for your coming is stated: near (upa) the sacrificial ground, a savana — a rite of the morning pressing and so on, accompanied by pressed soma — is now being performed. Therefore, like a gaura — a pale-coloured deer (gaura-mṛga) — being thirsty, drink this soma." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: saḥ imam (in the Saṃhitā the su is dropped before a vowel by P. 6-1-134 so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam); gahi (as before); savanam (sū "to bring forth" with lyuṭ in the locative sense — "that in which soma is pressed" — the accent before the suffix by P. 6-1-193 liti; the locative ending dropped [?]; or accusative with sutam); tṛṣitaḥ (tṛṣ "to thirst", kta, with suffix accent; the augment iṭ unaccented).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | सः (saḥ) — you [being thus] | नः (naḥ) — our | इमम् (imam) — this | स्तोमम् (stomam) — praise (for hearing) | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come | उप (upa) — near [the sacrificial altar] | सुतम् (sutam) — accompanied by the pressed soma-juice | इदम् (idam) — this | सवनम् (savanam) — the rite of the morning pressing [that is going on] | तृषितः (tṛṣitaḥ) — thirsty | गौरः (gauraḥ) — a gaura deer | न (na) — like | पिब (piba) — drink [the soma-juice].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The soma-juice needed for the morning pressing is ready. For the sake of that rite, come, pleased with the praise that we make, and, like a deer thirsty from the mouth [i.e. from the dryness of the mouth], drink the soma-juice.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, accept this our praise and come to this our sacrifice of the expressed soma ; drink like a thirsty stag.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

गौरः (gauraḥ) — a pale-coloured deer. Here the word na is a particle of comparison; gauro na means "like a deer".

तृषितः (tṛṣitaḥ) — thirsty. A deer, parched with thirst, drinks water eagerly; so you also should drink our soma-juice as much as you wish, with eagerness.

Grammar pages (pp. 691 lower half–692), noted briefly. Saḥ + imam: here, in the Saṃhitā, with saḥ + imam, the loss of su by P. 6-1-134 so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam takes place only if the pāda is thereby made up (to eight syllables); the guṇa of P. 6-1-87 ād guṇaḥ then makes the a+i into e [semam]; the Kannada gives the śikṣā verses on the "kaṇṭhya, tālavya" nature of e and ai (kaṇṭhatālavya e ai, as in Pāṇinīya-śikṣā, verses read in small print: akuhavisarjanīyānāṃ kaṇṭhaḥ, icuyaśānāṃ tālu, … e ai tu kaṇṭhatālavyau, o au kaṇṭhoṣṭhajau smṛtau), and argues that if the su is not dropped (sa imam) the pāda would not be complete, so the dropping applies; the ru-sandhi alternative (P. 8-3-34 visarjanīyasya saḥ etc. [?]) is discussed and set aside, since by P. 8-2-1 pūrvatrāsiddham and P. 6-1-87 the y from ro would not interfere. Gahi: explained earlier [Rik 4]. Savanam: sū "to bring forth", dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64, lyuṭ in the sense of place by P. 3-3-117 karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca, yuvor anākau P. 7-1-1 for ana, guṇa by P. 7-3-84, av by P. 6-1-78; first-syllable accent before lyuṭ, by P. 6-1-193 liti; "savanam" is a lyuṭ neuter ending, to which su is added in the locative [? the passage is not clear to me]. ॥5॥ Crowded; outline only; the Pāṇinīya-śikṣā verses are partly read from small print and are given as pointers only.

original pp. 692–694

Sūkta 16, Rik 6

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ The Saṃhitā prints the nasalised tām̐ indra; the Pada has tān.

इमे सोमास इन्दवः सुतासो अधि बर्हिषि । ताँ इन्द्र सहसे पिब ॥६॥

ime somāsa indavaḥ sutāso adhi barhiṣi | tām̐ indra sahase piba ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इमे । सोमासः । इन्दवः । सुतासः । अधि । बर्हिषि ॥ तान् । इन्द्र । सहसे । पिब ॥६॥

ime | somāsaḥ | indavaḥ | sutāsaḥ | adhi | barhiṣi || tān | indra | sahase | piba ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्दुशब्द उन्दी क्लेदन इति धातोरुत्पन्नः । इन्दवः क्लेदनयुक्ता इमे वेद्यामवस्थिताः सोमासस्तत्तत्पात्रगताः सोमा बर्हिषि यज्ञेऽधिकेन सुतासः । अभिषुताः । हे इन्द्र सहसे बलार्थं तान् सोमान्पिब ॥ सोमासः । आज्जसेरसुगिति जसोऽसुगागमः । इन्दवः । उक्तम् । सुतासः । पूर्ववदसुक् । संहितायां प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपरे इति प्रकृतिभावात्स्वरपूर्वत्वं न भवति । बर्हिषि । बृंहेर्नलोपश्च । उ. [२-१००?] । इसिस् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । तां इन्द्रेत्यत्र दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति रुत्वम् । यत्वयलोपौ । अनुनासिकः । सहसे । षह मर्षणे । असुनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥६॥

indu-śabda undī kledana iti dhātor utpannaḥ | indavaḥ kledana-yuktā ime vedyām avasthitāḥ somāsas tat-tat-pātra-gatāḥ somā barhiṣi yajñe 'dhikena sutāsaḥ | abhiṣutāḥ | he indra sahase balārthaṃ tān somān piba || somāsaḥ | āj jaser asug iti jaso 'sugāgamaḥ | indavaḥ | uktam | sutāsaḥ | pūrvavad asuk | saṃhitāyāṃ prakṛtyāntaḥ-pādam avyapare iti prakṛtibhāvāt svara-pūrvatvaṃ na bhavati | barhiṣi | bṛṃher nalopaś ca | u. [2-100?] | isis | pratyaya-svaraḥ | tām̐ indretyatra dīrghād aṭi samānapāda iti rutvam | yatva-yalopau | anunāsikaḥ | sahase | ṣaha marṣaṇe | asunanto nittvād ādyudāttaḥ ||6||

Translation: "The word indu is formed from the root undī 'to wet'. Indavaḥ — wet, flowing: these soma-juices (somāsaḥ), standing in the several vessels on the altar, are sutāsaḥ — pressed — on the barhis (the sacred grass) at the sacrifice [the word before 'pressed', printed adhikena, is as read and uncertain: the Kannada takes adhi as 'in abundance']. O Indra! Drink those soma-juices for strength (sahase)." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: somāsaḥ (the ending jas takes the augment asuk by P. 7-1-50 āj jaser asuk); indavaḥ (explained at Rik 14.4); sutāsaḥ (asuk as before; in the Saṃhitā, by P. 6-1-115 prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare, the o before a keeps its form, so the a is not elided); barhiṣi (bṛh with the Uṇādi isi, the n dropped); tām̐ indra (n → ru by P. 8-3-9; y dropped, nasalisation); sahase (ṣah 'to endure', the suffix asun, first-syllable accent). Grammar, noted briefly; the Uṇādi number is as read and uncertain.

Grammar pages (p. 694), noted briefly. The Kannada treats somāsaḥ (suñ 'to press', dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; the Uṇādi man after su, Uṇ. 1-142 [as read]; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; the n-mark gives first-syllable accent; jas with asuk by P. 7-1-50, and the asuk's k mark, being kit, makes it the final part of the stem by P. 1-1-46 ādyantau ṭakitau; pūrvasavarṇadīrgha; ru and visarga), indavaḥ (explained at 14.4), sutāsaḥ (suñ + kta; no iṭ, by P. 7-2-10 ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt; asuk; ru → u by P. 6-1-113 ato roraplutād aplute and guṇa P. 6-1-87 ād guṇaḥ, giving sutāso adhi; the question whether pūrvarūpa by P. 6-1-109 eṅaḥ padāntād ati should apply is answered by P. 6-1-115 prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare, which keeps the o unchanged; "but if the following is v or y [aspirate-initial?] this prakṛtibhāva does not apply; here it applies, so no pūrvarūpa"), barhiṣi (bṛhi vṛddhau 'to grow'; idit, so the num augment by P. 7-1-58 idito num dhātoḥ; bṛnh + isi by Uṇ. 2-[?] bṛṃher nalopaś ca; bṛh + is, n dropped; guṇa by P. 7-3-86 pugantalaghūpadhasya ca; ur aṇ raparaḥ; barhis; suffix accent, so end-accent; locative ṅi → i; ādeśapratyayayoḥ P. 8-3-59 gives ṣ), and tām̐ indra (tān + indra: dīrghād aṭi samānapāde P. 8-3-9 gives ru for the n; ato 'ṭi nityam [?] P. 8-3-3 nasalises the preceding vowel; bho-bhago-agho-apūrvasya yo 'śi P. 8-3-17 changes ru to y; lopaḥ śākalyasya P. 8-3-19 drops y; so tām̐ indra), and sahase (ṣah marṣaṇe, dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; sarvadhātubhyo 'sun Uṇ. 4-[?]; accent; dative ṅe). ॥6॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सुतासः (sutāsaḥ) — made ready, pressed | इन्दवः (indavaḥ) — [full of] juice (or: flowing in drops) | इमे (ime) — these [that are on the altar] | सोमासः (somāsaḥ) — soma-juices [lying in various vessels] | बर्हिषि (barhiṣi) — at the sacrifice | अधि (adhi) — in abundance (put on the sacred grass) | इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | सहसे (sahase) — for the increase of strength | तान् (tān) — those soma-juices | पिब (piba) — drink.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The soma-juices lying in the various vessels on this altar are not drawn in the ordinary way; they have been prepared with mantras as a part of the sacrifice. O Indra, drink them for the increase of your strength.

॥ English Translation ॥

These dripping Soma juices are effused upon the sacred grass; drink them Indra, to recruit your strength.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

इन्दवः (indavaḥ) — when the soma-creeper is crushed with stones and the juice pressed out, the juice trickles in drops. There is a convention of calling the soma-juice that thus trickles by the name indavaḥ. This word is formed from the root undī "to wet".

original pp. 695–697

Sūkta 16, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अयं ते स्तोमो अग्रियो हृदिस्पृगस्तु शंतमः । अथा सोमं सुतं पिब ॥७॥

ayaṃ te stomo agriyo hṛdispṛg astu śaṃtamaḥ | athā somaṃ sutaṃ piba ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened athā, the Pada atha.

अयम् । ते । स्तोमः । अग्रियः । हृदिऽस्पृक् । अस्तु । शम्ऽतमः ॥ अथ । सोमम् । सुतम् । पिब ॥७॥

ayam | te | stomaḥ | agriyaḥ | hṛdi-spṛk | astu | śam-tamaḥ || atha | somam | sutam | piba ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र अयमस्माभिः क्रियमाणः स्तोमः स्तोत्रविशेषोऽग्रियः श्रेष्ठः सन् ते तव हृदिस्पृक् मनस्यङ्गीकृतः शंतमः सुखकरतमोऽस्तु । अथ स्तुतेरनन्तरं सुतमभिषुतं सोमं पिब ॥ अग्रियः । अग्राद्यत् । पा. [४-४-११६] । इति घच् । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । हृदिस्पृक् । हृदि स्पृशतीति हृदिस्पृक् । स्पृशोऽनुदके क्विन् । पा. [३-२-५८] । क्विन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः । पा. [८-२-६२] । इति कुत्वम् । … तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलम् । पा. [६-३-१४] । इत्यलुक् । क्विनप्रत्ययस्य कुः । … कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । शंतमः । सुखकरद्रव्यवचनोऽत्र शंशब्दः । तत्तस्तमुप् । अत्र सुखप्रकर्षस्य गुणद्वारा गुणनिष्ठद्रव्ये सङ्क्रान्तत्वादद्रव्यप्रकर्ष इति निषेधात् किमेत्तिङ्व्ययघादाम्वद्रव्यप्रकर्षे । पा. [५-४-११] । आम् न भवति द्रव्यस्य स्वतः प्रकर्षाभावात् । ईदृगर्थ एव हि स निषेधः । अथा सोमम् । संहितायां निपातस्येति दीर्घः ॥७॥

he indra ayam asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇaḥ stomaḥ stotra-viśeṣo 'griyaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ san te tava hṛdispṛk manasy aṅgīkṛtaḥ śaṃtamaḥ sukha-karatamo 'stu | atha stuter anantaraṃ sutam abhiṣutaṃ somaṃ piba || agriyaḥ | agrād yat | pā. [4-4-116] | iti ghac | cittvād antodāttaḥ | hṛdispṛk | hṛdi spṛśatīti hṛdispṛk | spṛśo 'nudake kvin | pā. [3-2-58] | kvin-pratyayasya kuḥ | pā. [8-2-62] | iti kutvam | … tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam | pā. [6-3-14] | ity aluk | … kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | śaṃtamaḥ | sukha-kara-dravya-vacano 'tra śaṃ-śabdaḥ | tat-tastamup | atra sukha-prakarṣasya guṇa-dvārā guṇa-niṣṭha-dravye saṅkrāntatvād adravya-prakarṣa iti niṣedhāt kim-etti-ṅ-vyaya-ghād ām-vadravya-prakarṣe | pā. [5-4-11] | ām na bhavati dravyasya svataḥ prakarṣābhāvāt | īdṛg-artha eva hi sa niṣedhaḥ | athā somam | saṃhitāyāṃ nipātasyeti dīrghaḥ ||7||

Translation: "O Indra! May this stoma — this particular hymn of praise being made by us — be agriya, the foremost; may it be hṛdispṛk, touching your heart, accepted in your mind; may it be śaṃtama, the most productive of comfort (happiness). Then, after the praise, drink the pressed (suta) soma." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: agriyaḥ (agra + ghac by P. 4-4-116 agrād yat as read [the Kannada reads the sūtra as agrāc ghac ca]; accent on the last syllable because of the c mark); hṛdispṛk (hṛdi spṛśati, spṛś + kvin when the object is not water, P. 3-2-58; k for the final of the root by P. 8-2-62; the locative ending kept — aluk — by P. 6-3-14 tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam; the accent of the final member of the compound); śaṃtamaḥ (the word śam here means a thing that causes comfort; the suffix tamap; the augment ām of P. 5-4-11 kimettiṅavyayaghād āmv adravyaprakarṣe is not added, because the superlative here concerns a substance and the rule bars ām where the excess belongs to a substance — "the substance has no excellence of its own"); athā somam (the lengthened athā in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-136 nipātasya ca). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 3-2-58, P. 8-2-62 and P. 5-4-11 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 696 lower half–698 upper half), noted briefly. The Kannada treats agriyaḥ (P. 4-4-116 agrāt ghac ca [the ghac and yat suffixes after agra in the sense "being in front"], so here the sense agre bhavaḥ "being first" takes ghac; the cuṭū of P. 1-3-7 for the c, tasya lopaḥ; āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām P. 7-1-2 gives iy for gh — agra + iya; yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148 drops the a; agriya accented on the end by cit P. 6-1-163; the nominative su, ru, visarga), hṛdispṛk (hṛdi spṛśati; spṛśo 'nudake kvin P. 3-2-58; the sūtra tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam P. 6-3-14 for the aluk of the locative in a tatpuruṣa before a kṛt; kvin's k gives kutva by P. 8-2-62 kvinpratyayasya kuḥ; the ṣ of spṛś; vraśca-bhrasja-sṛja-mṛja-yaja-rāja-bhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ P. 8-2-36 is taken first, then spṛṣ → spṛg by P. 8-2-39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte, and kutva by P. 8-2-62; vāvasāne P. 8-4-56 gives spṛk; compound accent that of the final member by P. 6-2-139), śaṃtamaḥ (śam 'comfort' + tamap by P. 5-3-55 atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau; the long note, as given in the Mahābhāṣya and by Kaiyaṭa on the tamap sūtra: "adravyaprakarṣe" bars the ām augment of P. 5-4-11 when the excellence is not of a substance; here śam is a quality-word and the excellence is first in the quality, then transferred to the substance, so the bar applies and ām is not added; tarap-tamapau ghaḥ P. 1-1-22 gives these suffixes the name gha), and athā somam (the lengthening by P. 6-3-136 nipātasya ca). ॥7॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे इन्द्र) ((he indra)) — O Indra | अग्रियः (agriyaḥ) — the foremost, the best | अयम् (ayam) — this (praise, made by us) | स्तोमः (stomaḥ) — hymn of praise | ते (te) — your | हृदिस्पृक् (hṛdi-spṛk) — touching the heart (agreeable to the mind) | शंतमः (śaṃ-tamaḥ) — most productive of comfort | अस्तु (astu) — may it be | अथ (atha) — after the praise is over | सुतम् (sutam) — ready | सोमम् (somam) — the soma-juice | पिब (piba) — drink.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! May this hymn which we make about you touch your heart and give you delight. Afterwards, drink the soma-juice that we have made ready.

॥ English Translation ॥ The print has "you heart" for "your heart" — [sic].

May this excellent hymn touching you heart be most agreeable to you. Drink, then Indra, the extracted Soma-juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अग्रियः (agriyaḥ) — agre bhavaḥ: the foremost, the best, the highest.

हृदिस्पृक् (hṛdispṛk) — hṛdi spṛśatīti hṛdispṛk: touching the heart; moving the heart; pleasing the mind. [The print adds the English "touching your heart, etc."] The sense is: may the hymn we make please your mind.

शंतमः (śaṃtamaḥ) — productive of comfort; may the hymn we make give you delight.

अथ (atha) — the final syllable of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text to suit the metre.

original pp. 698–702

Sūkta 16, Rik 8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वमित्सवनं सुतमिन्द्रो मदाय गच्छति । वृत्रहा सोमपीतये ॥८॥

viśvam it savanaṃ sutam indro madāya gacchati | vṛtrahā somapītaye ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वम् । इत् । सवनम् । सुतम् । इन्द्रः । मदाय । गच्छति ॥ वृत्रऽहा । सोमऽपीतये ॥८॥

viśvam | it | savanam | sutam | indraḥ | madāya | gacchati || vṛtra-hā | soma-pītaye ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

वृत्रहा शत्रुघातक इन्द्रः सोमपीतये सोमपानाय मदाय तत्पानजन्यहर्षाय च विश्वमित्सर्वमपि सुतमभिषुतसोमयुक्तं सवनं प्रातःसवनादिरूपं कर्म गच्छति ॥ विश्वम् । अशूप्रुषिलटिकणिखटिविशिभ्यः क्वन् । उ. [१-१५१]। नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सवनं सुतम् । पूर्ववत् । मदाय । मदोऽनुपसर्गे । पा. [३-३-६७]। इत्यप्प्रत्ययः । पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । गच्छति । इषुगमियमां छः । वृत्रहा । वृत्रं हतवान् । ब्रह्मभ्रूणवृत्रेषु क्विप् । पा. [३-२-८७]। इन्हन्पूषार्यम्णां शौ । सौ च । पा. [६-४-१२,१३]। इति प्रतिप्रसवाद्दीर्घवति । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सोमपीतये । वधिकरणबहुव्रीहिरित्युक्तम् । तत्पुरुषे वा दासीभारादित्वात् । पा. [६-२-४२ ?] । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥८॥

vṛtrahā śatru-ghātaka indraḥ somapītaye soma-pānāya madāya tat-pāna-janya-harṣāya ca viśvam it sarvam api sutam abhiṣuta-soma-yuktaṃ savanaṃ prātaḥsavanādi-rūpaṃ karma gacchati || viśvam | aśūpruṣi-laṭi-kaṇi-khaṭi-viśibhyaḥ kvan | u. [1-151] | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | savanaṃ sutam | pūrvavat | madāya | mado 'nupasarge | pā. [3-3-67] | ity ap-pratyayaḥ | pittvād dhātu-svaraḥ | gacchati | iṣu-gami-yamāṃ chaḥ | vṛtrahā | vṛtraṃ hatavān | brahma-bhrūṇa-vṛtreṣu kvip | pā. [3-2-87] | in-han-pūṣāryamṇāṃ śau | sau ca | pā. [6-4-12, 13] | iti pratiprasavād dīrghavati | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | somapītaye | vadhikaraṇa-bahuvrīhir ity uktam | tatpuruṣe vā dāsībhārāditvāt | pā. [6-2-42 ?] | pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||8||

Translation: "Indra, vṛtrahā — the slayer of enemies — goes (gacchati) to every (viśvam it) savana — the rite of the morning pressing and the like — accompanied by the pressed soma, for the drinking of soma (somapītaye) and for the exhilaration (madāya) — the delight that arises from drinking it." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: viśvam (viś + kvan, Uṇ. 1-151 [as read]; first-syllable accent); madāya (mad + ap by P. 3-3-67 mado 'nupasarge; ap is pit, so the accent stays on the root); gacchati (gam → gaccha by P. 7-3-77 iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ); vṛtrahā ("he who has slain Vṛtra"; han + kvip after vṛtra by P. 3-2-87 brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu kvip; the lengthening by P. 6-4-12 in-han-pūṣārya-mṇāṃ śau and 6-4-13 sau ca; the accent of the final member); somapītaye (a vyadhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi, as explained earlier; or a tatpuruṣa; by the dāsībhārādi class [P. 6-2-42] the accent of the first member). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 3-3-67 and P. 3-2-87 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 699 lower half–702), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: viśvam (viś "to enter" + kvan, Uṇ. 1-151 aśūpruṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan; first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; savanaṃ sutam and sīmaṃ naḥ [print: somaṃ naḥ? — the reference given is to Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-16-5 and the earlier explanation]), madāya (P. 3-3-67 mado 'nupasarge: ap after mad when the upapada is not an upasarga; the ap's p mark makes it unaccented by P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau; the root accent remains), gacchati (gamḷ gatau; iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ P. 7-3-77), and, at great length, vṛtrahā (vṛtraṃ hatavān: han "to strike" with kvip by P. 3-2-87 brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu kvip; the Kāśikā and the Mahābhāṣya views on niyama — that P. 3-2-87, though kvip is already available by P. 3-2-76 kvip ca, is a restricting rule [niyama] with three possible shapes: a restriction of upapada, of suffix, or of tense — the Kannada works through the examples puruṣahā, vṛtrajit, brāhmaṇaghātī, pitṛvyaghātī, and concludes with the usages puruṣaṃ hanti / haniṣyati (present or future: no kvip), brahmāṇaṃ hatavān ('he who has killed a brahman', with ṇini by P. 3-2-89 karmaṇi hanaḥ?) and the remark that Kaiyaṭa regards the niyamas as set aside by the Mahābhāṣya's own statement ubhayato niyamo 'yam — "the restriction is both ways"; the point is a grammarians' dispute about the scope of a restriction, and the Kannada reproduces it in nearly three pages; then vṛtrahan + su, sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau P. 6-4-8 [lengthening, which would apply], but in-han-pūṣārya-mṇāṃ śau P. 6-4-12 and sau ca P. 6-4-13 [as read, the standard 6-4-13] specially extend the lengthening to the sau; hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal P. 6-1-68 drops su; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya P. 8-2-7 drops the n; accent by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt: hā has the accent of its root), and somapītaye (here a vyadhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi — "of whom the drinking of soma is the aim" — as already explained at Rik 14.1 [print: "Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-1"], with soma having first-syllable accent by the n-mark, retained in the bahuvrīhi by P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam; if taken as a tatpuruṣa — somasya pītiḥ, tasmai — then samāsasya P. 6-1-223 would give the end accent, but this is set aside, since somapīti belongs to the dāsībhārādi class (an ākṛtigaṇa, with kurugārhapata, rikta-guru, sūta-jaratī, śleṣa-dṛḍha-rūpā, pārevaḍavā, taikala-droṇa, paṇya-kambala, dāsībhāra — as read, in small print) by P. 6-2-42 [as read], so the accent of the first member remains; "the vyadhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi is not otherwise available, so a tatpuruṣa analysis is also given"). ॥8॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वृत्रहा (vṛtrahā) — the slayer of enemies (or of the demon Vṛtra) | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for drinking soma | मदाय (madāya) — for the delight that arises from drinking soma | विश्वम् (viśvam) — all | सुतम् (sutam) — [that has] pressed soma | सवनम् (savanam) — the rites [beginning with the morning pressing] | गच्छति इत् (gacchati it) — goes indeed.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra, the slayer of the demons or of Vṛtra, goes to all the rites, the morning pressing and the rest, in which soma-juice is drawn; he drinks the soma-juice and is thereby satisfied.

॥ English Translation ॥ The print has "ceremoney" for "ceremony" — [sic].

Indra, the killer of Vritra (or of enemies) goes to every ceremony where Soma is prepared that he may drink the Soma and be intoxicated.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

वृत्रहा (vṛtrahā) — the word vṛtra is used for many meanings, such as cloud, strength, water, the demon Vṛtra; but here the commentator takes vṛtra to mean "enemy". It may also be taken to mean the demon Vṛtra. Accordingly, vṛtrahā means "the destroyer of enemies" or "the slayer of the demon Vṛtra".

मदाय (madāya) — for the exhilaration (mattu) that arises from drinking soma, or for delight; [the print adds the English word] "Intoxication".

original pp. 703–707

Sūkta 16, Rik 9 (last rik of the sūkta)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ The print of the first line has kāmamā; kāmam ā is given, the form the Pada and the bhāṣya both show.

सेमं नः कामुमा पृण गोभिरश्वैः शतक्रतो । स्तवाम त्वा स्वाध्यः ॥९॥

semaṃ naḥ kāmam ā pṛṇa gobhir aśvaiḥ śatakrato | stavāma tvā svādhyaḥ ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । इमम् । नः । कामम् । आ । पृण । गोभिः । अश्वैः । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो ॥ स्तवाम । त्वा । सुऽआध्यः ॥९॥

saḥ | imam | naḥ | kāmam | ā | pṛṇa | gobhiḥ | aśvaiḥ | śatakrato iti śata-krato || stavāma | tvā | su-ādhyaḥ ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे शतक्रतो स त्वं नोऽस्मदीयमिमं कामं काम्यमानं फलं गोभिरश्वैश्च सहा पृण । सर्वतः पूरय । वयमपि स्वाध्यः सुष्ठु सर्वतो ध्यानयुक्ताः सन्तस्त्वां स्तवाम ॥ सेमम् । संहितायां सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणमिति सुलोपः । कामम् । कमेर्णिङ् । कर्मणि घञ् । कृञ्हलश्चेत्यादिना । पा. [३-३-१२१]। इत्यंसोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते वृषादिषु पाठादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । पृण । पृण प्रीणने । लोटि सेर्हिः । तुदादिभ्यः शः । तस्य ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । गोभिः । साबेकाचेति प्राप्तं विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषिध्यते । अश्वैः । क्वनन्त इत्युक्तम् । असामर्थ्यान्न पराङ्गवद्भावः । स्तवाम । ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ । धात्वादेः षः सः । लोडुत्तमबहुवचनस्य लोटो लङ्वदिति लङ्वद्भावान्नित्यं ङितः । … आडुत्तमस्य पिच्च । पा. [३-४-९२]। इत्याडागमः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादसुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव । स्वाध्यः । ध्यै चिन्तायाम् । सु आङ् इत्युपसर्गाभ्यां पूर्वभागे प्रयोगः । आदेश उपदेशेऽशितीति [?] ... क्विप् । संप्रसारणम् । स्वाधी । … जसि ॥९॥

he śatakrato sa tvaṃ no 'smadīyam imaṃ kāmaṃ kāmyamānaṃ phalaṃ gobhir aśvaiś ca sahā pṛṇa | sarvataḥ pūraya | vayam api svādhyaḥ suṣṭhu sarvato dhyāna-yuktāḥ santas tvāṃ stavāma || semam | saṃhitāyāṃ so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam iti su-lopaḥ | kāmam | kamer ṇiṅ | karmaṇi ghañ | kṛñ-halaś cety-ādinā | pā. [3-3-121] | ity aṃsodāttatve prāpte vṛṣādiṣu pāṭhād ādyudāttatvam | pṛṇa | pṛṇa prīṇane | loṭi ser hiḥ | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | tasya ṅittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | ato her iti her luk | gobhiḥ | sāv ekāca iti prāptaṃ vibhakter udāttatvaṃ na go-śvan-sāv-avarṇeti pratiṣidhyate | aśvaiḥ | kvananta ity uktam | asāmarthyān na parāṅgavad-bhāvaḥ | stavāma | ṣṭuñ stutau | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | loḍ-uttama-bahuvacanasya loṭo laṅvad iti laṅvad-bhāvān nityaṃ ṅitaḥ | … āḍ uttamasya pic ca | pā. [3-4-92] | ity āḍāgamaḥ | pratyayasya pittvād asudāttatvam | dhātu-svara eva | svādhyaḥ | dhyai cintāyām | su āṅ ity upasargābhyāṃ pūrvabhāge prayogaḥ | … kvip | saṃprasāraṇam | svādhī | … jasi ||9||

Translation: "O Śatakratu [Indra, 'of a hundred powers']! Such as you are, fulfil (ā pṛṇa, 'fill all round') this our desired object (kāma) with cows and horses. We too, being svādhyaḥ — well absorbed in meditation on all sides — praise you." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: semam (saḥ + imam with the loss of su by P. 6-1-134); kāmam (kam 'to desire' with ṇic/ghañ by P. 3-3-121 halaś ca, whose accent would fall on the end, but by its inclusion in the vṛṣādi list the first syllable is accented); pṛṇa (pṛṇ 'to please'; loṭ, si → hi; śa of the tudādi class with no guṇa as it is ṅit; hi dropped by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ); gobhiḥ (the ending would be accented by P. 6-1-168 sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ but is barred by P. 6-1-182 na go-śvan-sāv-avarṇa-rāḍ-aṅkyu-kṣmāy-ātmanām, here go); aśvaiḥ (as for kvan-words); stavāma (ṣṭuñ 'to praise', loṭ first person plural mas; āṭ augment by P. 3-4-92 āḍ uttamasya pic ca); svādhyaḥ (dhyai 'to think' with the prefixes su and ā, kvip, saṃprasāraṇa, the compound svādhī and the nominative plural jas). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 3-3-121 and P. 3-4-92 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 704 lower half–707), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats semam (tad + su; tadoḥ saḥ sāv anantyayoḥ P. 7-2-106 [as read, 7-2-106] gives s for t; tyadādīnām aḥ P. 7-2-102 a for d; ato guṇe P. 6-1-97 pararūpa; the Kannada refers to the explanation at sīmaṃ naḥ stomam ā gahi [Rik 5 above; the print gives the earlier reference as "Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-16-5"]; then saḥ imam with so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam P. 6-1-134, guṇa), kāmam (kamu kāntau, halaś ca P. 3-3-121 ghañ; ata upadhāyāḥ P. 7-2-116 vṛddhi; the ñit would give the first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam, which is set aside by P. 6-1-159 karṣātvato ghaño 'nta udāttaḥ [roots with ṛ… or kṛṣ… take end-accent with ghañ] and that again by P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca, since kāma is in the vṛṣādi list, so first-syllable), pṛṇa (pṛṇ prīṇane of the tudādi class; loṭ, sip, serhy apicca P. 3-4-87; tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ P. 3-1-77; sārvadhātukam apit P. 1-2-4 makes it ñit, so no guṇa by P. 1-1-5; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca P. 7-3-86 is then also barred; ato heḥ P. 6-4-105 drops hi; wholly unaccented by P. 8-1-28; in the Saṃhitā the ā before it is udātta, so the pṛ's svarita arises by P. 8-4-66 and the following ṇa is unaccented by P. 1-2-40 udāttasvaritaparasya sannataraḥ [as read]), gobhiḥ (sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ P. 6-1-168, barred by P. 6-1-182 — the Kannada gives the full text of the barring sūtra — so gobhiḥ is not end-accented: the stem go is itself the accent bearer, and in goṣu the go is monosyllabic and would give the ending its accent; the bar is stated, and the ending is not accented), aśvaiḥ (aśva from aś with kvan, Uṇ. 1-[?] aśūpruṣi…; first-syllable accent by the n-mark; there is the vocative śatakrato near it, but the two have no mutual connexion, so by P. 3-1-2 [?] and P. 8-1-74 supāmantrite parāṅgavat svare the vocative is not treated as part of the other word), stavāma (ṣṭuñ stutau; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; loṭ first-person plural mas; loṭo laṅvat P. 3-4-85, making the mas as if laṅ, so nityaṃ ṅitaḥ P. 3-4-99 drops the s; āḍ uttamasya pic ca P. 3-4-92; śap P. 3-1-68, its luk [here śap with guṇa]; aṃ from a + ām [stu + a + āma, lengthening by P. 6-1-101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ]; the suffix being pit, unaccented; the root accent remains by P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau), and svādhyaḥ (dhyai cintāyām; the prefixes su and āṅ [here the Kannada notes that the prefix ā is used before the root in the Veda, with a long discussion of the upasarga's position]; kvip is found after roots other than bhrājanaṃ-type [P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante]; saṃprasāraṇa; su-ādhī + jas → svādhī + as; halaḥ P. 6-4-2 lengthens the vowel of a stem before a saṃprasāraṇa-bearing consonant — so svādhī; aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau P. 6-4-77 would give iy for the final ī but is barred in favour of yaṇ P. 6-4-82 eranekācaḥ…, since svādhī is a stem of several vowels not preceded by a conjunct [the Kannada's argument: the final ī of dhī is the end of an aṅga of more than one vowel, so yaṇ], giving svādhy-as; jas is not accented by P. 6-1-171 udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt, because the yaṇ here, though preceded by a consonant, is not followed by a sarvanāmasthāna-ending in the sense of that sūtra (the Kannada explains that jas here is asarvanāmasthāna, because P. 1-1-43 sudṅapuṃsakasya names only su, au, jas, am, auṭ as sarvanāmasthāna after a non-neuter — and here, after the udātta-yaṇ, the unaccented jas gets svarita by P. 8-4-66 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya and P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau)). ॥9॥ A crowded run of three-and-a-half pages; outline only; numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हे शतक्रतो (he śatakrato) — O Indra | सः त्वम् (saḥ tvam) — such as you are | नः (naḥ) — our | इमम् (imam) — this | कामम् (kāmam) — desired fruit (the object wished for) | गोभिः अश्वैः (gobhiḥ aśvaiḥ) — with cows and horses | आ पृण (ā pṛṇa) — fulfil | (वयम्) ((vayam)) — we | स्वाध्यः (svādhyaḥ) — having good power of meditation | त्वा (tvā) — you | स्तवाम (stavāma) — praise.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Give us cows, horses and the like, and fulfil our desired objects. We always praise you with a meditative mind.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Satakratu (Indra) fulfil this our desire by giving us cows and horses. Profoundly meditating we praise you.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

गोभिरश्वैः आपृण (gobhir aśvaiḥ āpṛṇa) — "fill [us] with cows and horses" — that is, fulfil our desire by giving us cows and horses.

स्वाध्यः (svādhyaḥ) — dhyai cintāyām; su-ādhyaḥ: suṣṭhu sarvato dhyāna-yuktāḥ santaḥ: "being thoroughly and on all sides devoted to meditation on you [Indra]" — that is, meditating on you well in the mind.

Close of Sūkta 16. The grammar of Rik 9 ends at the foot of p. 707, followed by an ornament; no large colophon follows, as for Sūktas 14 and 15.

॥ ಹದಿನೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 17 — "indrāvaruṇayor aham" ("The Seventeenth Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 708)

इन्द्रावरुणयोरित्यादिकं नवर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तम् । अत एव नवर्चत्वानुवृत्त्या [?] ऽनुक्रम्यते । इन्द्रावरुणयोरैन्द्रावरुणं युवाकु पादनिचृताविति [?] । अत्र देवता विस्पष्टा । ऋषिच्छन्दसी तु पूर्ववदनुवर्तेते । अयं तु विशेषः । युवाकु हीत्यादिके द्वे ऋचौ पादनिचृन्नामकच्छन्दोयुक्ते ॥ विनियोगस्तु स्मार्तो लैङ्गिको वा कश्चिदवगन्तव्यः ॥

indrāvaruṇayor ity-ādikaṃ navarcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktam | ata eva navarcatvānuvṛttyā [?] 'nukramyate | indrāvaruṇayor aindrāvaruṇaṃ yuvāku pādanicṛtāv iti [?] | atra devatā vispaṣṭā | ṛṣi-chandasī tu pūrvavad anuvartete | ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ | yuvāku hīty-ādike dve ṛcau pādanicṛn-nāmaka-chandoyukte || viniyogas tu smārto laiṅgiko vā kaścid avagantavyaḥ ||

Translation: "The nine-rik sūkta beginning indrāvaruṇayoḥ is the sixth [of this anuvāka]. So the Anukramaṇikā says [the quotation, read as indrāvaruṇayor aindrāvaruṇaṃ yuvāku pādanicṛtau, is uncertain [?]]: 'to Indra and Varuṇa; the two riks yuvāku hi … [are] pādanicṛt'. Here the deity is plain [Indra and Varuṇa]. The ṛṣi and meter continue as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]; but there is this particularity: the two riks beginning yuvāku hi [and indraḥ sahasradāvnām] are in the meter called pādanicṛt. Its application (viniyoga) is to be understood from the smārta or laiṅgika usage [i.e. from the Smṛti or from the sense of the rik]."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The sūkta indrāvaruṇayoḥ is the sixth sūkta of the fourth anuvāka and has nine riks. In the Anukramaṇikā the riks 4 and 5 [yuvāku hi śacīnām and indraḥ sahasradāvnām] are said to be in the meter pādanicṛt. Indra and Varuṇa are the deities. The ṛṣi and meter are as in the earlier sūktas, but those two riks alone have the meter pādanicṛt. The application is to be learnt from the smārta usage.

original pp. 708–711

Sūkta 17, Rik 1

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 17 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 4 ॥ Sūkta — 17 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 32, 33 [?] ॥ small-print Kannada digits, re-read at 300 dpi; reasonably clear, but given [?] as for earlier headings ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–9 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indrāvaruṇau ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — 1–3 and 6–9, Gāyatrī; 4 and 5, Pādanicṛt ॥ as printed: "೧–೩, ೬–೯, ಗಾಯತ್ರೀ । ೪, ೫, ಪಾದನಿಚೃತ್"

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणयोरहं सम्राजोरव आ वृणे । ता नो मृळात ईदृशे ॥१॥

indrāvaruṇayor ahaṃ samrājor ava ā vṛṇe | tā no mṛḷāta īdṛśe ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks are printed in the source; not reproduced, per the convention for the later riks of this volume.

इन्द्रावरुणयोः । अहम् । सम्ऽराजोः । अवः । आ । वृणे ॥ ता । नः । मृळातः । ईदृशे ॥१॥

indrāvaruṇayoḥ | aham | sam-rājoḥ | avaḥ | ā | vṛṇe || tā | naḥ | mṛḷātaḥ | īdṛśe ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ compressed; [?] marks doubtful readings

अहमनुष्ठाता सम्राजोः समीचीनराज्योपेतयोः सम्यग्दीप्यमानयोर्वेन्द्रावरुणयोर्देवयोः सम्बन्ध्यवो रक्षणमा वृणे । सर्वतः प्रार्थये । ता तौ देवावीदृशे एवंविधेऽस्मदीयवरणे निमित्तभूते सति मृळातः । अस्मान्सुखयतः ॥ इन्द्रशब्दो रन्प्रत्ययान्तः । वरुणशब्द उनन्प्रत्ययान्तः । उभौ नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तौ । समासे देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति पूर्वपदस्यानङादेशः । उभे युगपदित्यनुवृत्तौ देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति युगपदुभयपदे प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सम्राजोः । राज दीप्तौ । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । समो मोऽनुस्वारः । पा. [८-३-२३] इत्यनुस्वारे प्राप्ते नो राजि समुः क्वौ । पा. [८-३-२५] इति मकारादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अवः । अव रक्षणादिषु । भावेऽसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ता । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना द्विवचनस्य डादेशः । टिलोपे विभक्तेरुदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरः । मृळातः । मृड सुखने । प्रार्थनायां लिङर्थे लेट् । द्विवचनं तस् । लेटोऽडाटाविति नित्यमडागमः । तुदादिभ्यः शः । जित्त्वाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । ईदृशे । त्यदादिषु दृशोऽनालोचने कञ् च । पा. [३-२-६०] । इतीदंशब्द उपपदे दृशेः कञ् । उपपदसमास । इदंकिमोरीश्की । पा. [६-३-९०] । इतीदमु ईश् । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः । कञः कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । ञित्त्वादुत्तरपदस्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । उपपदसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन तदेव शिष्यते ॥१॥

aham anuṣṭhātā samrājoḥ samīcīna-rājyopetayoḥ samyag-dīpyamānayor vendrāvaruṇayor devayoḥ sambandhy avo rakṣaṇam ā vṛṇe | sarvataḥ prārthaye | tā tau devāv īdṛśe evaṃvidhe 'smadīya-varaṇe nimitta-bhūte sati mṛḷātaḥ | asmān sukhayataḥ || indra-śabdo ran-pratyayāntaḥ | varuṇa-śabda unan-pratyayāntaḥ | ubhau nittvād ādyudāttau | samāse devatā-dvandve ceti pūrvapadasyānaṅādeśaḥ | ubhe yugapad ity anuvṛttau devatā-dvandve ceti yugapad ubhaya-pade prakṛti-svaratvam | samrājoḥ | rāja dīptau | sat-sūd-viṣety-ādinā kvip | samo mo 'nusvāraḥ | pā. [8-3-23] | ity anusvāre prāpte no rāji samuḥ kvau | pā. [8-3-25] | iti makārādeśaḥ | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | avaḥ | ava rakṣaṇādiṣu | bhāve 'sun | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | tā | supāṃ sulug ity-ādinā dvivacanasya ḍādeśaḥ | ṭilope vibhakter udātta-nivṛtti-svaraḥ | mṛḷātaḥ | mṛḍa sukhane | prārthanāyāṃ liṅarthe leṭ | dvivacanaṃ tas | leṭo 'ḍāṭāv iti nityam aḍāgamaḥ | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | ñittvāl laghūpadha-guṇābhāvaḥ | īdṛśe | tyadādiṣu dṛśo 'nālocane kañ ca | pā. [3-2-60] | itīdaṃ-śabda upapade dṛśeḥ kañ | upapada-samāsa | idaṃ-kimor īśkī | pā. [6-3-90] | itīdam u īś | śittvāt sarvādeśaḥ | kañaḥ kittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | ñittvād uttarapadasyādyudāttatvam | upapada-samāse kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvena tad eva śiṣyate ||1||

Translation: "I, the performer [of the rite], choose (ā vṛṇe) — pray for on all sides — the protection (avaḥ) belonging to the two gods Indra and Varuṇa, who are samrājau: possessed of sovereign power, well radiant. May those two gods, on this occasion — which is the occasion of our such choice [prayer] — make us happy (mṛḷātaḥ)." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: indra (Uṇādi ran) and varuṇa (Uṇādi unan), both first-syllable accented through the n-mark; the dvandva of deities takes the substitute ānaṅ for the first member (P. 6-3-26 devatādvandve ca) and both members keep their own accent; samrājoḥ (rāj "to shine", kvip, m for s; P. 8-3-25 no rāji samaḥ kvau; P. 8-3-23 mo 'nusvāraḥ would give an anusvāra, but the rule makes it m); avaḥ (av "to protect", asun, first-syllable accent); tā (the dual ending replaced by ā by P. 7-1-39); mṛḷātaḥ (mṛḍ "to make happy", leṭ in the sense of a wish; the augment aṭ; śa of the tudādi class, no guṇa); īdṛśe (dṛś with kañ after idam, P. 3-2-60 tyadādiṣu dṛśo 'nālocane kañ ca; idam → īś by P. 6-3-90 idaṃkimor īśkī). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 8-3-25, 3-2-60 and 6-3-90 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 712–714 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 1 treats: indrāvaruṇayoḥ (a dvandva indraś ca varuṇaś ca; indra from indi "to be powerful" [sic: the print gives the root as idi/indi with num] with Uṇādi ran [Uṇ. 2-28 as read], the num augment by P. 7-1-58 idito num dhātoḥ; varuṇa from vṛñ "to choose/cover" [or dvi-dāraṇe "to split"] with the Uṇādi unan, guṇa by P. 7-3-84, raparatva by P. 1-1-51, ṇatva by P. 8-4-2 [aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi]; both end in a suffix carrying n, so are first-syllable accented by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; the substitute ānaṅ for the first member by P. 6-3-26 devatādvandve ca, which has the ñ marker so replaces the final letter by P. 1-1-53 ṅic ca; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya P. 8-2-7; both members keep their own accent by P. 6-2-141 devatādvandve ca with ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat P. 6-2-140 [as read]; and the genitive dual os — the Kannada adds a long note, on the compound as an instance of kṛt-derived words, that indrāvaruṇayoḥ in the genitive means "of the two who are the subjects of protection" by P. 2-3-65 kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti — the genitive case after a word ending in a kṛt suffix whose root's agent or object it is: ava "protection", from av + asun, has indrāvaruṇayoḥ as its agent, so the genitive; the same applies to samrājoḥ), samrājoḥ (rāj "to shine", kvip by P. 3-2-61 sat-sūdviṣa-druha-duha-yuja-vida-bhida-chida-jī-nī-rājām upasarge 'pi kvip; sam + rāj, with mo 'nusvāraḥ P. 8-3-23 applying to the m; but no rāji samaḥ kvau P. 8-3-25 gives m itself, hence samrāj), avaḥ (ava rakṣaṇe; sarvadhātubhyo 'sun Uṇ. 4-[?]; n-mark so first-syllable accent; the genitive-agent point above), tā (tad + au; supāṃ sulug… P. 7-1-39 giving ḍā; ṭeḥ dropped by P. 6-4-143 [as read]; the accent of the ending lost by anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ P. 6-1-161), mṛḷātaḥ (mṛḍ sukhane; liṅarthe leṭ P. 3-4-7; tas; leṭo 'ḍāṭau P. 3-4-94 gives the augment aṭ, which, being kit, is the first part of the word; tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ P. 3-1-77; sārvadhātukam apit P. 1-2-4 makes it ṅit, so no guṇa by P. 1-1-5 kṅiti ca; and pugantalaghūpadhasya ca P. 7-3-86 is therefore also barred; ḍ → ḷ in the Veda by the Ṛgvedic rule on ḍ), and īdṛśe (idam + dṛś; P. 3-2-60 tyadādiṣu dṛśo 'nālocane kañ ca: kañ after dṛś in a sense other than seeing when a word of the tyadādi group precedes; the ca adds kvin optionally; the compound upapadam atiṅ P. 2-2-19; supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ P. 2-4-71 drops the case-ending; P. 6-3-90 idaṃkimor īśkī gives īś for idam [īś has the ś marker, so replaces the whole word by P. 1-1-55 anekāl-śit sarvasya]; dṛś + a with no guṇa because kañ is kit; ñ marker gives the accent of the final member by P. 6-1-197 [read as 6-1-193?]; the locative singular ṅi → e; the first-syllable accent of dṛśa retained by the compound rule P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; the whole īdṛśe thus accented on mṛ? — the print ends īdṛśe, ಎಂಬುದು ಮಧ್ಯೋದಾತ್ತ, i.e. "īdṛśe is middle-accented" [?], which I give as read). ॥1॥ Numerals as read; pointers only; a crowded run; outline only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अहम् (aham) — I (the performer of the rite) | सम्राजोः (samrājoḥ) — those who shine well, or those possessed of good sovereignty | इन्द्रावरुणयोः (indrāvaruṇayoḥ) — of Indra and Varuṇa | अवः (avaḥ) — protection | आ वृणे (ā vṛṇe) — I pray for [from all sides] | ता (tā) — those two deities | ईदृशे (īdṛśe) — in this our prayer | नः (naḥ) — to us | मृळातः (mṛḷātaḥ) — let them make us happy.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

I, who have begun the sacrifice, come to Indra and Varuṇa — mighty with radiance and kingship — in order that my sacrifice may be completed in all its parts, and I pray for their protection. May they hear this prayer of mine and make me happy.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

I seek the protection of the sovereign rulers Indra and Varuna; may they both favour us accordingly.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The deities of this sūkta are the two, Indra and Varuṇa. In the Ṛgveda it is seen that two deities are very often invoked together, and praised together. The mantras that praise two deities together (devatādvandva) are called saṃstavika mantras. The chief deities in them are — Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, Brahmaṇaspati, Parvata, Kutsa, Viṣṇu, Vāyu, Mitra, Rudra, Vāta and Parjanya — fourteen in all. For example [the Kannada gives each pair with a citation; the small reference numerals in the print are partly unclear, so each is marked [?] and I give only the part of the reference I can read]:

  • इन्द्राग्नी (indra + agni) — indrāgnī rocanā divaḥ — "Indra and Agni [light up] the bright places of the sky" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-12-9 [?]).
  • इन्द्रासोमा (indra + soma) — indrāsomā sam aghaśaṃsam (Ṛ. Saṃ. [7-104-2 ?]).
  • इन्द्रावरुणा (indra + varuṇa) — indrāvaruṇā yuvam adhvarāya naḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. [8-59-1 ?]).
  • इन्द्रापूषणा (indra + pūṣan) — indrāpūṣaṇā vayam (Ṛ. Saṃ. [6-57-1 ?]).
  • इन्द्राबृहस्पती (indra + bṛhaspati) — idaṃ vām āsye haviḥ priyam indrābṛhaspatī (Ṛ. Saṃ. [4-49-1 ?]).
  • इन्द्राब्रह्मणस्पती (indra + brahmaṇaspati) — [the citation, read as] ā … indrābrahmaṇaspatī haviṣā [?] (the print shows ātyaiṃdrā…; I cannot give this one with confidence; Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]).
  • इन्द्रापर्वता (indra + parvata) — indrāparvatā bṛhatā rathena (Ṛ. Saṃ. [3-53-1 ?]).
  • इन्द्राकुत्सा (indra + kutsa) — indrākutsā vahamānā rathena (Ṛ. Saṃ. [5-31-9 ?]).
  • इन्द्राविष्णू (indra + viṣṇu) — indrāviṣṇū dṛṃhitāḥ śambarasya (Ṛ. Saṃ. [6-69-5 ?]).
  • इन्द्रवायू (indra + vāyu) — indravāyū ime sutāḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-4).
  • मित्रावरुणा (mitra + varuṇa) — ā no mitrāvaruṇā (Ṛ. Saṃ. [3-62-16 ?]).
  • सोमापूषणा (soma + pūṣan) — somāpūṣaṇā jananā rayīṇām (Ṛ. Saṃ. [2-40-1 ?]).
  • सोमारुद्रा (soma + rudra) — somārudrā yuvam etāny asme (Ṛ. Saṃ. [6-74-2 ?]).
  • वातापर्जन्या (vāta + parjanya) — dhartāro divo ṛbhavaḥ suhastā vātāparjanyā mahiṣasya tanyatoḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. [10-66-10 ?]).
  • अग्नीषोमौ (agni + soma) — agnīṣomāv imaṃ su me (Ṛ. Saṃ. [1-93-1 ?]).
  • अग्नीपर्जन्यौ (agni + parjanya) — agnīparjanyāv avataṃ dhiyaṃ me (Ṛ. Saṃ. [6-52-16 ?]).
  • अग्नाविष्णू (agni + viṣṇu) — agnāviṣṇū sajoṣasā (Taittirīya Saṃhitā [4-2-?]).

Each IAST line above is also given in Devanagari in the print's Kannada script; The IAST and the Devanagari heading of the pair are given, as the Kannada glosses supply no English. Glosses of the pairs are the obvious ones — "Indra and Agni", etc. — and are editorial. The Kannada adds that many riks have the dvandva deities in the singular rather than the dual — for example agna indraś ca dāśuṣe duroṇe (Ṛ. Saṃ. [3-25-4 ?]), tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvān (Ṛ. Saṃ. [4-1-4 ?]), marutaḥ pibata ṛtunā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-1 [?]; the print gives "೧-೧೫-೨", i.e. 1-15-2, which is the rik of this very volume, the Rik 15.2 marutaḥ pibata ṛtunā; I follow the print's 1-15-2 [?]).

original pp. 714–718

Sūkta 17, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

गन्तारा हि स्थोऽवसे हवं विप्रस्य मावतः । धर्तारा चर्षणीनाम् ॥२॥

gantārā hi stho 'vase havaṃ viprasya māvataḥ | dhartārā carṣaṇīnām ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

गन्तारा । हि । स्थः । अवसे । हवम् । विप्रस्य । माऽवतः ॥ धर्तारा । चर्षणीनाम् ॥२॥

gantārā | hi | sthaḥ | avase | havam | viprasya | mā-vataḥ || dhartārā | carṣaṇīnām ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्रावरुणा अवसेऽवितुमनुष्ठातारं रक्षितुं मावतो मद्विधस्य विप्रस्य ब्राह्मणर्त्विजो हवमाह्वानं गन्तारौ स्थो हि प्राप्तिशीलौ भवथः खलु । कीदृशौ । चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणां धर्तारौ योगक्षेमसंपादनेन धारयितारौ ॥ गन्तारा । गमेः स्तृच्छीले तृन् । द्विवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्यादिनाकारादेशः । ऋदुशनस्पुरुदंसोऽनेहसां च । पा. [७-१-९४] । इत्यनङ्गुणः । … तृनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । स्थः । अस भुवि । लटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनं थस् । आदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः इति शपो लुक् । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । अवसे । अव रक्षणे । तुमर्थे सेसेनसेनित्यादिना असेन् । नित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तः । हवम् । ह्वेञो बहुलं छन्दसीत्यनेनैमित्तिके संप्रसारणे परपूर्वत्वे च ऋदोरबिति अप् । गुणावादेशौ । अपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव । विप्रस्य । डुवप् बीजसन्ताने । अस्य ऋजेन्द्रेत्यादिना रन् निपातितः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । मावतः । वतुप्प्रकरणे युष्मदस्मद्भ्यां छन्दसि सादृश्य उपसंख्यानम् । पा. [५-२-३९-१] । वतुप् । प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्च । पा. [७-२-९८] । इत्यस्मदो मपर्यन्तस्य मादेशः । आ सर्वनाम्नः । पा. [६-३-९१] । इति दीर्घः । … मतुपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । प्रातिपदिकान्तोदात्तत्वे स एव शिष्यते । धर्तारा । धृञ् धारणे । ण्वुल्तृचौ । पा. [३-१-१३३] । इति तृच् । … चर्षणीनाम् । कृषेराद्येश्च चः । उ. [२-१०३ ?] । इत्यनिप्रत्ययः । … नामि । पा. [६-४-३] । इति दीर्घः ॥२॥

he indrāvaruṇā avase 'vitum anuṣṭhātāraṃ rakṣituṃ māvato madvidhasya viprasya brāhmaṇartvijo havam āhvānaṃ gantārau stho hi prāptiśīlau bhavathaḥ khalu | kīdṛśau | carṣaṇīnāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ dhartārau yogakṣema-saṃpādanena dhārayitārau || gantārā | gameḥ stṛc-chīle tṛn | dvivacanasya supāṃ sulug ity-ādinākārādeśaḥ | ṛd-uśanas-puru-daṃso-'nehasāṃ ca | pā. [7-1-94] | ity anaṅ-guṇaḥ | … tṛno nittvād ādyudāttatvam | sthaḥ | asa bhuvi | laṭi madhyama-puruṣa-dvivacanaṃ thas | ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ iti śapo luk | hi ceti nighāta-pratiṣedhaḥ | avase | ava rakṣaṇe | tumarthe sesenasen ity-ādinā asen | nit-svareṇādyudāttaḥ | havam | hveño bahulaṃ chandasīty anenaimittike saṃprasāraṇe parapūrvatve ca ṛdor ab iti ap | guṇāvādeśau | apaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | dhātu-svara eva | viprasya | ḍuvap bīja-santāne | asya ṛjrendrety-ādinā ran nipātitaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | māvataḥ | vatup-prakaraṇe yuṣmad-asmadbhyāṃ chandasi sādṛśya upasaṃkhyānam | pā. [5-2-39-1] | vatup | pratyayottarapadayoś ca | pā. [7-2-98] | ity asmado mapayantasya mādeśaḥ | ā sarvanāmnaḥ | pā. [6-3-91] | iti dīrghaḥ | … matupaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | prātipadikāntodāttatve sa eva śiṣyate | dhartārā | dhṛñ dhāraṇe | ṇvul-tṛcau | pā. [3-1-133] | iti tṛc | … carṣaṇīnām | kṛṣer ādyeś ca caḥ | u. [2-103 ?] | ity ani-pratyayaḥ | … nāmi | pā. [6-4-3] | iti dīrghaḥ ||2||

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa! You are gantārau — you are given to coming (prāptiśīlau) — to the call (havam) of a vipra, a wise priest such as I (māvataḥ, 'one like me'), in order to protect (avase) the one who performs the rite. Of what sort are you? Dhartārau — upholders of the carṣaṇayaḥ, the people, by securing for them what they have and what they lack [yogakṣema]." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: gantārā (gam with tṛn in the sense of habit, with the dual ending ā by P. 7-1-39 and anaṅ/guṇa by P. 7-1-94 ṛd-uśanas-purudaṃso-'nehasāṃ ca; first-syllable accent through the n-mark of tṛn); sthaḥ (as "to be", laṭ dual thas, śap dropped; the particle hi before it bars the loss of accent); avase (the infinitive asen, by P. 3-4-9 tumarthe sesenasenasena…, with first-syllable accent); havam (hve with saṃprasāraṇa, ap); viprasya (vap "to sow", Uṇādi ran given by nipātana); māvataḥ (mad + vatup, in the sense of resemblance, by the Vārttika on P. 5-2-39 for the Veda; ma for mad by P. 7-2-98, lengthened by P. 6-3-91 ā sarvanāmnaḥ); dhartārā (dhṛ + tṛc by P. 3-1-133 ṇvultṛcau); carṣaṇīnām (kṛṣ with the Uṇādi ani and c for the first letter; the lengthening by P. 6-4-3 nāmi). Grammar, noted briefly; numerals as read; pointers only.

Grammar pages (pp. 716 upper to 718), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: gantārā (gamḷ gatau + tṛn by P. 3-2-135 tācchīlyavayovacanaśaktiṣu cānaś [as read, 3-2-135 tṛn]; gam + tṛ with the num → anusvāra by P. 8-3-24 naś cāpadāntasya jhali, then anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ P. 8-4-58 → ngantṛ / gantṛ [gan-tṛ]; tṛ + au → ā by P. 7-1-39; ṛto ṅi sarvanāmasthānayoḥ P. 7-3-110 for the guṇa of the ṛ; ur aṇ raparaḥ P. 1-1-51; ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ P. 7-4-16 [as read] is the Kannada's note on a rule that does not apply here, since there is no aṅ suffix, hence the guṇa here is by the Prāmādika sūtra [i.e. a form that is not to be derived from that sūtra]; tṛn has n-mark so ñnityādir nityam P. 6-1-197 gives gantṛ first-syllable accent), sthaḥ (as bhuvi, adādi; laṭ thas; śap, luk by P. 2-4-72; śnasor allopaḥ P. 6-4-111; s → ru → visarga; hi ca P. 8-1-34 bars the loss of accent, so sthaḥ would stay accented, but since hi here is just before it with no tiṅ after, P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ does not make it unaccented), avase (ava rakṣaṇe; tumarthe sesenasenasen-kasenādhyaiādhyaike kadhyaikena śadhyaiśadhyaina tavaitaven tavenaḥ P. 3-4-9, a list of infinitive suffixes, among them asen; av + asen → avase; the n-mark gives first-syllable accent), havam (hveñ "to call"; hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam P. 6-1-32; bahulaṃ chandasi P. 6-1-34 makes it aimittika — that is, saṃprasāraṇa applies; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108 pūrvarūpa; ṛdoraP P. 3-3-57 — ap after roots ending in ṛ or u; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ P. 7-3-84; eco 'yavāyāvaḥ P. 6-1-78 gives hav; ap is pit, so unaccented by P. 3-1-4, root accent remains; am with ami pūrvaḥ P. 6-1-107), viprasya (ḍuvap "to sow"; ṛjrendrāgravajravipra… Uṇ. 2-28 as read, ran; first-syllable accent by the n-mark), māvataḥ (yatparimāṇe 'vatup P. 5-2-39; vatup in the sense of resemblance after yuṣmad/asmad in the Veda by the Vārttika vatup prakaraṇe yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ chandasi sādṛśya upasaṃkhyānam; asmad + vat; pratyayottarapadayoś ca P. 7-2-98 gives ma for the part of asmad up to m; ato guṇe P. 6-1-97 pararūpa; mad + vat; ā sarvanāmnaḥ P. 6-3-91 gives ā for the final letter of a pronoun when followed by dṛk, dṛś, vatu, hence mā + vat; akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ P. 6-1-101 → māvat; vatup is pit, so unaccented; mā has the stem accent on the end, hence māvataḥ), dhartārā (dhṛñ dhāraṇe; ṇvultṛcau P. 3-1-133; dhṛ is anudātta in the upadeśa and monosyllabic, so by P. 7-2-10 ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt the iṭ augment that would come by P. 7-2-35 ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ is barred; guṇa by P. 7-3-84, raparatva; au → ā by P. 7-1-39; guṇa of ṛ by P. 7-3-110; upadhā-dīrgha by P. 6-4-11 apṛn-tṛj-ityādi; tṛc has c-mark so end accent by P. 6-1-163 cit; hence dhartā), and carṣaṇīnām (kṛṣ "to scratch", Uṇ. 2-[?] kṛṣer ādyeś ca caḥ, ani suffix, c for k, carṣ + ani; ॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे इन्द्रावरुणौ) ((he indrāvaruṇau)) — O Indra and Varuṇa | चर्षणीनाम् (carṣaṇīnām) — of men | धर्तारौ (dhartārau) — you who bear the burden of getting and keeping | अवसे (avase) — for the protection [of the performer of the sacrifice] | मावतः (māvataḥ) — like me | विप्रस्य (viprasya) — of the priest | हवम् (havam) — the call | गन्तारा स्थः हि (gantārā sthaḥ hi) — you are of a nature to come, surely.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa! You are the ones who look after the welfare (yogakṣema) of men. Therefore, in order to protect priests such as I, you are accustomed to come here in response to my call.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra and Varuna, you are the protectors of the people and you go at the call of a minister like me to protect him.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

विप्रस्य (viprasya) — though the word vipra has the sense "intelligent", the sense "one who praises" fits well here.

मावतः (māvataḥ) — madvidhasya: like me; that is, to a sacrificer who praises you as I do.

धर्तारा (dhartārā) — dhṛñ dhāraṇe: yogakṣema-saṃpādanena dhārayitārau: those who bear the burden of getting and preserving men's welfare; those who are concerned with it.

अनुकामं तर्पयेथामिन्द्रावरुण राय आ । ता वां नेदिष्ठमीमहे ॥३॥

anukāmaṃ tarpayethām indrāvaruṇa rāya ā | tā vāṃ nediṣṭham īmahe ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the shortened indrāvaruṇa; the Pada the long indrāvaruṇā.

anu-kāmam | tarpayethām | indrāvaruṇā | rāyaḥ | ā || tā | vām | nediṣṭham | īmahe ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा हे इन्द्रावरुणौ अनुकामं अस्मदीयाभिलाषमनु रायो धनस्य प्रदानेना तर्पयेथाम् । सर्वतोऽस्मांस्तृप्तान्कुरुतम् । वयं यदा यदा धनं कामयामहे तदा तदा प्रयच्छतमित्यर्थः । ता वां तादृशौ युवां नेदिष्ठमतिशयेन सामीप्यं यथा भवति तथा ईमहे । याचामहे कालविलम्बनं विना धनं दातव्यमित्यर्थः । सप्तदशसु या ज्ञाकर्मस्विमहे इति पठितम् ॥ अनुकामम् । कामस्य पश्चादनुकामम् । अथवा कामे कामेऽनुकामम् । अनुरिह पश्चादर्थे । अथवा वीप्सालक्षणे यथार्थे । योग्यता वीप्सा पदार्थानतिवृत्तिः सादृश्यं चेति चत्वारो हि यथार्था गृहीताः । अव्ययं विभक्तीत्यादिना । पा. [२-१-६] । अव्ययीभावसमासः । अव्ययीभावश्च । पा. [१-१-४१] । इत्यव्ययसंज्ञा । अव्ययादाप्सुपः । पा. [२-४-८२] । इति प्राप्तस्य लुकोऽपवादो नाव्ययीभावादतोऽम्त्वपञ्चम्याः । पा. [५-३-५५] । इष्ठन् । अन्तिकबाढयोर्नेदसाधौ । पा. [५-३-६३] । इति नेदादेशः । यस्येति लोपः । इष्ठन्प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ईमहे । ईङ् गतौ । ङित्त्वादात्मनेपदम् । बहुलं छन्दसीति श्यनो लुक् । निघातः ॥३॥

indrāvaruṇā he indrāvaruṇau anukāmaṃ asmadīyābhilāṣam anu rāyo dhanasya pradānenā tarpayethām | sarvato 'smāṃs tṛptān kurutam | vayaṃ yadā yadā dhanaṃ kāmayāmahe tadā tadā prayacchatam ity arthaḥ | tā vāṃ tādṛśau yuvāṃ nediṣṭham atiśayena sāmīpyaṃ yathā bhavati tathā īmahe | yācāmahe kāla-vilambanaṃ vinā dhanaṃ dātavyam ity arthaḥ | saptadaśasu yā jñā-karmasv imahe iti paṭhitam || anukāmam | kāmasya paścād anukāmam | athavā kāme kāme 'nukāmam | anur iha paścād arthe | athavā vīpsā-lakṣaṇe yathārthe | yogyatā vīpsā padārthānativṛttiḥ sādṛśyaṃ ceti catvāro hi yathārthā gṛhītāḥ | avyayaṃ vibhaktītyādinā | pā.
