[2-4-83] | iti vibhakter amādeśaḥ | samāsasyety antodāttatvam | tarpayethām | tṛpa prīṇane | ṇijantāt kartṛsthābhiprāye loṭ | … āthām | ṭer ettvam | āmetaḥ | … āto 'ṅ | … | indrāvaruṇā | supāṃ sulug iti dvivacanasyākāraḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | saṃhitāyām ākārasya hrasvatvam | rāyaḥ | rai śabdaḥ … jasi | rāyaḥ | … | tā | supāṃ sulug iti vibhakter ākāraḥ | vām | padāt parasyādyudāttasya vāmādeśo 'nudāttaḥ | nediṣṭham | antikasyātiśayenāntikam | atiśāyane tamab-iṣṭhanau | pā. [5-3-55] | iṣṭhan | antika-bāḍhayor nedasādhau | pā. [5-3-63] | iti nedādeśaḥ | yasyeti lopaḥ | iṣṭhan-pratyayasya nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | īmahe | īṅ gatau | ṅittvād ātmanepadam | bahulaṃ chandasīti śyano luk | nighātaḥ ||3||

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa! Anukāmam — according to our wish — satisfy (ā tarpayethām) us on all sides by giving wealth (rāyaḥ). The sense is: whenever we desire wealth, give it then. Such as you are, we ask you (īmahe) nediṣṭham — in the manner of being most near; the sense: we beg that wealth should be given without delay. Īmahe is read among the seventeen words for 'asking' (yācñā-karman)." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: anukāmam (kāmasya paścāt, or kāme kāme — here anu has the sense 'after' or 'each, in each case' [vīpsā]; an avyayībhāva compound by P. 2-1-6, with the name avyaya by P. 1-1-41; the case-ending would be dropped by P. 2-4-82 avyayād āpsupaḥ, but P. 2-4-83 nāvyayībhāvād ato 'm tv apañcamyāḥ gives am instead — except in the ablative; the accent of the final member of the compound); tarpayethām (tṛp "to please", causative; loṭ in the ātmanepada for the agent-sense; dual āthām, ṭi → e by P. 3-4-79, āmetaḥ P. 3-4-90); indrāvaruṇā (the dual ā; vocative accent; shortened in the Saṃhitā); rāyaḥ (rai + jas/as with āy, ru, visarga); tā; vām (the unaccented substitute for yuṣmad + au, after a word, by P. 8-1-20 yuṣmadasmador…); nediṣṭham (antika + iṣṭhan by P. 5-3-55 with neda for antika by P. 5-3-63; yasyeti ca; first-syllable accent through the n-mark of iṣṭhan); īmahe (īṅ "to go", ātmanepada from the ṅ-mark, śyan dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; the verb unaccented). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 2-1-6, 1-1-41, 2-4-82, 2-4-83, 5-3-55 and 5-3-63 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 719 lower to 723 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats: anukāmam (kāmasya paścāt or kāme kāme; anu is paścāt "after" in the first reading and yathārtha-vīpsā "each in turn" in the second; the Kannada lists the four senses of yathā — fitness, distribution, non-transgression of the sense of a word, and resemblance — and quotes the sūtra avyayaṃ vibhaktisamīpasamṛddhivyṛddhyarthābhāvātyayāsampratiśabdaprādurbhāvapaścādyathānupūrvyayaugapadyasādṛśyasampattisākalyāntavacaneṣu P. 2-1-6 — the sixteen meanings, beginning with vibhakti and ending with anta, as listed; the compound is avyayībhāva; avyayībhāvaś ca P. 1-1-41 gives it the name avyaya; P. 2-4-82 avyayād āpsupaḥ would drop the case-ending, but the exception nāvyayībhāvād ato 'm tv apañcamyāḥ P. 2-4-83 gives am after an a-ending avyayībhāva, except in the ablative, so the dropping does not occur, and am is substituted — anukāma + am, ami pūrvaḥ P. 6-1-107 → anukāmam; the compound's end accent by P. 6-1-223 samāsasya; am unaccented by P. 3-1-4; the substituted single vowel accented by P. 8-2-5 ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ), tarpayethām (tṛp prīṇane; tatprayojako hetuś ca P. 1-4-55 gives the causal agent the name hetu; hetumati ca P. 3-1-26 gives ṇic; the ṇic ending root takes ātmanepada by P. 1-3-74 ṇicaś ca in the agent-sense kartṛsthābhiprāye kriyāphale; tṛp + i + āthām; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e P. 3-4-79; āmetaḥ P. 3-4-90; guṇa of the ṛ by P. 7-3-86 pugantalaghūpadhasya ca; śap by P. 3-1-68 and guṇa by P. 7-3-84; eco 'yavāyāvaḥ; the āthām is not pit, so ñit by P. 1-2-4; āto ṅitaḥ P. 7-2-81 gives iy for the ā of a ṅit ending after a, and ad guṇaḥ P. 6-1-87 and lopo vyor vali P. 6-1-66 drop the y, giving tarpayethām; the Kannada's long note on āto yeyaḥ P. 7-2-80 — whether yā or yāsṭ takes iy — concludes that in tarpay-e-th-ām neither is present, so the iy of that sūtra does not arise, and the sūtra's use in explaining the shape of iya is prāmādika), indrāvaruṇā (explained at indrāvaruṇayor aham, Rik 1; here the vocative dual au → ā by P. 7-1-39 and savarṇadīrgha; at the start of the pāda so not unaccented, and first-syllable accented by P. 6-1-198; shortened in the Saṃhitā), rāyaḥ (rai — the word meaning wealth — + as; rāyo hali P. 7-2-85 gives rā for rai before a consonant; before a vowel ai → āy by P. 6-1-78; s → ru → visarga; the ending is accented by P. 6-1-171 ūḍidampadādyappumrai-dyubhyaḥ), tā (tad + au; P. 7-1-39 ḍā; tyadādīnām aḥ P. 7-2-102; ato guṇe; savarṇadīrgha), vām (follows a word; hence yuvām, in the dual accusative, replaced by the unaccented vām by P. 8-1-20 yuṣmadasmador ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayor vāṃnāvau), nediṣṭham (atiśayena antikam; atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau P. 5-3-55; antikabāḍhayor nedasādhau P. 5-3-63 [as read] gives neda for antika; yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148; iṣṭhan has the n-mark, so first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197), and īmahe (īṅ gatau — the ṅ shows ātmanepada by P. 1-3-12 anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam; laṭ mahiṅ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; divādibhyaḥ śyan P. 3-1-69; bahulaṃ chandasi P. 2-4-73 drops śyan; hence īmahe; unaccented by P. 8-1-28). ॥3॥ A crowded run of four pages; outline only; numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā) — O Indra and Varuṇa | अनुकामम् (anukāmam) — in accordance with our wishes, or one by one each of our wishes | रायः (rāyaḥ) — by giving wealth | आ तर्पयेथाम् (ā tarpayethām) — satisfy [us] | ता (tā) — such [as you are] | वाम् (vām) — you two | नेदिष्ठम् (nediṣṭham) — in the nearest manner (that is, without any delay) | ईमहे (īmahe) — we praise.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa! We praise you in order to be near you for the sake of wealth and the like. As soon as we ask, give us the wealth we need.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra and Varuna, satisfy us with wealth according to our desires. We therefore pray you to be nearest to us.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अनुकामम् (anukāmam) — kāmasya paścād anukāmam; or kāme kāme 'nukāmam. Here anu has the sense paścāt "after", or the sense of vīpsā "each, one by one" [the yathārtha]. [asmadīyam abhilāṣam anu:] "according to our wishes", or "each and every one of the things we desire".

नेदिष्ठम् (nediṣṭham) — atiśayena sāmīpyaṃ yathā bhavati tathā; atiśayenāntikam: "very near" — "you should be very near, so as to give us what we need".

ईमहे (īmahe) — īmahe, among the seventeen words of the group beginning with yāma [yāmaḥ?] that mean "to ask" (yācñā-karman), the word īmahe is read (Nighaṇṭu 3-19 [?]); so īmahe means "we ask, we beg".

original pp. 723–727

Sūkta 17, Rik 4 (meter Pādanicṛt)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युवाकु हि शचीनां युवाकु सुमतीनाम् । भूयाम वाजदाव्नाम् ॥४॥

yuvāku hi śacīnāṃ yuvāku sumatīnām | bhūyāma vājadāvnām ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युवाकु । हि । शचीनाम् । युवाकु । सुऽमतीनाम् ॥ भूयाम । वाजऽदाव्नाम् ॥४॥

yuvāku | hi | śacīnām | yuvāku | su-matīnām || bhūyāma | vāja-dāvnām ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हि यस्मात्कारणाच्छचीनामस्मदीयकर्मणां सम्बन्धि सोमरूपं हविर्युवाकु वसतीवर्येकधनात्मकैरुदकैः पयःसक्त्वादिद्रव्यान्तैश्च मिश्रितं [?] । तथा सुमतीनां शोभनबुद्धियुक्तानामृत्विजां स्तोत्ररूपं वचनमपि युवाकु नानाविधैः स्तुत्यगुणैर्मिश्रितम् । तस्मात्कारणात् हे इन्द्रावरुणौ तथाविधं हविः स्वीकुर्वतोर्युवयोः प्रसादाद्वयं वाजदाव्नामन्नप्रदानां पुरुषाणां मध्ये मुख्या भूयाम । भवेम । आपोज्योतिरित्यादिषु षट्त्रिंशत्सङ्ख्याकेषु कर्मनामसु शची शमीति पठितम् ॥ युवाकु । यु मिश्रणे । कटिकुषिभ्यां काकुः [?] । उ. [३-४२?] । इत्यत्र बाहुलकाद्यतेरपि काकुः प्रत्ययः । … शचीनाम् । शचीशब्दः केषांचिन्मते शार्ङ्गरवादिः ङीन् । नित्त्वाद्याद्युदात्तः [?] … सुमतीनाम् । विद्याम सुमतीनाम् । ऋ. सं. [१-४-३] । इत्युक्तम् । भूयाम । भू सत्तायाम् । प्रार्थनायां लिङ् । उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचनं मस् । … यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च । पा. [३-४-१०३] । इति यासुडागमः … सकारलोपः । … वाजदाव्नाम् । वाजं ददतीति वाजदाव्नः । आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च । पा. [३-२-७४] । इति वनिप् । … ।

hi yasmāt kāraṇāc chacīnām asmadīya-karmaṇāṃ sambandhi soma-rūpaṃ havir yuvāku vasatīvary-ekadhanātmakair udakaiḥ payaḥ-saktv-ādi-dravyāntaiś ca miśritaṃ [?] | tathā sumatīnāṃ śobhana-buddhi-yuktānām ṛtvijāṃ stotra-rūpaṃ vacanam api yuvāku nānā-vidhaiḥ stutya-guṇair miśritam | tasmāt kāraṇāt he indrāvaruṇau tathā-vidhaṃ haviḥ svīkurvatoḥ yuvayoḥ prasādād vayaṃ vājadāvnām anna-pradānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ madhye mukhyā bhūyāma | bhavema | āpo-jyotir ity-ādiṣu ṣaṭtriṃśat-saṅkhyākeṣu karma-nāmasu śacī śamī iti paṭhitam || yuvāku | yu miśraṇe | kaṭi-kuṣibhyāṃ kākuḥ [?] | u. [3-42?] | ity atra bāhulakād yater api kākuḥ pratyayaḥ | … śacīnām | śacī-śabdaḥ keṣāṃcin mate śārṅgaravādiḥ ṅīn | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ [?] … sumatīnām | vidyāma sumatīnām | ṛ. saṃ. [1-4-3] | ity uktam | bhūyāma | bhū sattāyām | prārthanāyāṃ liṅ | uttama-puruṣa-bahuvacanaṃ mas | … yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca | pā. [3-4-103] | iti yāsuḍāgamaḥ … sakāralopaḥ | … vājadāvnām | vājaṃ dadatīti vājadāvnaḥ | āto maninkvanibvanipaś ca | pā. [3-2-74] | iti vanip | …

Translation: "Because (hi) the soma-oblation belonging to our rites (śacīnām) is yuvāku — mixed — with waters called vasatīvarī [the water used at the soma pressing] and with milk, flour (saktu) and other substances [the clause is partly unclear, marked [?]]; and likewise the words of praise of the priests of good mind (sumatīnām) are yuvāku — mingled with praise of many kinds of qualities: therefore, O Indra and Varuṇa, by the favour of you two who accept such an oblation, may we become (bhūyāma) the foremost among those who give food (vājadāvnām). Among the thirty-six words for 'action' beginning with āpaḥ, śacī is read [Nighaṇṭu 2-1, cited 'ni. 2-1' in the Kannada; the numerals are as read [?]]." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: yuvāku (yu "to mix" with the Uṇādi kāku, which the Kannada gives as kaṭikuṣibhyāṃ kākuḥ [?] — by bāhulaka extended also to yu; first-syllable accent by the suffix); śacīnām (śacī by some in the śārṅgaravādi list, with ṅīn); sumatīnām (explained at Rik 1.4.3 [vidyāma sumatīnām]); bhūyāma (bhū "to be", the liṅ of prayer, first plural mas, the augment yāsuṭ by P. 3-4-103 and the loss of s); vājadāvnām (vāja + dā + vanip by P. 3-2-74 ato manin-kvanib-vanipaś ca). Grammar, noted briefly; the Uṇādi number is uncertain.

Grammar pages (pp. 726 lower to 727), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: yuvāku (yu miśraṇe; Uṇ. kaṭikuṣibhyāṃ kākaḥ [the Kannada discusses that kaṭ 'to cover' and kuṣ 'to tear' are the roots of that sūtra; some read kaṭikuśibhyāṃ, a reading that does not suit kapāka [?]; with bāhulaka the suffix kāku is added after yu also; the k of kāku is it, so no guṇa; acchnudhātu [aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau] P. 6-4-77 gives uv for u before a vowel-initial suffix; yu + aku → yuvāku; the first syllable is accented by ādyudāttaś ca P. 3-1-3 which accents the first vowel of a suffix; so yuvāku is middle-accented), śacīnām (śacī — from śac — in the śārṅgaravādi group [by the view of some]; ñīn — śārṅgaravādibhyo ṅīn P. 4-1-73; the suffix has ñ so ñnityādir nityam P. 6-1-197 gives first-syllable accent; the Kāśikā's vṛtti says in the sūtra ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat P. 6-2-140 that śacī has first-syllable accent), sumatīnām (explained at 1.4.3 [vidyāma sumatīnām]), bhūyāma (bhū sattāyām with the liṅ of prayer, first plural mas; the s dropped by P. 3-4-97 nityaṃ ṅitaḥ; yāsuṭ P. 3-4-103; yāsuṭ is ṭit, hence the first part of the suffix; the u of bhū + yāsa → bhūyāsma; sārvadhātukam apit; liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya P. 7-2-79 drops the s of yāsuṭ; śap (here by bahulaṃ chandasi luk); sati śiṣṭatve [the paribhāṣā that the accent of the śiṣṭa is stronger]; the Kannada concludes the stronger accent remains), vājadāvnām (vājam dadati iti; vāja is the object-word, dā + vanip by P. 3-2-74 [which in the Veda applies even with an upasarga or upapada]; vāja + dāvan, kṛttaddhita… P. 1-2-46 gives the name prātipadika; supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ P. 2-4-71 drops the case-ending; vanip is pit, so unaccented by P. 3-1-4, while dā has the accent of its root; vājam + dāvan by P. 3-2-19 upapadam atiṅ; then gatikārakopapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139 gives the accent of the final member; the genitive plural ām; vājadāvan + ām; ñibhaṃ P. 1-4-18 yaci bham gives the name bha; āllopo 'nasya P. 6-4-134 drops the a of an of the stem when it is bha — hence vājadāv-n-ām; the n of an [vājadāvan, here n + ām]; lopo vyor vali P. 6-1-66 would drop the v before a consonant [n], but acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau P. 1-1-57 makes the dropped a a sthānivat for purposes of the preceding rules; so the v is not dropped: vājadāvnām). ॥4॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हि (hi) — because | शचीनाम् (śacīnām) — of the [rites] done by us (the soma-oblation relating to them) | युवाकु (yuvāku) — [it is] mixed with milk, flour and other substances | सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — of the priests of good understanding (their praises) | युवाकु (yuvāku) — [they are] joined with various qualities | वाजदाव्नाम् (vājadāvnām) — among those who give food (the oblation) | भूयाम (bhūyāma) — may we be [accepted, by the grace of you who have accepted our oblation].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The oblation we offer to you is mingled with milk, flour and other substances; and the priests praise you with praises full of manifold excellences. Satisfied with these two, make us foremost among the givers of food, or the best of givers.

॥ English Translation ॥

The mingled libations of our pious rites, the different praises of our right-minded priests are prepared; may we be included among the givers of food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

युवाकु (yuvāku) — vasatīvarī-ekadhanātmakair udakaiḥ payaḥ-saktv-ādi-dravyāntaiś ca miśritam: the commentator here explains the word as "mixed with water, milk and saktu (meal), and the like, prepared for the soma-offering". Its second occurrence in the rik means a mingling of praises, or the rendering "a union of various kinds of praises". And in the following riks the word yuvāku is used:

अश्विना मधुषुत्तमो युवाकुः सोमस्तं पातमा गतं दुरोणे । (ऋ. सं. [२-४६?-?]) aśvinā madhuṣuttamo yuvākuḥ somas taṃ pātam ā gataṃ duroṇe | (ṛ. saṃ. [?])

ता विद्वांसा हवामहे वां ता नो विद्वांसा मन्म वोचेतमद्य । प्रार्चद्दयमानो युवाकुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-१२०-३ ?]) tā vidvāṃsā havāmahe vāṃ tā no vidvāṃsā manma vocetam adya | prārcad dayamāno yuvākuḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. [1-120-3 ?])

दुहीयन्मित्रधितये युवाकु रायेच नो मिमीतं वाजवत्यै । (ऋ. सं. [१-१२०-८ ?]) duhīyan mitradhitaye yuvāku rāye ca no mimītaṃ vājavatyai | (ṛ. saṃ. [1-120-8 ?])

धामानि मित्रावरुणा युवाकुः सं यो यूथेव जनिमानि चष्टे । (ऋ. सं. [२-४०?-?]) dhāmāni mitrāvaruṇā yuvākuḥ saṃ yo yūtheva janimāni caṣṭe | (ṛ. saṃ. [?])

आवोर्वां नूनमश्विना युवाकुर्हुवे यद्वां सुते माध्वी वसूयुः । (ऋ. सं. [२-४२?-४]) āvor vāṃ nūnam aśvinā yuvākur huve yad vāṃ sute mādhvī vasūyuḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. [?])

उत त्यं भुज्युमश्विना सखायो मध्ये जहुर्दुरेवासः समुद्रे । निरीं पर्षदरावा यो युवाकुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [२-४८?-२]) uta tyaṃ bhujyum aśvinā sakhāyo madhye jahur durevāsaḥ samudre | nir īm parṣad arāvā yo yuvākuḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. [?])

The mantra texts above are as read from the Kannada print; the numerals of every reference are small and all are marked [?], as they are incompletely read. The English glosses of these riks are not given in the source. In these riks the commentator has taken yuvāku as "desiring you" [yuvāṃ kāmayamānaḥ], that is, "one who seeks you" or "one for whom you are desirable", besides the sense "mixture" given above; but there seems to be some one fixed meaning proper to this word.

शचीनाम् (śacīnām) — among the śloka-words beginning with dharā [dharā…], śacī is read in the list of the fifty-seven [?] words for speech (vāṅnāma) (Ni. [1-11 ?]); so śacī means "speech". Again, śacī is read among the words for 'action' (karma-nāma), beginning with apaḥ, aḥnaḥ (Ni. [2-1 ?]), so it also means "action". Again, among the thirteen words for 'wisdom' (prajñā) beginning with ketaḥ, ketu (Ni. [3-9 ?]), śacī is read, so it also means "intellect". Though śacī thus has three senses — speech, action, intellect — the commentator gives primacy here to "action". Yāska too, with the rik

त्रयः केशिन ऋतुथा विचक्षते संवत्सरे वपत एक एषाम् । विश्वमेको अभि चष्टे शचीभिर्ध्राजिरेकस्य ददृशे न रूपम् ॥ trayaḥ keśina ṛtuthā vicakṣate saṃvatsare vapata eka eṣām | viśvam eko abhi caṣṭe śacībhir dhrājir ekasya dadṛśe na rūpam || (ṛ. saṃ. [1-164-44])

(three long-haired ones, who look on [the world] by the seasons; in the year one of them shaves; one looks at the whole [world] with his śacī; the course of one is seen, but not his form) — while explaining it says viśvam eko 'bhi vipaśyati karmabhir ("the one looks at all by his acts"), giving the sense "action" to śacī; and in explaining a rik in context, one may take any of the three senses of śacī as needed.

सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — śobhana-buddhi-yuktānām ṛtvijām: of the priests with good intelligence; or of the people with good minds.

वाजदाव्नाम् (vājadāvnām) — vājam annaṃ dadātīti vājadāvānaḥ teṣām: of those who give food, or offering. The commentator supplies the word mukhyāḥ ("chief") to complete the sense: "among those who give [i.e. offer] the chief ones". On the whole, the sense of this rik is somewhat disjointed; the meaning is not quite clear.

original pp. 728–732

Sūkta 17, Rik 5 (meter Pādanicṛt)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रः सहस्रदाव्नां वरुणः शंस्यानाम् । क्रतुर्भवत्युक्थ्यः ॥५॥

indraḥ sahasradāvnāṃ varuṇaḥ śaṃsyānām | kratur bhavaty ukthyaḥ ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रः । सहस्रऽदाव्नाम् । वरुणः । शंस्यानाम् ॥ क्रतुः । भवति । उक्थ्यः ॥५॥

indraḥ | sahasra-dāvnām | varuṇaḥ | śaṃsyānām || kratuḥ | bhavati | ukthyaḥ ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अयमिन्द्रः सहस्रदाव्नां सहस्रसंख्याकधनप्रदानां मध्ये क्रतुर्धनदानास्य [?] कर्ता भवति । प्रभूतं ददातीत्यर्थः । तथा वरुणः शंस्यानां स्तुत्यानां मध्ये उक्थ्यः स्तुत्यो भवति । अतिशयेन स्तुत्य इत्यर्थः ॥ वरुणः उनन्प्रत्यययो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । शंस्यानाम् । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । ईडवन्दवृशंसदुहां ण्यतः । क्रतुः । कृञः केतुः । उ. [१-२८] । इति केतुः । उक्थ्यः । उक्थं शस्त्रम् । तेन स्तुत्येन तत्र भव उक्थ्यः । भवे छन्दसि । पा. [४-४-११०] । इति यत् । यस्येति लोपः । … ॥५॥

ayam indraḥ sahasradāvnāṃ sahasra-saṅkhyāka-dhana-pradānāṃ madhye kratur dhana-dānāsya [?] kartā bhavati | prabhūtaṃ dadātīty arthaḥ | tathā varuṇaḥ śaṃsyānāṃ stutyānāṃ madhye ukthyaḥ stutyo bhavati | atiśayena stutya ity arthaḥ || varuṇaḥ unan-pratyayo nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | śaṃsyānām | ṛhaloṇ ṇyat | īḍa-vanda-vṛ-śaṃsa-duhāṃ ṇyataḥ | kratuḥ | kṛñaḥ ketuḥ | u. [1-28] | iti ketuḥ | ukthyaḥ | uktham śastram | tena stutyena tatra bhava ukthyaḥ | bhave chandasi | pā. [4-4-110] | iti yat | yasyeti lopaḥ | … ||5||

Translation: "Among the sahasradāvānaḥ — those who give thousands of [gifts of] wealth — this Indra is a kratu, the performer of acts of giving; the sense is that he gives abundantly. Likewise Varuṇa, among those worthy of praise (śaṃsyānām), is ukthya, worthy of praise — praiseworthy in the highest degree." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: varuṇaḥ (the Uṇādi unan, first-syllable accent); śaṃsyānām (śaṃs with ṇyat by P. 3-1-124 ṛhaloṇ ṇyat, the accent of P. 6-1-215 īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ); kratuḥ (kṛ with the Uṇādi ketu [Uṇ. 1-28, as read]); ukthyaḥ ("what is in the uktha, the recitation"; yat by P. 4-4-110 bhave chandasi; yasyeti ca). Grammar, noted briefly.

Grammar pages (pp. 729 lower half–732 upper half), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: varuṇaḥ (vṛñ with the Uṇādi unan, Uṇ. 3-[?] kvyādāribhyaḥ unan [as read]; first-syllable accent by the n-mark), śaṃsyānām (śaṃsu stutau; ṛhaloṇ ṇyat P. 3-1-124; tit svaritam P. 6-1-185 would give a svarita, but the special īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ P. 6-1-214 [as read] gives the first-syllable accent), kratuḥ (ḍukṛñ karaṇe; kṛñaḥ ketuḥ [Uṇ. 1-28]; lasya taddhite [laśakvataddhite P. 1-3-8] makes the initial k of a suffix an it — hence the Kannada notes the k; iko yaṇaci P. 6-1-77 gives y; kṛ + tu with the ṛ → ra by P. 1-1-51 [guṇa and raparatva]; the end accent, by the suffix), and — at great length — ukthyaḥ, the grammarians' dispute about its accent: uktha means śastra, a recitation without chant (the Kannada quotes the Yājñikas' definition aprāgītamantrasādhyaguṇaviśiṣṭaguṇābhidhānaṃ śastram); ukthe bhavaḥ — bhave chandasi P. 4-4-110 gives yat; the case-ending is dropped, uktha + ya; yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148 drops the a; so ukthya; yat has the t-mark, so by P. 6-1-185 tit svaritam the last syllable of the suffix is svarita; though ukthya is a word with two syllables [ukth-ya, in the Kannada's reckoning of ac], and so P. 6-1-213 yato 'nāvaḥ [the accent of words in yat that are not nau] would give a first-syllable accent — as in tīrthya and kūpya — in the Veda, where all rules are optional [P. paribhāṣā sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante], this accent does not apply; the Kannada then sets out the competing claims of yasyeti ca (P. 6-4-148), tit svaritam and yato 'nāvaḥ, applying the paribhāṣās vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam (P. 1-4-2), kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgi nityam, antaraṅgaṃ bahiraṅgāt, asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge and vārṇād āṅgaṃ balīyaḥ, and concludes — after about two-and-a-half pages — that ukthya in ukthyaḥ, as in ūrmyāya and sūrmyāya, should have the svarita accent as given by Pāṇini himself, and tīrthya's first-syllable accent is then the Vedic exception; "in some place or other one must grant that something is Vedic; in no way can both be escaped". ॥5॥ A very crowded run; outline only; numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(अयम्) इन्द्रः ((ayam) indraḥ) — [this] Indra [who, having accepted the oblations described above, gives us wealth] | सहस्रदाव्नाम् (sahasradāvnām) — among those who give thousands (of wealth) | क्रतुः (kratuḥ) — the performer [of giving] | भवति (bhavati) — becomes | वरुणः (varuṇaḥ) — Varuṇa | शंस्यानाम् (śaṃsyānām) — among those who are praised | उक्थ्यः (ukthyaḥ) — [especially] praiseworthy | भवति (bhavati) — becomes.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

As described before, Indra, satisfied, gives us wealth as we need it; in the same way Varuṇa is the one especially praised by us.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra is a giver among the givers of thousands; Varuna is to be praised among those who deserve to be praised.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of this rik is clearer if the meaning given above is varied a little: Indra is famed among those who give wealth and other things by the thousand, and Varuṇa among those who are much praised; their acts are worthy of praise.

क्रतुः (kratuḥ) — among the words for 'action' beginning with apaḥ, aḥnaḥ [the print "ಅಪಃ ಅಹ್ನಃ"], kratu is read (Ni. 2-1 [?]); so kratu means "action". Here it means the daring action done by Indra and Varuṇa, or the act of giving wealth to people.

उक्थ्यः (ukthyaḥ) — uktham śastram | tena stutyatvena tatra bhava ukthyaḥ: uktha is a śastra — a mantra recited without singing; "worthy of being praised by reciting that mantra" is the sense of ukthya. Here the sense is that the acts of giving wealth and the like done by Indra and Varuṇa are worthy of praise.

original pp. 732–735

Sūkta 17, Rik 6

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तयोरिदवसा वयं सनेम नि च धीमहि । स्यादुत प्ररेचनम् ॥६॥

tayor id avasā vayaṃ sanema ni ca dhīmahi | syād uta prarecanam ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तयोः । इत् । अवसा । वयम् । सनेम । नि । च । धीमहि ॥ स्यात् । उत । प्रऽरेचनम् ॥६॥

tayoḥ | it | avasā | vayam | sanema | ni | ca | dhīmahi || syāt | uta | pra-recanam ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

तयोरित्पूर्वोक्तयोरिन्द्रावरुणयोरेवावसा रक्षणेन वयमनुष्ठातारः सनेम । संभजेमहि धनमिति शेषः । नि धीमहि च । प्राप्ते धने यावदपेक्षितं तावद्भुक्त्वा ततोऽवशिष्टं धनं [?] निधिरूपेण स्थापयेमानुष्ठातारः । उतापि च प्ररेचनं भुक्तान्निहिताच्च प्रकर्षेणाधिकं धनं स्यात् । ससद्येताम् [?] ॥ अवसा । असुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वयम् । यूयं हि ष्ठेत्यृ. सं. [१-१५-२ ?] इत्यत्र यदुक्तं तदत्र द्रष्टव्यम् । सनेम । आशिषि लिङ् । तस्य मस् । नित्यं ङितः । इत्यनेन सलोपः । यासुट् । लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य । पा. [७-२-७९] । … सनेमेति पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । धीमहि । दुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः । आशिषि लिङः । … महिङ् । … सीयुट् । … लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य । … ईडागमः । … आतो लोप इटि च । पा. [६-४-६४] । इत्याकारलोपः । … निघातः । स्यात् । अस भुवि । विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रणाधीष्टसंप्रश्नप्रार्थनेषु लिङ् । पा. [३-३-१६१] । … यासुट् … । आदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः इति शपो लुक् । श्नसोरल्लोपः । … निघातः । उत । निपातः [?] । प्ररेचनम् । रिचिर् विरेचने । … भावे ल्युट् । … प्रादिसमासः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥६॥

tayor it pūrvoktayor indrāvaruṇayor evāvasā rakṣaṇena vayam anuṣṭhātāraḥ sanema | saṃbhajemahi dhanam iti śeṣaḥ | ni dhīmahi ca | prāpte dhane yāvad apekṣitaṃ tāvad bhuktvā tato 'vaśiṣṭaṃ dhanaṃ [?] nidhi-rūpeṇa sthāpayem' ānuṣṭhātāraḥ | utāpi ca prarecanaṃ bhuktān nihitāc ca prakarṣeṇādhikaṃ dhanaṃ syāt | sasadyetām [?] || avasā | asun | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | vayam | yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhety ṛ. saṃ. [1-15-2 ?] ity atra yad uktaṃ tad atra draṣṭavyam | sanema | āśiṣi liṅ | tasya mas | nityaṃ ṅitaḥ | ity anena salopaḥ | yāsuṭ | liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya | pā. [7-2-79] | … sanemeti pādāditvān nighātābhāvaḥ | dhīmahi | dudhāñ dhāraṇa-poṣaṇayoḥ | āśiṣi liṅaḥ | … mahiṅ | … sīyuṭ | … liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya | … īḍāgamaḥ | … āto lopa iṭi ca | pā. [6-4-64] | ity ākāralopaḥ | … nighātaḥ | syāt | asa bhuvi | vidhi-nimantraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭa-saṃpraśna-prārthaneṣu liṅ | pā. [3-3-161] | … yāsuṭ … | ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ iti śapo luk | śnasor allopaḥ | … nighātaḥ | uta | nipātaḥ [?] | prarecanam | ricir virecane | … bhāve lyuṭ | … prādi-samāsaḥ | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||6||

Translation: "Through the protection of those same (it) two, Indra and Varuṇa, we who perform the rite may sanema — may we obtain (saṃbhajemahi) wealth (the word 'wealth' being supplied) — and ni dhīmahi — when the wealth has come, having enjoyed as much as is needed, let us lay up the remaining wealth as a treasure [the clause is partly unclear, marked [?]]. Uta — and further — may there be prarecana, an excess: wealth in excess, above what is eaten and what is laid by." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: avasā (asun, first-syllable accent); vayam (as explained at Rik 1.15.2 [yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhā, i.e. 1.15.2]); sanema (san "to obtain", āśīrliṅ, mas; s dropped by P. 3-4-99 nityaṃ ṅitaḥ and by P. 7-2-79 liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya; yāsuṭ; unaccented, but not made so because it begins the pāda); dhīmahi (dhā "to hold, to nourish", āśīrliṅ, mahiṅ, sīyuṭ, the s dropped, the ā dropped by P. 6-4-64 āto lopa iṭi ca); syāt (as, liṅ in the sense of command, wish and so on by P. 3-3-161, yāsuṭ, śap dropped, śnasor allopaḥ); uta (a particle); prarecanam (ric "to empty", lyuṭ in the sense of the action; a prādi compound; the accent of the final member). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 7-2-79, 6-4-64 and 3-3-161 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 733 lower half–735 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: avasā (sarvadhātubhyo 'sun, Uṇ. 4-[?]; av + asun; first-syllable accent through the n; the instrumental singular ṭā), vayam (the process for yūyam at Rik 1.15.2 applies also to vayam; the stem of yūyam is yuṣmad, of vayam it is asmad; the difference is only in the isṭa, the intended form), sanema (vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; āśīrliṅ [P. 3-4-116 liṅ āśiṣi]; mas → s dropped by nityaṃ ṅitaḥ P. 3-4-99; yāsuṭ by P. 3-4-103 yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca; the ṭ mark makes it the first part of the suffix, so ādyantau ṭakitau P. 1-1-46; the s dropped by P. 7-2-79 liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya; san + yā + s + mu [sanema — mas → sma, with s dropped...]; the Vedic [chandasy ubhayathā] P. 3-4-117 makes the liṅ sārvadhātuka as well as ārdhadhātuka; liṅy āśiṣy aṅ P. 3-1-86 [as printed 3-1-86] gives aṅ after an āśīrliṅ — here, san + a + yā + mu; e yeyaḥ P. 7-2-80 gives iy for yā; lopo vyor vali P. 6-1-66 drops the y; ad guṇaḥ P. 6-1-87 → sanema; begins the pāda, so not made unaccented; the e is a single substituted vowel, hence udātta), dhīmahi (ḍudhāñ; āśīrliṅ; liṅaḥ sīyuṭ P. 3-4-102; sārvadhātuka by P. 3-4-117; liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya; sārvadhātukam apit P. 1-2-4 makes the liṅ ṅit; kartari śap P. 3-1-68, which is dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi P. 2-4-73 — or juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ P. 2-4-75; dhā + īy + mahi; āto lopa iṭi ca P. 6-4-64 drops the ā; lopo vyor vali drops the y → dhīmahi; the Kannada adds that since the suffix is itself ñit-natured by P. 1-2-4, the ñit-ness acquired by extension [ātideśika] serves no purpose, so the Kannada says the ñit-ness is stated only to show that the sārvadhātuka status also has a use; ni ca dhīmahi has a ca, but since the verb sanema before it is already in the sentence, dhīmahi is the second verb, so by P. 8-1-59 [?] cavāyoge prathamā the bar on the loss of accent is not applied, and dhīmahi is made wholly unaccented by P. 8-1-28), syāt (as bhuvi; liṅ by P. 3-3-161 vidhi-nimantraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭa-saṃpraśna-prārthaneṣu liṅ, here in the sense of prayer; yāsuṭ by P. 3-4-103, which being ñit [P. 1-2-4]…; as + śap + yāsuṭ + t; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72; śnasor allopaḥ P. 6-4-111 drops the a of as; liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya drops the s of yāsuṭ; so syāt; it begins the pāda, so not unaccented), uta (end-accented as in the evādi list of Phiṭ 4-[?] evādīnām antaḥ), and prarecanam (ricir virecane; iditaḥ hmm — the Kannada's irit: the root ricir has the marker ir and so gets iritaḥ; irito vā P. 3-1-57 [?] giving aṅ optionally — here not applicable; lyuṭ ca P. 3-3-115 in the neuter in the abstract sense; yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca P. 7-3-86 gives guṇa: recana; the accent: lyuṭ is lit-suffix so, by P. 6-1-193 liti, the syllable before the suffix is accented; with the prefix pra the compound is kugatiprādayaḥ P. 2-2-18 and accent of the final member by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt). ॥6॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

तयोः (tayoḥ) — O Indra and Varuṇa [of those two] | अवसा इत् (avasā it) — by protection alone | वयम् (vayam) — we [the sacrificers] | सनेम (sanema) — may we obtain [wealth] | नि धीमहि च (ni dhīmahi ca) — and may we lay it by, storing it up | उत (uta) — and | प्ररेचनम् (prarecanam) — [more] than that we have enjoyed and than that we have stored | स्यात् (syāt) — may there be more [wealth].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

By the grace of Indra and Varuṇa we obtain boundless wealth, enjoy it as we wish, and store up what remains. Again, may the wealth grow ever greater than what we have enjoyed and what we have stored.

॥ English Translation ॥

Through their protection we enjoy riches and heap them up; still may we have even a surplus.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

नि धीमहि (ni dhīmahi) — śekhari — [the Kannada word śekhari, 'to lay up, to hoard']; "heap up; lay by".

उत (uta) — it is not [here a particle of the sense] "also"; or one may take whichever sense is wanted, such as "and".

प्ररेचनम् (prarecanam) — bhuktān nihitāc ca prakarṣeṇādhikaṃ dhanam: wealth that is far greater than what we have used and what we have stored. The sense is that the wealth given by Indra and Varuṇa should increase abundantly through their favour, beyond what we have enjoyed and heaped up.

original pp. 735–737

Sūkta 17, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुण वामहं हुवे चित्राय राधसे । अस्मान्त्सु जिग्युषस्कृतम् ॥७॥

indrāvaruṇa vām ahaṃ huve citrāya rādhase | asmān tsu jigyuṣas kṛtam ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the shortened indrāvaruṇa.

इन्द्रावरुणा । वाम् । अहम् । हुवे । चित्राय । राधसे ॥ अस्मान् । सु । जिग्युषः । कृतम् ॥७॥

indrāvaruṇā | vām | aham | huve | citrāya | rādhase || asmān | su | jigyuṣaḥ | kṛtam ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा हे इन्द्रावरुणौ वां युवामुभावहं हुवे । आह्वयामि । किमर्थम् । चित्राय मणिमुक्तादिरूपेण विविधाय राधसे धनाय । ततः आहूतौ युवामस्माननुष्ठात्॒न् सु जिग्युषः । शत्रुविषये सुष्ठु जयोपेतान् कृतं कुरुतम् ॥ इन्द्रावरुणा । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना संबोधनस्याकारः । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति पूर्वपदस्यानङ् । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । संहितायां छान्दसं ह्रस्वत्वम् । हुवे । ह्वयतेर्लुटि [sic: लटि?] उत्तमैकवचनमिट् । शपि इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । ह्व इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वम् । अचि श्नुधात्विति [?] ... उवङादेशः । जुहोतेरेव हि प्रतिपदोक्तस्य ग्रहणं न पुनरस्य लाक्षणिकत्वात् । इटः प्रत्ययस्वरे ... राधसे । असुन् । नित्त्वाद्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । अस्मान् । शसि द्वितीयायां च । पा. [७-२-८७] । इत्यात्वम् । शसो नः । पा. [६-१-१०३] ... जिग्युषः । जि जये । लिटः क्वसुश्च । पा. [३-२-१०७] । द्विर्भावः । सन्लिटोर्जेः । पा. [७-३-५७] । इति द्वितीयस्य कुत्वम् । क्वसोः कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । … वसोः संप्रसारणम् । पा. [६-४-१३१] … कृतम् । डुकृञ् करणे । लोण्मध्यमद्विवचनस्य थस् । लोटो लङ्वत् । तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तन्तामः । पा. [३-४-१०१] । इति तमादेशः । कर्तरि शप् । बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् … ॥७॥

indrāvaruṇā he indrāvaruṇau vāṃ yuvām ubhāv ahaṃ huve | āhvayāmi | kimartham | citrāya maṇi-muktādi-rūpeṇa vividhāya rādhase dhanāya | tata āhutau yuvām asmān anuṣṭhātṝn su jigyuṣaḥ | śatru-viṣaye suṣṭhu jayopetān kṛtaṃ kurutam || indrāvaruṇā | supāṃ sulug ity-ādinā saṃbodhanasyākāraḥ | devatā-dvandve ceti pūrvapadasyānaṅ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | saṃhitāyāṃ chāndasaṃ hrasvatvam | huve | hvayater laṭi uttamaikavacanam iṭ | śapi ity anuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | hva ity anuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvam | aci śnudhātv iti [?] … uvaṅādeśaḥ | juhoter eva hi pratipadoktasya grahaṇaṃ na punar asya lākṣaṇikatvāt | iṭaḥ pratyaya-svare … rādhase | asun | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | asmān | śasi dvitīyāyāṃ ca | pā. [7-2-87] | ity ātvam | śaso naḥ | pā. [6-1-103] … jigyuṣaḥ | ji jaye | liṭaḥ kvasuś ca | pā. [3-2-107] | dvirbhāvaḥ | san-liṭor jeḥ | pā. [7-3-57] | iti dvitīyasya kutvam | kvasoḥ kittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | … vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam | pā. [6-4-131] … kṛtam | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | loṇ-madhyama-dvivacanasya thas | loṭo laṅvat | tasthasthamipāṃ tāntantāmaḥ | pā. [3-4-101] | iti tamādeśaḥ | kartari śap | bahulaṃ chandasīti luk … ||7||

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa! Both of you I invoke (huve). For what? For citra — various — rādhas, wealth (jewels, pearls and the like). Therefore, being invoked, make us, the performers [of the rite], su jigyuṣaḥ — well endowed with victory over enemies — kṛtam, do so." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: indrāvaruṇā (as before); huve (hve, first singular iṭ; śap dropped; saṃprasāraṇa "variously in the Veda", parapūrva; uvaṅ); rādhase (asun, first-syllable accent); asmān (ā for the a of asmad before the accusative plural, P. 7-2-87; n for the s of śas, P. 6-1-103); jigyuṣaḥ (ji "to conquer", kvasu in the sense of the perfect by P. 3-2-107; reduplication; kutva of the second j by P. 7-3-57 san-liṭor jeḥ; no guṇa because kvasu is kit; saṃprasāraṇa of vas by P. 6-4-131); kṛtam (kṛ, loṭ dual, tam by P. 3-4-101, śap dropped). Grammar, noted briefly; the sūtra numerals are as read and agree with the standard numbering where comparison was possible; the line beginning aci śnudhātv… is partly unclear [?].

Grammar pages (pp. 738–739), noted briefly. The Kannada treats huve (hveñ, ātmanepada by the ñ-mark; laṭ, first singular iṭ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; śap with luk by P. 2-4-73; hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam P. 6-1-32 with bahulaṃ chandasi; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108 pūrvarūpa; hu + i; the long scholastic discussion whether uvaṅ/yaṇ applies by P. 6-4-87 hu-śnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke — whether hu here is the lākṣaṇika (derived) hu from hve or the pratipadokta root hu "to offer", the conclusion being that only the root hu "to offer" is meant, so no yaṇ and uv is [read] by P. 6-4-77; the suffix iṭ has suffix accent; the verb is not unaccented as it begins the pāda, P. 8-1-18/19 does not apply), rādhase (rādh + asun), asmān (asmad + śas; śaso 'ta ... ā for the end of asmad by P. 7-2-87 dvitīyāyāṃ ca; śasaḥ na by P. 7-1-29 śaso na; ādeḥ parasya P. 1-1-54 so the n replaces the s; saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ P. 8-2-23 drops the s — asmān), jigyuṣaḥ (liṭ, kvasu by P. 3-2-107 kvasuś ca; doubling P. 6-1-8; iṭ would come by P. 7-2-67 vasv ekājādghasām optionally, barred where the root is not one that kryādi bars [as read]; saṃprasāraṇa of vas before śas by P. 6-4-131 vaso saṃprasāraṇam; bha-name by P. 1-4-18; halaḥ; yaṇādeśa by P. 6-4-82; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59; visarga; su jigyuṣaḥ kṛtam with the s of jigyuṣas before k — the Kannada discusses the visarga and the s in the Saṃhitā text jigyuṣaskṛtam — by P. 8-3-35/40 kaskādiṣu ca… sas retained [as read]), and kṛtam (ḍukṛñ karaṇe; loṭ; loṭo laṅvat P. 3-4-85; thas → tam P. 3-4-101; śap with the tanādi's u by P. 3-1-79 tanādikṛñbhya uḥ — barred in the Veda by sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante, whence kṛtam; wholly unaccented by P. 8-1-28). ॥7॥ Numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā) — O Indra and Varuṇa | वाम् (vām) — both of you | अहम् (aham) — I (the performer of the rite) | चित्राय (citrāya) — of various kinds (thunderbolt, jewels and the like) | राधसे (rādhase) — for wealth | हुवे (huve) — I invoke | अस्मान् (asmān) — us (the performers) | सु जिग्युषः (su jigyuṣaḥ) — those who are well endowed with victory | कृतम् (kṛtam) — make.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa! I praise you with hymns and invoke you. Give us various kinds of wealth, such as the thunderbolt and the like, and make us victorious over our enemies.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra and Varuna, I invoke you for several kinds of wealth ; make us victorious (over our enemies).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā) — though the last letter of this word is long, it is shortened in the Saṃhitā for the sake of the metre. As in this, so in the 1st and 8th [as printed: "೮, ೯ನೇ"] riks of this sūkta, the last letter of this word is short in the Saṃhitā.

चित्राय (citrāya) — the commentator says "of various kinds, in the form of jewels, pearls and so on". Rather than saying so, it would be more natural to say "various forms of wealth: cattle, food and other useful kinds of wealth". In that age, one may say, the need for cows, food, victory over enemies and the like was greater than for jewels and pearls.

जिग्युषः (jigyuṣaḥ) — ji jaye; śatruviṣaye suṣṭhu jayayuktān: those who have the power to conquer enemies.

original pp. 740–742

Sūkta 17, Rik 8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुण नू नु वां सिषासन्तीषु धीष्वा । अस्मभ्यं शर्म यच्छतम् ॥८॥

indrāvaruṇa nū nu vāṃ siṣāsantīṣu dhīṣv ā | asmabhyaṃ śarma yacchatam ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा । नु । नु । वाम् । सिषासन्तीषु । धीषु । आ ॥ अस्मभ्यम् । शर्म । यच्छतम् ॥८॥

indrāvaruṇā | nu | nu | vām | siṣāsantīṣu | dhīṣu | ā || asmabhyam | śarma | yacchatam ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा हे इन्द्रावरुणौ धीष्वस्मदीयबुद्धिषु वां युवां सिषासन्तीषु सनितुं संभक्तुं सम्यक् सेवितुमिच्छन्तीषु तदानीमा सर्वतोऽस्मभ्यं शर्म सुखं नू नु आशिषेन [?] क्षिप्रं यच्छतम् । दत्तम् । षट्त्रिंशत्सङ्ख्याकेषु क्षिप्रनामसु नु पठितम् । तस्य द्विरावृत्तेर्बहुशीघ्रत्वम् [?] ॥ इन्द्रावरुणा । उक्तम् । नू नु । ऋचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणाम् । पा. [६-३-१३३] । इति पूर्वस्य दीर्घत्वम् । सिषासन्तीषु । वन षण सम्भक्तौ । धात्वादेः षः सः । इच्छार्थे सन् । द्विर्वचनम् । हलादिः शेषः । सन्यतः । इत्वम् । आदेशप्रत्यययोः । पा. [८-३-५९] । षत्वम् । सनीवन्तर्धभ्रस्जदम्भुश्रिस्वृयूर्णुभरज्ञपिसनाम् । पा. [७-२-४९] । इडागमो विकल्पः । … जनसनखनां सञ्झलोः । पा. [६-४-४२] । … सिषास सेनाद्यन्ता धातवः । पा. [३-१-३२] । … लटः शतृ । कर्तरि शप् । अतो गुणे । पररूपम् । उगितश्च । पा. [४-१-६] । ङीप् । शप्श्यनोर्नित्यम् । पा. [७-१-८१] । नुमागमः । मिदचोऽन्त्यात्परः । पा. [१-१-४७] । जीप् शप् एतौ पित्त्वादनुदात्तौ । … धीषु । ध्यै चिन्तायाम् । ध्यायतेः संप्रसारणं च । पा. [३-२-१७८] । क्विप् संप्रसारणम् । … अस्मभ्यम् । अस्मभ्यमप्रतिष्मृतः । ऋ. सं. [१-२-६] । इत्यत्रोक्तम् । यच्छतम् । दाण् दाने । शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना यच्छादेशः ॥८॥

indrāvaruṇā he indrāvaruṇau dhīṣv asmadīya-buddhiṣu vāṃ yuvāṃ siṣāsantīṣu sanituṃ saṃbhaktuṃ samyak sevitum icchantīṣu tadānīm ā sarvato 'smabhyaṃ śarma sukhaṃ nū nu āśiṣena [?] kṣipraṃ yacchatam | dattam | ṣaṭtriṃśat-saṅkhyākeṣu kṣipra-nāmasu nu paṭhitam | tasya dvir āvṛtter bahu-śīghratvam [?] || indrāvaruṇā | uktam | nū nu | ṛci tunu-ghamakṣu-taṅ-kutro-ruṣyāṇām | pā. [6-3-133] | iti pūrvasya dīrghatvam | siṣāsantīṣu | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | icchārthe san | dvirvacanam | halādiḥ śeṣaḥ | san-yataḥ | itvam | ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ | pā. [8-3-59] | ṣatvam | sanīvantar-dha-bhras-ja-dambhu-śri-svṛ-yū-ūrṇu-bhara-jñapi-sanām | pā. [7-2-49] | iḍāgamo vikalpaḥ | … janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ | pā. [6-4-42] | … siṣāsa senādy-antā dhātavaḥ | pā. [3-1-32] | … laṭaḥ śatṛ | kartari śap | ato guṇe | pararūpam | ugitaś ca | pā. [4-1-6] | ṅīp | śap-śyanor nityam | pā. [7-1-81] | numāgamaḥ | mid-aco 'ntyāt paraḥ | pā. [1-1-47] | jīp śap etau pittvād anudāttau | … dhīṣu | dhyai cintāyām | dhyāyateḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca | pā. [3-2-178] | kvip saṃprasāraṇam | … asmabhyam | asmabhyam apratiṣmṛtaḥ | ṛ. saṃ. [1-2-6] | ity uktam | yacchatam | dāṇ dāne | śapi pā-ghrety-ādinā yacchādeśaḥ ||8||

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa! In our dhīs — our minds — which desire to sanitum — to share in, to serve properly — you two, then grant (yacchatam) to us from all sides śarma — comfort — nū nu, quickly. Nu is read among the thirty-six words meaning 'quick'; its being doubled [nū nu] gives great haste [?]." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: indrāvaruṇā (as above); nū nu (lengthening of the first by P. 6-3-133 ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutrorūṣyāṇām); siṣāsantīṣu (van "to serve" with the desiderative san, reduplication, i for a, ṣa for sa by P. 8-3-59; the optional iṭ by P. 7-2-49; śatṛ, śap, ṅīp by P. 4-1-6 ugitaś ca, with num by P. 7-1-81 śap-śyanor nityam); dhīṣu (dhyai "to think", saṃprasāraṇa, kvip); asmabhyam (as at Rik 1.2.6); yacchatam (dā, with yaccha for dā by P. 7-3-78 pāghrādhmā…). Grammar, noted briefly; the sūtra numerals are as read.

Grammar pages (p. 742 lower to 743 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats nū nu (ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutrorūṣyāṇām P. 6-3-133 lengthens the first nu), siṣāsantīṣu (van ṣaṇ sambhaktau; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā P. 3-1-7 for san; doubling by P. 6-1-9 sanyaṅoḥ; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60 dropping the n of the first; sanyataḥ P. 7-4-79 → i; san is ārdhadhātuka so the iṭ would come by P. 7-2-35 but is optional by P. 7-2-49 sanīvantardhabhrasjadambhuśrisvṛyūrṇubharajñapisanām; janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ P. 6-4-42 gives ā for the n of san, akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ siṣāsa; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ P. 3-1-32 gives it the name dhātu; then laṭ with śatṛ by P. 3-2-124; śap; ato guṇe; ugitaś ca P. 4-1-6 for ṅīp; śapśyanor nityam P. 7-1-81 num; mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ P. 1-1-47 puts it after the last vowel: siṣāsantī; ṅīp and śap both pit so unaccented, the sana's a — siṣāsat has the accent of sana on... [the Kannada: siṣāsa is first-syllable accented by ñnityādir nityam, as the san is nit; the same accent remains in the locative plural, siṣāsantīṣu]), dhīṣu (dhyai cintāyām; dhyāyater saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca P. 3-2-178 gives kvip and saṃprasāraṇa in the Veda; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108 pūrvarūpa → dhi; halaḥ P. 6-4-2 lengthens → dhī; locative plural sup; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59; the ending accented by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ), asmabhyam (explained at Rik 1.2.6 [print: "Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-6"]), and yacchatam (dāṇ dāne; loṭ; loṭo laṅvat; tasthasthamipāṃ…; śap; pāghrādhmā… P. 7-3-78 gives yaccha; tam). ॥8॥ Numerals as read; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā) — O Indra and Varuṇa | धीषु (dhīṣu) — [our] minds | वाम् (vām) — you two | सिषासन्तीषु (siṣāsantīṣu) — those wishing to serve | अस्मभ्यम् (asmabhyam) — to us | आ (ā) — from all sides | शर्म (śarma) — happiness | नू नु (nū nu) — very quickly | यच्छतम् (yacchatam) — give.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa! Our minds are always devoted to serving you; that is, we are constantly serving you. Therefore, be gracious and grant us comfort in every way.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra and Varuna, quickly bestow happiness upon us, for our minds are devoted to you both.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

नू नु (nū nu) — among the thirty-six words of the group meaning "quick" beginning with manaḥ [the print reads "ಮಂಕ್ಷು"], nu is read (Ni. [2-15?]); so nu means "quickly". Here the word nu is repeated, and so it means "very quickly, without even a little delay". For the sake of the metre the first nu is lengthened. Besides this, Yāska gives a few more meanings of nu:

नु इत्येषोऽनेककर्मा । इदं नु करिष्यतीति हेत्वपदेशे । अथाप्युपमार्थे भवति ॥ (नि. [१-४]) nu ity eṣo 'neka-karmā | idaṃ nu kariṣyatīti hetv-apadeśe | athāpy upamārthe bhavati || (ni. [1-4])

"This nu has many senses: in idaṃ nu kariṣyati ['he will surely do this'] it is a statement of reason; and it also has the sense of comparison." The Kannada gives an example of the last: vṛkṣasya nu te (Ṛ. Saṃ. [6-3-5?]) — "like a tree's [...]" (the rest of the example is cut off at the foot of p. 741).

सिषासन्तीषु धीषु (siṣāsantīṣu dhīṣu) — "our minds or intellects have an eagerness to serve you; they long for it". Here the locative is used in the sense of the nominative; such use is found especially in the Vedic Sanskrit.

original pp. 743–746

Sūkta 17, Rik 9 (last rik of the sūkta)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

प्र वामश्नोतु सुष्टुतिरिन्द्रावरुण यां हुवे । यामृधाथे सधस्तुतिम् ॥९॥

pra vām aśnotu suṣṭutir indrāvaruṇa yāṃ huve | yām ṛdhāthe sadhastutim ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The print has su-stutiḥ in the Pada, though the Saṃhitā has suṣṭutiḥ, as the conjoint form.

प्र । वाम् । अश्नोतु । सुऽस्तुतिः । इन्द्रावरुणा । याम् । हुवे ॥ याम् । ऋधाथे इति । सधऽस्तुतिम् ॥९॥

pra | vām | aśnotu | su-stutiḥ | indrāvaruṇā | yām | huve || yām | ṛdhāthe iti | sadha-stutim ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा हे इन्द्रावरुणौ यामस्मत्कर्तृकां शोभनस्तुतिं प्रति हुवे । युवामुभावाह्वयामि । किंच सधस्तुतिं युवयोरुभयोः साहित्येन क्रियमाणायाः स्तवनक्रियाया यां सुष्टुतिं प्रतिलब्ध्वा ऋधाथे युवां वर्धाथे । तादृशी सुष्टुतिः शोभनस्तुतिहेतुभूता वा ऋक्स्वनूहो वामश्नोतु । युवां व्याप्नोतु ॥ अश्नोतु । अशू व्याप्तौ । लोटो व्यत्ययेन तिप् । स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । सुष्टुतिः । न विन्दे अस्य सुष्टुतिम् । ऋ. सं. [१-२-२] । इत्यत्रोक्तम् । इन्द्रावरुणा । हुवे । उक्ते । अत्र तु यद्वृत्तयोगान्न निघातः । ऋधाथे । ऋधु वृद्धौ । लट् । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । मध्यमद्विवचने श्नोर्बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणाकार उदात्तः । यजब्द्योगान्न निघातः । सधस्तुतिम् । सह स्तुतिर्यस्यां सुष्टुतौ सा सधस्तुतिः । अत्र सुष्टुतिरित्यन्यपदार्थे स्तुतिशब्दस्य स्नूयते ऽनयेति करणसाधनत्वेन ऋक्स्वरत्नेऽयं स्तुतिशब्दो भावसाधनतया स्तवनक्रियापरः । … सहेत्यत्र हकारस्य व्यत्ययेन धकारः । सहशब्द एवमादित्वादन्तोदात्तः । बहुव्रीहित्वेन पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥९॥

indrāvaruṇā he indrāvaruṇau yām asmat-kartṛkāṃ śobhana-stutiṃ prati huve | yuvām ubhāv āhvayāmi | kiṃ ca sadhastutiṃ yuvayor ubhayoḥ sāhityena kriyamāṇāyāḥ stavana-kriyāyā yāṃ suṣṭutiṃ pratilabdhvā ṛdhāthe yuvāṃ vardhāthe | tādṛśī suṣṭutiḥ śobhana-stuti-hetu-bhūtā vā ṛksv anūho vām aśnotu | yuvāṃ vyāpnotu || aśnotu | aśū vyāptau | loṭo vyatyayena tip | svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | suṣṭutiḥ | na vinde asya suṣṭutim | ṛ. saṃ. [1-2-2] | ity atroktam | indrāvaruṇā | huve | ukte | atra tu yad-vṛtta-yogān na nighātaḥ | ṛdhāthe | ṛdhu vṛddhau | laṭ | vyatyayenātmanepadam | madhyama-dvivacane śnor bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | pratyaya-svareṇākāra udāttaḥ | yaj-ab-yogān na nighātaḥ | sadhastutim | saha stutir yasyāṃ suṣṭutau sā sadhastutiḥ | atra suṣṭutir ity anya-padārthe stuti-śabdasya snūyate 'neti karaṇa-sādhanatvena ṛk-svaratne 'yaṃ stuti-śabdo bhāva-sādhanatayā stavana-kriyā-paraḥ | … saheti hakārasya vyatyayena dhakāraḥ | saha-śabda evam-ādittvād antodāttaḥ | bahuvrīhitvena pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||9||

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa! To that suṣṭuti — good praise — made by us, I invoke you both. Further, that good praise which is a sadhastuti — a praise made by both of you jointly (saha) — having received which you two grow (ṛdhāthe): may such a good praise, or [the ṛk verses that are] the cause of good praise, reach you (aśnotu, 'pervade')." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: aśnotu (aś "to pervade", loṭ with tip by vyatyaya; śnu of the svādi class); suṣṭutiḥ (explained at Rik 1.2.2); huve (as above; here, because of the relative yām, the verb is not made unaccented); ṛdhāthe (ṛdh "to grow", laṭ with the ātmanepada by vyatyaya; the śnu dropped; accent on the ā of the suffix); sadhastutim ("that good praise in which the stuti is joint"; the word stuti here is the abstract ktin — the act of praising — while in suṣṭutiḥ it is taken as the instrument [stūyate 'nayā 'by which one praises', the ṛk]; saha with dh for h by vyatyaya; the compound keeps the accent of the first member).

Grammar pages (pp. 745–746 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: aśnotu (aśū vyāptau is anudāttet, so it would take the ātmanepada by P. 1-3-12 anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam; but "variously" vyatyayo bahulam P. 3-1-85 gives parasmaipada tip; svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ P. 3-1-73; aś + nu + ti, guṇa by P. 7-3-84, iko yaṇ… eruḥ P. 3-4-86 gives u for the i of ti in the imperative: aśnotu), suṣṭutiḥ (explained at 1.2.2 [print: "Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-2"]), indrāvaruṇā, huve (see the same sūkta, Rik 1: the verb is not unaccented since it begins the pāda; here, since the relative yām precedes, P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam bars the loss of accent), ṛdhāthe (ṛdhu vṛddhau; laṭ; ātmanepada by vyatyaya; third dual ātām → āthām for the second dual; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e P. 3-4-79; śnā/śnu dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi P. 2-4-73; ādyudāttaś ca P. 3-1-3 accents the first vowel of the suffix, so the ā of āthe; since yām precedes, no loss of accent by yadvṛttān nityam), and sadhastutim (saha stutir yasyāṃ sā, a bahuvrīhi by P. 2-2-24 anekam anyapadārthe, defined as one in which the sense is that of another word than those compounded; the Kannada notes the problem whether stuti can be a word of "another sense", and answers: stuti in the compound is the instrument-sense ktin meaning "the ṛk by which one praises", while in the bahuvrīhi sadhastuti, which is a feminine abstract form, it means "the act of praising"; hence the word of the compound is different in sense from the independent word; saha has dha for ha by vyatyaya [a Vedic licence]; end-accent for saha by the Phiṭ-sūtra vivādīnām antaḥ [Phiṭ 4-[?]]; the bahuvrīhi keeps the accent of its first member by P. 6-2-1). ॥9॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुण (indrāvaruṇa) — O Indra and Varuṇa | याम् (yām) — which praise of ours | हुवे (huve) — I invoke [you two with that praise] | (अथ) याम् ((atha) yām) — and which | सधस्तुतिम् (sadhastutim) — joint praise [of you two] | ऋधाथे (ṛdhāthe) — you who are pleased and grow by receiving | सुष्टुतिः (suṣṭutiḥ) — that excellent praise [the group of verses] | वाम् अश्नोतु (vām aśnotu) — may it reach you.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa! I invoke you separately with praise; sometimes I invoke you both together and praise you. May you both be pleased with such praises.

॥ English Translation ॥

May the earnest praise which I offer to Indra and Varuna reach you both ; and may you fulfil that prayer addressed to you both.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अश्नोतु (aśnotu) — vyāpnotu: "may the praise we make reach you; may it be pleasing to you".

ऋधाथे (ṛdhāthe) — ṛdhu vṛddhau "to grow": vardhethām: "you two, may you be pleased with, and praise, the hymn we make, and thereby become satisfied" — such senses may be given.

सधस्तुतिम् (sadhastutim) — saha stutir yasyāṃ suṣṭutau sā sadhastutiḥ: the praise made by joining the two together; the hymn which praises the two deities, Indra and Varuṇa, together.

Close of Sūkta 17. The grammar of Rik 9 ends at the head of p. 746, followed by an ornament and the heading of Sūkta 18; the print has no large colophon here either.

॥ ಹದಿನೆಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 18 — "somānaṃ svaraṇaṃ kṛṇuhi" ("The Eighteenth Sūkta"; first sūkta of the Fifth Anuvāka)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 746, lower half)

पञ्चमेऽनुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्र सोमानमित्यादिकं नवर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तम् । ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । देवताविशेषस्त्वेवमनुक्रम्यते । सोमानमिति पञ्च ब्राह्मणस्पत्यश्चतुर्थ्यामिन्द्रश्च सोमश्च पञ्चम्यां दक्षिणा चान्याः सादसस्पत्या नाराशंसी वान्त्येति । सूक्तगता आद्याः पञ्चर्चो ब्रह्मणस्पति देवताकाः । तासां मध्ये स घा वीर इत्येतस्याश्चतुर्थ्या ऋचो ब्रह्मणस्पतिरिन्द्रश्च सोमश्चेति तिस्रो देवताः । त्वं तमित्येतस्याः पञ्चम्या दक्षिणया सह पूर्वोक्तास्तिस्रो देवताः । षष्ठीमारभ्य तिसृणां सदसस्पतिर्देवता । नराशंसमित्येतस्या नवम्याः सदसस्पतिर्नराशंसो वा विकल्प्यते ॥ विनियोगस्तु पूर्ववत् ॥

pañcame 'nuvāke ṣaṭ sūktāni | tatra somānam ity-ādikaṃ navarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktam | ṛṣi-chandasī pūrvavat | devatā-viśeṣas tv evam anukramyate | somānam iti pañca brāhmaṇaspatyaś caturthyām indraś ca somaś ca pañcamyāṃ dakṣiṇā cānyāḥ sādasaspatyā nārāśaṃsī vāntyeti | sūkta-gatā ādyāḥ pañcarco brahmaṇaspati-devatākāḥ | tāsāṃ madhye sa ghā vīra ity etasyāś caturthyā ṛco brahmaṇaspatir indraś ca somaś ceti tisro devatāḥ | tvaṃ tam ity etasyāḥ pañcamyā dakṣiṇayā saha pūrvoktās tisro devatāḥ | ṣaṣṭhīm ārabhya tisṛṇāṃ sadasas-patir devatā | narāśaṃsam ity etasyā navamyāḥ sadasaspatir narāśaṃso vā vikalpyate || viniyogas tu pūrvavat ||

Translation: "In the fifth anuvāka there are six sūktas. Of them the first is the nine-rik sūkta beginning somānam; its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. The particular deities are stated in the Anukramaṇikā thus: 'the five [riks] somānam… are to Brahmaṇaspati; in the fourth [Rik 4] Indra and Soma [also]; in the fifth, Dakṣiṇā [also]; the others are to Sadasaspati; the last is to Narāśaṃsa [or Sadasaspati].' The first five riks of the sūkta have Brahmaṇaspati for their deity; among them the fourth, sa ghā vīraḥ, has three deities — Brahmaṇaspati, Indra and Soma; the fifth, tvaṃ tam, has Dakṣiṇā together with the previous three [Brahmaṇaspati, Indra, Soma]. From the sixth the three riks [6–8] have Sadasaspati for deity; for the ninth, narāśaṃsam, Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa — a choice. Its application is as before." The print's wording of the Anukramaṇikā quotation is slightly compressed, and the rendering of its last clause sādasaspatyā nārāśaṃsī vāntyā follows the Kannada's gloss.

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ With this sūkta the fifth anuvāka begins; it contains six sūktas. The first is the nine-rik sūkta somānam. The ṛṣi and meters are as in the preceding sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā gives the deities thus: the first three riks to Brahmaṇaspati; the fourth to Brahmaṇaspati, Indra and Soma; the fifth to Brahmaṇaspati and Dakṣiṇā; riks 6 to 8 to Sadasaspati; the ninth to Sadasaspati or, optionally, Narāśaṃsa. The application is as before.

original pp. 747–754

Sūkta 18, Rik 1

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 18 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 5 ॥ Sūkta — 18 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 34, 35 [?] ॥ small-print Kannada digits, read at 150 dpi: "೩೪, ೩೫"; unconfirmed ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–9 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ ॥ Devatā — 1–3: Brahmaṇaspati; 4: Brahmaṇaspati, Indra and Soma; 5: Brahmaṇaspati and Dakṣiṇā; 6–8: Sadasaspati; 9: Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa ॥ as printed; the Kannada numerals of the rik numbers are small and partly read from context ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सोमानं स्वरणं कृणुहि ब्रह्मणस्पते । कक्षीवन्तं य औशिजः ॥१॥

somānaṃ svaraṇaṃ kṛṇuhi brahmaṇas pate | kakṣīvantaṃ ya auśijaḥ ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks are printed in the source; not reproduced, per the convention for the later riks of this volume.

सोमानम् । स्वरणम् । कृणुहि । ब्रह्मणः । पते ॥ कक्षीवन्तम् । यः । औशिजः ॥१॥

somānam | svaraṇam | kṛṇuhi | brahmaṇaḥ | pate || kakṣīvantam | yaḥ | auśijaḥ ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ compressed; [?] marks doubtful readings

हे ब्रह्मणस्पते वितन्नामकदेव [?] सोमानमभिषवस्य कर्तारं मामनुष्ठातारं स्वरणं देवेषु प्रकाशनवन्तं कृणुहि । कुरु । अत्र दृष्टान्तः । कक्षीवन्तमेतन्नामकमृषिम् । इवशब्दो लुप्तोपमार्थः । कक्षीवानन्यथा देवेषु प्रसिद्धस्तद्वदित्यर्थः । यः कक्षीवान्यौशिज उशिजः पुत्रः । तमिवेति पूर्वत्र योजना । कक्षीवत्त्वेनाभिप्रेतोऽनुष्ठाता मुनिषु प्रसिद्ध इत्येवं पर आर्ष्टिषाणादि [?] । … सोमानम् । षुञ् अभिषवे । आन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यते इति मनिन् । … स्वरणम् । प्रख्यातम् । स्वृ शब्दोपतापयोः । कृत्यल्युटो बहुलम् । पा. [३-३-११३] । इति कर्मणि ल्युट् । लिति … कृणुहि । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । इदितो नुम् धातोः । पा. [७-१-५८] । कृण्वि … लोटः सिप् । सेर्ह्यपिच्च । पा. [३-४-८७] । हिः । शपि प्राप्ते धिन्विकृण्व्योर च । पा. [३-१-८०] । इत्युप्रत्ययः … ब्रह्मणः पते । षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रपृष्ठपारपदपयस्पोषेषु । पा. [८-३-५३] । इति विसर्गस्य सकारः । … कक्षीवन्तम् । कक्षे भवा कक्ष्या … मतुप् … आसन्दीवदष्ठीवच्चक्रीवत्कक्षीवद्रुमण्वच्चर्मण्वतीति । पा. [८-२-१२] निपातितः … औशिजः । वश कान्तौ । … उशिजः अपत्यम् । पा. [४-१-८३] । अण् । आदिवृद्धिः । ॥१॥

he brahmaṇaspate vitan-nāmaka-deva [?] somānam abhiṣavasya kartāraṃ mām anuṣṭhātāraṃ svaraṇaṃ deveṣu prakāśanavantaṃ kṛṇuhi | kuru | atra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | kakṣīvantam etan-nāmakam ṛṣim | iva-śabdo luptopamārthaḥ | kakṣīvān anyathā deveṣu prasiddhas tadvad ity arthaḥ | yaḥ kakṣīvān yauśija uśijaḥ putraḥ | tam iveti pūrvatra yojanā | kakṣīvattvenābhipreto 'nuṣṭhātā muniṣu prasiddha ity evaṃ para ārṣṭiṣāṇādi [?] | … somānam | ṣuñ abhiṣave | ānyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate iti manin | … svaraṇam | prakhyātam | svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ | kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam | pā. [3-3-113] | iti karmaṇi lyuṭ | liti … kṛṇuhi | kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca | idito num dhātoḥ | pā. [7-1-58] | kṛṇvi … loṭaḥ sip | ser hy apic ca | pā. [3-4-87] | hiḥ | śapi prāpte dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca | pā. [3-1-80] | ity u-pratyayaḥ … brahmaṇaḥ pate | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputrapṛṣṭhapārapadapayaspoṣeṣu | pā. [8-3-53] | iti visargasya sakāraḥ | … kakṣīvantam | kakṣe bhavā kakṣyā … matup … āsandīvad-aṣṭhīvac-cakrīvat-kakṣīvad-rumaṇvac-carmaṇvatīti | pā. [8-2-12] nipātitaḥ … auśijaḥ | vaśa kāntau | … uśijaḥ apatyam | pā. [4-1-83] | aṇ | ādivṛddhiḥ ||1||

Translation: "O Brahmaṇaspati [the first words read as vitan-nāmaka-deva — "god named …" — which I cannot resolve [?]]! Make me, the performer, who am the pressing-out of soma (somānam), svaraṇam — renowned (shining) among the gods. Here is an example: the ṛṣi named Kakṣīvān — [the particle iva, 'like', is dropped] — that is: 'as Kakṣīvān is famed among the gods, so [make me]'; [that Kakṣīvān is] the one who is auśija, the son of Uśij. 'Like him' is to be joined to the earlier [words]. [The next sentence, about the performer meant by the word kakṣīvat being famed among sages, is partly unclear to me.]" The rest is grammar, noted briefly: somānam (su "to press", the manin suffix "also seen with other roots"); svaraṇam (svṛ "to sound, to heat"; lyuṭ in the object sense by P. 3-3-113 kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam); kṛṇuhi (kṛvi "to hurt, to do", num by P. 7-1-58; loṭ, si → hi by P. 3-4-87; u in place of śap by P. 3-1-80 dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca); brahmaṇaḥ pate (visarga → s by P. 8-3-53 ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputrapṛṣṭhapārapadapayaspoṣeṣu); kakṣīvantam (kakṣya + matup, with the nipātana of P. 8-2-12 āsandīvadaṣṭhīvaccakrīvat kakṣīvad rumaṇvac carmaṇvatī); auśijaḥ (uśij's descendant, aṇ, P. 4-1-83, vṛddhi). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 3-3-113, 7-1-58, 3-4-87, 8-3-53 and 8-2-12 as read agree with the standard numbering; the last two lines of the bhāṣya are compressed, and only the portions that were read are given.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) ब्रह्मणस्पते ((he) brahmaṇaspate) — O Brahmaṇaspati | यः (yaḥ) — who | औशिजः (auśijaḥ) — the son of Uśij (or Uśik) | कक्षीवन्तम् (kakṣīvantam) — [like] the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān | सोमानम् (somānam) — the one who presses out the soma-juice [me, the sacrificer] | स्वरणम् (svaraṇam) — [make] renowned among the gods, or full of brahmavarcas | कृणुहि (kṛṇuhi) — make.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Kakṣīvān, the son of Uśij, is famed among the gods as one who performed the soma sacrifice. O Brahmaṇaspati, make me also, the sacrificer, famed as a soma-performer, like that Kakṣīvān.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

O Brahmanaspati, make (me) who offer Soma juice illustrious among the gods like Kakshivan, the son of Usij.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The deity of this sūkta is Brahmaṇaspati. Who is this Brahmaṇaspati? We shall describe briefly his place among the gods. Yāska, in the Nirukta (10-[?]) discusses Brahmaṇaspati thus:

ब्रह्मणस्पतिः । ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणः पाता वा पालयिता वा ॥ (नि. [१०-१४]) brahmaṇaspatiḥ | brahmaṇaspatir brahmaṇaḥ pātā vā pālayitā vā || (ni. [10-14])

Here brahman means food, wealth, or praise (Ni. [2-7]); so brahmaṇaspati means "the master or lord of food". How is he the lord of food? Yāska, as an example, quotes the rik

अश्माऽस्यमवतं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मधुधारमभि यमोजसातृणत् । तमेव विश्वे पपिरे स्वर्दृशो बहु साकं सिसिचुरुत्समुद्रिणम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. [२-२४-४]) aśmāsyam avataṃ brahmaṇaspatir madhudhāram abhi yam ojasātṛṇat | tam eva viśve papire svardṛśo bahu sākaṃ sisicur utsam udriṇam || (ṛ. saṃ. [2-24-4])

and then comments on it:

अशनवन्तमास्यन्तनवन्तमुदाकृतं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मधुधारमभियमोजसा बलेनाभ्यतृणत् तमेव सर्वे पिबन्ति रश्मयः सूर्यदृशो बह्वेनं सह सिञ्चन्त्युत्समुद्रिणमुदकवन्तम् ॥ (नि. [१०-१५]) aśanavantam āsyantanavantam udākṛtaṃ brahmaṇaspatir madhudhāram abhiyam ojasā balenābhyatṛṇat tam eva sarve pibanti raśmayaḥ sūryadṛśo bahv enaṃ saha siñcanty utsam udriṇam udakavantam || (ni. [10-15])

The two Sanskrit passages are given from small print at 150 dpi; the Ṛgveda verse and Yāska's comment have several doubtful words, which are given as read; Yāska's comment is not translated word for word, but its sense, as the Kannada gives it, is: the principal idea is that this Brahmaṇaspati, with the help of the sun's rays, drinks the clouds' [water] and makes it fall abundantly on the earth as rain; and by rain the herbs and trees, and with them food and the like, are obtained; therefore Brahmaṇaspati is "the protector of food". When brahman is taken to mean praise or wealth, Brahmaṇaspati is the lord of praise or of wealth. The commentator also quotes this same rik in explaining it.

The mantras addressed to Brahmaṇaspati are numerous in the Ṛgveda. In them Brahmaṇaspati is said to give wealth and food. Many are in doubt whether this Brahmaṇaspati is a separate deity or a changed form of Agni. Some argue that since Agni and other deities also give wealth and food, Brahmaṇaspati is some special form of Agni. Yāska keeps silent on this point; he says nothing clearly. In the riks addressed to Brahmaṇaspati there is no ground enough to call this deity a form of Agni. So one may say with confidence that Brahmaṇaspati is a distinct deity, like Indra and Agni.

सोमानम् (somānam) — abhiṣavasya kartāram: one who has prepared the soma-juice — [that is, the sacrificer] me.

स्वरणम् (svaraṇam) — deveṣu prakāśanavantam; prakhyātam: famous among the gods, renowned.

कक्षीवन्तम्, औशिजः (kakṣīvantam, auśijaḥ) — Kakṣīvān the ṛṣi was the son of Uśij, born of a woman called Uśik. It is said in the Purāṇas and elsewhere that this Uśik was a maid-servant of the queen of the king of Kaliṅga; the king, wishing for a son, sent his wife to the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas; the queen, unwilling, secretly sent her maid Uśik instead, and from Dīrghatamas this Kakṣīvān was born. Though born of a kṣatriya woman [a servant], through connection with a brahmin he is famed as a brahmin. This ṛṣi has been seen [as the seer] of many riks in the Ṛgveda. That this ṛṣi Kakṣīvān was famed among those who perform sacrificial rites is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā [5-6-5-3? — the print's numerals "೫-೬-೫-೩" are read with a query]:

एवं वै पर आट्णारः कक्षीवाँ औशिजो वीतहव्यः श्रायसस्सदस्युः पौरुकुत्स्यः प्रजाकामा आचिन्वत ॥ evaṃ vai para āṭṇāraḥ kakṣīvām̐ auśijo vītahavyaḥ śrāyasas sadasyuḥ paurukutsyaḥ prajākāmā ācinvata ||

— "Thus indeed did Para Āṭṇāra, Kakṣīvān the son of Uśij, Vītahavya Śrāyasa and Sadasyu Paurukutsya, desiring offspring, make the fire-altar" [the Sanskrit is as read, and the translation is mine and tentative]. Hence this ṛṣi is very famous both in making mantras and in performing sacrificial rites. Medhātithi, the ṛṣi of this sūkta, prays to the deity Brahmaṇaspati to make him, too, famed like this man.

Grammar pages (pp. 751–754 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: somānam (suñ abhiṣave; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; the manin suffix by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; ñit by the nit rule so first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197 [barred by some: the Kannada notes the suffix accent also applies, so somān may be end-accented by P. 6-1-163; the uñjvaladi list [uṇādi?] with ūḍhaṃ … P. 6-1-163; the conclusion is end accent for somān]), svaraṇam (svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ; kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam P. 3-3-113 gives lyuṭ in the object sense; yuvor anākau P. 7-1-1 gives ana; guṇa and raparatva P. 1-1-51; raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade P. 8-4-1 gives ṇ; the accent before lit suffix P. 6-1-193), kṛṇuhi (kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca; idito num dhātoḥ P. 7-1-58; kṛṇv + loṭ; sip → hi P. 3-4-87; u for śap by P. 3-1-80 dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca, which also makes v → a; the ut of P. 6-4-106 uto vṛddhir… and utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt P. 6-4-106 would drop the hi's u — utaś ca pratyayāc chandasi vā vacanam P. 6-4-106 [as read] makes this optional in the Veda, so the dropping does not happen; the verb is unaccented but pādādau ca — as it is at the start of the second pāda — it is not so by P. 8-1-19), brahmaṇaḥ pate (ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra… P. 8-3-53 gives s; pate is a vocative treated as parāṅgavat, so P. 8-1-72/73 āmantritasya ca leaves both words unaccented), kakṣīvantam (kakṣe bhavā kakṣyā — bhave chandasi P. 4-4-110 gives yat, ṭāp in the feminine; kakṣyā asya asti — tad asyāsty asmin P. 5-2-94 gives matup; the nipātana by P. 8-2-12 āsandīvad…kakṣīvat… — saṃprasāraṇa [kakṣyā → kakṣī] is declared by the nipātana; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108; halaḥ P. 6-4-2 lengthens; chandasīraḥ P. 8-2-15 gives va for the ma of matup; ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ P. 7-1-70 for num; the Kannada notes the Mahābhāṣya's view that saṃprasāraṇa of kakṣyā before matup was stated by Patañjali himself, and that kakṣīvat is from the sūtra's inclusion), and auśijaḥ (vaś kāntau; Uṇ. 2-[?] pañeriji ādeśaś ca vaḥ [as read] and vaśeḥ kit give ij with k; grahijyāvayivyadhivaṣṭi… P. 6-1-16 gives saṃprasāraṇa; uśij + aṇ by P. 4-1-83 tasyāpatyam; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ P. 7-2-117 vṛddhi; the ṭi dropped; auśija with suffix end-accent). ॥1॥ A crowded run of four pages; outline only; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 18, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यो रेवान्यो अमीवहा वसुवित्पुष्टिवर्धनः । स नः सिषक्तु यस्तुरः ॥२॥

yo revān yo amīvahā vasuvit puṣṭivardhanaḥ | sa naḥ siṣaktu yas turaḥ ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

यः । रेवान् । यः । अमीवऽहा । वसुऽवित् । पुष्टिऽवर्धनः ॥ सः । नः । सिषक्तु । यः । तुरः ॥२॥

yaḥ | revān | yaḥ | amīva-hā | vasu-vit | puṣṭi-vardhanaḥ || saḥ | naḥ | siṣaktu | yaḥ | turaḥ ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यो ब्रह्मणस्पती रेवान्धनवांश्च अमीवहा रोगाणां हन्ता वसुवित्धनलब्धा पुष्टिवर्धनः पुष्टेर्वर्धयिता यश्च तुरः त्वरायुक्तः शीघ्रफलदः स ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्नोऽस्मान्सिषक्तु । सेवताम् । परिगृह्यानुगृह्णात्वित्यर्थः । अत्र सिषक्तेः सेवार्थत्वस्य यास्क आह । सिषक्तु सचत इति सेवमानस्य । नि. [३-१०] । इति । प्रत्ययोकारशब्दावितीति शेषः ॥ रेवान् । रयिरस्यास्तीति मतुप् । रयेर्मतौ बहुलम् । पा. [६-१-३७ ?] । इति यकारस्य संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वम् । छन्दसीर इति वत्वम् । आद्गुणः । … अमीवहा । अम रोग इत्येतस्माद्वप्रत्ययेनामीवशब्दो निपातितः । तं हन्तीति बहुलं छन्दसीति क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वसुवित् । वसु विन्दतीति वसुवित् । क्विप् च । उत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पुष्टिवर्धनः । वर्धयतेर्नन्दादित्वाल्ल्युः । पा. [३-१-१३४] । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । पुष्टेर्वर्धन इति कर्मणि षष्ठ्या समासः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सिषक्तु । षच समवाये । लोटि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । श्लौ द्वित्वे हलादिशेषे बहुलं छन्दसीत्यभ्यासस्याकारस्येकारः । पा. [७-४-७८] । तुरः । तुर त्वरणे । इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः । कः प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥२॥

yo brahmaṇaspatī revān dhanavāṃś ca amīvahā rogāṇāṃ hantā vasuvid dhana-labdhā puṣṭivardhanaḥ puṣṭer vardhayitā yaś ca turaḥ tvarāyuktaḥ śīghra-phaladaḥ sa brahmaṇaspatir no 'smān siṣaktu | sevatām | parigṛhyānugṛhṇātv ity arthaḥ | atra siṣakteḥ sevārthatvasya yāska āha | siṣaktu sacata iti sevamānasya | ni. [3-10] | iti | pratyayokāra-śabdāv iti śeṣaḥ || revān | rayir asyāstīti matup | rayer matau bahulam | pā. [6-1-37 ?] | iti yakārasya saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvam | chandasīra iti vatvam | ād guṇaḥ | … amīvahā | ama roga ity etasmād vapratyayenāmīva-śabdo nipātitaḥ | taṃ hantīti bahulaṃ chandasīti kvip | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | vasuvit | vasu vindatīti vasuvit | kvip ca | uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | puṣṭivardhanaḥ | vardhayater nandādittvāl lyuḥ | pā. [3-1-134] | liti iti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvam | puṣṭer vardhana iti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyā samāsaḥ | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | siṣaktu | ṣaca samavāye | loṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | ślau dvitve halādiśeṣe bahulaṃ chandasīty abhyāsasyākārasyekāraḥ | pā. [7-4-78] | turaḥ | tura tvaraṇe | igupadha-jñā-prī-kiraḥ kaḥ | kaḥ pratyaya-svaraḥ ||2||

Translation: "That Brahmaṇaspati who is revān — wealthy; amīvahā — the slayer of diseases; vasuvit — the finder of wealth; puṣṭivardhanaḥ — the increaser of nourishment; and who is turaḥ — swift, quick to give fruit: may that Brahmaṇaspati siṣaktu — attend upon (favour) us, the sense being 'having taken us up, may he show favour'. As to sac having the sense of 'serve', Yāska says: 'siṣaktu: sacate, of one who serves' (Nirukta 3-10 [?])." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: revān (rayi + matup; saṃprasāraṇa of y; va by P. 8-2-15); amīvahā (amīva, 'disease', by nipātana from am; han + kvip); vasuvit (vid + kvip); puṣṭivardhanaḥ (lyu by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ; the genitive compound in the object sense); siṣaktu (sac "to be joined", loṭ, with śap replaced by ślu [reduplication] "variously in the Veda"; the vowel of the reduplicative a becomes i by P. 7-4-78); turaḥ (tur "to hasten", suffix ka by P. 3-1-135 igupadhajñāprīkirḥ kaḥ; suffix accent). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 3-1-134 and 7-4-78 as read agree with the standard numbering.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

यः (yaḥ) — which Brahmaṇaspati | रेवान् (revān) — [who is] wealthy | यः (yaḥ) — who | अमीवहा (amīvahā) — the remover of diseases | वसुवित् (vasuvit) — the finder of wealth | पुष्टिवर्धनः (puṣṭivardhanaḥ) — the increaser of nourishment | यः (yaḥ) — who | तुरः (turaḥ) — swift to give the fruit | सः (saḥ) — that Brahmaṇaspati | नः (naḥ) — us | सिषक्तु (siṣaktu) — let him serve (favour).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Brahmaṇaspati is greatly wealthy; he is worthy to give wealth to others; he brings increase of nourishment; and he gives fruit quickly. May such a Brahmaṇaspati favour us.

॥ English Translation ॥ The print has "increaser" misspelt in the Pratipadārtha lines as "increaaser" — [sic]; The corrected word is given.

May he (Brahmanaspati) who is wealthy, the healer of disease; the acquirer of riches, increaser of nourishments, the prompt bestower of rewards be favourable to us.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

रेवान् (revān) — rayir asyāsti iti revān: one who has wealth.

अमीवहा (amīvahā) — amī rogaḥ taṃ hantīti amīvahā: the destroyer of disease.

तुरः (turaḥ) — tvaropetaḥ śīghraphaladaḥ: one who gives fruits quickly. Though tura may mean "one who does work quickly or hurriedly", here the commentator takes it to mean one who gives quick fruit to actions.

Grammar pages (pp. 756 lower half–757 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats revān (rayiḥ asya asti; tad asyāsty asminn iti matup P. 5-2-94; the sup dropped by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ; rayer mator bahulam P. 6-1-37 [as read 6-1-37? — the Kannada gives the numerals as "೬-೧-೩೭-೬"; I give it as 6-1-37 [?]] gives saṃprasāraṇa of y variously when matup follows; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108 pūrvarūpa; chandasīraḥ P. 8-2-15 gives va for the ma of matup after a stem ending in i/ī or r; ād guṇaḥ P. 6-1-87 — with the scholastic question whether va [by chandasīraḥ] or guṇa [by ād guṇaḥ] comes first: since chandasīraḥ is in the eighth chapter and ād guṇaḥ in the sixth, by pūrvatrāsiddham P. 8-2-1 the earlier-chapter rule is stronger, so guṇa first; and also the antaraṅga and bahiraṅga paribhāṣās [asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge] give the same result — so re + vat, with ra + i + mat → re + mat, then va; anādivac ca P. 6-1-87? [the ekādeśa is treated as the end of the former and the beginning of the latter word — hence the e is the ādi of the matup's preceding stem and vat follows]). ॥2॥ A crowded run; outline only; numerals as read; pointers only.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

मा नः शंसो अररुषो धूर्तिः प्रणङ्मर्त्यस्य । रक्षा णो ब्रह्मणस्पते ॥३॥

mā naḥ śaṃso araruṣo dhūrtiḥ praṇaṅ martyasya | rakṣā ṇo brahmaṇas pate ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened rakṣā, and ṇaḥ for naḥ by the sandhi of P. 8-4-27 [as printed]; the Pada has rakṣa, naḥ.

मा । नः । शंसः । अररुषः । धूर्तिः । प्रणक् । मर्त्यस्य ॥ रक्ष । नः । ब्रह्मणः । पते ॥३॥

mā | naḥ | śaṃsaḥ | araruṣaḥ | dhūrtiḥ | praṇak | martyasya || rakṣa | naḥ | brahmaṇaḥ | pate ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अररुषो मर्त्यस्योपद्रवं कर्तुमस्मद्विनाशं प्राप्तस्य [?] शत्रुरूपस्य मनुष्यस्य धूर्तिर्हिंसकः शंसः शंसनम् । आक्षेप इत्यर्थः । तादृशो वाग्विशेषो नोऽस्मान्मा प्रणक् मा संपृणक्तु । शत्रुणा प्रयुक्तो विक्षेपः कदाचिदस्मान्मा प्राप्नोत्वित्यर्थः । तदर्थं हे ब्रह्मणस्पते नोऽस्मान् रक्ष । पालय ॥ मा । निपातः । शंसनम् । शंसः । भावे घञ् । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अररुषः । ऋतेरारुः । उ. [३-३-१७४] । उपधायाश्च । पा. [७-१-१०१] । इत्युपधादीर्घत्वम् । वलि लोपं बाधित्वोरि प्राप्ते । पा. [६-४-२०] । राल्लोपः । पा. [६-४-२१] । इति वकारलोपः । प्रणक् । पृची संपर्के । लङि तिप् । इतश्च । पा. araruṣo martyasyopadravaṃ kartum asmad-vināśaṃ prāptasya [?] śatrurūpasya manuṣyasya dhūrtir hiṃsakaḥ śaṃsaḥ śaṃsanam | ākṣepa ity arthaḥ | tādṛśo vāg-viśeṣo no 'smān mā praṇak mā saṃpṛṇaktu | śatruṇā prayukto vikṣepaḥ kadācid asmān mā prāpnotv ity arthaḥ | tad-arthaṃ he brahmaṇaspate no 'smān rakṣa | pālaya || mā | nipātaḥ | śaṃsanam | śaṃsaḥ | bhāve ghañ | ñittvād ādyudāttaḥ | araruṣaḥ | ṛter āruḥ | u.
