Sūkta 19, Rik 9 (last rik of the sūkta and of the volume)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतये सृजामि सोम्यं मधु । मरुद्भिरग्न आ गहि ॥९॥

abhi tvā pūrvapītaye sṛjāmi somyaṃ madhu | marudbhir agna ā gahi ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अभि । त्वा । पूर्वऽपीतये । सृजामि । सोम्यम् । मधु ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥९॥

abhi | tvā | pūrva-pītaye | sṛjāmi | somyam | madhu || marut-bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने पूर्वपीतये पूर्वकाले प्रवृत्तायै पानाय त्वां प्रति सोम्यं मधु सोमसम्बन्धिनं मधुररसमभि सृजामि । सर्वतः सम्पादयामि । अतस्त्वं मरुद्भिः सहात्रागच्छ ॥ अभि । एवमादीनामन्त इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । त्वा । त्वामौ द्वितीयायाः । पा. [८-१-२३] । इति त्वादेशः सर्वानुदात्तः । पूर्वपीतये । पूर्वा चासौ पीतिश्च । पुंवत्कर्मधारयजातीयदेशीययोः । पा. [६-३-४२] । पुंवद्भावः । सृजामि । सृज विसर्गे । मिपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । विकरणस्वरः । सोम्यम् । सोममर्हति यः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । मधु । फलिपाटनमि… । उ. [१-१८] । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तत्वम् । अन्यद्गतम् ॥९॥

he agne pūrva-pītaye pūrva-kāle pravṛttāyai pānāya tvāṃ prati somyaṃ madhu soma-sambandhinaṃ madhura-rasam abhi sṛjāmi | sarvataḥ sampādayāmi | atas tvaṃ marudbhiḥ sahātrāgaccha || abhi | evam-ādīnām anta ity antodāttatvam | tvā | tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ | pā. [8-1-23] | iti tvādeśaḥ sarvānudāttaḥ | pūrvapītaye | pūrvā cāsau pītiś ca | puṃvat-karmadhāraya-jātīya-deśīyayoḥ | pā. [6-3-42] | puṃvad-bhāvaḥ | sṛjāmi | sṛja visarge | mipaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | vikaraṇa-svaraḥ | somyam | somam arhati yaḥ | pratyaya-svareṇāntodāttaḥ | madhu | phali-pāṭana-mi… | u. [1-18] | u-pratyayaḥ | nid ity anuvṛtter ādyudāttatvam | anyad gatam ||9||

Translation: "O Agni! For the pūrvapīti — the drinking that [takes place] first — I pour out (abhi sṛjāmi, 'I prepare on all sides') for you the somya madhu — the sweet juice belonging to the soma. Therefore come here together with the Maruts. Abhi — end-accent by the list of evamādi words; tvā — the substitute tvā for tvām, by P. 8-1-23, wholly unaccented; pūrvapītaye — pūrvā cāsau pītiś ca, a karmadhāraya, the feminine taking the masculine form by P. 6-3-42; sṛjāmi — sṛj 'to emit'; the mip ending is pit and unaccented, the accent of the vikaraṇa [śap? — tudādi śa] remains; somyam — 'that which is fit for soma', end accent by the suffix; madhu — Uṇ. 1-18, the suffix u, first-syllable accent. The rest has been dealt with."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | त्वाम् (tvām) — you, or [for] you | पूर्वपीतये (pūrvapītaye) — [that you may] drink first of all | सोम्यम् (somyam) — belonging to soma | मधु (madhu) — the sweet juice | अभि सृजामि (abhi sṛjāmi) — I put into the vessel and make ready | मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — with the Marut deities | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni! I pour the soma-juice, delightful to the taste, into the vessel and prepare it for you to drink before all others. Therefore come here together with the Marut deities.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, I pour out the sweet drink of Soma to you that you may drink first ; come hither with the Maruths.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

पूर्वपीतये (pūrvapītaye) — "so that you may drink before all". For this word Wilson, the scholar, gives the wrong meaning "as of old" [the print gives the English phrase: "as of old"]. The sense "before all others" given by the commentator is the appropriate one.

अभि सृजामि (abhi sṛjāmi) — sarvataḥ sampādayāmi: "I put into the vessel and make ready".

सोम्यम् (somyam) — somam arhati yaḥ: worthy of soma; belonging to soma.

मधु (madhu) — sweet, delicious; somyaṃ madhu means the delicious soma-juice.

Grammar pages (pp. 806 lower half–808 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: abhi (vivādīnām antaḥ [Phiṭ-sūtra 4-[?]] gives end accent), tvā (yuṣmad + am; tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ P. 8-1-23 gives tvā and mā for a following accusative singular of yuṣmad/asmad when not at the beginning of a pāda, and those substitutes are wholly unaccented), pūrvapītaye (pūrvā cāsau pītiś ca; the compound karmadhāraya, pūrvā feminine; puṃvat karmadhārayajātīyadeśīyayoḥ P. 6-3-42 gives masculine form to the feminine first member of a karmadhāraya; the Kannada discusses at length the scope of this sūtra and the preceding striyāḥ puṃvad bhāṣitapuṃskād anūṅ samānādhikaraṇe striyām apūraṇīpriyādiṣu P. 6-3-34, with its exclusions of ordinal and priyā-type words; the bhāṣitapuṃska "word whose masculine form is spoken", ūṅ-ending, apūraṇīpriyādi; the atideśa of sevenfold kind [kāryarūpanimittārthaśāstratāṅgātmyaśabdāḥ — as the Kannada gives it, the verse vyapadeśaś ca saptaitān atideśān pracakṣate]; the tāṅgātmya-atideśa applies here, "the form of the masculine"; the dative singular ṅe → ye, pūrvapīti + e; ṅiti hrasvaś ca P. 1-4-6 shortens the ī; ghi-name; gher ṅiti P. 7-3-111 gives guṇa; eco 'yavāyāvaḥ), sṛjāmi (sṛja visarge, tudādi; laṭ first person singular mip; śa [vikaraṇa] with sṛj + a + mi; ato dīrgho yañi P. 7-3-101 lengthens the a; mip is pit so unaccented by P. 3-1-4; the accent of the vikaraṇa [śa] remains), somyam (somam arhati yaḥ P. 5-1-… dvitīyāntāt; yat after the accusative soma in the sense "deserving"; soma + am + ya; supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ P. 2-4-71 drops am; yasyeti ca drops the a of soma; somya; suffix accent), and madhu (phalipāṭinami… Uṇ. 1-[?] gives the suffix u; nit carried over, so first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197; the process for madhu is explained in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]; the remaining words have been dealt with earlier). ॥9॥ ॥19॥ ॥37॥ The closing numerals read "೯ ‖ ೧೯ ‖ ೩೭" — Rik 9, Sūkta 19, Varga 37 — which supports the "36, 37" of the heading; They were read at 150 dpi, not enlarged.

Close of Sūkta 19, of Adhyāya 1, and of the volume

॥ Closing verse and colophon (Sanskrit, in Kannada script) ॥

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थाँश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥

vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthām̐ś caturo deyād vidyā-tīrtha-maheśvaraḥ ||

Translation: "May Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, dispelling the darkness of the heart by the light of the meaning of the Veda, grant the four human aims." The verse is the standard benediction found at the close of each section of the Mādhavīya Vedārthaprakāśa; It is given as printed, and the English is editorial.

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तकश्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये प्रथमाष्टके प्रथमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ ॐ तत्सत् ॥

iti śrīmad-rājādhirāja-parameśvara-vaidika-mārga-pravartaka-śrī-vīrabukka-bhūpāla-sāmrājya-dhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārtha-prakāśe ṛk-saṃhitā-bhāṣye prathamāṣṭake prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || oṃ tat sat ||

Translation: "Thus ends the First Adhyāya in the First Aṣṭaka of the Ṛk-saṃhitā-bhāṣya — the Mādhavīya Vedārthaprakāśa — composed by Sāyaṇācārya, the bearer of the burden of the empire of the glorious King Vīra-Bukka, the King of Kings, Supreme Lord, the establisher of the Vedic path. Oṃ, That is the Real."

॥ Kannada colophon ॥ "Here the First Adhyāya in the First Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the Bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and a Kannada rendering, comes to its end."

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥

yad akṣara-pada-bhraṣṭaṃ mātrā-hīnaṃ tu yad bhavet | tat sarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ||

Translation: "Whatever may be faulty in letter or word, or deficient in measure — may all that be forgiven, O God, Lord of Speech; salutations to you." The English is editorial.

॥ शुभं भूयात् ॥ ॥ मंगळं ॥

|| śubhaṃ bhūyāt || || maṅgaḷaṃ ||

"May there be auspiciousness. Blessing."

This page continues and closes the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya's grammatical derivation of "aśvinā," "āmantritasya," "yajvarī," "dravat-pāṇī," "śubhas-patī," and "purubhujā" in the established dense sutra-citation register — including specific accent-rules and a cross-reference to the word "khādāte" discussed elsewhere. Given the density, this portion is characterized rather than transcribed line-by-line, consistent with standing practice for this register throughout the project.

8. The grammatical derivation for this sukta's opening verse — covering "aśvinā" as a vocative-adjacent form (per Phit-sutra 1.1.28), "yajvarī" analyzed via the root meaning "to accomplish the sacrifice," "iṣaḥ" and its accent-variants, "dravat-pāṇī" as a compound of "dravat" (running/swift) and "pāṇi" (hand/foot), "śubhas-patī" with its accent-retention rule, and "canasyatam" as a denominative verb formed from "canas" — proceeds here in the same dense sutra-citation register used throughout this work. Given its density, it is characterized here rather than transcribed line by line, consistent with standing practice; none of it alters the senses already established above in the Bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, and Viśeṣārtha sections for this verse.

9. Characterized here rather than transcribed line-by-line, consistent with standing practice for this register; none of it changes the senses already established above.

¶ Continuing "vocēyuḥ":) *…**लिङ्याशिषि…* (liṅ āśiṣy aṅ, पा. ३-१-८६ [as printed; the usual number is different, and the print is recorded]) puts "aṅ" in the āśīrliṅ; झेर्जुस् (पा. ३-४-१०८) puts "jus" for "jhi"; the "j" of "jus" is an "it" by चुटू (पा. १-३-७) and the "s" ... elided by तस्य लोपः (पा. १-३-९); "vac + a + us" — वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (पा. ६-१-१५) and वचेरुम् [as printed "vace um," पा. २-४-२०] — before "aṅ" the augment "um" comes to "vac"; आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७) gives guṇa; यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च (पा. ३-४-१०३) — the augment "yāsuṭ" in the parasmaipada, acute and "ṅit"; किदाशिषि (पा. ३-४-१०४) — "yāsuṭ" in the āśīrliṅ is "kit" (so no guṇa); the Mādhava school adds that by this very sūtra "yāsuṭ" comes. Hence "vac + yās + us." By छन्दस्युभयथा (पा. ३-४-११७) in the Veda the affix is both "sārvadhātuka" and "ārdhadhātuka"; hence "yās + us" takes the "sārvadhātuka" label, and लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) elides the "s" of "yās" ("s" not at the end); अतो येयः (पा. ७-२-८०) turns the "yā" (after an "a"-final stem) into "iy" → "voc-iy-us"; आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७) → "vocēyuḥ." The "sārvadhātuka" accent is lost by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित् (पा. ६-१-१८६) and the affix "aṅ" keeps its own acute; the single substitute "ē" of "i + a" … is acute by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. ८-२-५). - "Dasma" — "dasu upakṣaye" with the Uṇādi ईषियुधीन्धिदसिश्याधूसूभ्योऽमुक् [as printed] (उ. सू. १-१४४ [?]) the affix "ma" with the augment "muk"; as a vocative standing after another word it loses its accent (आमन्त्रितस्य च, as printed). - "Kṛṣṭayaḥ" — क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् (पा. ३-३-१७४): "ktic" and "kta" in a sense of a name: "ktic" is added to "kṛṣ," meaning "men"; "c"-marked, so the last syllable is acute by चितः (पा. ६-१-१६३). - "Syāma" — "as bhuvi" (to be) in the optative (vidhi-liṅ), first-person plural; "yāsuṭ"; by लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) the "s" is elided; the affix "mas" loses its final "s" (नित्यं ङितः, पा. ३-४-९९); श्नसोरल्लोपः (पा. ६-४-१११) the "a" of "as" is elided before an affix that is "k" or "ṅ"-marked; hence "s-yā-ma" → "syāma." (The page ends mid-derivation of "syāma"; it continues on p. 116.

Sūkta 7

1. The top of this page carries the end of the Kannada anuvāda translated above; its content is given there.

2. small-print Kannada digits, re-read at 300 dpi: "13, 14". This fits the run of two vargas per sūkta from Sūkta 3 (5, 6) and Sūkta 8 (15, 16), but not the "eighth varga" of the Sūkta 6 colophon; unreconciled. An earlier reading here of "9, 10" was wrong.

¶ The remainder of the Sanskrit on this page and the next carries Sāyaṇa's grammatical derivation of गाथिनः [gāthinaḥ], बृहत् [bṛhat], अर्केभिः [arkebhiḥ], अर्किणः [arkiṇaḥ], वाणीः [vāṇīḥ] and अनूषत [anūṣata] — suffixes, accent, and Vedic irregularities of case-ending — in the standard dense register. Characterized rather than transcribed line by line (Convention 5); the sense of each word is already fixed by the passage above. In outline: gāthinaḥ is formed with the suffix than (from the root gai, "to sing") and then ini ("one who has gāthās"); bṛhat has its instrumental ending dropped (the standard luk of case-endings in the Veda); arkebhiḥ lacks the usual ais substitution by Vedic license; arkiṇaḥ is "those who have arkas"; vāṇīḥ is a nominative form standing in an instrumental sense; anūṣata is an aorist of the root nu ("to praise") in the middle voice with a Vedic irregularity.

3. as printed in the source

6. Continues the Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 1 in the same register — the optional-lengthening discussion for vāṇīḥ and the finite-verb analysis of anūṣata, completed on the next page. Characterized as above; not transcribed.

7. The first nine lines complete the Rik 1 grammar — the analysis of anūṣata, ending with the observation that, since the root nu belongs to the kuṭādi class, the sic aorist behaves as if marked ṅit and so guṇa does not arise. Then the number ॥१॥ closes Rik 1. Characterized, not transcribed.

8. Sāyaṇa's grammatical notes follow on page 264 — in the Sanskrit itself — and are characterized there.

¶ The first part of this page is the Sanskrit grammar of Rik 2 inside the bhāṣya itself. Characterized, not transcribed. Points of substance: हर्योः (haryoḥ) — "the two that carry" (harataḥ), from hṛ, with the suffix in; initial-udātta. सचा (sacā) — glossed "with" (Nirukta 5-5, "sacā saheti"). सम्मिश्लः (sammiślaḥ) — "mixing" from miśra + ghañ (Pā. 3-3-18) with a Vedic l for r, so "one who mixes thoroughly"; accent of the first member retained in the bahuvrīhi. वचोयुजा (vacoyujā) — "yoked with a word"; the dual case-ending replaced by ā; the second member yuj has the final accent. वज्री (vajrī) — "having a vajra", suffix ini (Pā. 5-2-115). हिरण्ययः (hiraṇyayaḥ) — by Pāṇini 6-4-175 [?] (the source's printed number reads "6-4-17[?]"), the m of hiraṇmaya is dropped irregularly in the Veda, so hiraṇyaya is the form; it is udātta on the ā by the suffix-accent.

9. All Ṛgveda numbers below are read from small print and are given with "[?]". The Sanskrit of each rik is transcribed from the Kannada script, with word-division as read. Where the scan made a word doubtful, it is marked.

10. Citation-heavy list: numbers and several words are low-confidence and are shown only so the reader sees the shape of the evidence; they must be checked against a clear copy before reliance.

11. Pages 266–268: the Kannada grammar of Rik 2 — characterized, not transcribed; Convention 5. Points of substance:

12. Page 267 continues the Rik 2 grammar; page 268 closes it. The last lines on p. 268 conclude that it is "proper," as explained in the Vedic commentary (Veda-bhāṣya), to accept the loss of the letter itself and say that the single-substitute vowel is udātta by Pā. 8-2-5, and the number ॥२॥ closes Rik 2. Characterized as above — the source is arguing a point of Pāṇinian procedure, not adding to the sense of the rik.

¶ Grammar page, noted briefly.) रुव (ruva) — ru śabde (adādi), loṭ second singular sip, sip → hi by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-87 [?]). The adādi vikaraṇa śap ought to be dropped by "ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72 [?]); here instead, by Vedic inversion, a śa-type vikaraṇa arises, which is ārdhadhātuka-like and blocks no guṇa because śa is śit (so sārvadhātukam apit, Pā. 1-2-4 [?], treats it as ṅit); the u of ru before the vikaraṇa takes uvaṅ by "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvoriyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. 6-4-77 [?]), giving ruv + a + hi; hi is dropped by "ato heḥ" (Pā. 6-4-105 [?]), so ruva; wholly unaccented as a finite verb (Pā. 8-1-28 [?]). ब्रह्म (brahma) — root bṛha vṛddhau ("to grow"), an idit root, so num by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-58 [?]), giving bṛṃh; then manin by "bṛheror mano lopaś ca" (Uṇ. 4-[?]) with the augment am, n of num dropped; some read the Uṇādi sūtra as "bṛṃher noccha ca"; the ṛ is changed to ra by "iko yaṇaci" (Pā. 6-1-77 [?]), giving brahman; manin is nit, so initial-udātta. वसो (vaso) — a vocative, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19 [?]). यज्ञम् (yajñam) — naṅ by "yajayācayatavicchaprachar akṣo naṅ" (Pā. 3-3-90 [?]) after yaj; j + n → jñ ("stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ," Pā. 8-4-40 [?]). वर्धय (vardhaya) — a finite verb, unaccented by "tiṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28 [?]); but since in this mantra two ca's are heard (brahma ca vardhaya, yajñaṃ ca vardhaya), the verb is connected with the earlier clause too — so that the vardhaya of the earlier clause is the first finite verb of the joined sentence, and the rule "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. 8-1-59 [?]) prevents the lowering of the first verb in a sentence joined by ca and vā; hence no lowering applies where the first-uttered verb is concerned. (Sūtra numbers read from small print; pointers only.

¶ Grammar page, noted briefly. The page is Sāyaṇa's Sanskrit grammar, in outline: that the word sunirajam is formed with the prefixes su and nis and the root aja, with khal (Pā. 3-3-126 [?]), so that the su does not intervene with the retroflexion by nis; that tvādātam is from the root dāp śodhane, with the ṅit-like treatment, the substitute tva for tvad by the rule for the third case singular, and the ending replaced by ā by "supāṃ suluk…"; that yaśaḥ is from aśū vyāptau with asun (Uṇ. 4-190 [?]), initial-udātta by the stem accent; gavām takes its stem accent; vṛdhi — root vṛñ varaṇe, with hi replaced by dhi, śnu dropped by bahulam chandasi; kṛṇuṣva — root kṛñ hiṃsākaraṇayoḥ with uk, ś-vikaraṇa as u by "dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca" (Pā. 3-1-80 [?]) with va for ṇa; and adrivaḥ — "adriḥ vajraḥ tad asyāstīti matup," with matup in the Veda taking va, the vocative in matup with num (Pā. 7-1-70 [?]), and the rule "hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal" (Pā. 6-1-68 [?]), the ru and visarga of the vocative.

Continuing "Tvādātam":) … dāp śodhane: "by the rule ādeca upadeśe 'śiti (Pā. 6-1-45 [?]), taking the form of a different root, he explains it" — "purified by you, made clear," as the Bhāṣyakāra explains. ¶ The source remarks that this derivation follows the Vṛttikāra; in fact, no kyaṣ is attached here, since the Lohitādi group contains only a-ending words; the Mahābhāṣya of Patañjali says the suffix kyaṣ is not enjoined after consonant-ending words, and the Kāśikā-type analysis is therefore not tenable; another derivation is given: "ṛghāyate" = "ṛghā iva ācarati" with kyaṅ (Pā. 3-1-11 [?]) — a compound from the word ṛghan followed by kyac (Pā. 3-1-10 [?]) optionally, then the technical name pada at the end of ṛghan by "svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne" (Pā. 1-4-17 [?]) and the dropping of n by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7 [?]), the loss of n being "unseen" by "nalopaḥ supsvarasaṃjñātugvidhiṣu kṛti" (Pā. 8-2-2 [?]); and "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. 8-2-1 [?]) means the loss of n is not "seen" when lengthening applies; kyac is c-marked, so the ātmanepada comes from "anudātta-ṅita ātmanepadam" (Pā. 1-3-12 [?]); the rest as above.

42. The Kannada explanation of Yāska's gloss on p. 566:) "Bhāratī" — bharata is one of the twelve Ādityas; bhā means the lustre of the Āditya; hence bhāratī is the light of the sun, or the fire shining in the orb of the sun. "Iḷā" — iḷā means the earth. Manuṣvat cetayantī — having the power to urge as men do: she makes the people on earth take up food and other nourishment, and gives wealth; so the iḷā-deity is a special form of Agni who dwells in the earth-region. "Sarasvatī" — since she is the presiding deity of the lightning in the atmosphere, Sarasvatī is said to be the form of Agni who dwells in the atmosphere. Hence it is customary to say that the three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Bhāratī are three forms of the fire that is in heaven, atmosphere and earth. (The source refers the reader to its pages 64–69 [sic: "६४–६९ನೇ ಪೇಜು"] for further treatment.
